770.i: have your ˈcake and eat it (too)
770.cn: 既要…又要…；鱼和熊掌不可兼得
770.e: You can't have your cake and eat it too, so choose one holiday.  鱼和熊掌不可兼得，所以你只能挑一次假期。

771.i: a share/slice of the ˈcake (BrE) (AmE a piece/share/slice of the ˈpie)
771.cn: 分得的一份好处；应得的一份利益
771.e: Local firms all want a slice of the cake now that the new port is open.  新港口一开，本地企业都想分一杯羹。

772.cn: 超出职责要求；分外尽力
772.e: Staying all night to finish the report went far beyond the call of duty.  熬通宵写完报告，这远远超出了本职要求。

773.i: above and beyond the call of ˈduty (formal)
773.cn: 远超职责范围；格外尽责
773.e: The young officer acted above and beyond the call of duty and later received a bravery award.  那名年轻警察的表现远超职责所在，后来获得了英勇奖。

774.cn: 要求某人摊牌；逼某人兑现威胁
774.e: She threatened to quit, so I called her bluff and handed her a resignation form.  她扬言要辞职，我就把辞职表递过去逼她摊牌。

775.e: The referee called a halt to the match when the rain got too heavy.  雨下得太大，裁判叫停了比赛。

776.e: We've been painting since dawn, so let's call it a day and grab a beer.  我们从天亮就在刷漆，今天就到这儿吧，去喝杯啤酒。

777.e: You paid for dinner and I paid for the taxi, so let's call it quits.  你请了饭我付了车钱，就算两清吧。

778.e: He got detention for calling the new boy names during the lunch break.  他午休时辱骂新来的男生，被罚留校。

779.e: After ten years of renting, they finally have a small flat to call their own.  租了十年房，他们终于有了一套属于自己的小公寓。

780.e: Now that Dad's retired, my sister calls the shots in the family business.  爸爸退休后，家里的生意由我姐姐说了算。

781.e: Let's call a spade a spade: the plan failed because nobody bothered to test it.  说白了吧，计划失败是因为根本没人去测试。

782.cn: 责成某人解释；追究某人责任
782.e: The minister was called to account for the missing funds at yesterday's hearing.  昨天的听证会上，部长被要求就资金去向作出交代。

783.i: call yourself a ˈteacher, a ˈfriend, etc.? (informal)
783.cn: 你也配称作教师（朋友等）
783.e: You call yourself a friend? You didn't even answer the phone when I needed help.  你也配叫朋友？我需要帮忙时你连电话都不接。

784.cn: 你也好意思自称音乐家
784.e: How can he call himself a musician when he's never even heard of Schubert?  他连舒伯特都没听说过，怎么好意思自称音乐家？

785.i: cannot hold a candle to sb/sth (informal)
785.cn: 远远比不上；无法与…相媲美
785.e: Her new album is fine, but it cannot hold a candle to her first one.  她的新专辑还行，但跟第一张比差远了。

786.i: be like taking ˌcandy from a ˈbaby (also be like shooting ˌfish in a ˈbarrel)
786.e: Beating that team was like taking candy from a baby—we won by four goals.  赢那支球队易如反掌，我们净胜四球。

787.e: The general treated the new recruits as little more than cannon fodder.  那位将军把新兵不过当成炮灰。

788.i: go cap in ˈhand (to sb) (BrE) (AmE go hat in ˈhand)
788.cn: 低声下气地求人；恭敬讨要
788.e: He had to go cap in hand to his father for next month's rent.  他只好低声下气地找父亲要下个月的房租。

789.i: if the cap fits (, wear it) (BrE) (AmE if the shoe fits (, wear it)) (saying)
789.cn: 说得对就接受；有则改之
789.e: I never said you were lazy, but if the cap fits, wear it.  我可没说你懒，不过要是说中了就认了吧。

790.e: Winning that contract was a real feather in her cap at such a young age.  这么年轻就拿下那份合同，实在是她的一大荣耀。

791.e: The opposition made capital out of the minister's clumsy remarks about teachers.  反对党拿部长关于教师的失言大做文章。

792.i: with a capital ˈA, ˈB, ˈC, etc.
792.e: He's lazy with a capital L—he hasn't washed a dish all week.  他懒得出奇，一整周连个碗都没洗过。

793.e: The dinner was full of captains of industry swapping stories about the new tax.  晚宴上满是工商界巨头，都在议论新税。

794.cn: 极其相似的人（或物）；翻版
794.e: Their second album is a carbon copy of the first, right down to the artwork.  他们的第二张专辑简直是第一张的翻版，连封面都一样。

795.i: keep/hold/play your cards ˌclose to your ˈchest
795.e: The manager kept his cards close to his chest until the transfer deadline.  转会截止前，主教练一直守口如瓶。

796.i: play your cards ˌclose to your ˈvest (AmE)
796.e: She played her cards close to her vest during the whole salary negotiation.  整个薪资谈判过程中她都不露口风。

797.i: on the ˈcards (BrE) (AmE in the ˈcards) (informal)
797.e: A cabinet reshuffle has been on the cards ever since the election result.  自从选举结果出来，内阁改组就一直被看作大有可能。

798.i: put/lay your ˈcards on the table (informal)
798.e: Let's put our cards on the table: how much are you really willing to pay?  咱们摊牌吧，你到底愿意出多少钱？

799.e: If you play your cards right, the boss might send you to Tokyo.  你要是会来事儿，老板说不定会派你去东京。

800.i: ˈcare of sb (AmE also in ˈcare of sb)
800.e: Send the letter care of my sister; I'll be travelling all next month.  信寄给我姐姐转交吧，我下个月一直在外面跑。

801.e: He couldn't care less what the neighbours think about his purple front door.  邻居怎么看他那扇紫色大门，他压根不在乎。

802.i: for all I, you, etc. ˈcare (spoken)
802.e: For all I care, he can stay out there in the rain all night.  他要愿意在雨里站一夜，我才不管呢。

803.cn: 由政府照管；受福利机构监护
803.e: The two boys were taken into care after their mother fell seriously ill.  母亲重病后，两个男孩被政府接管照料。

804.i: not have a ˌcare in the ˈworld
804.e: Lying on the beach, she looked like she didn't have a care in the world.  躺在沙滩上的她，看着一副无忧无虑的样子。

805.i: without a ˌcare in the ˈworld
805.e: The kids ran through the sprinkler without a care in the world all afternoon.  孩子们一下午都在洒水器下疯跑，无忧无虑。

806.e: Take care to lock the back door when you leave the cottage.  离开小屋时务必锁好后门。

807.e: Don't worry about the bills—I'll take care of them while you're away.  账单别操心，你不在的时候我来处理。

808.e: Take care, and text me as soon as your plane lands in Sydney.  保重，飞机一落地悉尼就给我发消息。

809.e: Would you care for another slice of cake before I put it away?  我收起来之前，您还要再来一块蛋糕吗？

810.e: Would you care to join us for dinner at the hotel this evening?  今晚您愿意到酒店和我们一起吃饭吗？

811.cn: 越小心越好；再小心也不为过
811.e: Lock your bike even in the yard—you can't be too careful these days.  就算在院子里也把车锁上，如今再小心也不为过。

812.e: So the shirt's a bit creased—who cares? It's only a picnic.  衬衫皱一点又怎样？管它呢，不过是去野餐。

813.i: what do I, you, etc. ˈcare? (informal)
813.e: What do I care if he's angry? He started the whole argument.  他生气关我什么事？这场争吵是他挑起的。

814.e: After three delays at the airport, I was beyond caring about my luggage.  在机场被延误三次后，我已经懒得管行李了。

815.i: be on the ˈcarpet (informal, especially AmE)
815.e: He was on the carpet again for missing two deadlines in one week.  他一周误了两个期限，又被叫去挨训了。

816.e: The school tried to sweep the bullying complaints under the carpet for years.  多年来学校一直想把霸凌投诉压下去。

817.i: sweep sth under the ˈrug (AmE, informal)
817.e: You can't just sweep the budget shortfall under the rug and hope nobody notices.  你不能把预算缺口一藏了之，指望没人发现。

818.e: I got carried away at the sale and spent half my salary on shoes.  打折时我一激动，半个月工资全买了鞋。

819.cn: 胡萝卜加大棒；软硬兼施
819.e: The coach used the carrot and stick approach to get everyone training again.  教练软硬兼施，让大家重新开始训练。

820.e: The young team carried all before them and won the league by ten points.  这支年轻队伍所向披靡，以十分优势夺冠。

821.e: With the director away, Maria carried the ball on the whole marketing launch.  总监不在，整个营销发布由玛丽亚挑大梁。

822.e: As usual, the junior staff carried the can for their manager's bad decision.  和往常一样，经理决策失误却由基层员工背黑锅。

823.cn: 推卸责任；把责任推给别人
823.e: Stop passing the buck and admit that the mistake was yours from the start.  别再推卸责任了，承认这错从一开始就是你的。

824.e: He's carried a torch for her since university, but he's never said a word.  他从大学起就暗恋她，却始终没开过口。

1155.cn: 处于鼎盛时期；春风得意
1155.e: Right after the album went platinum the band was on the crest of a wave.  专辑大卖之后，乐队正当红得发紫。

1156.cn: 最低限度的人员；基本运作的班子（或服务）
1156.e: Over Christmas the hospital runs with a skeleton staff and only urgent cases.  圣诞期间医院只留最少人手，仅处理急诊。

1157.e: Reading someone else's emails is just not cricket, even if you're the boss.  偷看别人的邮件太不地道了，就算你是老板也一样。

1158.i: put a ˈcrimp in/on sth (AmE, informal)
1158.e: The rain really put a crimp in our plans for the weekend barbecue.  这场雨把我们周末烧烤的计划全搅黄了。

1159.i: put a ˈcrimp on sth (AmE, informal)
1159.e: The extra expense of moving can put a crimp on your monthly budget.  搬家多出来的花销会把你每月的预算压得很紧。

1160.i: a ˌcrock of ˈshit (taboo, slang, especially AmE)
1160.e: Honestly, that excuse about traffic is a crock of shit and everyone knows it.  说什么堵车，全是屁话，谁都看得出来。

1161.e: He cried crocodile tears at the funeral of the uncle he'd ignored for years.  他在多年不理的叔叔葬礼上挤出几滴鳄鱼的眼泪。

1162.e: By hook or by crook, I'll get those tickets before the concert sells out.  不管用什么办法，我一定在售罄前弄到票。

1163.e: He came a cropper on the icy steps and broke his wrist.  他在结冰的台阶上摔了一跤，手腕都断了。

1164.e: We talked for ten minutes at cross purposes before realizing we meant different people.  我们各说各话聊了十分钟，才发现说的不是同一个人。

1165.cn: 谈话时误会对方的意思；说岔了
1165.e: We were talking at cross purposes: I meant Anne Smith, she meant Anne Harris.  我们说岔了，我指的是安妮·史密斯，她说的是安妮·哈里斯。

1166.i: cross a ˈbridge when you ˈcome to it
1166.cn: 问题出现时再解决；船到桥头自然直
1166.e: Let's cross that bridge when we come to it instead of worrying about it now.  等真出了问题再说吧，现在别瞎操心。

1167.i: cross your ˈbridges when you ˈcome to them
1167.cn: 待问题出现时再设法解决；到时再说
1167.e: She always crosses her bridges when she comes to them and never plans ahead.  她总是遇到问题再解决，从不提前打算。

1168.cn: 掠过某人心头；某人想到
1168.e: It suddenly crossed my mind that I hadn't seen her for months.  我突然想起，好几个月没见到她了。

1169.cn: 我从未想到；压根没想过
1169.e: It never crossed my mind that she would turn down such a generous offer.  我从没想过她会拒绝这么优厚的条件。

1170.i: cross my ˈheart (and hope to ˈdie) (spoken)
1170.e: I didn't touch your chocolate, cross my heart and hope to die.  我真没动你的巧克力，我发誓。

1171.i: cross sb's ˈpath • our/their paths ˈcross
1171.cn: 与某人不期而遇；偶然相遇
1171.e: Our paths crossed again at a conference ten years after university.  毕业十年后我们在一次会议上又碰上了。

1172.cn: 破釜沉舟；作出不可逆的重大决定
1172.e: By handing in her resignation she crossed the Rubicon and never looked back.  递上辞呈那一刻她已破釜沉舟，再没回头。

1173.cn: 背负沉重的负担；有难言的苦衷
1173.e: Caring for both parents alone, she has a heavy cross to bear.  独自照顾双亲，她的担子实在太重。

1174.cn: 背负自己的十字架；默默承受苦难
1174.e: Everyone has to bear their own cross, and complaining rarely makes it lighter.  人人都有自己的苦要吃，抱怨也轻不了多少。

1175.e: We got our wires crossed and both showed up at the wrong café.  我们沟通串了线，两个人都跑错了咖啡馆。

1176.e: Somewhere along the way we had crossed wires about who was booking the hotel.  中间不知哪里说岔了，谁订酒店都没弄清。

1177.cn: 处于十字路口；面临重大抉择
1177.e: After losing the job he was at a crossroads in his career.  丢了工作后，他的事业正处在十字路口。

1178.e: The village is only five miles away as the crow flies, but twelve by road.  那村子直线距离才五英里，走公路却要十二英里。

1179.cn: 忠言逆耳；为对方好而狠心
1179.e: Sometimes you have to be cruel to be kind and tell them the truth.  有时候必须狠下心说实话，才是真为他好。

1180.i: if/when it comes to the ˈcrunch (informal)
1180.cn: 到了紧要关头；关键时刻
1180.e: When it comes to the crunch, she always backs her team without hesitation.  到了关键时刻，她总会毫不犹豫地力挺自己的团队。

1181.cn: 关键时刻到了；到了紧要关头
1181.e: With two days until the deadline, it's crunch time for the whole department.  离截止只剩两天，整个部门都到了拼命的时候。

1182.e: She cried her eyes out when the puppy had to be put down.  小狗不得不安乐死时，她哭得眼睛都肿了。

1183.e: The losing team cried foul over the referee's decision in the final minute.  输球的一方对最后一分钟的判罚大喊不公。

1184.e: He's cried wolf so often that nobody believes he's really ill now.  他谎报了太多次，现在真病了也没人信。

1185.e: It's a crying shame that such a beautiful old theatre is being demolished.  这么漂亮的老剧院要拆掉，真是太可惜了。

1186.e: There's a crying need for affordable housing in this part of the city.  这一带迫切需要能负担得起的住房。

1187.cn: 我的天哪；真是岂有此理
1187.e: For crying out loud, will somebody please answer that phone?  我的天，谁去接一下电话行不行？

1188.i: it's no good/use crying over spilt ˈmilk
1188.e: The money's gone, and it's no use crying over spilt milk now.  钱已经没了，现在后悔也没用。

1189.e: Let me make one thing crystal clear: nobody leaves until the job's finished.  我把话说明白：活儿干完之前谁也不许走。

1190.i: take up the ˈcudgels for sb/sth
1190.cn: 挺身而出支持；毅然力挺
1190.e: She took up the cudgels for the students whose grants had been cut.  她挺身而出，为被削减助学金的学生说话。

1191.e: I mentioned his name and, right on cue, he walked through the door.  我刚提到他，他就正好推门进来了。

1192.cn: 效仿某人；照某人的样子做
1192.e: Just take your cue from Lisa; she knows how these meetings work.  照着丽莎做就行，她熟悉这种会怎么开。

1193.cn: 从某事物中得到启示；仿照某做法
1193.e: We took our cue from designers who combined low cost with low fuel use.  我们借鉴了那些兼顾低成本与低油耗的设计者的思路。

1194.i: not be sb's cup of ˈtea (informal, spoken)
1194.cn: 非某人所好；不合某人心意
1194.e: Opera really isn't my cup of tea, but I'll come along anyway.  歌剧真不合我胃口，不过我还是陪你去。

1195.cn: 有所图的假亲热；为好处装亲昵
1195.e: The cat only rubs against my legs at dinner time — pure cupboard love.  猫只在开饭时蹭我的腿，纯粹是有所图。

1196.e: Stop trying to play Cupid; I can find my own girlfriend, thanks.  别老想着给我做媒，我自己会找女朋友。

1197.e: My aunt loves to play Cupid at every family wedding she attends.  我姑妈每次参加家族婚礼都爱给人牵红线。

1198.e: The new album is a bit of a curate's egg, brilliant in places.  这张新专辑好坏参半，有几首确实精彩。

1199.e: His performance was good in parts, though the ending fell completely flat.  他的表演有些段落不错，可结尾彻底垮了。

1200.cn: 好奇害死猫；过于好奇会惹祸
1200.e: Don't open that box — curiosity killed the cat, you know.  别开那个盒子，好奇害死猫，你懂的。

1201.i: curry ˈfavour (with sb) (BrE) (AmE curry ˈfavor (with sb)) (disapproving)
1201.e: He's always bringing the boss coffee to curry favour with management.  他老给老板端咖啡，就为了讨好上头。

1202.e: That defeat brought down the curtain on his long international career.  那场失利为他漫长的国家队生涯画上了句号。

1203.e: The company rang the curtain down on the project after three costly years.  烧了三年钱之后，公司叫停了这个项目。

1204.i: the curtain comes down on sth
1204.e: The curtain came down on the festival with a huge fireworks display.  音乐节在一场盛大的烟花中落下帷幕。

1205.e: If the bank refuses the loan, it's curtains for the little bookshop.  银行要是不批贷款，这家小书店就完了。

1206.i: ahead of/behind the ˈcurve (especially AmE, business)
1206.e: Their design team stayed ahead of the curve for almost a decade.  他们的设计团队领先行业将近十年。

1207.cn: 出其不意地为难某人；抛出难题
1207.e: The interviewer threw me a curveball with that question about my worst failure.  面试官问我最惨的失败，一下把我问懵了。

1208.e: Watching the car park all night sounds like a cushy number to me.  整晚看着停车场，在我看来算是美差。

1209.i: be cut ˈout for sb/sth • be cut ˈout to be sth
1209.e: I'm just not cut out for office work; I need to be outdoors.  我天生不是坐办公室的料，我得在户外干活。

1210.e: Her cooking is a cut above anything else you'll find in this town.  她做的菜比这镇上任何一家都强。

1211.e: When the police arrived, his partners decided to cut and run.  警察一到，他的同伙就撒腿开溜了。

1212.cn: 小巧可爱（多指婴儿或小物件）
1212.e: Their new baby is as cute as a button in that little hat.  他们的宝宝戴着小帽子，可爱得不得了。

1213.e: This lab is at the cutting edge of cancer research in Europe.  这家实验室处在欧洲癌症研究的最前沿。

1214.e: With everyone back from holiday, the office is firing on all cylinders again.  大家休假回来后，办公室又开足了马力。

1215.i: be a dab ˈhand at sth/at doing sth (BrE, informal)
1215.e: My dad's a dab hand at fixing bikes, so bring yours over.  我爸修自行车是把好手，把你的推过来吧。

1216.e: He's as daft as a brush, but everyone in the office loves him.  他傻里傻气的，可办公室里人人都喜欢他。

1217.e: The two brothers have been at daggers drawn since their father's will was read.  自从宣读父亲遗嘱，兄弟俩就势不两立。

1218.e: She looked daggers at me when I mentioned her ex-husband.  我一提她前夫，她就狠狠瞪了我一眼。

1219.e: Driving a taxi at night is how he earns his daily bread.  他靠晚上开出租车养家糊口。

1220.e: By the time they finish arguing about it, we'll all be pushing up daisies.  等他们吵完，我们早就入土了。

1221.e: That was a great meal — so what's the damage?  这顿吃得真好，一共多少钱？

1222.cn: 管它什么后果（或花多少钱）
1222.e: He booked the flight anyway, damn the expense, because his sister was ill.  他还是订了机票，管它多贵，妹妹病了。

1223.e: Damn it, I've left my keys locked inside the car again.  见鬼，我又把钥匙锁车里了。

1224.cn: 寓贬于褒；用淡淡的赞扬贬低
1224.e: The review damned her novel with faint praise, calling it competent but forgettable.  那篇书评寓贬于褒，说她的小说尚可却难留印象。

1225.cn: 毫不在乎；根本不放在心上
1225.e: He doesn't give a damn about what the neighbours think of him.  邻居怎么看他，他根本不在乎。

1226.e: Well, I'll be damned — you actually finished the whole thing yourself!  哎哟，真没想到，你居然自己全做完了！

1227.i: I'm/I'll be ˈdamned if… (BrE also I'm/I'll be ˈblowed if…) (spoken)
1227.e: I'll be damned if I apologize to him after what he said.  他说了那种话，我才不会向他道歉。

1228.e: We did our damnedest to finish before the deadline, but the server crashed.  我们拼了命想赶在截止前完成，结果服务器崩了。

1229.e: He tried his damnedest to make me uncomfortable so that I would leave.  他想尽办法让我难受，好把我逼走。

1230.cn: 虎头蛇尾的事；令人扫兴之事
1230.e: The much-hyped launch party turned out to be a complete damp squib.  炒得沸沸扬扬的发布会最后完全没掀起水花。

1231.i: put a ˈdamper on sth (also put a ˈdampener on sth) (informal)
1231.e: The bad weather put a damper on our first day at the beach.  坏天气让我们海边第一天玩得很扫兴。

1232.cn: 落难少女；等人搭救的女子
1232.e: She hates being treated like a damsel in distress just because she's small.  就因为个子小，她讨厌被当成待人搭救的弱女子。

1233.e: The junior staff were expected to dance attendance on him all afternoon.  下属们整个下午都得在他跟前殷勤伺候。

1234.e: I'm tired of dancing to his tune every time he changes the schedule.  他一改日程我就得跟着转，我受够了。

1235.cn: 处于病危状态；脱离危险
1235.e: Her father came off the danger list two days after the operation.  手术两天后，她父亲脱离了危险期。

1236.e: Asking about his divorce is dangerous ground, so let's talk about football.  问他离婚的事很犯忌，还是聊球吧。

1237.e: Don't you dare tell my mother about the parking ticket!  你敢跟我妈说罚单的事试试！

1238.cn: 你（他等）怎么敢；岂有此理
1238.e: How dare you go through my bag without even asking me first!  你怎么敢不打招呼就翻我的包！

1239.e: I dare say she's forgotten all about it by now, honestly.  说真的，我想她这会儿早忘干净了。

1240.e: You're a dark horse — you never told us you could sing!  你可真深藏不露，从没说过你会唱歌！

1241.e: They kept the staff in the dark about the merger until the last minute.  直到最后一刻，公司才把合并的事告诉员工。

1242.e: It was a shot in the dark, but my guess turned out right.  纯属瞎猜，可我居然蒙对了。

1243.e: Darn it, the store closed five minutes before I got there.  真见鬼，我到之前五分钟店就关门了。

1244.e: Well, I'll be darned, they actually let him back on the team.  嘿，真没想到，他们居然让他回队里了。

1245.e: He cut quite a dash in his white suit at the wedding.  他穿一身白西装出席婚礼，格外惹眼。

1246.e: Half the information on that website is completely out of date.  那个网站上一半的信息都过时了。

1247.e: To date we've had over three hundred applications for the single post.  到目前为止，这一个职位已收到三百多份申请。

1248.cn: 最新的；包含最新信息的
1248.e: Please keep the sales figures up to date so I can check them.  请把销售数据随时更新，方便我核对。

1249.e: Nothing daunted, she climbed back on the horse and rode off.  她毫不气馁，重新翻身上马跑了。

1250.e: He plays that same song all day and every day.  他天天从早到晚都放那首歌。

1251.e: Dealing with angry passengers is all in a day's work for her.  应付发火的乘客对她来说是家常便饭。

1252.e: The baby could arrive any day now, so keep your phone on.  孩子这一两天就可能出生，手机别关。

1253.cn: 无论何时都；怎么都（表示更喜欢）
1253.e: I'd take a quiet beach over a crowded city any day.  安静的海滩和拥挤的城市，我怎么都选前者。

1254.e: Her calm argument finally carried the day at the committee meeting.  她冷静的论述最终在委员会上占了上风。

1255.e: Day after day he waited by the phone for news from the hospital.  他一天又一天守在电话旁等医院的消息。

1256.e: Day by day her Chinese improved until she could argue with taxi drivers.  她的中文一天天进步，后来都能跟出租车司机吵架了。

1257.cn: 天天如此；日复一日不间断
1257.e: He eats the same sandwich day in, day out, and never complains.  他天天吃同一种三明治，从来不抱怨。

1258.cn: 算账的日子；遭报应之时
1258.e: The accounts were a mess, and the day of reckoning came in April.  账目一团糟，四月份终于到了算账的时候。

1259.i: don't give up the ˈday job (informal, humorous)
1259.cn: 别丢了老本行（讽刺水平不行）
1259.e: That was an interesting song, Dave, but don't give up the day job.  戴夫，这歌挺有意思，不过老本行还是别丢。

1260.e: From day one she knew the job wasn't going to work out.  从第一天起她就知道这份工作干不长。

1261.cn: 过一天算一天；日复一日地
1261.e: They live from day to day, never knowing where the rent will come from.  他们过一天算一天，房租都不知道从哪来。

1262.i: from ˌone day to the ˈnext
1262.e: His moods change from one day to the next, so nobody knows what to expect.  他的情绪一天一个样，谁也摸不准。

1263.e: Fax machines have definitely had their day in most modern offices.  在多数现代办公室里，传真机早就风光不再了。

1264.i: ˌif he's, she's, etc. a ˈday (informal)
1264.e: She's seventy if she's a day, though she still runs marathons.  她少说也有七十了，可还在跑马拉松。

1265.cn: 在某人的年代；在某人的鼎盛时期
1265.e: In my grandfather's day you could buy a house for a few thousand pounds.  在我爷爷那年头，几千英镑就能买套房。

1266.e: In this day and age nobody should have to work without a contract.  在当今这个年代，谁都不该没有合同就上班。

1267.e: Your postcard from Lisbon absolutely made my day.  你从里斯本寄来的明信片让我高兴了一整天。

1268.e: Since we're driving all that way, let's make a day of it.  既然要开那么远，就干脆玩上一整天。

1269.e: First I missed the bus, then I lost my wallet — not my day.  先是错过公交，又丢了钱包，今天真不是我的日子。

1270.cn: 有朝一日；（过去的）某一天
1270.e: One day I'll save enough money to travel across South America.  总有一天我会攒够钱去南美旅行。

1271.e: Some day you'll look back on all this and laugh about it.  将来某一天你回头看这些，会笑出来的。

1272.i: take it/things one ˌday at a ˈtime (spoken)
1272.cn: 一天天慢慢来；不去多想以后
1272.e: Since the diagnosis he's just taking things one day at a time.  确诊之后，他只能一天一天地过。

1273.e: Him cooking dinner for everyone? That'll be the day.  他给大家做饭？那才怪呢。

1274.e: We met exactly ten years ago today, to the day.  我们相识到今天正好十年，一天不差。

1275.e: To this day nobody knows who left the flowers on her doorstep.  直到今天也没人知道是谁在她门口放的花。

1276.e: Five pounds for a small coffee is absolute daylight robbery.  一小杯咖啡卖五镑，简直是明抢。

1277.e: After weeks of confusing accounts, I'm finally beginning to see daylight.  对着乱账折腾几周后，我总算看出点门道了。

1278.i: beat/scare the (living) ˈdaylights out of sb
1278.cn: 把某人痛打一顿；把某人吓个半死
1278.e: That horror film scared the living daylights out of my little brother.  那部恐怖片把我弟弟吓得魂都没了。

1279.i: your, its, etc. days are ˈnumbered
1279.cn: 时日无多；撑不了多久了
1279.e: With sales falling like this, the shop's days are numbered.  销量这么跌下去，这家店撑不了多久了。

1280.e: One of these days I'm going to tell him exactly what I think.  总有一天我要把心里话全告诉他。

1281.e: The printer jammed, then the coffee spilled — it's just one of those days.  打印机卡纸，咖啡又洒了，今天真是诸事不顺。

1282.e: These days hardly anyone writes letters by hand any more.  如今几乎没人再手写信了。

1283.cn: 那才是好时光；那才叫好年头
1283.e: We played football until dark every evening — those were the days!  我们每天踢球踢到天黑，那才叫好日子！

1284.e: This old jacket has seen better days, but I can't throw it out.  这件旧外套早不行了，可我舍不得扔。

1285.cn: 故意不理睬某人；装作没看见
1285.e: She cut me dead in the corridor as if we'd never met.  她在走廊里当没看见我，好像从不认识。

1286.e: That argument is dead and buried, so let's not bring it up.  那场争执早就翻篇了，别再提。

1287.e: Cassette tapes are as dead as a dodo in most people's homes.  磁带在多数人家里早就绝迹了。

1288.e: I tried the engine again, but the battery was as dead as a doornail.  我又试了一次，可电瓶彻底没电了。

1289.e: With that lineup, they're a dead cert for the semi-finals.  凭这个阵容，他们进半决赛十拿九稳。

1290.cn: 注定失败的计划；没戏的想法
1290.e: Without funding, the whole recycling scheme is a dead duck.  没有资金，整个回收计划就是没戏。

1291.e: The investigation reached a dead end when the only witness disappeared.  唯一的证人一消失，调查就走进了死胡同。

1292.e: The merger talks have been dead in the water since last month.  合并谈判从上个月起就彻底停摆了。

1293.cn: 形同虚设的规定；无人理会的建议
1293.e: That old parking rule is a dead letter now; nobody enforces it.  那条老停车规定形同虚设，没人执行。

1294.e: As a plumber he's a dead loss; the leak is worse now.  他当水管工一无是处，现在漏得更厉害了。

1295.e: If Mum finds out we broke the vase, we're dead meat.  要是妈发现花瓶是我们打碎的，我们就死定了。

1296.e: They loaded the van in the dead of night so nobody would notice.  他们趁夜深人静装车，免得被人看见。

1297.e: The phone rang at dead of night and everyone jumped out of bed.  半夜电话响起，所有人都从床上蹦起来。

1298.e: Your cousin is a dead ringer for that actor in the crime series.  你表哥跟那部罪案剧里的演员长得一模一样。

1299.e: After the long flight he was dead to the world by nine.  长途飞行之后，他九点就睡得不省人事。

1300.e: The new manager wants to cut out the dead wood in our department.  新经理想清掉我们部门的冗员。

1301.e: She wouldn't be seen dead in a pink dress at a wedding.  她打死也不会穿粉裙子去参加婚礼。

1302.e: Speak up, Grandad's as deaf as a post without his hearing aid.  说大声点，爷爷不戴助听器什么都听不见。

1303.e: Her warnings about the budget fell on deaf ears at the board meeting.  她对预算的警告在董事会上没人听进去。

1304.e: The landlord turned a deaf ear to our complaints about the heating.  房东对我们关于暖气的投诉充耳不闻。

1305.i: cut a ˈdeal (with sb) • cut (sb) a ˈdeal (business)
1305.e: They cut a deal with the supplier to keep prices fixed for two years.  他们和供应商谈成协议，两年内价格不变。

1306.i: deal sb/sth a ˈblow • deal a blow to sb/sth
1306.e: The factory closure dealt a blow to the whole town's economy.  工厂关闭给全镇经济带来沉重打击。

1307.e: Part-time staff got a raw deal when the bonuses were handed out.  发奖金时，兼职员工受到了不公平的对待。

1308.cn: 哎呀；天哪（表示担忧或同情）
1308.e: Dear me, you've spilt tea all over the new carpet.  哎呀，你把茶全洒在新地毯上了。

1309.e: Oh dear, it's started to rain and I've just hung out the washing.  哎呀，下雨了，我刚把洗好的衣服晾出去。

1310.i: for dear ˈlife • for your ˈlife
1310.e: The rope snapped and she hung on to the branch for dear life.  绳子断了，她死命抓住树枝不放。

1311.e: He holds his grandmother's letters dear and keeps them in a tin.  他很珍视祖母的信，放在一个铁盒里。

1312.cn: 生命垂危；病得快不行了
1312.e: He's got a slight cold but acts as if he's at death's door.  他就是有点感冒，却装得像快不行了。

1313.i: be the ˈdeath of sb (often humorous)
1313.cn: 让某人操碎心；要了某人的命
1313.e: These kids and their late-night parties will be the death of me.  这帮孩子天天开夜场派对，非把我折腾死不可。

1314.e: She stayed up all night to be in at the death of the election.  她熬了一整夜，就为亲眼看到选举尘埃落定。

1315.e: That joke has been done to death; try something new tonight.  那个段子早被讲烂了，今晚换点新的。

1316.i: like death warmed ˈup (BrE) (AmE like death warmed ˈover) (informal)
1316.cn: 面色极差；累（或病）得要命
1316.e: You look like death warmed up — go home and get some sleep.  你脸色难看得要命，回家睡一觉吧。

1317.e: Hundreds of prisoners were put to death during those two brutal years.  在那残酷的两年里，数百名囚犯被处死。

1318.e: I was bored to death during that three-hour lecture on tax law.  那场三小时的税法讲座把我闷死了。

1319.e: They swore to defend their village to the death.  他们发誓要誓死保卫自己的村子。

1925.cn: 转弯抹角地讨人恭维；沽名钓誉
1925.e: She kept saying her cake was awful, obviously fishing for compliments from her guests.  她一个劲儿说自己的蛋糕难吃，明摆着是想让客人夸她。

1926.cn: 要么动手要么拉倒；快作抉择
1926.e: You've thought about this job offer for a month—time to fish or cut bait.  这份工作你考虑一个月了，是接是推，该拿主意了。

1927.cn: 不适应环境的人；不得其所的人
1927.e: At the fancy dinner party, wearing jeans, I felt like a fish out of water.  在那种高级晚宴上我穿着牛仔裤，浑身别扭得像条离水的鱼。

1928.e: He skipped the meeting because he had bigger fish to fry that afternoon.  他没去开会，那天下午他有更要紧的事得办。

1929.e: The new building is neither fish nor fowl—half office, half shopping mall.  这栋新楼不伦不类，一半是写字楼，一半是商场。

1930.e: Our neighbour is an odd fish who only goes out after midnight.  我们邻居是个怪人，只在半夜之后才出门。

1931.i: there are plenty/lots more fish in the ˈsea
1931.cn: 天涯何处无芳草；好对象多的是
1931.e: Stop crying over him—there are plenty more fish in the sea, believe me.  别为他哭了，天涯何处无芳草，信我的。

1932.i: there are (plenty of) other fish in the ˈsea
1932.cn: 还有很多同样好的人或物；天涯何处无芳草
1932.e: She lost that contract, but there are plenty of other fish in the sea.  那份合同她丢了，不过好机会多的是。

1933.i: make a better/ˌgood, poor, etc. ˈfist of sth
1933.cn: 某事做得较好；做得不错；做得糟糕
1933.e: For a beginner, he made a pretty good fist of repairing the old bicycle.  作为新手，他把那辆旧自行车修得相当不错。

1934.i: an iron fist/hand (in a velvet glove)
1934.cn: 外柔内刚的强硬手腕；笑里藏刀
1934.e: She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.  她管理这个部门是绵里藏针，看着温和其实极强硬。

1935.i: (as) ˌfit as a ˈfiddle (also ˌfighting ˈfit)
1935.e: At eighty, my grandfather still swims daily and is as fit as a fiddle.  我爷爷八十岁了还天天游泳，身体棒得很。

1936.e: We need someone patient and bilingual, and this candidate fits the bill perfectly.  我们要找有耐心又懂两门语言的人，这位应聘者正合适。

1937.e: The suit he borrowed from his brother fitted him like a glove.  他从哥哥那儿借的西装穿上正合身。

1938.e: My mum will have a fit when she sees the mess in the kitchen.  我妈看到厨房这么乱肯定要发飙。

1939.e: Dad had a blue fit when he found out I'd scratched his new car.  我把爸的新车刮花了，他知道后大发雷霆。

1940.i: see/think ˈfit (to do sth) (formal, often disapproving)
1940.cn: 认为做某事恰当（或合适）
1940.e: The manager saw fit to cancel the trip without telling any of us.  经理自认为有理，取消了行程却谁也没通知。

1941.cn: 断断续续地；时停时续地
1941.e: The old engine started in fits and starts before it finally settled down.  那台旧发动机断断续续地响了半天才终于平稳下来。

1942.cn: 断断续续地；忽快忽慢地
1942.e: He made progress in fits and starts at first, but now he's improving fast.  他起初进步时断时续，现在提高得很快。

1943.cn: 与某人击掌（问候或庆祝）
1943.e: After scoring the winning goal, he ran over and gave his coach five.  他攻入制胜一球后跑过去和教练击了个掌。

1944.e: I'm in a bit of a fix—I've locked my keys inside the flat again.  我有点麻烦，又把钥匙锁在屋里了。

1945.i: how are you, etc. ˈfixed (for sth)? (spoken)
1945.cn: 你有多少；你有什么安排
1945.e: How are you fixed for cash this weekend? I might need to borrow some.  这周末你手头钱宽裕吗？我可能得借点。

1946.cn: 表示支持自己的国家（或组织、思想）
1946.e: Someone from our office should go to the conference and fly the flag.  我们办公室得派个人去那个会议撑撑场面。

1947.cn: 为自己一方助威；公开表示支持
1947.e: Even in the rain, the fans stayed to wave the flag for their team.  就算下着雨，球迷们还是留下来为球队呐喊助威。

1948.cn: 强烈民族情绪的表现；沙文主义作派
1948.e: The speech was pure flag-waving, with almost no real policy in it.  那篇演讲全是煽情的爱国口号，几乎没有实质政策。

1949.cn: 继续支持濒临消亡的思想或活动
1949.e: Only three members are left, but they're keeping the flag flying for folk music.  只剩三个成员了，可他们还在为民谣音乐撑着这面旗。

1950.i: in flaˈgrante (delicto) (from Latin, literary or humorous)
1950.e: The two thieves were caught in flagrante, stuffing watches into their pockets.  两个小偷正把手表往兜里塞时被当场抓获。

1951.e: Don't get into a flap—the guests aren't arriving for another two hours.  别慌，客人还要两个小时才到呢。

1952.i: his, her, etc. ˈears are flapping (BrE, informal)
1952.cn: 竖着耳朵偷听别人说话
1952.e: Lower your voice—her ears are flapping and she'll tell everyone tomorrow.  小点声，她正竖着耳朵听呢，明天准传遍。

1953.e: Their first album sold well, but the band turned out to be a flash in the pan.  他们首张专辑卖得不错，可这乐队终究只是昙花一现。

1954.i: flash sb a ˈsmile, ˈlook, etc.
1954.cn: 向某人投以一笑（或一瞥等）
1954.e: She flashed me a smile across the room and then went back to her book.  她隔着房间冲我一笑，又低头看书去了。

1955.e: I asked him to fetch the ladder and he was back in a flash.  我让他去搬梯子，他一转眼就回来了。

1956.cn: 就这么定了；这是最后决定
1956.e: You're not going to that party on a school night, and that's flat!  明天要上学，今晚你不许去那个派对，就这么定了！

1957.cn: （笑话等）没能逗乐；未收到预期效果
1957.e: His opening joke fell flat and the whole room went awkwardly silent.  他开场那个笑话没人笑，全场尴尬地安静下来。

1958.e: He bragged for weeks about his business plan, then fell flat on his face.  他吹嘘自己的创业计划好几周，结果摔了个大跟头。

1959.i: be flat ˈbroke (BrE also be stony ˈbroke)
1959.e: I can't join you for dinner tonight—I'm flat broke until payday.  今晚饭我不去了，发薪水前我身上一分钱没有。

1960.e: The countryside here is as flat as a pancake for miles in every direction.  这一带的乡野方圆几英里平得像张饼。

1961.cn: 全力以赴地；开足马力地
1961.e: We worked flat out all weekend to get the report finished on time.  我们整个周末拼命赶工，才按时把报告做完。

1962.i: in two minutes, ten seconds, etc. ˈflat
1962.cn: 仅用两分钟（或十秒等）；极快
1962.e: He changed the flat tyre in five minutes flat and we drove on.  他五分钟就换好了瘪胎，我们接着上路。

1963.cn: 阿谀奉承会（不会）让你如愿
1963.e: Flattery will get you nowhere—you still have to finish the dishes tonight.  拍马屁没用，今晚碗还是得你洗。

1964.i: if you've ˌgot it, ˈflaunt it (humorous, saying)
1964.cn: 有本事就亮出来；有能耐别藏着
1964.e: She wore the diamond earrings to the office—if you've got it, flaunt it.  她戴着钻石耳环上班，有就得显摆嘛。

1965.cn: 时下走红的人物；一时的宠儿
1965.e: That young director is flavour of the month with every studio in town.  那个年轻导演眼下是各家制片厂争抢的红人。

1966.i: with a ˈflea in your ear
1966.e: He asked for a raise and was sent away with a flea in his ear.  他去要求加薪，结果被训了一顿轰了出来。

1967.e: I'm only flesh and blood—I can't work eighteen hours a day forever.  我也是血肉之躯，不可能天天干十八个小时。

1968.e: How could you turn away your own flesh and blood on a night like this?  这样的夜里，你怎么忍心把自家亲人拒之门外？

1969.e: I'd only seen her on television, so meeting her in the flesh was strange.  我只在电视上见过她，真人站在面前感觉挺奇妙。

1970.cn: 使人毛骨悚然；令人起鸡皮疙瘩
1970.e: The way that man stared at us made my flesh creep.  那男人盯着我们看的样子让我起了一身鸡皮疙瘩。

1971.i: more than ˈflesh and blood can enˈdure, etc.
1971.e: Three night shifts in a row is more than flesh and blood can endure.  连上三个夜班，血肉之躯实在扛不住。

1972.i: put flesh on (the bones of) sth
1972.e: The idea sounds promising, but you need to put flesh on the bones of it.  这个想法听着不错，但你得把细节填充起来。

1973.cn: 跃跃欲试；摩拳擦掌显示实力
1973.e: The new manager is flexing his muscles by rewriting all our procedures.  新经理正在大显身手，把我们的流程全改了一遍。

1974.e: With the flu going round the office, people are dropping like flies.  办公室流感一传开，人一个接一个地倒下。

1975.cn: 某人很精明；不容易上当
1975.e: Don't try to overcharge her—there are no flies on that woman.  别想多收她钱，那女人精着呢。

1976.cn: 异想天开；不切实际的想象
1976.e: His plan to buy an island was just another flight of fancy.  他要买座岛的计划不过是又一次异想天开。

1977.e: She is now in the top flight of British tennis after that win.  赢下那场比赛后，她跻身英国网球一流选手之列。

1978.e: The burglars took flight the moment the alarm started screaming.  警报一响，窃贼们立刻逃之夭夭。

1979.cn: 尽情玩乐；短暂的风流韵事
1979.e: Before settling down, he had one last fling travelling around Asia.  安定下来之前，他最后放纵了一回，跑遍了亚洲。

2310.e: The strike brought the whole factory to a grinding halt within a few hours.  罢工几小时内就让整个工厂彻底停了下来。

2311.i: keep your ˈnose to the ˈgrindstone
2311.e: She kept her nose to the grindstone all summer and finally passed the exam.  她整个夏天埋头苦读，最后终于通过了考试。

2312.cn: 控制情绪；使自己镇定下来
2312.e: Get a grip on yourself — crying won't help us find the missing keys.  振作点，哭也帮不了我们找到丢的钥匙。

2313.e: The whole town was in the grip of panic after the second robbery.  第二起抢劫案之后，整座小镇陷入了恐慌。

2314.e: He's losing his grip on the business, and everyone in the office knows it.  他对生意的掌控力在下降，办公室里人人都看得出来。

2315.e: It took me a month to come to grips with the new accounting software.  我花了一个月才摸清这套新会计软件。

2316.cn: 对某人有用的东西；有利可图的素材
2316.e: Every celebrity divorce is grist to the mill for those cheap gossip magazines.  每一桩明星离婚案都是那些八卦杂志的好材料。

2317.cn: 咬紧牙关；下定决心忍耐
2317.e: I gritted my teeth and finished the last three miles of the race.  我咬紧牙关跑完了比赛最后三英里。

2318.i: groan under the weight of sth (written)
2318.cn: 在重压下发出嘎吱声；不堪重负
2318.e: The table groaned under the weight of roast turkey, pies and three enormous cakes.  烤火鸡、派和三个大蛋糕压得桌子直响。

2319.e: After twenty years here he's stuck in a groove and refuses to try anything new.  在这儿干了二十年，他早已墨守成规，不肯尝试新东西。

2320.i: be, come, get, etc. in on the ground ˈfloor
2320.cn: 一开始就参与（日后可能获利）
2320.e: I got in on the ground floor of that startup and made a small fortune.  我在那家初创公司刚起步时就加入了，赚了一小笔。

2321.e: Her research on sleep and memory really broke new ground in the field.  她关于睡眠与记忆的研究在这个领域真正开创了新局面。

2322.i: cut the ground from under sb/sb's ˈfeet
2322.cn: 破坏某人的计划；拆某人的台
2322.e: By cutting prices first, they cut the ground from under our feet completely.  他们抢先降价，把我们的路彻底堵死了。

2323.e: You'll work yourself into the ground if you keep taking on extra shifts.  你要是老加班，非把自己累垮不可。

2324.cn: 使（计划等）开始；顺利启动
2324.e: We need more funding to get this project off the ground by the spring.  我们需要更多资金，才能在春天前把这个项目启动起来。

2325.e: The party lost ground to its rivals in almost every northern city.  该党在北方几乎每座城市都被对手抢去了地盘。

2326.e: She stood her ground and refused to lower the price by a single cent.  她寸步不让，一分钱也不肯降。

2327.e: Aid workers on the ground say the situation is far worse than reported.  身处一线的救援人员说，情况比报道的糟得多。

2328.e: The suspect went to ground for six months before the police finally traced him.  嫌疑人躲藏了六个月，警方才最终找到他。

2329.e: He ran that poor van into the ground driving it across the country twice.  他开着那辆破面包车横穿全国两趟，彻底把它开报废了。

2330.e: Good plumbers are pretty thin on the ground in this part of town.  这一带的好水管工少得可怜。

2331.e: The little book club grew like Topsy until nearly two hundred people had joined.  这个小读书会飞速壮大，最后有近两百人加入。

2332.e: The restaurant had a few growing pains, but business is steady now.  这家餐馆经历了一些初期的磕碰，现在生意稳定了。

2333.e: At best I can make an educated guess about how long the repairs will take.  我最多只能凭经验估算一下修理要多久。

2334.cn: 让某人捉摸不透；吊某人胃口
2334.e: The writer keeps you guessing right up to the very last page.  这位作家吊足了读者胃口，直到最后一页才揭晓。

2335.e: Do you mind if I borrow your bike? Sure, be my guest.  我能借下你的自行车吗？当然，请便。

2336.e: My mother laid a real guilt trip on me for missing Sunday dinner.  我没回家吃周日晚饭，我妈让我内疚得不行。

2337.e: They used first-year students as guinea pigs for the new online course.  他们拿大一学生给新的网课当试验品。

2338.cn: 把事情弄糟；使运转停滞
2338.e: One missing signature gummed up the works for the entire department.  一个签名没签，整个部门的活儿都卡住了。

2339.e: Without a car and without money, we were well and truly up a gum tree.  没车又没钱，我们真是彻底陷进去了。

2340.i: have a ˈgun to your head (informal)
2340.e: I signed the contract, but honestly I had a gun to my head.  我签了合同，但说实话我是被逼的。

2341.i: hold/put a ˈgun to sb's head
2341.e: Nobody put a gun to your head — you chose this job all by yourself.  没人拿枪逼你，这份工作是你自己选的。

2342.e: The whole team is under the gun to ship the app by Friday.  整个团队压力巨大，周五前必须把应用上线。

2343.e: Don't jump the gun and announce the deal before the contract is actually signed.  别操之过急，合同没签就别宣布这笔交易。

2344.e: Nobody had the guts to tell the boss his presentation was boring.  没人有胆量告诉老板他的演示很无聊。

2345.i: have sb's ˌguts for ˈgarters (BrE, informal)
2345.e: If you scratch my car again, I'll have your guts for garters.  你要是再刮花我的车，我饶不了你。

2346.e: She worked her guts out for that company and they let her go anyway.  她为那家公司拼死拼活，结果还是被辞退了。

2347.e: He's hated my guts ever since I got the promotion he wanted.  自从我拿到他想要的晋升，他就恨透了我。

2348.e: The gutter press hounded the actress for weeks after her sudden divorce.  她突然离婚后，八卦小报纠缠了这位女演员好几周。

2349.cn: 使某人疼痛难忍；折磨某人
2349.e: My knee's been giving me gyp ever since that long walk on Sunday.  自从周日走了那么远，我的膝盖就一直疼得厉害。

2350.i: be in the ˈhabit of doing sth
2350.e: I'm not in the habit of staying up this late on a weeknight.  我平常工作日可没有熬这么晚的习惯。

2351.e: Ignore her snapping at everyone; she's just having a bad hair day.  别理她冲人发火，她今天诸事不顺。

2352.e: Come on, let your hair down for once — it's your own birthday party!  来吧，就放纵一回，今天是你的生日派对！

2353.e: The kids have been getting in my hair all morning, so nothing got done.  孩子们缠了我一上午，什么活都没干成。

2354.cn: 使某人震惊；令人毛骨悚然
2354.e: Some of the stories he told about prison would make your hair curl.  他讲的一些监狱里的事能让你头皮发麻。

2355.i: not a ˈhair out of place
2355.e: After ten hours on a plane she stepped off with not a hair out of place.  坐了十小时飞机下来，她依然仪容整洁、纹丝不乱。

2356.i: not harm/touch a hair of sb's ˈhead
2356.e: I promise nobody will touch a hair of your head while I am here.  我保证只要我在，没人能动你一根汗毛。

2357.e: She didn't turn a hair when the waiter dropped the whole tray beside her.  服务员在她旁边摔了整盘东西，她连眉头都没皱一下。

2358.i: put ˈhairs on your chest (informal, humorous)
2358.e: Drink this whisky, lad — it'll put hairs on your chest.  小子，把这杯威士忌喝了，长长男子汉气概。

2359.i: have/get sb by the short ˈhairs (informal)
2359.cn: 抓住某人把柄；完全控制某人
2359.e: The bank has us by the short hairs until the mortgage is finally paid off.  房贷还清之前，银行牢牢捏着我们的命门。

2360.i: give sb the hairy ˈeyeball (AmE, informal)
2360.cn: 以怀疑或不以为然的眼神看人
2360.e: The librarian gave me the hairy eyeball when my phone rang twice.  我手机响了两次，图书管理员用怀疑的眼神盯着我。

2361.e: At ninety-two my grandfather is still hale and hearty and gardens every day.  我爷爷九十二了，依然精神矍铄，天天侍弄花园。

2362.cn: 非同一般的；超乎寻常的
2362.e: That was a meal and a half — I really couldn't eat another bite.  那顿饭真够丰盛的，我一口也吃不下了。

2363.e: I'd love to come, but I'll have to check with my better half first.  我很想去，不过得先问问我那口子。

2364.i: give sb half a ˈchance (to do sth) (informal)
2364.e: Give him half a chance and he'll talk about football all evening.  只要给他一点机会，他能聊一晚上足球。

2365.cn: 最困难的部分；成功的一半
2365.e: Getting the kids out of bed on time is half the battle.  按时把孩子们弄起床，事情就成功了一半。

2366.i: half the ˈfun, ˈtrouble, etc. of sth (informal)
2366.cn: 乐趣（或麻烦等）的一大部分
2366.e: Half the fun of camping is cooking badly over an open fire.  露营的乐趣有一半在于生着火胡乱做饭。

2367.i: have half a ˈmind to do sth
2367.e: I've half a mind to call the landlord and complain about all this noise.  我真想给房东打电话投诉这些噪音。

2368.i: half a ˌloaf is better than ˈnone/no ˈbread (saying)
2368.cn: 有总比没有好；聊胜于无
2368.e: They only offered part of the refund, but half a loaf is better than none.  他们只退了一部分钱，不过聊胜于无。

2369.i: half a ˈminute, ˈtick, ˈsecond, etc. (informal)
2369.e: Hang on half a minute while I find my other shoe.  等一小会儿，我找找另一只鞋。

2370.e: You've heard about the flood? Believe me, that's not the half of it.  你听说水灾了？信我，那还只是一部分呢。

2371.e: By nine o'clock he was already half cut and singing to the barman.  九点钟他就已经半醉，冲着酒保唱起歌来。

2372.e: Half the time he doesn't even bother answering his phone.  他多半时候连电话都懒得接。

2373.cn: 另一阶层的人如何生活
2373.e: Staying in that fancy hotel showed me how the other half lives.  住那家豪华酒店让我见识了另一个阶层是怎么生活的。

2374.cn: 用比预期短得多的时间
2374.e: With the new machine we finished the whole order in half the time.  用了新机器，我们用一半的时间就完成了整批订单。

2375.e: When my mother cleans the house there are no half measures at all.  我妈打扫房子从来都彻彻底底，绝不马虎。

2376.e: Did you enjoy the concert? Not half — it was the best night ever.  演唱会好玩吗？太好玩了，这是最棒的一晚。

2377.i: not ˈhalf as good, nice, etc. as sb/sth
2377.e: The sequel was not half as good as the original film.  续集远不如第一部好看。

2378.cn: 相当不错；出乎意料地好
2378.e: I tried her homemade bread and honestly it was not half bad.  我尝了她自己烤的面包，说实话相当不错。

2379.i: too clever, quick, etc. by ˈhalf (BrE, informal, disapproving)
2379.e: That young lawyer is too clever by half, and everyone finds him irritating.  那个年轻律师聪明过头了，人人都嫌他讨厌。

2380.e: The campaign went off at half-cock because nobody had printed the posters.  这次活动仓促上马，因为没人把海报印出来。

2381.e: This arrangement is a halfway house between full-time work and complete retirement.  这种安排是全职工作与彻底退休之间的折中。

2382.e: If you drop your price a little, I'll happily meet you halfway.  你稍微降点价，我很乐意跟你各让一步。

2383.i: have all the ˈhallmarks of sb/sth
2383.e: The burglary has all the hallmarks of the gang that hit the bank.  这起入室盗窃完全是抢银行那伙人的手法。

2384.i: do nothing/not do anything by ˈhalves
2384.e: She never does anything by halves — the party took three months to plan.  她做事从不半途而废，这场派对筹备了三个月。

2385.i: go ˈhalves (with sb) • go ˌhalf and ˈhalf
2385.e: Let's go halves on the taxi since we're heading the same way.  我们顺路，打车费平摊吧。

2386.cn: 表演过火；故意夸张做作
2386.e: The lead actor hammed it up so much that the audience started laughing.  男主角表演太夸张，观众都笑了起来。

2387.i: be/go at sb/sth ˌhammer and ˈtongs (informal)
2387.e: The neighbours were at it hammer and tongs again until well past midnight.  邻居们又吵得不可开交，一直闹到过了午夜。

2388.e: Her grandmother's diamond ring goes under the hammer next Thursday morning.  她祖母的钻戒下周四上午将被拍卖。

2389.e: Our team got a real hammering in the second half of the match.  我们队在下半场被打得落花流水。

2390.e: He asked for her hand at Christmas and they married the following spring.  他在圣诞节向她求婚，第二年春天他们就结婚了。

2391.e: Help was close at hand when the car broke down outside the village.  车在村外抛锚时，援手就在近旁。

2392.cn: 束缚某人；限制某人行动
2392.e: The new rules tie small shopkeepers hand and foot with endless paperwork.  新规定用没完没了的文书把小店主捆得死死的。

2393.e: The police believe all three men had a hand in planning the robbery.  警方认为这三个人都参与策划了抢劫。

2394.e: The postmen are on strike, so we'll have to deliver these invitations by hand.  邮政工人罢工，这些请帖只好我们派人送了。

2395.cn: 迫使某人摊牌；逼某人表态
2395.e: The leaked email forced the minister's hand and he resigned that same evening.  邮件外泄逼得部长摊牌，当晚就辞职了。

2396.e: The party got out of hand once the neighbours' friends all turned up.  邻居的朋友一来，派对就失控了。

2397.e: Could you give me a hand with these heavy boxes before you leave?  你走之前能帮我搬一下这些重箱子吗？

2398.e: Poverty tends to go hand in hand with poor health and shorter lives.  贫困往往与健康差、寿命短相伴而生。

2399.e: We still have twenty minutes in hand before the last train leaves.  离末班车还有二十分钟可用。

2400.cn: 与某人密切勾结；狼狈为奸
2400.e: The inspector had been working hand in glove with the smugglers for years.  这名检查员多年来一直与走私者狼狈为奸。

2401.e: The two little girls walked hand in hand all the way to school.  两个小女孩手拉着手一路走到学校。

2402.i: hand sth to sb on a ˈplate • hand sb sth on a ˈplate (informal)
2402.e: He was handed that job on a plate because his uncle owns the firm.  这份工作是白送给他的，因为公司是他叔叔的。

2403.e: I still teach one class a year just to keep my hand in.  我每年还教一门课，就是为了不生疏。

2404.e: After losing his job they lived from hand to mouth for nearly a year.  他失业后，他们勉强糊口过了将近一年。

2405.i: have to ˈhand it to sb (informal)
2405.e: You have to hand it to her — she organized the whole festival alone.  你不得不佩服她，整个音乐节都是她一个人办的。

2406.i: wait on sb hand and ˈfoot
2406.e: His mother waited on him hand and foot until he was nearly thirty.  他妈妈无微不至地伺候他到快三十岁。

2407.i: talk to/tell it to the ˈhand (because/ˈcos the face ain't ˈlistening) (AmE, informal)
2407.e: Don't bother explaining again — talk to the hand, I've heard quite enough.  别再解释了，我不想听，真够了。

2408.e: The manager rejected my proposal out of hand without even reading it.  经理看都没看就断然否决了我的提案。

2409.e: After two failed auditions he threw his hand in and went back home.  两次试镜失败后，他放弃了，回了老家。

2410.e: This winter I want to try my hand at making my own bread.  今年冬天我想试试自己做面包。

2411.e: Keep a torch ready to hand in case the power goes out again.  手边备好手电筒，以防又停电。

2412.e: Ask Dave — he's an old hand at fixing these ancient boilers.  问戴夫吧，修这种老锅炉他是行家。

2413.e: Since retiring he has turned his hand to carpentry and repairs everyone's furniture.  退休后他做起了木工，帮大家修家具。

2414.i: with your ˌhand on your ˈheart • ˌhand on ˈheart
2414.e: Hand on heart, I never told anyone what you said that night.  我发誓，那晚你说的话我从没告诉过任何人。

2415.e: The board wanted a safe pair of hands, not a risk-taking visionary.  董事会想要个办事稳妥的人，而不是敢冒险的空想家。

2416.i: with one hand tied behind your ˈback
2416.cn: 束手束脚地；不尽全力地
2416.e: I could beat him at chess with one hand tied behind my back.  我下棋赢他，不费吹灰之力。

2417.i: at the hands of sb • at sb's ˈhands (written)
2417.cn: 出自某人之手；由某人造成
2417.e: The prisoners suffered terribly at the hands of their own guards.  囚犯在自己看守手里吃尽了苦头。

2418.e: After the third warning she washed her hands of the whole project.  第三次警告之后，她就撒手不管整个项目了。

2419.e: My brother is good with his hands and built that garden shed himself.  我哥哥手很巧，花园里那个棚子是他自己搭的。

2420.i: fall into sb's ˈhands/the ˈhands of sb
2420.e: If those letters fall into the hands of a journalist, the scandal will explode.  这些信要是落到记者手里，丑闻就会爆发。

2421.cn: 亲自动手干活；插手不正当勾当
2421.e: A good manager isn't afraid to get his hands dirty on the factory floor.  好经理不怕在车间里亲自动手干活。

2422.e: With three toddlers and a new puppy, she really has her hands full.  三个学步的孩子加一只小狗，她真是忙得不可开交。

2423.e: I can't lay my hands on the receipt, so they won't refund me.  我找不到收据，所以他们不给我退款。

2424.e: Keep your hands off my sandwich — I've been saving it all morning.  别碰我的三明治，我留了一上午了。

2425.i: in the hands of sb • in sb's ˈhands
2425.cn: 由某人掌管；在某人控制下
2425.e: The future of the industry is now in the hands of the government.  这个行业的未来现在掌握在政府手中。

2426.cn: 得到妥善照顾；交托可靠
2426.e: Leave the cat with me; she'll be in safe hands for two weeks.  猫交给我吧，这两周包在我身上。

2427.cn: 人多好办事；众人拾柴火焰高
2427.e: Come and help with the dishes — many hands make light work.  过来帮忙洗碗，人多好办事。

2428.e: Once the twins start school, that's six hours a day off my hands.  双胞胎一上学，我每天就能省出六个小时。

2429.cn: 待某人处理；由某人负担
2429.e: With the wedding cancelled, we had two hundred meals on our hands.  婚礼取消了，两百份餐食砸在我们手里。

2430.e: I spent an hour on my hands and knees looking for that lost earring.  我趴在地上找了一个小时那只丢的耳环。

2431.cn: 不再由某人控制或负责
2431.e: The decision is out of my hands now; head office will decide everything.  这事我已经做不了主了，一切由总部决定。

2432.cn: 正中某人下怀；自投罗网
2432.e: By resigning angrily, you would be playing right into your rival's hands.  你要是气得辞职，正中对手下怀。

2433.cn: 某人受制于人；无能为力
2433.e: I'd love to give you a discount, but honestly my hands are tied.  我很想给你打折，可我实在做不了主。

2434.e: I'll take the children off your hands for the weekend so you can rest.  这周末孩子我来带，你们好好休息。

2435.e: The old bakery on the corner has changed hands three times this year.  街角那家老面包房今年已经三次易主了。

2436.i: throw your ˈhands up in ˈhorror, etc. (often humorous)
2436.e: My aunt threw her hands up in horror when she saw my new tattoo.  我姑妈看见我的新纹身，吓得直摆手。

2437.e: He claims he caught that huge fish with his bare hands.  他说那条大鱼是他徒手抓到的。

2438.e: Take the spare rope — it might come in handy on the boat.  把备用绳带上，在船上说不定用得着。

2439.e: It took me a week to get the hang of driving on the left.  我花了一周才掌握靠左行驶的窍门。

2440.e: Oh, hang the expense — let's order the lobster and enjoy ourselves.  管它多贵呢，点龙虾，好好享受一顿。

2441.e: After the second heart attack his life hung by a thread for days.  第二次心脏病发作后，他好几天命悬一线。

2442.e: The council decided to hang fire on the new road until after the election.  议会决定把新路的事拖到选举之后再说。

2443.e: He hung his head in shame when the teacher read out his feeble excuse.  老师念出他蹩脚的借口时，他羞愧地低下了头。

2444.e: Hang in there — only two more weeks until the exams are over.  坚持住，再有两周考试就结束了。

2445.e: Hang a left at the traffic lights and the museum is straight ahead.  在红绿灯处左转，博物馆就在正前方。

2446.cn: 聚精会神地听；一字不漏
2446.e: The children sat quietly, hanging on every word of the ghost story.  孩子们静静坐着，听鬼故事听得一字不落。

2447.cn: 挂牌开业（尤指医生、律师）
2447.e: After passing the bar exam she hung out her shingle in her home town.  通过律师考试后，她在家乡挂牌开业。

2448.e: It's Friday night — let it all hang out and forget about work.  周五晚上，放开了玩，把工作忘掉。

2449.i: hang sb out to ˈdry (AmE, informal)
2449.e: When the scandal broke, the company hung its own manager out to dry.  丑闻一曝光，公司就把自己的经理丢在一边不管了。

2450.i: hang over sb's ˈhead • hang ˈover sb
2450.e: The threat of redundancy has been hanging over my head since January.  裁员的威胁从一月起就一直压在我心头。

2451.e: The union told its members to hang tough and reject the latest offer.  工会让会员们坚持到底，拒绝最新的方案。

2452.e: After twenty seasons the old striker finally hung up his boots.  踢了二十个赛季，这位老前锋终于挂靴了。

2453.e: They're expecting the happy event some time in early October.  他们预计十月初就要添丁了。

2454.cn: 淘宝乐园；能找到所需物之地
2454.e: That flea market is a happy hunting ground for anyone who collects old records.  那个跳蚤市场是老唱片收藏者的淘宝乐园。

2455.e: We need a happy medium between strict rules and complete chaos.  我们需要在严规和彻底混乱之间找到折中。

2456.e: Many happy returns of the day, Grandma — here's your birthday cake.  祝您生日快乐，奶奶，这是您的生日蛋糕。

2457.e: The builders have been hard at it since six o'clock this morning.  建筑工人从今早六点起就一直在拼命干。

2458.cn: 受到不公平对待；感到委屈
2458.e: She felt hard done by when everyone else in the office got a bonus.  办公室里别人都拿了奖金，她觉得很委屈。

2459.e: Don't be too hard on him; it's only his second week here.  别对他太苛刻，他才来第二周。

2460.e: We were so hard up that winter that we sold the piano.  那年冬天我们太缺钱了，把钢琴都卖了。

2461.e: The team is hard up for defenders after two injuries last month.  上个月两名球员受伤，球队后卫严重不足。

2462.e: I learned the hard way that you should never lend friends money.  我吃了苦头才明白，千万别借钱给朋友。

2463.e: Hard luck about the interview — there'll be other chances very soon.  面试没成，真不走运，很快还会有机会的。

2464.e: Speak up a bit — my grandfather is rather hard of hearing.  说话大声点，我爷爷有点耳背。

2465.i: hard ˈput (to it) to do sth • hard ˈpressed/ˈpushed to do sth
2465.cn: 很难做到；勉强能做某事
2465.e: You'd be hard pushed to find a better mechanic anywhere in this town.  在这个镇上，你很难找到比他更好的技工。

2466.e: The new head teacher takes a hard line on students arriving late.  新校长对学生迟到态度强硬。

2467.e: He gave up the hard stuff and drinks nothing but beer now.  他把烈酒戒了，现在只喝啤酒。

2468.cn: 把简单的事做得很费力
2468.e: You're making hard work of that knot — let me untie it for you.  这个结你解得太费劲了，我来帮你解吧。

2469.e: You won fair and square, so no hard feelings from me.  你赢得光明正大，我不往心里去。

2470.e: Stop playing hard to get and just tell him that you'd like to go.  别再欲擒故纵了，直接告诉他你想去。

2471.e: She took her father's death very hard and barely left the house.  父亲去世让她极为伤心，几乎足不出户。

2472.e: Cycling to work in winter is too much like hard work for me.  冬天骑车上班对我来说太累了，我不干。

2473.e: Put the scissors on the top shelf, well out of harm's way.  把剪刀放到最上层，免得伤着人。

2474.i: there's no harm in (sb's) doing sth • it does no ˈharm (for sb) to do sth
2474.e: There's no harm in asking whether they still have any tickets left.  问问他们还有没有余票，也没什么损失。

2475.i: he, she, etc. wouldn't harm/hurt a ˈfly
2475.cn: 心地善良；连苍蝇都不忍伤害
2475.e: My uncle looks fierce, but honestly he wouldn't hurt a fly.  我叔叔看着凶，其实连只苍蝇都不忍心伤害。

2476.cn: 在日常工作中；重返岗位
2476.e: It felt strange being back in harness after three weeks on the beach.  在海滩待了三周后重回工作岗位，感觉怪怪的。

2477.e: The two charities have worked in harness with each other for many years.  这两家慈善机构多年来一直携手合作。

2478.e: More haste, less speed — you'll finish sooner if you stop rushing.  欲速则不达，别慌反而更快做完。

2479.e: Keep this under your hat, but I'm leaving the company in June.  这事你别声张，我六月要离职了。

2480.i: take your ˈhat off to sb • hats ˈoff to sb (especially BrE) (informal)
2480.e: I take my hat off to anyone who can run a marathon barefoot.  谁能赤脚跑完马拉松，我真是佩服。

2481.e: Those special effects looked amazing once, but they're all old hat now.  那些特效当年很惊艳，如今全是老一套了。

2482.i: throw your ˈhat into the ring
2482.e: She threw her hat into the ring just two days before nominations closed.  提名截止前两天，她才宣布参选。

2483.e: Right, everyone raise your glasses and down the hatch!  好了，大家举杯，干了！

2484.cn: 严阵以待；准备应对困难
2484.e: With budget cuts coming, we'd better batten down the hatches for a hard year.  预算要削减了，我们最好做好过苦日子的准备。

2485.e: The reviewer did a real hatchet job on her first novel.  那位评论家把她的第一部小说批得一无是处。

2486.i: haul sb over the ˈcoals (BrE) (AmE rake sb over the ˈcoals)
2486.e: The coach hauled us over the coals for turning up late to training.  我们训练迟到，教练把我们狠狠训了一顿。

2487.cn: 长期艰苦的努力；长途运输
2487.e: Rebuilding the business after the fire will be a long haul.  火灾后重建生意会是一场持久战。

2488.e: I'm going to have it out with my flatmate about the unwashed dishes.  我要跟室友把没洗碗的事说清楚。

2489.e: The drawer's full of pens, batteries, old keys and what have you.  抽屉里塞满了笔、电池、旧钥匙之类的东西。

2490.cn: 坏透了无法修复；完蛋了
2490.e: This kettle has had it — the element burned out this morning.  这水壶报废了，今早加热管烧坏了。

2491.e: The gap between the haves and the have-nots keeps getting wider every year.  富人和穷人之间的差距一年比一年大。

2492.i: he, she, etc. isn't ˈhaving any (of it)
2492.e: I offered to explain everything, but she wasn't having any of it.  我想把一切解释清楚，可她根本不听。

2493.cn: 对…造成严重破坏或混乱
2493.e: The snowstorm wreaked havoc with flights all along the east coast.  暴风雪把整个东海岸的航班搅得一团糟。

2494.i: make hay while the ˈsun shines (saying)
2494.e: Tourists are everywhere this month, so make hay while the sun shines.  这个月游客很多，趁热打铁多赚点。

2495.e: The heating went haywire and the whole flat was boiling all night.  暖气失灵了，整间公寓热了一整夜。

2496.e: Most of that lecture went completely over my head, I'm afraid.  恐怕那堂课大部分我都听不懂。

2497.i: be banging, etc. your head against a brick ˈwall (informal)
2497.e: Asking him to tidy his room is like banging your head against a brick wall.  让他收拾房间简直是白费口舌。

2498.i: off the top of your ˈhead (informal)
2498.e: Off the top of my head, I'd say about forty people came.  我随口一说，大概来了四十人吧。

2499.e: I only asked about dinner and she bit my head off.  我不过问了一句晚饭，她就冲我发火。

2500.e: The argument over money finally came to a head at Christmas.  关于钱的争执在圣诞节终于到了摊牌的地步。

2501.i: knock sth on the ˈhead (BrE, informal)
2501.e: We had to knock the whole idea on the head when the funding disappeared.  资金一断，我们只好把整个想法作罢。

2502.i: build up/work up, etc. a head of ˈsteam
2502.e: The campaign is finally building up a head of steam in the northern towns.  这场运动终于在北方各镇形成了势头。

2503.i: bury/hide your ˌhead in the ˈsand
2503.cn: 回避现实；采取鸵鸟政策
2503.e: Stop burying your head in the sand and open those bank letters.  别再逃避现实了，把银行的信拆开看看。

2504.i: can't make head or/nor ˈtail of sth (informal)
2504.e: I can't make head or tail of these assembly instructions.  这些组装说明我完全看不懂。

2505.cn: 使某人烦躁；让人受不了
2505.e: All this paperwork is really doing my head in this week.  这周这么多文书工作快把我逼疯了。

2506.e: He came in from the garden covered in mud from head to foot.  他从花园进来，从头到脚都是泥。

2507.e: I'll get my head down and finish the report before lunch.  我埋头把报告在午饭前写完。

2508.i: get your ˈhead round sth (BrE, informal)
2508.e: I still can't get my head round the fact that she's moving abroad.  她要移居国外，我到现在还想不明白。

2509.e: Get it into your thick head that the shop closes at five.  你给我记牢了，店里五点关门。

2510.i: get/take it into your ˈhead that... (informal)
2510.e: He got it into his head that everyone in the office was laughing at him.  他认定办公室里人人都在笑话他。

2511.e: Give the new designer her head and see what she comes up with.  放手让新设计师去做，看看她能拿出什么。

2512.e: That second glass of wine has gone straight to my head.  第二杯酒一下就让我上头了。

2513.i: have a good ˈhead on your shoulders
2513.e: She's only nineteen but she has a good head on her shoulders.  她才十九岁，但很有头脑。

2514.e: You need a good head for figures to survive in this job.  干这行得有很强的数字头脑才行。

2515.e: I don't have a head for heights, so you can clean the gutters.  我恐高，清理屋檐排水槽的活儿归你。

2516.i: have your head in the ˈclouds (informal)
2516.e: He has his head in the clouds and never notices what's happening around him.  他整天想入非非，从不留意周围的事。

2517.i: have your ˈhead screwed on (the right way)
2517.e: Don't worry about her — that girl has her head screwed on.  别为她操心，那姑娘明白着呢。

2518.e: Dinner worked out at about thirty pounds a head, including wine.  连酒算下来，晚饭人均三十英镑左右。

2519.e: Her design was head and shoulders above everything else we received.  她的设计比我们收到的其他作品高出一大截。

2520.e: Share prices headed south the moment the results were announced.  业绩一公布，股价立刻下跌。

2521.cn: 深深迷恋；爱得神魂颠倒
2521.e: They met in March and by June were head over heels in love.  他们三月相识，到六月就爱得死去活来。

2522.cn: 先起步的优势；领先一步
2522.e: Studying abroad gave her a head start over the other applicants.  留学经历让她比其他申请者抢先一步。

2523.e: You did nothing wrong, so hold your head up high in there.  你没做错事，进去时把头抬起来。

2524.e: I took the contract on and quickly realized I was in over my head.  我接下了这份合同，很快就发现自己力不从心。

2525.e: She kept her head when the engine caught fire and led everyone out.  发动机着火时她保持镇静，把大家带了出去。

2526.cn: 勉强维持；不致陷入困境
2526.e: Two jobs are just enough to keep our heads above water.  打两份工才勉强让我们不至于入不敷出。

2527.e: Don't put ideas into his head — he can't afford a motorbike.  别给他灌输这些念头，他买不起摩托车。

2528.cn: 低调行事；避免引人注意
2528.e: Just keep your head down for a week until the boss calms down.  低调一周，等老板消气再说。

2529.e: Everyone else lost their heads, but the pilot stayed completely calm.  其他人都慌了神，只有飞行员十分镇定。

2695.i: hit the ˈroad (also hit the ˈtrail especially AmE)
2695.e: We should hit the road early tomorrow if we want to beat the traffic.  如果想避开车流，我们明天得早点出发。

2696.e: My boss hit the roof when he saw how much the party had cost.  老板看到聚会花了多少钱，气得暴跳如雷。

2697.e: When Dad found out I'd crashed the car, he hit the ceiling.  爸爸发现我撞坏了车，顿时大发雷霆。

2698.e: I'm exhausted after that long drive, so I'm going to hit the sack.  开了这么久的车，我累坏了，这就去睡觉。

2699.e: His career hit the skids after that scandal appeared in the papers.  报上曝出那桩丑闻后，他的事业一路下滑。

2700.e: A cold beer after mowing the lawn really hits the spot.  割完草坪来杯冰啤酒，真是舒服到位。

2701.i: hit the ˈstreets ◆ hit the ˈshops/ˈstores
2701.e: The new phone hits the stores next Friday and people are already queuing.  新手机下周五上市，已经有人在排队了。

2702.e: Firing her right after the divorce was really hitting someone when they're down.  刚离婚就把她辞了，真是落井下石。

2703.e: If you want him to listen, hit him where it hurts and cut his budget.  想让他听话，就砍他预算，直击痛处。

2704.e: Our sales took a hit when the factory closed for three weeks.  工厂停工三周，我们的销售额受到了重创。

2705.e: The police are still looking for the driver in last night's hit-and-run accident.  警方仍在追查昨晚肇事逃逸的司机。

2706.i: hitch your ˌwagon to a ˈstar
2706.cn: 借他人之势；攀附成功者
2706.e: She hitched her wagon to a star by joining the young senator's campaign team.  她加入那位年轻参议员的竞选团队，借势而上。

2707.e: After ten years together, they finally got hitched in a tiny country church.  在一起十年后，他们终于在乡下小教堂结了婚。

2708.e: Leaves blew hither and thither across the empty playground all afternoon.  一整个下午，树叶在空荡的操场上四处飘飞。

2709.cn: 老生常谈的话题；热衷谈论的事
2709.e: Don't mention taxes or he'll climb onto his hobby horse again.  别提税的事，不然他又要老调重弹了。

2710.e: It was Hobson's choice: take the night shift or lose the job entirely.  这是别无选择：要么上夜班，要么丢饭碗。

2711.e: The whole committee disagreed, but she stood her ground and won in the end.  全委员会都反对，但她顶住压力，最后赢了。

2712.e: After the renovation we were in hock to the bank for years.  装修之后，我们欠了银行好几年的债。

2713.cn: 开始完全控制；扎下根来
2713.e: Panic took hold in the crowd as soon as the lights went out.  灯一灭，人群里立刻陷入恐慌。

2714.e: We were repainting the kitchen anyway, so we went the whole hog and retiled it.  反正要重刷厨房，我们索性一不做二不休，连瓷砖也换了。

2715.e: The kids went hog-wild when they saw the pile of presents.  孩子们看到一堆礼物，兴奋得快疯了。

2716.i: be hoist/hoisted by/with your own peˈtard
2716.cn: 搬起石头砸自己的脚；害人害己
2716.e: He spread the rumour and was hoist with his own petard when nobody trusted him.  他造谣生事，结果没人信他，搬石头砸了自己的脚。

2717.cn: 暂停射击；先别急着批评
2717.e: Hold your fire until you've heard the whole story from her side.  先别急着开火，听完她那边的说法再说。

2718.e: Grab hold of the rope and don't let go until I say so.  抓住绳子，我不说放手就别松开。

2719.e: That old advice about saving early still holds true for young workers today.  尽早储蓄这个老建议，对今天的年轻人依然适用。

2720.e: Hold it, I think you've left your wallet on the kitchen table.  等一下，你的钱包好像落在厨房桌上了。

2721.e: She's only nineteen but she holds her own against much older players.  她才十九岁，跟年长得多的选手打也毫不逊色。

2722.e: The whole project is on hold until the funding comes through next spring.  整个项目暂时搁置，要等明年春天拨款到位。

2723.e: Can you hold the fort in the shop while I run to the bank?  我去趟银行，你能在店里照看一下吗？

2724.i: leave sb holding the ˈbaby (AmE also leave sb holding the ˈbag) (informal)
2724.e: My partner quit halfway and left me holding the baby on the whole project.  合伙人中途退出，把整个项目的烂摊子丢给了我。

2725.cn: 某人势不可挡；拦也拦不住
2725.e: Once she decides to learn something, there's no holding her.  她一旦决定要学什么，谁也拦不住。

2726.e: It was a debate with no holds barred, and both sides said exactly what they thought.  那是一场毫无顾忌的辩论，双方都把话说透了。

2727.e: We're in a hole financially and the rent is due on Monday.  我们手头很紧，房租周一就要交了。

2728.e: The restaurant was fifty thousand dollars in the hole by December.  到十二月，那家餐馆已经欠了五万美元。

2729.i: burn a ˈhole in your pocket
2729.e: That bonus is burning a hole in his pocket, so he's already booked a trip.  奖金在他兜里待不住，他已经订好旅行了。

2730.i: need/want sb/sth like (you need/want) a ˌhole in the ˈhead (informal)
2730.e: I need another meeting today like I need a hole in the head.  今天再来一场会，我可真是一点都不想要。

2731.e: Buying the new car made a serious hole in our savings.  买了新车，我们的存款被啃掉一大块。

2732.e: For a chef, cooking for friends on Sunday is a real busman's holiday.  对厨师来说，周日给朋友做饭简直是换汤不换药的假期。

2733.e: Their team beat us hollow in the final, six goals to nothing.  决赛中他们六比零把我们打得落花流水。

2734.e: Nobody enters the director's office; it's the holy of holies around here.  没人能进主任办公室，那可是这里的禁地。

2735.e: She was completely at home talking to strangers at the reception.  在招待会上跟陌生人聊天，她一点都不拘束。

2736.e: He works two jobs to bring home the bacon for his family.  他打两份工养活一家人。

2737.cn: 使某人深切体会到（重要性或严重性）
2737.e: The photographs really brought home to us how bad the flooding was.  那些照片让我们真切感受到洪水有多严重。

2738.e: It finally came home to me that I'd been wrong about her all along.  我终于彻底明白，自己一直都误会了她。

2739.cn: 反复强调使人透彻理解
2739.e: The coach hammered home the point that discipline matters more than talent.  教练反复强调，纪律比天赋更重要。

2740.e: Her comment about my laziness struck home and I said nothing.  她说我懒的那句话戳中要害，我一句也没回。

2741.cn: 恋家的人；喜欢待在家的人
2741.e: My brother travels constantly, but I've always been a home bird.  我哥老在外面跑，我却一直是个恋家的人。

2742.i: a ˌhome from ˈhome (BrE) (AmE a ˌhome away from ˈhome)
2742.cn: 像家一样舒适自在的地方
2742.e: That little café by the station has become a home from home for us.  车站旁那家小咖啡馆成了我们的第二个家。

2743.e: They set up home together in a tiny flat above a bakery.  他们在一家面包店楼上的小公寓里安了家。

2744.i: ˌhome is where the ˈheart is (saying)
2744.e: I asked if he missed England, and he just said home is where the heart is.  我问他想不想英国，他只说心安处即是家。

2745.e: It's time somebody told him a few home truths about his behaviour.  该有人当面跟他说说他那些行为的实话了。

2746.e: Business is fine, but on the home front things have been rather tense.  生意还行，但家里最近气氛挺紧张。

2747.e: One more chapter and I'll be on the home straight with this thesis.  再写一章，这篇论文就进入最后冲刺了。

2748.cn: 事先做足功课；做好准备
2748.e: She'd done her homework on the company and asked very sharp questions.  她事先把这家公司研究透了，问题问得非常犀利。

2749.e: Honest to God, I had no idea the tickets were fake when I bought them.  我发誓，买票的时候真不知道那是假的。

3080.e: Her homemade pizza knocks spots off anything you can buy frozen.  她自己做的比萨比冷冻的强太多了。

3081.i: knock the ˈstuffing out of sb (informal)
3081.cn: 挫某人锐气；使某人元气大伤
3081.e: Losing the final really knocked the stuffing out of the whole team.  输掉决赛让整支队伍元气大伤。

3082.cn: 遭受挫折；受到沉重打击
3082.e: His confidence took a nasty knock after the interview went badly.  面试搞砸后，他的自信心受了重创。

3083.i: you could have knocked me, etc. down with a ˈfeather
3083.cn: （表示极度惊讶）真让人大吃一惊
3083.e: When she said she was quitting, you could have knocked me down with a feather.  她说要辞职时，我惊得半天说不出话。

3084.e: You could have knocked him down with a feather when the prize was announced.  宣布获奖名单时，他惊得目瞪口呆。

3085.i: before you know where you ˈare
3085.e: Start chatting online and before you know where you are it's two in the morning.  一上网聊天，转眼就到凌晨两点了。

3086.e: Don't blame him for the mix-up—he wasn't to know the meeting had moved.  别怪他弄错了，他哪知道会议改期了。

3087.i: for all ˈI, ˈyou, etc. know (spoken)
3087.cn: （强调不知情）说不定；亦未可知
3087.e: For all I know, she could be living in Australia by now.  说不定她现在已经住在澳大利亚了。

3088.e: People in the know say the factory will close before Christmas.  知情人士说这家工厂圣诞节前就要关门。

3089.i: it takes one to ˈknow one (informal, disapproving)
3089.cn: 半斤八两；五十步笑百步
3089.e: You're calling me lazy? Well, it takes one to know one.  你说我懒？彼此彼此吧。

3090.cn: 对…了如指掌；背得滚瓜烂熟
3090.e: She's played that part so often she knows the script backwards.  这个角色她演过太多次，剧本早已倒背如流。

3091.cn: 最懂得该怎么做；比谁都明白
3091.e: Fine, do it your way—you always know best, apparently.  行，照你的来，反正你总是最懂。

3092.i: know ˈbetter (than that/than to do sth)
3092.cn: 明白事理；不至于糊涂到…
3092.e: At your age you should know better than to believe every ad you see.  你这个岁数了，不该轻信每条广告。

3093.e: I know the man next door by sight, but we've never actually spoken.  隔壁那位我脸熟，但从没说过话。

3094.cn: 知道并非如此；掌握的情况不同
3094.e: He claims he was home all evening, but the neighbours know different.  他说自己整晚在家，邻居可知道不是这么回事。

3095.e: After twenty years here, she knows this old building inside out.  在这儿待了二十年，这栋老楼她了如指掌。

3096.i: know sth like the back of your ˈhand (informal)
3096.e: Ask the taxi driver—he knows these back streets like the back of his hand.  问司机吧，这些小巷他闭着眼都认得。

3097.e: When the baby finally arrived, their joy knew no bounds.  孩子终于降生，他们喜不自胜。

3098.cn: 有主见；知道自己要什么
3098.e: She's only sixteen, but she certainly knows her own mind.  她才十六岁，主意可正得很。

3099.e: In those days a junior clerk was expected to know his place.  那年头，小职员得知道自己几斤几两。

3100.e: Don't sugar-coat it—I've worked here long enough to know the score.  别粉饰了，我在这儿干这么久，什么情况都清楚。

3101.e: Watch the way she fixes that engine—she really knows her stuff.  看她修发动机的手法，真是行家。

3102.i: know a thing or two (about sb/sth) (informal)
3102.e: Ask Grandad about roses—he knows a thing or two about growing them.  养玫瑰的事问爷爷，他挺有一套。

3103.e: Give me a week and I'll know my way around the new office.  给我一周，我就熟悉新办公室了。

3104.i: know what it is to be/do sth
3104.cn: 亲身经历过；深知其中滋味
3104.e: She grew up poor, so she knows what it is to go hungry.  她穷苦出身，深知挨饿是什么滋味。

3105.e: Relax, let him carry the ladder—he knows what he's doing.  放心让他扛梯子，他有经验。

3106.e: I'm worried about David using that machine—don't be, he knows what he's doing.  我不放心戴维用那台机器。别担心，他有经验。

3107.e: Listen to her on childcare—she's raised four kids and knows what she's talking about.  育儿的事听她的，她带大四个孩子，都是经验之谈。

3108.cn: 知道好歹；懂得趋利避害
3108.e: You'll apologize to the boss tomorrow, if you know what's good for you.  你要是识相，明天就去跟老板道歉。

3109.e: Take the old mechanic with you—he knows what's what about used cars.  带上那位老技工，二手车的门道他门儿清。

3110.cn: 知道自己的处境（或地位）
3110.e: Just tell me straight, so at least I know where I stand.  直说吧，好歹让我知道自己是什么处境。

3111.cn: 目标明确；有清楚的追求
3111.e: She's only twenty-two, but she clearly knows where she's going.  她才二十二岁，可目标非常清楚。

3112.i: know which side your ˈbread is buttered
3112.cn: 知道利益所在；善于为自己打算
3112.e: He never argues with the boss—he knows which side his bread is buttered.  他从不跟老板顶嘴，知道好处在哪边。

3113.e: Let me know as soon as the delivery arrives at the shop.  货一到店里就通知我。

3114.e: He grabbed the last cake without asking—he just doesn't know any better.  他没问就抓走最后一块蛋糕，实在是没教养。

3115.e: Kids today with their heating and hot water don't know they're born.  如今的孩子有暖气有热水，身在福中不知福。

3116.i: not know your ˌarse from your ˈelbow (BrE)
3116.e: Don't let him wire the lamp—he doesn't know his arse from his elbow.  别让他接灯线，他啥也不懂。

3117.i: (AmE not know your ˌass from your ˈelbow) (△, slang)
3117.e: The new manager doesn't know his ass from his elbow about scheduling.  新经理排班的事一窍不通。

3118.i: not know ˈbeans about sth (AmE, informal)
3118.cn: 对…一窍不通；完全不懂行
3118.e: I don't know beans about fixing cars, so I called a mechanic.  我修车一窍不通，就叫了技工。

3119.i: not know the first thing aˈbout sb/sth
3119.e: He doesn't know the first thing about babies, yet he's giving advice.  他对带孩子一无所知，还在那儿指点。

3120.e: A man waved at me in the street, but I didn't know him from Adam.  街上有人朝我挥手，我压根不认识他。

3121.i: not know the ˈmeaning of the word (disapproving)
3121.cn: 根本不懂；毫无这种概念
3121.e: Patience? My brother doesn't know the meaning of the word.  耐心？我弟弟压根不知道这两个字怎么写。

3122.e: The tackle came so fast the poor kid didn't know what hit him.  那一下铲球太快，那孩子完全懵了。

3123.cn: 不知道错过了多好的事
3123.e: You've never tried snorkelling? You don't know what you're missing.  你没浮潜过？你真是错过太多了。

3124.e: Not interested in snowboarding? Try it—you don't know what you're missing.  对单板滑雪不感兴趣？试试吧，你不知道有多好玩。

3125.i: not know what to ˈdo with yourself
3125.e: With the kids away for a week, she didn't know what to do with herself.  孩子走了一周，她都不知道怎么打发时间。

3126.i: not know whether you're ˈcoming or ˈgoing
3126.cn: 忙得晕头转向；理不清头绪
3126.e: Between the new baby and the move, I don't know whether I'm coming or going.  又添了孩子又搬家，我忙得晕头转向。

3127.i: not know whether to ˈlaugh or ˈcry
3127.e: When the cake collapsed, I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.  蛋糕塌了的时候，我真是哭笑不得。

3128.i: not know which way/where to ˈlook
3128.cn: 尴尬得不知所措；狼狈不堪
3128.e: When he started singing in the restaurant, I didn't know where to look.  他在餐厅里唱起歌来，我尴尬得没处躲。

3129.i: not know which way/where to ˈturn
3129.e: After losing the job and the flat, he didn't know which way to turn.  丢了工作又丢了房子，他不知道该怎么办。

3130.e: She passed the test first time—well, what do you know about that!  她一次就考过了，真没想到！

3131.e: And what do you know, the missing keys were in my coat pocket.  你猜怎么着，丢的钥匙就在我大衣口袋里。

3132.i: you ˈknow (informal) (1 used when you are thinking of what to say)
3132.e: It was, you know, one of those days when nothing goes right.  就是那种，嗯，什么都不顺的日子。

3133.i: you know as well as ˈI do
3133.e: You know as well as I do that he never returns anything he borrows.  你我都清楚，他借东西从不还。

3134.e: Careful what you say—you know who is standing right behind you.  说话当心，你知道谁就站在你后面。

3135.e: Take an umbrella—you never know with the weather in April.  带把伞吧，四月的天气说不准。

3136.e: You never know with him; one day he's smiling and the next he ignores everyone.  他叫人捉摸不透，今天笑脸相迎，明天谁都不理。

3137.e: There's no knowing how long the repairs will take once they open the wall.  墙一拆开，修多久谁也说不准。

3138.e: It's common knowledge in the office that the two of them are dating.  他们俩在谈恋爱，办公室里人尽皆知。

3139.cn: 为某人所知；被某人获悉
3139.e: It has come to my knowledge that several files were removed last night.  我获悉昨晚有几份档案被人拿走了。

3140.e: To my knowledge, nobody has ever complained about the noise before.  据我所知，从没人抱怨过噪音。

3141.i: to the best of your belief/knowledge
3141.e: To the best of my knowledge, the shop closes at six on Saturdays.  据我所知，这家店周六六点关门。

3142.i: have a working knowledge of sth
3142.cn: 对…有实用的了解；能应付日常使用
3142.e: You'll need a working knowledge of Spanish to handle calls from Madrid.  接马德里的电话，你得会点日常西班牙语。

3143.i: let it be ˈknown/make it ˈknown that...
3143.e: The manager let it be known that late arrivals would no longer be tolerated.  经理放话出来，以后迟到概不容忍。

3144.e: If you arrive early, make yourself known to the woman at the desk.  你要是早到，就先跟前台那位女士报个到。

3145.e: God knows why he painted the kitchen bright orange.  天知道他为什么把厨房刷成亮橙色。

3146.i: (Some people may find the use of God knows offensive.)
3146.e: Some people may find the use of God knows offensive, so choose your words carefully.  有人会觉得这种说法冒犯，用词要留心。

3147.i: give sb, get, etc. a rap over the knuckles
3147.e: The reporter got a rap over the knuckles for printing the family's address.  那记者因登出这家人的地址挨了训。

3148.e: Months of hard labour finally turned the wasteland into a garden.  几个月的辛苦劳作，终于把荒地变成了花园。

3149.cn: 乐在其中的苦差；心甘情愿做的事
3149.e: Restoring that old motorbike was a labour of love that took him three years.  修复那辆老摩托是他甘之如饴的苦差，干了三年。

3150.cn: 反复解释；一再重复已明白的事
3150.e: I don't want to labour the point, but we really cannot afford this.  我不想啰嗦，可我们真的负担不起。

3151.e: After thirty years she finally reached the top of the tree in publishing.  干了三十年，她终于站上了出版界的顶端。

3152.cn: 讨女人喜欢的男子；爱与女人厮混的男子
3152.e: My uncle was a ladies' man in his youth and never missed a dance.  我叔叔年轻时是个情场高手，逢舞会必到。

3153.e: The seaside town is tired of lager louts wrecking the place every summer.  这座海滨小城受够了每年夏天来撒酒疯的年轻人。

3154.e: We rowed across the lake just as the mist was lifting off the water.  雾刚散，我们就划船横渡了湖面。

3155.e: The pair have been on the lam since the bank job last spring.  自去年春天抢银行后，这两人一直在逃。

3156.e: She thinks that miniskirt suits her, but it's mutton dressed up as lamb.  她觉得那条超短裙很衬她，其实是老来俏。

3157.cn: 跛脚鸭；处境艰难的人（或机构）
3157.e: The government refused to keep pouring money into a lame duck airline.  政府拒绝继续给这家难以为继的航空公司砸钱。

3158.i: in the land of the ˈliving (humorous)
3158.e: You're finally up? Good to see you back in the land of the living.  你总算起床了？欢迎回到人间。

3159.i: in the ˌland of ˈNod (old-fashioned, humorous)
3159.e: By nine o'clock both children were safely in the land of Nod.  九点钟，两个孩子都已进了梦乡。

3160.e: He barely landed a punch before the referee stopped the fight.  裁判叫停之前，他几乎没打中一拳。

3161.i: a/the land of ˌmilk and ˈhoney
3161.e: Their grandparents crossed the ocean expecting a land of milk and honey.  他们的祖辈漂洋过海，指望找到一片乐土。

3162.i: see, etc. how the ˈland lies (BrE)
3162.e: Let's have coffee with her first and see how the land lies.  先跟她喝杯咖啡，摸摸情况再说。

3163.e: That concrete car park is a real blot on the landscape here.  那座水泥停车场在这儿实在大煞风景。

3164.e: Watch your language—there are small children in the next room.  说话注意点，隔壁屋里有小孩。

3165.cn: 谈得来（或谈不来）；有无共同语言
3165.e: The engineers and the designers simply don't speak the same language.  工程师和设计师根本说不到一块儿去。

3166.e: He dumped the whole budget mess in my lap and went on holiday.  他把整摊预算烂事丢给我，自己度假去了。

3167.cn: 轻易到手；从天上掉下来
3167.e: A job like that doesn't just fall into your lap—you have to chase it.  这种工作不会从天上掉下来，得自己去争取。

3168.i: in the lap of the ˈgods
3168.cn: 听天由命；非人力所能左右
3168.e: We've done all we can; the result is in the lap of the gods now.  我们能做的都做了，结果就听天由命吧。

3169.e: He grew up in the lap of luxury and has never washed a dish.  他从小锦衣玉食，连碗都没洗过。

3170.e: We're on the last lap of the project, so hang on for another week.  项目进入最后阶段了，再撑一周。

3171.cn: （用于名词后）整体而言；一般大众
3171.e: The proposal is popular with staff but society at large remains unconvinced.  这项提议员工欢迎，但整个社会仍不买账。

3172.e: By and large, the new timetable has made the commute much easier.  总的来说，新时刻表让通勤轻松多了。

3173.i: in ˈlarge part • in ˌno small ˈpart (formal)
3173.e: The team's success is in large part due to their new goalkeeper.  球队的成功在很大程度上归功于新门将。

3174.cn: 本人赫然在场；千真万确
3174.e: I turned the corner and there he was, as large as life, selling flowers.  我一拐弯，他就赫然站在那儿卖花。

3175.e: Her father was a larger than life character who filled any room he entered.  她父亲是个气场十足的人，走到哪儿都是焦点。

3176.cn: 一大早就起床；鸡鸣即起
3176.e: Farmers here are up with the lark, even in the middle of winter.  这里的农民天不亮就起，隆冬也不例外。

3177.e: At long last the builders finished and we could move back in.  工人们总算完工，我们可以搬回去了。

3178.cn: 据最新统计；最新消息说
3178.e: At the last count, over three hundred people had signed the petition.  据最新统计，已有三百多人在请愿书上签名。

3179.e: She cancelled at the last minute and left us one player short.  她最后一刻取消，害我们少了一个人。

3180.i: the day, week, month, etc. before ˈlast
3180.e: I saw him at the market the week before last, looking perfectly well.  上上周我在市场见过他，气色好得很。

3181.e: They ate every last crumb of the cake before I got home.  我到家前，蛋糕被他们吃得一点渣都不剩。

3182.e: They mocked her little shop, but she had the last laugh when it expanded.  他们嘲笑她那家小店，可她最后笑到了最后。

3183.cn: 作最后决定；说最后一句话
3183.e: She always has to have the last word in an argument.  吵架时她总要说最后一句才罢休。

3184.i: last but not ˈleast • last but by no means ˈleast
3184.e: Last but not least, I want to thank the volunteers who cooked for us.  最后但同样重要的，感谢为我们做饭的志愿者。

3185.e: The last I heard, they were still living somewhere near Leeds.  我最后听说，他们还住在利兹附近。

3186.cn: 后进先出（裁员时最晚来的最先走）
3186.e: The factory is cutting staff on a last in, first out basis.  工厂按后进先出的原则裁员。

3187.e: This kitchen is the last word in gadgets, but nobody ever cooks here.  这厨房里的电器最先进，可从来没人做饭。

3188.e: That old washing machine is on its last legs and floods the floor weekly.  那台旧洗衣机快散架了，每周都漏一地水。

3189.e: He defended his brother's name to the last, even in court.  他至死都在维护弟弟的名声，连在法庭上也是。

3465.cn: 取得很大进步；大有长进
3465.e: Cancer treatment has come a long way since my grandmother was first diagnosed.  自我祖母初次确诊以来，癌症治疗已有了长足进步。

3466.i: have a long way to ˈgo
3466.cn: 还有很长的路要走；差距还很大
3466.e: Her Spanish is improving, but she still has a long way to go before fluency.  她的西班牙语在进步，但离流利还差得远。

3467.i: how long is a piece of ˈstring? (BrE, spoken)
3467.e: You ask how much the repair will cost—well, how long is a piece of string?  你问修理要多少钱，这可真说不准。

3468.e: Buying decent boots costs more now but saves you money in the long run.  买双好靴子眼下费钱，长远看反而省钱。

3469.e: Why did I quit my job in Beijing? It's a long story, buy me a drink first.  我为什么辞掉北京的工作？说来话长，先请我喝一杯。

3470.i: the long and (the) ˈshort of it
3470.cn: 总而言之；总的情况就是这样
3470.e: The long and the short of it is that we can't afford the house.  总而言之，这房子我们买不起。

3471.i: the long arm of the ˈlaw
3471.e: He hid in Thailand for years, but the long arm of the law finally reached him.  他在泰国躲了多年，最终还是没能逃出法网。

3472.e: Don't pull a long face just because your team lost one match.  别只因球队输了一场就哭丧着脸。

3473.cn: 漫长而艰辛的事；长途跋涉
3473.e: Getting the factory back to full production will be a long haul.  让工厂恢复满负荷生产会是件漫长又费劲的事。

3474.i: (be) ˌlong in the ˈtooth (humorous, especially BrE)
3474.e: I'm getting a bit long in the tooth for climbing mountains in winter.  我这把年纪，冬天爬山有点吃不消了。

3475.cn: 成功机会不大的尝试；胜算很小的猜测
3475.e: Applying to Oxford was a long shot, but she got in anyway.  申请牛津本是碰碰运气，结果她真考上了。

3476.e: Wei! Long time no see—how have you been these past three years?  阿伟！好久不见，这三年过得怎么样？

3477.i: not by a ˈlong chalk (BrE) (also not by a ˈlong shot AmE, BrE) (informal)
3477.e: The job isn't finished, not by a long chalk—we've barely started.  活儿还差得远呢，我们才刚开了个头。

3478.cn: 不久于人世；活不了多久
3478.e: The old dog can barely walk now; I'm afraid he's not long for this world.  这条老狗几乎走不动了，恐怕活不了多久。

3479.cn: 从长远看；在很长一段时间里
3479.e: Over the long haul, small daily savings add up to a real cushion.  长远看来，每天省下的一点点会攒成一笔应急钱。

3480.e: So long for now—I'll call you when I land in Shanghai.  先这样，等我落地上海再给你打电话。

3481.i: take a long (cool/hard) ˈlook at sth
3481.e: You should take a long hard look at your spending before buying that car.  买那辆车之前，你该好好审视一下自己的开销。

3482.e: Good investors take the long view and ignore one bad quarter.  优秀的投资者着眼长远，不会在意一个季度的亏损。

3483.i: to cut a long story ˈshort (BrE) (AmE to make a long story ˈshort) (spoken)
3483.e: To cut a long story short, we missed the flight and drove instead.  长话短说，我们误了航班，改成开车了。

3484.e: She no longer answers his messages, and honestly I don't blame her.  她不再回他消息了，说实话我不怪她。

3485.e: By the look of things, this meeting is going to run past six.  看样子，这个会要开到六点以后了。

3486.e: It would look bad if you skipped your own brother's wedding.  你要是缺席亲弟弟的婚礼，那可太说不过去了。

3487.cn: 看来充满希望；形势看好
3487.e: Sales are up two months running—things are finally starting to look good.  销售连涨两个月，情况总算开始看好了。

3488.e: Look here, I've paid on time every month and I won't be spoken to like that.  喂，听着，我每月都按时付款，不许这么跟我说话。

3489.e: The doorman looked me up and down and decided my jacket wasn't smart enough.  门童把我上下打量一番，认定我的外套不够体面。

3490.cn: 气色（不）如常；看来（不）像平时那样
3490.e: You don't look yourself today—did you sleep at all last night?  你今天气色不太对，昨晚睡了吗？

3491.i: not be much to ˈlook at (informal)
3491.e: The car isn't much to look at, but the engine runs like new.  这车外表不起眼，可发动机跟新的一样。

3492.i: to ˈlook at sb/sth • by the ˈlook of sb/sth
3492.e: To look at him, you'd never guess he once ran marathons.  从外表看，你绝想不到他当年跑过马拉松。

3493.cn: 没有机会参与；没有得胜的希望
