3493.e: With three older brothers, he never got a look-in at the dinner table.  上头三个哥哥，饭桌上从来轮不到他。

3494.e: Thanks, I'm just looking—I'll shout if I need help with sizes.  谢谢，我随便看看，要试尺码再叫你。

3495.e: Ever since the layoffs, everyone in the office is looking over their shoulder.  自从裁员以来，办公室里人人都提心吊胆。

3496.cn: 打算做某事；正想着做某事
3496.e: We're looking to move somewhere quieter before the baby arrives.  我们打算在孩子出生前搬到清静点的地方。

3497.cn: 是某人自己的事；后果自负
3497.e: If he wants to invest his savings in crypto, that's his own lookout.  他要拿积蓄去炒币，那是他自己的事。

3498.i: be on the ˈlookout (for sb/sth) • keep a
3498.e: I'm on the lookout for a secondhand piano that won't cost a fortune.  我在留意一台价格不离谱的二手钢琴。

3499.e: Keep a lookout for a red door—the café is just behind it.  留心找一扇红门，咖啡馆就在门后面。

3500.cn: 如果目光能杀人（形容目光极其愤怒）
3500.e: If looks could kill, the waiter would have dropped dead on the spot.  要是目光能杀人，那服务员当场就没命了。

3501.cn: （问题、事件）迫近而令人忧虑；显得突出
3501.e: With exams two weeks away, failure began to loom large in her mind.  考试还有两周，落榜的念头在她心里越来越沉重。

3502.e: The road makes a wide loop around the lake before heading north.  这条路绕湖兜了一个大圈，然后向北去。

3503.i: be in the ˈloop • be out of the ˈloop (informal, especially AmE)
3503.cn: 属于（或不属于）知情圈子
3503.e: Copy me on those emails so I stay in the loop about the merger.  那些邮件抄送我一份，好让我了解并购进展。

3504.i: knock/throw sb for a ˈloop (AmE, informal)
3504.cn: 使某人大为震惊；打得某人措手不及
3504.e: His sudden resignation really threw the whole team for a loop.  他突然辞职，把整个团队都搞蒙了。

3505.e: The old biplane looped the loop twice and the crowd went wild.  那架老双翼机连翻两个筋斗，观众都疯了。

3506.i: at a loose ˈend (BrE) (AmE at loose ˈends)
3506.e: If you're at a loose end on Sunday, come and help me paint the fence.  你周日要是闲着没事，来帮我刷围栏吧。

3507.e: At eighteen he broke loose from his family and moved across the country.  十八岁时他挣脱家庭束缚，搬到了国家的另一头。

3508.e: Just hang loose—the results won't be posted until Friday anyway.  别急，反正成绩要到周五才公布。

3509.e: Don't tell him anything private; he has a very loose tongue.  别跟他说私事，他嘴太不严了。

3510.e: After finals we all let loose and danced until three in the morning.  期末考完，我们彻底放开，跳舞跳到凌晨三点。

3511.e: When the goal went in, he let loose a yell that woke the neighbours.  球进的那一刻，他大吼一声，把邻居都吵醒了。

3512.cn: 放开；释放；任其自由行动
3512.e: Never let that dog loose in the park without checking the gate first.  没先检查大门，绝不要在公园里放开那条狗。

3513.cn: 言行难以预料的危险人物
3513.e: The manager is talented but a loose cannon in front of reporters.  这位经理很有才，但面对记者时口无遮拦、难以掌控。

3514.cn: 尚待处理的枝节问题；未了结的细节
3514.e: The film is fun, but it leaves far too many loose ends unexplained.  这部电影挺好看，可留下的伏笔太多没交代。

3515.i: You know who committed the murder, but there
3515.cn: 凶手已知，细节却未交代清楚
3515.e: You know who committed the murder, but there are still loose ends everywhere.  你知道凶手是谁，可到处都是没交代清楚的细节。

3516.e: Two bears are on the loose near the campsite, so keep food inside.  有两头熊在营地附近游荡，食物请收在屋里。

3517.e: The company played fast and loose with safety rules until someone got hurt.  这家公司一直无视安全规定，直到出了工伤。

3518.cn: 使某人无拘无束地说话；使人说话没顾忌
3518.e: Two glasses of wine loosened his tongue and out came the whole story.  两杯红酒下肚，他话匣子打开，全说了。

3519.cn: 天哪；主啊（表示惊讶或懊恼）
3519.e: Oh Lord, I've left my passport on the kitchen table again.  天哪，我又把护照落在厨房桌上了。

3520.i: (Some people may find these idioms offensive.)
3520.cn: （有人可能认为这些习语含冒犯意）
3520.e: Some people may find these idioms offensive, so use them carefully in class.  有人可能觉得这些习语冒犯，课堂上要慎用。

3521.e: Lord knows why he sold the flat right before prices doubled.  天晓得他为什么在房价翻倍前把房子卖了。

3522.cn: 对某人盛气凌人；摆架子
3522.e: Ever since her promotion she's been lording it over the rest of us.  自从升职以后，她就对我们其他人颐指气使。

3523.i: off the ˌback of a ˈlorry (BrE, informal, humorous)
3523.cn: 来路不明（通常指偷来的）
3523.e: That watch was suspiciously cheap—it probably fell off the back of a lorry.  那块表便宜得可疑，八成是来路不明的货。

3524.i: come ˈoff the back of a lorry (BrE, informal, humorous)
3524.e: He never asks where the stock comes off the back of a lorry from.  他从不问那些来路不明的货究竟是哪儿来的。

3525.e: When the printer jammed for the fifth time, I completely lost it.  打印机第五次卡纸时，我彻底崩溃了。

3526.e: I'm at a loss to explain why the server crashed again this morning.  我实在说不清今早服务器为什么又崩了。

3527.cn: 无言以对；不知说什么好
3527.e: When she handed me the keys to the flat, I was at a loss for words.  她把公寓钥匙交给我时，我一时说不出话来。

3528.e: The shop lost money for two years, so we cut our losses and closed it.  店里亏了两年，我们只好止损关门。

3529.e: We missed the deadline, but all is not lost—they'll accept late entries.  我们错过了截止日期，但还有希望，他们收迟交的。

3530.e: He was lost for words when the whole street turned up to help.  整条街的人都来帮忙，他感动得说不出话。

3531.e: She was lost in her book and didn't hear the doorbell at all.  她看书入了神，压根没听见门铃。

3532.cn: 未被某人领会；对某人不起作用
3532.e: The joke about the tax code was completely lost on the children.  那个关于税法的笑话，孩子们根本没听懂。

3533.cn: 浑然忘我；不理会周围一切
3533.e: With his headphones on, he's lost to the world for hours at a time.  戴上耳机，他能一连几个小时与世隔绝。

3534.e: I'd be lost without my phone's calendar—I can't remember a single date.  没了手机日历我就抓瞎，什么日子都记不住。

3535.e: I told the guy selling fake tickets to get lost before I called security.  我叫那个卖假票的滚开，不然就叫保安。

3536.cn: 认定…已无望找回；认定某人已死
3536.e: After ten days the rescuers had almost given the climbers up for lost.  十天过后，救援队几乎认定那些登山者已经遇难。

3537.cn: 注定失败的事；败局已定的目标
3537.e: Teaching my father to use video calls is frankly a lost cause.  教我爸用视频通话，说实话是件没指望的事。

3538.e: After a year apart, they travelled everywhere together to make up for lost time.  分开一年后，他们四处同游，把耽误的时光补回来。

3539.e: Her second husband was a bad lot who ran off with her savings.  她的第二任丈夫不是好东西，卷走了她的积蓄。

3540.cn: 以抽签方式；用抓阄的办法
3540.e: The last two tickets were given out by lot among the waiting fans.  最后两张票是在等候的粉丝中抽签发放的。

3541.i: from a container and the one whose paper has
3541.e: Each name is drawn from a container and the one whose paper has a cross wins.  名字从容器里抽出，纸上画叉的那位获胜。

3542.i: throw in your ˈlot with sb
3542.cn: 与某人共命运；与某人同甘共苦
3542.e: He threw in his lot with the strikers even though it cost him his job.  他和罢工者站到一起，哪怕因此丢了工作。

3543.e: We drew lots to decide who would sleep on the sofa that night.  我们抓阄决定那晚谁睡沙发。

3544.e: The message from the voters came through loud and clear last night.  昨晚选民传递的信号清清楚楚。

3545.e: He read the letter out loud so everyone at the table could hear.  他把信念出声来，好让桌边的人都听见。

3546.i: (just) for ˈlove/for the ˈlove of sth
3546.cn: 出于爱好；无偿；不图回报
3546.e: She coaches the village team just for love, not for a single penny.  她带村里的球队纯粹出于喜欢，一分钱不收。

3547.i: for the love of ˈGod (old-fashioned, spoken)
3547.cn: 看在上帝的份上（表示愤怒或不耐烦）
3547.e: For the love of God, will someone turn that alarm off?  看在上帝的份上，谁去把那警报关了行吗？

3548.e: Give my love to your parents when you get home for the holiday.  放假回家时代我向你父母问好。

3549.e: It was love at first sight—he proposed six weeks after they met.  那是一见钟情，认识六周他就求婚了。

3550.i: ˈlove from • lots of ˈlove (from) (written, informal)
3550.e: She ended every postcard with 'lots of love from your silly aunt'.  她每张明信片都以“爱你的傻姑姑”结尾。

3551.cn: 情人眼里出西施；爱是盲目的
3551.e: Everyone can see he's using her, but love is blind, I suppose.  谁都看得出他在利用她，可惜爱是盲目的。

3552.i: love you and ˈleave you (spoken, humorous)
3552.e: This has been fun, but I must love you and leave you—last train's at eleven.  聊得真开心，可我得走了，末班车十一点。

3553.e: They made love for the first time in a freezing flat with no heating.  他们第一次做爱是在一间没暖气的冰冷公寓里。

3554.cn: 无论如何也不；说什么也不
3554.e: You couldn't get a taxi that night for love nor money.  那天晚上你无论如何也叫不到出租车。

3555.i: there's no ˈlove lost between A and B (informal)
3555.e: There's no love lost between the two coaches since last season's final.  自上赛季决赛以来，两位教练彼此厌恶。

3556.i: lovely and ˈwarm, ˈcold, ˈquiet, etc. (BrE, spoken)
3556.cn: 非常暖和（或凉快、安静等）
3556.e: Come inside, it's lovely and warm by the fire in here.  快进来，这儿炉火边可暖和了。

3557.e: We're running low on coffee, so add a jar to the shopping list.  咖啡快没了，购物单上加一罐。

3558.e: Morale in the department was at a low ebb after the third round of cuts.  第三轮裁员后，部门士气跌到了谷底。

3559.e: Sit down and give me the low-down on your new boss.  坐下来，跟我讲讲你新上司的底细。

3560.cn: 降低（某场合、作品的）格调
3560.e: One rude joke like that can lower the tone of the whole evening.  那样一个粗俗笑话就能把整晚的格调拉低。

3561.e: I won't lower myself by arguing with strangers in the comments.  我不会自降身份，去跟评论区的陌生人吵架。

3562.e: Any luck with the job applications you sent out last week?  上周投的那些简历有消息了吗？

3563.e: He's been down on his luck since the restaurant closed last winter.  自从去年冬天餐馆关门，他就一直不走运。

3564.e: She always touches the doorframe for luck before an exam.  她考试前总要摸一下门框讨个吉利。

3565.e: Good luck with your driving test—remember to check the mirrors.  祝你路考顺利，记得看后视镜。

3566.e: If he wants to cycle across Mongolia, good luck to him.  他要骑车穿越蒙古，那就祝他好运吧。

3567.i: you're in ˈluck • your ˈluck is in
3567.e: You're in luck—there's exactly one seat left on the evening train.  你走运了，晚班车刚好还剩一个座位。

3568.i: the luck of the ˈdevil • the luck of the ˈIrish
3568.e: He walked away from that crash with the luck of the devil.  那场车祸他毫发无伤，运气好得出奇。

3569.e: Which examiner you get is just the luck of the draw.  碰上哪个考官，全凭运气。

3570.e: I hoped the meeting was cancelled, but no such luck.  我盼着会议取消，可惜没那么走运。

3571.cn: 真不走运；活该（视语气而定）
3571.e: Tough luck about the concert tickets—they sold out in four minutes.  演唱会门票四分钟就没了，真不走运。

3572.i: have a ˈlump in your throat
3572.e: I had a lump in my throat watching my daughter walk onto the stage.  看着女儿走上台，我喉咙一阵发哽。

3573.e: He made the mistake, so he'll have to take his lumps at the meeting.  错是他犯的，会上挨批他就得受着。

3574.cn: （团体中的）极端分子；狂热的少数人
3574.e: Most members are reasonable; it's the lunatic fringe that gets on television.  多数成员都很理性，上电视的偏偏是那帮极端分子。

5005.e: He was on the rack all weekend waiting for the biopsy results to arrive.  整个周末他都在焦灼不安地等活检结果。

5006.i: rack your ˈbrains (also wrack your ˈbrains less frequent) (informal)
5006.e: I racked my brains for an hour but still couldn't remember her name.  我绞尽脑汁想了一个小时，还是想不起她的名字。

5007.e: The startup grew below the radar for two years before anyone really noticed.  这家初创公司低调发展了两年才被人注意到。

5008.e: Experts say a lot of corporate crime stays under the radar for years.  专家说，许多公司犯罪多年都无人察觉。

5009.e: Climate change is finally on the radar of every major political party here.  气候变化终于进入了这里各大政党的视野。

5010.cn: 一直不受关注；始终无人留意
5010.e: Eastern Europe has remained off the radar of most British investors until quite recently.  直到最近，东欧仍不在多数英国投资者的视野内。

5011.e: Dad completely lost his rag when he saw the scratch on his new car.  爸爸看到新车上的划痕，一下就火了。

5012.e: She spent thirty years in the rag trade before opening her own boutique.  她在服装业干了三十年，后来开了自己的精品店。

5013.e: Those chunky white trainers were all the rage when I was at university.  我上大学那会儿，那种厚底白运动鞋特别火。

5014.cn: 使精疲力竭；使过度操劳
5014.e: The twins run me ragged from breakfast until bedtime every single day.  这对双胞胎每天从早到晚把我折腾得筋疲力尽。

5015.i: take a ˈrain check (on sth) (informal, especially AmE)
5015.e: Can I take a rain check on dinner? I'm swamped with work tonight.  晚饭能改天吗？我今晚忙得不可开交。

5016.i: it never ˌrains but it ˈpours (BrE) (AmE when it ˌrains, it ˈpours) (saying)
5016.cn: 祸不单行；不雨则已，一雨倾盆
5016.e: My car broke down, then the boiler died — it never rains but it pours.  车坏了，锅炉又罢工，真是祸不单行。

5017.i: save, keep, etc. it for a ˌrainy ˈday (informal)
5017.cn: 储蓄以备不时之需；未雨绸缪
5017.e: Put some of that bonus aside and save it for a rainy day.  把奖金存下一部分，以备不时之需。

5018.e: Residents raised hell at the meeting about the new motorway through their village.  居民在会上为穿村而过的新高速公路大闹了一场。

5019.cn: 扬眉（表示惊讶或不赞同）
5019.e: She raised her eyebrows at the price but paid for the coat anyway.  她看到价格扬了扬眉，但还是买下了那件大衣。

5020.e: Let's raise our glasses to the happy couple and wish them many good years.  让我们举杯祝这对新人幸福长久。

5021.e: Even his oldest jokes still raise a laugh at the family dinner table.  他那些老掉牙的笑话在家庭餐桌上仍能逗乐大家。

5022.i: raise the ˈspectre of sth (BrE) (AmE raise the ˈspecter of sth)
5022.cn: 引起对…的恐惧；使人担忧
5022.e: The factory closure raises the spectre of mass unemployment across the whole region.  工厂关闭让人担心整个地区会出现大规模失业。

5023.cn: 使精神振奋；使高兴起来
5023.e: A phone call from her grandson always raises her spirits on a gloomy day.  孙子的一通电话总能在阴郁的日子里让她开心起来。

5024.e: Don't raise your voice at me — it wasn't my fault the train was late.  别冲我嚷，火车晚点又不是我的错。

5025.cn: 公开反对；大声疾呼抗议
5025.e: Only one councillor raised her voice against the plan to sell the park.  只有一位议员公开反对出售公园的计划。

5026.i: rake over the ˈashes/the ˈpast (informal, disapproving)
5026.e: There's no point raking over the past every time we have an argument.  每次吵架都翻旧账，毫无意义。

5027.e: The coach rammed home the point that fitness matters more than raw talent.  教练反复强调，体能比天赋更重要。

5028.cn: 横冲直撞；到处撒野搞破坏
5028.e: A group of fans went on the rampage through the town after the match.  一群球迷赛后在镇上到处闹事。

5029.i: ˌramrod ˈstraight • (as) ˌstraight as a ˈramrod
5029.e: The old sergeant stood ramrod straight even while waiting in the supermarket queue.  这位老军士连在超市排队时都站得笔直。

5030.cn: 背挺得直直的；神情严肃郑重
5030.e: She sat as straight as a ramrod through the entire three-hour interview.  整整三小时的面试，她都坐得笔直。

5031.e: They run a cattle ranch in Montana that has been in the family for generations.  他们在蒙大拿经营着一家几代相传的养牛牧场。

5032.cn: 在可及（可视、可听）的范围内
5032.e: Stay within range of the wifi or the video call will keep dropping.  待在无线网范围内，不然视频通话会一直断。

5033.cn: 在可及（可视、可听）的范围之外
5033.e: The deer was out of range, so the photographer never got his shot.  那只鹿超出了距离，摄影师始终没拍到。

5034.e: The rank and file voted against the deal their union leaders had negotiated.  普通会员投票否决了工会领导谈成的协议。

5035.cn: 拒绝支持本团体；公开唱反调
5035.e: Two ministers broke ranks and criticised the policy in public last night.  两位大臣昨晚公开批评该政策，与内阁唱了反调。

5036.cn: 从底层干起升至高位；行伍出身
5036.e: She rose through the ranks from cashier to regional manager in just eight years.  她八年间从收银员一路升到大区经理。

5037.e: The department closed ranks and refused to say anything to the waiting reporters.  该部门上下一心，拒绝对守候的记者透露任何情况。

5038.cn: 绑架某人索取赎金；要挟
5038.e: A handful of rebels are holding the whole peace process to ransom.  少数反对者正在挟持整个和平进程。

5039.e: That little painting in the hallway is apparently worth a king's ransom.  走廊里那幅小画据说值一大笔钱。

5040.cn: 大叫大嚷；不停地大声抱怨
5040.e: He ranted and raved about the noise for twenty minutes before finally calming down.  他为噪音大吵大嚷了二十分钟才平静下来。

5041.e: The paper got a rap over the knuckles for printing the leaked memo.  这家报纸因刊登泄露的备忘录而受到了批评。

5042.e: Why should I take the rap for a mistake the whole team made?  凭什么全队犯的错要我来背黑锅？

5043.e: The critics went into raptures over her first novel and its strange ending.  评论家们对她的处女作及其古怪结尾赞不绝口。

5044.e: A politician who happily admits mistakes is a rare bird these days.  如今肯痛快承认错误的政客实属罕见。

5045.e: The kids were up at six, dressed and raring to go to the beach.  孩子们六点就起床穿好衣服，急着要去海边。

5046.cn: （大城市里的）激烈竞争；疯狂角逐
5046.e: He quit the rat race at forty and now grows vegetables in Wales.  他四十岁退出职场角逐，如今在威尔士种菜。

5047.e: The flight might be delayed; at any rate, don't wait up for me.  航班可能晚点；不管怎样，别等我了。

5048.i: at a rate of ˈknots (BrE, informal)
5048.e: He got through the paperwork at a rate of knots and left early.  他飞快地处理完文件，提早走了。

5049.e: At this rate we won't finish painting the kitchen before Christmas arrives.  照这个速度，圣诞节前我们刷不完厨房。

5050.cn: 现行价格；通行收费标准
5050.e: What's the going rate for babysitting round here on a Saturday night?  这一带周六晚上看孩子的行情价是多少？

5051.e: We took the train rather than driving, which saved us a lot of stress.  我们坐火车而不是开车，省了不少心。

5052.i: rather you, etc. than ˈme (also sooner you, etc. than ˈme) (especially BrE)
5052.cn: 幸亏不是我；这事儿我可不干
5052.e: You're swimming in the sea in January? Rather you than me, honestly.  一月还下海游泳？说实话，幸亏不是我。

5053.e: Forty pounds for a taxi to the airport seems a bit steep.  打车去机场四十镑，似乎贵了点。

5054.e: Don't mention the referee's decision — it really rattles his cage every time.  别提裁判那个判罚，每次都能把他惹毛。

5055.cn: 彻底疯了的；疯疯癫癫的
5055.e: You'd have to be stark raving mad to swim across that freezing river.  游过那条冰冷的河，你得是彻底疯了。

5056.cn: 触到某人痛处；揭某人伤疤
5056.e: His joke about her divorce clearly caught her on the raw.  他拿她离婚开玩笑，显然戳到了她的痛处。

5057.cn: 自然状态下的；不加掩饰的
5057.e: This documentary shows life in the raw for families on the city's edge.  这部纪录片真实呈现了城郊家庭的生活。

5058.e: The new treatment is the only ray of hope for patients like him.  新疗法是像他这样的病人唯一的一线希望。

5059.e: The bank is still a ray of hope; they might agree to lend us the money.  银行还是一线希望，他们也许会借钱给我们。

5060.cn: 带来快乐的人（或事物）；一缕阳光
5060.e: My little niece is a ray of sunshine on even the darkest days.  我的小侄女在最阴郁的日子里也是一缕阳光。

5061.i: be/go out on the ˈrazzle (BrE, informal)
5061.cn: 外出寻欢作乐；出去纵饮狂欢
5061.e: The lads went out on the razzle on Friday and stumbled home at dawn.  小伙子们周五出去疯玩，天亮才踉跄回家。

5062.cn: 志向远大；胸怀雄心壮志
5062.e: My grandmother always told me to reach for the stars and ignore the doubters.  奶奶总叫我志存高远，别理会那些唱衰的人。

5063.e: The cottage is within easy reach of both the beach and the station.  那间小屋离海滩和车站都很近。

5064.cn: 领悟言外之意；看出弦外之音
5064.e: Reading between the lines, I'd say she's not very happy in that job.  从字里行间看，我觉得她并不喜欢那份工作。

5065.cn: 对某人了如指掌；看透某人
5065.e: After twenty years of marriage she can read me like a book.  结婚二十年了，她把我看得透透的。

5066.cn: 看出某人的心思；猜透某人的想法
5066.e: I was just about to make tea — you read my mind!  我正想去泡茶，你真会猜我的心思！

5067.e: Read my lips: I am not lending you the car again.  给我听好了，我不会再把车借给你。

5068.cn: 严厉警告某人收敛；狠狠训斥
5068.e: The head teacher read the whole class the Riot Act about the graffiti.  校长就涂鸦的事把全班狠狠训了一顿。

5070.cn: 认定某事不必再讨论；视为当然
5070.e: We can take it as read that everyone here supports the new proposal.  可以认定在座各位都支持这项新提议。

5071.e: She stood quietly by the door with her camera at the ready.  她静静守在门口，相机随时准备好。

5072.e: The whole village made ready for the storm that was forecast overnight.  全村都为预报中夜间来袭的风暴做好了准备。

5073.i: ready, steady, ˈgo! (BrE) (also (get) ready, (get) set, ˈgo! AmE, BrE)
5073.cn: 各就位，预备，跑！；准备开始
5073.e: Ready, steady, go! The children raced across the field towards the finish line.  各就位，预备，跑！孩子们冲过田野奔向终点。

5074.cn: 我已准备就绪，就等你了
5074.e: Ready when you are — the car's warmed up and the bags are in.  我这边好了，就等你，车热好了，行李也装上了。

5075.e: Is this offer for real, or is somebody playing a joke on me?  这个报价是真的吗，还是有人在跟我开玩笑？

5076.e: You want to buy a house on that salary? Get real.  就那点工资还想买房？醒醒吧。

5077.e: He seems shy online but in real life he never stops talking.  他网上看着腼腆，现实中却话多得停不下来。

5078.e: This isn't a copy — the dealer swears it's the real McCoy.  这不是仿品，卖家发誓说是真货。

5079.e: Instant coffee is fine, but nothing beats the real thing in the morning.  速溶咖啡凑合，但早上还是真咖啡最好。

5080.e: He looks confident on stage, but in reality he's terrified every single time.  他台上看着自信，其实每次都怕得要命。

5081.e: A February heatwave isn't beyond the realms of possibility these days.  如今二月出现热浪也并非没有可能。

5082.e: After years of careful training, the team is finally reaping the harvest.  经过多年精心训练，这支队伍终于收获了成果。

5083.cn: 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆；自食其果
5083.e: He cheated everyone for years, and now he's learning you reap what you sow.  他骗了大家多年，现在明白了什么叫自食其果。

5084.i: (sow the wind,) reap the ˈwhirlwind (especially AmE)
5084.e: The company sowed the wind with those layoffs and is now reaping the whirlwind.  公司当初大裁员，如今自食恶果。

5085.e: Grandad brought up the rear, stopping every few minutes to catch his breath.  爷爷走在最后，每隔几分钟就停下喘口气。

5086.i: rearrange the ˌdeckchairs on the Tiˈtanic
5086.e: Repainting the office while sales collapse is just rearranging the deckchairs on the Titanic.  销量崩盘还给办公室刷漆，纯属做无用功。

5087.cn: 合情合理；在合理范围内
5087.e: You can order whatever you like, within reason — I'm not made of money.  你想点什么都行，别太离谱，我可不是有钱人。

5088.cn: 感情受挫后心灰意懒之际；反弹时
5088.e: She married him on the rebound and regretted it within a year.  她失恋后草率嫁给了他，不到一年就后悔了。

5089.e: The old village is gone beyond recall, buried under the new reservoir.  那个老村庄已无法找回，淹没在新水库下面。

5090.i: be on/at the reˈceiving end (of sth) (informal)
5090.cn: 成为（不快之事的）承受者
5090.e: Nobody wants to be on the receiving end of one of his lectures.  谁都不想成为他训人的对象。

5091.cn: 养精蓄锐；休整恢复精力
5091.e: A week by the sea should help you recharge your batteries properly.  在海边待一周应该能让你好好恢复精力。

5092.i: a recipe for diˈsaster, sucˈcess, etc.
5092.cn: 招致灾难（或成功等）的做法
5092.e: Cheap parts and a rushed deadline are a recipe for disaster.  劣质零件加上赶工期，是招致灾难的组合。

5093.e: Hard work plus a little luck is her simple recipe for success.  努力加上一点运气，就是她朴素的成功秘诀。

5094.e: Two more wins would put us back in the reckoning for the title.  再赢两场，我们就重新有望争冠。

5095.cn: 算总账的日子；清算之日
5095.e: The day of reckoning came when the auditors opened the second set of books.  审计员翻开第二套账本时，清算的日子到了。

5096.i: change, alter, etc. beyond/out of (all) recogˈnition
5096.cn: 变得认不出来；面目全非
5096.e: The waterfront has changed beyond all recognition since I last visited fifteen years ago.  自我十五年前上次来，滨水区已面目全非。

5097.e: The old mill was altered out of all recognition when they turned it into flats.  老磨坊改成公寓后完全变了样。

5098.i: be/go on ˈrecord • put sth on ˈrecord
5098.e: The mayor went on record saying he would never raise local taxes.  市长公开表示绝不会提高地方税。

5099.cn: 仅供记录在案；为准确起见
5099.e: Just for the record, I never agreed to pay for the repairs.  说明一下，我从没答应过承担修理费。

5100.e: Off the record, the minister admitted the whole scheme was in serious trouble.  私下里，那位大臣承认整个方案陷入了大麻烦。

5101.cn: 记录在案的；有正式记载的
5101.e: That was the hottest summer on record since measurements began in this city.  那是本市有记录以来最热的夏天。

5102.cn: 澄清误解；说明事实真相
5102.e: Let me set the record straight: I resigned, I wasn't sacked.  我澄清一下，我是辞职，不是被开除。

5103.e: The shop has been in the red every month since the new supermarket opened.  自从新超市开业，这家店月月亏损。

5104.i: not have a red ˈcent (AmE, informal)
5104.e: By the end of the trip I didn't have a red cent left.  旅行结束时我身上一分钱都没剩。

5105.e: Hospitals across the county were on red alert as the blizzard moved in.  暴风雪来袭时，全郡医院都进入了紧急戒备。

5106.i: (as) red as a ˈbeetroot (BrE) (AmE (as) red as a ˈbeet) (informal)
5106.cn: 满脸通红（因难堪、生气或觉得热）
5106.e: He went as red as a beetroot when she mentioned his old nickname.  她一提他的旧外号，他脸就红得发烫。

5107.e: They rolled out the red carpet for the visiting delegation from Japan.  他们隆重接待了来访的日本代表团。

5108.e: There were plenty of red faces when the mistake appeared on the front page.  错误上了头版，不少人都很尴尬。

5109.cn: 转移注意力的话题（或事物）
5109.e: The missing key turned out to be a red herring in the investigation.  那把丢失的钥匙原来是调查中的一个幌子。

5110.e: Another quarter of red ink and the board will start closing branches.  再亏一个季度，董事会就要关闭分店了。

5111.e: Publishing looks genteel, but it's red in tooth and claw underneath.  出版业看着斯文，骨子里却残酷无情。

5112.i: (like) a red rag to a ˈbull (BrE)
5112.cn: 肯定会激怒某人的事物
5112.e: Mentioning the referee to my uncle is like a red rag to a bull.  在我叔叔面前提裁判，无异于火上浇油。

5113.i: (AmE like waving a red flag in front of/at a ˈbull)
5113.cn: 必定激怒某人的事物；火上浇油
5113.e: Bringing up her ex is like waving a red flag at a bull.  提她前男友就像拿红布逗牛，准惹她发火。

5114.e: We waited eight months for the permit, buried in bureaucratic red tape.  我们等许可证等了八个月，全被繁文缛节耽误了。

5115.e: I saw red when he blamed the accident on my daughter.  他把事故怪到我女儿头上，我一下就火了。

5116.cn: 可弥补缺点的优点；可取之处
5116.e: The flat is tiny, but the huge balcony is its one redeeming feature.  房子很小，但大阳台是它唯一的可取之处。

5117.cn: 值得纪念的日子；有特殊意义的一天
5117.e: The day her son graduated was a real red-letter day for the family.  儿子毕业那天对全家来说是个值得纪念的日子。

5118.e: Their hotel turned out to be right in the middle of the red-light district.  他们的酒店竟然就在红灯区正中间。

5119.cn: 恢复平衡；重新做到公平合理
5119.e: Hiring more women engineers would help redress the balance in the department.  多招些女工程师有助于扭转部门的失衡。

5120.e: The old actress lived out her final years in reduced circumstances near Brighton.  这位老演员晚年在布莱顿附近过着拮据的生活。

5121.e: After the business failed they had to live in reduced circumstances for years.  生意失败后，他们过了好些年的拮据日子。

5122.e: I'm writing with reference to your advertisement in Saturday's local paper.  我来信是关于贵方在周六本地报纸上的广告。

5123.i: reflect well, badly, etc. on sb/sth
5123.cn: 使显得好（或坏）；给人某种印象
5123.e: The way the staff handled the complaint reflects well on the whole company.  员工处理投诉的方式给整个公司加了分。

5124.e: He basks in reflected glory every time his daughter wins another swimming medal.  女儿每次拿游泳奖牌，他都跟着沾光。

5125.i: a sad, poor, etc. reflection on sth
5125.cn: 有损…名誉的事；反映出…的不足
5125.e: The state of these classrooms is a sad reflection on our education budget.  这些教室的状况反映出我们的教育经费有多可怜。

5126.e: On mature reflection, I've decided not to accept the job in Berlin.  经过慎重考虑，我决定不接受柏林那份工作。

5127.e: Let me refresh your memory — you promised to return the ladder last spring.  我提醒你一下，你答应去年春天还梯子的。

5128.e: The court must have regard to the child's welfare above everything else.  法院必须首先顾及孩子的福祉。

5129.e: With regard to your complaint, we have already contacted the delivery company.  关于您的投诉，我们已联系了配送公司。

5130.e: Sales have improved, and in this regard the new website has helped enormously.  销售有所好转，在这一点上新网站帮了大忙。

5131.e: As regards pay, the union and the management are still far apart.  至于薪酬，工会和资方分歧仍然很大。

5132.e: Repairing the roof will cost somewhere in the region of five thousand pounds.  修屋顶大概要花五千英镑左右。

5133.e: He walks his dog past our window at seven, regular as clockwork.  他七点准时遛狗经过我们窗前，从不例外。

5134.cn: 对…不加约束；放手让…去做
5134.e: The editor gave her free rein to write about whatever she liked.  编辑放手让她想写什么就写什么。

5135.e: Try giving full rein to your imagination instead of just following the instructions.  试着放开想象力，别只照着说明走。

5136.i: keep a tight ˈrein on sb/sth
5136.e: The new manager keeps a tight rein on spending in every single department.  新经理对各部门开支管得很紧。

5137.cn: 重复劳动做无用功；重新发明轮子
5137.e: Use the template we already have; there's no need to reinvent the wheel.  用现成的模板吧，没必要重复造轮子。

5138.e: Relatively speaking, this winter has been mild compared with the last one.  相对而言，今年冬天比去年暖和。

5139.cn: 突然变得虔诚；皈依宗教
5139.e: My cousin got religion after his accident and now volunteers at the church.  我表哥出事后突然信教，现在在教堂做义工。

5140.cn: 给点厉害瞧瞧；惩罚（尤指体罚）
5140.e: The bouncer gave him something to remember him by outside the club.  保安在夜店门口给了他点厉害瞧瞧。

5141.e: She will be remembered as the teacher who changed how we taught reading.  她会作为改变我们阅读教学方式的老师被人铭记。

5142.cn: 与…大相径庭；与…毫不相干
5142.e: His version of events is far removed from what the witnesses actually saw.  他的说法与目击者所见大相径庭。

5143.e: Talking about the trial again would only reopen old wounds for her family.  再谈那场官司只会让她家人重揭旧伤。

5144.e: The flood damaged the piano beyond repair, so we finally gave it away.  洪水把钢琴泡得无法修复，我们最后送人了。

5145.i: in good, bad, etc. reˈpair (also in a good, bad, etc. state of reˈpair) (formal)
5145.cn: 状况良好（或不佳等）；保养得如何
5145.e: The cottage is old but the roof and windows are in good repair.  这小屋虽旧，但屋顶和窗户保养得不错。

5146.e: Always keep a bit of cash in reserve for emergencies like this one.  总要留点现金备用，以应对这种急事。

5147.cn: 驻留的；（在大学等）有正式职位的
5147.e: The flag shows that the Queen is in residence at the castle today.  旗帜表明女王今天正驻跸城堡。

5148.e: The company is liable in respect of all damage caused by its lorries.  公司须对其卡车造成的一切损失负责。

5149.cn: 恕我直言（委婉表示不同意）
5149.e: With all due respect, minister, that figure simply doesn't match our own data.  恕我直言，部长，那个数字与我们的数据对不上。

5150.e: With respect to delivery times, we can offer a same-day service locally.  关于送达时间，本地我们可提供当日送达服务。

5151.cn: 一视同仁；不分高低贵贱
5151.e: Illness is no respecter of persons; it strikes rich and poor alike.  疾病不分贵贱，穷人富人都难幸免。

5152.e: He says the repairs cost two hundred pounds — and the rest!  他说修车花了两百镑，远不止吧！

5153.e: She brought maps, snacks, spare socks and all the rest of it.  她带了地图、零食、备用袜子等等一大堆东西。

5154.e: The pendulum finally came to a stop and hung completely at rest.  钟摆终于停了下来，一动不动地垂着。

5155.e: The runaway trolley rolled downhill and came to rest against a lamp post.  失控的手推车滑下坡，撞在路灯柱上停住了。

5156.e: The kitchen needs work; for the rest, the house is in decent shape.  厨房需要整修，除此之外房子状况还不错。

5157.i: (why don't you) give it a ˈrest! (BrE, spoken)
5157.e: Give it a rest! You've complained about that neighbour all evening.  消停会儿吧，你抱怨那个邻居一整晚了。

5158.e: I'm giving running a rest until my knee stops hurting properly.  膝盖不疼了我再跑步，先歇一阵。

5159.i: I ˌrest my ˈcase (spoken, law or humorous)
5159.cn: 我陈述完毕；我的话说完了
5159.e: He arrived late again — I rest my case about his timekeeping.  他又迟到了，关于他守不守时，我不必多说了。

5160.e: Rest assured that your parcel will arrive well before the weekend.  请放心，您的包裹周末前肯定送到。

5161.cn: 后来的事大家都知道了
5161.e: We met at a bus stop in the rain, and the rest is history.  我们在雨中的公交站相遇，后来的事就不用说了。

5162.cn: 吃老本；躺在功劳簿上不思进取
5162.e: One good season is no reason to rest on your laurels.  一个赛季打得好，不是躺平吃老本的理由。

5163.e: In retrospect, turning down that job was the best decision I ever made.  现在回想，拒掉那份工作是我做过的最好决定。

5164.cn: 立即回复；下一班邮件即回
5164.e: Please send the signed contract back to us by return of post.  请在收到后立即将签好的合同寄回。

5165.e: She fed their cat and got a bottle of wine in return.  她帮忙喂猫，得到了一瓶葡萄酒作为回报。

5166.e: He praised my cooking, so I returned the compliment about his garden.  他夸我做饭好，我就回夸他的花园。

5167.cn: 重返原团体（尤指宗教或政治团体）
5167.e: After ten years abroad, the old striker has returned to the fold.  在国外踢了十年后，这位老前锋回归了母队。

5168.i: pay sth back/return sth with ˈinterest
5168.e: They humiliated him last season, and yesterday he returned it with interest.  上赛季他们羞辱了他，昨天他加倍奉还。

5169.cn: 令人大开眼界；出乎意料
5169.e: Living without a car for a year came as a revelation to me.  一年不开车的生活让我大开眼界。

5390.e: You said it! This job is way harder than anyone warned us about.  可不是嘛！这活儿比谁说的都难得多。

5391.cn: 打擦边球；冒险行事（近乎违法）
5391.e: He sails close to the wind with his taxes, and one day he'll get caught.  他在报税上老打擦边球，早晚得栽跟头。

5392.i: the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob
5392.cn: 极大的耐心；圣人般的耐性
5392.e: You need the patience of a saint to teach thirty toddlers all day.  带三十个小娃娃上一整天课，得有圣人般的耐性。

5393.i: je ne sais quoi /ˌʒə nə seɪ ˈkwɑː/ (from French, often humorous)
5393.e: Her cooking has a certain je ne sais quoi that restaurant chefs can never copy.  她做的菜有种说不清的味道，大厨都学不来。

5394.i: for God's, heaven's, pity's, etc. ˈsake
5394.cn: 看在上帝的分上；天哪；行行好
5394.e: For God's sake, turn that music down, I'm trying to sleep here!  行行好，把音乐关小点，我还想睡觉呢！

5395.i: (Some people find the use of God here offensive.)
5395.cn: 有人认为这里用 God 一词含冒犯意
5395.e: For heaven's sake, watch your language in front of my grandmother.  拜托，在我奶奶面前说话注意点。

5396.cn: 为其本身的缘故；因其自身价值
5396.e: He studies history for its own sake, not to pass any exam.  他学历史纯粹是喜欢，不是为了考试。

5397.i: for the sake of sb/sth • for sb's/sth's sake
5397.e: They stayed together for the sake of the children, though both were miserable.  两人都过得难受，却为了孩子勉强没分开。

5398.cn: 为了便于讨论；姑且假定
5398.e: For the sake of argument, let's say the train is delayed by two hours.  姑且假定火车晚点两个小时吧。

5399.cn: 年少不谙世事的岁月；青葱年华
5399.e: In my salad days I thought I could change the world overnight.  年轻不懂事那会儿，我以为一夜之间就能改变世界。

5400.cn: 待售；供出售（尤指由物主出售）
5400.e: The house next door has been for sale for almost a year now.  隔壁那房子挂牌卖了快一年了。

5401.e: Tickets go on sale this Friday, so set an alarm on your phone.  票周五开售，手机上定个闹钟吧。

5402.cn: 诚实可靠的人；社会中坚
5402.e: Our neighbours drove me to hospital at midnight — they're the salt of the earth.  邻居半夜开车送我去医院，真是难得的好人。

5403.i: take sth with a pinch of ˈsalt
5403.e: Take his fishing stories with a pinch of salt; he always exaggerates the size.  他那些钓鱼故事听听就好，鱼多大他从来都往大了说。

5404.e: Uncle Sam takes a big slice of every paycheck I earn here.  在这儿挣的每份工资，山姆大叔都要拿走一大块。

5405.cn: 乐善好施的人；见义勇为者
5405.e: Some good Samaritan found my wallet and posted it back to me.  有位好心人捡到我的钱包，还寄了回来。

5406.e: It rained all weekend, but we had a great time all the same.  整个周末都在下雨，可我们还是玩得很开心。

5407.e: Same again, please, and get one for yourself while you're there.  照旧再来一杯，你也给自己来一杯吧。

5408.e: 'I hate Mondays.' 'Same here, especially when the alarm goes off early.'  “我讨厌星期一。”“我也是，尤其闹钟还响得早。”

5409.cn: 你也一样（回应问候或辱骂）
5409.e: 'Merry Christmas!' 'And the same to you, love — see you next year.'  “圣诞快乐！”“也祝你快乐，明年见。”

5410.e: The builder fixed the leak to my satisfaction, so I paid him immediately.  师傅把漏水修得让我很满意，我当场就付了钱。

5411.e: The minister announced a face-saving compromise minutes before the vote was due.  部长在表决前几分钟宣布了一个保全面子的折中方案。

5412.cn: 救某人（或自己）一命；使摆脱困境
5412.e: He lied to the boss just to save his own skin.  他为了自保，居然对老板撒谎。

5413.i: save sb or yourself from a dangerous or difficult situation
5413.cn: 使某人（或自己）脱离危险或困境
5413.e: She testified against her partner to save her own neck in court.  她在法庭上指证同伙，就是为了保住自己。

5414.cn: 在最后一刻脱险；及时解围
5414.e: The fire alarm rang and I was saved by the bell before answering.  火警响了，我还没回答就被解了围。

5415.cn: 唯一可取之处；可弥补缺点的优点
5415.e: The film was dull, but the soundtrack was its one saving grace.  电影很闷，配乐算是唯一的亮点。

5416.cn: 处世机敏；应付裕如的本领
5416.e: He handled the angry customers with real savoir faire and everyone left smiling.  他应付那些恼火的顾客游刃有余，人人都是笑着走的。

5417.i: as they ˈsay (also as the saying ˈgoes)
5417.e: Money can't buy happiness, as they say, but it certainly helps a lot.  常言道钱买不来幸福，不过确实帮得上大忙。

5418.i: before you can say Jack ˈRobinson (old-fashioned)
5418.e: She grabbed the last cake before you could say Jack Robinson.  说时迟那时快，最后一块蛋糕就被她抢走了。

5419.e: Let everyone have their say before we vote on the new schedule.  在表决新排班之前，让大家都说说自己的看法。

5420.i: have something, nothing, etc. to ˈsay for yourself
5420.cn: 能（或不能）为自己的行为辩解
5420.e: You're three hours late — have you nothing to say for yourself?  你迟到了三个小时，就没什么话要说吗？

5421.e: I must say, that was the best curry I've eaten in years.  我得说，这是我这几年吃过最好的咖喱。

5422.e: I wouldn't say no to a cold beer after all that digging.  挖了这么半天，来杯冰啤酒我可不会拒绝。

5423.e: We're two goals down, but never say die — there's still half an hour.  我们落后两球，可别泄气，还有半小时呢。

5424.e: His plan was ambitious, not to say completely impossible for a small team.  他的计划很有野心，对小团队来说甚至可以说是天方夜谭。

5425.e: Everyone squeeze in and say cheese — I want one photo without blinking.  大家挤紧点，笑一个，我想拍张没人眨眼的。

5426.e: You want to leave early because of the match? Say no more, mate.  你要为看球早走？不用说了，明白。

5427.e: Let him say his piece, then we can all go home.  让他把话说完，然后大家就能回家了。

5428.e: Say what? You drove all the way to Chicago without a map?  你说什么？你没带地图就一路开到芝加哥？

5429.cn: 够了请说一声（倒饮料时用）
5429.e: I'm pouring the wine now, so say when and I'll stop.  我在倒酒了，够了你就说一声。

5430.e: Just say the word and I'll drive over to help you move.  你只要说一声，我就开车过去帮你搬家。

5431.e: He's a night owl, that is to say he never wakes before noon.  他是个夜猫子，也就是说中午前从不起床。

5432.cn: 至少可以说；说得客气些
5432.e: The hotel was disappointing, to say the least, and the staff were rude.  那家酒店说得客气些也让人失望，服务员还没礼貌。

5433.e: The trip cost a fortune, to say nothing of the time we wasted.  这趟旅行花了一大笔钱，更别提浪费的时间了。

5434.i: ˌwhat would/do you ˈsay (to sth/doing sth)?
5434.cn: 你觉得…怎么样；你愿意吗
5434.e: What do you say to a walk along the river before dinner tonight?  今晚饭前沿河边走走，你觉得怎么样？

5435.e: Whatever you say — I'm too tired to argue about paint colours tonight.  随你吧，今晚我累得懒得为墙漆颜色争。

5436.e: Who can say how long this rain will last in the mountains?  谁知道山里这场雨要下多久呢？

5437.e: Who's to say she wouldn't have won if she'd trained a bit harder?  谁说得准呢，她要是再多练点也许就赢了。

5438.i: he, she, etc. wouldn't say ˌboo to a ˈgoose
5438.e: My brother wouldn't say boo to a goose, yet he became a lawyer.  我弟弟胆小得不敢跟人红脸，却当上了律师。

5439.cn: 说得太对了；我完全同意
5439.e: 'This queue is ridiculous.' 'You can say that again — we've waited an hour.'  “这队排得离谱。”“可不是嘛，都等一小时了。”

5440.i: you can't say ˈfairer (than ˈthat) (BrE, spoken)
5440.e: I'll knock fifty pounds off — you can't say fairer than that, mate.  我给你便宜五十镑，这够公道了吧。

5441.cn: 不会吧；真的吗（亦表毫不意外）
5441.e: You don't say! I'd never have guessed he was afraid of heights.  真的吗？我可看不出他还恐高。

5442.e: It goes without saying that we'll cover your travel costs for the interview.  不用说，面试的路费我们会给你报销。

5443.e: 'Will you keep this confidential?' 'That goes without saying, obviously.'  “这事你会保密吧？”“那还用说。”

5444.cn: 这说明不了什么；没什么了不起
5444.e: He's the tallest in the family, but that's not saying much really.  他是家里最高的，不过这也说明不了什么。

5775.e: His new job title doesn't sit comfortably with the way he actually behaves.  他的新头衔跟他的实际做派实在不搭。

5776.e: Who are you to sit in judgement on how I raise my own kids?  你凭什么对我怎么带孩子指手画脚？

5777.cn: 对某人妄加评判；褒贬某人
5777.e: The committee loves to sit in judgment over people who never asked for advice.  委员会最爱对没求教的人评头论足。

5778.e: Stop sitting on the fence and tell us which candidate you actually support.  别再骑墙了，说说你到底支持哪个候选人。

5779.cn: 原地不动；静观事态变化
5779.e: Just sit tight until the storm passes and the roads reopen again.  先待着别动，等风暴过去道路重开。

5780.e: With two job offers in hand, she's sitting pretty for the first time.  手握两个录用通知，她头一回这么有底气。

5781.e: He finished the whole novel in one sitting and forgot to eat dinner.  他一口气读完整本小说，晚饭都忘了吃。

5782.cn: 易受攻击的人或物；活靶子
5782.e: Parked out in the open, the old truck was a sitting duck for thieves.  停在空地上，那辆旧卡车成了小偷的活靶子。

5783.e: The archaeologists left the pottery in situ and photographed everything before digging.  考古队让陶器留在原处，开挖前先全部拍照。

5784.cn: 使某人大受打击；令某人震惊
5784.e: The news of the layoffs knocked the whole department for six.  裁员的消息把整个部门打懵了。

5785.i: it's six of ˌone and half a dozen of the
5785.e: It's six of one and half a dozen of the other; both routes take an hour.  半斤八两，两条路都得走一小时。

5786.cn: 半斤八两；两者没什么两样
5786.e: Bus or train? It's six of one and half a dozen of the other.  坐大巴还是火车？反正半斤八两。

5787.e: I'll be six feet under before I ever agree to that deal.  我死也不会答应那笔交易。

5788.e: The office was at sixes and sevens the week after the move.  搬完家那一周，办公室里乱成一团。

5789.e: Some sixth sense told her not to get into that car.  某种第六感告诉她别上那辆车。

5790.e: Who's going to pay for all this? That's the sixty-four thousand dollar question.  这钱谁出？这才是最难回答的问题。

5791.cn: 难以回答的重量级问题
5791.e: Whether he'll actually show up is the million dollar question tonight.  他到底会不会来，这才是今晚的头号悬念。

5792.i: sand dollar question for modern astronomy is ˈIs
5792.cn: 当代天文学的重大难题
5792.e: The sixty-four thousand dollar question for modern astronomy is: is anybody else out there?  当代天文学的头号难题是：宇宙别处还有生命吗？

5793.i: This phrase originated in the 1940s as ˈthe
5793.cn: 该说法源于二十世纪四十年代
5793.e: This phrase originated in the 1940s as the title of a popular American radio quiz.  这个说法源于四十年代一档美国热门广播问答节目。

5794.cn: 挫某人锐气；使有自知之明
5794.e: One bad review was enough to cut the young director down to size.  一篇差评就把这位年轻导演的傲气打没了。

5795.i: that's about the ˈsize of it (spoken)
5795.e: So we're broke until payday? Yeah, that's about the size of it.  所以发薪前我们没钱了？对，大概就这样。

5796.e: Get your skates on, the last train leaves in twelve minutes.  快点儿，末班车十二分钟后就开了。

5797.cn: 最低限度的人员；基本运转的服务
5797.e: The hospital runs on a skeleton staff over the New Year holiday.  元旦假期医院只留最低限度的值班人员。

5798.e: Every respectable family has a skeleton in the closet somewhere.  再体面的家庭也总有点不可外扬的隐情。

5799.e: After the divorce he drank himself onto skid row within two years.  离婚后他酗酒，两年就沦落街头。

5800.e: Their marriage has been on the skids since he lost the business.  自从生意垮了，他们的婚姻就一直在走下坡路。

5801.e: One leaked email put the skids under the entire merger plan.  一封外泄邮件就让整个并购计划泡了汤。

5802.e: Rich or poor, we're all brothers under the skin when disaster strikes.  灾难当头，不论贫富，人心都是一样的。

5803.e: The stray dog was nothing but skin and bone when we found him.  我们发现那只流浪狗时，它瘦得只剩皮包骨。

5804.i: do sth by the ˌskin of your ˈteeth (informal)
5804.e: She passed the driving test by the skin of her teeth.  她驾照考试险险过关。

5805.cn: 惹恼某人；让某人念念不忘
5805.e: His constant humming really gets under my skin during meetings.  他开会时不停哼歌，真把我惹毛了。

5806.i: have/put skin in the ˈgame (AmE, especially business)
5806.cn: 有切身利害；亲自投入风险
5806.e: Investors trust founders who have real skin in the game.  投资人信任那些自己也押上身家的创始人。

5807.i: it's no skin off ˈmy, ˈyour, ˈhis, etc. nose
5807.cn: 与某人无关；对某人没损失
5807.e: If they want to walk home in the rain, it's no skin off my nose.  他们想淋雨走回去，反正跟我没关系。

5808.cn: 使人毛骨悚然；让人起鸡皮疙瘩
5808.e: The way he stared at us made my skin crawl.  他那样盯着我们看，让我浑身发毛。

5809.cn: 严惩某人；扒了某人的皮
5809.e: My mum will skin me alive if she finds out I skipped class.  我妈要是发现我逃课，非扒了我的皮不可。

5810.e: You need a thick skin to survive a year in customer service.  干一年客服，你得有副厚脸皮。

5811.e: He's too thin-skinned to work in politics for very long.  他脸皮太薄，在政坛待不长久。

5812.i: eyes keep your eyes open/peeled/skinned (for sb/sth)
5812.e: Keep your eyes peeled for a red van parked near the gate.  留意一下门口附近停着的红色面包车。

5813.e: Skip it, I don't want to argue about money again tonight.  算了，今晚我不想再为钱吵。

5814.e: With her talent and drive, the sky's the limit.  凭她的天赋和拼劲，前途不可限量。

5815.i: cut sb some ˈslack (informal, especially AmE)
5815.cn: 对某人网开一面；宽容些
5815.e: Cut him some slack, it's only his second day on the job.  别太苛刻，他才上班第二天。

5816.cn: 补上空缺；充分利用闲置人力
5816.e: When two colleagues quit, the rest of us took up the slack.  两个同事辞职后，剩下的人把活儿补上了。

5817.e: With that evidence, winning the case should be a slam dunk.  有那份证据，这官司赢定了。

5818.e: The debate turned into a slanging match within about ten minutes.  辩论不到十分钟就变成了对骂。

5819.i: (a bit of) slap and ˈtickle (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
5819.e: They snuck off for a bit of slap and tickle behind the shed.  他们溜到棚子后面卿卿我我。

5820.e: Being passed over for promotion again was a real slap in the face.  又一次没能升职，真是狠狠一记耳光。

5821.e: He crashed the company car and got only a slap on the wrist.  他撞了公司的车，却只挨了轻描淡写的一句批评。

5822.i: (put sth) on the ˈslate (informal (put sth) on your account in a shop, a bar, etc.)
5822.e: Put the drinks on the slate and I'll settle up on Friday.  酒钱先记账，周五我一起结。

5823.cn: 像待宰羔羊；不知危险地前往
5823.e: The new recruits walked into that meeting like lambs to the slaughter.  新来的几个人像待宰羔羊一样进了会议室。

5824.e: He's become a slave to his phone and checks it every minute.  他成了手机的奴隶，一分钟看一次。

5825.i: be able to do sth in your ˈsleep (informal)
5825.cn: 闭着眼也会做；轻车熟路
5825.e: After ten years here, I could do this paperwork in my sleep.  干了十年，这些表格我闭着眼都能填。

5826.e: I sat cross-legged too long and my left foot went to sleep.  盘腿坐太久，我左脚麻了。

5827.i: not sleep a ˈwink ◆ not get a ˈwink of sleep
5827.e: The neighbours' party meant I didn't sleep a wink last night.  邻居开派对，我昨晚一眼没合。

5828.cn: 使麻醉；给动物实施安乐死
5828.e: The vet gently explained that we'd have to put the old dog to sleep.  兽医委婉地说，得让这条老狗安乐死了。

5829.i: sleep like a ˈlog/ˈtop (also sleep like a ˈbaby)
5829.e: After that ten-mile hike I slept like a log all night.  走了十英里山路，我一夜睡得像死猪。

5830.cn: 把某事留到第二天再决定
5830.e: Don't answer them tonight; sleep on it and call back tomorrow morning.  今晚别答复，睡一觉明早再回电话。

5831.e: Goodnight, kiddo, sleep tight and don't let the bedbugs bite.  晚安，小家伙，睡个好觉。

5832.cn: 别惹麻烦；不要旧事重提
5832.e: She's finally calmed down, so let sleeping dogs lie for now.  她好不容易消气了，这事就别再提了。

5833.i: have an ˌace/a ˌtrick up your ˈsleeve (BrE)
5833.e: Don't count him out; he always has an ace up his sleeve.  别以为他输定了，他总留着一手。

5834.i: (AmE have an ˌace in the ˈhole) (informal)
5834.e: The coach had an ace in the hole: a striker nobody had scouted.  教练藏着张王牌：一个没人考察过的前锋。

5835.cn: 暗中留着后手以备不时之需
5835.e: I've got one more argument up my sleeve if they refuse.  他们要是拒绝，我还留着一个理由。

5836.e: The budget balances only through some clever sleight of hand with the numbers.  这预算能平衡，全靠在数字上耍了点花招。

5837.e: The film is a quiet slice of life about three taxi drivers.  这部电影平静地截取了三个出租车司机的生活片段。

5838.i: best the best thing since sliced bread
5838.cn: 极好的东西；了不起的发明
5838.e: He thinks his new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.  他觉得他的新咖啡机简直是伟大发明。

5839.e: No, her comments didn't bother me in the slightest.  不，她那些话我一点都不介意。

5840.e: He told the reporters to sling their hook and slammed the door.  他叫记者们滚开，砰地关上了门。

5841.e: She endured the slings and arrows of tabloid gossip for years.  她多年忍受小报流言的种种中伤。

5842.i: ˈthe slings and arrows of outrageous fortune'.
5842.cn: 命运无情的摧残（出自《哈姆雷特》）
5842.e: Hamlet asks whether to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune.  哈姆雷特问，是否该忍受命运无情的摧残。

5843.e: The thief gave the police the slip in the crowded market.  小偷在拥挤的市场里甩掉了警察。

5844.e: She let slip that they'd already chosen someone else for the job.  她说漏了嘴，他们已经另选了人。

5845.e: Sorry I missed your birthday, it completely slipped my mind.  抱歉错过你生日，我全给忘了。

5846.i: a ˈslip of a boy, girl, etc. (old-fashioned)
5846.cn: 瘦小的男孩或女孩；小不点儿
5846.e: She was just a slip of a girl when she left the village.  她离开村子时还是个瘦小的小姑娘。

5847.e: Calling her by his ex's name was an unfortunate slip of the tongue.  把她叫成前女友的名字，真是要命的口误。

5848.e: The minister slipped on a banana skin by misquoting his own report.  部长引错了自己的报告，当众出了洋相。

5849.e: He let a golden opportunity slip through his fingers last spring.  去年春天他让一个大好机会白白溜走了。

5850.e: A few faulty batteries slipped through the net during inspection.  几块次品电池在检验中漏了网。

5851.i: there's ˌmany a ˈslip (ˈtwixt ˌcup and ˈlip)
5851.cn: 事情难料；万事难十拿九稳
5851.e: The deal looks certain, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.  交易看着十拿九稳，可变数总是难免。

5852.i: before 7 oˈclock, but there's many a slip ˈtwixt cup
5852.cn: 还没到手就别高兴太早
5852.e: We should arrive before 7 o'clock, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.  我们应该七点前能到，不过意外总难免。

5853.e: Ask him a direct question and he's as slippery as an eel.  你直接问他，他就滑得像条泥鳅。

5854.e: You can trust old Frank, he's as straight as a die.  老弗兰克你尽管信，他为人正派得很。

5855.cn: 危险的下坡路；每况愈下的开端
5855.e: One skipped payment can start you down the slippery slope into debt.  漏还一期，就可能滑向负债的深渊。

5856.e: You forgot the passwords again? You must be slipping.  你又忘了密码？看来你是退步了。

5857.i: be no ˈslouch (at sth/at doing sth) (informal)
5857.e: She's no slouch at fixing engines, despite what the guys assume.  别看那些人小瞧她，修发动机她可是行家。

5858.e: He said nothing but did a slow burn all through dinner.  他一声没吭，整顿饭都在暗自窝火。

5859.e: Management asked us to go slow on hiring until spring.  管理层要求春天前放慢招聘节奏。

5860.e: Their factory is stuck in the slow lane while rivals automate everything.  对手全面自动化，他们的工厂却还在慢车道上。

5861.e: Slowly but surely, she paid off every penny of the loan.  她慢慢地却踏实地把贷款一分不差还清了。

5862.e: We slummed it in a tiny hostel to save money for flights.  我们挤在小旅舍将就，把钱省下来买机票。

5863.e: He's been smoking on the sly behind the garage for months.  他在车库后面偷偷抽了好几个月烟。

5864.e: The car's damaged but nobody was hurt, so be thankful for small mercies.  车坏了但没人受伤，该知足了。

5865.e: You know my cousin too? It's a small world.  你也认识我表哥？世界真小。

5866.cn: 感到难堪；觉得自己渺小
5866.e: His sarcastic reply in front of everyone made me feel small.  他当众那句挖苦，让我抬不起头。

5867.e: A hundred pounds is small beer compared with what they lost.  跟他们的损失比，一百英镑不值一提。

5868.e: That wedding must have cost them a small fortune.  那场婚礼准花了他们一大笔钱。

5869.cn: 小人物；无关紧要的小公司
5869.e: The police caught the small fry but the ringleaders escaped.  警方抓到的都是小喽啰，头目跑了。

5870.i: the ˈsmall print (BrE) (AmE the ˈfine print)
5870.e: Always read the small print before you sign a rental agreement.  签租房合同前一定要看清附加条款。

5871.cn: 电视屏幕（相对电影而言）
5871.e: After three blockbusters, the actor returned to the small screen.  拍完三部大片后，这位演员重回电视荧屏。

5872.e: I'm terrible at making small talk with strangers at parties.  在派对上跟陌生人寒暄，我特别不在行。

5873.e: They argued into the small hours and woke the whole building.  他们吵到后半夜，把整栋楼都吵醒了。

5874.e: Some smart alec at the back kept correcting the teacher's grammar.  后排有个自作聪明的家伙老纠正老师的语法。

5875.e: Give her the case, she's one smart cookie under pressure.  这案子交给她，她压力下特别机灵。

5876.i: the ˈsmart money is on sb/sth
5876.e: The smart money is on the underdog winning tonight's final.  内行都看好弱队赢下今晚的决赛。

5877.e: He threatened to smash my face in over a parking space.  为个车位，他扬言要打得我满脸开花。

5878.cn: 轰动之作；一炮而红的作品
5878.e: Her debut album was a smash hit across three continents.  她的首张专辑在三大洲都火得一塌糊涂。

5879.e: When he offered to pay in cash upfront, I smelled a rat.  他提出预付现金时，我就觉得不对劲。

5880.i: come up/out of sth smelling of ˈroses (informal)
5880.e: Somehow he came out of the scandal smelling of roses.  不知怎的，他从丑闻里全身而退。

5881.i: ear beam/grin/smile from ear to ear
5881.e: She was grinning from ear to ear when they handed her the trophy.  他们把奖杯递给她时，她笑得合不拢嘴。

5882.e: He was all smiles after hearing the test results.  听到检查结果后，他一脸笑容。

5883.i: blow, smash, etc. sth to smitheˈreens (informal)
5883.cn: 把某物炸得或砸得粉碎
5883.e: The old chimney was blown to smithereens in about three seconds.  那根老烟囱三秒钟就被炸得粉碎。

5884.e: Twenty years of savings went up in smoke when the business failed.  生意一垮，二十年积蓄化为乌有。

5885.cn: 障眼法；掩人耳目的手段
5885.e: The company's growth figures turned out to be pure smoke and mirrors.  这家公司的增长数字纯属障眼法。

5886.e: My grandfather smoked like a chimney right up to his eightieth birthday.  我爷爷一直抽烟抽得凶，直到八十岁生日。

5887.e: I don't believe every rumour, but there's no smoke without fire.  我不是全信谣言，可无风不起浪。

5888.cn: 无火不生烟；事出必有因
5888.e: Three people complained about him, and where there's smoke, there's fire.  三个人投诉他，无火不生烟。

5889.cn: 烟幕；掩饰真实意图的手段
5889.e: The press conference was just a smokescreen for the coming layoffs.  那场发布会不过是为裁员放的烟幕。

5890.cn: 烟幕；掩饰真实意图的说辞
5890.e: His jokes are a smokescreen to hide how nervous he really is.  他开玩笑只是烟幕，掩饰他有多紧张。

5891.e: The auditors finally found the smoking gun in an old email thread.  审计人员终于在一串旧邮件里找到了铁证。

5892.i: (as) smooth as ˈsilk (also (as) smooth as a baby's ˈbottom humorous)
5892.e: After sanding and two coats, the tabletop was as smooth as silk.  打磨加两遍漆后，桌面光滑如丝。

5893.e: Her introduction smoothed the way for our meeting with the mayor.  她的引荐为我们见市长铺平了路。

5894.e: It took two apologies to smooth the client's ruffled feathers.  道了两次歉才把客户的火气压下去。

5895.e: Traffic crawled along the motorway at a snail's pace all morning.  整个上午高速上的车都在蜗牛似地爬。

5896.e: Just email it, snail mail would take another five days.  发邮件吧，寄信还得再等五天。

5897.cn: 笑面虎；伪装成朋友的阴险小人
5897.e: He smiled at us all week, the snake in the grass.  他笑了整整一周，真是个笑面虎。

5898.e: With the new software, filing taxes is a snap.  用了新软件，报税轻而易举。

5899.e: He snapped his fingers at the waiter, which everyone found rude.  他冲服务员打响指，大家都觉得没礼貌。

5900.i: ˌsnap ˈout of it ◆ ˌsnap sb ˈout of it (informal)
5900.e: You've been moping for a week, snap out of it.  你都消沉一星期了，振作点。

5901.e: Snap to it, those boxes won't load themselves.  快点儿，那些箱子不会自己上车。

5902.e: Order whatever you want, but make it snappy, we're late.  想点什么随你，但快点，我们迟到了。

5903.e: With a newborn at home, I only sleep in snatches.  家里有新生儿，我只能断断续续地睡。

5904.e: Fans got a sneak preview of the film two weeks before release.  影迷在上映前两周看了内部试映。

5905.cn: 不可小看；值得认真对待
5905.e: A ten per cent discount is not to be sneezed at.  九折优惠可不能小看。

5906.i: when A ˈsneezes, B catches a ˈcold (also if A)
5906.cn: 甲有风吹草动，乙就跟着遭殃
5906.e: When Wall Street sneezes, the rest of the world catches a cold.  华尔街一打喷嚏，全世界就感冒。

5907.i: catches a ˈcold, B gets pneuˈmonia less frequent)
5907.cn: 甲感冒，乙就得肺炎；牵连更重
5907.e: If America catches a cold, smaller economies get pneumonia.  美国一感冒，小经济体就得肺炎。

5908.e: Let me have a good sniff around the garage before we buy it.  买之前让我把这车库仔细看一遍。

5909.i: not get a ˈsniff of sth (informal)
5909.cn: 连边都沾不上；根本得不到
5909.e: The reserves never got a sniff of the ball all afternoon.  整个下午替补球员连球都没碰到。

5910.e: Half the class has the sniffles this week.  这周班里一半人都感冒了。

5911.e: She's been in a snit since I forgot to call back.  自我忘了回电话，她就一直闹别扭。

5912.e: That sales pitch was a total snow job from start to finish.  那套推销说辞从头到尾都是蒙人的。

5913.i: not have a ˌsnowball's chance in ˈhell (of doing sth) (informal)
5913.e: We don't have a snowball's chance in hell of finishing by Friday.  我们周五前完工是绝无可能的。

5914.cn: 取胜的可能；公平的机会
5914.e: Give the kid a sporting chance and let him try the audition.  给这孩子个机会，让他去试镜吧。

5915.cn: 忙得不可开交；应接不暇
5915.e: I'm snowed under with marking until the end of term.  期末前我被批作业埋得喘不过气。

5916.e: The old cat finally snuffed it at the age of twenty.  那只老猫活到二十岁终于走了。

5917.cn: 达到标准；身体状况良好
5917.e: The kitchen wasn't up to snuff, so the inspector closed it.  厨房不达标，检查员把它关了。

5918.e: The baby's had the snuffles since the weather turned.  天一变，宝宝就一直鼻塞流涕。

5919.i: (as) snug as a bug (in a rug) (informal, humorous)
5919.e: Wrapped in two blankets, she was as snug as a bug in a rug.  裹着两条毯子，她舒服得不得了。

5920.e: His promises were so much hot air, as everyone soon discovered.  他的承诺不过是空话，大家很快就看出来了。

5921.e: The whole repair should take an hour or so.  整个维修大概要一小时左右。

5922.e: Each guest is allowed so many drinks and no more.  每位客人只能喝规定杯数，不能再多。

5923.e: We got soaked to the skin waiting twenty minutes for the bus.  等了二十分钟公交，我们浑身湿透。

5924.cn: 大发议论；发表长篇高论
5924.e: Don't mention taxes or he'll get on his soapbox again.  别提税的事，不然他又要长篇大论了。

5925.e: She sobbed her heart out in the car after the funeral.  葬礼后她在车里哭得死去活来。

5926.e: He turned up with another sob story about needing rent money.  他又编了套没钱交房租的苦情故事。

5927.e: I only had juice all night; I'm as sober as a judge.  我整晚只喝了果汁，清醒得很。

5928.e: He came home as drunk as a lord and fell over the doormat.  他烂醉如泥地回家，绊在门垫上摔倒了。

5929.i: put a ˈsock in it (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
5929.e: Put a sock in it, some of us are trying to sleep.  闭嘴吧，有人还想睡觉呢。

5930.i: To play records more quietly, people used to
5930.cn: 旧时为把唱片放轻些的做法
5930.e: To play records more quietly, people used to stuff a sock into the horn.  旧时想让唱片声音小些，人们就往喇叭里塞袜子。

5931.i: ˈsock it to sb (informal or humorous)
5931.cn: 痛快地说给某人听；狠狠还击
5931.e: Get up there and sock it to them, they won't know what hit them.  上去给他们点厉害瞧瞧，让他们发懵。

5932.e: Her performance in the second act knocked our socks off.  她第二幕的表演把我们震住了。

5933.cn: 墨菲定律；越怕什么越来什么
5933.e: Sod's Law says it'll rain the one day I forget my umbrella.  按墨菲定律，我忘带伞那天准下雨。

5934.i: be/go soft in the ˈhead (informal, disapproving)
5934.e: Lending him money again? You must be going soft in the head.  又借钱给他？你脑子是不是坏了。

5935.i: have a soft ˈspot for sb/sth (informal)
5935.cn: 对某人或某物情有独钟
5935.e: She's tough with everyone but has a soft spot for the youngest apprentice.  她对谁都严，唯独偏爱最小的学徒。

5936.cn: 省事的选择；轻松的出路
5936.e: Quitting now would be the easy option, but I'd regret it.  现在放弃是省事，可我会后悔。

5937.cn: 耐心细致的做法；温和的处理方式
5937.e: The police took a softly-softly approach with the frightened witness.  警方对那位受惊的证人采取了温和的方式。

5938.e: I'm not sold on the new logo, honestly.  说实话，新标志我不太买账。

5939.e: Through all the chaos, her support was as solid as a rock.  在一片混乱中，她的支持坚如磐石。

5940.e: He said he was a consultant or some such thing.  他说自己是顾问还是别的什么类似的职业。

5941.e: The editor clearly has something on him, or he'd have quit already.  编辑显然抓着他的把柄，不然他早辞职了。

5942.i: ing like nothing on sb (2) ˈsth
5942.e: She wants a cottage, a dog, something like that.  她想要个小屋、一条狗，诸如此类的东西。

5943.cn: 了不起的人或事；另当别论
5943.e: Honestly, that last goal in the final was really something else.  说实话，决赛最后那个进球真是绝了。

5944.i: ˈsomething like that ◆ ˌsomething like ˈsb/
5944.e: It cost three hundred pounds or something like that.  那东西花了三百英镑左右吧。

5945.i: our walk home turned out to be something of
5945.cn: 结果颇有几分（某种性质）
5945.e: Our walk home turned out to be something of an adventure in the dark.  摸黑走回家，一路上颇有几分历险的味道。

5946.cn: 某人或某物有点特别之处
5946.e: There's something about that old house that makes me uneasy.  那所老房子总有点让我心里发毛。

5947.i: a/the ˌson of a ˈbitch (also SOB especially in)
5947.e: That son of a bitch took my parking space again this morning.  那混蛋今早又抢了我的车位。

5948.i: a/the ˌson of a ˈgun (AmE, informal, spoken)
5948.e: Well, you old son of a gun, I haven't seen you in years.  嘿，你这老家伙，好多年没见了。

5949.i: (buy sth, go, etc.) for a ˈsong (informal)
5949.e: They picked up the piano for a song at a house clearance.  他们在清仓拍卖上用极低的价钱买下那架钢琴。

5950.i: make a song and ˈdance about sth (informal, disapproving)
5950.e: Don't make a song and dance about one late email.  一封邮件晚了而已，别小题大做。

5951.e: The whole team was on song in the second half.  下半场全队状态火热。

5952.e: I don't think prices will drop anytime soon.  我看短期内价格不会降。

5953.cn: 来得正是时候；差点就晚了
5953.e: The ambulance finally arrived at the scene, and none too soon.  救护车总算赶到现场，一点也不早。

5954.i: lamp in the children's room. ˈNone too soon.
5954.e: I finally fixed the lamp in the children's room. None too soon.  我总算把孩子房里的灯修好了，早该修了。

5955.cn: 说到就做到；一说就办妥
5955.e: She asked for extra chairs and, no sooner said than done, they appeared.  她要多加几把椅子，说到就做到，椅子马上就来了。

5956.e: No sooner had we sat down than the fire alarm went off.  我们刚坐下，火警就响了。

5957.e: Book the tickets, and the sooner the better.  赶紧订票，越早越好。

5958.e: Sooner or later he'll have to tell his parents the truth.  他迟早得把实情告诉父母。

5959.e: We need that decision sooner rather than later.  这个决定我们得尽早拿到。

5960.i: I, etc. would sooner do sth (than sth else)
5960.e: I'd sooner walk home than squeeze onto that bus.  我宁愿走回家，也不挤那班车。

5961.e: Don't mention the promotion, it's a sore point with her.  别提升职的事，那是她的痛处。

5962.i: stand/stick out like a sore ˈthumb (informal)
5962.e: In jeans at that black-tie dinner, he stuck out like a sore thumb.  在正装晚宴上穿牛仔裤，他显得特别扎眼。

5963.i: do sth more in ˌsorrow than in ˈanger
5963.e: She wrote the resignation letter more in sorrow than in anger.  她写辞职信更多是出于痛心而非气愤。

5964.e: I felt sorry for the driver stuck in that downpour.  我很同情那个困在暴雨里的司机。

5965.e: Stop feeling sorry for yourself and go apply for something else.  别自怨自艾了，去投别的工作吧。

5966.e: I'm sorry to say the repairs will cost more than we thought.  很遗憾，维修费比我们想的要高。

5967.i: be, feel, etc. out of ˈsorts (especially BrE)
5967.e: She's been out of sorts since the flight home.  从回国的航班下来后她就一直不太舒服。

5968.i: it takes all ˈsorts (to make a ˈworld) (saying)
5968.e: He collects vacuum cleaners? Well, it takes all sorts.  他收集吸尘器？林子大了什么鸟都有。

5969.e: We made a meal of sorts out of rice and old vegetables.  我们用米和剩菜凑合做了顿饭。

5970.e: The old porter was the soul of discretion about the guests.  那位老门房对客人的事守口如瓶。

5971.e: Cold showers in winter are supposedly good for the soul.  冬天冲冷水澡据说对身心有好处。

5972.i: like, love, etc. the ˌsound of your own
5972.cn: 爱听自己说话；喜欢滔滔不绝
5972.e: He just loves the sound of his own voice at these meetings.  开这种会他就爱听自己说个没完。

5973.cn: 喜欢说个没完；自我陶醉地讲话
5973.e: The chairman likes the sound of his own voice far too much.  主席太爱听自己讲话了。

5974.e: The old van's engine is still as sound as a bell.  那辆旧货车的发动机还好得很。

5975.e: By nine o'clock both kids were sound asleep.  九点钟两个孩子就睡熟了。

5976.i: sound the ˈdeath knell of sth
5976.e: Streaming sounded the death knell of the local video shop.  流媒体敲响了本地录像店的丧钟。

5977.i: be in the ˈsoup ◆ land yourself/sb in the
5977.cn: 陷入困境；使某人惹上麻烦
5977.e: If the auditors call today, we're really in the soup.  审计要是今天打电话来，我们就麻烦大了。

5978.cn: 使陷入困境；给某人惹麻烦
5978.e: His careless remark landed the whole team in the soup.  他一句失言把全队害惨了。

5979.e: She planned the wedding from soup to nuts in six weeks.  她六周内把婚礼从头到尾安排妥当。

5980.e: Calling the prize meaningless is just sour grapes.  说那奖没意义，纯属吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸。

5981.i: A fox cannot reach some grapes so he decides
5981.cn: 狐狸够不着葡萄的寓言
5981.e: A fox cannot reach some grapes, so he decides they must be sour anyway.  狐狸够不着葡萄，就认定葡萄是酸的。

5982.cn: 年轻时纵情玩乐；放荡不羁
5982.e: He sowed his wild oats in his twenties and settled down at thirty.  他二十几岁玩够了，三十岁就安定下来。

5983.i: reap you reap what you sow
5983.e: He cheated his partners for years; you reap what you sow.  他坑了合伙人多年，如今自食其果。

5984.i: in the space of a ˈminute, an ˈhour, a
5984.e: In the space of an hour the sunny sky turned black.  一小时之内，晴空就变得乌云密布。

5985.cn: 在一个上午等时段之内
5985.e: In the space of a morning she cleared the whole attic.  一个上午的工夫，她把整个阁楼清空了。

5986.i: during the period of a minute, an hour, etc.
5986.cn: 在一分钟、一小时等时段内
5986.e: Everything changed during the period of a minute on that platform.  在站台上那一分钟里，一切都变了。

5987.e: He sat staring into space long after the phone call ended.  电话挂了很久，他还坐在那儿发呆。

5988.cn: 喘息的机会；短暂的间歇
5988.e: The loan gave the shop a breathing space until Christmas.  这笔贷款让小店撑到圣诞节前有了喘息之机。

5989.e: She's got determination in spades, whatever else you say.  别的先不说，她的决心是十足的。

5990.i: put/throw a ˈspanner in the works (BrE)
5990.e: The strike threw a spanner in the works of our launch plan.  罢工把我们的发布计划全搅乱了。

5991.i: (AmE throw a (monkey) ˈwrench in the works)
5991.e: One missing signature threw a wrench in the works for weeks.  少了一个签名，事情卡了好几周。

5992.e: Dad went spare when he saw the scratch on the car.  爸看到车上的划痕，气得暴跳如雷。

5993.cn: 顾及某人感受；避免让人难过
5993.e: She lied about the painting to spare his feelings.  为了照顾他的感受，她对那幅画说了谎。

5994.i: ˌspare the ˈrod and ˌspoil the ˈchild (saying)
5994.e: My grandmother believed in spare the rod and spoil the child.  我奶奶信奉孩子不打不成器那一套。

5995.i: a ˌspare ˈtyre (BrE) (AmE a ˌspare ˈtire)
5995.e: Six months of desk work gave him a definite spare tyre.  伏案六个月，他腰上明显长出一圈赘肉。

5996.e: We arrived at the airport with two hours to spare.  我们到机场时还富余两个小时。

5997.cn: 将大吵一架；将闹得不可开交
5997.e: Put those two in one room and the sparks will fly.  把那两个人关一个屋里，非吵翻天不可。

5998.e: After three days of rain the river was in full spate.  下了三天雨，河水暴涨。

5999.i: no sth/nothing/not anything to ˈspeak of
5999.e: There's no traffic to speak of on that road at dawn.  破晓时那条路上几乎没什么车。

6000.i: so to ˈspeak (also ˌas it ˈwere)
6000.e: He's the family's black sheep, so to speak.  他可以说是家里的害群之马。

6001.e: The sales figures speak for themselves, no presentation needed.  销售数字不言自明，不用做汇报了。

6002.cn: 自己表达意见；亲自说明
6002.e: Let the boy speak for himself instead of answering for him.  让孩子自己说，别替他回答。

6003.i: express what you think or want yourself, rather
6003.cn: 自己表达想法而不由他人代言
6003.e: She's old enough to express what she wants herself, rather than through you.  她大了，能自己说想要什么，不必你代言。

6004.e: Boring? Speak for yourself, I loved the second half.  无聊？那是你的看法，我很喜欢下半场。

6005.cn: 高度评价某人；称赞某人
6005.e: Everyone at the clinic speaks highly of the new nurse.  诊所里人人都夸那位新来的护士。

6006.e: She's never afraid to speak her mind in front of the board.  她在董事会面前从不怕直言。

6007.e: I said the weather was fine, but I spoke too soon.  我说天气不错，结果话说早了。

6008.cn: 充分说明；很能说明问题
6008.e: His silence at the meeting spoke volumes about his real opinion.  他在会上的沉默很说明他的真实想法。

6009.cn: 与某人还说话；关系未闹僵
6009.e: After the argument they're barely on speaking terms.  吵完那一架，他们几乎不说话了。

6010.i: manner in a manner of speaking
6010.cn: 可以这么说；某种意义上
6010.e: In a manner of speaking, we're all still beginners here.  某种意义上说，我们在这儿都还是新手。

6011.e: We went down to the theatre on spec and got returned tickets.  我们碰运气去剧院，买到了退票。

6012.e: He made a spectacle of himself singing on the office table.  他站在办公桌上唱歌，出尽了洋相。

6013.i: look at, see, etc. sth through ˌrose-tinted/
6013.cn: 戴着玫瑰色眼镜看；过于乐观
6013.e: You're seeing your school days through rose-tinted glasses again.  你又在用美化的眼光回忆学生时代了。

6014.cn: 玫瑰色眼镜；过于乐观的眼光
6014.e: He views the countryside through rose-coloured spectacles, having never farmed.  他没种过地，看乡村总戴着玫瑰色眼镜。

6015.e: The spectre of another recession hangs over the whole industry.  又一场衰退的阴影笼罩着整个行业。

6016.e: The old dog showed a surprising turn of speed chasing that squirrel.  那条老狗追松鼠时突然快得惊人。

6017.cn: 了解最新情况；达到应有水平
6017.e: Can you bring me up to speed on the contract before lunch?  午饭前能跟我说说合同的最新进展吗？

6018.e: The whole class was under her spell within a week.  一星期之内全班都被她迷住了。

6019.e: They spent the night together and regretted it by morning.  他们共度一夜，天亮就后悔了。

6020.e: Wait a second, I need to spend a penny before we leave.  等一下，走之前我得去趟洗手间。

6021.cn: 已失去影响力的人或团体
6021.e: Critics wrote the party off as a spent force after the election.  选举过后，评论者认定该党已成强弩之末。

6022.i: spick and ˈspan (also ˌspic and ˈspan)
6022.e: She keeps that little kitchen spick and span every single day.  她天天把那间小厨房收拾得干干净净。

6023.cn: 在某人饮料中偷加酒或药
6023.e: Someone spiked her drink at the party and she blacked out.  有人在派对上往她饮料里下了东西，她昏了过去。

6024.e: Announcing the merger early spiked their guns completely.  提前宣布合并，把他们的算盘全打乱了。

6025.e: Don't let him near the party plans, he'll spill the beans.  别让他知道派对安排，他准说漏嘴。

6026.e: No cause is worth spilling innocent blood for.  没有哪种主张值得让无辜者流血。

6027.e: Two drinks in and he spilled his guts to a total stranger.  两杯下肚，他就跟陌生人掏了心窝子。

6028.i: ink much ink has been spilled (on/over sth)
6028.cn: 对某事著述甚多；笔墨已耗费不少
6028.e: Much ink has been spilled over who really wrote the play.  关于这剧本究竟出自谁手，已有大量笔墨。

6029.e: The sudden inspection put the whole office in a flat spin.  突击检查把整个办公室搞得手忙脚乱。

6030.e: We're just spinning our wheels until the budget is approved.  预算批下来之前，我们只是在空转。

6031.e: Save yourself some wheel-spinning and go straight to the library.  别再白费工夫了，直接去图书馆吧。

6032.e: He spun us a yarn about missing his train again.  他又编了套没赶上火车的说辞。

6033.i: unlikely stories of their adventures, which is be sb's ˌspiritual ˈhome
6033.e: Paris was always her spiritual home, even before she lived there.  巴黎一直是她的精神家园，尽管她还没住过。

6034.e: A shiver ran down my spine when the lights went out.  灯一灭，我脊背发凉。

6035.i: (do sth) as/if/when the spirit ˈmoves you
6035.e: He paints only when the spirit moves him, sometimes twice a year.  他兴致来了才画画，有时一年才两次。

6036.e: I can't attend the funeral, but I'll be with you in spirit.  我去不了葬礼，但心与你同在。

6037.i: get/enter into the ˈspirit of sth
6037.e: Everyone entered into the spirit of the costume party.  大家都投入到化装派对的气氛里去了。

6038.e: I meant to go running, but the spirit is willing and the flesh is weak.  本想去跑步，无奈心有余而力不足。

6039.e: So you'll take the exam again next month? That's the spirit!  这么说你下个月再考一次？这才对嘛！

6040.i: be in high/low ˈspirits (also in good/poor ˈspirits)
6040.e: She's been in low spirits since the results came out.  成绩出来后她一直情绪低落。

6041.e: The two of them finally got spliced after eleven years together.  他俩在一起十一年，总算结婚了。

6042.e: You want ninety, I said seventy; let's split the difference.  你要九十，我说七十，折中一下吧。

6043.e: The vote split the committee right down the middle.  这次表决把委员会分成了对半的两派。

6044.cn: 吹毛求疵；在细节上纠缠
6044.e: Stop splitting hairs and tell me whether it works.  别抠字眼了，就说它管不管用。

6045.e: For a split second I thought the car would hit us.  有那么一瞬，我以为车要撞上我们了。

6046.e: We split our sides watching him try to assemble that shelf.  看他装那个架子，我们笑得肚子疼。

6047.cn: 把票分投给不同党派的候选人
6047.e: Plenty of voters here split the ticket rather than back one party.  这里很多选民不专投一党，而是分票。

6048.i: reminding voters that they may ˈsplit their ticket"
6048.cn: 提醒选民可以分票投给不同党派
6048.e: The notice reminded voters that they may split their ticket in November.  通知提醒选民十一月可以分票投给不同党派。

6049.i: in the November election, unlike a state primary
6049.cn: 在十一月大选中（与州初选不同）
6049.e: You can split your ticket in the November election, unlike a state primary.  十一月大选可以分票，州初选则不行。

6160.e: Mind your step on those wet stairs, someone slipped there this morning.  下那几级湿台阶小心点，今早还有人在那儿滑倒了。

6161.i: one step forward, two steps ˈback (saying)
6161.cn: 进一步，退两步；进展反复
6161.e: Fixing this app feels like one step forward, two steps back every single week.  修这个应用感觉每周都是进一步退两步。

6162.e: She stays one step ahead of her rivals by testing new ideas early.  她总是早早试验新点子，因此比对手领先一步。

6163.cn: 一步一步地；循序渐进地
6163.e: He explained the recipe step by step until even I could follow it.  他一步一步讲这道菜，连我都跟得上了。

6164.cn: 顶替；临时接替他人工作
6164.e: When the pianist fell ill, a student stepped into the breach at short notice.  钢琴师病了，一个学生临时顶了上来。

6165.e: She'll step into her boss's shoes when he retires next spring.  等老板明年春天退休，她就接他的班。

6166.i: ˈstep on it (also step on the ˈgas especially in AmE) (informal)
6166.e: Step on it, or we'll miss the last train home tonight.  快开，不然今晚末班车就赶不上了。

6167.i: step out of ˈline •be/get out of ˈline
6167.e: Step out of line once more and you'll be off the team.  再出格一次你就会被踢出队。

6168.e: The council took steps to reduce traffic near the school after several accidents.  出了几次事故后，市政会采取措施减少学校附近的车流。

6169.e: Most people would quit, but Ana is made of sterner stuff than that.  换了别人早不干了，可安娜没那么容易被打倒。

6170.e: Dad's in a stew about the wedding seating plan again this evening.  今晚老爸又为婚礼座位安排的事急得团团转。

6171.cn: 为某事坐立不安；心烦意乱
6171.e: Don't get yourself into a stew over one bad exam result.  别为一次考砸了就把自己急得心慌意乱。

6172.i: let sb ˈstew (in their own juice) (informal)
6172.cn: 让某人自作自受；听其自食其果
6172.e: He lied to us, so let him stew in his own juice for now.  他骗了我们，先让他自作自受吧。

6173.e: I got a lot of stick from my mates for that haircut.  就因为那个发型，我被哥们儿狠狠奚落了一顿。

6174.e: The fans gave the referee stick for missing an obvious foul.  裁判漏判了一个明显犯规，球迷把他骂惨了。

6175.e: The robber waved his gun and shouted 'Stick 'em up!' at the cashier.  劫匪挥着枪冲收银员大喊：举起手来！

6176.e: The car's wheels stuck fast in the mud after two days of rain.  下了两天雨，车轮牢牢陷在泥里。

6177.e: That final scene really sticks in my mind days after the film.  电影看完好几天了，最后那场戏还印在我脑子里。

6178.e: Apologizing to him really stuck in my throat, but I did it.  向他道歉实在让我咽不下这口气，但我还是道了。

6179.e: I'll stick my neck out and say we'll win the contract.  我就冒险说一句：这份合同我们拿定了。

6180.e: She stuck to her guns and refused to lower the price.  她坚持自己的立场，拒不降价。

6181.i: a rod/stick to beat sb ˈwith
6181.e: Those old emails gave his critics a stick to beat him with.  那些旧邮件成了对手攻击他的把柄。

6182.e: They live out in the sticks, an hour from the nearest shop.  他们住在偏僻乡下，离最近的商店都有一小时车程。

6183.e: At sixty he upped sticks and moved to a village in Spain.  六十岁时他收拾东西搬到了西班牙的一个村子。

6184.cn: 手脚不干净；爱偷小东西
6184.e: Watch the new intern, because word is that he has sticky fingers.  留神那个新实习生，据说他手脚不干净。

6185.e: We're on a sticky wicket asking for more money after missing the deadline.  误了期限还要加钱，我们的处境很不利。

6186.i: be on a ˌsticky ˈwicket (BrE, informal)
6186.e: Don't be too confident about the contract; we're on a sticky wicket now.  别对合同太有把握，我们现在处境很被动。

6187.e: The towels froze on the line and came in stiff as a board.  毛巾在晾衣绳上冻住了，收进来硬得像块板。

6188.e: He sat stiff as a poker through the whole awkward interview.  整场尴尬的面试他都坐得直挺挺的。

6189.e: After that phone call she poured herself a stiff drink and sat down.  接完那通电话，她给自己倒了杯烈酒坐了下来。

6190.e: He kept a stiff upper lip even when the news was devastating.  即便消息如此沉重，他也不动声色。

6191.e: The band formed in 1975 and is still going strong today.  这支乐队 1975 年成立，如今依然活跃。

6192.e: In the still of the night you can hear the river clearly.  夜深人静时，能清清楚楚听见河水声。

6193.e: The still small voice of conscience kept him awake most of the night.  良心的低语让他大半夜没睡着。

6194.cn: 静水流深；沉默者未必浅薄
6194.e: He barely speaks, but still waters run deep and he notices everything.  他话很少，可静水流深，什么都逃不过他的眼睛。

6195.e: The offer sounds great, but there's a sting in the tail: no refunds.  这优惠听着不错，可后头有个坑：概不退款。

6196.i: take the ˈsting out of sth
6196.cn: 减轻痛苦；使不那么难受
6196.e: A small bonus took the sting out of losing the promotion.  一笔小奖金冲淡了没能升职的失落。

6197.e: Parents kicked up a stink about the sudden change to school hours.  学校突然改上课时间，家长们大闹了一场。

6198.e: His uncle is stinking rich and owns three houses by the sea.  他叔叔富得流油，海边有三套房子。

6199.cn: 慷慨地做；不遗余力地做
6199.e: She gave her time without stint to the neighbourhood clinic for years.  多年来她毫无保留地把时间投入社区诊所。

6200.e: Her resignation caused quite a stir in the office that morning.  那天上午她辞职的事在办公室引起了不小的轰动。

6201.cn: 使人热血沸腾；激起热情
6201.e: The old marching song still stirs the blood of everyone in the hall.  那首老进行曲仍让全场的人热血沸腾。

6202.e: Stir your stumps, you two, or we'll be late for the ferry.  你们俩快点动身，不然赶不上渡轮了。

6203.i: not have a stitch ˈon •without a stitch ˈon
6203.e: He ran out of the sauna without a stitch on and everyone laughed.  他一丝不挂地从桑拿房跑出来，大家都笑翻了。

6204.e: Fix that small leak now, because a stitch in time saves nine.  趁漏得还小赶紧修，小洞不补大洞吃苦。

6205.e: His impression of the boss had us all in stitches for ages.  他学老板的样子把我们笑得半天直不起腰。

6206.e: Sorry, that model is out of stock until the end of the month.  抱歉，那款要到月底才有货。

6207.e: After the layoffs I took stock of my career and changed direction.  裁员之后我重新审视了自己的职业，换了方向。

6208.e: She padded downstairs in her stockinged feet so nobody would wake up.  她只穿袜子轻手轻脚下楼，怕吵醒别人。

6209.e: The studio has two more films on the stocks for next year.  这家制片厂明年还有两部片子在筹备中。

6210.e: The deer stood stock-still until the car finally drove past.  那头鹿一动不动，直到汽车终于开过去。

6211.e: After the scandal he had no stomach for another election campaign.  丑闻之后，他再没心思去打一场选战。

6212.i: turn sb's ˈstomach •make sb's ˈstomach turn
6212.e: The smell in that kitchen was enough to turn your stomach.  那间厨房的味道足以让人恶心。

6213.e: Never take these pills on an empty stomach or you'll feel sick.  这些药千万别空腹吃，不然会难受。

6214.e: The schedule isn't set in stone, so tell me if it clashes.  日程还不是定死的，冲突了就告诉我。

6545.cn: 某事该归功（或归咎）于某人
6545.e: We have Maria to thank for getting the whole project back on schedule.  整个项目能重回正轨，全靠玛丽亚。

6546.i: I'll thank you (not) to do sth • I'll thank you for sth
6546.cn: （恼火地要求）请你（不要）做某事
6546.e: I'll thank you not to comment on my cooking until you've tried it.  没尝之前，请你别对我的菜指手画脚。

6547.i: (Some people find the phrase thank God offensive.)
6547.cn: 有人认为 thank God 一语含冒犯意
6547.e: Some people find the phrase thank God offensive, so she avoids it at work.  有人觉得 thank God 冒犯人，所以她在单位不说。

6548.e: You should thank your lucky stars that nobody was hurt in that crash.  那场车祸没伤到人，你该谢天谢地。

6549.i: he, she, etc. won't ˈthank you for sth
6549.cn: 某人不会为此感激你；某人会因此生气
6549.e: Dad won't thank you for waking him up at six on his day off.  休息日六点把爸叫醒，他可不会谢你。

6550.e: We finished on time, and that was no thanks to the printing company.  我们按时完工了，这可不是印刷厂的功劳。

6551.e: Thanks to her quick thinking, the fire was out before anyone panicked.  多亏她反应快，火在大家慌乱前就扑灭了。

6552.e: He talked about budgets, deadlines and all that for a solid hour.  他讲了整整一小时预算、期限之类的东西。

6553.e: She bought a second-hand bike, and a rusty one at that.  她买了辆二手自行车，而且还是生了锈的。

6554.cn: （表示不害怕或不相信）是吗；当真
6554.e: 'I could have you fired.' 'Is that so? Go ahead and try.'  「我能让你卷铺盖。」「是吗？你试试看。」

6555.e: He never called back, not that I was really expecting him to.  他一直没回电话，倒也不是说我真指望他回。

6556.cn: 真有意思；说得妙；（讥讽）说得真好
6556.e: 'He says he's too busy to help.' 'That's a good one — he watches TV all day.'  「他说忙得没空帮忙。」「说得真好，他整天看电视。」

6557.e: Sign here, hand in your badge, and that's about it — you're done.  这里签字，交回工牌，就这样，你可以走了。

6558.cn: （事情已定）就这么定了；就这样吧
6558.e: You're not going to the party on a school night, and that's that.  上学日晚上不许去派对，就这么定了。

6559.cn: 他们和我们；（对立的）两派之分
6559.e: The new pay rules created a real them and us feeling in the office.  新的薪酬规定让办公室里真有了「他们和我们」的隔阂。

6560.e: The repair cost me two thousand pounds and then some.  这次维修花了我两千英镑，还不止。

6561.e: In theory the trains run every ten minutes, but I've waited half an hour.  理论上火车十分钟一班，可我等了半小时。

6562.cn: 头脑不太正常；神志不清
6562.e: The old man mutters at lamp posts; I don't think he's quite there.  那老人对着路灯自言自语，我看他脑子不太正常。

6563.e: After the divorce, my sister was there for me every single day.  离婚以后，我姐姐每天都陪在我身边。

6564.cn: （强调拒绝或满意）就是这样，没什么可说的
6564.e: I'm not sharing my sweets with you, so there!  我不把糖分给你，就这样！

6565.i: (do sth) there and ˈthen • (do sth) then and ˈthere
6565.e: He read the offer, liked it, and signed the contract there and then.  他看完报价很满意，当场就把合同签了。

6566.e: She heard the news and booked a flight home then and there.  她一听到消息，当场就订了回家的机票。

6567.i: ˌthere you ˈare (also ˌthere you ˈgo) (spoken)
6567.e: There you are — one black coffee and a croissant, just as you ordered.  给你，一杯黑咖啡和一个牛角包，跟你点的一样。

6568.e: There you go again, blaming the weather for your own laziness.  你又来这一套，自己懒还怪天气。

6569.cn: （表示赞同）说得没错；确实如此
6569.e: 'At least the rain kept the crowds away.' 'There is that, I suppose.'  「起码下雨把人群挡住了。」「这倒也是。」

6570.cn: 情况就是这样；事实如此
6570.e: The funding was cut and the club closed; but there it is, nothing we can do.  经费砍了，俱乐部关门，事情就是这样，我们无能为力。

6571.i: (and/but/so) there you ˈgo • (and/but/so) there we/you ˈare
6571.cn: 情况就是这样；事实如此
6571.e: He never apologized and he never will, but there you go.  他从没道歉，也永远不会，事情就是这样。

6572.cn: （绝好的例子）这才是；这才称得上
6572.e: She cycled forty miles in the rain to visit him — there's devotion for you.  她冒雨骑车四十英里去看他，这才叫真心。

6573.i: ˈthere's a good boy, girl, dog, etc. (informal)
6573.cn: （赞扬或鼓励小孩、动物）乖，好孩子
6573.e: Finish your vegetables, there's a good boy, and then you can play.  把菜吃完，乖孩子，然后就能去玩了。

6574.e: He wants fame without effort, and therein lies the whole problem.  他想不劳而获出名，问题就在这里。

6575.i: give sb/get a thick ˈear (BrE, informal)
6575.e: Say that to your grandmother again and you'll get a thick ear.  你再对奶奶那样说话，就要挨耳光了。

6576.i: in the ˈthick of sth/of doing sth
6576.cn: 在…最紧张（或最忙）的时候
6576.e: Don't call him now; he's in the thick of moving house this week.  别现在给他打电话，他这周正忙着搬家。

6577.e: Once the story broke, the phone calls came thick and fast all night.  消息一出，电话整晚接连不断地打来。

6578.cn: 过从甚密；非常亲密（常令人生疑）
6578.e: Those two have been as thick as thieves since they shared an office.  他俩自从同一间办公室起就形影不离。

6579.i: (as) thick as two short ˈplanks (informal) (also (as) thick as ˈshit ⚠, slang) (BrE)
6579.e: He's as thick as two short planks, but he's honest and works hard.  他笨得要死，可是老实肯干。

6580.cn: thick 在非正式场合可表示愚蠢
6580.e: In British slang, thick means 'stupid', so avoid calling a colleague that.  英式俚语里 thick 是「笨」的意思，别这么说同事。

6581.e: I woke up with a thick head after just two glasses of red wine.  才喝了两杯红酒，我醒来就头昏脑涨。

6582.cn: 不顾艰难险阻；甘苦与共
6582.e: She stood by her brother through thick and thin for thirty years.  三十年来她与弟弟同甘共苦，不离不弃。

6583.i: like a ˌthief in the ˈnight
6583.e: Winter arrived like a thief in the night and froze all the pipes.  冬天来得悄无声息，把水管全冻住了。

6584.cn: 盗亦有道；坏人之间也讲义气
6584.e: Neither burglar named the other, proving there is honour among thieves.  两个窃贼谁也没供出对方，可见盗亦有道。

6585.i: appear, etc. out of thin ˈair
6585.e: A taxi appeared out of thin air just as the rain got heavier.  雨下大的时候，一辆出租车凭空冒了出来。

6586.e: Joking about the boss's divorce means you're skating on thin ice.  拿老板离婚开玩笑，你可是在冒险。

6587.e: He's only thirty but already getting a bit thin on top.  他才三十岁，头顶就已经有点稀疏了。

6588.e: My keys were on the table and then vanished into thin air.  我的钥匙本来在桌上，后来就凭空不见了。

6590.e: She eats like a horse but stays as thin as a rake.  她饭量惊人，人却还是瘦得像根竹竿。

6591.i: the thin ˌend of the ˈwedge (especially BrE)
6591.e: Charging for water at the gym is the thin end of the wedge.  健身房连水都收费，这只是个开头。

6592.e: Whether he resigned or was pushed, it amounts to the same thing.  他是辞职还是被赶走，结果都一样。

6593.i: be just the ˈthing (also be the very ˈthing less frequent)
6593.e: A hot bowl of soup is just the thing after a long walk in the cold.  在寒风里走了半天，一碗热汤正合适。

6594.cn: 不见得是坏事；或许是好事
6594.e: It's no bad thing that the meeting was cancelled; we all needed a break.  会议取消倒不是坏事，大家都该歇歇。

6595.cn: 境遇不错；处于有利形势
6595.e: Rent-free flat and a company car — she's onto a good thing there.  免租的公寓加公司配车，她这日子过得可真不错。

6596.i: can/could teach/tell sb a ˈthing or two
6596.cn: 能教某人不少东西；懂得比某人多
6596.e: That old fisherman could teach the experts a thing or two about tides.  那位老渔民在潮汐上能教专家不少东西。

6597.i: a close/near ˈthing • a close-run ˈthing (informal)
6597.e: We caught the last train, but it was a close thing.  我们赶上了末班车，不过真是好险。

6598.cn: 做自己喜欢的事；自行其是
6598.e: After she quit the bank, she moved to Lisbon and did her own thing.  从银行辞职后，她搬到里斯本，过起了自己想要的生活。

6599.i: for ˈone thing, ... (, and for aˈnother, ...)
6599.cn: 一来…（二来…）；一方面…（另一方面…）
6599.e: I'm not going: for one thing it's too far, and for another it's expensive.  我不去，一来太远，二来太贵。

6930.cn: 不加证实就相信；凭信任接受
6930.e: I took his story on trust, but it turned out to be completely false.  我当时轻信了他的说法，结果全是假的。

6931.i: trust ˈyou, ˈhim, ˈher, etc. (to do sth) (spoken, informal)
6931.cn: （言行一贯如此）管保；就知道会这样
6931.e: Trust him to show up late on the most important day of all.  就知道他会在最要紧的日子迟到。

6932.e: If truth be told, I never really liked that job in the first place.  说实话，我从一开始就不喜欢那份工作。

6933.e: She smiled politely, but in truth she was furious about the whole thing.  她礼貌地笑着，其实心里对整件事气坏了。

6934.e: He survived three plane crashes, which proves truth is stranger than fiction.  他从三次空难中生还，可见现实比小说更离奇。

6935.e: Keep lying if you like, but the truth will out sooner or later.  你尽管撒谎，真相迟早会大白。

6936.e: After retiring, he tried his hand at painting and turned out to be good.  退休后他试着画画，居然画得不错。

6937.cn: 试探某人的底线；耍花招
6937.e: The kids always try it on with their grandmother because she never says no.  孩子们总跟奶奶蹬鼻子上脸，因为她从不拒绝。

6938.e: I thought I would try my luck at the audition, even without any training.  我想去试镜碰碰运气，虽然一点儿也没受过训练。

6939.cn: 使人不耐烦；让人忍无可忍
6939.e: That child really tries my patience with his endless questions at bedtime.  那孩子睡前没完没了地问问题，真让我受不了。

6940.e: She did her damnedest to finish the report before the midnight deadline.  她拼了命想在午夜截止前写完报告。

6941.cn: 并非不努力；已经尽力了
6941.e: We never won the contract, though not for lack of trying on our part.  我们始终没拿到合同，但并不是我们不努力。

6942.e: Their family business went down the tubes after the second lockdown last winter.  去年冬天第二次封锁之后，他们的家族生意就垮了。

6943.e: That advert with the abandoned puppy really tugs at your heartstrings.  那个流浪小狗的广告真是特别催泪。

6944.e: He refuses to touch his forelock to anyone just because they have money.  他才不会因为谁有钱就对谁点头哈腰。

6945.e: The new manager is completely out of tune with what the staff actually want.  新经理跟员工真正的想法完全不在一个频道上。
