6946.e: The repairs ended up costing us to the tune of three thousand pounds.  这次维修最后花了我们足足三千英镑。

6947.e: Coaches with tunnel vision only care about winning and ignore player welfare.  目光狭隘的教练只在乎赢球，不管球员死活。

6948.e: A turf war broke out between the two departments over the new budget.  两个部门为新预算打起了地盘之争。

6949.e: Our plans were blocked at every turn by the local planning committee.  我们的计划处处受到当地规划委员会的阻挠。

6950.e: During the trip she was by turns excited, exhausted and terribly homesick.  旅途中她时而兴奋，时而疲惫，时而想家想得厉害。

6951.cn: 不按次序做；说话不合时宜
6951.e: Sorry if I spoke out of turn, but somebody had to say it.  抱歉我要是说了不该说的话，可总得有人说。

6952.e: You gave me quite a turn, creeping up behind me like that.  你那样悄悄溜到我身后，真把我吓了一跳。

6953.e: Each student read a paragraph aloud in turn while the others listened quietly.  每个学生依次朗读一段，其他人安静地听。

6954.e: The milk smells like it is on the turn, so do not drink it.  这牛奶闻着快坏了，别喝。

6955.cn: 翻个底朝天；翻得乱七八糟
6955.e: Burglars turned the whole flat upside down looking for cash and jewellery.  窃贼把整套公寓翻得乱七八糟，就为找现金和首饰。

6956.e: As it turned out, the meeting was cancelled and nobody bothered to tell us.  结果会议取消了，却没人想着通知我们。

6957.i: be well, badly, etc. turned ˈout
6957.e: He is always beautifully turned out, even for a casual Sunday lunch.  他总是衣着体面，哪怕只是周日的家常午饭。

6958.i: take ˈturns doing sth/to do sth (BrE also take it in ˈturns to do sth)
6958.e: We take turns doing the washing up so nobody gets stuck with it.  我们轮流洗碗，免得老落在一个人头上。

6959.i: a ˌturn-up for the ˈbook(s) (BrE, informal)
6959.e: Him passing the exam first time was a real turn-up for the books.  他一次就考过了，真是出人意料。

6960.e: The little fishing boat turned turtle in the storm, but everyone was rescued.  那条小渔船在风暴中翻了，好在人都获救了。

6961.cn: 悬而未决；孤立无援任人责难
6961.e: The company left him twisting in the wind while reporters demanded answers.  公司把他晾在那儿，任凭记者追问。

6962.cn: 在两者之间（旧式或诗体用法）
6962.e: There is many a slip twixt cup and lip, so do not celebrate yet.  没到最后关头什么都可能变，先别庆祝。

6963.i: be in two ˈminds about sth/about doing sth
6963.e: I am in two minds about accepting the job offer in Shanghai.  我对要不要接受上海那份工作还拿不定主意。

6964.i: (BrE) (AmE be of two ˈminds about sth/about doing sth)
6964.e: She was of two minds about whether to sell the old family house.  她对要不要卖掉那栋老宅一直下不了决心。

6965.i: a ˈday, ˈmoment, etc. or two
6965.e: Give me a moment or two and I will have the answer ready.  给我一会儿，我马上就能给你答案。

6966.e: The film falls between two stools: too silly for adults, too scary for kids.  这部电影两头不讨好：大人嫌幼稚，孩子嫌吓人。

6967.e: For two pins I would quit this job and move to the coast.  我真恨不得辞掉这份工作搬到海边去。

6968.e: Please do not ask me to dance, I have two left feet.  千万别叫我跳舞，我笨得要命。

6969.i: in two ˈshakes • in a ˌcouple of ˈshakes (also)
6969.e: Hang on, I will be back in two shakes with the spare keys.  等一下，我马上拿备用钥匙回来。

6970.i: in two ˌshakes of a ˈlamb's tail (old-fashioned)
6970.e: She promised to be ready in two shakes of a lamb's tail.  她保证一转眼就收拾好。

6971.i: it takes ˈtwo (to do sth) (also it takes two to ˈtango) (saying)
6971.cn: 一个巴掌拍不响；双方都有责任
6971.e: Do not blame her for the argument; it takes two to tango.  别把吵架都怪到她头上，一个巴掌拍不响。

6972.i: (there are) no two ways aˈbout it (informal)
6972.cn: 毫无疑问；没有别的说法
6972.e: There are no two ways about it, we have to cut costs now.  毫无疑问，我们现在必须削减开支。

6973.i: not have two brain ˌcells, pennies, etc. to
6973.e: He does not have two pennies to rub together, yet he still buys rounds.  他穷得叮当响，还照样请大家喝酒。

6974.e: She has not got two brain cells to rub together, but she means well.  她脑子不太够用，不过心是好的。

6975.e: One or two people complained about the noise, but most enjoyed the party.  有一两个人抱怨吵，但多数人玩得很开心。

6976.e: He always has to put in his two pennyworth at every family meeting.  每次家庭会议他都非要插上一嘴。

6977.i: (BrE) (AmE put in your two ˈcents' worth) (informal)
6977.cn: 发表意见（即使别人不想听）
6977.e: Nobody asked her, but she put in her two cents' worth anyway.  没人问她，她还是发表了一通意见。

6978.cn: 根据现有情况推断；猜出真相
6978.e: She saw them leaving together and quickly put two and two together.  她看见他俩一起出去，很快就猜出是怎么回事。

6979.i: put/stick two ˈfingers up at sb (BrE, informal)
6979.cn: 对某人做侮辱手势；表示蔑视
6979.e: The driver stuck two fingers up at me and sped off down the road.  那司机冲我做了个侮辱手势就飞驰而去。

6980.i: stand on your own two feet
6980.e: At twenty-five it is time you learned to stand on your own two feet.  都二十五了，该学着自食其力了。

6981.e: You are exhausted? That makes two of us after last night's long shift.  你累坏了？昨晚那个长班上完，我也一样。

6982.i: ˌtwo can play at ˈthat game (saying)
6982.cn: 这一套我也会；以牙还牙
6982.e: If he keeps ignoring my messages, two can play at that game.  他要是一直不回我信息，这一套我也会。

6983.i: two heads are better than ˈone (saying)
6983.cn: 人多智广；两人智慧胜一人
6983.e: Let me look at your draft too; two heads are better than one.  让我也看看你的草稿，两个人想总比一个人强。

6984.i: two ˌsides of the same ˈcoin
6984.e: Freedom and responsibility are really two sides of the same coin.  自由和责任其实是一体两面。

6985.i: two ˌwrongs don't make a ˈright (saying)
6985.cn: 以错纠错仍是错；冤冤相报无休止
6985.e: Do not key his car; two wrongs don't make a right.  别去划他的车，以错纠错还是错。

6986.e: I will skip the cinema tonight, since two's company and three's a crowd.  今晚电影我就不去了，两人成伴，三人不欢。

6987.i: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
6987.cn: 一鸟在手胜过双鸟在林
6987.e: Take the offer now, because a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.  现在就接受这个报价吧，一鸟在手胜过双鸟在林。

6988.e: He is nice enough, but he is really not my type at all.  他人挺好，可实在不是我喜欢的类型。

6989.cn: 丑小鸭（先平庸后出众者）
6989.e: She was the ugly duckling at school and is now a famous actress.  她上学时是只丑小鸭，如今成了名演员。

6990.i: ˌum and ˈaah (about sth) (also ˌhum/ˌhem and ˈhaw less frequent) (informal)
6990.e: Stop umming and aahing about the tickets and just book them today.  别再为买票支支吾吾了，今天就订吧。

6991.i: After a lot of umming and aahing, he finally
6991.e: After a lot of umming and aahing, he finally agreed to lend us the van.  他支吾了半天，终于同意把货车借给我们。

6992.e: My aunt took umbrage at not being invited to the family dinner.  我姑姑因为没被请去家宴而生了闷气。

6993.cn: 使某人措手不及；出其不意
6993.e: The question caught me unawares and I had no answer ready.  这个问题问得我措手不及，我完全没准备。

6994.cn: 明白无误地；直截了当地
6994.e: She told him in no uncertain terms that his behaviour was unacceptable.  她直截了当地告诉他，他的行为无法接受。

6995.cn: 山姆大叔（指美国或美国政府）
6995.e: Every April a big chunk of my salary goes straight to Uncle Sam.  每年四月我工资的一大块都直接交给了山姆大叔。

6996.e: He twisted my arm until I finally cried uncle and let him win.  他把我胳膊拧得生疼，我只好认输让他赢。

6997.i: in which the child has to say the word ˈuncle
6997.cn: 源自儿童游戏，认输者须喊叔叔
6997.e: It comes from a game in which the child has to say the word uncle.  这个说法源自一种游戏，孩子必须喊出叔叔这个词。

6998.cn: 无冕之王；某领域的头号人物
6998.e: For twenty years she was the uncrowned queen of British crime writing.  二十年来她一直是英国犯罪小说的无冕之王。

6999.e: We finally reached an understanding after two hours of very difficult talks.  经过两小时艰难的谈判，我们终于达成了谅解。

7000.e: I lent him the car on the understanding that he would fill the tank.  我把车借给他，条件是他要把油加满。

7001.e: My Spanish is poor, but I can usually make myself understood in shops.  我西班牙语很差，但在商店里通常能把意思说清楚。

7002.e: They discussed the bad news in an undertone so the children would not hear.  他们低声谈论那个坏消息，怕孩子们听见。

7003.cn: 在极不合适的时间（尤指太早）
7003.e: My flight leaves at some unearthly hour, so I will sleep at the airport.  我的航班时间早得离谱，我干脆在机场睡了。

7004.cn: 心烦意乱；崩溃；（计划）落空
7004.e: He completely came unglued when he heard the verdict in court.  在法庭上听到判决时，他整个人崩溃了。

7005.cn: 在极不合适的时间；大清早
7005.e: Who rings people at this ungodly hour on a Sunday morning?  谁会在周日大清早这种时候给人打电话？

7006.e: The whole crowd shouted his name in unison as he walked onto the stage.  他走上台时，全场观众齐声喊他的名字。

7007.cn: 未知数；不摸底的人或事
7007.e: The new striker is still an unknown quantity in the Premier League.  这名新前锋在英超还是个未知数。

7008.cn: 某人不知道地；瞒着某人
7008.e: Unknown to his parents, he had already dropped out of university.  他父母毫不知情，其实他早就退学了。

7009.cn: 精神失常（不负行为责任）
7009.e: The court found that he was of unsound mind when the fire started.  法庭认定起火时他精神失常。

7010.e: Their expansion plan came unstuck when the bank refused another loan.  银行拒绝再放贷，他们的扩张计划就此泡汤。

7011.i: She came unstuck in the last part of the exam.
7011.e: She came unstuck in the last part of the exam and lost thirty marks.  她在考试最后一部分栽了跟头，丢了三十分。

7012.cn: 乐意做某事；可供（出售等）
7012.e: The old cottage is up for sale again after only six months.  那座老农舍才过半年就又挂牌出售了。

7013.e: When the boss told him to work Sunday, he just shouted up yours.  老板叫他周日加班，他直接吼了一句去你的。

7014.cn: 艰难的斗争；艰巨的任务
7014.e: Getting teenagers to read books is an uphill struggle these days.  如今让青少年读书真是件难上加难的事。

7015.e: The exam season is almost upon us and nobody has started revising.  考试季近在眼前，可谁都还没开始复习。

7016.i: get, have, gain, etc. the ˌupper ˈhand (over sb)
7016.e: By the second half our team had clearly gained the upper hand.  下半场我们队明显占了上风。

7017.e: The club was once reserved for the upper crust of London society.  这家俱乐部当年只对伦敦上流社会开放。

7019.e: Every long marriage has its ups and downs, and ours is no exception.  长久的婚姻都有起有落，我们也不例外。

7020.e: Her sudden resignation really upset the apple cart just before the launch.  她突然辞职，把发布会前的安排全打乱了。

7021.e: Be patient with him, he is a bit slow on the uptake sometimes.  对他耐心点，他有时候反应是慢半拍。

7022.e: That lift has been out of use since the flood last summer.  自从去年夏天发水，那部电梯就一直停用。

7023.i: be no ˈuse (to sb) (also be of no ˈuse formal)
7023.e: A car is no use to me in a city with such good trains.  在火车这么方便的城市，车对我没什么用。

7024.e: Please tell me if these old maps are of any use to you.  这些旧地图要是对你有用，就跟我说一声。

7025.e: Fax machines went out of use in our office years ago.  我们办公室的传真机好多年前就不用了。

7026.i: I, you, etc. could use a ˈdrink, etc. (spoken)
7026.e: After that meeting I could really use a drink and a long walk.  开完那个会，我真想喝一杯，再好好走走。

7027.e: I have no use for people who criticise but never offer any help.  我最烦那种只会批评、从不帮忙的人。

7028.e: It is no use arguing with him once he has made up his mind.  他一旦拿定主意，跟他争也没用。

7029.e: You should make use of the free gym while you still live here.  趁你还住这儿，该好好用用免费健身房。

7030.e: She finally put her law degree to good use at the charity.  她终于在这家慈善机构把法律学位派上了用场。

7031.i: use your ˈhead (BrE also use your ˈloaf) (informal)
7031.e: Use your head, you cannot post a parcel without a proper address.  动动脑子，没有详细地址怎么寄包裹？

7032.i: use a ˌsledgehammer to crack a ˈnut
7032.e: Sending three lawyers over a parking fine is using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.  为张停车罚单派三个律师，纯属小题大做。

7033.i: what's the ˈuse (of doing sth)? (also what ˈuse is there (in doing sth)?)
7033.e: What is the use of saving money if you never enjoy any of it?  存钱要是从来不花，那有什么意义？

7034.e: Instead of watching me cook, make yourself useful and lay the table.  别光看我做饭，帮把手把桌子摆好。

7035.i: have your, his, its, etc. ˈuses (informal, often humorous)
7035.e: My noisy old bicycle has its uses when the buses are on strike.  公交罢工时，我那辆破自行车还挺管用。

7036.e: As usual, he arrived twenty minutes late and blamed the traffic.  照例，他晚到二十分钟，还怪路上堵车。

7037.e: The team did their utmost to finish the bridge before the rainy season.  施工队拼尽全力想在雨季前修完这座桥。

7038.cn: 脱离实际；孤立地做某事
7038.e: Designers cannot work in a vacuum; they need feedback from real users.  设计师不能闭门造车，需要真实用户的反馈。

7039.e: We searched the whole beach in vain for her missing wedding ring.  我们把整片沙滩找遍了，还是没找到她丢的婚戒。

7040.cn: 价值判断（凭主观意见的）
7040.e: Calling the film immoral is a value judgement, not a piece of criticism.  说这部电影不道德是价值判断，算不上批评。

7041.e: Try to describe what happened without making a value judgment about anyone.  尽量描述事情经过，别对任何人做价值判断。

7042.e: Do not take his promises at face value until you see a contract.  没看到合同之前，别把他的承诺当真。

7043.cn: 处于前列；处于领先地位
7043.e: This small college has long been in the van of teaching reform.  这所小学院长期走在教学改革的前列。

7044.e: His account of the accident is at variance with what the witnesses said.  他对事故的说法与目击者所讲的不一致。

7045.i: variations on the theme of sth
7045.cn: 同一事物的不同做法或说法
7045.e: Her three novels are really variations on the theme of leaving home.  她那三部小说其实都是离家主题的不同写法。

7046.i: variety is the spice of ˈlife (saying)
7046.e: Try a different route to work sometimes; variety is the spice of life.  偶尔换条路上班，生活多变才有滋味。

7047.cn: 避而不谈；回避（不快之事）
7047.e: Let us draw a veil over what happened at last year's office party.  去年公司聚会那档子事，咱们就不提了吧。

7048.i: an ˌiron ˈfist/ˈhand (in a velvet glove)
7048.e: She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.  她管理部门是笑里藏刀，手段其实很硬。

7049.cn: 猛烈地做；变本加厉地做
7049.e: The rain came back with a vengeance just as we reached the tent.  我们刚回到帐篷，雨就又猛下起来。

7050.e: He gave full vent to his anger once the customers had left.  客人一走，他就把火气全撒了出来。

7051.e: She vented her spleen in a long email she later regretted sending.  她写了封长邮件泄愤，后来又后悔发了出去。

7052.e: Apply for the scholarship anyway, nothing ventured, nothing gained.  奖学金还是申请一下吧，不试怎么知道。

7053.i: on/to the verge of sth/of doing sth
7053.e: The company was on the verge of collapse before the new investor arrived.  新投资人到来之前，这家公司濒临倒闭。

7054.e: Oil companies have a vested interest in delaying stricter climate rules.  石油公司在拖延更严的气候法规上有既得利益。

7055.cn: 棘手的问题；争论不休的问题
7055.e: The vexed question of school funding came up again at the meeting.  学校经费这个老大难问题在会上又被提了出来。

7056.e: Debt and poor health can trap families in a vicious circle.  债务和健康不佳会让家庭陷入恶性循环。

7057.e: Hundreds of small shops fell victim to the new shopping centre.  上百家小店都成了那家新购物中心的牺牲品。

7058.e: She bought the old barn with a small guesthouse in view.  她买下那座旧谷仓，心里打算开个小民宿。

7059.e: In view of the weather, we have decided to postpone the picnic.  考虑到天气，我们决定把野餐推迟。

7060.e: Her early sketches are on view at the museum until the end of May.  她的早期素描在博物馆展出到五月底。

7061.i: take a dim/poor ˈview of sb/sth
7061.e: My boss takes a dim view of people checking their phones in meetings.  我老板很不喜欢开会时有人看手机。

7062.e: The committee takes the view that the current rules are too strict.  委员会认为现行规定过于严苛。

7063.i: the ˈvillain of the piece (especially humorous)
7063.e: The villain of the piece turned out to be a faulty kitchen socket.  罪魁祸首原来是厨房里一个坏插座。

7064.e: She got the job by virtue of her long experience in the field.  她凭着在这行的多年经验拿到了这份工作。

7065.e: With no car, he made a virtue of necessity and cycled everywhere.  没车，他索性顺水推舟，到哪儿都骑车。

7066.e: Nobody thanked her for helping, but virtue is its own reward.  没人谢她帮忙，可行善本身就是回报。

7067.e: What is our position vis-a-vis the new safety rules from Brussels?  就布鲁塞尔的新安全规定而言，我们是什么立场？

7068.i: be in good, poor, etc. ˈvoice
7068.e: The tenor was in fine voice despite his terrible cold last night.  尽管重感冒，昨晚那位男高音的嗓子依然很棒。

7069.e: The report gives voice to workers who are rarely asked anything.  这份报告替那些很少被问及意见的工人发了声。

7070.e: Keep your voice down, the baby has only just fallen asleep.  小声点，宝宝刚睡着。

7071.cn: 让别人听到自己的意见
7071.e: Parents marched to the town hall to make their voices heard.  家长们游行到市政厅，为的是让自己的声音被听见。

7072.cn: 无人理会的呼声或警告
7072.e: For years he was a voice in the wilderness warning about the dam.  多年来他关于大坝的警告一直无人理会。

7073.e: The residents spoke with one voice against the new motorway plan.  居民们异口同声反对新的高速公路方案。

7074.e: The minister performed a complete volte-face on the tax proposal.  这位大臣在税收提案上来了个一百八十度大转弯。

7075.e: If we cannot agree, we will simply put the matter to the vote.  要是谈不拢，我们就直接把这事付诸表决。

7076.e: The head teacher gave a short vote of thanks to all the volunteers.  校长向全体志愿者致了简短的谢词。

7077.cn: 用脚投票；以离开表示不满
7077.e: Customers voted with their feet when the shop raised its prices again.  店里又涨价，顾客们用脚投了票。

7078.e: Walking into that hotel lobby gave me a strong sense of déjà vu.  走进那家酒店大堂，我有种强烈的似曾相识感。

7079.e: He has been on the wagon since his doctor saw the test results.  自从医生看了化验结果，他就一直戒着酒。

7080.e: She always collects waifs and strays and feeds them at Christmas.  她总把无家可归的人聚起来，圣诞节请他们吃饭。

7081.i: I, he, etc. can't ˈwait • I, he, etc. can
7081.e: I cannot wait to see their faces when we tell them the news.  我等不及想看他们听到消息时的表情。

7082.e: The children could hardly wait for the school holidays to begin.  孩子们盼着放假，一天也等不了了。

7083.e: We will just have to wait and see what the doctor says tomorrow.  我们只能等着瞧明天医生怎么说。

7084.cn: 稍等；（下文出人意料）听好了
7084.e: He turned up late and, wait for it, asked us to pay for lunch.  他迟到了，你听好了，还让我们请他吃午饭。

7085.e: Wait a minute, I think we have taken the wrong turning again.  等一下，我觉得咱们又拐错弯了。

7086.e: She waited tables at a diner while studying for her nursing degree.  她一边读护理学位，一边在小餐馆当服务员。

7087.e: Wait till you taste my mother's dumplings, you will forget the restaurant.  等你尝了我妈包的饺子，就把饭馆忘了。

7088.e: Just you wait, I will beat you at chess one of these days.  你等着瞧，总有一天我下棋能赢你。

7089.i: an ˌaccident/a diˌsaster waiting to ˈhappen
7089.e: That broken staircase is an accident waiting to happen.  那段坏楼梯迟早要出事。

7090.e: Sorry to keep you waiting, the earlier meeting ran on and on.  抱歉让你久等了，前一个会一直拖着没散。

7091.e: The buyers are playing a waiting game, hoping the price will drop.  买家在打拖延战，盼着价格降下来。

7092.e: The taxi is here and the tickets are booked, so what are we waiting for?  出租车到了，票也订好了，我们还等什么？

7093.e: The form takes five minutes, so what are you waiting for?  表格五分钟就填完了，你还在等什么？

7094.e: Food prices rose sharply in the wake of the summer drought.  夏季干旱之后，食品价格猛涨。

0.e: She spends two hours a day just getting from A to B in traffic.  她每天光是堵在路上从一处赶到另一处就要两小时。

1.e: He knows this old engine from A to Z, so let him fix it.  这台老发动机他门儿清，让他修吧。

2.e: I was taken aback by how rude the waiter was to my mother.  服务员对我妈那么无礼，我简直惊呆了。

3.cn: 正要做某事；即将做某事
3.e: I was about to call you when your message popped up on my screen.  我正想给你打电话，你的消息就跳出来了。

4.cn: （询问情况或提出建议）怎么样
4.e: We've tried everything else, so how about asking your brother for help?  别的法子都试过了，找你哥帮忙怎么样？

5.cn: （表示惊讶或赞叹）是吗；太妙了
5.e: She got the scholarship on her first try — how about that, then!  她第一次申请就拿到奖学金了，你说妙不妙！

6.i: not be about to do sth
6.cn: 不愿做某事；无意做某事
6.e: I'm not about to lend him money again after what happened last time.  出了上次那事，我可不打算再借他钱。

7.e: Milk, bread, a bag of rice — that's about it for the shopping list.  牛奶、面包、一袋米，购物清单就这些了。

8.e: Above all, remember to lock the back door before you leave tonight.  最要紧的是，今晚走之前记得锁后门。

9.e: Staying up all night with the patient was above and beyond her normal duties.  整夜守着病人，远远超出了她的分内职责。

10.e: Ever since his promotion he's been getting a bit above himself.  自从升职以后，他就有点儿不知天高地厚了。

11.cn: 了解…的最新情况；跟上…的发展
11.e: As a nurse she has to keep abreast of the latest research on infections.  当护士就得随时了解感染方面的最新研究。

12.i: ˌabsence makes the heart grow ˈfonder (saying)
12.cn: 离别情更浓；小别胜新婚
12.e: They text all day now he's abroad — absence makes the heart grow fonder.  他出国后两人整天发消息，真是小别胜新婚。

13.e: He asked for three months' leave of absence to look after his sick father.  他申请了三个月假期去照顾生病的父亲。

14.e: I found the old photo album by accident while clearing out the attic.  我清理阁楼时偶然翻出了那本旧相册。

15.e: Whether by accident or design, his email went to the whole company.  不管是无心还是有意，他那封邮件发给了全公司。

16.cn: 故作意外地；假装无意地
16.e: She accidentally on purpose left her number on his desk.  她故作无意地把电话号码留在了他桌上。

17.e: Don't cry over the broken vase, sweetheart — accidents will happen.  别为打碎的花瓶哭了，宝贝，意外总是难免的。

18.e: Nobody pushed him; he handed in his resignation of his own accord.  没人逼他，辞职信是他自己主动交的。

19.e: To the manager, our objections were clearly of no account at all.  在经理看来，我们的反对意见根本无足轻重。

20.i: on ˈno account •not on ˈany account
20.e: On no account should you open that door while the machine is running.  机器运转时你决不能打开那扇门。

21.e: She quit the agency and started trading on her own account last spring.  去年春天她离开中介，开始自己单干做买卖。

22.e: He put his years in the kitchen to good account when he wrote the book.  写这本书时，他把多年的厨房经验用了个够。

23.i: take sth into acˈcount •take account of sth
23.e: We must take rising prices into account when we plan next year's budget.  做明年预算时我们一定要把物价上涨考虑进去。

24.cn: 人各有所好；好恶无从解释
24.e: He put ketchup on his noodles — well, there's no accounting for taste.  他往面条上浇番茄酱，唉，人各有所好吧。

25.e: By all accounts the new manager is much easier to work with.  据大家说，新来的经理好相处多了。

26.e: He waited until the last minute of the meeting to play his ace.  他一直等到会议最后一刻才打出王牌。

27.i: within an ace of sth/of doing sth (BrE)
27.e: Our team came within an ace of winning the championship last night.  昨晚我们队差一点点就拿下冠军了。

28.i: have/hold (all) the ˈaces (also hold all the ˈcards)
28.e: With three job offers in hand, she holds all the aces in this negotiation.  手握三个录用通知，这场谈判她占尽优势。

29.cn: 致命弱点；阿喀琉斯之踵
29.e: His temper has always been his Achilles' heel in front of clients.  在客户面前，他的脾气一直是他的致命弱点。

30.i: the ˌacid ˈtest (of sth) (also the ˈlitmus test especially in AmE)
30.e: The real acid test of the new brakes will be a rainy mountain road.  这套新刹车真正的考验是雨天的山路。

31.i: make sb's acˈquaintance •make the acˈquaintance of sb
31.cn: 结识某人；与某人初次相见
31.e: I made her acquaintance at a rather boring conference in Shanghai.  我是在上海一个挺无聊的会议上认识她的。

32.e: Blue cheese is definitely an acquired taste, but now I love it.  蓝纹奶酪绝对是慢慢才吃得惯的，可现在我爱死它了。

33.cn: 严厉训斥；警告不得再犯
33.e: Dad read us the Riot Act after he saw the mess in the kitchen.  爸爸看到厨房一团糟，把我们狠狠训了一顿。

34.e: The insurer refused to pay, calling the flood an act of God.  保险公司称洪水属不可抗力，拒绝赔付。

35.e: Raising twins while finishing her thesis was a constant balancing act.  一边带双胞胎一边写论文，她天天都在走钢丝。

36.cn: （在他人成功后）插一手；参与分羹
36.e: Once the café took off, every landlord wanted to get in on the act.  咖啡馆一火，每个房东都想来插一脚。

37.e: Whenever there's washing-up to do, my brother does a disappearing act.  一到要洗碗的时候，我弟弟就消失得无影无踪。

38.e: He pulled his usual vanishing act the moment the bill arrived.  账单一送来，他又照例玩起了人间蒸发。

39.i: get your ˈact together •get sth/it toˈgether
39.cn: 振作起来；把事情安排妥当
39.e: You need to get your act together before the exams start next month.  下个月考试前你得好好振作起来。

40.cn: 更有条理；更好地安排（或管理）
40.e: Give him a week to get his shit together and he'll finish the report.  给他一周把事情理顺，报告他就能写完。

41.e: Our old teacher was so popular that she's a tough act to follow.  以前那位老师太受欢迎了，谁接手都难以企及。

42.e: Action stations, everyone — the inspectors will be here in ten minutes!  各就各位，各位，检查员十分钟后就到！

43.i: There's a bus full of tourists arriving in five
43.cn: 还有五分钟一车游客就到（例句片段）
43.e: There's a bus full of tourists arriving in five minutes, so look busy.  再过五分钟一大巴游客就到，都装忙一点。

44.e: I'd love to see the new printing press in action before we buy it.  买之前我很想看看这台新印刷机怎么运转。

45.cn: （因伤病）不能工作；（因损坏）失灵
45.e: A knee injury has put our best striker out of action for six weeks.  膝伤让我们的主力前锋六周不能上场。

46.e: Everyone wants a slice of the action now the shop is making money.  店里开始赚钱了，人人都想分一杯羹。

47.e: If you want nightlife, the harbour district is where the action is.  想找夜生活，港口区才是热闹的地方。

48.e: They set up an ad hoc committee to deal with the parking complaints.  他们成立了一个临时委员会处理停车投诉。

49.e: He repeats the same three jokes ad infinitum at every family dinner.  每次家宴他都把那三个笑话翻来覆去地讲。

50.e: The coach discussed our defensive mistakes ad nauseam after the match.  赛后教练把我们的防守失误说得人耳朵起茧。

51.e: He waved at me in the street, but I don't know him from Adam.  他在街上冲我招手，可我根本不认识他。

52.e: Bringing up her ex at dinner just added fuel to the flames.  晚饭时提起她前任，简直是火上浇油。

53.e: Grandma poured oil on troubled waters by changing the subject quickly.  奶奶赶紧换了话题，把这场争吵平息了下去。

54.cn: 雪上加霜；伤害之外又加侮辱
54.e: They cancelled my flight, then, to add insult to injury, lost my suitcase.  航班取消了，更气人的是他们还弄丢了我的箱子。

55.e: Without further ado, let me introduce tonight's very special guest.  闲话少说，我来介绍今晚这位特别嘉宾。

56.e: You have to book the tickets at least two weeks in advance.  票必须至少提前两周订。

57.cn: 利用某机会；占某人便宜
57.e: We took advantage of the sunny weather and cycled along the river.  我们趁着天气晴朗，沿着河骑了一圈车。

58.e: Learning Spanish will be to your advantage if you move to Madrid.  如果你搬去马德里，学西班牙语对你有好处。

59.e: The soft lighting shows the old paintings to great advantage.  柔和的灯光把这些旧画衬托得格外好看。

60.e: She turned her boss's mistake to her own advantage and got promoted.  她把老板的失误变成了自己的机会，还升了职。

61.e: We looked for cheaper rent further afield, out past the ring road.  我们把找便宜房租的范围扩大到了环路以外。

62.i: Journalists came from as far afield as China
62.cn: 记者远自中国等地赶来（例句片段）
62.e: Journalists came from as far afield as China and Brazil to cover it.  来采访的记者远自中国、巴西等国。

63.e: The prosecutor argued he had acted with malice aforethought that night.  检察官称他那晚是有预谋地行事。

64.e: I'm afraid the last train left about twenty minutes ago, sir.  先生，恐怕末班车二十分钟前就开走了。

65.e: The rain stopped, so we had the picnic in the garden after all.  雨停了，我们最后还是在院子里野餐了。

66.e: I told him again and again not to leave the gate open at night.  我一遍遍跟他说晚上别让大门开着。

67.e: The flat is small, but then again the rent is really cheap.  房子是小，不过话说回来，租金真便宜。

68.cn: 别孩子气；举止要与年龄相称
68.e: Stop sulking about the cake and act your age, you're forty!  别为块蛋糕生闷气了，都四十的人了，成熟点！

69.cn: 成年；达到法定年龄；发展成熟
69.e: Electric cars have really come of age in the last five years.  近五年电动车真正走向成熟了。

70.e: She's sixty but she certainly doesn't look her age at all.  她六十了，可看着一点都不像。

71.e: The bar was fined for serving drinks to underage customers.  这家酒吧因向未成年人售酒被罚款。

72.e: They lost four-three on aggregate after a dramatic second leg.  次回合跌宕起伏，他们总比分三比四出局。

73.cn: 各自保留意见；同意存异
73.e: We'll never agree about politics, so let's agree to differ.  政治上我们永远谈不拢，还是各持己见吧。

74.e: The service here has gone downhill — I couldn't agree with you more.  这儿的服务越来越差，我完全同意你的看法。

75.cn: 为支援（或帮助）某人（某事）
75.e: The whole village ran a concert in aid of the children's hospital.  全村办了一场音乐会为儿童医院筹款。

76.i: what's (all) ˈthis, etc. in aid of? (BrE, spoken)
76.cn: 这究竟是为什么；这有什么用
76.e: Balloons, cake, streamers — what's all this in aid of, exactly?  气球、蛋糕、彩带，这一通折腾究竟为哪般？

77.e: The mayor took aim at developers who leave building sites unfinished.  市长把矛头对准了那些烂尾的开发商。

78.e: She's been walking on air since she heard she got the job.  自从听说拿到那份工作，她一直乐得飘飘然。

79.cn: （想法、气氛等）在流传；即将到来
79.e: There's change in the air at the office, and everyone can feel it.  办公室里有种要变天的气氛，人人都感觉得到。

80.e: Our holiday plans are still up in the air until Dad hears about work.  爸爸的工作没定，我们的假期计划还悬着。

81.e: Careful what you say — we're back on the air in ten seconds.  说话注意点，十秒后我们就恢复直播了。

82.e: She came back from Paris full of airs and graces about food.  她从巴黎回来，一谈到吃就装腔作势。

83.e: He puts on airs at parties, but he grew up on our street.  他在派对上装模作样，其实就在我们这条街长大。

84.e: Her grandfather's workshop was an Aladdin's cave of tools and old radios.  她爷爷的工作间简直是个工具和旧收音机的宝库。

85.e: The old pub is still alive and kicking after eighty years.  这家老酒吧开了八十年，如今依旧红火。

86.e: Her funny stories really brought the history lesson alive for us.  她那些趣事让历史课一下子生动了起来。

87.cn: （话题或活动）活跃起来；变得有趣
87.e: The square comes alive at night when the food stalls open.  夜里小吃摊一开张，广场就热闹起来了。

88.e: All in all, it was a pretty good trip despite the awful weather.  总的来说，尽管天气糟糕，这趟旅行还不错。

89.e: It was a better performance all round than the one last season.  比起上赛季，这场表现全面提升。

90.e: Grandpa is ninety-two and still completely all there.  爷爷九十二了，脑子还清楚得很。

91.e: He kept going on about targets and deadlines and all that stuff.  他一个劲儿念叨指标、期限之类的事。

92.e: I didn't enjoy the film at all, and neither did my sister.  这电影我一点儿也不喜欢，我妹妹也是。

93.e: For my father, weekends are all about football and nothing else.  对我爸来说，周末就只有足球这一件事。

94.i: be all sb can/could ˈdo (not) to do sth (informal)
94.e: It was all I could do not to laugh when his wig slipped.  他假发歪了，我憋着不笑真是费了老劲。

95.i: (not) be/take all ˈday, ˈmorning, etc. (to do sth)
95.e: Don't take all day choosing a shirt; the shop closes at six.  别挑衬衫挑一整天，店里六点关门。

96.e: Hurry up and decide — I haven't got all day to stand here.  快点定吧，我可没工夫在这儿干站着。

97.i: be all for sth/for doing sth
97.cn: 完全赞成；坚信应该做某事
97.e: I'm all for letting the kids walk to school by themselves.  我完全赞成让孩子们自己走路上学。

98.e: It's been all go in the kitchen since the tour bus arrived.  旅游大巴一到，厨房里就忙得不可开交。

99.cn: 巴结某人；对某人大献殷勤
99.e: The salesman was all over us the moment we walked in.  我们一进门，销售员就围上来大献殷勤。

100.i: be all the ˈsame to sb (also be all ˈone to sb old-fashioned)
100.e: Tea or coffee, it's all the same to me this early.  这么早，茶还是咖啡对我都一样。

101.e: He thinks he's all that just because he drives a new car.  就因为开了辆新车，他就觉得自己了不得。

102.e: There were about forty people in all at the wedding lunch.  婚宴午餐一共来了大约四十人。

103.e: Here are the keys and the paperwork — it's all yours now.  钥匙和文件都在这儿，现在全归你了。

104.i: Mr Brown, ˈshe said, taking him into the class-
104.cn: 她把他带进教室时说道（例句片段）
104.e: Mr Brown, she said, taking him into the classroom, they're all yours.  她把他领进教室说：布朗先生，这些孩子交给你了。

105.i: not all that ˈgood, ˈwell, etc.
105.e: The soup smells great but it's not all that good, honestly.  汤闻着香，说实话味道并没多好。

106.i: not as ˌbad(ly), ˌtall, etc. as all ˈthat
106.cn: 没有说的那么糟（或高等）
106.e: The exam wasn't as hard as all that; I finished with time to spare.  考试没传的那么难，我还提前做完了。

107.e: Thanks for driving me home. Not at all, it was on my way.  谢谢你送我回家。不客气，顺路而已。

108.i: of ˌall the ˈcheek, ˈnerve, stupid things to
108.e: Of all the cheek, he asked to borrow my car again this morning!  真够厚脸皮的，今早他又来借我的车！

109.e: Of all the stupid things to do, he posted the photo online!  真是蠢到家了，他居然把照片发到网上！

110.cn: 发出／收到警报解除的信号
110.e: The doctors gave her the all-clear after the second scan last week.  上周第二次检查后，医生说她没事了。

111.cn: 死胡同；徒劳无功的路子
111.e: That line of research turned out to be a blind alley after two years.  两年下来，那条研究路线证明是条死胡同。

112.e: Allow me, that suitcase looks far too heavy for one person.  我来吧，那箱子一个人拎太沉了。

113.e: The editor gave the young writer free rein with the travel column.  编辑放手让这位年轻作者自由写旅行专栏。

114.cn: 体谅某人；考虑到某人的难处
114.e: You should make allowances for him; he's only been here a month.  你该体谅他，他才来了一个月。

115.e: After the partnership broke up, she decided to go it alone.  合伙散了以后，她决定自己单干。

116.e: Just leave him alone for an hour; he'll calm down on his own.  让他一个人待一小时，他自己会平静下来。

117.e: Leave that wound alone or it will never heal properly.  别老碰那个伤口，不然永远好不了。

118.e: He can't boil an egg, let alone cook dinner for eight people.  他连鸡蛋都煮不好，更别提给八个人做饭了。

119.e: Send your passport along with two recent photos to this address.  请把护照连同两张近照寄到这个地址。

120.e: As always, she arrived ten minutes early and made the coffee.  一如既往，她提早十分钟到，还煮好了咖啡。

121.i: make aˈmends (to sb) (for sth/for doing sth)
121.e: He cooked dinner to make amends for forgetting their anniversary.  他做了顿晚饭，弥补自己忘了纪念日的过失。

122.e: Pick-up trucks and county fairs are as American as apple pie.  皮卡车和乡村集市是地道的美国味儿。

123.cn: 倒也不错；正合时宜；有用
123.e: A cup of hot tea wouldn't go amiss on a night like this.  这样的夜里来杯热茶倒是不错。

124.e: Please don't take it amiss if I leave the party early tonight.  今晚我要是早走，请别见怪。

125.i: opp take sth in good ˈpart
125.cn: 不见怪地接受；一笑置之
125.e: He took the teasing about his haircut in good part.  大家拿他的发型开玩笑，他一笑置之。

126.e: The puppy ran amok in the kitchen while we were out.  我们出门时，小狗在厨房里撒了欢儿地闹。

127.e: There are any number of reasons why the deal might fall through.  这笔生意谈不成的理由多得很。

128.e: No amount of apologising will get your sister's bike back.  再怎么道歉也换不回你姐姐那辆自行车。

129.cn: 让某人开心；给某人解闷
129.e: A box of crayons kept the kids amused for the whole train ride.  一盒蜡笔让孩子们在整趟火车上都玩得开心。

130.e: In the final analysis, it comes down to whether we trust him.  归根结底，问题在于我们信不信他。

131.i: do sth more in ˈsorrow than in ˈanger
131.cn: 痛心多于气愤地做某事
131.e: She spoke to her son more in sorrow than in anger about the lies.  说起那些谎话，她对儿子是痛心多过生气。

132.e: That second-hand washing machine was the answer to our prayers.  那台二手洗衣机简直是我们的救命稻草。

133.i: not take ˌno for an ˈanswer
133.cn: 非让人答应不可；不容拒绝
133.e: Come to dinner on Sunday — and I won't take no for an answer.  周日来吃饭，别想拒绝我。

134.cn: 自以为无所不知；万事通
134.e: My nephew is sixteen and thinks he knows all the answers.  我侄子十六岁，觉得自己什么都懂。

135.e: The union raised the ante by threatening a strike before Christmas.  工会以圣诞前罢工相要挟，加大了筹码。

136.e: He's had ants in his pants all morning waiting for the results.  等成绩等得他一上午坐立不安。

137.e: The journey was anything but relaxing with three kids in the car.  车里坐着三个孩子，这趟旅程一点也不轻松。

138.cn: 怎么都行；没有任何规矩
138.e: At my aunt's house on New Year's Eve, anything goes.  除夕在我姑妈家，什么都随便。

139.cn: （用于否定或疑问）差不多；有点像
139.e: Is the sequel anything like as funny as the first film?  续集有第一部一半好笑吗？

140.i: (as) easy, clear, quick, etc. as ˈanything
140.cn: 极其容易（或清楚、迅速等）
140.e: Fixing that leak was as easy as anything once I found the valve.  找到阀门以后，修那个漏水口简单得很。

141.e: It was raining like anything when we got off the bus.  我们下车时雨下得特别大。

142.e: I wouldn't move back to that town for anything.  打死我也不搬回那个镇子。

143.e: If you need a lift or anything, just give me a ring.  要是需要搭车什么的，给我打个电话就行。

144.e: The two brothers are poles apart when it comes to money.  在花钱这件事上，兄弟俩天差地别。

145.e: The band started coming apart at the seams during the second tour.  第二轮巡演途中，乐队开始分崩离析。

146.i: After only six months, their marriage has come
146.cn: 才半年他们的婚姻就破裂了（例句片段）
146.e: After only six months, their marriage has come apart at the seams.  才过了六个月，他们的婚姻就散了架。

147.e: They served us a sad apology for a breakfast at that hotel.  那家旅馆给我们端上的所谓早餐真够寒碜的。

148.cn: 不为某事道歉；问心无愧
148.e: I make no apologies for asking hard questions at the meeting.  我在会上问了尖锐的问题，对此毫不抱歉。

149.e: They kept up appearances long after the money had run out.  钱早就花光了，他们还硬撑着面子。

150.i: the apple doesn't fall/never falls far from
150.cn: 苹果落地离树不远（谚语上半句）
150.e: Look at him arguing like his dad — the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.  瞧他跟他爸一样爱争论，真是有其父必有其子。

151.e: She paints just like her mother; the apple never falls far from the tree.  她画画跟她妈一模一样，真是一脉相承。

152.e: His youngest granddaughter has always been the apple of his eye.  小孙女一直是他的掌上明珠。

153.e: One rotten apple in the team can ruin the mood for everyone.  队里一个害群之马能坏了所有人的心情。

154.e: She left the workshop in apple-pie order before her holiday.  休假前她把工作间收拾得井井有条。

155.cn: 截然不同的事物；不可比
155.e: Comparing his novel to her poetry is apples and oranges.  拿他的小说比她的诗，根本不是一回事。

156.i: how do you like ˈthem apples? •how
156.e: I finished the whole race without walking — how do you like them apples?  全程跑下来没走一步，怎么样，服不服？

157.i: about ˈthem apples? (AmE, informal, usually spoken)
157.e: We beat the champions on their own field — how about them apples?  我们在冠军队主场赢了他们，你说厉害不厉害？

158.e: Fix the tyre and she's apples, mate, we'll be on the road again.  轮胎补好就没问题了，哥们儿，咱们又能上路了。

159.e: With teenagers, a softly-softly approach usually works better.  对青春期的孩子，温和一点的办法通常更管用。

160.e: The bookshop sent me the atlas on approval for ten days.  书店把那本地图册寄给我试看十天。

161.e: The plan finally got the council's seal of approval last Thursday.  这项计划上周四总算得到了议会的正式认可。

162.i: (tied to) your mother's, wife's, etc. ˈapron strings
162.e: At thirty he's still tied to his mother's apron strings.  三十岁了，他还事事听母亲的。

163.i: continue to disagree about a decision, especial-
163.cn: 对已定之事作无谓争执
163.e: They continue to disagree about a decision that was made years ago.  他们对多年前的决定还在争个没完。

164.i: be out of the ˈark •went out with the ˈark
164.e: That printer is out of the ark; it still uses floppy disks.  那台打印机老掉牙了，还在用软盘。

165.i: cost/pay an ˌarm and a ˈleg (informal)
165.e: Getting the roof fixed cost us an arm and a leg last winter.  去年冬天修屋顶花了我们一大笔钱。

166.cn: 与某人保持距离；不与之亲近
166.e: She keeps her colleagues at arm's length outside working hours.  下班后她跟同事保持距离。

167.i: put the ˈarm/ˈbite on sb (AmE, informal)
167.e: My cousin put the arm on me for gas money again yesterday.  我表弟昨天又找我要油钱。

168.e: He sank into the old armchair and fell asleep before the news ended.  他陷进那把旧扶手椅，新闻没播完就睡着了。

169.i: a person who knows about a subject only from
169.cn: 纸上谈兵者；坐而论道的人
169.e: He's a person who knows about sailing only from books, an armchair sailor.  他只从书上懂航海，是个纸上谈兵的水手。

170.e: The hikers arrived armed to the teeth with maps, ropes and snacks.  徒步的人带着地图、绳子和零食，装备到了牙齿。

171.cn: armour 的拼写与读音标注
171.e: The museum displays a full suit of armour from the fifteenth century.  博物馆展出了一套十五世纪的全身盔甲。

172.e: The knight's arm guard was the only piece of armour left intact.  骑士的护臂是唯一完好的盔甲部件。

173.e: Parents are up in arms about the plan to close the village school.  家长们对关闭村小学的计划强烈反对。

174.cn: 襁褓中的婴儿；天真无助的人
174.e: In business he's still a babe in arms and trusts everyone.  在生意场上他还是个雏儿，谁都信。

175.e: She has survived the slings and arrows of twenty years in politics.  她挺过了二十年政坛的种种打击。

176.e: He was stuck in traffic? My arse! He just overslept again.  他堵车了？扯淡！他不过是又睡过头了。

177.i: work your ˈarse off (BrE) (AmE work your ˈass off) (◆ slang)
177.e: I worked my arse off all summer to pay for that guitar.  整个夏天我拼命打工，就为买那把吉他。

178.i: can't be ˈarsed (to do sth) (BrE, ◆ slang)
178.e: I can't be arsed to cook tonight; let's just order noodles.  今晚我懒得做饭，叫碗面吧。

179.e: We sold nine hundred units this month as against six hundred last year.  本月售出九百台，而去年同期是六百台。

180.e: I'll deal with those emails as and when I get a free hour.  等哪会儿有空我再处理那些邮件。

181.e: As for the leftovers, just put them in the fridge for tomorrow.  至于剩菜，放冰箱里明天吃吧。

182.i: ˈas from (also ˈas of especially AmE)
182.e: As from Monday, the office will open half an hour earlier.  从周一起，办公室提前半小时开门。

183.cn: （表不信或否认）才怪；好像似的
183.e: Me, marry him? As if! We've argued every day this week.  我嫁他？才怪！这周我们天天吵。

184.e: He talks about the war as though he had actually been there.  他谈起那场战争，好像自己真去过一样。

185.e: I'd love another coffee, but as it is I'm already late.  我很想再来杯咖啡，可眼下我已经迟到了。

186.e: As to the cost, we'll discuss that after you see the plans.  至于费用，等你看过图纸我们再谈。

187.e: So I bought a boat on holiday, as you do, and now regret it.  度假时我买了条船，人之常情嘛，现在后悔了。

188.e: Riding without a helmet in this traffic is just asking for trouble.  这种车流里不戴头盔骑车纯属自找麻烦。

189.e: How was the interview? Oh, don't ask, it was a disaster.  面试怎么样？唉，别问了，一塌糊涂。

190.e: Don't ask me why he left early; he never explains anything.  别问我他为什么早走，他从来不解释。

191.cn: （表震惊）真是的；你说气不气人
191.e: He charged forty pounds for a haircut. I ask you!  剪个头发收四十镑，你说这像话吗！

192.e: If you ask me, that jacket is far too thin for winter.  依我看，那件夹克过冬太薄了。

193.e: The spare room is yours for the asking whenever you visit.  你来的时候想住客房，说一声就行。

194.cn: 玩忽职守；没留意潜在问题
194.e: The regulators were asleep at the wheel while the bank collapsed.  银行垮台时，监管机构完全在打瞌睡。

195.e: Someone was asleep at the switch when these figures were checked.  核对这些数字时，有人明显在开小差。

196.i: get your ˈass over/in ˈhere, etc. (◆ slang, especially AmE)
196.e: Get your ass over here and help me move this couch!  快给我滚过来帮忙抬沙发！

197.e: Two of the parcels went astray somewhere between Leeds and here.  有两个包裹在利兹到这儿的路上弄丢了。

198.cn: 把某人引入歧途；带坏某人
198.e: His mother blamed the older boys for leading him astray.  他母亲怪那些大孩子把他带坏了。

199.i: you could ˌcut the atmosphere with a
199.cn: 气氛极其紧张（习语前半）
199.e: You could cut the atmosphere with a knife when the two rivals met.  两个对头一碰面，气氛紧张得能拿刀切开。

200.e: At the family dinner you could cut the atmosphere with a knife.  那顿家宴上，气氛压抑得让人喘不过气。

201.e: Two doctors were in attendance throughout the long ceremony.  整场冗长的典礼上都有两名医生在场。

202.e: The teacher takes attendance every morning before the first lesson.  老师每天早上第一节课前点名。

203.e: Put your phone down — I want your undivided attention for five minutes.  把手机放下，我要你专心听我说五分钟。

204.cn: 有可靠根据；消息来源可靠
204.e: I have it on good authority that the shop is closing in June.  我有可靠消息，这家店六月要关门。

205.cn: 不假思索地做；机械地做
205.e: I was so tired I drove home on automatic pilot.  我累得糊里糊涂，一路机械地开回了家。

206.cn: 没有多大用处；无济于事
206.e: His long letters of complaint were of no avail whatsoever.  他那些长篇投诉信一点用都没有。

207.e: We searched the whole beach for her ring, to no avail.  我们把整片海滩找遍了，还是没找到她的戒指。

208.cn: 极力躲避；避之唯恐不及
208.e: Since the argument he's been avoiding me like the plague.  自从吵过之后，他躲我躲得像躲瘟疫。

209.e: As a student I stood in awe of that quiet old professor.  当学生时，我对那位安静的老教授敬畏有加。

210.e: He's at the awkward age when nothing his parents say is right.  他正处在那个别扭的年纪，爸妈说什么都不对。

211.e: He split the firewood with an old axe he found in the shed.  他用棚子里翻出的旧斧头劈柴。

212.e: She has no axe to grind; she just wants the road repaired.  她没什么私心，只是想把路修好。

213.cn: 襁褓中的婴儿；不谙世事的人
213.e: When it comes to contracts, he's still a babe in arms.  一说到合同，他还完全是个新手。

214.cn: 毫无经验的人；易受骗的人
214.e: On his first day trading he was a babe in the woods.  他做交易的头一天完全是只小白兔。

215.i: the Woods in which two children are left alone
215.cn: 《林中孩子》故事：两孩子被弃林中
215.e: The old ballad tells of two children left alone in the woods to die.  那首老歌谣讲两个孩子被丢在林中等死。

216.i: boom), especially after the Second World War
216.cn: （尤指二战后）生育高峰期出生的人
216.e: My parents were born in the boom, especially after the Second World War.  我父母就出生在二战后的生育高峰。

217.cn: 是某人的心血；归某人负责
217.e: The community garden is entirely her baby, from plan to planting.  这个社区花园从设计到种植全是她的心血。

218.i: throw the ˌbaby out with the ˈbathwater
218.cn: 把精华与糟粕一起丢掉
218.e: Scrapping the whole system throws the baby out with the bathwater.  把整套系统废掉，等于连好东西一块儿扔了。

219.e: We've put the kitchen renovation on the back burner until spring.  厨房翻新的事我们先搁到春天再说。

220.e: The kids' bikes are in back of the garage, behind the old fridge.  孩子们的自行车在车库后面，旧冰箱那边。

221.e: Her cottage is out in the back of beyond, an hour from the nearest shop.  她的小屋在鸟不拉屎的地方，离最近的商店一小时。

222.e: We watched two films back to back and forgot to have dinner.  我们连着看了两部电影，忘了吃晚饭。

223.e: His know-it-all tone really put my back up at the meeting.  他那副什么都懂的口气在会上真把我惹毛了。

224.i: get off sb's ˈback •get sb off your ˈback
224.cn: 不再纠缠某人；摆脱某人的烦扰
224.e: Just finish the report and your boss will get off your back.  把报告写完，你老板就不烦你了。

225.cn: 从此一帆风顺；蒸蒸日上
225.e: She opened the bakery in 2019 and has never looked back since.  她二〇一九年开了那家面包房，此后一路顺风。

226.cn: 全力以赴做某事；卖力干
226.e: If we all put our backs into it, we'll finish the fence today.  大家一起使把劲，今天就能把栅栏弄好。

227.cn: 不理睬；拒绝帮助；弃之不顾
227.e: He turned his back on his old friends the moment he got rich.  一发财，他就把老朋友都甩在了脑后。

228.i: a ˌbackhanded ˈcompliment (AmE also a ˌleft-handed ˈcompliment)
228.cn: 假恭维；表面赞扬实则讥讽
228.e: Saying I look rested for my age was a backhanded compliment.  说我这个年纪气色不错，这夸奖听着真别扭。

229.cn: 幕后工作的科研人员；幕后英雄
229.e: The back-room boys spent two years perfecting that tiny battery.  幕后那帮技术员花了两年才把这块小电池做好。

230.cn: 指手画脚的人；爱管闲事者
230.e: My uncle is a terrible back-seat driver on every family trip.  每次全家出游，我叔叔都在后座上指挥个不停。

231.i: bend/lean over ˈbackwards to do sth
231.e: The staff bent over backwards to find us a room that night.  那天晚上工作人员想尽办法给我们找了间房。

232.cn: 在自家后院；在身边不远处
232.e: Nobody wants a waste plant in their own backyard.  谁都不想垃圾处理厂建在自家门口。

233.i: for the nouns or verbs in the idioms, for
233.cn: 习语按其中名词或动词编排（体例说明）
233.e: Look for the nouns or verbs in the idioms, for they head each entry.  查习语要看其中的名词或动词，词条按它们排列。

234.e: He's texting her at three in the morning — he's got it bad.  凌晨三点还给她发消息，他这是陷得不轻。

235.e: The soup's not bad at all, considering I used leftovers.  用剩菜煮的汤，味道居然还不赖。

236.i: take the ˌbad with the ˈgood
236.e: Farming means taking the bad with the good, drought years included.  务农就得好坏都受着，包括旱年。

237.e: Too bad you missed the concert; the band played for three hours.  你没赶上演唱会真可惜，乐队演了三个小时。

238.e: They were badly off for years before he found steady work.  他找到稳定工作前，他们家穷了好几年。

239.e: We're badly off for chairs, so bring one if you can.  我们这儿椅子不够，你能带一把最好。

240.e: Loud clubs really aren't my bag; I'd rather sit and talk.  吵闹的夜店真不是我的菜，我宁愿坐着聊天。

241.e: They threw him out, bag and baggage, on a Sunday morning.  周日早上，他们把他连人带行李都轰了出去。

242.e: A bag lady sleeps in the church doorway most winter nights.  冬天的夜里，常有个流浪女睡在教堂门口。

243.e: The stray dog was a bag of bones when we first took him in.  我们刚收养这只流浪狗时，它瘦得皮包骨。

244.e: With two goals in ten minutes, the match was in the bag.  十分钟进两球，这场比赛稳了。

245.i: let the ˌcat out of the ˈbag
245.e: Don't let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.  惊喜派对的事你可别说漏嘴。

246.i: way out of a paper ˈbag
246.cn: （否定用法）极其无能；一无是处
246.e: He couldn't fight his way out of a paper bag, let alone win.  他连纸袋都撕不开，还想赢？

247.e: Bags I the window seat on the way back!  回程靠窗的座位归我！

248.e: She came home with a baker's dozen of eggs from the market.  她从集市带回来十三个鸡蛋。

249.e: His place on the team hung in the balance until the final trial.  直到最后一次选拔，他能否入队都还悬着。

250.cn: 使失去平衡；使措手不及
250.e: Her blunt question caught the minister completely off balance.  她那个直白的问题让部长完全乱了阵脚。

251.e: On balance, I think moving to a smaller town was the right call.  权衡下来，我觉得搬到小城是对的。

252.e: Running a shop and studying at night is quite a juggling act.  一边开店一边上夜校，真是两头兼顾不容易。

253.e: By forty my uncle was as bald as a coot and quite proud of it.  我叔叔四十岁就全秃了，还挺得意。

254.i: the whole ball of ˈwax (AmE, informal)
254.e: The rent, the bills, the repairs — she pays for the whole ball of wax.  房租、账单、维修，全都是她掏钱。

255.e: Dad went ballistic when he saw the scratch on the car door.  爸爸看到车门上的划痕，气得暴跳如雷。

256.e: Keep your phone on; when the balloon goes up we'll need everyone.  手机开着，一出事我们就得召集所有人。

257.e: Just give me a ballpark figure for the repairs before I decide.  你先给个修理费的大概数，我再决定。

258.i: be in the same/right ˈballpark (especially AmE)
258.e: Their quote and ours are in the same ballpark, so either works.  他们的报价和我们的差不多，选哪个都行。

259.e: I broke my balls on that job and still got no bonus.  那活儿我拼了老命，奖金还是没有。

260.e: The crowd went bananas when the winning goal went in.  制胜球一进，全场都疯了。

261.e: Every café jumped on the bandwagon and started selling bubble tea.  每家咖啡馆都跟风卖起了奶茶。

262.cn: 让人不得安宁的祸根；灾星
262.e: That noisy scooter outside is the bane of my existence.  外面那辆吵人的摩托简直是我的克星。

263.e: This little car gives you more bang for your buck than the newer models.  这辆小车比新款更划算。

264.e: It's pouring again — bang goes our afternoon at the beach.  又下大雨了，我们下午去海边的计划泡汤了。

265.e: Your guess about the price was bang on, to the penny.  你猜的价格分毫不差。

266.i: bang to ˈrights (BrE) (AmE dead to ˈrights)
266.e: The security camera got him bang to rights with the stolen watch.  监控把他偷表的过程拍了个正着。

267.e: The balloon went bang and the baby burst into tears.  气球砰的一声炸了，宝宝哇地哭了。

268.e: The school concert went off with a bang this year.  今年的学校音乐会办得非常成功。

269.e: She's been banging the drum for local farmers for a decade.  十年来她一直为本地农民奔走呼吁。

270.cn: 花不了多少钱；负担得起
270.e: A weekend in the countryside won't break the bank.  在乡下待个周末花不了几个钱。

271.cn: 严峻的初次考验；火的洗礼
271.e: Teaching thirty teenagers alone was a real baptism of fire.  独自面对三十个青少年，真是一场严酷的初考验。

272.e: She is the best cook in this family, bar none.  她是我们家最会做饭的，没有之一。

273.i: be all over, bar the ˈshouting
273.e: With a four-goal lead it's all over bar the shouting.  领先四球，胜负已经没有悬念了。

274.i: not have a ˈbar of sth (AustralE, New Zealand)
274.e: He wouldn't have a bar of their plan to sell the farm.  他们要卖农场，他一点也不肯掺和。

275.e: He gave me the bare bones of the story on the phone last night.  昨晚他在电话里把事情的大概跟我说了。

276.e: After two glasses of wine he bared his soul to a total stranger.  两杯酒下肚，他对一个陌生人吐尽了心事。

277.e: The dog bared its teeth as soon as we got near the gate.  我们一走近大门，那狗就龇起了牙。

278.e: He built that stone wall with his bare hands over one summer.  那道石墙是他一个夏天徒手垒起来的。

279.i: into the ˈbargain (AmE in the ˈbargain)
279.e: The flat is cheap and has a balcony into the bargain.  这套房便宜，而且还带阳台。

280.e: The unused land became their main bargaining chip in the talks.  那块闲置土地成了他们谈判的主要筹码。

281.i: not touch sb/sth with a ˈbargepole
281.cn: 唯恐避之不及；碰都不愿碰
281.e: That car's been in two crashes; I wouldn't touch it with a bargepole.  那车撞过两次，白送我都不要。

282.e: Swimming in the river in February? You're barking mad.  二月份去河里游泳？你真是疯了。

283.i: be barking up the wrong ˈtree
283.e: If you think I took your charger, you're barking up the wrong tree.  你要是以为充电器是我拿的，那可找错人了。

284.e: With no other supplier left, they've got us over a barrel.  没有别的供货商了，我们只能任他们摆布。

285.e: He spent nine years behind bars for a crime he didn't commit.  他为一桩没犯过的罪蹲了九年牢。

286.e: Your estimate of the crowd size was way off base.  你对人数的估计错得离谱。

287.cn: 迈出第一步；取得初步进展
287.e: We never even got to first base with the planning committee.  我们在规划委员会那儿连第一步都没迈出去。

288.i: have a ˈbash at (doing) sth (BrE, spoken)
288.e: I've never baked bread, but I'll have a bash at it tonight.  我从没烤过面包，今晚试试看。

289.e: The coach took us back to basics after three straight defeats.  三连败之后，教练带我们从基本功练起。

290.cn: 濒临崩溃的国家（或组织）
290.e: Ten years ago the airline was a complete basket case.  十年前这家航空公司简直是烂摊子一个。

291.e: She batted her eyelashes and he agreed to pay for lunch.  她眨了眨眼，他就答应请午饭了。

292.e: Three job offers in one week — you're batting a thousand.  一周三个录用通知，你可真是无往不利。

293.i: go to ˈbat for sb (AmE, informal)
293.e: My old boss went to bat for me when the funding was cut.  经费被砍时，我以前的老板站出来替我说话。

294.i: like a ˌbat out of ˈhell (informal)
294.e: He came out of the driveway like a bat out of hell.  他把车从车道上开出来，快得像飞一样。

295.i: not bat an ˈeyelid (BrE) (AmE not bat an ˈeye)
295.e: She didn't bat an eyelid when the bill came to two hundred pounds.  账单两百镑，她眼皮都没眨一下。

296.e: Right off the bat he told us the roof would need replacing.  他一上来就告诉我们屋顶得换。

297.e: She organised the whole fundraiser off her own bat.  这场募捐活动全是她自己张罗起来的。

298.e: We waited with bated breath for the exam results to appear.  我们屏住呼吸等着成绩公布。

299.e: Investors took a bath when the property market collapsed.  楼市崩盘时投资者亏得很惨。

300.e: Ask the driver to stop; the little one needs to go to the bathroom.  让司机停一下，小家伙要上厕所。

301.e: She poured the cold bathwater down the drain and refilled the tub.  她把凉了的洗澡水放掉，重新放了一缸。

302.i: have ˌbats in the ˈbelfry (old-fashioned, informal)
302.e: The neighbours say the old man has bats in the belfry.  邻居们说那老头有点神神叨叨。

303.e: With the audit coming, it's time to batten down the hatches.  审计要来了，该做好应对准备了。

304.cn: 战线已划定；阵营已分明
304.e: The battle lines are drawn between the residents and the developer.  居民和开发商之间已经摆开了阵势。

305.e: Bedtime with a toddler is a nightly battle of wills.  哄幼儿睡觉每晚都是一场意志的较量。

306.e: The trial turned into a long battle of wits between the two lawyers.  庭审变成了两位律师之间漫长的斗智。

307.cn: 与某人激烈交锋（或争论）
307.e: She joined battle with the council over the parking charges.  她为停车费的事和市政会杠上了。

308.e: The fox stood at bay against the wall, surrounded by dogs.  狐狸被狗围住，靠着墙做困兽之斗。

309.e: Hot soup and thick socks kept the cold at bay all evening.  热汤加厚袜子，整晚都挡住了寒气。

310.cn: 在忙着做；争论（或做得）没完
310.e: The neighbours were at it again, shouting until well past midnight.  邻居又吵上了，一直闹到后半夜。

311.e: Just be yourself at the interview and they'll like you.  面试时自然点就行，他们会喜欢你的。

312.e: If he'd rather walk home in the rain, then so be it.  他宁愿冒雨走回家，那就随他吧。

313.i: keep a beady ˈeye on sb/sth •have your
313.e: Keep a beady eye on the soup while I answer the door.  我去开门，你帮我盯着点儿汤。

314.e: She had her beady eye on the boys near the sweet counter.  她一直盯着糖果柜台旁边那几个男孩。

315.e: Winning isn't the be-all and end-all of playing football.  踢球并不是只有赢球才重要。

316.e: His guess about the cause of the fault was completely off beam.  他对故障原因的猜测完全跑偏了。

317.e: How much have you saved? Not a bean, I'm afraid.  你攒了多少钱？一分也没有。

318.cn: 首当其冲；承受主要压力
318.e: Coastal villages bore the brunt of the storm on Tuesday night.  周二夜里的风暴中，沿海村庄首当其冲。

319.e: After three years the language classes finally began to bear fruit.  三年之后，语言课终于见到了成效。

320.e: Give me a minute to get my bearings in this huge station.  这站太大了，让我先弄清方向。

321.e: We lost our bearings in the fog and ended up by the river.  我们在雾里迷了路，最后走到了河边。

322.i: beat about the ˈbush (BrE) (AmE ˌbeat around the ˈbush)
322.e: Stop beating about the bush and tell me how much it cost.  别绕弯子了，直说多少钱吧。

323.i: beat sb at their own ˈgame
323.cn: 以其人之道还治其人之身
323.e: The small shop beat the chain at its own game with cheaper prices.  小店以更低的价格在对手的强项上赢了连锁店。

324.i: beat your ˈbrains out (informal, especially AmE)
324.e: I beat my brains out for hours over that last puzzle.  最后那道谜题我想了好几个钟头，脑袋都想破了。

325.e: The team beat the bushes for a goalkeeper before the season started.  赛季开始前，球队到处找门将。

326.cn: 提前完成；抢在时限之前
326.e: We beat the clock and posted the forms ten minutes before closing.  我们赶在关门前十分钟把表格寄了出去。

327.e: Her homemade bread beats the supermarket stuff hollow.  她自己烤的面包比超市的强太多了。

328.e: The shopkeeper told the kids to beat it before he called the police.  店主叫那几个孩子快走，不然就报警。

329.i: beat a path to sb's ˈdoor
329.e: Once word got out, buyers beat a path to her door.  消息一传开，买家纷纷找上门来。

330.e: He beat the rap because the main witness never showed up.  主要证人没出庭，他就这么逃过了处罚。

331.e: When her father appeared, the boys beat a hasty retreat.  她父亲一出现，那几个男孩撒腿就跑。

332.e: Grandma beat time on the arm of her chair throughout the song.  整首歌里，奶奶都在椅子扶手上打拍子。

333.e: He forgot his own birthday party — can you beat that?  他连自己的生日会都忘了，你说奇不奇？

334.i: if you can't ˈbeat them, ˈjoin them (saying)
334.cn: 打不赢就加入；不如随大流
334.e: Everyone's cycling to work now, so if you can't beat them, join them.  现在人人骑车上班，打不过就加入吧。

335.i: a rod/stick to ˈbeat sb with
335.cn: 用来指责（或惩罚）某人的把柄
335.e: One late report became a stick to beat him with for years.  一份报告交晚了，成了多年攻击他的把柄。

336.e: We found a quiet guesthouse well off the beaten track.  我们找到一家偏僻幽静的小客栈。

337.i: take a ˈbeating (AmE also take a ˈlicking)
337.e: Our reputation took a beating after the story hit the papers.  报纸一登，我们的名声大受打击。

338.e: Her lemon cake takes some beating, and I have tried plenty.  她做的柠檬蛋糕真难有人比得上，我可吃过不少。

339.cn: 我真不明白；这可难倒我了
339.e: It beats me how he passed that exam without opening a book.  他连书都没翻就过了考试，我真想不通。

340.i: ˌbeauty is in the ˌeye of the beˈholder (saying)
340.cn: 情人眼里出西施；美丑因人而异
340.e: You hate that green sofa, but beauty is in the eye of the beholder.  你讨厌那张绿沙发，可各人审美不同嘛。

341.cn: 美貌只是表象；不可以貌取人
341.e: He's handsome but unkind — beauty is only skin-deep.  他长得帅却不厚道，美貌不过一层皮。

342.i: the beauty of sth/of doing sth
342.e: The beauty of working from home is that I skip the commute.  在家办公的妙处就是不用挤通勤。

343.e: I'm off to bed early; I need my beauty sleep before the wedding.  我早点睡了，婚礼前得睡个美容觉。

344.e: She's tired of being at her brother's beck and call every weekend.  每个周末都得随叫随到伺候哥哥，她烦透了。

345.e: I often wonder what became of the boy who sat next to me.  我常想，当年坐我旁边那男孩后来怎么样了。

346.i: be in bed with sb/sth •get into bed with
346.e: Critics say the regulator is in bed with the big banks.  批评者说监管方与大银行走得太近。

347.i: > Investors are wary of getting into bed with an
347.cn: 投资者不愿与…扯上关系（例句片段）
347.e: Investors are wary of getting into bed with an industry run by gangs.  投资者不愿和黑帮把持的行业扯上关系。

348.i: get out of bed on the wrong ˈside (BrE) (AmE
348.e: Don't mind him; he got out of bed on the wrong side today.  别理他，他今天起床气重。

349.e: She told him she wasn't going to bed with anyone on a first date.  她跟他说，第一次约会她不会跟谁上床。

350.i: have ˌmade your bed and have to ˈlie on it
350.e: He quit without a plan, so he's made his bed and has to lie on it.  他没打算就辞了职，只能自食其果。

351.e: They rarely argue, but they don't talk much in bed either.  他们很少吵架，但床上也没什么话。

352.e: Granny took to her bed for a week with a bad chest.  奶奶胸闷得厉害，卧床躺了一星期。

353.e: A rock band and a church choir make strange bedfellows indeed.  摇滚乐队和教堂唱诗班凑一块儿真是奇怪的组合。

354.e: He thinks his new phone is the bee's knees.  他觉得自己的新手机简直棒极了。

355.i: have a ˈbee in your bonnet (informal)
355.e: Dad has a bee in his bonnet about turning off every light.  爸爸对随手关灯这事儿念叨个没完。

356.e: The kids made a beeline for the cake as soon as they arrived.  孩子们一到就直奔蛋糕去了。

357.cn: 早经历过了；没什么新鲜
357.e: Backpacking across Europe with a tent? Been there, done that, twice.  背着帐篷穿越欧洲？我早玩过了，还两回呢。

358.e: Ask Mei about landlords; she's been around and knows the tricks.  房东的事问阿梅，她见得多，门道清楚。

359.e: I know how you feel about failing; I've been there before.  失败的滋味我懂，我也经历过。

360.e: Dad finally explained the birds and the bees to my little brother.  爸爸终于给我弟弟讲了讲男女之事。

361.i: ˌbeg, ˌborrow or ˈsteal (also ˌbeg, ˌsteal or ˈborrow)
361.e: We'll beg, borrow or steal a van to move the piano tomorrow.  明天搬钢琴，我们想尽办法也得弄辆货车。

362.cn: 引出尚未触及的问题；回避实质
362.e: That answer begs the question of who is paying for all this.  这个回答让人不禁要问，这一切谁来买单。

363.e: You say the film was boring; I beg to differ.  你说这电影无聊，恕我不能苟同。

364.e: I beg your pardon, I didn't mean to step on your foot.  对不起，我不是故意踩到你的。

365.e: There's a slice of pizza going begging if anyone wants it.  还剩一块披萨没人要，谁想吃？

366.cn: 难以置信；令人无法相信
366.e: The queue at the passport office was long beyond belief.  护照办事处的队伍长得难以置信。

367.e: To begin with, we only had two customers a day.  起初我们一天只有两个客人。

368.e: She won her first game of chess, but that was beginner's luck.  她第一盘棋就赢了，不过是新手的运气。

369.e: Believe you me, that road is far worse in the rain.  相信我，那条路一下雨更难走。

370.cn: 千万别信；根本不是那么回事
370.e: He says the exam is easy? Don't you believe it!  他说考试简单？你可千万别信！

371.cn: （常用被动）使某人相信（或明白）
371.e: I was given to believe that the rent included the water bill.  我一直以为房租里包含水费。

372.cn: （表惊讶或恼怒）我简直不敢相信
372.e: I don't believe it — they've cancelled the train again!  真是的，火车又取消了！

373.e: He thinks the moon landing was faked; they'll believe anything.  他觉得登月是假的，这种人什么都信。

374.i: I'll believe it/that when I ˈsee it (informal)
374.e: He's giving up sweets? I'll believe that when I see it.  他要戒甜食？我要亲眼看到才信。

375.i: says he's going to give up smoking. ˈYl believe
375.cn: 他说要戒烟，我才不信（例句片段）
375.e: He says he's going to give up smoking. I'll believe it when I see it.  他说要戒烟，我得亲眼见了才信。

376.e: The children made believe that the sofa was a pirate ship.  孩子们把沙发当成了海盗船。

377.cn: 不敢相信自己的眼睛（或耳朵）
377.e: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the price tag.  看到价签时我简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

378.e: Would you believe it, he turned up two hours late again.  你敢信吗，他又迟到了两个小时。

379.e: The advert led us to believe breakfast was included.  广告让我们以为含早餐。

380.i: be a great/firm beˈliever in sth
380.e: My aunt is a firm believer in a cold shower every morning.  我姑妈笃信每天早上冲个冷水澡。

381.e: Give me a bell when you get to the station and I'll come.  你到站给我打个电话，我去接你。

382.e: I just want a basic phone without all the bells and whistles.  我只想要个简单手机，不需要那些花哨功能。

383.e: The little printing firm went belly up after the contract fell through.  合同一黄，那家小印刷厂就倒闭了。

384.i: have had a ˈbellyful of sb/sth (informal)
384.e: I've had a bellyful of his excuses this month.  这个月他的借口我听够了。

385.e: That joke about his divorce was really below the belt, and everyone went quiet.  那句拿他离婚开玩笑的话太下作了，全场都安静了。

386.cn: 缠着某人唠叨；向某人诉苦
386.e: He bent my ear about his noisy neighbours for a solid two hours.  他缠着我唠叨了整整两个小时他那吵闹的邻居。

387.cn: 专心于某事；竭尽全力做某事
387.e: She bent her mind to the problem and found a solution by midnight.  她全神贯注地琢磨这个难题，半夜前就想出了办法。

388.cn: 歪曲事实；说得不尽属实
388.e: He bent the truth a little to make his fishing story sound better.  他把事实稍微歪曲了一下，好让钓鱼的故事更精彩。

389.e: That dripping tap is driving me round the bend at three in the morning.  凌晨三点那个滴水的龙头快把我逼疯了。

390.e: I'm going round the twist trying to repair this ancient washing machine.  修这台老掉牙的洗衣机快把我逼疯了。

391.e: At best the repair takes a week; at worst, it takes a month.  往好里说修一周，往坏里说得一个月。

392.cn: 跪着恳求；低声下气地请求
392.e: He practically begged on bended knee for one more chance at the job.  他几乎是跪下来求人再给他一次工作机会。

393.cn: 为了帮助某人；为某人好
393.e: I repeated the whole announcement for the benefit of the people who arrived late.  我把整个通知又说了一遍，是为了照顾迟到的人。

394.e: There's no need to repeat everything for my benefit; I heard it fine.  不用专门为我把所有内容再说一遍，我听清楚了。

395.i: give sb the ˌbenefit of the ˈdoubt
395.cn: 因证据不足而姑且相信某人
395.e: She was late again, but I gave her the benefit of the doubt.  她又迟到了，但我还是姑且相信她有苦衷。

396.e: Put on your best bib and tucker — we're eating at a fancy restaurant.  换上你最好的行头，我们要去高档餐厅吃饭。

397.cn: 最好的良药；最有效的办法
397.e: After a rotten week, a long walk by the sea is the best medicine.  过了糟糕的一周，去海边走走就是最好的良药。

398.i: the best of a bad ˈbunch/ˈlot (BrE)
398.cn: 差中较好者；矮子里拔将军
398.e: None of the flats were nice, but this one was the best of a bad bunch.  这些公寓都不理想，这套算是矮子里拔将军。

399.cn: 两全其美；兼得多方好处
399.e: Working from home two days a week gives me the best of both worlds.  每周在家办公两天，让我两头的好处都占了。

400.i: the best of ˈluck (to sb) (old-fashioned, informal, often ironic)
400.cn: 祝你好运（多含反语，暗指难成）
400.e: You want him to apologize? Well, the best of luck to you.  你想让他道歉？那祝你好运吧。

401.i: the best of ˈthree, ˈfive, etc.
401.cn: 三局两胜（或五局三胜等）
401.e: Let's play the best of three and the loser buys dinner.  我们打三局两胜，输的人请客吃饭。

402.i: the best thing since sliced ˈbread (informal, spoken)
402.e: He thinks his new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.  他觉得他那台新咖啡机简直是天底下最棒的发明。

403.i: bring out the ˈbest in sb
403.cn: 使某人显现出最佳品质
403.e: A crisis like this really brings out the best in ordinary people.  这样的危机最能激发出普通人身上最好的一面。

404.i: do, mean, etc. sth for the ˈbest
404.e: I know I upset you, but I only said it for the best.  我知道惹你不高兴了，可我说那话是出于好意。

405.i: for a/some reason/reasons best known to himˈself, herˈself, etc. (humorous)
405.cn: 出于只有本人才明白的理由
405.e: For reasons best known to himself, he painted the whole kitchen bright orange.  出于只有他自己清楚的原因，他把整个厨房刷成了亮橙色。

406.i: for a/some reason/reasons best known to himˈself, herˈself, etc. (humorous)
406.cn: 出于只有本人才清楚的原因
406.e: For some reason best known to herself, she turned down the promotion.  出于只有她自己明白的理由，她拒绝了升职。

407.e: She had the best of the argument and he finally stopped talking.  这场争论她占了上风，他最后不吭声了。

408.e: I know the exam is hard, but just give it your best shot.  我知道考试很难，你尽力一试就行。

409.cn: 呈现最佳状态；显得最漂亮
409.e: The garden looks its best in late May when the roses open.  五月底玫瑰开放的时候，这座花园最好看。

410.i: make the best of sth/things/a bad job
410.cn: 在逆境中尽力而为；随遇而安
410.e: The hotel was awful, but we made the best of a bad job.  酒店很糟，但我们还是尽量往好处过。

411.e: If we put our best foot forward, we can finish before it gets dark.  我们加把劲的话，天黑前就能干完。

412.i: to the best of your beˈlief/ˈknowledge
412.cn: 据某人所知；就某人所信
412.e: To the best of my knowledge, nobody has lived in that house for years.  据我所知，那房子已经好些年没人住了。

413.cn: 不亚于任何人；不比别人差
413.e: She's seventy, but she can dance with the best of them all night.  她七十岁了，可跳起舞来一点不输年轻人。

414.i: with the ˌbest will in the ˈworld
414.cn: 不管用意多好；纵然竭尽全力
414.e: With the best will in the world, I can't finish this by Friday.  就算我再想帮忙，周五前也做不完。

415.cn: 孤注一掷；押上全部身家
415.e: Don't bet the farm on a start-up that hasn't earned a penny yet.  别把全部身家押在一家还没赚过一分钱的初创公司上。

416.i: (you can) bet your bottom ˈdollar/your ˈlife
416.e: You can bet your bottom dollar he'll be late to his own wedding.  可以打包票，他连自己的婚礼都会迟到。

417.e: I bet that she forgot the tickets again — she always does.  我敢打赌她又忘带票了，她老这样。

418.i: I wouldn't ˈbet on it • don't ˈbet on it
418.e: He says he'll pay you back tomorrow, but I wouldn't bet on it.  他说明天还你钱，可我看未必。

419.e: "Coming to the match tonight?" "You bet, I've had my ticket for weeks."  “今晚来看比赛吗？”“当然，票我几周前就买好了。”

420.i: your, his, etc. bête ˈnoire (from French)
420.e: Early morning meetings are my bête noire, especially on a rainy Monday.  一大早开会是我最讨厌的事，尤其是下雨的周一。

421.cn: 结果难料；一切都说不准
421.e: If the star player is injured, all bets are off for the final.  要是主力受伤，决赛的结果就完全说不准了。

422.i: against your better ˈjudgement (especially BrE) (AmE usually against your better ˈjudgment)
422.e: Against my better judgement, I lent him the car for the whole weekend.  尽管明知不妥，我还是把车借给他过了整个周末。

423.i: against your better ˈjudgement (especially BrE) (AmE usually against your better ˈjudgment)
423.e: She went back to him against her better judgement, and regretted it immediately.  她明知不该，还是回到了他身边，随即就后悔了。

424.e: We're better off now that both of us are working full-time.  我们俩都全职上班以后，日子宽裕多了。

425.i: better the ˌdevil you ˈknow (than the devil you don't) (saying)
425.cn: 宁用熟悉的坏，不用陌生的坏
425.e: I'll stay with my old boss — better the devil you know.  我还是跟着老板干吧，熟悉的魔鬼总好过陌生的。

426.e: He sent the birthday card in March, but better late than never.  他三月才寄来生日贺卡，不过迟到总比不到强。

427.e: You missed the penalty, mate — better luck next time.  兄弟，你罚丢了点球，下次好运吧。

428.e: Take an umbrella with that sky; better safe than sorry.  这天色，带把伞吧，小心总比后悔强。

429.i: the ˌbigger, ˌfaster, etc. the ˈbetter
429.e: When it comes to pizza, the bigger the better as far as I'm concerned.  说到披萨，在我看来越大越好。

430.cn: 最好做某事；做某事更明智
430.e: You'd do better to apologize now than wait until she hears it elsewhere.  你最好现在就道歉，别等她从别处听说。

431.cn: 不管是好是坏；无论结果如何
431.e: For better or worse, we've sold the house and moved to the coast.  不管是好是坏，我们卖了房子搬到海边了。

432.cn: 战胜；占上风；使无法克制
432.e: Curiosity got the better of me and I opened the letter.  好奇心占了上风，我把那封信拆开了。

433.e: She baked a cake, then he went one better and cooked a whole dinner.  她烤了个蛋糕，他更胜一筹，做了一整桌晚饭。

434.cn: 最好做某事；应该做某事
434.e: You'd better leave now if you want to catch the last train.  你要赶末班车的话，最好现在就走。

435.e: That armchair has seen better days, but I can't bear to throw it out.  那把扶手椅早就旧了，可我舍不得扔。

436.e: The so-called hotel was little better than a shed with beds in it.  那所谓的旅馆简直就是个摆了床的棚子。

437.e: If he brings the car, so much the better; we won't need a taxi.  他要是把车开来就更好了，我们就不用打车了。

438.i: take a ˌturn for the ˈbetter/ˈworse
438.e: Her health took a turn for the worse a week after the operation.  手术一周后，她的身体状况恶化了。

439.e: You've stopped crying — that's much better. Now tell me what happened.  你不哭了，这样好多了。现在告诉我出了什么事。

440.cn: 那是千真万确；你别不信
440.e: Is the boss angry? You'd better believe it — he's been shouting all morning.  老板生气了吗？你别不信，他吼了一上午。

441.i: what's the ˈbetting...? • the betting ˈis that...
441.e: What's the betting he turns up an hour late with no apology?  他八成会迟到一小时还不道歉，你信不信？

442.i: between ourˈselves • between you and ˈme
442.cn: 你我之间的秘密；私下说说
442.e: Between you and me, I think she's planning to hand in her notice.  私下跟你说，我觉得她打算辞职了。

443.e: He's not tall and not short — somewhere in between, I'd say.  他不高也不矮，我看是介于二者之间。

444.e: The colour is twixt and between — neither proper blue nor proper green.  这颜色不上不下，说蓝不蓝说绿不绿。

445.cn: 为某人所不能理解；某人力所不及
445.e: Why anyone would queue overnight for a phone is quite beyond me.  为什么会有人为买手机通宵排队，我实在想不通。

446.e: He bided his time and asked for a raise after the deal closed.  他等待时机，等合同签下来才开口要求加薪。

447.cn: 老大哥（监控一切的当权者）
447.e: With cameras on every corner, Big Brother really is watching you now.  街角都是摄像头，老大哥真的在盯着你。

448.e: He's a big cheese at the bank now, with his own corner office.  他现在是银行里的大人物，有自己的独立办公室。

449.e: Her uncle is a big wheel in the film industry over there.  她叔叔在那边的电影圈里是个大亨。

450.e: So he won one game against me. Big deal.  他不过赢了我一局，有什么了不起。

451.e: What's the big deal? It's only a scratch on the car door.  这有什么大不了的？车门上不过划了一道。

452.cn: 最重要的人（或事物）；头号角色
452.e: Forget the small contracts; this deal is the big enchilada.  别管那些小合同了，这笔生意才是重头戏。

453.i: a big ˈfish (in a little/small pond)
453.e: He was a big fish in a small pond until he moved to London.  搬到伦敦之前，他在小地方算是个大人物。

454.cn: 娘娘腔；软弱怯懦的男人
454.e: Stop being such a big girl's blouse and get in the cold water.  别那么娘们儿唧唧的了，下冷水里去。

455.i: a big ˈname/ˈnoise • a ˈbig shot (informal)
455.e: They hired a big name to open the new shopping centre.  他们请了个大腕来给新商场剪彩。

456.e: After that album she finally hit the big time and toured the world.  那张专辑之后她终于大红大紫，开始全球巡演。

457.e: Let's give the band a big hand — they played for three hours.  我们给乐队热烈鼓掌，他们演了三个小时。

458.cn: 我这张大嘴巴；我真多嘴
458.e: I told her about the surprise party — me and my big mouth.  我把惊喜派对的事说漏了，我这张大嘴巴。

459.e: You forgot my birthday? Honestly, it's no big deal.  你忘了我生日？说真的，没什么要紧的。

460.e: In this office we're one big happy family, at least most days.  我们办公室就像个欢乐的大家庭，至少大多数时候是。

461.e: Since the promotion he's got far too big for his boots.  自从升职以后，他就变得特别自以为是。

462.e: On your bike! I'm not lending you money a third time.  滚吧！我不会第三次借钱给你了。

463.e: A local band will top the bill at the festival this summer.  今年夏天的音乐节将由一支本地乐队压轴。

464.e: It rained like billy-o all afternoon and the match was called off.  整个下午雨下得特别猛，比赛取消了。

465.e: I'm in a bind — my babysitter cancelled an hour before the show.  我进退两难，保姆在演出前一小时取消了。

466.e: The police kicked the door in, but the bird had already flown.  警察踹开了门，可要抓的人早跑了。

467.i: a ˌbird in the ˈhand is worth two in the ˈbush (saying)
467.cn: 一鸟在手胜过二鸟在林
467.e: Take the offer they made; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.  接受他们的报价吧，双鸟在林不如一鸟在手。

468.i: a ˌbird in the ˈhand is worth two in the ˈbush (saying)
468.cn: 奢求不如实得；见好就收
468.e: Don't quit yet — a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.  先别辞职，一鸟在手胜过二鸟在林。

469.e: He's a bird of passage who never stays in one city long.  他是个漂泊不定的人，从不在一个城市久留。

470.cn: 冲某人竖中指（表示侮辱）
470.e: The driver gave me the bird when I honked at the traffic lights.  我在红灯处按喇叭，那司机冲我竖了中指。

471.i: the birds and the ˈbees (old-fashioned or humorous)
471.e: Dad went red trying to explain the birds and the bees to us.  爸爸满脸通红地想给我们讲那些性知识。

472.e: Those two are always plotting together — birds of a feather, I suppose.  那俩人总凑一块儿谋划，真是物以类聚。

473.e: She gave birth to twin boys in the back of a taxi.  她在出租车后座生下了一对双胞胎男孩。

474.cn: 一整套典型做派（或说辞）
474.e: He gave us the whole struggling-artist bit again over dinner.  晚饭时他又把那套穷困艺术家的说辞搬了出来。

475.e: Charging for tap water is a bit much, even in this city.  自来水都收费，就算在这座城市也有点过分了。

476.e: She told her friends she rather fancied a bit of rough.  她跟朋友说，她还挺喜欢粗野型的男人。

477.i: not a ˈbit • not one (little) ˈbit
477.e: I'm not a bit surprised that he forgot to call again.  他又忘了打电话，我一点都不意外。

478.i: not a ˈbit of it! (BrE, informal)
478.cn: 根本不是那样；压根儿没有
478.e: I expected him to apologize, but not a bit of it.  我以为他会道歉，结果压根儿没有。

479.e: Everyone deserves a bite at the cherry before the jobs are filled.  职位定下来之前，每个人都该有一次机会。

480.i: a second/another bite at/of the ˈcherry (BrE)
480.cn: 第二次机会；再来一次的机会
480.e: He failed the driving test but gets another bite at the cherry in June.  他驾照没考过，六月还有一次机会。

481.e: This assignment bites the big one; I've rewritten it four times already.  这作业烂透了，我都重写四遍了。

482.cn: 咬紧牙关应付；硬着头皮做
482.e: I finally bit the bullet and told my boss I was leaving.  我终于咬紧牙关告诉老板我要走了。

483.e: Another small bookshop on the high street has bitten the dust.  大街上又一家小书店倒闭了。

484.i: bite the hand that ˈfeeds you
484.e: Criticizing the charity that pays your salary is biting the hand that feeds you.  批评给你发工资的慈善机构，就是恩将仇报。

485.cn: 咬住嘴唇忍住不说（或不哭）
485.e: She bit her lip and said nothing when he took all the credit.  他把功劳全揽走时，她咬着嘴唇一句话没说。

486.e: He sat biting his nails while the jury argued in the next room.  陪审团在隔壁争论时，他坐着咬指甲。

487.i: bite off ˌmore than you can ˈchew (informal)
487.e: Taking three courses at once, she'd bitten off more than she could chew.  一下选三门课，她真是贪多嚼不烂。

488.e: I bit my tongue when she criticized my cooking in front of guests.  她当着客人批评我的厨艺，我忍住没吭声。

489.e: Go and ask her yourself — honestly, she won't bite you.  你自己去问她，真的，她又不会吃了你。

490.e: The biter bit: his own prank ended up soaking him instead.  作法自毙，他自己的恶作剧最后把他淋了个透。

491.cn: 欲骗人反受骗；自食其果
491.e: She'd tried to make him look foolish; it was a clear case of the biter bit.  她想让他出丑，结果自食其果。

492.i: bits and ˈpieces (also ˌbits and ˈbobs BrE)
492.e: I keep bits and pieces of old jewellery in this biscuit tin.  我把零星的旧首饰都放在这个饼干盒里。

493.e: Losing the final at home was a bitter pill for the fans to swallow.  在主场输掉决赛，对球迷来说是难以下咽的苦果。

494.e: They fought the eviction to the bitter end and lost anyway.  他们抗争驱逐令直到最后，结果还是输了。

495.cn: 青一块紫一块；遍体鳞伤
495.e: He fell off his bike and his knees were black and blue.  他从自行车上摔下来，膝盖青一块紫一块。

496.cn: 非黑即白；看问题绝对化
496.e: She sees every issue in black and white, with no middle ground.  她看什么问题都非黑即白，没有中间地带。

497.cn: 倒霉的一天；黑暗的日子
497.e: It was a black day for the town when the factory closed.  工厂关闭那天，对这个镇子来说是黑暗的一天。

498.e: Tickets for the final were selling on the black market for hundreds.  决赛的门票在黑市上炒到了好几百。

499.cn: 事故多发地段；问题严重的地方
499.e: This junction is a notorious black spot for cyclists in winter.  这个路口是冬天骑车人出事的著名黑点。

500.e: The café has finally been in the black for three months running.  这家咖啡馆终于连续三个月有盈余了。

501.e: I want the terms in black and white before I sign anything.  签字之前我要看到白纸黑字的条款。

502.i: he, it, etc. is not as black as he, it, etc. is ˈpainted
502.cn: 并不像人们说的那么坏
502.e: Her new boss isn't as black as he's painted, honestly.  说实话，她新老板并不像传言说的那么坏。

503.i: he, it, etc. is not as black as he, it, etc. is ˈpainted
503.e: The neighbourhood is not as black as it is painted by the papers.  这一带并不像报纸描绘的那么糟。

504.e: Things looked black for the team after two players were sent off.  两名队员被罚下后，球队前景一片暗淡。

505.e: Nobody is to blame for the accident; the road was simply icy.  这场事故谁也不怪，路面结冰了。

506.e: Swim in that river if you like, but don't blame me afterwards.  你爱去那条河游就去，出了事别怪我。

507.i: I don't ˈblame you/her, etc. (for doing sth)
507.cn: 我不怪你（或她等）；情有可原
507.e: You walked out of the meeting? I don't blame you one bit.  你退出了会议？我一点也不怪你。

508.i: a blank ˈcheque (BrE) (AmE a blank ˈcheck)
508.e: The board gave her a blank cheque to rebuild the whole department.  董事会给了她全权去重建整个部门。

509.cn: 扫兴的人；爱泼冷水的人
509.e: Don't be a wet blanket; everyone else wants to stay out longer.  别扫大家的兴，其他人都还想再待会儿。

510.cn: 勾起回忆的旧人旧事旧物
510.e: That song on the radio was a real blast from the past.  收音机里那首歌真是勾起了满满的回忆。

511.e: Her lab blazed a trail in treating the disease with cheap drugs.  她的实验室在用廉价药治这种病上开了先河。

512.e: We ran like blazes to catch the last bus home.  我们飞奔着去赶回家的末班车。

513.e: Where the blazes did I put my reading glasses this time?  我这回到底把老花镜放哪儿了？

514.e: Who the blazes left the front door wide open all night?  到底是谁把大门整夜敞着？

515.e: The lawsuit bled the small company dry within a single year.  这场官司一年之内就把这家小公司榨干了。

516.cn: 真可爱；真难为他（表示喜爱）
516.e: He made me a birthday card all by himself — bless!  他自己给我做了张生日卡，真可爱！

517.i: ˌbless his, her, etc. (little) cotton ˈsocks (BrE, humorous)
517.e: He waited two hours in the rain for me, bless his cotton socks.  他在雨里等了我两个小时，真是难为他了。

518.cn: 上帝保佑你（他人打喷嚏时说）
518.e: "Atishoo!" "Bless you — there's a box of tissues on the table."  “阿嚏！”“上帝保佑你，桌上有纸巾。”

519.cn: 因祸得福；看似祸实是福
519.e: Missing that flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise.  没赶上那班飞机，结果是因祸得福。

520.e: The investigation went down a blind alley for almost six months.  调查在死胡同里绕了将近六个月。

521.e: Without my glasses I'm as blind as a bat in this light.  不戴眼镜，这种光线下我几乎什么都看不见。

522.e: My sister set me up on a blind date with her colleague.  我姐姐给我安排了和她同事的相亲。

523.e: He came home blind drunk and fell asleep on the stairs.  他烂醉如泥地回到家，睡在了楼梯上。

524.e: The salesman tried to blind us with science instead of quoting a price.  推销员净拿专业术语唬人，就是不肯报价。

525.cn: 视而不见；睁一只眼闭一只眼
525.e: Managers turned a blind eye to staff leaving early on Fridays.  经理对员工周五早退睁一只眼闭一只眼。

526.i: in the blink of an ˈeye
526.e: The whole summer went by in the blink of an eye.  整个夏天一眨眼就过去了。

527.e: The washing machine is on the blink again, twice this month.  洗衣机又出毛病了，这个月第二回。

528.i: have been around the ˈblock (a few times)
528.e: Don't try to trick her; she's been around the block a few times.  别想骗她，她可是见过世面的。

529.i: put/lay your head/neck on the ˈblock
529.cn: 甘冒风险；把自己置于受责难之地
529.e: I put my neck on the block by recommending him for the job.  我推荐他做这份工作，是把自己搭进去了。

530.e: There's been bad blood between the two families since the land dispute.  自那场土地纠纷后，两家就一直有积怨。

531.i: be after/out for sb's ˈblood (informal, often humorous)
531.cn: 想报复某人；找某人算账
531.e: The coach is out for my blood after I missed training twice.  我两次没去训练，教练正找我算账呢。

532.e: The film is all blood and guts with hardly any plot.  这部电影全是血腥场面，几乎没什么情节。

533.e: The old play is pure blood and thunder, and the crowd loves it.  这出老戏纯是刀光剑影，观众就爱看。

534.cn: 血浓于水；家人总比外人亲
534.e: They argue constantly, but blood is thicker than water when trouble comes.  他们老吵架，可一有事就血浓于水。

535.e: Once his blood was up, nobody could talk him out of fighting.  他一上火，谁也劝不住他动手。

536.e: This restaurant took ten years of blood, sweat and tears to build.  这家餐馆是十年的血汗才做起来的。

537.e: The committee badly needs new blood and a few younger voices.  委员会很需要新鲜血液和一些年轻人的声音。

538.e: The company has blood on its hands after ignoring the safety warnings.  公司无视安全警告，手上沾着人命。

539.e: Sailing is in his blood; his grandfather fished these waters for decades.  航海是他骨子里的东西，他祖父在这片海打了几十年鱼。

540.i: like getting ˌblood out of/from a ˈstone
540.e: Getting an apology out of him is like getting blood from a stone.  想让他道歉，比登天还难。

541.e: The way he talks to waiters makes my blood boil every time.  他跟服务员说话的那副样子每次都让我火冒三丈。

542.i: make sb's ˈblood run cold • make sb's ˈblood freeze
542.e: The scream from the empty flat made my blood run cold.  空屋里传出的尖叫让我毛骨悚然。

543.i: make sb's ˈblood run cold • make sb's ˈblood freeze
543.e: His calm description of the crime made my blood freeze completely.  他平静地描述那桩罪行，让我浑身发冷。

544.e: You can't turn your back on her; she's your own flesh and blood.  你不能不管她，她是你的亲骨肉。

545.cn: 煞风景的东西（尤指丑陋建筑）
545.e: That concrete car park is a real blot on the landscape.  那座水泥停车场真是大煞风景。

546.cn: 开枪打爆脑袋；饮弹自尽
546.e: In the film the villain threatens to blow his own brains out.  电影里那个反派威胁说要开枪自尽。

547.e: He ate three hot dogs and then blew chunks on the ride.  他吃了三个热狗，然后在游乐设施上吐了。

548.cn: 暴露某人身份；揭穿伪装
548.e: One careless phone call completely blew the agent's cover last night.  昨晚一个不小心的电话彻底暴露了那名特工的身份。

549.e: Dad blew a fuse when he saw the dent in the car.  爸爸看到车上的凹痕，勃然大怒。

550.e: Somebody blew the gaff on the surprise party before the weekend.  周末前有人把惊喜派对的秘密抖了出去。

551.e: She blows hot and cold about moving abroad, so nothing gets decided.  她对出国的事忽冷忽热，什么也定不下来。

552.e: The view from the top of the ridge completely blew my mind.  从山脊顶上看到的景色让我震撼极了。

553.cn: 令人震撼的；极其惊人的
553.e: We were stunned by the mind-blowing scenery on the drive north.  北上路上那令人震撼的景色让我们都看呆了。

554.i: blow sb/sth out of the ˈwater (informal)
554.cn: 彻底击败；证明毫无价值
554.e: Their new phone blows the competition out of the water on price.  他们的新手机在价格上把对手打得落花流水。

555.e: He never stops blowing his own trumpet about that one big sale.  他没完没了地吹嘘那一笔大单。

556.e: I hate to toot my own horn, but I fixed the boiler myself.  我不想自夸，但锅炉确实是我自己修好的。

557.e: One spark could blow the whole fuel depot sky-high.  一个火星就可能把整个油库炸上天。

558.e: Stop blowing smoke and tell me what the repair actually costs.  别跟我兜圈子了，直说修一下到底多少钱。

559.i: blow your ˈtop (BrE) (AmE blow your ˈstack)
559.e: She blew her top when she found the kitchen in that state.  她看到厨房那副样子，气得暴跳如雷。

560.e: His clever plan to impress the boss blew up in his face.  他讨好老板的妙计彻底砸了锅。

561.e: An accountant blew the whistle on the firm's fake expense claims.  一名会计揭发了公司虚假报销的事。

562.e: A month's extra pay helped soften the blow of losing the job.  多发一个月工资，多少缓和了失业的打击。

563.cn: 逐一细述的；一五一十的
563.e: She gave me a blow-by-blow version of the whole argument.  她把整场争吵一五一十地讲给我听。

564.e: He gave a blow-by-blow account of the match to everyone at work.  他把比赛过程一五一十地讲给单位同事听。

565.cn: 按事情发生顺序的细致描述
565.e: I don't need a blow-by-blow description of your dentist appointment.  我不需要听你看牙的全过程细节。

566.e: The two neighbours nearly came to blows over a parking space.  两个邻居为一个车位差点动起手来。

567.e: She called me out of the blue after twenty years of silence.  沉寂二十年后，她突然给我打来电话。

568.i: (do sth) till you're ˌblue in the ˈface
568.cn: 说到口干舌燥（也无济于事）
568.e: You can explain till you're blue in the face; he won't listen.  你说到口干舌燥也没用，他根本不听。

569.e: The job pays very little, but board and lodging are included.  这份工作工资很低，不过包食宿。

570.i: your, sb's, etc. ˌblue-eyed ˈboy (informal, disapproving)
570.e: Everyone knows he's the manager's blue-eyed boy around this office.  谁都知道他是经理在办公室里的红人。

571.e: I changed the subject quickly to spare her blushes at dinner.  我赶紧换了话题，免得她在饭桌上难堪。

572.e: The accounts were all above board when the inspectors checked them.  检查员查账时，账目全都清清白白。

573.e: Wages went up three per cent across the board this April.  今年四月工资全面上涨了百分之三。

574.e: Our holiday plans went by the board when the baby arrived early.  孩子提前出生，我们的假期计划就泡汤了。

575.e: There were forty passengers on board when the engine suddenly failed.  发动机突然故障时，船上有四十名乘客。

576.e: The designers took our complaints on board and changed the whole layout.  设计师采纳了我们的意见，把布局全改了。

577.e: Don't worry, we're all in the same boat with these rising rents.  别急，房租都在涨，大家处境都一样。

578.e: Add the eggs, stir for a minute, and Bob's your uncle.  加进鸡蛋，搅一分钟，就大功告成了。

579.e: The empty seats did not bode well for the rest of the tour.  空荡荡的座位对后面的巡演可不是好兆头。

580.e: She threw herself body and soul into running the little corner shop.  她全身心地扑在经营那家街角小店上。

581.i: keep body and ˈsoul together (often humorous)
581.e: Two part-time jobs barely keep body and soul together these days.  如今两份兼职也只够勉强糊口。

582.cn: 普普通通的；毫无特色的
582.e: It's a bog standard hotel room, but the bed is comfortable.  就是间普普通通的酒店房间，不过床挺舒服。

583.e: Their relationship has gone off the boil since he moved away.  他搬走以后，他们的关系就淡下来了。

584.e: The campaign is really on the boil in this final week.  最后这一周，竞选活动搞得如火如荼。

585.i: be/make so ˈbold (as to do sth) (formal)
