585.e: Might I be so bold as to ask what this painting cost?  恕我冒昧，能问问这幅画多少钱吗？

586.e: He walked in bold as brass and helped himself to the coffee.  他大模大样地走进来，自己倒了杯咖啡。

587.cn: 晴天霹雳；突如其来的事
587.e: The redundancy notice came as a complete bolt from the blue.  裁员通知来得像晴天霹雳。

588.e: She sat bolt upright when she heard the front door open.  听到前门打开的声音，她一下子直挺挺地坐了起来。

589.e: When the rain eased, we made a dash for the car.  雨小些时，我们撒腿冲向汽车。

590.e: That taco place downtown is the bomb, especially late at night.  市中心那家玉米卷店特别棒，尤其是深夜。

591.i: go down a ˈbomb • go (like) a ˈbomb (BrE)
591.e: Her speech went down a bomb with the students last night.  昨晚她的演讲在学生中大受欢迎。

592.e: That old van still goes like a bomb on the motorway.  那辆旧货车在高速上还是跑得飞快。

593.e: With him a handshake is enough; his word is his bond.  跟他握个手就行了，他说话向来算数。

594.e: He's bone idle and hasn't cut the grass since April.  他懒到家了，四月以来一次草都没割。

595.e: The shared driveway has long been a bone of contention between them.  那条共用车道一直是他们之间的争议焦点。

596.e: His jokes about her weight were a bit close to the bone.  他拿她体重开的玩笑有点太伤人了。

597.i: cut, pare, etc. sth to the ˈbone
597.e: The council has cut library funding to the bone this year.  今年市政厅把图书馆经费砍到了最低。

598.i: have a ˈbone to pick with sb (informal)
598.cn: 要跟某人理论；有账要算
598.e: I've got a bone to pick with you about last night's phone call.  昨晚那通电话，我得跟你说道说道。

599.i: not have a ... ˈbone in your body
599.e: She doesn't have a jealous bone in her body, honestly.  说真的，她身上一点嫉妒心都没有。

600.e: The boss threw me a bone and let me leave early on Friday.  老板给了点甜头，让我周五早走。

601.i: make no ˈbones about sth/about doing sth
601.e: She makes no bones about wanting her old job back.  她毫不掩饰想要回原来的工作。

602.i: he, she, etc. wouldn't say ˈboo to a goose
602.e: Quiet Tom wouldn't say boo to a goose, let alone argue.  文静的汤姆连大气都不敢出，更别提争辩了。

603.i: bring sb to ˈbook (for sth) (formal, especially BrE)
603.e: The families want the company brought to book for the accident.  遇难者家属要求追究公司在这起事故中的责任。

604.e: Our new manager does everything by the book, even the coffee rota.  新经理什么都照章办事，连轮流泡咖啡都不例外。

605.cn: 依某人看；照某人的观点
605.e: In my book, anyone who helps a stranger like that deserves thanks.  在我看来，那样帮陌生人的人值得道谢。

606.cn: 严厉惩处某人；从重发落
606.e: The judge threw the book at him for driving without insurance again.  他又无保险驾驶，法官从重判了他。

607.e: Police have closed the book on the case after thirty long years.  三十年后，警方给这个案子画上了句号。

608.i: be in/get into sb's ˈgood/ˈbad books (informal)
608.e: Washing his car got me back into my father's good books.  给我爸洗了车，我又讨他喜欢了。

609.cn: 记（或不记）在正式账目上
609.e: The firm has forty staff on the books and a few casuals.  公司账上有四十名员工，另有几个临时工。

610.cn: 值得记上一笔的稀奇事
610.e: Snow in April — now that really is one for the books.  四月下雪，这可真是件稀罕事。

611.i: the boot is on the other ˈfoot (BrE, informal)
611.cn: 情况反过来了；此一时彼一时
611.e: Now that she's the manager, the boot is on the other foot.  现在她当了经理，情况可反过来了。

612.i: the shoe is on the other ˈfoot (AmE, informal)
612.e: He used to lend me money; now the shoe is on the other foot.  过去是他借钱给我，如今反过来了。

613.e: He got the boot for turning up drunk on a Monday morning.  他周一早上喝醉了来上班，被炒了鱿鱼。

614.e: The papers put the boot in when the manager was already struggling.  经理本已焦头烂额，报纸还落井下石。

615.e: The flat is cheap, central, and has a small garden to boot.  这套公寓便宜、地段好，还带个小花园。

616.i: drag/pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps (informal)
616.e: He dragged himself up by his own bootstraps after leaving school at fifteen.  他十五岁辍学，全靠自己打拼出头。

617.i: drag/pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps (informal)
617.e: She pulled herself up by her bootstraps and now owns three shops.  她白手起家，如今开了三家店。

618.i: bore sb to ˈtears • bore sb ˈstiff (informal)
618.e: His holiday photos bored us to tears for a solid hour.  他的度假照片让我们整整烦了一个小时。

619.i: bore sb out of their ˈmind (informal)
619.e: I was bored out of my mind during that three-hour lecture.  那节三小时的课听得我烦透了。

620.i: be born with a silver ˈspoon in your mouth
620.cn: 生于富贵之家；含着金汤匙出生
620.e: He was born with a silver spoon in his mouth and never worked.  他生在富贵人家，从来没上过班。

621.e: She's a Yorkshire woman born and bred, and proud of it.  她是土生土长的约克郡人，对此很自豪。

622.e: Don't tell me the dog ate it — I wasn't born yesterday.  别说是狗吃了，我可不是三岁小孩。

623.i: in all my born ˈdays (old-fashioned, informal)
623.e: I've never seen such a mess in all my born days.  我这辈子就没见过这么乱的场面。

624.e: He paid double for that car; there's one born every minute.  那车他花了双倍的钱，真是傻瓜年年有。

625.e: Kids today don't know they're born, with heating in every room.  现在的孩子身在福中不知福，每间屋子都有暖气。

626.e: The old bridge has been living on borrowed time for several years.  那座老桥这几年一直是勉强撑着。

627.e: He spent Christmas in the bosom of his family for once.  他难得一回在家人的怀抱里过了圣诞。

628.i: the bottom drops/falls out of the ˈmarket
628.e: The bottom fell out of the market for second-hand phones last year.  去年二手手机的市场行情一落千丈。

629.e: Pizza or curry — honestly, I'm not bothered either way.  披萨还是咖喱都行，我真的无所谓。

630.e: He was going to propose, but he bottled it at the restaurant.  他本打算求婚，到了餐厅却怂了。

631.i: have, show, etc. (a lot of) ˈbottle (BrE, informal)
631.e: It takes real bottle to speak up at a meeting like that.  在那种会上敢开口，是真有胆量。

632.i: have, show, etc. (a lot of) ˈbottle (BrE, informal)
632.cn: 表现出极大的勇气（或自信）
632.e: She showed a lot of bottle standing up to those bullies.  她敢跟那些恶霸对着干，真有种。

633.i: from the ˌbottom of your ˈheart
633.e: I thank you from the bottom of my heart for staying tonight.  今晚你能留下来，我打心底里感谢你。

634.e: At bottom, the argument was about money rather than principles.  归根结底，这场争论是为了钱而不是原则。

635.i: at the bottom/top of the ˈpile/ˈheap
635.cn: 处于社会最底层（或最上层）
635.e: You've no idea what life at the bottom of the pile is like.  你根本不知道社会最底层的日子是什么样。

636.e: The bottom line is that we simply cannot afford another delay.  说到底，我们再也拖不起了。

637.i: be/lie at the ˈbottom of sth
637.e: Money worries lay at the bottom of most of their arguments.  钱的烦恼是他们大多数争吵的根源。

638.i: the bottom of the ˈhour (especially AmE)
638.e: The station broadcasts headlines at the top and bottom of the hour.  电台在整点和半点播报新闻提要。

639.i: get to the ˈbottom of sth
639.e: I'm determined to get to the bottom of who took the money.  我一定要查清是谁拿走了那笔钱。

640.e: Repairing this old house is a bottomless pit for our savings.  修这栋老房子简直是吞钱的无底洞。

641.e: Bottoms up, everyone — here's to the happy couple!  大家干杯，祝这对新人幸福！

642.cn: 兴奋得坐不住；激动难平
642.e: The kids were bouncing off the walls after all that chocolate.  吃了那么多巧克力，孩子们兴奋得停不下来。

643.i: be/feel duty/honour ˈbound to do sth (BrE)
643.e: I felt duty bound to tell her what I had overheard.  我觉得有义务把无意听到的事告诉她。

644.i: be/feel duty/honor ˈbound to do sth (AmE)
644.cn: 责无旁贷；有不可推卸的责任
644.e: As a doctor she feels honor bound to report the injury.  作为医生，她觉得有责任上报这处伤情。

645.e: She's bound and determined to run the marathon before she turns forty.  她铁了心要在四十岁前跑完马拉松。

646.e: The ball landed out of bounds, so the throw goes to us.  球出界了，所以由我们发界外球。

647.e: The staff kitchen is out of bounds to visitors during the day.  白天员工厨房不许访客进入。

648.cn: 禁止入内的；不准接近的
648.e: The old quarry is off limits to anyone without a permit.  没有许可证的人不得进入这座旧采石场。

649.e: I refuse to bow and scrape just to keep this contract.  我才不愿为保住这份合同而卑躬屈膝。

650.cn: 离不开母亲的男孩（或男人）
650.e: At thirty he's still a mummy's boy who phones her daily.  三十岁了他还是个妈宝男，天天给他妈打电话。

651.cn: 妈宝男；离不开母亲的男人
651.e: Her new boyfriend is a total mama's boy, and everyone notices.  她新男友完全是个妈宝男，谁都看得出来。

652.e: The boys in blue turned up ten minutes after we called.  我们报警十分钟后警察就到了。

653.e: They came home covered in mud again — boys will be boys.  他们又浑身是泥地回来了，男孩就是男孩。

654.e: The brain drain has left the country short of qualified doctors.  人才外流让这个国家缺少合格的医生。

655.e: She was the brains behind the campaign that saved the local library.  她是那场拯救社区图书馆运动的幕后策划人。

656.e: They promised a brave new world of paperless offices and endless leisure.  他们许诺了一个无纸办公、闲暇无限的美好新世界。

657.i: put a brave ˈface on sth • put on a brave ˈface
657.e: She put a brave face on the news and went back to work.  她强作镇定地接受了消息，回去继续工作。

658.i: put a brave ˈface on sth • put on a brave ˈface
658.cn: 强颜欢笑；装作满不在乎
658.e: He put on a brave face at the funeral for his mother's sake.  为了母亲，他在葬礼上强颜欢笑。

659.e: Wedding photography is my bread and butter; the art shows are extra.  婚礼摄影是我的饭碗，办画展只是额外的。

660.e: Three years of rising bills left the family on the breadline.  账单连涨三年，这家人过得极其困窘。

661.e: The car missed the cyclist by a hair's breadth this morning.  今早那辆车差一根头发丝就撞上骑车人。

662.i: break your ˈback doing sth/to do sth
662.e: I broke my back getting the garden ready before the guests arrived.  客人来之前，我拼了老命把花园收拾好。

663.cn: 完成某事最艰难的部分
663.e: We've broken the back of the move; only the books remain.  搬家最难的部分已经搞定，只剩书了。

664.e: He was charged with breaking and entering a shop on Mill Street.  他被控非法闯入米尔街的一家商店。

665.e: She answered the question without breaking stride and kept walking to class.  她脚步不停地回答了问题，径直走向教室。

666.i: make a clean ˈbreast of sth
666.e: He made a clean breast of it and admitted taking the cash.  他和盘托出，承认拿了那笔现金。

667.cn: 令人耳目一新的人（或事物）
667.e: The new teacher is a breath of fresh air in this school.  这位新老师给学校带来一股清新之风。

668.e: Let me sit down and get my breath back after those stairs.  爬完那些楼梯，让我坐下喘口气。

669.cn: 屏住呼吸（因紧张或期待）
669.e: We held our breath as the referee walked over to check.  裁判走过去查看时，我们都屏住了呼吸。

670.i: ˌsay, etc. sth in the same ˈbreath
670.e: He praised the plan and criticized the cost in the same breath.  他刚夸完这个方案，紧接着又批评成本。

671.cn: 令人惊叹；美得让人屏息
671.e: The view from the cliff top simply took my breath away.  崖顶的景色让我惊叹得说不出话。

672.e: He swore under his breath when the printer jammed again.  打印机又卡纸时，他低声骂了一句。

673.e: The old king breathed his last late that same night.  老国王就在那天深夜咽了气。

674.e: The festival breathed new life into the sleepy little seaside town.  这个节庆给冷清的海滨小镇注入了新活力。

675.i: not breathe a ˈword (of/about sth) (to sb)
675.e: Promise me you won't breathe a word of this to my sister.  答应我，这事对我妹妹只字别提。

676.cn: 喘息的机会；短暂的休整
676.e: The loan gives us a breathing space until the harvest comes in.  这笔贷款让我们在收成之前有了喘息的机会。

677.cn: 碰壁；遇到难以逾越的障碍
677.e: Plans to build a new road around the town hit a brick wall.  在镇子周边修新路的计划碰了壁。

678.cn: 实体与网络并行的经营方式
678.e: The chain went bricks and clicks and doubled its sales last year.  这家连锁店线上线下并行，去年销售额翻了一番。

679.i: a few, two, etc. ˌbricks short of a ˈload
679.e: Anyone who parks there is a few bricks short of a load.  在那儿停车的人脑子多少有点缺。

680.i: a few, two, etc. ˌsandwiches short of a ˈpicnic
680.e: He's a sandwich short of a picnic, but he's kind enough.  他脑子不太灵光，人倒是挺善良。

681.i: a few ˌcards short of a full ˈdeck
681.e: Talking to the parking meter? He's a few cards short of a full deck.  跟停车计时器说话？他脑子有点缺弦。

682.cn: 做无米之炊；无材料强做事
682.e: Without any data we're making bricks without straw in this report.  没有数据，写这份报告就是做无米之炊。

683.e: Evening classes help bridge the gap between school and full-time work.  夜校有助于弥合学校与全职工作之间的落差。

684.i: bridge the ˈgulf (between A and B) (less frequent)
684.e: Nothing could bridge the gulf between the two sides of the family.  什么也弥合不了这个家族两边的鸿沟。

685.e: I hold no brief for the council, but this decision seems fair.  我并不袒护市政厅，但这个决定看着还算公道。

686.e: In brief, we need more staff and a much bigger budget.  简而言之，我们需要更多人手和大得多的预算。

687.e: Be here bright and early tomorrow; the van leaves at six.  明天一大早就到，车六点出发。

688.e: Her little boy is as bright as a button at four.  她的小男孩才四岁，机灵得很。

689.e: He left the village for the bright lights of the capital.  他离开村子，奔向首都的繁华。

690.cn: 机灵鬼（常反语指办蠢事者）
690.e: Some bright spark left the freezer door open all weekend.  某个“机灵鬼”整个周末都没关冰柜门。

691.e: Her recovery was the one bright spot in a dreadful year.  她的康复是那个糟糕年头里唯一的亮点。

692.cn: 看事情积极的一面；保持乐观
692.e: Look on the bright side: the rain means we can skip watering.  往好处想，下雨了我们就不用浇水了。

693.e: She arrived bright-eyed and bushy-tailed after only four hours' sleep.  她只睡了四小时，来时却精神抖擞。

694.e: Our party is a broad church, so arguments are only natural.  我们党内兼容各派，有争论很正常。

695.e: The bike was stolen in broad daylight outside the police station.  自行车是在警局门口光天化日下被偷的。

696.i: it's as ˌbroad as it's ˈlong (old-fashioned, BrE, spoken)
696.e: Bus or train, it's as broad as it's long at this hour.  这个点儿坐公交还是坐火车都一样。

697.e: With ten minutes left they went for broke and pushed everyone forward.  还剩十分钟，他们孤注一掷，全线压上。

698.i: if it ain't ˈbroke, don't ˈfix it
698.cn: 没坏就别修；好用就别改
698.e: The old system works fine; if it ain't broke, don't fix it.  旧系统好好的，没坏就别瞎改。

699.e: He washed everyone's mugs to earn a few brownie points.  他给大家洗杯子，是想挣点好印象。

700.cn: 责任到此为止；责无旁贷
700.e: I'm the head teacher here, so the buck stops here.  我是这里的校长，出了事责任在我。

701.i: buck up your ˈideas • buck your ˈideas up
701.e: You'd better buck your ideas up before the inspection next week.  下周检查之前，你最好打起精神来。

702.i: make a fast/quick ˈbuck (informal, often disapproving)
702.e: He's just trying to make a quick buck off the tourists.  他只不过想从游客身上赚点快钱。

703.e: You've got Buckley's chance of getting tickets the day before.  提前一天才想买票，你根本没戏。

704.e: He answered the door in the buff and horrified the poor postman.  他光着身子去开门，把邮递员吓坏了。

705.e: Since that trip she's been bitten by the travel bug.  自那次旅行以后，她就迷上了到处跑。

706.e: Bug off and let me finish this crossword in peace.  走开，让我安安静静把这填字游戏做完。

707.e: Stop playing silly buggers with the thermostat and just leave it.  别瞎摆弄温控器了，就那么放着。

708.i: build ˈbridges (between A and B/with sb)
708.cn: 搭建沟通桥梁；改善关系
708.e: The visit helped build bridges between the two neighbouring villages.  这次走访帮两个邻村搭起了沟通的桥梁。

709.i: be built like a ˈtank (also be built like a ˌbrick ˈshithouse, slang)
709.e: The new goalkeeper is built like a tank and fears nothing.  新守门员体格壮得像坦克，什么都不怕。

710.i: like a ˌbull in a ˈchina shop
710.e: He went through the negotiations like a bull in a china shop.  他在谈判中横冲直撞，全无分寸。

711.i: take the ˌbull by the ˈhorns (informal)
711.e: She took the bull by the horns and asked for a raise.  她果断出手，开口要求加薪。

712.e: The guy at the desk gave us a bum steer about the ferry.  柜台那家伙给我们指错了渡轮的路。

713.i: give sb/get the ˌbum's ˈrush (slang, especially AmE)
713.e: He got the bum's rush from the club well before midnight.  他没到半夜就被轰出了俱乐部。

714.e: Traffic was bumper to bumper for six miles on the motorway.  高速上车辆首尾相接，堵了六英里。

825.e: Her opinion carries a lot of weight with the hiring committee this year.  今年招聘委员会很看重她的意见。

826.i: put the ˌcart before the ˈhorse
826.e: Buying furniture before you've found a flat is putting the cart before the horse.  房子还没找到就先买家具，这是本末倒置。

827.e: The new chef was given carte blanche to redesign the entire dinner menu.  新主厨获得全权，可以重新设计整个晚餐菜单。

828.e: The board gave her carte blanche to cut costs however she thought best.  董事会授予她全权，怎么削减成本由她定。

829.e: The schedule isn't carved in stone, so tell me if Friday doesn't work.  日程不是定死的，周五不行你就说。

830.e: You'll be fined or simply warned, as the case may be, after the review.  复核之后，视情况你会被罚款或只是被警告。

831.cn: 不停地数落某人；纠缠某人
831.e: My mother's been on my case about finding a job since I graduated.  自打毕业，我妈就一直催我找工作。

832.e: Don't worry about the leak—the plumber is on the case already.  漏水的事别担心，水管工已经在处理了。

833.e: Cheap flights harm small airports, and this closed runway is a case in point.  廉价航班伤害小机场，这条关闭的跑道就是明证。

834.e: The police think the two men were casing the joint before the robbery.  警方认为这两人在抢劫前先去踩了点。

835.cn: 别再唠叨某人；别再挑剔
835.e: Get off my case—I said I'd wash the car on Sunday.  别念叨我了，我说了周日会洗车。

836.e: It's raining, and in any case the museum closes at four on Mondays.  在下雨，再说周一博物馆四点就关门了。

837.e: Take an umbrella just in case the weather turns while you're out walking.  带把伞，以防你散步时天气变脸。

838.cn: 既然那样；如果那样的话
838.e: You've already booked the tickets? In that case, I'll cancel my other plans.  你已经订好票了？那我就把别的安排取消。

839.e: I've already made up my mind. In that case, there's no point discussing it further.  我已经拿定主意了。既然如此，再讨论也没意义。

840.cn: 提出理由支持；据理论证
840.e: She made out a strong case for hiring two more nurses this year.  她有力地论证了今年应再招两名护士。

841.i: cash ˈdown (BrE) (also ˌcash up ˈfront AmE, BrE)
841.e: The dealer wanted cash down before he'd hand over the keys to the van.  车商要求先付现款才交出货车钥匙。

842.cn: 兑换筹码收手；抽身退出
842.e: After thirty years in the trade, he cashed in his chips and moved abroad.  干了三十年这行，他收手不干，搬到了国外。

843.e: The farmer sells his hay cash on the barrelhead—no cheques, no credit.  这农户卖干草只收现金，不收支票也不赊账。

844.e: We can ship the parts tomorrow if you agree to cash on delivery.  只要你同意货到付款，配件明天就能发出。

845.i: cast/run an ˈeye/your ˈeyes over sth
845.e: Could you cast an eye over my essay before I send it to the tutor?  我交给导师之前，你能帮我扫一眼论文吗？

846.i: cast your ˈmind back to sth
846.e: Cast your mind back to that summer we spent fixing up the old boat.  回想一下我们修那条旧船的那个夏天。

847.e: Serving him vintage wine is casting pearls before swine; he adds lemonade.  给他喝年份酒纯属对牛弹琴，他还要兑汽水。

848.e: She spoke out about the casting couch long before anyone else dared to.  早在别人不敢开口时，她就揭露了选角潜规则。

849.e: Stop building castles in the air and send out a few real job applications.  别做白日梦了，实实在在投几份简历吧。

850.cn: 猫捉老鼠般戏弄；欲擒故纵
850.e: The detective played cat and mouse with the suspect for nearly two hours.  警探同嫌疑人玩了近两个小时的猫鼠游戏。

851.e: In his new leather jacket he thinks he's the cat's whiskers.  穿上那件新皮夹克，他觉得自己帅得没边了。

852.i: let the ˈcat out of the bag (informal)
852.e: Dad let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party before Saturday.  周六还没到，爸爸就把惊喜派对的事说漏了嘴。

853.i: (look) like sth the ˈcat brought/dragged in
853.e: You look like something the cat dragged in—did you sleep in that shirt?  你这一身狼狈样，是穿着那件衬衫睡的吗？

854.i: like a ˌcat on hot ˈbricks (BrE, informal)
854.e: She was like a cat on hot bricks waiting for her exam results.  等考试成绩时，她急得如坐针毡。

855.i: like a ˌcat on a hot tin ˈroof (AmE, informal)
855.cn: 焦躁不安；像热锅上的蚂蚁
855.e: He paced the corridor like a cat on a hot tin roof all morning.  他一上午都在走廊里踱步，像热锅上的蚂蚁。

856.i: like the ˌcat that got, stole, etc. the ˈcream
856.e: She walked in grinning like the cat that got the cream after her promotion.  升职后她笑着进来，一脸得意。

857.i: not have a cat in ˈhell's chance (also not have a ˈdog's chance) (informal)
857.cn: 毫无机会；一点希望也没有
857.e: Without a passport you don't have a cat in hell's chance of boarding.  没有护照，你根本别想登机。

858.i: when the cat's aˈway the mice will ˈplay (saying)
858.e: The teacher stepped out and chaos erupted: when the cat's away the mice will play.  老师一出门就乱成一锅粥，真是猫儿不在鼠儿造反。

859.i: be in the ˈcatbird seat (AmE, informal)
859.cn: 处于有利地位；掌控局面
859.e: With two rival firms bidding, the small studio is suddenly in the catbird seat.  两家对手同时竞标，这家小工作室一下占了上风。

860.e: Put a coat on or you'll catch your death out there in the wind.  穿上外套，不然在外头吹风会感冒得厉害。

861.cn: 引起某人注意；吸引某人目光
861.e: A red dress in the window caught my eye as we walked past.  路过时，橱窗里一条红裙子吸引了我的目光。

862.i: catch sb in the ˈact (of doing sth)
862.e: The guard caught him in the act of slipping a watch into his pocket.  保安当场抓住他正把一块表塞进口袋。

863.i: ˈcatch it (BrE) (AmE catch ˈhell, ˈget it) (spoken)
863.e: You'll catch it from Mum when she sees the mess in the kitchen.  妈妈看到厨房这么乱，你可要挨骂了。

864.cn: 使人措手不及；趁人不备
864.e: The defence was caught napping and conceded a goal in the first minute.  后防线一时松懈，开场一分钟就丢了球。

865.cn: 趁某人不备；使措手不及
865.e: The question about her divorce caught her off guard during the live interview.  直播采访中关于离婚的提问让她措手不及。

866.i: catch sb on the ˈhop (BrE, informal)
866.cn: 使某人措手不及；出其不意
866.e: The early inspection caught the whole kitchen staff on the hop.  提前到来的检查让整个后厨措手不及。

867.e: We're heading to the roof to catch some rays before the clouds roll in.  云还没上来，我们去屋顶晒会儿太阳。

868.e: You've caught the sun on your shoulders—they're already bright pink.  你肩膀晒着了，都红得发亮了。

869.i: catch sb with their ˈpants down (informal)
869.cn: 使人措手不及；当场撞破
869.e: The surprise audit caught the whole department with their pants down.  突击审计打了整个部门一个措手不及。

870.i: catch sb with their ˈtrousers down (BrE, informal)
870.cn: 出其不意抓个正着；冷不防
870.e: The reporters caught the minister with his trousers down over the missing files.  记者就失踪文件一事把部长打了个措手不及。

871.e: Rehearsals were catch-as-catch-can, with actors turning up whenever work allowed.  排练全凭凑合，演员什么时候有空就什么时候来。

872.i: the early ˈbird catches the ˈworm (saying)
872.cn: 早起的鸟儿有虫吃；捷足先登
872.e: Get to the market at six, because the early bird catches the worm.  六点就去市场，早起的鸟儿才有虫吃。

873.e: After a slow first quarter, the company has been playing catch-up all year.  第一季度开局不利，公司一整年都在追赶。

874.cn: 殃及池鱼；卷入争斗受害
874.e: Junior staff got caught in the crossfire when the two directors started arguing.  两位总监一吵起来，基层员工就跟着遭殃。

875.e: He wouldn't be caught dead in a suit, not even at his own wedding.  他打死也不肯穿西装，连自己婚礼上都不穿。

876.e: The run was exhausting, but it was all in a good cause for the hospice.  跑得筋疲力尽，但都是为了给临终关怀院做善事。

877.cn: 注定失败的事；没指望的人
877.e: Persuading Dad to use a smartphone is a lost cause at this point.  到这份上，劝我爸用智能手机已经没戏了。

878.i: throw caution to the ˈwind(s) (often humorous)
878.e: She threw caution to the wind and booked a one-way ticket to Lisbon.  她一狠心，订了张飞里斯本的单程票。

879.i: be the ˌcentre of atˈtention (BrE) (AmE be the ˌcenter of atˈtention)
879.e: At every party my little brother has to be the centre of attention.  每次聚会我弟弟都非得当全场焦点。

880.e: The house was built around the turn of the century by a local shipbuilder.  这房子约在世纪之交由本地造船匠建造。

881.e: Don't stand on ceremony—grab a plate and help yourself to the food.  别客气，拿个盘子自己动手吃吧。

882.cn: 不拘礼节地；随随便便地
882.e: He dropped the box on my desk without ceremony and walked straight out.  他随手把箱子往我桌上一放就走了。

883.e: Nobody knows for certain why the factory closed so suddenly last winter.  去年冬天工厂为何突然关门，谁也说不准。

884.e: Make certain that the windows are shut before you set the alarm.  设警报前先确认窗户都关好了。

885.i: make certain of sth/of doing sth
885.e: Book early to make certain of a seat on the last train home.  早点订票，确保回家末班车有座位。

886.e: Do you have a spare charger by any chance? Mine died this morning.  你身上碰巧有多余的充电器吗？我的今早没电了。

887.e: Chances are that the shop is shut by now, so try again tomorrow.  这会儿店多半关门了，明天再去吧。

888.e: I don't take chances with ice on the road; I just stay home.  路上结冰我从不冒险，干脆待在家里。

889.e: There's no guarantee of a refund, but you can take your chances at the desk.  不保证能退款，不过你可以去柜台碰碰运气。

890.e: The pub has changed hands three times since we moved to the village.  自从我们搬到村里，这家酒馆已经转手三次了。

891.e: She changed her mind about the job the night before she was due to start.  上班前一晚，她改主意不去那份工作了。

892.e: He had a change of heart and let his son keep the stray dog.  他转了念头，让儿子留下那只流浪狗。

893.e: Every time I mention money, he changes the subject to the weather.  我一提钱，他就把话题扯到天气上。

894.e: You'll change your tune when you see how much the repairs actually cost.  等你看到维修真要多少钱，就会改口了。

895.e: The doctor told him to change his ways or expect another heart attack.  医生让他改改生活方式，否则还会再犯心脏病。

896.e: Let's walk to work for a change instead of squeezing onto the bus.  换个花样走路上班吧，别再挤公交了。

897.i: get no ˈchange out of sb (BrE, informal)
897.cn: 从某人处得不到帮助（或消息）
897.e: You'll get no change out of the landlord about the broken heating.  暖气坏了的事，你从房东那儿问不出什么来。

898.e: A wind of change is blowing through the department since the new director arrived.  新总监到任后，部门里刮起了一阵变革之风。

899.e: He can quote chapter and verse on every rule in the tenancy agreement.  租约里的每条规定他都能说出确切出处。

900.cn: 接二连三的不幸；祸不单行
900.e: The trip was a chapter of accidents: lost bags, food poisoning and a strike.  这趟旅行祸不单行：丢行李、食物中毒，还赶上罢工。

901.cn: 符合（或不符合）某人性格
901.e: Shouting at a waiter is completely out of character for my gentle uncle.  冲服务员大喊大叫，完全不像我那温和的叔叔。

902.i: get a ˈcharge out of sth (AmE)
902.e: My grandmother gets a real charge out of beating us all at cards.  我奶奶打牌赢我们所有人，觉得特别过瘾。

903.e: When the manager fell ill, Priya took charge of the whole project.  经理病倒后，普里娅接管了整个项目。

904.cn: 仁爱始于家庭；先顾自家人
904.e: Before donating abroad, remember that charity begins at home.  往国外捐款前，别忘了行善要先从家里做起。

905.e: A spoonful of honey worked like a charm on my sore throat.  一勺蜂蜜治我的嗓子疼特别灵。

906.e: He's walked away from two crashes, so the man leads a charmed life.  两次车祸他都毫发无伤，这人真是命大。

907.cn: 高得离谱；超出正常范围
907.e: Ticket demand for the reunion tour has been off the charts all week.  重组巡演的票务需求这一周高得离谱。

908.e: I spent all morning chasing my own tail between three different offices.  我一上午在三个办公室之间瞎跑，一无所获。

909.e: After a week of pure tail-chasing, we finally got a straight answer.  瞎折腾了一星期，我们总算得到一个明确答复。

910.e: Let's cut to the chase: can you finish the design by Friday or not?  说重点吧，你周五前到底能不能做完设计？

911.e: The dog bolted and three of us gave chase across the muddy field.  狗窜了出去，我们三个追过泥泞的田地。

912.e: These strawberries are going cheap because the market closes in ten minutes.  这些草莓在贱卖，因为市场十分钟后就收摊。

913.e: It's a cheap and cheerful little diner, but the breakfasts are excellent.  这是家便宜实惠的小餐馆，早餐特别棒。

914.e: The souvenirs were cheap and nasty, so I bought nothing at the airport.  纪念品又便宜又劣质，我在机场什么也没买。

915.cn: 非常划算；再贵一倍也值
915.e: That old bike lasted me ten years, so it was cheap at twice the price.  那辆旧自行车我骑了十年，再贵一倍也值。

916.e: Good childcare doesn't come cheap in this part of the city.  在城里这一带，好的托儿服务可不便宜。

917.e: They renovated the whole flat on the cheap using second-hand materials.  他们用二手材料，花小钱翻新了整套公寓。

918.e: Regular exercise keeps his blood pressure in check without any medication.  规律锻炼让他不吃药也能把血压控制住。

919.e: Without proper checks and balances, one loud person can run any committee.  没有像样的制衡，任何委员会都会被一个大嗓门把持。

920.e: Tiny workshops sit cheek by jowl with luxury hotels in this old district.  在这片老城区，小作坊和豪华酒店紧挨在一起。

921.e: He insulted her twice, but she turned the other cheek and kept working.  他两次出言侮辱，她却不予计较，继续做事。

922.i: a blank ˈcheque (BrE) (AmE a blank ˈcheck)
922.e: The council gave the developer a blank cheque to redesign the waterfront.  议会给了开发商全权，随意重新规划滨水区。

923.e: Tell me what's wrong—you'll feel better once you get it off your chest.  说说怎么了，吐露出来你会好受些。

924.i: ˌchew the ˈfat (BrE) (AmE ˌchew the ˈrag)
924.e: We sat on the porch chewing the fat until it got completely dark.  我们坐在门廊上闲聊，一直聊到天全黑。

925.e: Two hundred pounds is chicken feed compared with what the repairs will cost.  跟修理费一比，两百英镑只是小钱。

926.e: His chickens came home to roost when the inspectors found the faulty wiring.  检查员查出线路有问题，他终于自食其果。

927.i: don't count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched) (saying)
927.cn: 别过早乐观；勿盲目自信
927.e: Don't count your chickens—the buyer hasn't actually signed anything yet.  别高兴太早，买家其实还没签任何字。

928.i: too many ˌchiefs and not enough ˈIndians (saying)
928.e: Nothing gets finished here: too many chiefs and not enough Indians.  这儿什么都做不完，指挥的多，干活的少。

929.e: After climbing that mountain, a five-mile walk feels like child's play.  爬过那座山之后，走五英里简直是小菜一碟。

930.i: a ˈchill runs/goes down sb's spine
930.cn: 令人毛骨悚然；不寒而栗
930.e: A chill ran down my spine when I heard footsteps in the empty house.  空房子里传来脚步声，我不寒而栗。

931.i: send a ˈchill up/down sb's spine
931.e: The recording of that phone call sent a chill down my spine.  那通电话的录音让我脊背发凉。

932.cn: 使人透心凉；使极为恐惧
932.e: The wind off the sea chilled us to the bone within five minutes.  海风吹了不到五分钟就把我们冻透了。

933.e: Chin up—there'll be other auditions before the end of the year.  振作点，年底前还有别的试镜机会。

934.e: She took the criticism on the chin and rewrote the whole chapter.  她坦然接受批评，把整章重写了一遍。

935.i: a chink in sb's ˈarmour (BrE) (AmE a chink in sb's ˈarmor)
935.e: His impatience is the one chink in his armour as a negotiator.  作为谈判者，他唯一的软肋就是缺乏耐心。

936.i: a ˌchip off the old ˈblock (informal)
936.e: The boy fixes engines just like his dad—a real chip off the old block.  这男孩修发动机跟他爸一个样，真是有其父必有其子。

937.i: have a ˈchip on your shoulder (informal)
937.e: He's had a chip on his shoulder ever since they passed him over.  自从升职没轮到他，他就一直忿忿不平。

938.e: One more loss and the manager has had his chips at this club.  再输一场，主教练在这家俱乐部就干到头了。

939.i: let the chips fall where they ˈmay (AmE, informal)
939.e: Tell them the truth and let the chips fall where they may.  把真相告诉他们，后果怎样就怎样吧。

940.e: When the chips are down, you find out who your real friends are.  到了关键时刻，你才看得出谁是真朋友。

941.e: With twelve desserts on offer, we were spoilt for choice at the bakery.  面包店有十二种甜点，我们挑花了眼。

942.e: He works nights by choice because the office is quiet after midnight.  他自愿上夜班，因为过了午夜办公室很安静。

943.e: Denim is still the fabric of choice for anyone working outdoors all day.  对整天在户外干活的人来说，牛仔布仍是首选面料。

944.e: The winner gets dinner for two at a restaurant of their choice.  获胜者可在自选餐厅享用双人晚餐。

945.e: The kids were chomping at the bit to open their presents before breakfast.  孩子们早饭前就急着要拆礼物。

946.i: there's nothing, not much, etc. to ˈchoose between A and B
946.cn: 两者不相上下；难分高低
946.e: There's nothing to choose between the two phones; both take excellent photos.  这两款手机不相上下，拍照都很出色。

947.e: Three regional offices are for the chop under the new cost-cutting plan.  按新的削减成本方案，三个地区办事处要被砍掉。

948.e: Stop chopping and changing—pick one supplier and stick with them.  别再变来变去了，选定一家供应商就别换了。

949.e: Her show got the chop after just two seasons on the network.  她的节目在该台只播了两季就被砍掉了。

950.e: The new coffee place is not much chop; the beans taste burnt.  新开的咖啡店不怎么样，豆子有糊味。

951.e: Chop-chop, everyone—the bus leaves in four minutes and nobody's packed.  都快点，车四分钟后就开，谁都还没收拾好。

952.e: The tailoring on this old jacket is first chop, even after twenty years.  这件旧夹克的做工是一流的，二十年了还挺括。

953.e: You guessed the year but not the month—close but no cigar.  年份猜对了月份没猜中，就差那么一点。

954.e: The meeting went round in circles for two hours without a single decision.  会开了两小时一直在兜圈子，一个决定也没做。

955.i: run around in ˈcircles (BrE also run round in ˈcircles)
955.e: I ran around in circles all day and still didn't finish the paperwork.  我一整天瞎忙活，文件还是没弄完。

956.e: By force of circumstance, she took over the shop when her father died.  形势所迫，父亲去世后她接手了店铺。

957.cn: 在这种情况下；既然如此
957.e: Under the circumstances, a written apology is the least he owes us.  在这种情况下，他至少该写份书面道歉。

958.e: Under no circumstances should you open that door while the machine runs.  机器运转时，你绝对不能打开那扇门。

959.e: The village's only claim to fame is a bridge that appeared in a film.  这村子唯一出名的地方是一座上过电影的桥。

960.e: Give him a fishing rod and a quiet lake and he's happy as a clam.  给他一根鱼竿和一片静湖，他就乐得不行。

961.e: We ran like the clappers and just caught the last train home.  我们撒腿狂奔，刚好赶上回家的末班车。

962.i: be in a ˈclass of your, its, etc. own
962.e: As a live performer, she is in a class of her own.  论现场表演，她是独一无二的。

963.e: The team clawed their way back into the league after two terrible seasons.  苦熬两个糟糕赛季后，这支队伍艰难重返联赛。

964.e: His mother thinks that girl has got her claws into him already.  他妈妈觉得那姑娘已经把他缠得死死的。

965.e: The kitchen was as clean as a whistle when the inspectors came round.  检查员来的时候，厨房干净得一尘不染。

966.e: The surveyor gave the old cottage a clean bill of health, surprisingly enough.  勘验师居然给这栋老屋出具了合格证明。

967.e: She made a clean break with her old firm and started her own agency.  她与老东家彻底了断，自己开了家代理公司。

968.e: The new owner cleaned house and replaced most of the senior managers.  新老板大清洗，换掉了大部分高层经理。

969.e: The restaurant cleaned up its act after failing two hygiene inspections.  两次卫生检查不合格后，这家餐馆彻底整改了。

970.e: He finally came clean about denting the car on the way to work.  他终于坦白，上班路上把车刮凹了。

971.i: have clean ˈhands ◆ your hands are ˈclean
971.e: Whatever the papers say, my hands are clean in this whole affair.  不管报纸怎么写，这件事上我是清白的。

972.i: make a clean ˈbreast of sth
972.e: He made a clean breast of the missing money before anyone accused him.  还没人指责他，他就把钱的去向全招了。

973.e: The team made a clean sweep of every medal at the regional championships.  这支队伍在地区锦标赛上包揽了全部奖牌。

974.e: Keep your nose clean for six months and they'll consider you for parole.  安分守己半年，他们就会考虑给你假释。

975.cn: 骗光某人钱财；痛宰某人
975.e: The divorce lawyers took him to the cleaners and he lost the house.  离婚律师把他榨得精光，房子都没了。

976.cn: 消除误会；缓和紧张气氛
976.e: A long, honest talk cleared the air between the two flatmates at last.  一次坦诚长谈终于化解了两个室友间的芥蒂。

977.cn: 非常清晰；听得一清二楚
977.e: Her voice came through the old radio as clear as a bell.  她的声音从旧收音机里传出来，清晰得很。

978.e: Let's clear the decks this morning so we can start the audit tomorrow.  今天上午先把杂事清掉，明天好开始审计。

979.e: It took eight years of appeals to clear her brother's name completely.  申诉了八年，才彻底为她哥哥洗清了罪名。

980.e: He cleared his throat nervously before reading the speech to the guests.  给来宾念讲稿前，他紧张地清了清嗓子。

981.i: clear the ˈway (for sth/for sth to happen)
981.e: The ruling clears the way for thousands of similar compensation claims.  这项裁决为数千宗类似索赔扫清了障碍。

982.e: I skip wine at lunch so I can keep a clear head all afternoon.  午饭我不喝酒，好让整个下午头脑清醒。

983.e: The tests came back fine, so the doctor says she's in the clear.  检查结果正常，医生说她没事了。

984.e: Steer clear of the coast road tonight; there's flooding near the bridge.  今晚别走海滨公路，桥附近发大水了。

985.e: She's caught in a cleft stick: quit the course or lose the scholarship.  她进退两难：要么退课，要么丢掉奖学金。

986.i: ˈclever Dick (also ˈclever clogs) (BrE, informal, disapproving)
986.e: Some clever Dick reprogrammed the office printer to beep every hour.  哪个自作聪明的家伙把办公室打印机改成每小时叫一次。

987.e: All right, clever clogs, if you know the answer, come and fix it.  行了，聪明人，你既然知道答案就过来修吧。

988.e: Stuck indoors for a week with flu, I was climbing the walls.  得流感在家闷了一周，我快憋疯了。

989.i: at a fast, good, steady, etc. ˈclip (especially AmE)
989.e: Orders have been coming in at a steady clip since the review appeared.  自从那篇评论出来，订单一直稳步不断。

990.cn: 限制某人的自由（或权力）
990.e: The new rules have clipped the wings of the more ambitious department heads.  新规定限制住了那些野心较大的部门主管。

991.e: Engineers worked around the clock to get the power back on by Monday.  工程师昼夜赶工，赶在周一前恢复了供电。

992.e: You can't turn the clock back and undo what was said last night.  你没法让时光倒流，收回昨晚说过的话。

993.e: Leading by two, they simply ran out the clock in the final minutes.  领先两分，他们在最后几分钟干脆拖时间。

994.e: The whole wedding went like clockwork, right down to the last speech.  整场婚礼顺利极了，连最后的致辞都分毫不差。

995.e: The police finally closed the book on the case after thirty long years.  三十年后，警方终于给这桩案子画上句号。

996.e: Don't close your mind to online courses just because you prefer classrooms.  别因为偏爱课堂就对网课一概不听。

997.cn: 思想封闭的；固执己见的
997.e: He's too closed-minded to admit that the younger staff might be right.  他太固执，不肯承认年轻同事也许是对的。

998.e: Watching the sculptor at close quarters, you notice how tiny each cut is.  近距离看雕刻家干活，你会发现每一刀都极细。

999.e: They bought a cottage close by the lake so the kids could swim.  他们在湖边不远处买了间小屋，方便孩子游泳。

1000.e: The painting looks messy close up, but it's stunning from the doorway.  这幅画近看很乱，从门口望过去却很惊艳。

1001.e: His joke about lazy relatives hit a bit close to home for me.  他拿懒亲戚开的玩笑，对我来说有点戳心。

1002.i: be ˌcut from the same ˈcloth
1002.e: The two brothers are cut from the same cloth: stubborn and impossible to argue with.  兄弟俩是一个路子，倔得没法跟他们讲理。

1003.i: be ˌcut from the same ˈcloth (informal)
1003.cn: 一个模子里出来的；十分相像
1003.e: Don't assume all the women in our family are cut from the same cloth.  别以为我们家的女人都是一个模子刻出来的。

1004.i: cut your ˈcoat according to your ˈcloth (saying)
1004.e: We cut our coat according to our cloth and skipped the holiday this year.  我们量入为出，今年的假期就不去了。

1005.cn: 皇帝的新装；自欺欺人的假象
1005.e: The strategy is the emperor's new clothes: nobody dares say it makes no sense.  这套战略就是皇帝的新装，没人敢说它根本讲不通。

1006.e: A cloud has hung over the company since the fraud investigation began.  自欺诈调查开始，公司就一直笼罩在阴影中。

1007.e: Rising fuel prices are the only cloud on the horizon for the airline.  油价上涨是这家航空公司眼下唯一的隐忧。

1008.i: every ˌcloud has a silver ˈlining (saying)
1008.e: I lost the job but met my business partner: every cloud has a silver lining.  我丢了工作却遇到合伙人，真是祸中有福。

1009.e: She's been on cloud nine since the university offered her a place.  自从大学录取她，她就一直乐得飘飘然。

1010.e: He left the department under a cloud after the expenses story broke.  报销丑闻曝光后，他不光彩地离开了部门。

1011.e: Since the shop took off, the family has been living in clover.  自打店里生意火起来，这家人过得相当滋润。

1012.e: Word got round the office that Anna is in the club again.  办公室里传开了，安娜又怀上了。

1013.e: I don't have a clue how the boiler works, so call a plumber.  我完全不懂锅炉怎么运作，还是叫水管工吧。

1014.e: Managers should spend a week at the coalface before rewriting the rules.  经理们该先去一线待一周，再来改规矩。

1015.e: Bringing wine to a vineyard is like carrying coals to Newcastle.  带酒去酒庄，简直是多此一举。

1016.e: Wait until the coast is clear before you sneak the cake upstairs.  等没人注意了，再把蛋糕偷偷端上楼。

1017.i: cut your ˈcoat acˌcording to your ˈcloth
1017.e: They cut their coat according to their cloth and bought a smaller car.  他们量入为出，买了辆小一点的车。

1018.e: He rode into parliament on the coat-tails of a far more popular leader.  他靠着一位更受欢迎的领袖的提携进了议会。

1019.e: He gave me some cock and bull story about his phone falling in the canal.  他编了套鬼话，说手机掉进运河里了。

1020.e: The dog cocked an ear at the sound of keys in the front door.  听见大门钥匙响，狗竖起了耳朵。

1021.i: cock a ˈsnook at sb/sth (BrE, informal)
1021.cn: 公然蔑视；做鬼脸表示不敬
1021.e: The young artists cocked a snook at the gallery by exhibiting in a car park.  年轻艺术家在停车场办展，公然蔑视那家画廊。

1022.i: a cog in the maˈchine/the ˈwheel (informal)
1022.cn: 大机构中无足轻重的一员
1022.e: After twenty years he still felt like a cog in the machine.  干了二十年，他还是觉得自己只是颗螺丝钉。

1023.e: A refund is cold comfort when you've missed your daughter's graduation.  错过女儿的毕业典礼，退钱也无济于事。

1024.e: He's a cold fish at work but surprisingly warm with his grandchildren.  他工作中冷冰冰的，对孙辈却出奇地热络。

1025.e: Ever since the argument, the neighbours have given us the cold shoulder.  自那次争吵以后，邻居就一直对我们爱答不理。

1026.e: The novel opens with two strangers murdered in cold blood on a farm.  小说开篇便是两名陌生人在农场被冷血杀害。

1027.i: in the ˌcold light of ˈday
1027.cn: 冷静下来时；事后清醒地看
1027.e: In the cold light of day, quitting my job seemed a terrible idea.  冷静下来一想，辞职真是个糟糕的主意。

1028.cn: 打动不了某人；提不起兴趣
1028.e: Everyone raves about that band, but their music leaves me completely cold.  人人都夸那支乐队，可他们的音乐一点也打动不了我。

1029.e: Dad poured cold water on my plan to cycle across France alone.  我想独自骑车穿越法国，被爸爸泼了冷水。

1030.e: Come off it—you can't have finished the whole report in twenty minutes.  得了吧，你不可能二十分钟写完整份报告。

1031.i: come to ˈnothing ◆ not come to ˈanything
1031.e: All those meetings about the new library came to nothing in the end.  关于新图书馆的那些会最后都不了了之。

1032.e: Fashions come and go, but a good wool coat lasts forever.  潮流来来去去，一件好羊毛大衣却能穿一辈子。

1033.e: Come, come, nobody is going to be sacked over one broken mug.  好啦好啦，没人会为一个摔碎的杯子被开除。

1034.i: come ˈeasily, ˈnaturally, etc. to sb
1034.cn: 对某人而言轻而易举；天生就会
1034.e: Talking to strangers comes naturally to her, which makes her a great host.  跟陌生人搭话对她来说毫不费力，所以她很会招待人。

1035.e: Don't come it with me—I've known you since you were seven.  别跟我摆谱，你七岁起我就认识你了。

1036.e: He had it coming after ignoring every warning the inspector gave him.  检查员的警告他一概不听，落到这步是活该。

1037.e: The dealer saw him coming and charged double for a rusty old bike.  车贩子看他好糊弄，一辆锈自行车要了双倍价。

1038.e: Nobody saw the closure coming; the shop was busy right up to Christmas.  没人料到会关门，店里一直忙到圣诞节。

1039.i: where sb is ˈcoming from (informal, spoken)
1039.cn: 某人的出发点；某人的用意
1039.e: Once you know where she's coming from, her objections make much more sense.  一旦明白她的出发点，她的反对就说得通了。

1040.e: From her window she watches all the comings and goings on the street.  她从窗口看着街上的人来人往。

1041.e: With three languages at her command, she had no trouble finding work abroad.  她掌握三门语言，在国外找工作毫不费劲。

1042.e: The whole kitchen staff was at the duchess's command for the entire weekend.  整个周末，全体厨房人员都听候公爵夫人差遣。

1043.e: He got into bad company at sixteen and dropped out of school soon after.  他十六岁交了坏朋友，没多久就辍学了。

1044.e: I'll keep you company at the hospital until your sister arrives.  你姐姐来之前，我在医院陪着你。

1045.e: The view from that ridge at sunrise is truly beyond compare.  日出时从那道山脊望去的景色实在无与伦比。

1046.e: After the exam we met in the café to compare notes on the questions.  考完试我们在咖啡馆碰头，交流各自的答题情况。

1047.i: put a new/different comˈplexion on sth
1047.cn: 使事情呈现新面貌；改变看法
1047.e: Her resignation letter puts a very different complexion on the whole affair.  她的辞职信让整件事完全变了个样。

1048.e: Only two advisers were really in the president's confidence during those years.  那些年真正得到总统信任的只有两位顾问。

1049.e: She took her sister into her confidence about the job offer in Berlin.  她向姐姐透露了柏林那份工作邀约。

1050.e: Judging a contest your own students entered is a clear conflict of interest.  给自己学生参加的比赛当评委，明显存在利益冲突。

1051.e: The course runs in conjunction with a local hospital and includes ward placements.  这门课与本地医院合办，包含病房实习。

1052.i: connect the ˈdots (BrE also join (up) the ˈdots)
1052.cn: 把线索联系起来；理清关系
1052.e: Once you connect the dots, the two robberies were obviously planned together.  把线索一串，两起抢劫显然是一起策划的。

1053.e: I cannot in all conscience recommend a builder who left our roof leaking.  凭良心讲，我没法推荐一个把我家屋顶弄漏的建筑商。

1054.e: Sacking him just before Christmas will be on your conscience, not mine.  圣诞前把他辞了，那是你良心上的事，不是我的。

1055.e: If you skip training all week, you take the consequences on match day.  一周不训练，比赛日的后果你自己扛。

1056.e: The missing page turned out to be of no consequence to the final report.  那页丢失的纸对最终报告并无影响。

1057.e: The bridge closed and, in consequence, the village lost its bus service.  桥关闭了，村里因此没了公交服务。

1058.e: He received a small pension in consideration of forty years of loyal service.  为酬谢他四十年的忠诚服务，他领到一笔小额养老金。

1059.e: The judge took his age and clean record into consideration when sentencing him.  量刑时法官考虑了他的年龄和无前科记录。

1060.e: It is my considered opinion that the roof needs replacing before another winter.  我仔细想过，屋顶得在下个冬天前换掉。

1061.cn: 依我看；我仔细想来认为
1061.e: In my considered opinion, 'Trainspotting' is the best British film of the nineties.  仔细想来，《猜火车》是九十年代最好的英国电影。

1062.e: The manager was conspicuous by his absence at yesterday's staff meeting.  昨天的员工会上，经理的缺席格外显眼。

1063.e: There was a conspiracy of silence in the village about what happened that night.  那晚发生的事，村里人默契地都不吭声。

1064.e: The bonfire got out of control and the fire brigade had to come.  篝火失控了，消防队只好赶来。

1065.e: Stealing from a charity box is beneath contempt, whatever your excuses are.  偷募捐箱的钱，不管什么理由都卑劣至极。

1066.e: One more win puts them back in contention for a European place.  再赢一场，他们就重新有望拿到欧战名额。

1067.e: A 'peace offensive' sounds to me like a contradiction in terms.  在我听来，“和平攻势”本身就自相矛盾。

1068.e: Contrary to popular belief, most bats have excellent eyesight and hunt visually.  与普遍看法相反，多数蝙蝠视力极好，靠视觉捕食。

1069.i: on the ˈcontrary ◆ ˌquite the ˈcontrary
1069.e: I'm not bored; on the contrary, I could listen to him all evening.  我不觉得无聊，恰恰相反，我能听他讲一整晚。

1070.e: She stayed calm and in control of the class throughout the fire drill.  整个消防演习中她都镇定自若，把班级管得井井有条。

1071.cn: 毁掉某人的计划；断送前程
1071.e: That leaked email really cooked his goose with the board of directors.  那封外泄的邮件彻底断送了他在董事会的前途。

1072.e: Once the second engine started, we were really cooking with gas.  第二台发动机一启动，我们就干得顺风顺水了。

1073.cn: 在搞什么名堂；怎么回事
1073.e: You two look guilty—what's cooking in here this early on a Sunday?  你俩一脸心虚，周日一大早在这儿捣鼓什么呢？

1074.i: too many cooks spoil the ˈbroth (saying)
1074.cn: 厨子多了烧坏汤；人多手杂反坏事
1074.e: Three of us in one kitchen? Too many cooks spoil the broth.  三个人挤一个厨房？人多反而坏事。

1075.e: She stayed as cool as a cucumber while the alarms went off around her.  警报响成一片，她却依旧镇定自若。

1076.e: They left me cooling my heels in reception for nearly an hour.  他们让我在前台干等了将近一个小时。

1077.i: leave sb to cool their ˈheels (informal)
1077.e: The manager left her to cool her heels outside his office for forty minutes.  经理让她在办公室外干等了四十分钟。

1078.e: Cool it, you two—the neighbours can hear every word through the wall.  你俩冷静点，隔着墙邻居一句不落全听得见。

1079.e: He lost his cool when the referee awarded the penalty against him.  裁判判他犯规罚点球时，他沉不住气了。

1080.e: Play it cool at the interview and don't mention money until they do.  面试时沉住气，他们不提钱你就别提。

1081.e: You'll cop it if Mum finds out you took the car again.  要是妈妈发现你又开走了车，你可要挨训了。

1082.e: His lawyer advised him to cop a plea rather than risk a trial.  律师建议他认罪求轻判，别冒险受审。

1083.e: That new detective series isn't much cop after the first two episodes.  那部新侦探剧头两集之后就不怎么样了。

1084.i: it's a fair ˈcop (BrE, informal, humorous)
1084.e: It's a fair cop—I did eat the last three biscuits after all.  我认了，最后三块饼干确实是我吃的。

1085.e: He's a Yorkshireman to the core and won't hear a word against it.  他是个地道的约克郡人，容不得别人说半句不是。

1086.e: By promising everyone a raise, he painted himself into a corner.  他答应给每个人加薪，把自己逼进了死角。

1087.e: One family has cornered the market in wedding cakes in this small town.  这座小城的婚礼蛋糕生意被一家人垄断了。

1088.e: Bestsave has the market cornered in cheap groceries across the whole region.  倍省超市垄断了整个地区的廉价杂货生意。

1089.e: Exam season is just around the corner and nobody has started revising.  考试季马上就到，可谁都还没开始复习。

1090.e: Success is around the corner, so the work must not be stopped now.  成功就在眼前，现在决不能停下来。

1091.i: out of the corner of your ˈeye
1091.e: Out of the corner of my eye I saw him slip the envelope into his bag.  我用余光瞥见他把信封塞进了包里。

1092.e: That little handbag must have cost the earth—just look at the stitching.  那只小包肯定贵得要命，看看那针脚。

1093.e: The patient turned the corner on Tuesday and is now sitting up eating.  病人周二挺过了危险期，现在能坐起来吃饭了。

1094.e: The builders cut corners on the insulation and now the flat is freezing.  施工队在保温上偷工减料，现在屋里冷得要命。

1095.i: the four corners of the ˈearth/ˈworld
1095.e: Fans came from the four corners of the earth for the band's final concert.  歌迷从世界各地赶来看乐队的告别演唱会。

1096.e: She spent thirty years in the corridors of power advising four different ministers.  她在权力中枢待了三十年，先后为四位大臣出谋划策。

1097.e: They wanted to keep the factory open at any cost, even losing money.  他们想不惜代价保住工厂，哪怕亏本。

1098.e: I can get you tickets for tonight, but it will cost you.  今晚的票我能弄到，不过你得出血。

1099.cn: 吃了亏才知道；付出代价后才明白
1099.e: As I know to my cost, that garage never finishes a job on time.  我是吃过亏才知道，那家修车行从不按时完工。

1100.e: We must avoid a strike at all costs before the holiday season starts.  假期旺季开始前，我们必须不惜一切代价避免罢工。

1101.cn: 终日窝在沙发看电视的懒人
1101.e: His mother warns him he'll turn into a couch potato over the long summer.  他妈妈警告说，这个长假他会变成沙发土豆。

1102.i: be able to count sb/sth on (the fingers of) one ˈhand
1102.e: You can count the good restaurants in this town on one hand.  这镇上好餐馆一只手就数得过来。

1103.i: count sth on the fingers of one ˈhand
1103.e: I could count on the fingers of one hand the times he has apologised.  他道歉的次数一只手就数得完。

1104.cn: 知足；想想还有什么值得庆幸
1104.e: Count your blessings—at least the car was insured when the tree fell.  知足吧，树砸下来时车好歹上了保险。

1105.e: The town is still counting the cost of last winter's floods.  这座小镇仍在承受去年冬天洪水带来的损失。

1106.e: I lay there counting sheep until nearly three in the morning.  我躺着数羊，一直数到快凌晨三点。

1107.e: I've stopped keeping count of how many times he has changed jobs.  他换过多少次工作，我已经懒得数了。

1108.e: I've lost count of the emails I've sent about that broken lift.  为那部坏电梯我发了多少封邮件，自己都记不清了。

1109.i: not count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched)
1109.cn: 别过早乐观；勿盲目自信
1109.e: Don't count your chickens—the results aren't published until Friday afternoon.  别高兴太早，结果周五下午才公布。

1110.i: out for the ˈcount (BrE) (AmE ˌdown for the ˈcount)
1110.e: Two minutes on the sofa and Dad was out for the count.  在沙发上待了两分钟，老爸就睡得人事不省。

1111.cn: 公开表明立场；挺身表态
1111.e: It's time for parents to stand up and be counted at the council meeting.  家长们该在议会会议上公开表态了。

1112.e: You can buy these painkillers over the counter at any chemist here.  这些止痛药在这里任何一家药店都能直接买到。

1113.e: During the shortage, sugar was sold under the counter at triple the price.  短缺期间，白糖以三倍价格私下出售。

1114.e: That's my fourth coffee today, but who's counting?  这是我今天第四杯咖啡了，不过谁数着呢？

1115.cn: 乡巴佬；没见过世面的人
1115.e: He felt like a country bumpkin during his first week in London.  在伦敦的头一周，他觉得自己像个乡巴佬。

1116.e: The prime minister decided to go to the country a full year early.  首相决定提前整整一年举行大选。

1117.i: have/lack the courage of your conˈvictions
1117.cn: 有（或没有）勇气坚持信念
1117.e: She had the courage of her convictions and voted against her own party.  她坚持自己的信念，投票反对本党。

1118.i: have the courage of your conˈvictions
1118.cn: 敢于坚持自己认为对的事
1118.e: Few people have the courage of their convictions when their job is at risk.  饭碗受威胁时，很少有人还敢坚持己见。

1119.e: It took him a month to pluck up the courage to ask her out.  他花了一个月才鼓起勇气约她出去。

1120.i: take your ˌcourage in both ˈhands
1120.e: She took her courage in both hands and told the boss she was leaving.  她鼓起勇气告诉老板自己要走。

1121.i: take your ˌcourage in both ˈhands (informal)
1121.e: I took my courage in both hands and swam out to help him.  我壮着胆子游过去救他。

1122.e: The safest course of action is to postpone the trip until early spring.  最稳妥的做法是把行程推迟到早春。

1123.i: in the ˌnormal/ˌordinary course of eˈvents
1123.e: In the normal course of events, the results arrive within about ten days.  通常情况下，结果十天左右就会寄到。

1124.e: Of course you can borrow the car, just fill the tank afterwards.  你当然可以借车，用完加满油就行。

1125.e: Can I use your phone? Of course—help yourself, it's on the table.  我能用下你的电话吗？当然，请便，就在桌上。

1126.i: of ˈcourse not (also ˈcourse not informal)
1126.e: Of course not! I'd never tell your sister about the surprise trip.  当然不会！我绝不会把这次惊喜旅行告诉你姐姐。

1127.cn: 成为众人焦点；高谈阔论
1127.e: Uncle Ray was holding court in the kitchen with his fishing stories again.  雷叔叔又在厨房里大讲他的钓鱼故事，众人围听。

1128.e: The committee threw the proposal out of court before lunch on the first day.  委员会第一天午饭前就把这份提案否决了。

1129.i: the ball is in your/sb's ˈcourt
1129.e: I've made my offer, so now the ball is in their court.  我已经开出条件，现在轮到他们决定了。

1130.e: The photographs are reproduced courtesy of the city museum and its archive.  这些照片蒙市博物馆及其档案室惠允转载。

1131.i: do sb the courtesy of doing sth
1131.cn: 出于礼貌为某人做某事
1131.e: At least do me the courtesy of telling me before you cancel.  你要取消，至少有礼貌地事先跟我说一声。

1132.i: have the courtesy to do sth
1132.cn: 有礼貌地做某事；懂规矩
1132.e: He didn't even have the courtesy to reply to my second email.  他连回一封我第二封邮件的礼貌都没有。

1133.e: Bring both passports and the printout so we cover all the bases.  两本护照和打印件都带上，这样万无一失。

1134.i: cover your ˈback (informal) (AmE also cover your ˈass, slang)
1134.cn: 预防日后被追责；留一手
1134.e: Copy me into that email just to cover your back if things go wrong.  那封邮件抄送我一份，万一出事你也有个交代。

1135.e: The thieves covered their tracks by wiping the security footage before leaving.  窃贼离开前删掉监控录像，抹去了痕迹。

1136.e: She read the manual from cover to cover before touching the machine.  她把说明书从头读到尾才去碰那台机器。

1137.e: Two officers worked under cover in the warehouse for almost six months.  两名警官在仓库卧底了将近半年。

1138.e: They crossed the river under cover of darkness and reached the border.  他们借着夜色掩护渡过河，抵达了边境。

1139.e: Don't have a cow—I'll pay for the window I broke.  别急得跳脚，我打碎的窗户我赔。

1140.e: You can argue about politics till the cows come home and change nothing.  你可以没完没了地争政治，什么也改变不了。

1141.e: He cracked a joke about the weather and the whole room relaxed.  他拿天气开了个玩笑，全场气氛顿时轻松下来。

1142.e: We left at the crack of dawn to beat the holiday traffic.  我们天一亮就出发，好避开假日车流。

1143.cn: 严加督促；施压逼人干活
1143.e: The deadline is Friday, so the editor is cracking the whip today.  周五截稿，所以编辑今天开始严加督促。

1144.i: not be all it's cracked ˈup to be (informal)
1144.cn: 并不像人们说的那么好
1144.e: The famous beach was not all it's cracked up to be: crowded and grey.  那片名滩并没有传说中那么好，又挤又灰蒙蒙。

1145.e: Let's get cracking on the packing or we'll miss the morning ferry.  赶紧收拾行李吧，不然赶不上早班渡轮。

1146.i: from the ˌcradle to the ˈgrave
1146.e: The system was meant to care for citizens from the cradle to the grave.  这套制度本意是从生到死照顾国民。

1147.cn: 妨碍某人自由发挥；碍手碍脚
1147.e: Having my little brother along really cramped my style at the party.  带着弟弟去派对，实在让我放不开。

1148.i: do sb ˈcredit ◆ do ˈcredit to sb
1148.e: Her calm handling of the whole crisis really does her credit.  她冷静应对整场危机，实在令人称许。

1149.e: It is to his credit that he apologised in front of the whole team.  他能在全队面前道歉，这一点值得称赞。

1150.e: She already has three novels and a stage play to her credit.  她名下已有三部小说和一部舞台剧。

1151.cn: 就好的方面而言；从有利一面看
1151.e: On the credit side, the flat is cheap and close to the station.  好的方面是，这公寓便宜，又离车站近。

1152.i: up the ˈcreek (informal) (also up shit ˈcreek (without a ˈpaddle), slang)
1152.e: If the generator fails tonight, we are really up the creek.  今晚发电机要是罢工，我们就麻烦大了。

1153.cn: 使人毛骨悚然；起鸡皮疙瘩
1153.e: The way he stared at us across the room made my flesh creep.  他隔着房间那样盯着我们，看得我头皮发麻。

1154.i: the ˌcreme de la ˈcreme (from French, formal or humorous)
1154.e: These students are the creme de la creme of the entire music school.  这些学生是整所音乐学院里的精英。

1320.e: He worked himself to death trying to finish the book before Christmas.  为了赶在圣诞前写完书，他把自己累垮了。

1321.e: They ran into debt after both of them lost their jobs.  两人都失业后，他们欠了一屁股债。

1322.e: He acts confident, but deep down he's terrified of failing again.  他装得很自信，其实心底怕极了再失败。

1323.e: Dad went off the deep end when he saw the scratch on the car.  爸看到车上的划痕，一下就炸了。

1324.e: The company is in deep water after losing its biggest client.  丢了最大的客户后，公司陷入了大麻烦。

1325.i: jump in/be thrown in at the ˈdeep end
1325.cn: 一上来就被推去做难事
1325.e: On my first day I was thrown in at the deep end with angry customers.  上班第一天我就被推去应付发火的顾客。

1326.cn: 因无人竞争而（获胜）；默认地
1326.e: She became captain by default when nobody else wanted the job.  没人愿意干，她就顺理成章当上了队长。

1327.e: In default of better evidence, the case against him was dropped.  因缺乏更有力的证据，对他的指控被撤销。

1328.cn: 处于守势；采取戒备姿态
1328.e: Every question about the money put him on the defensive immediately.  一问到钱的事，他立刻就摆出防守的架势。

1329.cn: 迫使某人转入防御（或戒备）
1329.e: Warnings of an enemy attack forced the troops onto the defensive.  收到敌军进攻的警报，部队被迫转入防御。

1330.e: By degrees the noise died down and the children fell asleep.  声音渐渐小了，孩子们都睡着了。

1331.e: Walking into that kitchen gave me a strange sense of déjà vu.  走进那间厨房，我有种奇怪的似曾相识感。

1332.e: He's got delusions of grandeur since they made him deputy manager.  自从当上副经理，他就有点自我膨胀。

1333.e: Good electricians are always in demand in this part of town.  这一带好电工总是很抢手。

1334.e: The new service lets you watch any episode on demand.  新服务让你随时点播任何一集。

1335.e: By popular demand, the band added a second night in Manchester.  应观众要求，乐队在曼彻斯特加演了一场。

1336.e: He blames the demon drink for everything he said at the party.  派对上说的那些话，他全怪罪于酒。

1337.cn: 毫无异议地；毫不犹豫地
1337.e: She paid the extra charge without demur and left quickly.  她二话没说付了附加费，很快就走了。

1338.cn: 藏污纳垢之地；罪恶之所
1338.e: Their parents called that little jazz club a den of iniquity.  他们的父母把那家小爵士俱乐部叫作藏污纳垢之地。

1339.e: The new roof made a serious dent in our savings this year.  换屋顶今年花掉了我们一大笔积蓄。

1340.cn: 是某人的职责（或专长）范围
1340.e: Don't ask me about the wiring; that's really my brother's department.  别问我线路的事，那是我哥的专长。

1341.e: We need to discuss the safety report in depth before Friday.  周五之前我们得深入讨论这份安全报告。

1342.e: The cheat finally got his just deserts when the club expelled him.  那个作弊的人终于遭了报应，被俱乐部开除了。

1343.i: leave sb to their own deˈvices
1343.cn: 听任某人自便；不加干涉
1343.e: Left to his own devices, he'd eat crisps and play games all day.  没人管的话，他能整天吃薯片打游戏。

1344.cn: 大胆试一次吧；放纵一下
1344.e: Go on, be a devil and buy yourself that ridiculous red coat.  来吧，大胆点，把那件夸张的红大衣买下来。

1345.i: between the ˌdevil and the deep blue ˈsea
1345.e: Stay in a bad job or risk unemployment — between the devil and the deep blue sea.  是继续做烂工作还是冒险失业，真是进退两难。

1346.e: That old lock is the devil to open in cold weather.  天冷的时候那把旧锁难开得要命。

1347.i: the ˌdevil is in the ˈdetail(s)
1347.cn: 细节最要命；魔鬼藏在细节里
1347.e: The contract looks fine, but the devil is in the detail.  合同看着没问题，可细节最要命。

1348.i: the ˌdevil looks after his ˈown (saying)
1348.cn: 坏人反倒走运；恶人自有魔鬼护佑
1348.e: He crashed the car and walked away unhurt — the devil looks after his own.  他撞了车却毫发无伤，真是坏人有坏福。

1349.i: the devil makes work for idle ˈhands (saying)
1349.e: Give the boys a job — the devil makes work for idle hands.  给孩子们找点活干，闲着容易生事。

1350.i: a/the ˈdevil of a job, nuisance, fellow, etc.
1350.cn: 极费劲的事；极难缠的人
1350.e: It was a devil of a job getting the piano up those stairs.  把钢琴搬上那道楼梯真是费死劲了。

1351.e: Let me play devil's advocate and argue against your plan for a minute.  我来唱个反调，暂且反驳一下你的方案。

1352.cn: 各人顾各人；落后者活该
1352.e: In that market it's every trader for himself and devil take the hindmost.  在那个市场里人人自顾，落后的活该。

1353.e: He told his landlord to go to the devil and slammed the door.  他叫房东见鬼去吧，然后摔上了门。

1354.e: We ran like the devil to catch the last train home.  我们拼了命地跑，才赶上回家的末班车。

1355.e: Speak of the devil — we were just talking about you, Leo.  说曹操曹操到，我们刚还在说你呢，利奥。

1356.e: Where the devil did I put my glasses this time?  我这回到底把眼镜放哪儿了？

1357.cn: 被（强烈情感）吞噬；心中充满
1357.e: He was devoured by jealousy every time she mentioned her old boyfriend.  她一提起旧男友，他心里就被嫉妒吞噬。

1358.i: the ˌdice are loaded aˈgainst sb
1358.cn: 形势对某人不利；毫无胜算
1358.e: With no money and no contacts, the dice were loaded against her.  没钱没人脉，形势对她极为不利。

1359.e: Cycling through that junction without lights is dicing with death.  不开灯骑车穿那个路口简直是玩命。

1360.e: I asked for another week off, but the boss said no dice.  我想再请一周假，老板说没门。

1361.cn: （多用于否定）一点也没有；毫无
1361.e: He knows diddly-squat about engines but insists on fixing the car.  他对发动机一窍不通，还非要修车。

1362.e: Our fundraising appeal died a death once the council withdrew support.  议会一撤支持，我们的募捐活动就彻底黄了。

1363.e: His Othello died the death, and he never got another leading role.  他的奥赛罗演砸了，此后再没拿到主角。

1364.e: After all those wars he was lucky to die in his bed.  打了那么多仗，他能寿终正寝算是幸运。

1365.e: We've signed the lease, so the die is cast now.  租约已经签了，木已成舟。

1366.e: I nearly died laughing when he tried to dance at the wedding.  他在婚礼上跳舞那会儿，我差点笑死。

1367.i: make a, no, some, etc. ˈdifference (to/in sb/sth)
1367.cn: 有（或没有、有些）影响；起作用
1367.e: Your age shouldn't make any difference to whether you get the job.  你能否得到这份工作，不该跟年龄有关。

1368.cn: 还不都一样；没什么区别
1368.e: Bus or train, same difference — we'll still be late.  坐公交还是坐火车，还不都一样，反正要迟到。

1369.cn: 不是一个档次；高出一大截
1369.e: Their new striker is in a different league from the rest of us.  他们的新前锋跟我们完全不是一个档次。

1370.cn: 另一码事；截然不同的事
1370.e: Cooking for two is one thing; feeding thirty is a different kettle of fish.  给两个人做饭是一回事，喂三十个人完全是另一码事。

1371.e: He collects stamps and I collect records — different strokes for different folks.  他集邮我收唱片，各有各的爱好。

1372.cn: 给某人添麻烦；让某人日子难过
1372.e: Losing the keys really made life difficult for everyone that weekend.  钥匙丢了，那个周末大家都被折腾惨了。

1373.cn: 深挖细查；（也指）慷慨解囊
1373.e: You'll have to dig deep in the archives to find that letter.  你得在档案里深挖，才能找到那封信。

1374.e: She dug her heels in and refused to change the deadline.  她死不松口，坚决不肯改截止日期。

1375.i: dig your own ˈgrave • dig a ˈgrave for yourself
1375.e: By lying to the auditors he was digging his own grave.  对审计员撒谎，他这是在自掘坟墓。

1376.cn: 使自己陷入难以脱身的困境
1376.e: The more he explained, the deeper he dug himself into a hole.  他越解释，把自己陷得越深。

1377.e: Apparently washing his own coffee cup is beneath his dignity.  看来自己洗咖啡杯有失他的身份。

1378.cn: 摆架子；坚持要受到应有的礼遇
1378.e: She stood on her dignity and refused to answer such a rude question.  她摆出架子，拒绝回答这么无礼的问题。

1379.i: on a ˈdime (AmE) (BrE less frequent on a ˈsixpence)
1379.cn: 在极小的范围内；说停就停
1379.e: This little car can turn on a dime in a narrow street.  这辆小车在窄街上能原地掉头。

1380.cn: 为小钱斤斤计较；微不足道的
1380.e: Stop nickel-and-diming the staff over parking fees and coffee.  别在停车费和咖啡上跟员工斤斤计较了。

1381.cn: 亲自动手干活；沾手不干净的事
1381.e: A good manager isn't afraid to get their hands dirty on site.  好经理不怕到现场亲自动手。

1382.e: There's a dirty great hole in the road outside our house.  我们家门口路上有个大得吓人的坑。

1383.cn: 犯忌的字眼；忌讳的说法
1383.e: In this office the word 'overtime' has become a dirty word.  在这间办公室里，「加班」成了忌讳的字眼。

1384.i: do the ˈdirty on sb (BrE, informal)
1384.e: He did the dirty on his partner and took all the profits.  他暗算了合伙人，独吞了全部利润。

1385.e: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.  丢了那份工作反倒因祸得福。

1386.cn: 揭某人的隐私；说人闲话
1386.e: After a couple of drinks she started dishing the dirt on her boss.  几杯下肚，她开始爆老板的料。

1387.cn: 供某人随意使用；由某人支配
1387.e: The car and driver are at your disposal for the whole weekend.  车和司机整个周末都由你随意支配。

1388.e: You do her a disservice by calling her work amateurish.  你说她的作品业余，这对她不公平。

1389.e: From a distance the old barn still looks solid enough.  从远处看，那座旧谷仓还挺结实。

1390.e: Nobody thought the boxer would go the full distance against the champion.  没人想到那名拳手能跟冠军打满全场。

1391.e: We watched the ferry disappear into the distance from the harbour wall.  我们站在防波堤上看渡轮消失在远处。

1392.e: Since the argument she's kept her distance from the whole family.  自那次争吵后，她一直和全家人保持距离。

1393.e: He keeps new colleagues at a distance until he really trusts them.  他对新同事保持距离，直到真正信任对方。

1394.e: I could do with a strong coffee before this afternoon's meeting.  下午开会前我真想来杯浓咖啡。

1395.cn: 用不着；不需要（表示厌烦）
1395.e: I could do without him telling me what to say all the time.  我不需要他时时刻刻教我该怎么说话。

1396.e: I can do without your sarcastic comments while I'm trying to concentrate.  我正专心呢，用不着你在旁边说风凉话。

1397.e: The leaflet lists the do's and don'ts of driving in Italy.  这份传单列出了在意大利开车的注意事项。

1398.i: the do's and ˈdon'ts of sth (informal)
1398.e: She explained the do's and don'ts of choosing and buying your first car.  她讲了挑选和购买第一辆车的注意事项。

1399.e: That blue jacket really does something for you.  那件蓝外套特别衬你。

1400.i: it/that (just) won't ˈdo • it/that will never ˈdo
1400.e: Turning up late for every lesson simply won't do.  每节课都迟到，这可不行。

1401.e: Right, that does it — I'm not driving you anywhere again.  行了，够了，我再也不开车送你了。

1402.i: not ˈdo anything/a lot/much for sb (informal)
1402.e: That haircut really doesn't do much for you, if I'm honest.  说实话，那个发型真不怎么衬你。

1403.e: That will do, children — put the toys away and sit down.  行啦，孩子们，把玩具收好坐下。

1404.e: It's dog eat dog in this industry; nobody helps a rival.  这个行业里你死我活，没人会帮对手。

1405.e: Bad luck dogged his footsteps throughout that miserable season.  那个糟糕的赛季里，霉运一直缠着他。

1406.e: He won't use the garage himself but won't let us park there, a real dog in the manger.  他自己不用车库也不让我们停，真是占着茅坑不拉屎。

1407.e: He thinks his new sound system is the dog's bollocks.  他觉得自己的新音响棒得不得了。

1408.e: They've made a complete dog's breakfast of the new timetable.  新时刻表被他们弄得一团糟。

1409.cn: 悲惨的生活；猪狗不如的日子
1409.e: Working double shifts for that pay is a dog's life.  拿那点钱上两班倒，日子过得像狗一样。

1410.e: Don't give up now — every dog has his day, remember.  现在别放弃，人人都有走运的时候。

1411.i: give a dog a bad ˈname (and ˈhang him) (saying)
1411.e: One mistake and nobody trusts him — give a dog a bad name.  一次失误就没人信他了，名声坏了难翻身。

1412.i: why keep a ˌdog and bark yourˈself? (informal, saying)
1412.cn: 既然有人代劳，何必事必躬亲
1412.e: You hired an accountant, so why keep a dog and bark yourself?  你都请了会计，何必自己动手？

1413.i: be in the ˈdoghouse (South African be in the ˈdogbox) (informal)
1413.cn: 惹人生气而受冷落；失宠
1413.e: I forgot our anniversary, so I'm in the doghouse again.  我忘了结婚纪念日，又要被冷落了。

1414.i: go to the ˈdogs (AmE also go to hell in a ˈhandbasket) (informal)
1414.e: Since the new owners took over, the club has gone to the dogs.  新老板接手后，俱乐部就一路衰败下去。

1415.e: I can't be doing with all this paperwork before breakfast.  早饭前处理这一堆文件，我实在受不了。

1416.i: take some ˈdoing • take a lot of ˈdoing
1416.e: Getting all three kids ready by seven takes some doing.  七点前把三个孩子都收拾好可真不容易。

1417.e: What is my umbrella doing in the fridge, exactly?  我的伞到底怎么会在冰箱里？

1418.e: Sales have been in the doldrums since the shop moved.  搬店之后销售一直很萧条。

1419.e: If the rain doesn't stop soon, the whole harvest is done for.  雨要是再不停，这一季庄稼就完了。

1420.i: be/get ˈdone for sth/for doing sth (BrE, informal)
1420.e: He got done for speeding on the motorway last Tuesday.  他上周二在高速上超速被罚了。

1421.e: I've done with lending him money; he never pays it back.  我不再借钱给他了，他从来不还。

1422.e: Let's tell her tonight and get the whole thing over and done with.  今晚就跟她说，把这事彻底了结。

1423.e: The paperwork is done and dusted, so we can finally relax.  文件全部搞定，我们总算能歇口气了。

1424.cn: 板上钉钉的事；已定的安排
1424.e: Don't celebrate yet; the transfer isn't a done deal.  先别庆祝，转会还没板上钉钉。

1425.e: After moving furniture all day I'm completely done in.  搬了一天家具，我彻底累瘫了。

1426.cn: 合乎礼数的做法；得体的举止
1426.e: Arriving empty-handed at a dinner party isn't really the done thing.  空手去参加晚宴不太合规矩。

1427.e: The lamb came out of the oven done to a turn.  羊肉出炉时火候恰到好处。

1428.i: he, she, etc. has gone/been and ˈdone sth
1428.cn: 竟然干出（蠢事）；怎么搞的
1428.e: Now he's gone and told everyone about the surprise party.  他倒好，把惊喜派对的事跟所有人都说了。

1429.e: I haven't seen Maggie in donkey's years — how is she?  我好久没见玛吉了，她还好吗？

1430.e: She's been teaching at that school for donkey's years now.  她在那所学校教书已经好多年了。

1431.cn: 耍大牌的人；难伺候的角色
1431.e: The lead singer is a total prima donna about hotel rooms.  主唱在酒店房间的事上特别耍大牌。

1432.i: ˌdoom and ˈgloom • ˌgloom and ˈdoom
1432.e: It's not all doom and gloom; sales did rise last month.  也没那么悲观，上个月销量确实涨了。

1433.e: We could argue about this till doomsday and still not agree.  这事我们能吵到世界末日也谈不拢。

1434.e: Tom's on the door tonight, so tell him you're with the band.  今晚汤姆把门，就说你是乐队的人。

1435.cn: 走后门；通过不正当途径
1435.e: He got the job through the back door because his uncle owns the firm.  他走后门拿到工作，他叔叔是公司老板。

1436.cn: 从一处到另一处；挨家挨户
1436.e: The journey takes two hours door to door if the traffic behaves.  路上不堵的话，门到门要两小时。

1437.e: The manager left the door open for him to return next season.  经理留了余地，让他下赛季可以回来。

1438.e: Signing that contract closes the door on any further negotiation.  签了那份合同，就把再谈的门堵死了。

1439.e: The children spend all summer out of doors, whatever the weather.  不管天气如何，孩子们整个夏天都在户外。

1440.e: We've got a beautiful park right on our doorstep.  我们家门口就有个漂亮的公园。

1441.i: like a dose of ˈsalts (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
1441.e: She went through the paperwork like a dose of salts.  她处理那堆文件又快又利索。

1442.i: dot the/your ˌi's and cross the/your ˈt's
1442.e: Before we sign, let's dot the i's and cross the t's.  签字前，咱们把细节都抠清楚。

1443.e: She arrives at nine on the dot every single morning.  她每天早上九点整准时到。

1444.e: I'm not in my dotage yet — I can still read the timetable!  我还没老糊涂呢，时刻表我还看得懂！

1445.e: Refusing puts her in a double bind with both her boss and her family.  一拒绝，她在老板和家人之间都难做人。

1446.i: at the ˈdouble (BrE) (AmE on the ˈdouble)
1446.e: Get down to the office at the double; the inspector's already here.  快点到办公室来，检查员已经到了。

1447.e: I did a double take when I saw him wearing a suit.  看到他穿西装，我愣了一下才认出来。

1448.e: The instruction manual was complete double Dutch to me.  那本说明书对我来说就是天书。

1449.i: double or ˈquits (BrE) (AmE ˌdouble or ˈnothing)
1449.e: He offered me double or quits on the next hand of cards.  他提议下一把牌赌注加倍或一笔勾销。

1450.e: Rising rents and falling wages were a double whammy for young families.  房租涨、工资跌，对年轻家庭是双重打击。

1451.e: She is without doubt the best cellist in the whole orchestra.  她无疑是整个乐团最好的大提琴手。

1452.i: give sb the benefit of the ˈdoubt
1452.cn: 姑且相信某人；不妄下断语
1452.e: I'll give him the benefit of the doubt and assume he simply forgot.  我姑且相信他，就当他是忘了。

1453.e: Don't be such a doubting Thomas; come and see the results yourself.  别这么疑神疑鬼，自己来看看结果。

1454.e: I have my doubts about whether that roof will survive the winter.  那屋顶能不能撑过冬天，我很怀疑。

1455.e: The team's success is largely down to their new goalkeeper.  球队的成功很大程度上归功于新门将。

1456.e: We're down to our last packet of coffee, so add it to the list.  咖啡只剩最后一包了，记到清单上。

1457.e: He was down and out for two years before the shelter took him in.  收容所收留他之前，他潦倒流浪了两年。

1458.e: The recipe has been passed on down through the generations.  这道菜谱代代相传至今。

1459.e: Everyone came, down to the youngest child in the village.  所有人都来了，连村里最小的孩子都来了。

1460.cn: 在（或去）澳大利亚和新西兰
1460.e: My sister spent three years working down under before coming home.  我姐在澳洲工作了三年才回国。

1461.e: Once we passed the exam, it was all downhill from there.  考试一过，后面就轻松多了。

1462.e: The restaurant has gone downhill since the old chef left.  老厨师走后，这家餐厅一路下滑。

1463.i: keep it on the ˈdown-low (AmE, slang)
1463.e: Keep it on the down-low, but they're getting engaged next month.  别声张，他们下个月要订婚了。

1464.e: Complaints arrived by the dozen after the price increase.  涨价之后投诉成堆地涌来。

1465.e: The bakery gave us a baker's dozen instead of the twelve we ordered.  面包店给了我们十三个，我们只订了十二个。

1466.e: The council keeps dragging its feet over repairing the footbridge.  议会在修人行桥的事上一直拖着不办。

1467.i: pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps
1467.cn: 自力更生翻身；白手起家
1467.e: He pulled himself up by his bootstraps and now owns three shops.  他白手起家，现在有三家店。

1468.i: (go) down the ˈdrain (BrE also (go) down the ˈplughole) (informal)
1468.e: Ten years of research went down the drain when the lab burned.  实验室一烧，十年研究付诸东流。

1469.e: We drew straws for who had to tell the boss the bad news.  我们抽签决定谁去跟老板报坏消息。

1470.e: They've got three local ales on draught at the pub tonight.  今晚酒吧有三种本地桶装啤酒。

1471.e: He's quick on the draw with a joke whenever things get tense.  一有紧张气氛，他总能马上抖个包袱。

1472.e: Police searched the woods all day but drew a blank.  警方搜了一整天树林，却一无所获。

1473.cn: 在筹划阶段；尚在考虑中
1473.e: The new library is still on the drawing board, sadly.  可惜新图书馆还停留在图纸阶段。

1474.e: I dread to think what that repair is going to cost us.  我都不敢想那次维修要花我们多少钱。

1475.cn: 那要命的小毛病（如感冒）
1475.e: Half the office is off with the dreaded lurgy this week.  这周办公室一半人都染上那要命的感冒请假了。

1476.e: You think he'll pay you back? Dream on!  你觉得他会还钱？别做梦了！

1477.e: The whole week felt like a bad dream I couldn't wake from.  那一整周像一场醒不来的噩梦。

1478.i: not ˈdream of sth/of doing sth
1478.e: I wouldn't dream of asking her to work on a Sunday.  我绝不会叫她周日来上班。

1479.e: The new engine goes like a dream on the motorway.  新发动机在高速上跑得棒极了。

1480.e: A pay rise this year? In your dreams!  今年加薪？你做梦吧！

1481.cn: 远超想象；做梦也想不到
1481.e: The book sold beyond her wildest dreams in the first month.  第一个月的销量远远超出她的想象。

1482.cn: 打扮得极为惹眼；花枝招展
1482.e: She arrived at the party dressed to kill in scarlet silk.  她一身猩红丝裙出现在派对上，惊艳全场。

1483.e: Everyone turned up dressed to the nines for the awards dinner.  颁奖晚宴上人人都盛装出席。

1484.cn: 零零星星地；一点一点地
1484.e: Guests arrived in dribs and drabs all through the afternoon.  客人整个下午零零星星地陆续到来。

1485.e: Nothing about this case is cut and dried, so keep an open mind.  这案子没有定论，你先别下结论。

1486.e: I didn't hear every word, but I got the drift of his complaint.  我没听清每个字，但大概明白他在抱怨什么。

1487.cn: 跟不上思路；找不着头绪
1487.e: I lost the thread of the lecture about halfway through.  讲座讲到一半我就跟不上思路了。

1488.e: Let's raise our glasses and drink Anna's health on her birthday.  举杯，为安娜的生日祝她健康。

1489.cn: 把某人喝倒；酒量胜过某人
1489.e: She could drink most of the rugby team under the table.  橄榄球队大半人都能被她喝趴下。

1490.e: He drinks like a fish at weekends but never touches a drop midweek.  他周末喝起来没完，平时却滴酒不沾。

1491.i: drive a coach and ˈhorses through sth
1491.e: Their lawyers drove a coach and horses through the new tax rules.  他们的律师把新税规的空子钻了个透。

1492.cn: 某人想说的是；某人的言外之意
1492.e: I'm not sure what you're driving at — just say it plainly.  我不太明白你想说什么，直说吧。

1493.cn: 把某人逼疯；让人受不了
1493.e: That dripping tap is driving me insane at night.  那个滴水的龙头晚上快把我逼疯了。

1494.i: drive sb out of their ˈmind/ˈwits (informal)
1494.cn: 使某人发疯；让人焦虑万分
1494.e: Waiting for the test results drove her out of her mind.  等检查结果快把她逼疯了。

1495.e: These endless meetings will drive me to drink one day.  这没完没了的会，总有一天逼我借酒消愁。

1496.i: drive a wedge between A and B
1496.e: Gossip slowly drove a wedge between the two old friends.  流言渐渐离间了那两位老友。

1497.cn: （某事背后的）推动力量；主要推手
1497.e: She was the driving force behind the new road safety campaign.  她是新一轮道路安全运动的主要推手。

1498.i: in the ˈdriving seat (BrE) (AmE in the ˈdriver's seat)
1498.e: With the new contract signed, we're finally in the driving seat.  新合同一签，我们终于掌握了主动。

1499.cn: 抛出惊人消息；投下一颗炸弹
1499.e: He dropped a bombshell by announcing his resignation at breakfast.  他在早餐时宣布辞职，扔了颗重磅炸弹。

1500.cn: 无意中失言；说错话闯祸
1500.e: I dropped a clanger by asking about his wife — they divorced last year.  我一问他太太就说错话了，他们去年离婚了。

1501.e: He told the reporters to drop dead and walked off.  他叫记者们见鬼去，转身就走。

1502.i: drop a ˈhint (to sb) • drop sb a ˈhint
1502.e: She dropped a hint about wanting a bicycle for her birthday.  她暗示想要辆自行车当生日礼物。

1503.e: She's dropped me a few hints about what she'd like for her birthday.  她暗示过我几次她想要什么生日礼物。

1504.cn: 害某人陷入尴尬（或麻烦）
1504.e: Thanks for dropping me in it by telling Mum where I was.  谢谢你告诉我妈我在哪，把我给坑了。

1505.i: a ˌdrop in the ˈocean (BrE) (AmE a ˌdrop in the ˈbucket)
1505.e: A hundred pounds is a drop in the ocean compared with the repair bill.  跟维修账单比，一百镑不过是杯水车薪。

1506.cn: 给某人写封短信（或便条）
1506.e: Drop me a line when you get settled in the new flat.  在新公寓安顿好了就写封短信给我。

1507.e: He drops names constantly, as if we care who he met.  他老提认识的名人，好像谁在乎似的。

1508.e: After the double shift I was fit to drop.  连上两班之后我累得快垮了。

1509.e: Let it drop, will you? Nobody wants to argue tonight.  这事就别提了行吗？今晚谁也不想吵。

1510.e: After the interview he went to the pub to drown his sorrows.  面试完他去酒吧借酒浇愁。

1511.e: She came in from the storm looking like a drowned rat.  她冒着暴雨进来，活像只落汤鸡。

1512.e: He was drugged up to the eyeballs after the operation.  手术后他被打了一身的药。

1513.e: She's been banging the drum for local libraries all year.  她整年都在为本地图书馆奔走呼吁。

1514.i: (as) drunk as a ˈlord (BrE) (AmE (as) drunk as a ˈskunk) (informal)
1514.e: He came home drunk as a lord and fell asleep on the stairs.  他烂醉如泥地回家，倒在楼梯上就睡着了。

1515.e: The soil in these pots is as dry as a bone.  这些花盆里的土干得不能再干了。

1516.e: His lecture on drainage law was as dry as dust.  他那堂排水法的课枯燥得要命。

1517.e: The agents milked the young singer dry and then dropped her.  经纪人把那位年轻歌手榨干后就甩了她。

1518.e: You'll receive a written reply in due course, probably next week.  你会在适当的时候收到书面答复，大概下周。

1519.i: not a dry eye in the ˈhouse (humorous)
1519.e: When she sang that last song there wasn't a dry eye in the house.  她唱最后一首时，全场无不落泪。

1520.e: The village well ran dry after that long, hot summer.  那个漫长炎热的夏天过后，村里的井干了。

1521.i: (take to sth) like a ˌduck to ˈwater
1521.cn: 如鱼得水；毫不费力就上手
1521.e: She took to teaching like a duck to water in her first week.  第一周她就把教书干得如鱼得水。

1522.e: Their new model leaves every competitor in the dust on price.  他们的新型号在价格上把对手全甩在了后面。

1523.i: let the ˈdust settle (also wait for the ˈdust to settle)
1523.cn: 等尘埃落定；等局势明朗
1523.e: Let the dust settle for a week before you talk to him again.  等一周尘埃落定，再去跟他谈。

1524.e: Mention washing up and you won't see him for dust.  一提洗碗，他立马就没影了。

1525.cn: 生硬的答复；毫无帮助的回答
1525.e: My request for more time got a dusty answer from the committee.  我要求延期，委员会给了个冷冰冰的回复。

1526.e: He had two whiskies for Dutch courage before the speech.  演讲前他喝了两杯威士忌壮胆。

1527.e: We always go Dutch when the four of us eat out.  我们四个出去吃饭一向各付各的。

1528.e: I'd love to stay for another coffee, but duty calls now.  我真想留下再喝杯咖啡，可正事要紧。

1529.e: The nurse goes off duty at eight and won't be back until Monday.  护士八点下班，要到周一才回来。

1530.i: be ˈdying for sth/to do sth (informal)
1530.e: I'm dying for a cold drink after that walk up the hill.  爬完那座山，我特别想来杯冷饮。

1531.e: Open a window, I'm dying of heat in here.  开扇窗吧，我在这儿热死了。

1532.e: He'll insist he was right until his dying day.  他到死都会坚称自己没错。

1533.cn: 干劲十足的人；工作热心的人
1533.e: The new intern is a real eager beaver, always first in.  新来的实习生特别积极，总是第一个到。

1534.e: Nothing escapes the manager's eagle eye on the shop floor.  车间里什么也逃不过经理的火眼金睛。

1535.e: Turn up late once more and you'll be out on your ear.  再迟到一次，你就得卷铺盖走人。

1536.cn: 笑得合不拢嘴；眉开眼笑
1536.e: He was grinning from ear to ear when they announced his name.  报到他名字时，他笑得合不拢嘴。

1537.i: go in ˈone ear and out the ˈother (informal)
1537.cn: 左耳进右耳出；当耳边风
1537.e: Everything I say about tidying goes in one ear and out the other.  我说的收拾屋子的话，他左耳进右耳出。

1538.i: have sb's ˈear • have the ear of sb (formal)
1538.e: She has the ear of the minister, so her opinion carries weight.  她在部长那里说得上话，意见很有分量。

1539.e: He has a good ear for accents and mimics them perfectly.  他对口音很敏感，模仿得惟妙惟肖。

1540.cn: 不看乐谱凭听觉演奏；见机行事
1540.e: We don't have a plan for the meeting, so let's just play it by ear.  会议没什么计划，咱们见机行事吧。

1541.e: Please return the signed contract to our office at your earliest convenience.  请尽早将签好的合同寄回我们办公室。

1542.i: the ˌearly bird catches the ˈworm (saying)
1542.cn: 早起的鸟儿有虫吃；捷足先登
1542.e: She queued at six to grab the sale item: the early bird catches the worm.  她六点就去排队抢特价品，真是早起的鸟儿有虫吃。

1543.e: We realized early on that the software would never be ready by June.  我们很早就意识到这软件六月前根本做不完。

1544.e: He drives a taxi at night to earn a crust while writing his novel.  他晚上开出租车糊口，白天写小说。

1545.cn: 挣得自己的开销；值得雇用
1545.e: Even the old cat earns his keep by scaring the mice out of the barn.  连那只老猫也靠赶走谷仓里的老鼠挣自己的口粮。

1546.e: After the holidays, work on the new bridge finally began in earnest.  假期一过，新桥的施工终于正式动了起来。

1547.e: Tell me what happened at the party last night, I'm all ears.  快说说昨晚聚会上发生了什么，我洗耳恭听。

1548.i: be up to your ˈears in sth
1548.e: I can't come out tonight, I'm up to my ears in marking papers.  今晚我出不去，改卷子改得焦头烂额。

1549.cn: 传入某人耳中；终于让某人知道
1549.e: News of the merger reached his ears long after everyone else knew.  合并的消息传到他耳朵里时，别人早都知道了。

1550.i: his, her, etc. ˈears are burning
1550.cn: 耳朵发热（觉得有人在议论自己）
1550.e: We were talking about Tom all afternoon, so his ears must be burning.  我们整个下午都在说汤姆，他耳朵准发热了。

1551.i: his, her, etc. ˈears are flapping (BrE, informal)
1551.cn: 有人在竖着耳朵偷听；隔墙有耳
1551.e: Lower your voice, the neighbour's ears are flapping over the garden fence.  小点声，隔壁正隔着篱笆竖着耳朵听呢。

1552.e: He simply shut his ears to every warning his colleagues gave him.  同事们的警告他一概充耳不闻。

1553.e: She waited until the children were out of earshot before mentioning the divorce.  她等孩子们走远听不见了才提起离婚的事。

1554.e: Don't say anything about the surprise while Grandma is within earshot.  奶奶还听得见，别提惊喜的事。

1555.i: bring sb/come (back) down to ˈearth (with a ˈbang, ˈbump, etc.)
1555.e: The rejection letter brought him back down to earth with a bump.  那封拒信一下子把他打回了现实。

1556.e: That little handbag looks plain but it must have cost the earth.  那只小包看着普通，肯定贵得吓人。

1557.e: After the robbery the gang went to ground in a farmhouse for weeks.  抢劫之后，那伙人在一处农舍躲了好几个星期。

1558.i: how, what, why, etc. on ˈearth... (informal)
1558.e: How on earth did you manage to lose your passport twice in one week?  你到底是怎么做到一周丢两次护照的？

1559.e: After three nights without sleep she looked like nothing on earth.  三夜没睡，她看上去糟糕透了。

1560.cn: 任何东西都不；无论如何也不
1560.e: Nothing on earth would persuade me to go back and work for him.  说什么我也不会回去给他干活。

1561.e: The reporter finally ran the missing witness to earth in a seaside hotel.  记者最终在一家海边旅馆找到了失踪的证人。

1562.e: Her warm smile put the nervous candidates completely at their ease.  她温暖的笑容让紧张的应聘者彻底放松下来。

1563.e: The sergeant barked at the recruits to stand at ease before the inspection.  检阅前，军士喝令新兵稍息。

1564.e: Saving half your salary every month is easier said than done.  每月存下一半工资，说起来容易做起来难。

1565.e: He lost his lottery winnings in a month, but shrugged: easy come, easy go.  他一个月就把彩票奖金输光了，只耸耸肩说来得容易去得快。

1566.cn: 易受攻击的对象；容易上钩的人
1566.e: Tourists with open backpacks are easy game for pickpockets in this square.  背着敞口背包的游客在这个广场上是扒手的活靶子。

1567.cn: 来得容易的钱；不义之财
1567.e: He thought reselling concert tickets was easy money until the police called.  他以为倒卖演唱会门票是轻松来钱，直到警察找上门。

1568.i: ˌeasy on the ˈeye, ˈear, etc.
1568.e: The new website is simple and very easy on the eye.  新网站简洁，看着很舒服。

1569.cn: 对某人别太苛刻；温和对待某人
1569.e: Go easy on him, it's only his second day behind the counter.  别太严厉，他站柜台才第二天。

1570.e: Go easy on the chilli, my parents can't handle spicy food at all.  辣椒少放点，我爸妈完全吃不了辣。

1571.i: have an easy ˈtime of it (BrE, informal)
1571.cn: 日子过得顺当；境况轻松
1571.e: Nurses on the night shift certainly don't have an easy time of it.  上夜班的护士日子可真不轻松。

1572.e: Pizza or noodles? I'm easy, you two decide tonight.  披萨还是面条？我都行，你俩定吧。

1573.e: One good patent and the whole family was suddenly on easy street.  一项好专利，全家一下子就衣食无忧了。

1574.cn: 选择最省事的解决办法
1574.e: Instead of apologizing, he took the easy way out and just quit.  他没道歉，图省事直接辞职了。

1575.e: The doctor told her to take things easy for at least two weeks.  医生让她至少休养两周，别太累。

1576.cn: 严厉责骂某人；彻底击败某人
1576.e: Walk into that debate unprepared and they will eat you alive.  毫无准备就上台辩论，他们会把你吃得连渣都不剩。

1577.e: It's your last night in Rome, so eat, drink and be merry.  这是你在罗马的最后一晚，好好吃喝玩乐吧。

1578.cn: （夸自己更胜一筹）某某该羡慕了
1578.e: Look at my homemade pasta. Eat your heart out, Italian chefs!  瞧我做的手擀意面，意大利大厨都得眼红。

1579.i: eat your ˈheart out (for sb/sth) (especially BrE)
1579.cn: 因得不到而伤心；苦苦思念
1579.e: She spent that whole winter eating her heart out for a man who never wrote.  那整个冬天她都在为一个从不来信的男人黯然神伤。

1580.e: When the figures proved him wrong, the manager had to eat humble pie.  数据证明他错了，经理只好低头认错。
