1581.e: She eats like a bird, half a sandwich and she's already full.  她吃得跟小鸟似的，半个三明治就饱了。

1582.e: My teenage son is thin but he eats like a horse every evening.  我那十几岁的儿子很瘦，可每天晚上吃得像头牛。

1583.i: eat sb out of ˌhouse and ˈhome (informal, often humorous)
1583.cn: 把某人的食物吃个精光
1583.e: Three hungry students stayed a week and ate us out of house and home.  三个饿坏了的学生住了一周，把我家吃了个精光。

1584.cn: 收回前言；承认自己说错
1584.e: You said I'd never finish the marathon, now eat your words.  你说我跑不完马拉松，现在收回你的话吧。

1585.e: Is dinner nearly ready? I skipped lunch and I could eat a horse.  饭快好了吗？我没吃午饭，饿得能吞下一头牛。

1586.e: If that lazy team wins the cup, I'll eat my hat.  那支懒散的队要是能夺冠，我把帽子吃了。

1587.i: he, she, etc. won't ˈeat you (informal)
1587.e: Just knock on the boss's door and ask, she won't eat you.  去敲老板的门问一声，她又不会吃了你。

1588.e: The extra training gave our team the edge over their rivals.  额外的训练让我们队比对手略胜一筹。

1589.cn: 某人为何发愁（或不高兴）
1589.e: He's been slamming doors all morning, what's eating him?  他一上午都在摔门，到底怎么了？

1590.e: The novel traces the ebb and flow of a marriage over thirty years.  这部小说描写了一段婚姻三十年的起起落落。

1591.e: Everyone in the office was on edge waiting for the layoff announcement.  等着裁员通知，办公室里人人都提心吊胆。

1592.cn: 说话有所隐瞒；不全说实话
1592.e: The minister wasn't lying exactly, just being economical with the truth.  部长算不上撒谎，只是没把话说全。

1593.cn: 减轻；缓和；使不那么强烈
1593.e: A hot bath took the edge off the pain in her shoulders.  洗个热水澡缓解了她肩膀的疼痛。

1594.cn: 有根据的猜测；有把握的估计
1594.e: I'd make an educated guess that the repairs will cost about two thousand.  我大致估摸修理费在两千左右。

1595.e: The council will bring the new parking rules into effect next Monday.  市政会下周一起实施新的停车规定。

1596.e: The ban on plastic bags comes into effect at the start of next year.  塑料袋禁令将于明年年初生效。

1597.e: He still signs the letters, but in effect his daughter runs the company.  信还是他签，可实际上是女儿在管公司。

1598.cn: 无效；没有达到预期效果
1598.e: She argued with the referee for ten minutes, but to no effect.  她跟裁判争了十分钟，一点用也没有。

1599.e: Wait twenty minutes for the painkiller to take effect before you drive.  等二十分钟让止痛药起效再开车。

1600.i: to the effect that... ◆ to this/that efˈfect
1600.e: He left a note to the effect that he would not be coming back.  他留了张条，大意是说他不回来了。

1601.e: She used her three minutes to great effect and won the whole room over.  她把那三分钟用得极好，赢得了全场支持。

1602.i: with effect from... ◆ with immediate efˈfect
1602.e: Ticket prices will rise with effect from the first of April.  票价自四月一日起上调。

1603.e: The driver got out effing and blinding about the dent in his bumper.  司机下了车，对着凹进去的保险杠骂骂咧咧。

1604.e: The minister was left with egg on his face when the figures turned out wrong.  数据被证明是错的，部长丢尽了脸。

1605.i: put all your eggs into one ˈbasket
1605.cn: 孤注一掷；把全部希望寄托于一事
1605.e: Apply to several universities, don't put all your eggs into one basket.  多申请几所大学，别在一棵树上吊死。

1606.e: Judging by his singing, Dave has had one over the eight tonight.  听他那唱腔，戴夫今晚是喝多了。

1607.cn: 处于困境；面临不利局面
1607.e: Losing our biggest client put the whole team behind the eight ball.  丢了最大的客户，整个团队都陷入了困境。

1608.e: Grandma always said children should listen to their elders and betters.  奶奶总说小孩子该听长辈的话。

1609.e: He writes with a strong coffee and an old dictionary at his elbow.  他写作时手边总放着浓咖啡和一本旧词典。

1610.e: That old stove will shine again with soap and a bit of elbow grease.  那台旧炉子用肥皂加把力气擦擦还能亮起来。

1611.e: The new budget gives the department some elbow room for research.  新预算给这个部门留了些做研究的余地。

1612.e: At that charity dinner she rubbed elbows with half the city council.  在那场慈善晚宴上，她跟半个市议会都打了照面。

1613.e: She finally gave him the elbow after he forgot her birthday again.  他又忘了她生日，她终于把他甩了。

1614.cn: 资深政治家；德高望重的元老
1614.e: Now retired, he acts as an elder statesman for the younger members.  他已退休，如今给年轻成员当元老顾问。

1615.cn: 否则；要不然（含威胁意味）
1615.e: Hand in the report by Friday, or else you'll be explaining it to the boss.  周五前交报告，否则你自己跟老板解释去。

1616.cn: 了不起的人（或事物）；与众不同
1616.e: You have to hear her sing live, that voice is really something else.  你得听她现场唱，那嗓子真是绝了。

1617.e: With four excellent candidates, the panel faced an embarrassment of riches.  四位候选人都很优秀，评委反倒难以取舍。

1618.cn: 尚在萌芽阶段；处于初期
1618.e: The festival existed only in embryo when we first discussed it.  我们最初谈起时，这个音乐节还只是个雏形。

1619.cn: 皇帝的新装（众人不敢说破的虚假）
1619.e: Critics called the whole project a case of the emperor's new clothes.  评论家说整个项目就是一场皇帝的新装。

1620.cn: 皇帝没穿衣服（其实并不出色）
1620.e: One junior analyst finally said the emperor has no clothes, and the room fell silent.  一个初级分析师终于说破了真相，全场鸦雀无声。

1621.cn: 空巢（子女离家后的家庭）
1621.e: They bought a puppy to fill the empty nest after their son left.  儿子走后，他们养了只小狗来填补空巢。

1622.e: Never take these tablets on an empty stomach, they'll make you sick.  千万别空腹吃这些药，会难受的。

1623.e: He wants the corner office, the car, the whole enchilada.  他要角落的办公室、要车，什么都想要。

1624.i: at the ˌend of the ˈday (BrE, spoken)
1624.e: At the end of the day, it's your money and your decision.  说到底，钱是你的，主意也该你拿。

1625.e: After forty years of service, his career at the bank was at an end.  在银行干了四十年，他的职业生涯到此结束。

1626.i: be at the ˌend of your ˈtether (BrE) (AmE be at the ˌend of your ˈrope)
1626.e: With three sick children at home, she was at the end of her tether.  家里三个孩子都病了，她已经撑到极限。

1627.cn: 让人无法忍受；讨厌至极
1627.e: Honestly, that man is the end, he complains about everything.  说真的，那人烦死了，什么都要抱怨。

1628.e: We argued for hours and in the end just tossed a coin.  我们争了几小时，最后干脆抛硬币决定。

1629.e: It rained for days on end and the campsite turned into mud.  连着下了好几天雨，营地成了一片泥浆。

1630.i: not be the ˌend of the ˈworld (spoken)
1630.cn: 不是世界末日；没那么糟
1630.e: If you fail the test, it's not the end of the world, you can retake it.  考砸了也不是世界末日，还能重考。

1631.e: When the bank refused another loan, it was the end of the road for the shop.  银行拒绝再贷款，这家店也就走到头了。

1632.cn: 使收支相抵；勉强维持生活
1632.e: With rent this high, two salaries barely make ends meet.  房租这么贵，两份工资也就勉强够花。

1633.i: to the ˌends of the ˈearth
1633.cn: 天涯海角；任何遥远的地方
1633.e: He said he would follow her to the ends of the earth.  他说他愿意跟着她走到天涯海角。

1634.e: Can you explain the contract in plain English for the rest of us?  你能用大白话给我们解释一下合同吗？

1635.i: an ˌEnglishman's ˌhome is his ˈcastle (BrE) (saying)
1635.cn: 英国人的家就是他的城堡
1635.e: He locked the gate and muttered that an Englishman's home is his castle.  他锁上大门，嘟囔说自己的家就是自己的城堡。

1636.i: a ˌman's ˌhome is his ˈcastle (AmE) (saying)
1636.cn: 家是私人领地，不容他人干涉
1636.e: You can't just walk in here, a man's home is his castle.  你不能就这么闯进来，家是人家的地盘。

1637.e: That last summer by the lake is engraved on my memory forever.  湖边的最后一个夏天永远刻在我记忆里。

1638.e: He was seen leaving her flat at dawn. Enough said.  有人看见他天亮时从她公寓出来，不用多说了。

1639.e: Funnily enough, I was just thinking about you when you called.  说来也巧，你打来时我正想着你呢。

1640.e: I've covered his shifts three times this month, enough is enough.  这个月我替他值了三次班，够了。

1641.e: I've had enough of these excuses, just finish the job.  这些借口我听够了，把活干完吧。

1642.cn: 被某人想到；进入某人脑中
1642.e: It never entered my head that she might say no.  我压根没想过她会拒绝。

1643.cn: 为某人（或自己）报名参加
1643.e: Her father entered her name for the piano competition without telling her.  她父亲没告诉她就给她报了钢琴比赛。

1644.i: get/enter into the ˈspirit of sth
1644.e: Even the shy new intern entered into the spirit of the office party.  连腼腆的新实习生也玩进了办公室派对的气氛。

1645.e: The speech was broadcast in its entirety on the evening news.  这篇讲话在晚间新闻中全文播出。

1646.e: This young director really pushes the envelope with every new film.  这位年轻导演每拍一部新片都在突破界限。

1647.e: Their public transport system is the envy of every neighbouring city.  他们的公共交通系统让周边城市都羡慕。

1648.i: be without ˈequal ◆ have no ˈequal (formal)
1648.e: As a cellist of her generation, she is quite without equal.  在同代大提琴家中，她无人能及。

1649.i: be ˈequal to sth/to doing sth
1649.e: Nobody thought the young lawyer would be equal to such a difficult case.  谁都没想到这位年轻律师能应付这么棘手的案子。

1650.e: The small firm now competes on equal terms with the big studios.  这家小公司如今能和大制片厂平起平坐地竞争了。

1651.e: Part-time staff are paid on the same terms as everyone else here.  这里的兼职员工和其他人待遇相同。

1652.i: some ˌanimals are more ˈequal than others (saying)
1652.cn: 有些人比别人更享特权
1652.e: The boss's nephew got the promotion; some animals are more equal than others.  老板的侄子升职了，有些人就是比别人更平等。

1653.e: Speed is of the essence if we want to catch the last ferry.  想赶上末班渡轮，快是关键。

1654.i: err on the side of ˈcaution, ˈgenerosity, etc.
1654.cn: 宁可失之于（谨慎、宽厚等）
1654.e: When marking papers I always err on the side of generosity.  改卷子时我宁可打分宽一点。

1655.cn: 即使现在（那时）；尽管如此
1655.e: He apologized twice, but even now she refuses to speak to him.  他道了两次歉，可她到现在还是不理他。

1656.e: They beat us last season, so tonight we're here to even the score.  上赛季他们赢了我们，今晚我们是来扯平的。

1657.e: The tickets were expensive; even so, the concert was worth every penny.  票很贵，尽管如此，这场音乐会还是很值。

1658.i: have an even ˈchance (of doing sth)
1658.cn: 有一半的机会；成败各半
1658.e: The doctors say she has an even chance of making a full recovery.  医生说她完全康复的机会有一半。

1659.cn: 结果；到头来（与预期相反）
1659.e: We feared a storm, but in the event the wedding day was sunny.  我们担心会有暴风雨，结果婚礼那天阳光明媚。

1660.i: in the event of sth ◆ in the event that sth
1660.e: In the event of a power cut, the emergency lights come on automatically.  万一停电，应急灯会自动亮起。

1661.cn: 金钱（或取胜等）并非最重要
1661.e: He turned down the offer, saying money isn't everything at his age.  他拒绝了这份工作，说到他这年纪钱不是一切。

1662.i: turn King's/Queen's ˈevidence (BrE) (AmE turn State's ˈevidence)
1662.cn: 指证同伙以求从轻发落
1662.e: The youngest robber turned Queen's evidence and named the other three.  那个最年轻的劫匪转做污点证人，供出了另外三人。

1663.cn: 难熬的时刻；不愉快的日子
1663.e: He kept watching videos to put off the evil hour of writing his essay.  他一直看视频，好推迟写论文那个难熬的时刻。

1664.e: The old woman gave the noisy boys the evil eye across the bus.  老太太隔着车厢恶狠狠地瞪了那几个吵闹的男孩一眼。

1665.e: The head teacher made an example of him to stop others cheating.  校长拿他开刀，以免别人再作弊。

1666.e: Parents who read every night set a good example for their children.  每晚读书的父母给孩子树立了好榜样。

1667.i: the exˈception that proves the ˈrule (saying)
1667.e: He's the one honest politician here, the exception that proves the rule.  他是这里唯一诚实的政客，正是那个证明通例的例外。

1668.e: I take exception to your suggestion that I did it purely for money.  我不能接受你暗示我这么做纯粹是为了钱。

1669.e: Every essay, without exception, must be handed in before noon.  所有论文一律必须在中午前交。

1670.e: Excuse me, is this seat taken or may I sit here?  劳驾，这位子有人吗，我可以坐吗？

1671.cn: 某人的祸根；烦恼的根源
1671.e: That leaking roof has been the bane of my life all winter.  那个漏雨的屋顶让我整个冬天不得安宁。

1672.e: You left the door open all night, so what do you expect?  你整夜开着门，还能指望什么呢？

1673.e: Against all expectations, the little team reached the final that year.  出乎所有人意料，那支小球队那年打进了决赛。

1674.e: A few mistakes in the first week are only to be expected.  头一周出点差错是很正常的。

1675.e: She's expecting again, due some time around Christmas.  她又怀孕了，预产期在圣诞节前后。

1676.cn: 由某人付账；拿某人取笑
1676.e: The whole trip was arranged at the company's expense.  整趟旅行的费用都由公司承担。

1677.e: He built the business at the expense of his health and his marriage.  他把生意做起来，代价是健康和婚姻。

1678.i: go to the exˈpense of sth/of doing sth
1678.e: They went to the expense of hiring a band for the anniversary party.  他们不惜花钱为周年派对请了乐队。

1679.i: go to a lot of, great, etc. exˈpense
1679.e: Please don't go to a lot of expense, a simple dinner is fine.  别太破费了，简单吃顿饭就行。

1680.i: put sb to the exˈpense of sth/of doing sth
1680.e: The delay put us to the expense of booking another hotel room.  延误害得我们又花钱订了一间旅馆房。

1681.i: put sb to a lot of, great, etc. exˈpense
1681.e: Sending the piano abroad put her parents to considerable expense.  把钢琴运到国外让她父母花了不少钱。

1682.i: put sth down to exˈperience (also chalk it up to exˈperience especially AmE)
1682.cn: 吃一堑长一智；当作教训
1682.e: We lost the deposit, so let's just put it down to experience.  定金打了水漂，就当买个教训吧。

1683.e: You came home at three in the morning, now explain yourself.  你凌晨三点才回家，说清楚是怎么回事。

1684.i: boring, silly, etc. in the exˈtreme
1684.e: His speech about tax forms was boring in the extreme.  他那篇讲报税表的发言无聊透顶。

1685.e: She goes to extremes, cleaning the kitchen floor three times a day.  她做事太极端，一天擦三遍厨房地板。

1686.e: Being careful is fine, but you're taking it to extremes by never going out.  谨慎是好事，可你从不出门就过头了。

1687.i: an ˌeye for an ˈeye (and a ˌtooth for a ˈtooth) (saying)
1687.e: Their whole feud runs on an eye for an eye and nobody ever wins.  他们这场世仇就是以眼还眼，谁也没赢过。

1688.e: Once she got her eye in, she hit four boundaries in a row.  一找到手感，她连着打出四个边界球。

1689.i: give your eye ˈteeth for sth/to do sth (informal)
1689.cn: 极想得到某物；不惜代价想做某事
1689.e: Any young pianist would give their eye teeth for a chance like this.  任何年轻钢琴家都会为这样的机会付出一切。

1690.e: She has a good eye for colour and puts outfits together beautifully.  她对色彩很有眼光，衣服搭得漂亮。

1691.e: I've had my eye on that little flat by the river for months.  河边那套小公寓我已经惦记好几个月了。

1692.i: have an eye to/for the main ˈchance (BrE, disapproving)
1692.cn: 善于抓住机会为己谋利
1692.e: With an eye to the main chance, he bought the land before prices rose.  他很会算计，赶在涨价前买下了那块地。

1693.i: have one eye/half an eye on sth
1693.e: He listened to me with half an eye on the football match.  他一边听我说，一边分神看着球赛。

1694.e: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy the tickets?  我去买票，你帮我看一下包好吗？

1695.e: Would you run an eye over this letter before I send it?  这封信我寄出去之前，你能帮我扫一眼吗？

1696.i: keep your eye on the ˈball
1696.cn: 专注要点；不分散注意力
1696.e: Too many side projects, we need to keep our eye on the ball.  副业太多了，我们得盯紧正事。

1697.e: Keep an eye out for a red van, that's the delivery man.  留意一辆红色面包车，那是送货的。

1698.e: He says he forgot the meeting? Too busy at work, my eye!  他说他忘了开会？说什么工作太忙，胡扯！

1699.i: one in the eye for sb/sth (informal)
1699.cn: 对…的打击；令…难堪的挫折
1699.e: The court ruling was one in the eye for the property developers.  这项判决给开发商当头一棒。

1700.e: My brother and I have never seen eye to eye about money.  我和哥哥在钱的事上从来谈不拢。

1701.cn: 在某人的注视（或监督）下
1701.e: The apprentices worked under the watchful eye of an old carpenter.  学徒们在一位老木匠的注视下干活。

1702.i: what the eye doesn't ˈsee (the heart doesn't ˈgrieve over) (saying)
1702.e: I never tell him how much the shoes cost; what the eye doesn't see.  我从不告诉他鞋子多少钱，眼不见心不烦。

1703.i: with an eye to sth/to doing sth
1703.e: She's taking an interpreting course with an eye to working abroad.  她在上口译课，想着以后到国外工作。

1704.e: Working night shifts in the hospital was a real eye-opener for me.  在医院上夜班让我大开眼界。

1705.e: The two managers stood eyeball to eyeball arguing about the referee's decision.  两位主教练面对面站着，为裁判的判罚争执不下。

1706.e: Come up to the roof and get an eyeful of that sunset.  上屋顶来，好好看看那片晚霞。

1707.e: All eyes are on the young striker as he steps up to take the penalty.  年轻前锋走上前主罚点球，全场目光都盯着他。

1708.e: The children were all eyes when the magician opened his box.  魔术师打开箱子时，孩子们看得目不转睛。

1709.i: be up to your ˈeyes/ˈeyeballs in sth
1709.e: She's up to her eyeballs in paperwork and can't take another case.  她被文书工作淹没了，接不了新案子。

1710.e: The old cinema was torn down before our very eyes in a single morning.  那家老电影院一个上午就在我们眼前被拆掉了。

1711.e: The moment I set eyes on the house, I knew I wanted to live there.  第一眼看见那房子，我就知道我想住那儿。

1712.cn: 留心观察；睁大眼睛注意
1712.e: Keep your eyes peeled for a parking space near the entrance.  留意一下入口附近有没有停车位。

1713.i: have eyes in the back of your ˈhead (informal)
1713.e: You can't fool that teacher, she has eyes in the back of her head.  别想骗那位老师，她后脑勺上都长着眼睛。

1714.e: Our accountant has eyes like a hawk and spots every missing receipt.  我们的会计眼睛毒得很，少一张收据都逃不过。

1715.e: Her comedy is loud and in your face, but the audience loves it.  她的喜剧张扬又冲，可观众就吃这一套。

1716.i: disappear/vanish off the face of the ˈearth
1716.e: After the trial he seemed to vanish off the face of the earth.  庭审之后，他好像从地球上消失了。

1717.cn: 不被接纳；不合某处的口味
1717.e: He was well qualified, but in that office his face just didn't fit.  他条件很好，可在那家公司就是不受待见。

1718.e: Her face fell when she saw the exam paper on the desk.  她看见桌上那张考卷，脸色一下子垮了。

1719.e: He broke the window, so now he has to go and face the music.  窗户是他打破的，现在得去承担后果。

1720.e: We finally met face to face after three years of emails.  通了三年邮件，我们终于见了面。

1721.e: Lay the cards face down on the table before you shuffle them.  洗牌前把牌面朝下放在桌上。

1722.cn: 纠缠某人；对某人穷追不舍
1722.e: Stop getting in my face about the rent, I'll pay on Friday.  别老为房租烦我，我周五就付。

1723.e: She stayed remarkably calm in the face of all that criticism.  面对那么多批评，她异常镇定。

1724.e: Let's face it, nobody is going to read a two hundred page report.  说实话吧，两百页的报告没人会看。

1725.e: Giving the award to an outsider was a slap in the face for the staff.  把奖颁给外人，对员工来说就是一记耳光。

1726.e: A coat of paint gave the old shopfront a much-needed facelift.  刷了一层漆，这个旧店面焕然一新。

1727.e: Telling me after the fact that you sold the car isn't much help.  车都卖了才告诉我，有什么用。

1728.cn: 无法改变（或避免）的事实
1728.e: Traffic jams are simply a fact of life in this part of the city.  在城里这一带，堵车就是没法改变的事。

1729.e: He looks about forty, but in actual fact he's nearly sixty.  他看着四十来岁，其实快六十了。

1730.e: You climbed the mountain in four hours? Is that a fact?  你四小时就爬上山了？真的假的？

1731.e: Her mother explained the facts of life to her when she turned eleven.  她十一岁时，母亲给她讲了生理常识。

1732.e: Three failed inspections in one year, the facts speak for themselves.  一年三次检查不合格，事实不言自明。

1733.e: The forecast says the weather is set fair for the whole weekend.  天气预报说整个周末都会晴好。

1734.e: He phones his mother every Sunday evening without fail.  他每个星期天晚上必给母亲打电话。

1735.e: Fair dinkum, I saw a kangaroo right outside the shop this morning.  真的，今早我在店门口看见一只袋鼠。

1736.e: You'd rather split the bill? Fair enough, let's do that.  你想各付各的？行吧，就这样。

1737.cn: 可任意取笑（或抨击）的对象
1737.e: Once you're a politician, your private life becomes fair game.  一旦当了政客，私生活就任人评说了。

1738.e: Every employee deserves a fair hearing before being dismissed.  每个员工在被解雇前都应有申辩的机会。

1739.e: The coach cares more about fair play than about winning trophies.  这位教练看重公平竞赛胜过拿奖杯。

1740.cn: 公平的机会；公道的待遇
1740.e: All the new applicants deserve a fair shake at the job.  所有新申请人都该得到公平的机会。

1741.i: (more than) your fair ˈshare of sth
1741.e: That family has had more than its fair share of bad luck this year.  那家人今年真是倒霉透顶。

1742.e: The union accused the company of bargaining in bad faith.  工会指责公司谈判缺乏诚意。

1743.e: They paid a deposit as a sign of good faith.  他们付了定金以示诚意。

1744.e: The smoke in the kitchen turned out to be a false alarm.  厨房冒烟原来只是虚惊一场。

1745.e: After two false starts, the business finally began to make money.  两次失败的开头之后，这生意终于开始赚钱了。

1746.cn: 显得不恰当；给人不真诚之感
1746.e: His cheerful joke struck a false note at such a sad occasion.  在这么悲伤的场合，他那个笑话显得很不合适。

1747.e: That excuse has a familiar ring to it, you used it last week.  这借口听着耳熟，你上周就用过。

1748.e: They shared an office for years and, familiarity breeds contempt, ended up quarrelling.  他们同办公室多年，熟不拘礼，最后闹翻了。

1749.e: By the time they moved house, she was already in the family way.  他们搬家的时候，她已经有身孕了。

1750.e: Red hair and stubbornness both run in that family.  红头发和倔脾气在他们家都是祖传的。

1751.cn: 鬼才信的漂亮话；话说得太早
1751.e: "This train is never late." Famous last words, we sat there an hour.  “这趟车从不晚点。”话说得太满，我们干坐了一小时。

1752.cn: 变卖祖产；贱卖重要资产
1752.e: Critics said privatizing the railways was selling off the family silver.  批评者说铁路私有化就是在变卖祖产。

1753.e: My mother and my new boyfriend got on famously over dinner.  我妈和我新男友吃饭时相处得极好。

1754.e: His angry tweets only fanned the flames of an already ugly dispute.  他那些愤怒的推文只是给这场丑陋的争端火上浇油。

1755.i: when the ˈshit hits the fan (slang)
1755.e: Delete nothing, when the shit hits the fan we'll need those emails.  什么都别删，出了事我们还得靠这些邮件。

1756.i: as, whenever, etc. the fancy ˈtakes you
1756.e: You can paint the walls whatever colour the fancy takes you.  墙想刷什么颜色随你高兴。

1757.e: A little blue teapot in the window caught my fancy at once.  橱窗里一只蓝色小茶壶一下子把我迷住了。

1758.cn: 自认为有胜算；看好…能成功
1758.e: He fancies his chances against a player ranked twenty places above him.  他觉得自己能赢一个排名高二十位的选手。

1759.e: She's moving to Iceland to open a bakery. Just fancy that!  她要搬去冰岛开面包店，真想不到！

1760.i: take a ˈfancy to sb/sth (especially BrE)
1760.e: The cat took a fancy to our new neighbour and moved in with him.  那只猫看上了新邻居，索性搬去他家住了。

1761.e: As far as the money goes, we can manage until the end of the month.  就钱而言，我们撑到月底没问题。

1762.i: as far as the eye can/could ˈsee
1762.cn: 一望无际；视线所及之处
1762.e: There were sunflower fields as far as the eye could see.  向日葵田一望无际。

1763.cn: 就其本身而言（暗指不够）
1763.e: His plan is fine as far as it goes, but it ignores the cost.  他的方案就本身而言还行，可没考虑成本。

1764.i: as far as I ˈknow ◆ as far as I can reˈmember, etc.
1764.cn: 据我所知；就我记忆所及
1764.e: As far as I know, the shop still opens at seven on Sundays.  据我所知，那家店周日还是七点开门。

1765.e: Teasing him about his accent is taking the joke too far.  拿他的口音开玩笑就过分了。

1766.e: She is far and away the best cook in the whole family.  她做菜远远胜过家里其他人。

1767.e: That young engineer works hard and will go far in this company.  那个年轻工程师肯干，在公司里前途无量。

1768.e: People came from far and wide to hear the old singer one last time.  人们从四面八方赶来，听老歌手最后唱一次。

1769.e: This tiny flat is a far cry from the house we had in the country.  这间小公寓和我们乡下那栋房子天差地别。

1770.e: Is he generous? Far from it, he spends everything on himself.  他大方吗？才不呢，钱全花自己身上了。

1771.i: in so ˈfar as (also insoˈfar as)
1771.e: The report is useful in so far as it shows what must be fixed.  就其指出需要修正之处而言，这份报告是有用的。

1772.i: as ˈfar as sb is concerned
1772.cn: 就某人而言；在某人看来
1772.e: As far as I'm concerned, the whole trip was a waste of money.  在我看来，这趟旅行纯属浪费钱。

1773.e: I guessed her age as thirty and I wasn't far off.  我猜她三十岁，还真差不太多。

1774.e: Twenty pounds doesn't go far when you're feeding four children.  养四个孩子，二十镑根本不经花。

1775.e: So far we've sold about half the tickets for Saturday's show.  到目前为止，周六演出的票卖了一半左右。

1776.e: Two exams down and both went well, so far so good.  两门考完都不错，目前为止一切顺利。

1777.e: He speaks Japanese after a fashion, enough to order dinner.  他会点日语，勉强够点菜。

1778.e: The chapel was built after the fashion of a Greek temple.  这座小教堂仿希腊神庙的样式建造。

1779.e: He answered every question in a calm and careful fashion.  他以冷静谨慎的方式回答了每个问题。

1780.i: like it's going out of ˈfashion (spoken)
1780.cn: （用于强调）没完没了地；毫无节制地
1780.e: Since the diet ended he's been eating chocolate like it's going out of fashion.  节食一结束，他吃巧克力就没个节制。

1781.i: as fast as your legs can ˈcarry you
1781.e: He ran home as fast as his legs could carry him when the storm started.  暴雨一来，他拔腿飞奔回家。

1782.cn: （比赛、活动）激烈的；热火朝天的
1782.e: The quiz got fast and furious in the final round.  最后一轮抢答变得又快又激烈。

1783.cn: 花言巧语的人；油嘴滑舌者
1783.e: Don't sign anything, that salesman is a fast talker.  什么都别签，那个推销员太会忽悠。

1784.cn: 很快博得他人青睐的人
1784.e: They met on Monday and he'd asked her out by Tuesday, what a fast worker.  他们周一认识，周二他就约她出去了，动作真快。

1785.cn: 坚持（信念、原则等）不放弃
1785.e: She held fast to her principles even when the whole board disagreed.  即便全体董事反对，她仍坚守自己的原则。

1786.e: After ten years of life in the fast lane, he moved to a quiet village.  过了十年紧张刺激的日子，他搬到了安静的村子。

1787.e: Our region is still in the slow lane when it comes to broadband.  在宽带方面，我们这个地区还是慢半拍。

1788.cn: 毫无用处；一点好处也没有
1788.e: A fat lot of good your advice was, the car still won't start.  你的建议一点用也没有，车还是发动不了。

1789.e: Fat chance of getting a table there without booking weeks ahead.  不提前几周订位，别想在那儿有座。

1790.i: the fat is in the ˈfire (informal)
1790.e: Once she read those messages, the fat was in the fire.  她一看到那些短信，事情就闹大了。

1791.e: He is generous to a fault and often lends money he needs himself.  他慷慨得过了头，常把自己要用的钱借出去。

1792.e: Calling the host by the wrong name was an awkward faux pas.  把主人的名字叫错了，实在失礼。

1793.i: be (all) in ˈfavour of sth/of doing sth
1793.e: I'm all in favour of starting the meeting half an hour earlier.  我完全赞成把会议提前半小时。

1794.cn: 帮我个忙；（表示不信）得了吧
1794.e: Do me a favour and hold the ladder while I fix this light.  帮个忙，我修灯时扶着梯子。

1795.e: The referee's decision went in our favour for once.  裁判的判罚这回总算对我们有利。

1796.cn: 得宠（或失宠）；受（不受）青睐
1796.e: Long coats are back in favour with young designers this winter.  今冬长外套又受年轻设计师青睐了。

1797.e: He stays late every day to curry favour with the new boss.  他天天加班到很晚，就为讨好新老板。

1798.cn: 家乡的名人；当地的骄傲
1798.e: The town welcomed its favourite son home with a brass band.  小镇用铜管乐队迎接这位家乡名人归来。

1799.e: You helped me move, so let me return the favour with dinner.  你帮我搬了家，让我请顿饭还个人情。

1800.cn: 得到某人的赞许（或喜爱）
1800.e: The simpler design found favour with the judges.  较为简洁的设计得到了评委的青睐。

1801.i: do sb no ˈfavours ◆ not do sb any ˈfavours
1801.e: Lending him money again does him no favours at all.  再借钱给他对他没有任何好处。

1802.i: be/go in fear of your ˈlife
1802.e: After the threats, the witness lived in fear of her life.  受到威胁后，那名证人整天担心性命难保。

1803.i: for fear of sth/of doing sth ◆ for fear (that)...
1803.e: She tiptoed upstairs for fear of waking the baby.  她踮着脚上楼，生怕吵醒宝宝。

1804.e: The pupils waited in fear and trembling outside the headmaster's door.  学生们提心吊胆地等在校长门外。

1805.e: You want me to jump into that freezing lake? No fear!  你要我跳进那冰冷的湖里？才不干呢！

1806.i: put the fear of ˈGod into sb (informal)
1806.cn: 把某人吓坏；恐吓某人就范
1806.e: One look at the exam timetable put the fear of God into us.  一看考试时间表，我们全吓坏了。

1807.cn: 不会发生某事；不必担心
1807.e: There's no fear of rain today, leave the umbrella at home.  今天不会下雨，伞就别带了。

1808.i: without ˌfear or ˈfavour (BrE) (AmE without ˌfear or ˈfavor) (formal)
1808.e: A judge must apply the law without fear or favour.  法官必须不偏不倚地适用法律。

1809.e: Come to the window and feast your eyes on that view.  到窗边来，好好欣赏一下那景色。

1810.e: Winning that contract was a real feather in her cap.  拿下那份合同是她一大荣耀。

1811.e: He spent years on the board quietly feathering his own nest.  他在董事会多年，一直悄悄中饱私囊。

1812.e: Put out some crumbs in winter for our feathered friends.  冬天撒些面包屑，给鸟儿们吃。

1813.i: fed up to the back ˈteeth with sb/sth (also ˌsick to the back ˈteeth of sb/sth) (informal)
1813.e: I'm fed up to the back teeth with their broken promises.  他们一再食言，我真是烦透了。

1814.cn: 疯抢；（媒体等的）疯狂追逐
1814.e: The scandal set off a media feeding frenzy outside her house.  这桩丑闻引来媒体在她家门外疯狂围堵。

1815.e: Everyone spoke Spanish at dinner and I felt completely out of it.  晚饭时大家都说西班牙语，我完全插不上话。

1816.e: After two hours of football with my nephews, I really felt my age.  和侄子们踢了两小时球，我真觉得自己老了。

1817.cn: 感到手头拮据；出现财政困难
1817.e: Small shops on the high street are starting to feel the draught.  大街上的小店开始感到日子难过了。

1818.e: Feel free to help yourself to coffee while you wait.  等的时候请随意喝咖啡。

1819.e: I can feel it in my bones that she's going to call tonight.  我有预感，她今晚会打电话来。

1820.e: I feel like a long walk before it gets dark.  天黑前我想去好好走一段路。

1821.e: With rents rising, young families are really feeling the pinch.  房租上涨，年轻家庭真的手头吃紧。

1822.e: I felt strange all morning, so I went home early.  我一上午都不太舒服，就提早回家了。

1823.e: He felt his way down the dark corridor to find the switch.  他摸索着走过漆黑的走廊去找开关。

1824.e: Give me a week to get the feel of the new software.  给我一周时间熟悉这个新软件。

1825.cn: 对…有悟性；有做某事的天分
1825.e: She has a real feel for languages and picks up accents quickly.  她对语言很有天分，口音学得很快。

1826.cn: 觉得身体（或心情）不如平时
1826.e: I haven't felt myself since that long flight home.  自从坐了那趟长途飞机回来，我一直不太对劲。

1827.e: He's putting out feelers about a job in Berlin.  他正在打听柏林那边的工作机会。

1828.e: I get the feeling that she isn't telling us the whole story.  我觉得她没把事情全说出来。

1829.e: You got the promotion and I didn't, but no hard feelings.  你升职了我没有，不过我不往心里去。

1830.cn: 拜倒在某人脚下；对某人倾倒
1830.e: After that performance the whole city was at her feet.  那场演出之后，全城的人都为她倾倒。

1831.cn: 忙得团团转；忙得不可开交
1831.e: The café was so busy we were run off our feet all afternoon.  咖啡馆太忙了，我们整个下午脚不沾地。

1832.e: He lost his job in May and landed on his feet with a better one.  他五月丢了工作，转头就找到个更好的。

1833.e: He swears he'll only leave this old house feet first.  他发誓自己只有死了才会离开这栋老房子。

1834.e: Fans were shocked to learn their hero had feet of clay.  得知偶像也有致命缺点，粉丝们大为震惊。

1835.i: have/keep both/your feet on the ˈground
1835.e: Despite all the praise, she keeps both feet on the ground.  尽管备受赞誉，她依然脚踏实地。

1836.e: Nurses are on their feet for twelve hours at a stretch.  护士一站就是连续十二个小时。

1837.e: Dinner's cooking, so put your feet up for half an hour.  饭在做着，你先歇半小时吧。

1838.cn: 拜倒在某人脚下恳求（帮助或宽恕）
1838.e: He threw himself at the judge's feet and begged for another chance.  他跪在法官面前，恳求再给一次机会。

1839.e: The kids are under my feet all day during the school holidays.  放假时孩子们整天在我脚边碍事。

1840.e: She's tired of fetching and carrying for her lazy flatmates.  她受够了给懒室友跑腿伺候。

1841.e: Grandad is ninety but still in fine fettle.  爷爷九十岁了，身子骨还硬朗。

1842.e: Excitement was at fever pitch before the final whistle.  终场哨响前，气氛热烈到了顶点。

1843.e: Buses out here are few and far between after eight.  八点以后这一带的公交车少得可怜。

1844.e: Don't let him drive, he's had a few too many.  别让他开车，他喝多了。

1845.e: Our coach is a man of few words but everyone listens to him.  我们教练话不多，可大家都听他的。

1846.e: Arguing about the logo while sales collapse is fiddling while Rome burns.  销量都垮了还在争标志，简直是大难临头不着急。

1847.e: The manager had been on the fiddle for years before anyone noticed.  那位经理骗了好几年钱才被人发现。

1848.cn: 大干一场；尽情发挥（尤指借机大做文章）
1848.e: The newspapers had a field day with the mayor's leaked emails.  市长的邮件外泄，报纸大做文章。

1849.i: leave the field ˈclear for sb
1849.e: Her withdrawal left the field clear for the younger candidate.  她的退出为那位年轻候选人扫清了障碍。

1850.i: leave sb in possession of the ˈfield
1850.cn: 让某人独占优势；使某人成为赢家
1850.e: The rival firm's collapse left them in possession of the field.  竞争对手垮台，让他们独占了市场。

1851.e: He wants to play the field for a few years before settling down.  他想先花几年到处交往，再安定下来。

1852.e: My knee has been aching something fierce since the game.  比赛之后我的膝盖疼得厉害。

1853.cn: 援引第五修正案拒绝作答
1853.e: The witness took the fifth rather than name his business partners.  证人援引第五修正案，拒绝说出生意伙伴的名字。

1854.cn: 以其人之道还治其人之身
1854.e: They ran negative ads, so we decided to fight fire with fire.  他们打负面广告，我们就决定以牙还牙。

1855.e: The climber is in hospital fighting for his life after the fall.  那名登山者坠落后正在医院里与死神搏斗。

1856.e: The two finalists will fight it out on Sunday afternoon.  两位决赛选手将在周日下午一决高下。

1857.e: Those brothers fight like cat and dog but would defend each other anywhere.  那对兄弟成天吵架，可对外总是护着彼此。

1858.e: Trying to keep the kitchen tidy with four kids is fighting a losing battle.  带着四个孩子想保持厨房整洁，纯属徒劳。

1859.cn: 自己解决问题；独立应对
1859.e: She's old enough now to fight her own battles at school.  她已经大了，学校的事该自己应付。

1860.i: fight ˈshy of sth/of doing sth
1860.e: The minister fought shy of answering questions about the budget.  部长回避了关于预算的问题。

1861.i: fight ˌtooth and ˈnail (for sb/sth/to do sth)
1861.e: Local people fought tooth and nail to save the village school.  当地人拼尽全力保住了村里的学校。

1862.e: They lost in the end, but they put up a good fight.  他们最后输了，但打得很顽强。

1863.e: With five minutes left, our team still has a fighting chance.  还剩五分钟，我们队仍有一线获胜的机会。

1864.e: After a month of rest he's fighting fit again.  休养一个月后，他又生龙活虎了。

1865.i: be in with a ˈchance (of doing sth) (BrE, informal)
1865.e: John Brown is still in with a chance of winning the nomination.  约翰·布朗仍有机会拿到提名。

1866.e: What the team lacks in skill it makes up for in fighting spirit.  这支队伍技术不足，却靠斗志弥补。

1867.cn: 挑战性的言论；豪言壮语
1867.e: Beat them by ten points? That's fighting talk from a new captain.  赢他们十分？新队长口气可真不小。

1868.cn: 凭空想象的事物；虚构之事
1868.e: The noises in the attic were just a figment of her imagination.  阁楼上的声响不过是她的想象罢了。

1869.i: cut a fine, poor, sorry, etc. ˈfigure
1869.cn: 显得出众（或狼狈、可怜等）
1869.e: Soaked and muddy, he cut a sorry figure at the front door.  他浑身湿透沾满泥，站在门口显得十分狼狈。

1870.e: That silly hat made him a figure of fun in the whole office.  那顶滑稽的帽子让他成了全办公室的笑柄。

1871.e: He hates the sea but bought a boat. Go figure.  他讨厌大海却买了条船，真搞不懂。

1872.e: It's hard to put a figure on the damage before the survey.  勘查之前很难给损失定出个数字。

1873.e: He was late again? That figures, he missed the early train.  他又迟到了？不奇怪，他没赶上早班车。

1874.e: The children walked in single file along the narrow mountain path.  孩子们排成一列走在狭窄的山路上。

1875.e: The leadership agreed, but the rank and file voted against the deal.  领导层同意了，可基层成员投票否决了这项协议。

1876.e: It won't be easy to fill her shoes after twenty years of teaching here.  她在这儿教了二十年书，接她的班可不容易。

1877.i: have had your ˈfill of sb/sth
1877.e: I've had my fill of meetings for this week.  这一周的会我算是开够了。

1878.e: He finds fault with everything I cook, however hard I try.  不管我多用心做饭，他总能挑出毛病。

1879.e: Give the new nurse a month to find her feet on the ward.  给这位新护士一个月时间适应病房工作。

1880.i: (not) find it in your heart to ˈdo sth (also (not) find it ˈin yourself to do sth) (literary)
1880.e: She couldn't find it in her heart to tell the boy his dog had died.  她不忍心告诉那男孩他的狗死了。

1881.cn: 终于开口说话；不再怯场
1881.e: After a nervous silence, she finally found her voice and answered.  紧张地沉默片刻后，她终于开口作答。

1882.e: Somehow my umbrella found its way into his car.  不知怎么，我的伞跑到他车里去了。

1883.i: take sb as you ˈfind them
1883.e: The house is a mess and so am I, you'll have to take me as you find me.  屋子乱，我也乱，你就将就着接受我这样吧。

1884.e: He kept the coin he found in the park, finders keepers.  他把公园里捡到的硬币留下了，谁捡到归谁嘛。

1885.i: have sth down to a fine ˈart (informal)
1885.e: After six children, she has bedtime down to a fine art.  养了六个孩子，她把哄睡这事做得炉火纯青。

1886.i: not to put too fine a ˈpoint on it
1886.cn: 直截了当地说；不客气地说
1886.e: Not to put too fine a point on it, the report is badly written.  不客气地说，这份报告写得很糟。

1887.i: go over/through sth with a fine-tooth ˈcomb
1887.e: The auditors went through the accounts with a fine-tooth comb.  审计人员把账目一笔一笔仔细查了一遍。

1888.i: work your ˌfingers to the ˈbone (informal)
1888.e: She worked her fingers to the bone to send both sons to college.  她拼死拼活干活，供两个儿子上了大学。

1889.e: A good guide has the city's history at her fingertips.  好导游对这座城市的历史了如指掌。

1890.e: He is a gentleman to his fingertips, even when provoked.  即便被激怒，他也是个十足的绅士。

1891.cn: 结束时在场；见证最后阶段
1891.e: She joined the project late but was in at the finish.  她中途才加入项目，但坚持到了最后。

1892.e: He was putting the finishing touches to the cake when we arrived.  我们到时他正在给蛋糕做最后的装饰。

1893.e: The airline came under fire for cancelling flights without warning.  这家航空公司因无预警取消航班而遭到抨击。

1894.i: fire ˈquestions, ˈinsults, etc. at sb
1894.cn: 连珠炮般地发问（或辱骂）
1894.e: Reporters fired questions at the coach as he left the stadium.  教练离开球场时，记者连珠炮般地向他发问。

1895.e: Hold your fire until we know what really happened.  先别急着发作，等弄清事情真相再说。

1896.e: My throat is on fire after eating that chilli.  吃了那个辣椒，我嗓子火烧火燎的。

1897.e: Lending money to that gambler is playing with fire.  借钱给那个赌徒简直是玩火。

1898.i: set the ˈworld on fire (BrE also set the ˈThames on fire)
1898.e: His first album didn't set the world on fire, but the second did.  他的首张专辑反响平平，第二张却红遍全国。

1899.e: Someone set the rubbish bins on fire behind the school.  有人把学校后面的垃圾桶点着了。

1900.i: be in the ˈfiring line (BrE) (AmE be on the ˈfiring line)
1900.cn: 首当其冲；处于易受批评之位
1900.e: As spokesman, he's always in the firing line when things go wrong.  作为发言人，一出事他总是首当其冲。

1901.e: Ask about the history, that's where she's on firm ground.  问历史吧，那是她有把握的领域。

1902.e: That class needs a firm hand from the very first lesson.  那个班从第一节课起就得严加管教。

1903.e: The committee held firm to its decision despite the protests.  尽管有抗议，委员会仍坚持原来的决定。

1904.e: The school takes a firm line on bullying of any kind.  学校对任何形式的欺凌都态度坚决。

1905.i: be a great/firm beˈliever in sth
1905.e: My grandmother is a firm believer in a walk before breakfast.  我外婆坚信早饭前该散散步。

1906.e: At first glance the twins look identical, but their voices differ.  乍一看这对双胞胎一模一样，声音却不同。

1907.e: For her, the children's health always comes first.  对她来说，孩子的健康永远排第一。

1908.e: The chairman is really just first among equals on this board.  在董事会里，主席其实只是同僚中的第一人。

1909.e: First and foremost, we need to make the building safe.  首要的是把这栋楼弄安全。

1910.cn: 归根到底；从头至尾就是
1910.e: He is, first and last, a teacher, whatever titles they give him.  不管给他什么头衔，他归根到底是个老师。

1911.e: She learned about the flood at first hand, wading through the streets.  她蹚着水走过街道，亲身体验了那场洪水。

1912.e: First off, let me thank everyone who stayed late last night.  首先，感谢昨晚留下加班的各位。

1913.e: The landlord gave us first refusal on the flat downstairs.  房东给了我们优先租下楼下那套房的权利。

1914.i: first ˈthing (tomorrow, in the morning, etc.)
1914.e: I'll call the bank first thing tomorrow morning.  我明天一早就给银行打电话。

1915.e: I'd be the last person to criticize her, she saved the project.  我最不会去批评她，是她救了这个项目。

1916.e: From the very first, I knew this job wasn't right for me.  从一开始我就知道这份工作不适合我。

1917.e: From first to last the whole trial took only three days.  整场审判从头到尾只用了三天。

1918.cn: 迈出第一步；取得初步进展
1918.e: We never even got to first base with the funding application.  我们的经费申请连第一步都没走成。

1919.e: The children's school fees have first call on our savings.  孩子的学费在我们的存款里排第一位。

1920.e: In the first instance, please write to the customer services team.  第一步请先写信给客服部。

1921.e: Why did you lend him the car in the first place?  你当初为什么要把车借给他？

1922.e: After the quarrel, he finally made the first move and phoned her.  吵架之后，他终于主动打了电话给她。

1923.e: Good managers put their team first when things go wrong.  出了问题时，好经理会把团队放在第一位。

1924.i: there's a ˌfirst time for ˈeverything (saying, humorous)
1924.e: You cooked dinner? Well, there's a first time for everything.  你居然做饭了？凡事都有第一次嘛。

1980.i: flip your ˈlid (AmE also flip your ˈwig) (informal)
1980.e: Dad flipped his lid when he saw the phone bill this month.  我爸看到这个月的话费单时暴跳如雷。

1981.cn: 合某人心意；讨某人喜欢
1981.e: Jazz doesn't really float my boat, but I'll come along anyway.  爵士乐我不太感冒，不过我还是跟你去吧。

1982.e: Asking him to apologize again is flogging a dead horse, honestly.  说实话，再让他道歉纯属白费力气。

1983.cn: 把某事说滥；反复使用以致乏味
1983.e: That advertising slogan has been flogged to death over the past year.  那句广告语这一年被用滥了。

1984.cn: 大量抛售商品；充斥市场
1984.e: Cheap imported toys have flooded the market and hurt local makers.  廉价进口玩具充斥市场，把本地厂家挤垮了。

1985.e: She was in floods of tears when she heard her dog had been found.  听说狗找到了，她哭得稀里哗啦。

1986.cn: 长时间独自发言；垄断谈话
1986.e: Uncle Bob held the floor for an hour telling stories about the war.  鲍勃叔叔滔滔不绝讲了一小时战争往事。

1987.e: The union representative took the floor and demanded better safety rules.  工会代表起身发言，要求改善安全规定。

1988.cn: 漂浮的残骸杂物；社会上的流浪者
1988.e: After the storm, the beach was covered with flotsam and jetsam.  暴风雨过后，海滩上满是漂来的杂物残骸。

1989.e: Stop planning every minute of the trip and just go with the flow.  别把行程每分钟都排满，顺其自然就好。

1990.e: The flower of a whole generation was lost in those four years.  整整一代人的精英都葬送在那四年里。

1991.cn: 会大吵一架；会闹得不可开交
1991.e: When she finds out he sold her car, the sparks will fly.  等她发现他把车卖了，非闹翻天不可。

1992.e: By the time the police arrived, the suspect had already flown the coop.  警察赶到时，嫌疑人早就溜之大吉了。

1993.e: Her design studio is flying high after winning that international prize.  拿下那个国际奖之后，她的设计工作室风生水起。

1994.i: fly in the face of ˈsth (written)
1994.e: His claims fly in the face of everything the research has shown.  他的说法与所有研究结果完全相悖。

1995.cn: 美中不足之处；扫兴的因素
1995.e: The hotel was lovely; the only fly in the ointment was the noisy road.  酒店很不错，唯一美中不足是马路太吵。

1996.i: fly into a ˈrage, ˈtemper, etc.
1996.e: He flew into a rage when the waiter brought the wrong order twice.  服务员两次上错菜，他一下子火冒三丈。

1997.e: The minister flew a kite about raising taxes to see how voters reacted.  部长放出加税的风声，看看选民什么反应。

1998.e: I told the pushy salesman to go fly a kite and shut the door.  我叫那个死缠烂打的推销员走开，然后关上了门。

1999.e: Now that both kids have flown the nest, the house feels enormous.  两个孩子都离家了，屋子显得空荡荡的。

2000.e: Try to explain calmly instead of flying off the handle at him.  好好跟他解释，别一上来就对他发火。

2001.e: I'd love to be a fly on the wall during their negotiation tomorrow.  真想明天躲在他们谈判现场偷偷看一眼。

2002.e: The boy let fly at the window with a stone and ran off.  那男孩朝窗户猛掷一块石头就跑了。

2003.cn: 匆匆地；同时忙别的事时
2003.e: I edited the whole speech on the fly during the taxi ride there.  我在去那儿的出租车上匆匆把整篇讲稿改完了。

2004.i: he, she, etc. wouldn't harm/hurt a ˈfly
2004.cn: 心地善良；连只苍蝇都不忍伤害
2004.e: That huge dog looks scary but he wouldn't hurt a fly.  那条大狗看着吓人，其实连只苍蝇都不会伤。

2005.e: She paid us a flying visit between two meetings and left after tea.  她在两个会之间来我们这儿坐了坐，喝完茶就走了。

2006.i: get off to a ˌflying ˈstart • get off to a ˈflyer
2006.e: The charity appeal got off to a flying start with a huge first donation.  头一笔捐款数额巨大，这次募捐开局大好。

2007.e: He tripped on the loose carpet and went flying across the hallway.  他被松脱的地毯绊了一下，在走廊上摔了个大跟头。

2008.i: with ˌflying ˈcolours (BrE) (AmE with ˌflying ˈcolors)
2008.e: She passed her driving test with flying colours on the first attempt.  她第一次考驾照就轻松高分通过。

2009.e: After the long flight I spent the whole day in a fog.  坐了那么久的飞机，我一整天都昏头昏脑的。

2010.cn: 引人深思的事；发人深省的内容
2010.e: Her talk on food waste gave us all plenty of food for thought.  她关于食物浪费的演讲让我们都陷入了思考。

2011.e: He folded his daughter in his arms and told her not to cry.  他把女儿搂进怀里，叫她别哭。

2012.cn: 步某人后尘；继承某人的事业
2012.e: She followed in her mother's footsteps and became a country doctor.  她追随母亲的脚步，也成了一名乡村医生。

2013.cn: 一直往前走；凭直觉行事
2013.e: Just follow your nose down this street and you'll see the market.  沿着这条街一直走，你就能看见市场。

2014.e: One bank cut its rates and the others quickly followed suit.  一家银行降息，其他银行很快跟进。

2015.cn: 傻子也能……（形容极其容易）
2015.e: Any fool can criticize the plan; try writing a better one yourself.  谁都会挑毛病，你倒是自己写个更好的出来。

2016.e: Don't try that trick on Grandma—she's nobody's fool.  别拿那套糊弄奶奶，她精明着呢。

2017.e: Driving across town for a shop that closed years ago was a fool's errand.  开车穿城去一家早就关门的店，纯属白跑一趟。

2018.cn: 虚幻的幸福；自欺欺人的美梦
2018.e: They're living in a fool's paradise if they think the debt will vanish.  要是以为债务会自己消失，他们就是在做白日梦。

2019.e: I made a complete fool of myself singing karaoke at the office party.  公司聚会上我唱卡拉OK，把自己丢人现眼了一回。

2020.e: You lent him money again? More fool you, he never pays anyone back.  你又借钱给他？你真够傻的，他从不还钱。

2021.i: (there's) ˌno fool like an ˈold fool (saying)
2021.cn: 老糊涂最糊涂；老年荒唐最可笑
2021.e: He's sixty and buying a sports car—there's no fool like an old fool.  他六十了还买跑车，真是老糊涂最糊涂。

2022.e: You say you cleaned the room? You could have fooled me!  你说你打扫过房间？我可不信！

2023.i: fools rush ˈin (where angels fear to ˈtread) (saying)
2023.cn: 无知者无畏；莽汉闯入天使止步之地
2023.e: He gave marriage advice to a couple he'd just met—fools rush in.  他给刚认识的一对夫妻出婚姻主意，真是无知者无畏。

2024.e: Her parents footed the bill for the entire wedding reception.  婚宴的全部费用都是她父母出的。

2025.i: get/have a/your ˌfoot in the ˈdoor
2025.e: The internship was badly paid but it got her foot in the door.  那份实习工资很低，却让她敲开了行业的大门。

2026.i: get/start off on the right/wrong ˈfoot (with sb) (informal)
2026.cn: （与某人）一开始就相处得好（或不好）
2026.e: I got off on the wrong foot with my new boss by arriving late.  我第一天就迟到，跟新老板开局就不顺。

2027.i: have a foot in both ˈcamps (informal)
2027.cn: 脚踏两只船；同时与对立双方有关系
2027.e: As both a farmer and a conservationist, he has a foot in both camps.  他既是农场主又是环保人士，两边都沾着。

2028.e: He's too busy to help? Too busy my foot, he's watching football.  他忙得没空帮忙？忙个鬼，他在看球呢。

2029.cn: 从不出错；从未走错一步
2029.e: In thirty years at the firm she never put a foot wrong.  在公司三十年，她从来没出过一次差错。

2030.e: The bridge was closed, so we crossed the river on foot further upstream.  桥封了，我们只好从上游徒步过河。

2031.e: Mum finally put her foot down and banned phones at the dinner table.  妈妈终于坚决表态，吃饭时不许玩手机。

2032.i: put your ˈfoot in it (BrE) (also put your foot in your ˈmouth AmE, BrE) (informal)
2032.cn: 说错话；无意中冒犯别人
2032.e: I really put my foot in it by asking about his ex-wife.  我问起他前妻，真是说错话了。

2033.e: She swore she would never set foot in that restaurant again.  她发誓再也不踏进那家餐厅一步。

2034.e: It's your first day, so put your best foot forward and smile a lot.  今天是你第一天上班，好好表现，多笑笑。

2035.e: At twenty-two, footloose and fancy-free, he bought a one-way ticket to Peru.  二十二岁时他无牵无挂，买了张去秘鲁的单程票。

2036.cn: （桌下）用脚碰脚调情；暗中勾搭
2036.e: She was playing footsie with him under the table all through dinner.  整顿饭她都在桌子底下用脚跟他调情。

2037.cn: 逐一对应；一项对一项地
2037.e: They checked the two lists A for B and found three names missing.  他们把两份名单逐一对照，发现少了三个名字。

2038.e: For all his money, he seems a rather lonely and unhappy man.  尽管他很有钱，看上去却孤单又不快乐。

2039.cn: 众目睽睽之下；显而易见
2039.e: Her disappointment was written on her face for all to see.  她脸上的失望之情谁都看得出来。

2040.e: God forbid that anything should happen to the children on that road.  但愿孩子们在那条路上别出什么事。

2041.cn: 但愿不会发生；上天保佑别这样
2041.e: Heaven forfend that we should ever have to sell the family house.  但愿我们永远不必卖掉这套祖屋。

2042.cn: 禁果；因被禁而更诱人的事物
2042.e: Sweets were forbidden fruit in our house, which made us want them more.  在我们家糖果是禁果，越不让吃越想吃。

2043.i: bring sth into ˈforce • come into ˈforce
2043.e: The new smoking ban comes into force at the beginning of next month.  新的禁烟规定从下月初开始生效。

2044.cn: 迫使某人提前或改变计划
2044.e: The leaked email forced the company's hand and they announced the layoffs.  邮件泄露逼得公司不得不提前宣布裁员。

2045.cn: 迫使问题摊牌；逼人迅速决断
2045.e: She forced the issue by asking him publicly whether he would resign.  她当众问他是否辞职，把问题挑明了。

2046.e: By force of circumstance, we ended up living with my parents for a year.  情势所迫，我们最后跟我父母同住了一年。

2047.e: I still reach for my keys at that door out of force of habit.  我还是会习惯性地在那扇门前掏钥匙。

2048.cn: 迫使加快速度；加紧推进
2048.e: The younger runners forced the pace over the last two kilometres.  最后两公里几个年轻选手加快了节奏。

2049.i: a force to be ˈreckoned with
2049.cn: 不可小觑的力量；须认真对待的人物
2049.e: Since hiring those engineers, the small firm is a force to be reckoned with.  招了那几位工程师后，这家小公司已不容小觑。

2050.i: a force to be ˈreckoned with
2050.cn: 厉害角色；不容轻视的对手
2050.e: Be very careful how you deal with her, because she's a force to be reckoned with.  跟她打交道千万小心，她可是个厉害人物。

2051.e: Police turned out in force to control the crowd outside the stadium.  警察大批出动，维持体育场外的人群秩序。

2052.cn: 人数众多地；成群结队地
2052.e: Party members appeared in strength to welcome the prime minister home.  大批党员到场欢迎总理归来。

2053.cn: 大自然的威力（尤指破坏性的）
2053.e: No sea wall can hold back the forces of nature for ever.  再坚固的海堤也挡不住大自然的力量。

2054.e: Two small charities joined forces to build the new children's library.  两家小慈善机构联手建起了这座儿童图书馆。

2055.i: be/come to the ˈfore (BrE) (AmE be at the ˈfore)
2055.e: Young designers have come to the fore since the competition last spring.  自去年春天那场比赛后，年轻设计师纷纷崭露头角。

2056.cn: 使某事突出；使受到关注
2056.e: The scandal brought the issue of factory safety to the fore.  这桩丑闻让工厂安全问题浮出水面。

2057.cn: 在最前列；处于领先地位
2057.e: This lab has been at the forefront of cancer research for a decade.  这个实验室十年来一直处在癌症研究的最前沿。

2058.e: He refuses to tug his forelock to anyone, however senior they are.  不管对方职位多高，他都不肯低三下四。

2059.cn: 对上级毕恭毕敬；卑躬屈膝
2059.e: In the past, people either took off their hats or touched their forelock to the squire.  从前人们见了乡绅不是脱帽就是躬身行礼。

2060.e: We won't be moving house in the foreseeable future, so stop worrying.  可预见的将来我们不会搬家，别操心了。

2061.cn: 有备无患；预先警告即预先武装
2061.e: Read the contract before the meeting—forewarned is forearmed.  开会前先把合同看一遍，有备无患。

2062.cn: 事先知道就能有所准备；未雨绸缪
2062.e: If you know the risks before they happen, forewarned is forearmed.  事先了解风险，就等于提前做好了准备。

2063.cn: 但愿不会；上天保佑别这样
2063.e: Heaven forbid that we should ever go through another winter like that.  但愿我们再也别过那样的冬天了。

2064.e: You want me to drive four hours in this snow? Forget it.  你要我在这大雪天开四个小时车？别想了。

2065.e: The goalkeeper has been badly off form since he came back from injury.  这名门将伤愈复出后状态一直很差。

2066.e: Grandpa was on great form at dinner, telling one joke after another.  爷爷晚饭时状态极佳，一个接一个地讲笑话。

2067.e: A plan for the new community garden slowly took form over the winter.  整个冬天，新社区花园的方案慢慢成形了。

2068.i: be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself
2068.e: After the factory closed, the town became a shadow of its former self.  工厂关闭后，这座小镇早已不复当年的模样。

2069.i: hold the ˈfort (BrE) (AmE hold down the ˈfort)
2069.e: Can you hold the fort in the shop while I take Mum to hospital?  我送我妈去医院，店里你先顶一下好吗？

2070.i: be like painting the Forth ˈBridge (BrE)
2070.cn: 永远做不完的活儿；没完没了
2070.e: Cleaning up after three kids is like painting the Forth Bridge.  给三个孩子收拾屋子，永远也收拾不完。

2071.i: and ˈso forth (also and ˈso on (and ˈso forth))
2071.e: Bring a towel, sunscreen, a hat and so forth—it'll be very hot.  带上毛巾、防晒霜、帽子等等，那边会很热。

2072.cn: 等等；诸如此类的一堆事
2072.e: I've got to pack my bags, find my passport and so forth before morning.  我得收拾行李、找护照等等，都得在早上之前弄完。

2073.i: back and ˈforth (also ˌbackwards and ˈforwards)
2073.e: The nurse walked back and forth in the corridor waiting for news.  护士在走廊里来回踱步，等着消息。

2074.e: She travels backwards and forwards between the factory and head office.  她在工厂和总部之间来回奔波。

2075.e: From that day forth he never spoke his brother's name again.  从那天起，他再没提过他弟弟的名字。

2076.cn: 喋喋不休；发表冗长议论
2076.e: He held forth about modern art for twenty minutes without pausing.  他滔滔不绝讲了二十分钟现代艺术，中间都没停。

2077.i: be like/as safe as Fort ˈKnox
2077.e: The new server room is as safe as Fort Knox, with three separate locks.  新机房固若金汤，装了三道独立的锁。

2078.i: be like/as safe as Fort ˈKnox
2078.cn: （建筑）坚固而戒备森严；固若金汤
2078.e: Their house is like Fort Knox—cameras, alarms and two enormous dogs.  他们家跟堡垒似的，摄像头、警报器，还有两条大狗。

2079.e: Fortune smiled on us and the rain stopped just before the ceremony.  我们运气不错，仪式开始前雨正好停了。

2080.e: He made a fortune selling bicycle parts online during the lockdown.  封控期间他在网上卖自行车配件发了财。

2081.cn: 授人以柄的言行；招致风险的承诺
2081.e: Promising zero delays was a hostage to fortune he later regretted.  承诺绝不延误成了他日后追悔的把柄。

2082.e: That leaking roof has already cost us a small fortune this year.  今年那个漏雨的屋顶已经花了我们一大笔钱。

2083.e: Dad always has forty winks in his armchair after Sunday lunch.  周日午饭后我爸总要在扶手椅上打个盹。

2084.cn: 与某人发生冲突；触犯（规定等）
2084.e: The company fell foul of the tax authorities and paid a huge fine.  这家公司触犯了税务部门，交了一大笔罚款。

2085.e: Do something like that and you'll fall foul of the school rules.  你那么干就会撞上校规的枪口。

2086.i: be in/out of the ˈframe (for sth)
2086.cn: 有（或没有）资格参与；被列入或排除
2086.e: After that win, our team is still in the frame for the championship.  赢下那场后，我们队仍有争夺冠军的资格。

2087.e: When the bill arrived, my generous friend was nowhere to be found.  账单一来，那位大方的朋友就不见人影了。

2088.e: We waited an hour, but the bus was still nowhere in sight.  我们等了一个小时，公交车还是连影子都没有。

2089.cn: 从根本上动摇；撼动根基
2089.e: The scandal rocked the whole sport to its foundations.  这桩丑闻从根基上撼动了整个体育项目。

2090.cn: （国家、组织、学科的）创始人；奠基者
2090.e: He is regarded as one of the founding fathers of modern computing.  他被视为现代计算机科学的奠基人之一。

2091.i: the four ˌcorners of the ˈearth
2091.e: Fans came from the four corners of the earth to see the final concert.  歌迷从世界各地赶来看那场告别演唱会。

2092.e: House prices in the region went into free fall after the factory closed.  工厂关闭后，这一带的房价直线下跌。

2093.e: The café gives day-old bread to students for free every evening.  那家咖啡馆每天傍晚把隔夜面包免费送给学生。

2094.e: The atmosphere in the studio is free and easy, and nobody wears a tie.  工作室气氛很随意，没人打领带。

2095.e: With the exams over, I felt as free as a bird all summer.  考完试后，整个夏天我都自由得像只鸟。

2096.i: get, have, etc. a free ˈhand
2096.e: The new chef was given a free hand to redesign the whole menu.  新厨师获准自行决定，把整份菜单重新设计。

2097.i: get, take, etc. a free ˈride
2097.cn: 白占便宜；不出力而得好处
2097.e: He's had a free ride for years while the rest of us do the work.  这些年活儿都是我们干，他一直白占便宜。

2098.cn: 这是自由的国家（我爱怎样就怎样）
2098.e: I'll sit here if I want to—it's a free country, isn't it?  我愿意坐这儿就坐这儿，这可是自由的国家。

2099.e: He makes free with my tools and never puts any of them back.  他随便拿我的工具用，还从来不放回去。

2100.e: She signed the agreement of her own free will, with no pressure at all.  她完全出于自愿签了协议，没有受到任何压力。

2101.e: The whole thing was a bloody disaster, pardon my French.  整件事糟透了，恕我说话难听。

2102.i: take French ˈleave (BrE, old-fashioned or humorous)
2102.e: Two of the workers took French leave and went fishing all afternoon.  有两个工人擅自溜号，钓了一下午鱼。

2103.e: After ten hours' sleep she came down as fresh as a daisy.  睡了十个小时后，她下楼时神清气爽。

2104.i: fresh out of sth (informal, especially AmE)
2104.e: Sorry, we're fresh out of chocolate cake, but the apple pie is good.  抱歉，巧克力蛋糕刚卖完，不过苹果派不错。

2105.e: The barman got fresh with a customer and was fired the next day.  那个酒保对顾客动手动脚，第二天就被辞退了。

2106.e: My son made friends with the boy next door on his very first day.  我儿子头一天就跟隔壁男孩交上了朋友。

2107.cn: 说漏嘴；无意中泄露真实想法
2107.e: Calling his wife by his ex's name was quite a Freudian slip.  他把妻子叫成前女友的名字，真是说漏了心里话。

2108.e: The permit came through fast because he has friends in high places.  许可证办得飞快，因为他上面有人。

2109.i: have a ˈfrog in your throat (informal)
2109.e: Sorry, I've got a frog in my throat this morning—let me get some water.  抱歉，今早我嗓子哑了，我喝口水。

2110.e: He rushed out with his sweater on back to front and didn't notice.  他匆匆出门，毛衣前后穿反了都没发现。

2111.cn: 处于最重要的位置；备受关注
2111.e: Housing costs are front and center in this year's local election.  住房成本是今年地方选举最受关注的议题。

2112.e: Nurses were in the front line throughout the whole outbreak.  整个疫情期间护士都在第一线。

2113.i: on the front ˈburner (informal, especially AmE)
2113.e: The bridge repairs are finally on the front burner at city hall.  修桥的事在市政厅终于被摆到了首要位置。

2114.e: The builder wants half the money up front before he starts work.  施工方要求开工前先付一半的钱。

2115.e: Talks between the two sides came to a full stop after the walkout.  一方退场后，双方的谈判彻底停了下来。

2116.e: The building work came to a full stop when the money ran out.  钱一花光，工程就完全停了。

2117.e: Now the permits are signed, it's full steam ahead with the new wing.  许可批下来了，新楼那边可以全速开工了。

2118.i: full ˈmarks (to sb for doing sth) (BrE)
2118.e: Full marks to the team for finishing the whole job in one weekend.  这个团队一个周末干完全部活儿，值得大大表扬。

2119.e: For breakfast he ordered the full monty—eggs, bacon, beans, the lot.  早餐他点了全套：鸡蛋、培根、豆子，样样都有。

2120.e: The puppy is full of beans again now that his leg has healed.  小狗的腿好了，又活蹦乱跳起来。

2121.cn: 在高潮中；进行得热火朝天
2121.e: By nine o'clock the street festival was in full swing.  到九点钟，街头庆典已经进入高潮。

2122.cn: 正热闹；处于最活跃的时候
2122.e: We arrived at ten o'clock and the party was already in full swing.  我们十点到的，派对已经闹得正欢。

2123.cn: 在众目睽睽之下；一览无余
2123.e: He dropped the tray in full view of the entire restaurant.  他当着整个餐厅的面把托盘摔了。

2124.i: not the full ˈquid (AustralE, NZE, informal)
2124.cn: 脑子不太灵光；不够聪明
2124.e: People say the old man isn't the full quid, but he beats me at chess.  人家说那老头儿脑子不灵光，可下棋我下不过他。

2125.e: After his illness he decided to live life to the full.  生了那场病之后，他决定要尽情地活。

2126.e: In the fullness of time she will understand why we did this.  时候到了，她自会明白我们为什么这么做。

2127.i: for ˈfun • for the ˈfun of it
2127.e: He learned to juggle just for the fun of it during the long winter.  漫长的冬天里，他纯粹为好玩学会了杂耍。

2128.e: I'd go further and say the whole system needs replacing.  我甚至想说，整个系统都该换掉。

2129.i: go no ˈfurther • not go any ˈfurther
2129.e: I'll tell you, but this must go no further than this room.  我可以告诉你，但这话不能传出这个房间。

2130.i: nothing could be further from the ˈtruth, etc.
2130.cn: 根本不是这么回事；完全不对
2130.e: People think he's arrogant, but nothing could be further from the truth.  人们觉得他傲慢，其实完全不是这么回事。

2131.i: nothing could be further from the ˈtruth
2131.e: You may think I'm judging your outfit, but nothing could be further from the truth.  你以为我在挑剔你的穿着，其实完全不是。

2132.cn: 进一步追究；把某事继续推进
2132.e: If the shop won't refund you, take it further with the ombudsman.  店里要是不退款，就找监察专员继续追究。

2133.i: the ˌgame is not worth the ˈcandle (old-fashioned, saying)
2133.cn: 得不偿失；不值得费这个劲
2133.e: Driving two hours to save five pounds—the game is not worth the candle.  开两小时车省五英镑，实在得不偿失。

2134.e: When the police showed him the video, he knew the game was up.  警察给他看录像时，他知道自己完了。

2135.e: Don't grin like that—you'll give the game away before she opens it.  别那么傻笑，她还没拆礼物你就露馅了。

2136.cn: 让某人捉摸不透；吊人胃口
2136.e: The director keeps us guessing right up to the final scene.  导演一直吊着观众胃口，直到最后一幕才揭晓。

2137.e: She wrote a book about young women who go on the game to survive.  她写了本书，讲那些为了活下去而卖身的年轻女子。

2138.cn: 唯一的选择；同类中最重要者
2138.e: For late-night food around here, that noodle shop is the only game in town.  这一带深夜想吃东西，只有那家面馆一个选择。

2139.e: He may be tough, but he always plays the game with his suppliers.  他也许不好说话，但对供应商一向讲规矩。

2140.i: play sb's ˈgame • play the same ˈgame (as sb)
2140.cn: 以对方的方式行事；跟着对方那一套来
2140.e: If they leak stories, we'll play the same game and talk to reporters too.  他们放风，我们也照着来，同样找记者。

2141.i: play sb at their own ˈgame
2141.cn: 以其人之道还治其人之身
2141.e: She undercut their prices and beat them at their own game.  她压低价格，用他们那一套把他们打败了。

2142.cn: 你搞什么鬼；你打什么算盘
2142.e: You've been hanging round my shop all week—what's your game?  你在我店门口转悠了一星期，到底打什么主意？

2143.e: Stop playing games with me and tell me what you actually want.  别跟我兜圈子了，直说你到底想要什么。

2144.cn: 经历全过程；涵盖各种情形
2144.e: Her films run the gamut of human emotion, from joy to despair.  她的电影涵盖了从欢愉到绝望的各种情感。

2145.cn: 最后一刻；奄奄一息之时
2145.e: They scored at the last gasp and stole the match from us.  他们在最后一刻进球，把比赛从我们手里抢走了。

2146.e: Come and take a gander at the old photos I found in the attic.  过来瞧瞧我在阁楼上找到的这些老照片。

2147.cn: 势头强劲；干得热火朝天
2147.e: Their little bakery is going like gangbusters since the article appeared.  那篇报道出来后，他们的小面包房生意火得不行。

2148.i: everything in the garden is ˈlovely/ˈrosy
2148.e: He talks as if everything in the garden is rosy, but the debts are huge.  他说得好像一切顺利，其实欠了一屁股债。

2149.e: Grandad joked that he'd argue his way through the Pearly Gates.  爷爷开玩笑说，他能靠嘴皮子混进天堂。

2150.e: His report has been gathering dust on the director's desk for months.  他的报告在主任桌上搁了好几个月没人理。

2151.cn: 遭到众人攻击；受夹道责难
2151.e: The players had to run the gauntlet of angry fans outside the stadium.  球员们不得不从愤怒的球迷夹道中穿过。

2152.e: Nobody else would debate him, so she took up the gauntlet.  没人肯跟他辩论，于是她接下了这个挑战。

2153.e: The small company threw down the gauntlet to the industry giants.  这家小公司向行业巨头发起了挑战。

2154.e: He spent his bonus with gay abandon and regretted it a month later.  他把奖金花得毫无节制，一个月后就后悔了。

2155.i: get into ˈgear • get sth into ˈgear
2155.e: It takes me two coffees to get into gear on Monday mornings.  周一早上我得喝两杯咖啡才能进入状态。

2156.e: The whole schedule was thrown out of gear by the sudden strike.  突如其来的罢工把整个日程都打乱了。

2157.e: In general, the food here is good, though tonight was disappointing.  这里的饭菜总体不错，不过今晚让人失望。

2158.e: I liked the whole album, but the last song in particular stayed with me.  整张专辑我都喜欢，尤其最后那首一直在我脑子里。

2159.i: the ˌgenie is out of the ˈbottle
2159.cn: 覆水难收；后果已无法收回
2159.e: Once the files were leaked, the genie was out of the bottle.  文件一泄露，就再也收不回来了。

2160.i: let the ˌgenie out of the ˈbottle
2160.cn: 放出魔鬼；引发难以收拾的后果
2160.e: Legalizing it now would let the genie out of the bottle, he warned.  他警告说，现在放开等于把魔鬼从瓶子里放出来。

2161.i: a ˌgentleman's aˈgreement (also a ˌgentlemen's aˈgreement)
2161.e: There was no contract, just a gentleman's agreement sealed with a handshake.  没有合同，只有握手为凭的君子协定。

2162.cn: 对……感到十分惊讶（或好笑）
2162.e: I can't get over how much your son has grown since last summer.  你儿子从去年夏天到现在长这么高，真让我吃惊。

2163.cn: 躲个清静；抛开一切去休息
2163.e: We rented a cabin in the hills to get away from it all for a week.  我们在山里租了间小屋，躲清静住了一周。

2164.e: I've been trying to get hold of the landlord since Friday morning.  从周五早上起我就一直想联系上房东。

2165.e: If the report is late again, we'll all get it in the neck.  报告要是再晚交，我们都得挨骂。

2166.i: get it ˈon (with sb) (slang, especially AmE)
2166.e: The gossip is that those two got it on after the office party.  有传言说那两个人在公司聚会后好上了。

2167.i: get sb ˈnowhere / not get sb ˈanywhere
2167.cn: 对某人毫无帮助；没有好处
2167.e: Shouting at the clerk will get you nowhere, so try being polite.  冲柜员嚷嚷没有用，客气点试试。

2168.e: After three hours of talks we finally started to get somewhere.  谈了三个小时，我们终于开始有点进展了。

2169.e: My Spanish is still rough, but I'm getting there slowly.  我的西班牙语还很糟，不过在慢慢接近目标了。

2170.i: how selfish, stupid, ungrateful, etc. can you ˈget? (spoken)
2170.cn: 怎么能这么自私（或愚蠢等）
2170.e: He ate the whole cake alone—how selfish can you get?  他一个人把整个蛋糕吃了，怎么能这么自私？

2171.i: how selfish, stupid, ungrateful, etc. can you ˈget? (spoken)
2171.cn: （表示惊讶或不满）也太自私（愚蠢）了吧
2171.e: She never even said thank you—how ungrateful can you get?  她连声谢都没说，怎么能这么不知感恩？

2172.e: Dad's getting on now and shouldn't be climbing ladders.  我爸上年纪了，不该再爬梯子。

2173.cn: 接近（某时刻、数目或年龄）
2173.e: It's getting on for midnight, so we'd better call a taxi.  快到半夜了，我们最好叫辆出租车。

2174.i: there's no getting aˈway from it (informal)
2174.cn: 这是躲不掉的事实；无法回避
2174.e: There's no getting away from it—we simply can't afford this house.  这事躲不过去：这房子我们真买不起。

2175.i: what are you, was he, etc. ˈgetting at?
2175.e: Just say it plainly—what exactly are you getting at?  你直说吧，到底想说什么？

2176.e: My old washing machine finally gave up the ghost last night.  我那台旧洗衣机昨晚终于彻底罢工了。

2177.i: not have a ˈghost of a chance (of doing sth)
2177.cn: 毫无机会；一点希望也没有
2177.e: Without a lawyer he hasn't a ghost of a chance of winning the case.  没有律师，他打赢这场官司的机会等于零。

2178.i: be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself
2178.e: Since the injury, the striker is a ghost of his former self.  受伤之后，这名前锋早已不复当年之勇。

2179.i: the gift of the ˈgab (BrE) (AmE a gift of/for ˈgab) (informal, sometimes disapproving)
2179.e: With the gift of the gab, he could sell sand in the desert.  凭那张嘴，他在沙漠里都能把沙子卖出去。

2180.e: The Irish have a reputation for having the gift of the gab.  爱尔兰人素以能言善辩著称。

2181.i: (not) look a ˌgift horse in the ˈmouth
2181.e: The car's free, so don't look a gift horse in the mouth.  车是白送的，就别挑三拣四了。

2182.e: Adding music to that beautiful film would be gilding the lily.  给那么美的片子再配乐纯属画蛇添足。

2183.e: The little car was packed to the gills with camping equipment.  那辆小车里塞满了露营装备。

2184.i: take the gilt off the ˈgingerbread (BrE)
2184.e: The parking fine rather took the gilt off the gingerbread of our day out.  一张停车罚单把我们这天的兴致全毁了。

2185.e: Gird up your loins—we've got four hours of packing ahead.  打起精神来，还有四个小时的行李要收拾。

2186.cn: 别跟我来这一套；我不信你那套
2186.e: Don't give me that—you knew about the meeting all along.  别跟我来这套，你一直都知道有这个会。

2187.cn: 给某人一次机会；宽容某人
2187.e: Give the kid a break; it's only his second day on the job.  别难为这孩子了，他才上班第二天。

2188.e: Any long marriage needs a lot of give and take from both sides.  长久的婚姻少不了双方的互相迁就。

2189.i: give as good as you ˈget
2189.e: She's small, but in an argument she gives as good as she gets.  她个子小，吵起架来却从不吃亏。

2190.e: You finished the whole essay in an hour? Give me a break!  你一小时写完整篇论文？得了吧！

2191.e: The journey takes about two hours, give or take twenty minutes.  这趟路大约两小时，前后差个二十分钟。

2192.i: give sb what ˈfor • ˈgive it to sb (BrE, spoken)
2192.cn: 狠狠训斥某人；严惩某人
2192.e: Mum gave him what for when she saw the broken window.  妈妈看到打碎的窗户，把他狠狠骂了一顿。

2193.cn: 这一点我承认；这话没错
2193.e: He's lazy, but he's very funny, I'll give you that.  他是懒，不过挺逗的，这我承认。

2194.cn: 不再留情；开始激烈交锋
2194.e: After that insult the gloves were off and the debate turned nasty.  那句羞辱之后双方就不再客气，辩论变得难看起来。

2195.i: handle/treat, etc. sb with kid ˈgloves
2195.e: You'll have to handle the client with kid gloves after yesterday's mistake.  出了昨天那档子事，对这客户你得格外小心。

2196.i: in glowing ˈterms/ˈcolours (BrE) (AmE in glowing ˈterms/ˈcolors)
2196.cn: 热情赞美地；大加褒扬地
2196.e: Her old boss described her in glowing terms to the interview panel.  她的老上司在面试小组面前对她大加称赞。

2197.cn: 目不转睛地盯着；紧贴着
2197.e: The kids were glued to the screen all afternoon.  孩子们整个下午都盯着屏幕不放。

2198.i: a ˌglutton for ˈpunishment, ˈwork, etc. (informal)
2198.e: He's taken a second job—the man's a glutton for punishment.  他又找了份工作，真是个自讨苦吃的人。

2199.e: He was gnashing his teeth after missing the penalty in the last minute.  最后一分钟点球罚丢，他懊恼得直咬牙。

2200.cn: 就一般情况而言；跟同类相比
2200.e: As small hotels go, this one is remarkably comfortable and cheap.  就小旅馆而言，这家算相当舒服又便宜了。

2201.e: He blew out all fifty candles in one go, to everyone's surprise.  他一口气吹灭了五十支蜡烛，大家都很惊讶。

2202.e: The launch is a go—everyone report to the site at six.  发射照常进行，所有人六点到场。

2203.e: With three children and a job, she's on the go from dawn till midnight.  又要带三个孩子又要上班，她从早忙到半夜。

2204.e: Don't go telling your mother about this before I've explained it.  在我解释清楚之前，你可别去跟你妈说这事。

2205.cn: 第一次（或第二次等）尝试
2205.e: She passed her driving test first go, which surprised everybody.  她第一次就考过了驾照，大家都很意外。

2206.i: go all ˈout for sth • go all out to ˈdo sth
2206.cn: 全力以赴争取；竭尽全力做
2206.e: The team went all out to win the cup in their captain's last season.  队长最后一个赛季，全队拼尽全力想夺冠。

2207.i: have a ˈgo (at sth/at doing sth) (informal)
2207.e: I've never made bread before, but I'll have a go this weekend.  我从没做过面包，这周末打算试一试。

2208.e: She's got three writing projects on the go at the same time.  她手头同时有三个写作项目在做。

2209.cn: 不想谈那个话题；别提了
2209.e: His divorce? Let's not even go there tonight.  他离婚的事？今晚咱们就别提了。

2210.e: Didn't you go on a date with him once? Don't go there, please.  你不是跟他约会过一次吗？拜托，别提这茬。

2211.e: Two exams down, one to go, and then I'm free for the summer.  考完两门还剩一门，考完暑假就自由了。

2212.e: Stop playing the goat and help me carry these boxes upstairs.  别耍宝了，帮我把这些箱子搬上楼。

2213.e: The way he chews his pen really gets my goat.  他咬笔的那副样子真让我火大。

2214.i: (good) ˈGod • God alˈmighty • God in ˈheaven (spoken)
2214.cn: （表示惊讶或愤怒）天哪；老天爷
2214.e: Good God, what happened to the front of your car?  天哪，你车头怎么成这样了？

2215.e: Oh my God, I've left the tickets on the kitchen table!  天哪，我把票落在厨房桌上了！

2216.cn: 天哪（有人认为此说法含冒犯意）
2216.e: Oh God, not another form to fill in before we can leave.  天哪，走之前又要填一张表。

2217.cn: （道别时的祝福）愿上帝保佑你
2217.e: Take care on the road tonight, and God bless.  今晚路上小心，愿上帝保佑你。

2218.cn: 自以为是的天之骄子；上天的恩赐
2218.e: He thinks he's God's gift to women, which is exhausting.  他自以为是女人心中的完美男人，真让人受不了。

2219.cn: 如果一切顺利；但愿如此
2219.e: We'll be back home by Friday evening, God willing.  顺利的话，我们周五晚上就到家了。

2220.cn: 自视全能；主宰他人命运
2220.e: Doctors sometimes have to decide who gets the organ, but they hate playing God.  医生有时得决定器官给谁，但没人愿意扮演上帝。

2221.e: I wish to goodness you'd told me before I bought the tickets.  你要是在我买票之前告诉我就好了。

2222.cn: 发誓；千真万确（有人觉得此说法冒犯）
2222.e: I swear to God I posted that letter on Tuesday morning.  我发誓，那封信我周二早上就寄了。

2223.i: in the lap of the ˈgods
2223.e: We've done all we can; the result is in the lap of the gods now.  我们能做的都做了，结果只能听天由命。

2224.e: He cheated everyone for years—what goes around comes around.  他骗了别人这么多年，善恶终有报。

2225.cn: 接近（某年龄、时刻或数目）
2225.e: It must be going on for twenty years since we last met.  我们上次见面到现在快二十年了吧。

2226.i: enough/something to be going ˈon with
2226.e: Here's fifty pounds—that should be enough to be going on with.  给你五十镑，暂时应该够用了。

2227.i: have a lot, something, nothing, etc. ˈgoing for you
2227.cn: 有很多（或一些）有利条件
2227.e: She's young, clever and kind—she's got a lot going for her.  她年轻、聪明又善良，条件真不错。

2228.i: get out while the ˌgoing/ˌgetting is ˈgood
2228.e: The market is still high, so sell up while the going is good.  行情还高，趁势好赶紧脱手。

2229.i: ˌall that ˌglitters/ˌglistens/ˌglisters is not ˈgold (saying)
2229.e: The job sounded glamorous, but all that glitters is not gold.  那份工作听着光鲜，可闪光的未必都是金子。

2230.i: ˌall that ˌglitters is not ˈgold (saying)
2230.cn: 发光的未必都是金子；表面好未必实在
2230.e: That mansion is falling apart inside—all that glitters is not gold.  那座豪宅里面都快塌了，中看不中用。

2231.i: ˌall that ˌglitters/ˌglistens is not ˈgold (saying)
2231.cn: 闪光的不都是金子（三个动词都指发光）
2231.e: Cheap online deals often prove that all that glistens is not gold.  网上的便宜货常常证明，闪光的未必是金子。

2232.e: That little car park behind the stadium is an absolute gold mine.  体育场后面那个小停车场简直是棵摇钱树。

2233.e: The twins were as good as gold during the whole four-hour flight.  四个小时的飞行里，这对双胞胎乖得不得了。

2234.e: Tickets for the final are like gold dust this year.  今年决赛的票简直一票难求。

2235.e: The thirties are often called the golden age of Hollywood cinema.  三十年代常被称为好莱坞电影的黄金时代。

2236.cn: 红人；备受赏识的年轻人
2236.e: He was the golden boy of British athletics until the injury.  受伤之前他一直是英国田径界的宠儿。

2237.i: (kill) the golden ˈgoose (also (kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈegg/ˈeggs)
2237.e: Raising rents that high would kill the goose that lays the golden eggs.  房租涨那么高，等于杀鸡取卵。

2238.i: (kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈeggs
2238.e: However, by killing the goose that lays the golden eggs, the farmer lost everything.  然而农夫杀了那只下金蛋的鹅，结果一无所有。

2239.cn: 巨额退职金；高额解雇费
2239.e: He left the bank with a golden handshake worth two years' salary.  他离开银行时拿到了相当于两年薪水的退职金。

2240.e: The golden rule of hiking is to tell someone where you're going.  徒步的首要准则是告诉别人你要去哪儿。

2241.e: Between strict rules and total freedom, she found the happy mean.  在严规和放任之间，她找到了中庸之道。

2242.e: If the train arrives early, that's all to the good.  火车要是早到，那更好。

2243.e: The repair is as good as finished—just one screw left.  修理基本上完工了，只剩一颗螺丝。

2244.e: With two goals in ten minutes, the match was as good as over.  十分钟内进两球，这场比赛基本上已经结束了。

2245.e: A hot shower after a long hike is as good as it gets.  长途徒步后洗个热水澡，没有比这更享受的了。

2246.e: The old van is still good for another two winters at least.  这辆旧货车至少还能再撑两个冬天。

2247.i: be no ˈgood • not be any/much ˈgood
2247.e: It's no good arguing with him when he's this tired.  他这么累的时候跟他争没有用。

2248.e: She left the bank to do good in a rural health charity.  她离开银行，去一家乡村医疗慈善机构做善事。

2249.cn: 帮某人一个忙；做件好事
2249.e: He did me a good turn once, so I owe him this favour.  他帮过我一次，这个忙我该还。

2250.cn: 对某人有好处；有益于某人
2250.e: A walk in the fresh air will do you good after all that studying.  学了这么久，出去走走对你有好处。

2251.i: for ˈgood (BrE also for ˌgood and ˈall)
2251.e: He's moving to Canada for good next spring.  他明年春天就要永远搬去加拿大了。

2252.e: I'm taking the car keys for your own good—you've been drinking.  我把车钥匙拿走是为你好，你喝酒了。

2253.e: Wait until the pan is good and hot before you add the oil.  等锅完全热了再倒油。

2254.i: good for ˈyou, ˈhim, etc. (especially AustralE good ˈon you, him, etc.) (informal)
2254.e: You finished the whole marathon? Good for you!  你跑完了全程马拉松？真棒！

2255.e: After paying for the stall, we were still forty pounds to the good.  付完摊位费，我们还净赚四十英镑。

2256.e: Those lads hanging round the shed are clearly up to no good.  在棚子边转悠的那几个小子明显不怀好意。

2257.i: kiss/say goodˈbye to sth • kiss sth goodˈbye
2257.cn: 放弃（得到某物的）希望；就此告别
2257.e: If you miss this deadline, you can kiss goodbye to the bonus.  错过这个截止日期，奖金你就别想了。

2258.i: out of the ˌgoodness of your ˈheart
2258.cn: 完全出于好心；不图回报
2258.e: She fixed my fence out of the goodness of her heart and refused payment.  她纯粹出于好心帮我修了篱笆，还不肯收钱。

2259.e: He talks a lot, but on match day he always delivers the goods.  他话是多，可到了比赛日总能拿出真本事。

2260.i: a ˈgoody-goody • a goody ˈtwo-shoes (informal, disapproving)
2260.cn: 装乖讨好的人；伪君子式的乖孩子
2260.e: Nobody liked the goody two-shoes who reported us to the teacher.  没人喜欢那个跟老师告状的乖乖牌。

2261.i: what's sauce for the goose is sauce for the ˈgander (saying)
2261.cn: 对甲适用的规矩对乙同样适用
2261.e: If he can leave early, so can I—what's sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander.  他能早走我也能，一碗水得端平。

2262.cn: 当电灯泡；夹在情侣中间
2262.e: I'm not coming to the cinema with those two—I'd just be playing gooseberry.  我才不跟他俩去看电影，纯粹当电灯泡。

2263.cn: 快刀斩乱麻；果断解决难题
2263.e: She cut the Gordian knot by simply closing the loss-making branch.  她快刀斩乱麻，直接关掉了那家亏损的分店。

2264.i: take sth as/for ˈgospel / ˌgospel ˈtruth (informal)
2264.cn: 把某事当真理；对……信以为真
2264.e: Don't take everything your cousin says as gospel.  你表哥说的话别句句都当真。

2265.cn: 对某事深信不疑；奉为真理
2265.e: It would be foolish to take everything in the papers as gospel.  报纸上说什么都信，那就太傻了。

2266.cn: 你觉得……怎么样；有兴趣吗
2266.e: How does a weekend in the mountains grab you?  去山里过个周末，你觉得怎么样？

2267.cn: 可供争夺；谁都有机会得到
2267.e: Three scholarships are up for grabs this year, so apply early.  今年有三个奖学金名额待争取，早点申请。

2268.e: The minister's fall from grace came after a single leaked recording.  一段录音泄露，这位部长便身败名裂。

2269.i: have the (good) grace to do sth
2269.cn: 有雅量做某事；通情达理地做某事
2269.e: At least he had the good grace to admit he'd been wrong.  他至少还有点雅量，承认自己错了。

2270.i: there but for the grace of ˈGod (go ˈI) (saying)
2270.cn: 若非侥幸，我也难逃此运
2270.e: Seeing him lose everything, I thought: there but for the grace of God go I.  看着他一无所有，我心想：换作我未必强到哪去。

2271.e: He accepted the referee's decision with good grace and shook hands.  他大度地接受了裁判的判罚，还握了手。

2272.cn: 得到某人的青睐；受某人赏识
2272.e: Since the presentation, she's firmly in the director's good graces.  那次汇报之后，她很得主任赏识。

2273.e: Only two of the twenty trainees made the grade this year.  今年二十名学员里只有两个达标。

2274.e: Asking strangers for money goes against the grain for her.  向陌生人开口要钱有违她的本性。

2275.e: He was still gardening at the grand old age of ninety-four.  他九十四岁高龄还在打理花园。

2276.e: He is the grand old man of British jazz and still tours.  他是英国爵士乐界的老前辈，如今仍在巡演。

2277.e: She left him because he took her for granted for years.  她离开他，是因为这些年他从没把她放在心上。

2278.cn: 想当然地认为；视为理所当然
2278.e: I took it for granted that someone had booked the hall.  我想当然地以为有人订好了礼堂。

2279.e: I heard through the grapevine that two managers are leaving.  我听小道消息说有两位经理要走。

2280.e: It's time to grasp the nettle and tell the team about the cuts.  该硬着头皮把裁减的事告诉团队了。

2281.i: the ˌgrass is (always) ˈgreener on the other ˌside (of the ˈfence) (saying)
2281.e: He keeps changing jobs because the grass is always greener on the other side.  他老换工作，总觉得别处更好。

2282.i: the ˌgrass is (always) ˈgreener on the other ˈside (of the ˈfence) (saying)
2282.cn: 别处的草更绿；总觉得别人的更好
2282.e: She envies our quiet village, but the grass is greener on the other side.  她羡慕我们这清静的村子，其实不过是这山望着那山高。

2283.e: The campaign started at the grass roots, with volunteers knocking on doors.  这场运动从基层做起，靠志愿者挨家敲门。

2284.i: not let the ˌgrass grow under your ˈfeet
2284.e: She doesn't let the grass grow under her feet—the shop opened in a month.  她一点不拖沓，一个月就把店开起来了。

2285.i: put/turn/send sb out to ˈgrass (informal, humorous)
2285.e: They put the old engineer out to grass after thirty years' service.  那位老工程师干了三十年后被打发退休了。

2286.i: turn in his, her, etc. ˈgrave (BrE) (AmE roll in his, her, etc. ˈgrave)
2286.e: Grandma would turn in her grave if she saw what we did to the kitchen.  要是奶奶看见我们把厨房改成这样，准会气得在坟里翻身。

2287.e: Consultants have been riding the gravy train on this project for years.  这个项目上的顾问们轻轻松松捞了好几年。

2288.e: The council finally gave us the green light to build the extension.  议会终于批准我们加建那部分了。

2289.e: The cat was out of the door like greased lightning when the vacuum started.  吸尘器一开，那猫像闪电一样窜出了门。

2290.i: be a ˈgreat one for sth/for doing sth
2290.cn: 特别喜欢做某事；很擅长某事
2290.e: My father is a great one for early morning walks in winter.  我父亲特别喜欢冬天一大早出去散步。

2291.e: The food was no great shakes, but the view was worth the trip.  东西不怎么样，不过那景色值回票价。

2292.e: The new bakery is going great guns three months after opening.  这家新面包店开张三个月就红火得不行。

2293.i: it's all ˈGreek to me (informal, saying)
2293.cn: 我完全看不懂；简直像天书
2293.e: He explained the tax rules twice, but it's all Greek to me.  税务规定他解释了两遍，我还是听得云里雾里。

2294.e: We can't order materials until we get the green light from head office.  总部不点头，我们就不能订料。

2295.e: My aunt has green fingers—even her cactus flowers twice a year.  我姑姑特别会种花，连仙人掌一年都开两次花。

2296.e: My colleagues were green with envy when they heard about the trip.  同事们听说这趟旅行，一个个眼红得很。

2297.e: The green-eyed monster appeared the moment she mentioned his new partner.  她一提他的新伴侣，醋意就冒了出来。

2298.e: The card simply said 'Season's greetings from all of us at the office'.  卡片上只写着：办公室全体同仁恭祝佳节愉快。

2299.cn: 灰色地带；界限不清的问题
2299.e: Whether volunteers count as staff is a grey area in the contract.  志愿者算不算员工，在合同里是个灰色地带。

2300.e: These puzzles are a good way to exercise your grey matter.  这些谜题挺能锻炼脑子。

2301.cn: 幕后的当权者；不为人知的决策者
2301.e: The men in grey suits decided the deal long before it was announced.  这笔交易早在宣布前就由幕后人物拍板了。

2302.e: His bicycle came to grief on the icy corner near the school.  他的自行车在学校旁的结冰拐角出了事。

2303.e: My boss gave me grief about arriving five minutes late.  就因为迟到五分钟，老板没完没了地说我。

2304.e: Good grief, have you really eaten the whole pizza already?  天哪，你真把整个披萨都吃完了？

2305.i: hang on/hold on (to sb/sth) like grim ˈdeath
2305.e: The child hung on to the rope like grim death until we pulled her up.  那孩子死死抓着绳子，直到我们把她拉上来。

2306.e: Working with Ann isn't easy, but Tony knows he must grin and bear it.  跟安一起工作不轻松，但托尼知道只能忍着。

2307.cn: 咧嘴傻笑；笑得合不拢嘴
2307.e: He came out of the interview grinning like a Cheshire cat.  他面试出来时笑得合不拢嘴。

2308.cn: 笑得合不拢嘴；喜形于色
2308.e: When she saw the puppy, she grinned from ear to ear.  看到那只小狗时，她笑得合不拢嘴。

2309.e: Traffic ground to a halt when the lorry blocked both lanes.  卡车堵住了两条车道，车流慢慢停了下来。

2530.i: need, want, etc. your ˈhead examined
2530.e: Anyone who swims in that river in January needs their head examined.  一月份还在那条河里游泳的人，脑子准有毛病。

2531.e: If you go climbing in this weather, on your own head be it.  这种天气你还去爬山，后果自负。

2532.e: He was completely out of his head and kept shouting at the traffic.  他神志不清，一直冲着车流大喊。

2533.cn: 越级；越过某人向上级反映
2533.e: She went over her manager's head and emailed the director directly.  她越过经理，直接给总监发了邮件。

2534.i: put your ˌhead in the lion's ˈmouth
2534.e: Testifying against them is putting your head in the lion's mouth.  出庭指证他们等于把脑袋往狮子嘴里送。

2535.i: put sth out of your ˈhead
2535.e: Put the exam out of your head and get some proper sleep tonight.  别再想考试了，今晚好好睡一觉。

2536.e: Racism reared its ugly head again during last weekend's match.  上周末的比赛中，种族主义又露头了。

2537.e: After three viewings my head was spinning with prices and mortgage rates.  看了三套房后，我被价格和房贷利率搞得晕头转向。

2538.i: scream, shout, etc. your ˈhead off (informal)
2538.e: The baby screamed her head off all the way to the airport.  一路到机场，宝宝哭喊个不停。

2539.e: Her new book stands the traditional theory of evolution on its head.  她的新书把传统进化论彻底颠覆了。

2540.i: take it into your head to do sth
2540.e: He suddenly took it into his head to cycle to Scotland alone.  他忽然心血来潮，要独自骑车去苏格兰。

2541.cn: 使某人得意忘形；冲昏头脑
2541.e: All that praise from the critics has clearly turned his head.  评论家的那些赞扬显然让他飘飘然了。

2542.i: run around like a ˌheadless ˈchicken
2542.e: I ran around like a headless chicken all morning and achieved nothing.  我一上午瞎忙一气，什么也没干成。

2543.cn: 成为头条新闻；被大肆报道
2543.e: The scandal hit the headlines just two days before the general election.  丑闻在大选前两天登上了头条。

2544.e: I'd like to bang those two boys' heads together and end this stupid argument.  我真想把这两个小子拉过来，结束这场愚蠢的争吵。

2545.e: Heads or tails? The winner gets to choose tonight's film.  正面还是反面？赢的人挑今晚的电影。

2546.e: If these figures reach the press, heads will roll in the accounts department.  这些数字要是让媒体知道了，财务部有人要倒霉。

2547.i: put your, their, etc. ˈheads together (informal)
2547.e: Let's put our heads together and find a way out of this mess.  咱们集思广益，想办法摆脱这个烂摊子。

2548.e: I offered to pay for dinner but she wouldn't hear of it.  我提出请客，可她根本不答应。

2549.e: You are not going out tonight — do you hear me?  你今晚不许出去，听见我说的没有？

2550.i: not say/hear a ˌdicky ˈbird (BrE, informal)
2550.e: I've written three times and haven't heard a dicky bird from them.  我写了三次信，他们那边一点音讯都没有。

2551.i: you could have heard a ˈpin drop
2551.e: When she announced her resignation, you could have heard a pin drop.  她宣布辞职时，全场鸦雀无声。

2552.e: The last I heard, they were still living somewhere near Leeds.  我最后一次听说时，他们还住在利兹附近。

2553.cn: 在某人听得见的范围内
2553.e: Please don't discuss the diagnosis within the patient's hearing.  请不要在病人听得见的地方讨论诊断结果。

2554.e: He shouts a lot, but at heart he is a very gentle man.  他常大声嚷嚷，但骨子里是个很温和的人。

2555.e: Animal welfare is a subject very close to my grandmother's heart.  动物福利是我奶奶特别关心的话题。

2556.i: by ˈheart (BrE also off by ˈheart)
2556.e: She learned the whole poem by heart in a single evening.  她一个晚上就把整首诗背了下来。

2557.cn: 使某人心碎；令人极为伤心
2557.e: It broke my heart to sell the piano my father gave me.  卖掉父亲送我的钢琴让我心碎。

2558.e: Look at my perfect soufflé — eat your heart out, Michelin chefs!  瞧我这完美的蛋奶酥，米其林大厨们羡慕去吧！

2559.e: We finally had a heart-to-heart about why he wants to leave school.  我们终于推心置腹地聊了聊他为什么想退学。

2560.i: do sb's heart ˈgood (to do sth)
2560.e: It does my heart good to see the two of you laughing again.  看到你俩又有说有笑，我心里真高兴。

2561.e: Her apology clearly came straight from the heart, and everyone forgave her.  她的道歉显然发自肺腑，大家都原谅了她。

2562.e: Have a heart — the poor dog has been walking for hours.  发发善心吧，这可怜的狗都走了好几个小时了。

2563.cn: 心肠极好；有金子般的心
2563.e: He looks grumpy but he has a heart of gold underneath.  他看着脾气坏，其实心肠特别好。

2564.e: You'd need a heart of stone not to cry at that film.  看那部电影不哭，除非你铁石心肠。

2565.e: She threw herself heart and soul into rebuilding the village school.  她全身心投入到重建村小学的工作中。

2566.e: So you had to fly business class? My heart bleeds for you.  这么说你只能坐商务舱？我可真同情你啊。

2567.e: The team came back from the tour tired but in good heart.  球队巡回赛回来，虽然疲惫但情绪很好。

2568.i: your heart is in your ˈmouth (informal)
2568.e: My heart was in my mouth as the plane bumped through the storm.  飞机在风暴中颠簸时，我的心提到了嗓子眼。

2569.e: My heart leapt when I saw his name on the caller display.  看到来电显示上他的名字，我心头一喜。

2570.e: My heart missed a beat when the headmaster called out my name.  校长叫我名字时，我心跳漏了一拍。
