2571.e: In my heart of hearts I knew the marriage was already over.  在内心深处，我知道这段婚姻已经结束了。

2572.i: let your ˌheart rule your ˈhead
2572.cn: 感情用事；情感胜过理智
2572.e: She let her heart rule her head and lent him the money anyway.  她感情用事，还是把钱借给了他。

2573.e: Don't lose heart — plenty of famous writers were rejected twenty times.  别灰心，很多名作家都被退过二十次稿。

2574.e: He lost his heart to that scruffy little dog at the shelter.  他爱上了收容所里那只邋遢的小狗。

2575.i: a man, woman, etc. after your own ˈheart
2575.e: Anyone who hates early mornings is a woman after my own heart.  讨厌早起的人正合我意。

2576.i: not have the ˈheart (to do sth)
2576.e: I didn't have the heart to tell her the puppy had died.  我不忍心告诉她小狗死了。

2577.i: rip/ˌtear the ˈheart out of sth
2577.e: Closing the mine tore the heart out of the whole town.  矿井关闭，把整个镇子的命脉都毁了。

2578.i: set your ˈheart/ˈmind on sth/on doing sth
2578.e: She set her heart on that flat the moment she saw the balcony.  她一看到那个阳台，就一门心思要买下那套房。

2579.i: have your heart/mind ˈset on sth/on doing sth
2579.cn: 渴望得到；一心想做某事
2579.e: He has his heart set on studying medicine in Edinburgh next year.  他一心想明年去爱丁堡学医。

2580.e: Take heart from the fact that your last two interviews went well.  想想你上两次面试都不错，别泄气。

2581.e: She took his criticism to heart and rewrote the entire chapter.  她把他的批评听进了心里，重写了整章。

2582.e: The garden is huge, so the children can run around to their heart's content.  花园很大，孩子们可以尽情地奔跑。

2583.i: with all your ˈheart/your whole ˈheart
2583.e: I thank you with all my heart for everything you did.  我衷心感谢你所做的一切。

2584.e: With a heavy heart she posted the keys back to the landlord.  她怀着沉重的心情把钥匙寄还给了房东。

2585.e: As vice-president, he was only a heartbeat away from the presidency.  身为副总统，他离总统之位只有一步之遥。

2586.e: If they offered me that job again, I'd take it in a heartbeat.  他们要是再给我那份工作，我立马就接。

2587.e: Cheap tickets alone won't win the hearts and minds of local football fans.  光靠低价票赢不了当地球迷的心。

2588.i: if you can't stand the ˈheat (get out of the ˈkitchen) (informal)
2588.e: The kitchen is chaotic at lunchtime; if you can't stand the heat, leave.  午餐时厨房乱成一团，受不了就别待着。

2589.i: in the ˌheat of the ˈmoment
2589.e: I said some awful things in the heat of the moment and deeply regret them.  一时冲动我说了些难听的话，现在很后悔。

2590.i: take the ˈheat out of sth
2590.e: The manager's apology took the heat out of a very tense meeting.  经理的道歉缓和了会议紧张的气氛。

2591.e: The bank turned on the heat and demanded repayment within thirty days.  银行开始施压，要求三十天内还款。

2592.cn: 解雇某人；与某人断绝关系
2592.e: After twelve years the club gave their manager the old heave-ho.  干了十二年，俱乐部把主教练炒了。

2593.e: That quiet beach at sunset was a heaven on earth for us.  日落时那片安静的沙滩对我们就是人间天堂。

2594.e: They're both quiet, kind and love hiking — a match made in heaven.  他俩都安静善良又爱远足，真是天作之合。

2595.e: Good Heavens! I had no idea it was already past midnight.  天哪！我都不知道已经过了半夜了。

2596.e: We'd just lit the barbecue when the heavens opened and everyone ran inside.  我们刚点上烧烤炉就下起倾盆大雨，大家全跑进屋。

2597.e: Things got heavy when he accused her of taking the money.  他指责她拿了钱，场面一下就紧张起来。

2598.e: A smell of damp hung heavy on the empty rooms upstairs.  楼上空房间里弥漫着一股浓重的潮气。

2599.i: time hangs/lies ˈheavy on your hands
2599.e: Time hangs heavy on his hands now that he has finally retired.  退休以后，他觉得时间特别难熬。

2600.e: The first hundred pages were heavy going, but the novel improves later.  头一百页读着很费劲，不过小说后面好多了。

2601.e: This old van is very heavy on fuel, especially in town traffic.  这辆旧面包车特别费油，市区堵车时尤其耗。

2602.cn: 高压手段；过于严厉的方式
2602.e: The new principal runs the school with a heavy hand.  新校长用高压手段管理学校。

2603.e: When he refused to pay, the landlord sent in the heavy mob.  他不肯付钱，房东就派了打手来。

2604.cn: 令人不安的沉默或气氛
2604.e: A heavy silence fell when she asked who had told the manager.  她问是谁告诉经理的，屋里顿时一片沉默。

2605.i: make heavy ˈweather of sth/of doing sth
2605.cn: 小题大做；把事情弄复杂
2605.e: You're making heavy weather of a simple form — just tick the boxes.  一张简单的表格你搞得这么复杂，打勾就行了。

2606.e: We drove to the coast at midnight just for the heck of it.  我们半夜开车去海边，纯粹是图个好玩。

2607.e: What the heck! It's a celebration, so let's order dessert too.  管它呢！今天是庆祝，甜点也点上吧。

2608.e: I applied to three universities in order to hedge my bets.  我申请了三所大学，多留几手。

2609.e: That empty hospital corridor at night gives me the heebie-jeebies.  夜里那条空荡荡的医院走廊让我心里发毛。

2610.i: give/pay ˈheed (to sb/sth) • take ˈheed (of sb/sth) (formal)
2610.e: Pay heed to the weather forecast before you set off up the mountain.  上山前留心一下天气预报。

2611.i: come to ˈheel • bring sb to ˈheel
2611.e: One sharp word from the chairman brought the whole committee to heel.  主席一句厉声，整个委员会就都服帖了。

2612.e: The hotel looked rather down at heel, with peeling paint everywhere.  这家旅馆显得破败寒酸，到处都是剥落的油漆。

2613.e: She turned on her heel and walked out without saying goodbye.  她转身就走，连声再见都没说。

2614.e: The village lived for years under the heel of a brutal landlord.  这个村子多年来受一个残暴地主的压迫。

2615.e: The little dog trotted at his heels all the way home.  小狗一路小跑跟着他回家。

2616.e: The police were hot on his heels as he crossed the border.  他越过边境时，警察正紧追不舍。

2617.e: The boys took to their heels the moment the angry farmer shouted.  愤怒的农夫一喊，男孩们撒腿就跑。

2618.e: The referee blew for a penalty and all hell broke loose.  裁判判了点球，全场顿时乱作一团。

2619.i: beat/knock/kick the ˈhell out of sb/sth (informal)
2619.e: Two men beat the hell out of him and stole his phone.  两个人把他狠揍一顿，抢走了手机。

2620.cn: 让某人吃苦头；痛骂某人
2620.e: The sergeant gave the new recruits hell during their very first week.  第一周里，中士把新兵折腾得够呛。

2621.e: He learned Finnish just for the hell of it, with no plans to travel.  他纯粹为了好玩学了芬兰语，根本没打算去旅行。

2622.cn: 糟糕透顶的；坏得要命的
2622.e: We had the flight from hell — three delays and lost luggage.  我们坐了趟糟糕透顶的航班，延误三次还丢了行李。

2623.e: Grab your coat and let's get the hell out of here.  拿上外套，咱们赶紧离开这儿。

2624.cn: 无论如何；不管多大困难
2624.e: Come hell or high water, I'll be at your wedding on Saturday.  无论如何，周六你的婚礼我一定到。

2625.e: Go to hell! I am not lending you any money again.  见你的鬼去！我不会再借钱给你了。

2626.e: He rode hell for leather down the lane to fetch the doctor.  他沿着小路飞奔去请医生。

2627.i: hell hath no ˈfury (like a woman ˈscorned)
2627.cn: 被抛弃的女人怒火难挡
2627.e: She burned all his letters — hell hath no fury like a woman scorned.  她烧光了他所有的信，女人翻脸真是不得了。

2628.e: The refugee camp in winter was a hell on earth.  冬天的难民营简直是人间地狱。

2629.e: Hell's teeth! Who left the freezer door wide open all night?  见鬼！谁把冰柜门整夜大敞着？

2630.e: We ran like hell to catch the last bus home.  我们拼命跑去赶末班车回家。

2631.e: The roadworks are playing merry hell with deliveries to the shop.  修路把送货到店的事搅得一团糟。

2632.i: scare, annoy, etc. the ˈhell out of sb (informal)
2632.cn: 把某人吓坏；使人极为恼火
2632.e: That horror film scared the hell out of my little sister.  那部恐怖片把我妹妹吓得魂不附体。

2633.e: Apologize to him? I'd see him in hell first.  向他道歉？我死也不干。

2634.e: She's been to hell and back this year, but she's still smiling.  她今年历尽劫难，可依然在笑。

2635.e: To hell with the diet — pass me another slice of cake.  减肥去它的吧，再给我来块蛋糕。

2636.e: What the hell! It's my birthday, so let's take a taxi.  管它呢！今天我生日，打车吧。

2637.e: He'll apologize when hell freezes over, and not a moment before.  他要道歉，除非太阳从西边出来。

2638.i: be ˌhell-ˈbent on sth/on doing sth
2638.e: She seems hell-bent on selling the house before anyone can stop her.  她像是铁了心要在别人阻止之前把房子卖掉。

2639.e: With his daughter at the helm, the family firm doubled its profits.  在女儿掌舵下，这家家族企业利润翻了一番。

2640.e: She took over the helm of the company after her father's sudden death.  父亲突然去世后，她接管了公司。

2641.i: can't help (doing) sth • can't help but do sth
2641.cn: 忍不住做某事；不可避免
2641.e: I can't help laughing every time I watch that old comedy sketch.  每次看那个老喜剧小品我都忍不住笑。

2642.cn: 老天保佑；某人可要糟了
2642.e: God help us if the boss finds out who broke the printer.  要是老板发现谁弄坏了打印机，那我们可就惨了。

2643.e: Give me a helping hand with this wardrobe and we'll be finished.  帮我搭把手抬这个衣柜，很快就好。

2644.e: I never touched your bike that evening, so help me God.  那天晚上我从没碰过你的自行车，我发誓。

2645.i: there's no ˈhelp for it (especially BrE)
2645.e: The last bus has gone; there's no help for it, we walk.  末班车走了，没办法，只能走路。

2646.e: Parking spaces near the station are as rare as hen's teeth on Fridays.  周五车站附近的车位少得跟凤毛麟角一样。

2647.e: Three weeks hence we shall know whether the merger has been approved.  三周之后我们就知道合并有没有获批了。

2648.e: I want an answer here and now, not next week.  我现在就要答案，不是下周。

2649.e: Wild flowers grew here and there along the old railway line.  野花零星地开在废弃铁路沿线。

2650.e: Right, here goes — wish me luck with this interview.  好了，开始了，祝我面试顺利吧。

2651.e: I've never skied before in my life, so here goes nothing.  我这辈子没滑过雪，碰碰运气吧。

2652.e: He's blaming the weather for the delay again — here we go again.  他又拿天气给延误当借口，又来了。

2653.i: here you ˈare • here you ˈgo (spoken)
2653.e: Here you are — one black coffee and a warm croissant.  给你，一杯黑咖啡和一个热羊角面包。

2654.e: Whether he apologized or not is neither here nor there now.  他有没有道歉，现在都无关紧要了。

2655.cn: 转移注意力的事物；幌子
2655.e: The missing passport turned out to be a red herring in the investigation.  那本丢失的护照结果只是调查中的一个幌子。

2656.e: Book the flight tonight — he who hesitates is lost.  今晚就订机票，犹豫就会错失良机。

2657.e: Add a little butter, stir twice, and hey presto, perfect sauce.  加点黄油，搅两下，瞧，完美的酱汁就成了。

2658.e: What the hey! Let's stay another night at the beach.  管它呢！咱们在海边再住一晚。

2659.i: hide your ˌlight under a ˈbushel (BrE)
2659.e: Don't hide your light under a bushel — tell them you speak Japanese.  别藏着掖着，告诉他们你会日语。

2660.i: not see ˌhide nor ˈhair of sb/sth (spoken)
2660.e: We haven't seen hide nor hair of the cat since Tuesday morning.  从周二早上起我们就没见过那只猫的影子。

2661.i: be on a ˌhiding to ˈnothing (BrE, informal)
2661.e: You're on a hiding to nothing trying to please both families at once.  你想同时让两家都满意，根本不可能成功。

2662.i: be for the ˈhigh jump (BrE, informal)
2662.e: If the manager sees this mess, you'll be for the high jump.  经理要是看到这么乱，你可要挨罚了。

2663.cn: 自以为是；愤愤不平地训人
2663.e: She got on her high horse about people not recycling properly.  她为别人不好好垃圾分类而摆出一副训人的架势。

2664.i: have a ˈhigh old time (old-fashioned, informal)
2664.e: We had a high old time at the village fair last Saturday.  上周六村里的集市我们玩得很尽兴。

2665.e: The travel company folded and left two hundred tourists high and dry.  旅行社倒闭，把两百名游客晾在了那里。

2666.e: I searched high and low for my glasses and found them upstairs.  我到处找眼镜，最后在楼上找到了。

2667.e: Don't be so high and mighty — you were once a beginner too.  别那么神气，你当初也是新手。

2668.e: By midnight half the guests were as high as a kite.  到半夜，一半的客人都嗨翻了。

2669.e: Grandmother's silver only came out on high days and holidays.  奶奶的银餐具只在节庆日子才拿出来。

2670.e: The children gave each other a high five after scoring the winning goal.  打进制胜球后，孩子们互相击掌。

2671.e: Swimming with dolphins was definitely the high point of our holiday.  和海豚一起游泳绝对是这次假期最精彩的部分。

2672.e: He left the meeting in high dudgeon after his idea was rejected.  提议被否后，他怒气冲冲地离开了会议。

2673.e: The order came from on high, so nobody dared question it.  命令是上头下的，没人敢质疑。

2674.e: The ship was still on the high seas when the storm hit.  风暴来袭时，船还在公海上。

2675.e: Feelings ran high at the meeting about closing the local library.  关于关闭社区图书馆的会上，大家情绪激动。

2676.e: That bin hasn't been emptied for weeks and stinks to high heaven.  那个垃圾桶几周没倒了，臭气熏天。

2677.e: She took the high road and refused to comment on the ugly rumours.  她选择了正派的做法，拒绝对那些难听的传言发表评论。

2678.e: As soon as the alarm sounded, he hightailed it out the back door.  警报一响，他就从后门飞奔而出。

2679.e: That album was the high-water mark of the band's entire career.  那张专辑是这支乐队整个生涯的巅峰。

2680.e: We cycled the highways and byways of Devon for two whole weeks.  我们骑车走遍了德文郡的大路小道，整整两周。

2681.e: He asked her for money again and she told him to take a hike.  他又向她要钱，她让他滚开。

2682.i: a hill of ˈbeans (old-fashioned, AmE, informal)
2682.e: Without proper funding, our whole plan isn't worth a hill of beans.  没有像样的资金，我们整个计划一文不值。

2683.e: He thinks anyone over forty is over the hill, which is nonsense.  他觉得过了四十就走下坡路了，真是胡说。

2684.e: We chased that runaway pony up hill and down dale all afternoon.  我们追那匹跑掉的小马，翻山越谷追了一下午。

2685.e: The whole family backed her decision to the hilt.  全家人全力支持她的决定。

2686.e: He kept yawning, so I took the hint and went home.  他一直打哈欠，我便识趣地回家了。

2687.e: Her run that morning went down in history as the fastest ever.  她那天早上的成绩作为史上最快载入了史册。

2688.e: That victory earned the little club a place in the history books.  那场胜利让这家小俱乐部名留史册。

2689.i: be/make a (big, etc.) ˈhit with sb
2689.e: Your chocolate cake was a big hit with all the neighbours.  你做的巧克力蛋糕大受邻居们欢迎。

2690.e: The band hit it big after their song appeared in a film.  这支乐队的歌上了电影后一炮而红。

2691.e: I'd better hit the books; the exam is on Monday morning.  我得用功了，周一上午就考试。

2692.e: He hit the bottle badly after losing his job last spring.  去年春天丢了工作后，他开始酗酒。

2693.e: The plan to build a new stadium has finally hit the buffers.  建新体育场的计划最终受挫了。

2694.i: hit the nail on the ˈhead (informal)
2694.e: You've hit the nail on the head — it's really a staffing problem.  你说到点子上了，这其实是人手问题。

2750.e: In all honesty, I never expected the film to be that good.  老实说，我真没想到这部电影会这么好看。

2751.cn: 蜜月期；最初的和谐时期
2751.e: The new manager's honeymoon period ended the moment sales started falling.  销售一下滑，新经理的蜜月期就结束了。

2752.e: It was a point of honour with him never to borrow money from friends.  从不向朋友借钱，是他的名誉底线。

2753.cn: 道义上必须偿还的债；人情债
2753.e: He paid back every penny; to him it was a debt of honour.  他一分不少地还清了，在他看来那是人情债。

2754.i: do sb an ˈhonour ◆ do sb the ˈhonour (of doing sth) (formal)
2754.cn: 使某人感到荣幸；给某人带来荣誉
2754.e: Would you do me the honour of opening our new library next month?  下个月能否有幸请您为我们的新图书馆揭幕？

2755.i: have the ˈhonour of sth/of doing sth (formal)
2755.e: I had the honour of introducing her at the awards ceremony last night.  昨晚颁奖典礼上，我有幸为她做了介绍。

2756.e: Neither of them told the police anything — there's honour among thieves.  两人都没向警方透露半句，果然盗亦有道。

2757.i: in ˈhonour of sb/sth ◆ in sb's/sth's ˈhonour
2757.e: The town held a concert in honour of the doctor who saved so many lives.  镇上办了一场音乐会，纪念那位救人无数的医生。

2758.e: You're on your honour not to look at the answers before Friday.  你得以名誉担保，周五之前不偷看答案。

2759.i: be/feel ˌduty/ˌhonour ˈbound to do sth
2759.cn: 有义务做某事；理应做某事
2759.e: She felt honour bound to tell him what his brother had said.  她觉得自己有义务把他弟弟说的话告诉他。

2760.e: I'd be honoured to speak at your daughter's graduation ceremony.  能在您女儿的毕业典礼上发言，我深感荣幸。

2761.e: The old soldier was buried with full honours in his home village.  那位老兵在故乡以隆重的礼仪下葬。

2762.e: She graduated with honours and had three job offers before June.  她以优异成绩毕业，六月前就拿到了三个工作邀约。

2763.cn: 代主人尽礼（如斟酒、切蛋糕）
2763.e: There's the cake and the knife — would you like to do the honours?  蛋糕和刀都在这儿了，要不你来代劳？

2764.e: After two draws and a win each, honours are even between the teams.  两平一胜各半，两队算是打成平手。

2765.e: We missed the last bus and had to hoof it three miles home.  我们错过了末班车，只好走三英里回家。

2766.e: He makes most of his decisions on the hoof between meetings.  他大多数决定都是在会与会之间匆匆做出的。

2767.e: By hook or by crook, we'll get these tickets before the show sells out.  无论如何，我们都要在票卖光前弄到票。

2768.cn: 使某人摆脱困境（或责任）
2768.e: Her honest apology got him off the hook with the angry customer.  她诚恳地道了歉，让他从那位怒气冲冲的顾客手里脱了身。

2769.e: He swallowed the whole story hook, line and sinker without asking questions.  他一句没问，把那套说辞全盘信了。

2770.cn: 放某人一马；让某人脱身
2770.e: The teacher let us off the hook and moved the deadline to Monday.  老师放了我们一马，把截止日期挪到了周一。

2771.cn: 控制某人；把某人牢牢抓住
2771.e: Once that agency gets its hooks into you, it's hard to leave.  那家中介一旦把你抓住，就很难脱身了。

2772.e: He doesn't give a hoot about what the neighbours think of his garden.  邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。

2773.cn: 满不在乎；一点也不在意
2773.e: She doesn't care two hoots about fashion and wears the same coat daily.  她对时尚毫不在意，天天穿同一件外套。

2774.e: The old car was beyond hope of repair, so we finally sold it.  那辆旧车已经修不好了，我们最后把它卖了。

2775.i: hold out little, etc. ˈhope (of sth/that...)
2775.e: Doctors hold out little hope that he will walk again this year.  医生对他今年能重新走路不抱多大希望。

2776.i: not hold out any, much, etc. ˈhope
2776.e: The rescue team didn't hold out much hope after the third night.  第三个夜晚过后，救援队已不抱多大希望。

2777.cn: 抱着一线希望；仍存幻想
2777.e: We hoped against hope that the letter had simply been delayed.  我们抱着一线希望，觉得信只是寄晚了。

2778.cn: 希望长存；人总心怀期待
2778.e: He's failed the test four times, but hope springs eternal and he's booked again.  他考挂了四次，可希望不灭，又报了名。

2779.e: She still lives in hope that her brother will one day write back.  她仍抱着希望，盼着哥哥有天会回信。

2780.i: I should ˈhope so/not ◆ so I should ˈhope
2780.cn: 希望如此；但愿不会如此
2780.e: You mean he apologized at last? I should hope so, after all that.  你是说他终于道歉了？闹成那样，本该如此。

2781.i: not have a ˌhope in ˈhell (informal)
2781.e: Without a passport he doesn't have a hope in hell of boarding that flight.  没有护照，他根本别想登上那班飞机。

2782.i: not a ˈhope ◆ some ˈhope(s)! (BrE, spoken)
2782.e: Him tidying his room by himself? Some hope!  指望他自己收拾房间？做梦吧！

2783.e: Don't raise her hopes until the hospital confirms the appointment.  医院确认预约之前，别让她抱太大希望。

2784.e: One bad injury shattered his hopes of playing in the World Cup.  一次重伤，让他参加世界杯的希望彻底破灭。

2785.e: Mum was hopping mad about the mess we'd left in the kitchen.  我们把厨房弄得一团糟，妈妈气得跳脚。

2786.e: With big layoffs on the horizon, nobody in the office feels safe.  大裁员在即，办公室里谁都不觉得安稳。

2787.e: His article about the mayor stirred up a real hornet's nest.  他那篇写市长的文章，真捅了马蜂窝。

2788.e: After the bad quarter, the company pulled in its horns and stopped hiring.  业绩糟糕的一季度后，公司开始收敛，停止了招聘。

2789.e: She was on the horns of a dilemma: take the job or finish her degree.  她左右为难：是接受这份工作，还是读完学位。

2790.i: take the ˈbull by the horns
2790.cn: 迎难而上；果断处理难题
2790.e: He took the bull by the horns and asked his boss for a raise.  他鼓起勇气，直接向老板提了加薪。

2791.i: ˌhorror of ˈhorrors (BrE, humorous or ironic)
2791.e: And then, horror of horrors, I realized I'd left the tickets at home.  接着，天哪，我发现票落在家里了。

2792.e: I heard it straight from the horse's mouth — she's leaving in June.  我是从当事人那儿听来的，她六月就走。

2793.i: you can ˌtake/ˌlead a horse to ˌwater, but you ˌcan't make it ˈdrink (saying)
2793.e: I've offered him lessons twice; you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.  我给他找了两次课，牛不喝水强按头也没用。

2794.e: Asking him to reconsider is flogging a dead horse — he's already signed.  再劝他重新考虑就是白费劲，他早签字了。

2795.i: close/shut the stable ˈdoor after the horse has bolted
2795.e: Installing an alarm now is shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted.  现在才装警报器，早就为时已晚了。

2796.cn: 中途换将；中途改变计划
2796.e: We're halfway through the build, so let's not change horses in midstream.  工程都盖到一半了，别在这时候临阵换人。

2797.e: Hold your horses — we haven't even read the contract yet.  别急，合同我们还没看呢。

2798.e: Put Ana on the phones and Sam on design — horses for courses.  让安娜接电话，山姆做设计，各尽所长。

2799.e: My son is fifteen and eats like a horse every single evening.  我儿子十五岁，每天晚上都吃得像头牛。

2800.e: Promising to cut taxes twice was a hostage to fortune he later regretted.  两度承诺减税成了后患，他后来很后悔。

2801.cn: 刚印出来的；最新出炉的
2801.e: These figures are hot off the press, so nobody else has seen them.  这些数据刚刚出炉，别人都还没见过。

2802.e: The detectives were hot on his trail by the time he reached the border.  他到边境时，警探已紧追不舍。

2803.e: School closures are a political hot potato nobody wants to touch.  关闭学校是个烫手山芋，没有政客愿碰。

2804.e: That street is the city's newest hot spot for live music.  那条街是全城最新的现场音乐热门去处。

2805.cn: 了不起的人（或事物）；性感的人
2805.e: Her first novel was hot stuff and sold out in a week.  她的第一部小说非常抢眼，一周就卖光了。

2806.e: Dad gets hot under the collar whenever anyone mentions parking fines.  一提到停车罚单，爸爸就火冒三丈。

2807.e: The thief ran off with two officers in hot pursuit down the alley.  小偷跑掉了，两名警察沿小巷紧追不舍。

2808.e: As the new head coach, he's in the hot seat from day one.  作为新任主教练，他从第一天起就如坐针毡。

2809.e: He landed in hot water after posting those photos online.  他把那些照片发到网上后惹上了麻烦。

2810.cn: 刁难某人；让某人不好过
2810.e: The union threatened to make it hot for any manager who ignored the rules.  工会扬言要让任何无视规定的经理不好过。

2811.e: She's been blowing hot and cold about moving abroad for months now.  几个月来，她对出国的事一直摇摆不定。

2812.i: more ˌtimes than sb has had hot ˈdinners (informal, often humorous)
2812.e: I've told him to lock the gate more times than he's had hot dinners.  我叫他锁门的次数多得数都数不清。

2813.e: I'm feeling not so hot today, so I'll skip the run.  我今天不太舒服，就不去跑步了。

2814.e: Those umbrellas sold like hot cakes the moment it started raining.  一下雨，那些伞立刻卖疯了。

2815.i: too ˈhot for sb (also too hot to ˈhandle)
2815.e: The story was too hot to handle, so the editor pulled it.  这条报道太烫手，编辑把它撤了。

2816.e: He hotfooted it to the station and just caught the last train.  他一路飞奔到车站，刚好赶上末班车。

2817.e: Everyone can tell he's got the hots for the new barista.  谁都看得出他迷上了新来的咖啡师。

2818.e: The builders started drilling at some unearthly hour this morning.  今天一大早，工人们就开始钻墙了。

2819.i: in your ˌhour of ˈneed (often humorous)
2819.e: She lent me her car in my hour of need and never mentioned it again.  我最急的时候她把车借给我，之后再没提过。

2820.e: Buses to the airport leave on the hour from stand four.  去机场的班车每逢整点从四号站台发车。

2821.e: His plans collapsed like a house of cards when the scholarship fell through.  奖学金没拿到，他的计划顿时土崩瓦解。

2822.cn: 在营业（或工作）时间以外
2822.e: The staff sometimes stay for a drink after hours on Fridays.  周五下班后，员工有时会留下喝一杯。

2823.e: Their neighbours play music at all hours and nobody dares complain.  他们邻居不分昼夜地放音乐，没人敢抱怨。

2824.e: Drinks are half price during happy hour, so we'll get there by six.  优惠时段酒水半价，我们六点前赶到。

2825.cn: 作息有规律（或常熬夜等）
2825.e: Since the baby arrived, we've kept very regular hours.  自从孩子出生，我们的作息就非常规律了。

2826.i: the ˈsmall/ˈearly hours (also the ˌwee (small) ˈhours)
2826.e: They sat talking in the kitchen into the small hours of the morning.  他们在厨房里一直聊到凌晨。

2827.i: work all the ˈhours God sends (BrE, informal)
2827.e: He works all the hours God sends just to pay the mortgage.  为了还房贷，他没日没夜地干。

2828.e: The students stayed up until all hours revising for their exams.  学生们复习备考，熬到了深更半夜。

2829.e: Her final song brought the house down and the audience stood up cheering.  她最后一首歌博得满堂彩，观众起立欢呼。

2830.e: That ugly old sofa? I wouldn't give it houseroom.  那张丑沙发？白送我也不要。

2831.i: get on/along like a ˈhouse on fire (informal)
2831.cn: 一见如故；相处极为融洽
2831.e: My mother and my girlfriend got on like a house on fire at dinner.  晚饭时我妈和我女友一见如故。

2832.e: Within two years the little brand had become a household name.  短短两年，这个小品牌就变得家喻户晓。

2833.i: go all round the ˈhouses (BrE, informal)
2833.e: Stop going all round the houses and tell me what you actually want.  别再绕圈子了，直说你到底想要什么。

2834.i: shout, etc. sth from the ˈhousetops/ˈrooftops (informal)
2834.e: He was so proud of the news he wanted to shout it from the rooftops.  这消息让他得意极了，恨不得昭告天下。

2835.e: The manager apologized and said our desserts were on the house.  经理道了歉，说甜点算店里请客。

2836.cn: 你怎么能这样（表示不满或吃惊）
2836.e: You told her about the surprise party? How could you!  你把惊喜派对的事告诉她了？你怎么能这样！

2837.e: How come you're already home when the meeting was at five?  会议五点开，你怎么这么早就回来了？

2838.cn: 你好（初次见面的正式问候）
2838.e: He shook my hand and said, "How do you do," very formally.  他握着我的手，很正式地说了句“您好”。

2839.e: How's this for a bargain — two jackets for the price of one.  这算不算便宜：两件夹克只收一件的钱。

2840.e: The lawyers went into a huddle in the corner before answering the judge.  律师们先在角落里密谈了一阵，才回答法官。

2841.e: There was a hue and cry when the council announced the library would close.  议会宣布关闭图书馆时，引起一片强烈抗议。

2842.e: He hummed and hawed for ten minutes instead of giving a straight answer.  他支支吾吾了十分钟，就是不肯直说。

2843.e: He huffed and puffed all the way up the stairs with the suitcase.  他提着行李箱上楼，一路气喘吁吁。

2844.e: She walked out of the meeting in a huff without saying goodbye.  她气呼呼地退出会议，连招呼都没打。

2845.cn: 人的善良天性；恻隐之心
2845.e: He's not exactly overflowing with the milk of human kindness these days.  他这阵子可算不上有多少善心。

2846.e: Don't tease him about his haircut or he'll get the hump.  别拿他的发型开玩笑，不然他要生气了。

2847.e: It's only hump day and I'm already counting down to the weekend.  才周三，我就开始盼周末了。

2848.e: Once the exams are finished we'll be over the hump for the year.  考完试，今年最难的一关就算过去了。

2849.e: I've got a hundred and one things to do before the guests arrive.  客人来之前，我有一大堆事情要做。

2850.e: I agree with her a hundred per cent about closing the road.  关于封路的事，我百分之百同意她的看法。

2851.e: He was down on his hunkers, fixing the bicycle chain in the rain.  他蹲在地上，冒着雨修自行车链条。

2852.i: in a ˈhurry to do sth
2852.e: She's in no hurry to move out of her parents' comfortable house.  她一点也不急着从父母舒服的家里搬出去。

2853.e: He told a silly joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.  会议一开始，他讲了个傻笑话来暖场。

2854.e: James told a very funny story as an ice-breaker and everyone relaxed.  詹姆斯讲了个很好笑的故事暖场，大家都放松了。

2855.e: His excuses cut no ice with the head teacher at all.  他那些借口在校长面前一点用都没有。

2856.e: We've put the extension on ice until the loan is approved.  贷款批下来之前，扩建的事先搁着。

2857.i: be the tip of the ˈiceberg
2857.e: These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg, believe me.  信我，这些投诉不过是冰山一角。

2858.e: Winning was great, and meeting the coach was the icing on the cake.  赢了球已经很棒，见到教练更是锦上添花。

2859.e: Watch me do it twice and you'll soon get the idea.  看我做两遍，你很快就明白了。

2860.i: not have the ˈfaintest/ˈfoggiest/ˈslightest, etc. iˈdea
2860.e: I haven't the faintest idea where she put the spare keys.  她把备用钥匙放哪儿了，我一点头绪也没有。

2861.e: You have no idea how cold it was standing on that platform.  你根本想象不到站在那个站台上有多冷。

2862.e: Charging children for a glass of tap water — the very idea!  连自来水都要收孩子的钱，亏他们想得出！

2863.e: Don't run away with the idea that this job is easy money.  别以为这份工作是轻松来钱，那是误会。

2864.e: Order pizza and watch the match here? That's an idea!  叫披萨在这儿看比赛？这主意不错！

2865.e: Keep your elbow down when you swing — that's the idea!  挥拍时手肘压低，对，就是这样！

2866.i: give sb iˈdeas (also put iˈdeas in/into sb's head)
2866.e: Don't tell him about the bonus; you'll only give him ideas.  别跟他提奖金的事，那只会让他想入非非。

2867.e: We'll discuss the budget if and when the project is approved.  项目一旦获批，我们再谈预算。

2868.cn: 要说有什么不同的话；倒不如说
2868.e: The weather isn't better today; if anything, it's worse.  今天天气没变好，要说有变化，反倒更糟了。

2869.cn: 要是我是你的话（用于提建议）
2869.e: If I were you, I'd apologize before she hears it from someone else.  要是我，我会在她从别人那儿听说之前先道歉。

2870.cn: 不然；要不（表示不同意见）
2870.e: Business is good for the builders, if not for everybody else.  对建筑商来说生意不错，虽然别人未必如此。

2871.e: If only we had booked the tickets a week earlier.  要是我们早一周订票就好了。

2872.cn: 种种借口；这样那样的条件
2872.e: I want the report on Monday, with no ifs and buts.  报告周一交，别跟我讲条件找借口。

2873.e: She never reads the news before bed — ignorance is bliss.  她睡前从不看新闻，眼不见心不烦。

2874.e: I'll help with the move if there's something in it for me.  要是对我也有点好处，我就帮忙搬家。

2875.e: She was in at the start of the company and still owns shares.  公司创立时她就在场，现在还持有股份。

2876.e: If you think the exam was hard, you're in for a shock next term.  你要觉得这次考试难，下学期还有得受呢。

2877.i: be ˈin for it (BrE also be ˈfor it) (informal)
2877.e: You're in for it when Mum sees what happened to the carpet.  等妈妈看到地毯变成这样，你可要倒霉了。

2878.e: Everyone in the office was in on the plan except the birthday girl.  除了寿星本人，办公室里人人都知道这个计划。

2879.cn: 与某人搞好关系（图好处）
2879.e: He keeps well in with the boss by remembering everyone's birthday.  他记得每个人的生日，借此跟老板搞好关系。

2880.e: The kids were in and out of the kitchen all afternoon looking for snacks.  孩子们整个下午在厨房进进出出找零食。

2881.e: The plan is risky in that it depends entirely on good weather.  这个计划有风险，因为它完全靠天气好。

2882.e: The dinner was full of politicians and captains of industry.  那场晚宴上尽是政客和实业界大佬。

2883.e: He lost his licence for driving under the influence last winter.  去年冬天他因醉驾被吊销了驾照。

2884.e: For your information, that meeting was cancelled two days ago.  提醒你一句，那个会两天前就取消了。

2885.e: She rewrote the whole proposal on her own initiative over the weekend.  周末她主动把整份方案重写了一遍。

2886.e: Someone had to take the initiative, so I called the landlord myself.  总得有人主动，于是我自己给房东打了电话。

2887.e: Be careful with that ladder or you'll do yourself an injury.  小心那梯子，不然你要弄伤自己了。

2888.i: much ˌink has been ˈspilled (on/over sth)
2888.cn: 关于某事已有大量论述
2888.e: Much ink has been spilled over whether the painting is genuine.  关于这幅画是否真迹，已有大量文章讨论。

2889.e: A long walk and a hot meal did wonders for the inner man.  走一趟长路再吃顿热饭，整个人从里到外舒服了。

2890.e: He died at ninety-four, so he'd had a good innings.  他九十四岁去世，也算是享尽天年了。

2891.e: The repairs made serious inroads into our holiday savings.  这些维修费大大侵蚀了我们的度假存款。

2892.e: You've got your jumper on inside out again.  你的毛衣又穿反了。

2893.e: Someone on the inside must have told the press about the merger.  一定是内部有人把合并的事透给了媒体。

2894.e: Take a cheap hobby, for instance running, and you'll save money.  找个便宜的爱好，比如跑步，就能省钱。

2895.e: I never for one instant doubted that she would come back.  我从未有一刻怀疑过她会回来。

2896.i: to all intents and ˈpurposes (BrE) (AmE for all intents and ˈpurposes)
2896.e: To all intents and purposes the deal was finished before lunch.  实际上这笔交易午饭前就谈成了。

2897.e: In the interests of safety, please keep the aisle clear.  为了安全起见，请保持通道畅通。

2898.i: pay sth back/return sth with ˈinterest
2898.e: They beat us last year and we returned the favour with interest.  去年他们赢了我们，今年我们加倍奉还。

2899.e: Your parents nag because they have your best interests at heart.  父母唠叨，是因为真心为你着想。

2900.cn: 为某人挡事；替某人开道
2900.e: My assistant runs interference so I can finish the report in peace.  助理帮我挡下杂事，我才能安心写完报告。

2901.e: The new manager starts in May; in the interim, Sara is in charge.  新经理五月上任，在此期间由萨拉负责。

2902.e: Buses run at ten-minute intervals until the evening rush ends.  晚高峰结束前，公交车每十分钟一班。

2903.i: be ˈinto sb for sth (AmE, informal)
2903.e: He's into his brother for two thousand dollars already.  他已经欠他哥两千美元了。

2904.e: My sister is really into rock climbing these days.  我妹妹最近特别迷攀岩。

2905.i: necessity is the mother of inˈvention (saying)
2905.e: He built a stove out of tin cans — necessity is the mother of invention.  他用铁罐子做了个炉子，需要真是发明之母。

2906.cn: 迫使做出决定；把问题挑明
2906.e: She forced the issue by asking him to decide before Friday.  她要求他周五前定下来，直接把问题挑明了。

2907.e: His so-called friend, in inverted commas, never once visited him.  他那位“朋友”，加个引号，一次都没来看过他。

2908.i: an iron ˈfist/ˈhand (in a velvet ˈglove)
2908.e: She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.  她管这个部门是绵里藏针，柔中带硬。

2909.i: have many/several irons in the ˈfire
2909.e: He's not worried about the rejection; he has plenty of irons in the fire.  被拒他并不担心，他手上还有不少别的路子。

2910.i: strike while the iron is ˈhot (saying)
2910.e: She liked your sample, so strike while the iron is hot and call her.  她喜欢你的样品，趁热打铁给她打电话吧。

2911.e: What's at issue here is whether he was honest, not whether he was clever.  这里的关键是他是否诚实，而不是他聪不聪明。

2912.i: make an ˈissue of/out of sth
2912.e: Who broke it doesn't matter; let's not make an issue out of it.  谁弄坏的不重要，咱们别揪着这事不放。

2913.e: I must take issue with you over your description of that evening.  你对那天晚上的描述，我不得不提出异议。

2914.e: Are those two an item, or just close friends?  他俩是在谈恋爱，还是只是好朋友？

2915.i: be ˌpatience, ˌhonesty, simˌplicity, etc. itˈself
2915.e: The nurse was patience itself with the frightened little boy.  那位护士对受惊的小男孩极有耐心。

2916.e: Come down from your ivory tower and talk to the people who use the system.  从象牙塔里下来，跟真正用这套系统的人聊聊。

2917.cn: 浪荡小子；吊儿郎当的年轻人
2917.e: He was a bit of a Jack the Lad at twenty, always out until dawn.  他二十岁时挺浪荡的，老是玩到天亮。

2918.e: As a jack of all trades, he can fix the roof but not the wiring properly.  他是个万金油，屋顶能修，电路就不行了。

2919.e: I'm in a bit of a jam — could you lend me twenty pounds?  我有点周转不开，能借我二十镑吗？

2920.i: jam on the ˈbrake(s) ◆ jam the ˈbrake(s) on
2920.e: A dog ran out and he jammed on the brakes just in time.  一条狗窜出来，他及时猛踩了刹车。

2921.cn: 许而不予的好处；画饼充饥
2921.e: Every year the boss promises jam tomorrow and nothing ever changes.  老板年年画大饼，什么都没变过。

2922.e: Her jaw dropped when she saw the price on the tag.  她看到吊牌上的价格，惊得下巴都快掉了。

2923.e: Taking the desert road at night was a jaw-dropping experience.  夜里走那条沙漠公路是一次让人瞠目的经历。

2924.i: the jaws of ˈdeath, deˈfeat, etc. (literary)
2924.e: The goalkeeper snatched victory from the jaws of defeat in the last minute.  守门员在最后一分钟把败局扳成了胜局。

2925.e: We had to fill in forms, show passports and all that jazz.  我们得填表、出示护照，诸如此类。

2926.e: He's a Jekyll and Hyde: charming at parties, impossible at home.  他有双重人格：聚会上迷人，在家却难以相处。

2927.i: be/feel like ˈjelly (also turn to ˈjelly)
2927.e: My legs turned to jelly the moment I stepped onto the stage.  一走上舞台，我的腿就软了。

2928.e: He said it in jest, but she took the remark seriously.  他是开玩笑说的，她却当了真。

2929.cn: 常乘飞机四处玩乐的富豪一族
2929.e: The little island became a playground for the jet set in the sixties.  六十年代，这座小岛成了富豪一族的游乐场。

2930.cn: 王冠上的明珠；最珍贵的部分
2930.e: The old library is the jewel in the crown of this university.  这座老图书馆是这所大学的镇校之宝。

2931.e: I always get the jitters the night before a big interview.  重要面试前一晚，我总是紧张得不行。

2932.e: Don't ask him for sympathy; he's a real Job's comforter.  别指望他安慰你，他越劝你越难受。

2933.i: the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob
2933.e: Teaching that class needs the patience of a saint.  教那个班需要极大的耐心。

2934.i: do a good, bad, etc. ˈjob (on sth) ◆ make a good, bad, etc. ˈjob of sth
2934.e: The painters did a lovely job on the front of the house.  油漆工把房子正面刷得非常漂亮。

2935.i: make the best of a bad ˈjob (BrE)
2935.e: The tent leaked, so we made the best of a bad job and sang songs.  帐篷漏雨，我们只好将就着唱起了歌。

2936.e: A bit of tape should do the trick until you buy a new one.  你买新的之前，贴点胶带应该就管用了。

2937.i: give sb/sth up as a bad ˈjob (informal)
2937.e: After three hours we gave the old printer up as a bad job.  折腾了三小时，我们放弃了那台旧打印机。

2938.e: Good job! You finished the whole wall by yourself.  干得漂亮！你一个人把整面墙弄完了。

2939.e: It's a good job you brought an umbrella, because it's pouring.  幸好你带了伞，外面下大了。

2940.e: They've banned cars from the square, and a good job too.  广场禁止通车了，这样才对。

2941.i: a job of ˈwork (BrE, old-fashioned or formal)
2941.cn: 一件正经活儿；分内的工作
2941.e: Clearing that garden was a real job of work for two people.  清理那个花园，对两个人来说真是不小的活儿。

2942.e: This little folding chair is just the job for camping.  这把小折叠椅露营用正合适。

2943.i: more than your ˈjob's worth (to do sth) (BrE, spoken)
2943.e: It's more than my job's worth to let you in without a pass.  没有通行证放你进去，我这饭碗可保不住。

2944.e: At work we can smoke in the canteen, but not on the job.  上班时可以在餐厅抽烟，但工作时间不行。

2945.i: jobs for the ˈboys (BrE, informal, disapproving)
2945.e: Three of his cousins got contracts — pure jobs for the boys.  他三个表亲都拿到了合同，纯粹是安插亲信。

2946.e: What does this tax cut really mean to Joe Bloggs and his family?  这项减税对普通老百姓一家到底意味着什么？

2947.e: Joe Public doesn't care who designed the bridge, only that it works.  老百姓不在乎桥是谁设计的，能用就行。

2948.e: Here's a photograph of you two — maybe it'll jog your memory.  这是你俩的合影，也许能帮你想起来。

2949.e: The business isn't growing, but it jogs along well enough.  生意没什么增长，但也还过得去。

2950.e: She and Scott were joined at the hip all evening.  整个晚上她和斯科特形影不离。

2951.e: He put his shoulder out of joint reaching for the top shelf.  他去够顶层架子，把肩膀弄脱臼了。

2952.e: Being two hours late every day has gone beyond a joke.  天天迟到两小时，这已经不是开玩笑了。

2953.cn: 不是轻松的事；很不容易
2953.e: It's no joke living on such a small income in this city.  在这座城市靠这点收入过日子可不轻松。

2954.cn: 老被拿来取笑的事（或人）
2954.e: His terrible parking has become a standing joke in the office.  他那烂车技已经成了办公室的老笑话。

2955.e: He hid my keys, but the joke's on him — they were his own.  他藏了我的钥匙，结果笑话闹到自己头上，那是他自己的。

2956.e: Stop making a joke of your health and see a doctor.  别拿身体开玩笑了，去看医生吧。

2957.e: He's a good boss because he can take a joke about himself.  他是个好老板，因为拿他开玩笑他也不介意。

2958.cn: 难以捉摸的人；不可预料的因素
2958.e: The weather is the joker in the pack for Saturday's race.  天气是周六比赛中最难预料的因素。

2959.e: Joking apart, we really do need to fix that roof before winter.  说正经的，入冬前我们真得把屋顶修好。

2960.i: you're ˈjoking ◆ you must be ˈjoking (spoken)
2960.e: The boss wants us to work Sunday too? You must be joking.  老板要我们周日也上班？别逗了。

2961.e: You've finished the whole report already? Jolly good!  报告全写完了？太棒了！

2962.e: You made the mess, so you can jolly well clean it up.  是你弄乱的，就该你收拾。

2963.i: keep up with the ˈJoneses (informal, disapproving)
2963.e: They bought a second car just to keep up with the Joneses.  他们又买了辆车，纯粹是跟邻居攀比。

2964.e: His attitude hasn't changed one jot since last year.  他的态度和去年比丝毫没变。

2965.e: I asked the airline for a refund but got no joy from them.  我向航空公司要退款，结果什么也没要到。

2966.i: don't judge a ˌbook by its ˈcover (saying)
2966.e: The café looks shabby, but don't judge a book by its cover.  这家咖啡馆看着破旧，可别以貌取人。

2967.e: Raising twins while studying is a constant juggling act.  一边带双胞胎一边读书，得时时刻刻两头兼顾。

2968.e: In the debate she went for the jugular and asked about his expenses.  辩论中她直击要害，追问他的开销问题。

2969.e: Good sellers stay one jump ahead of what customers will want next.  好的销售总能比顾客的需求抢先一步。

2970.e: When he asked to borrow money again, I told him to go jump in a lake.  他又来借钱，我叫他一边儿去。

2971.e: I only asked a simple question and she jumped down my throat.  我只是问了个简单问题，她就冲我发火。

2972.e: Don't jump the gun and book the hall before the date is confirmed.  日期没定下来就订场地，别操之过急。

2973.e: He jumped the lights at the crossroads and nearly hit a cyclist.  他在路口闯了红灯，差点撞到骑车人。

2974.e: I nearly jumped out of my skin when the balloon burst behind me.  身后气球一炸，我差点吓得跳起来。

2975.i: jump the ˈqueue (BrE) (AmE jump the ˈline, cut in ˈline)
2975.e: That man just jumped the queue and everyone started complaining.  那人插了队，大家都开始抱怨。

2976.cn: 由盛转衰；开始走下坡路
2976.e: The show jumped the shark when they added a talking dog.  剧里加了条会说话的狗，这剧就开始走下坡路了。

2977.e: Two of our best engineers jumped ship just before the launch.  产品发布前，我们两位最好的工程师跳了槽。

2978.cn: 经受层层刁难；费尽周折
2978.e: We had to jump through hoops to get the building permit approved.  为拿到建筑许可，我们费尽了周折。

2979.i: jump ˈto it (AmE also hop ˈto it) (informal)
2979.e: The train leaves in ten minutes, so jump to it!  火车十分钟后开，快点动起来！

2980.e: The jury is still out on whether the new timetable actually helps.  新时刻表到底有没有用，现在还很难说。

2981.e: The bus takes an hour, so we might just as well walk there.  坐车要一小时，我们还不如走过去。

2982.e: I've just about finished packing, give me five more minutes.  我行李差不多收拾好了，再给我五分钟。

2983.e: He handed in his notice and walked out, just like that.  他递了辞呈就走人，说走就走。

2984.e: Just a second — I'll check whether we still have your size.  稍等一下，我看看还有没有你的尺码。

2985.e: I can't talk just now; can I call you back after lunch?  我这会儿没空，午饭后回你电话行吗？

2986.e: Her desk is always just so, with every pen in its place.  她的桌子永远整整齐齐，每支笔都归位。

2987.e: I was about to leave, and just then the phone rang.  我正要出门，就在那时电话响了。

2988.e: We're not moving house just yet, but probably in the spring.  我们暂时还不搬家，大概春天吧。

2989.i: that's just ˈit (also that's just the ˈtrouble)
2989.e: That's just it — nobody told the neighbours about the roadworks.  问题就在这儿，谁都没通知邻居要修路。

2990.e: The family waited twenty years to see the killer brought to justice.  这家人等了二十年，才见凶手被绳之以法。

2991.i: do justice to ˈsb/ˈsth ◆ do sb/sth ˈjustice
2991.e: These photos don't do the mountains justice at all.  这些照片完全拍不出那些山的气势。

2992.e: He was too nervous in the interview to do himself justice.  面试时他太紧张，没能发挥出真实水平。

2993.e: The new intern is as keen as mustard and arrives before everyone.  新来的实习生干劲十足，总是最早到。

2994.e: It was raining hard, but we kept going until we reached the hut.  雨下得很大，但我们坚持走到了小屋。

2995.e: A sandwich at noon should keep you going until dinner.  中午吃个三明治，撑到晚饭应该没问题。

2996.e: You've lost five kilos already — keep it up!  你已经瘦了五公斤，继续保持！

2997.e: I'll tell you the news, but please keep it to yourself for now.  我告诉你这消息，但暂时请你保密。

2998.e: The old man next door keeps himself to himself and rarely speaks.  隔壁的老人独来独往，很少说话。

2999.e: The documents are in my lawyer's keeping until the sale is complete.  交易完成前，这些文件由我的律师保管。

3000.e: The new windows are in keeping with the rest of the old house.  新窗户和这栋老房子的其余部分很协调。

3001.e: That glass tower is completely out of keeping with the old square.  那座玻璃塔楼与老广场极不协调。

3002.e: Take the bike — it's yours for keeps.  这车拿去吧，永远归你了。

3003.e: How the software actually works is completely beyond my ken.  这软件到底怎么运作，我完全搞不懂。

3004.e: The paintings are kept under lock and key in the basement.  那些画锁在地下室里妥善保管。

3005.i: put the ˈkibosh on sth (old-fashioned, informal)
3005.e: The storm put the kibosh on our plans for a beach barbecue.  暴风雨让我们的海滩烧烤计划泡了汤。

3006.i: get a ˈkick from/out of sth (informal)
3006.cn: 从某事中获得乐趣（或刺激）
3006.e: She gets a real kick out of teaching kids to swim.  教孩子游泳让她特别有成就感。

3007.e: Complaining to head office is just kicking against the pricks.  向总部抱怨不过是以卵击石。

3008.e: Our team went out there and kicked butt in the second half.  下半场我们队上场后打得非常凶猛。

3009.i: kick the ˈbucket (BrE, informal or humorous)
3009.e: He joked that he'd sell the boat before he kicked the bucket.  他开玩笑说，翘辫子前要把船卖掉。

3010.i: kick the ˈhabit, ˈdrug, ˈbooze, etc.
3010.e: It took him two years to kick the habit for good.  他花了两年才彻底把这毛病戒掉。

3011.e: The old market is still alive and kicking every Saturday morning.  那个老市场每周六上午依旧热闹得很。

3012.e: I kicked my heels at the airport for four hours waiting for him.  我在机场干等了他四个小时。

3013.e: Cutting her hours after all that overtime really kicked her in the teeth.  加了那么多班还砍她工时，真是狠狠打击了她。

3014.i: kick sth into the long ˈgrass (BrE)
3014.e: The council kicked the parking plan into the long grass again.  议会又把停车方案束之高阁了。

3015.e: They kicked the whole proposal into touch after the first vote.  第一轮表决后，他们就把整个提案搁下了。

3016.e: At eighteen he kicked over the traces and moved to the city.  十八岁那年他挣脱管束，搬去了城里。

3017.i: kick the ˈtyres (BrE) (AmE kick the ˈtires)
3017.cn: 验货；检验某物是否合适
3017.e: Before signing, let's kick the tyres on this software for a week.  签约前，我们先把这软件试用一周看看。

3018.e: Most people at the car lot on Sundays are just tyrekickers.  周日来车行的人多半只看不买。

3019.i: a kick up the ˈbackside (also a kick in the ˈpants) (informal)
3019.e: That bad review was the kick up the backside he needed.  那篇差评正是他需要的当头一棒。

3020.i: kick up a ˈfuss, ˈrow, etc. (informal)
3020.e: She kicked up a fuss when the waiter brought the wrong bill.  服务员拿错账单，她大吵了一通。

3021.i: kick up your ˈheels (informal, especially AmE)
3021.e: After exams we all went out to kick up our heels downtown.  考完试我们都进城好好玩了一场。

3022.e: They kicked him upstairs to a title with no real power.  他们把他明升暗降，给了个没实权的头衔。

3023.e: Mocking her after the layoff is just kicking someone when they're down.  她被裁了还嘲笑她，纯属落井下石。

3024.e: I could kick myself for not writing down her number.  没记下她的号码，我真想抽自己一巴掌。

3025.i: beat/knock/kick the ˈhell out of sb/sth (informal)
3025.e: The storm knocked the hell out of the fence along the back garden.  暴风雨把后花园的围栏打得稀烂。

3026.e: Some bored teenagers around here break windows and steal signs just for kicks.  这一带有些无聊的青少年砸玻璃、偷路牌纯粹是为了找刺激。

3027.i: handle, treat, etc. sb with kid ˈgloves
3027.e: You'll have to handle the new client with kid gloves at first.  一开始你得小心翼翼地对待这位新客户。

3028.i: like a kid in a ˈcandy store/shop (AmE)
3028.cn: 兴奋得像进了糖果店的孩子
3028.e: At the tool sale he was like a kid in a candy store.  在工具特卖会上，他兴奋得像个进了糖果店的孩子。

3029.e: No kidding, I saw her win the whole tournament last year.  真的，我去年亲眼看她拿了整个锦标赛冠军。

3030.i: you're ˈkidding ◆ you must be ˈkidding
3030.e: They cancelled the flight again? You must be kidding.  航班又取消了？不会吧。

3031.e: For a climber like her, that route is kids' stuff.  对她这样的攀岩者，那条线路简直是小儿科。

3032.cn: 设宴款待；隆重迎接归来的人
3032.e: When their son came back from abroad, they killed the fatted calf.  儿子从国外回来，他们摆宴接风。

3033.e: My sleep has been out of kilter since the trip to Japan.  自从去了日本，我的作息就一直乱着。

3034.cn: 以实物支付；以同样方式
3034.e: The farmer paid the workers partly in kind, with milk and eggs.  农场主部分用牛奶和鸡蛋抵付工钱。

3035.e: He said I'd agreed, but I did nothing of the kind.  他说我同意了，我根本没有。

3036.e: Those two are very much of a kind — stubborn and generous.  这两人是一路货色：又倔又大方。

3037.cn: 徒有其名的；勉强算得上的
3037.e: They gave us a meal of a kind, mostly cold potatoes.  他们给了顿所谓的饭，主要是冷土豆。

3038.e: My grandmother's ring is one of a kind and can't be replaced.  奶奶的戒指独一无二，没法再配一个。

3039.cn: 诸如此类的事；类似的东西
3039.e: He mentioned a merger or something of the kind at lunch.  午饭时他提到合并之类的事。

3040.e: The committee did not look kindly on our late application.  委员会对我们迟交的申请并不认可。

3041.e: He doesn't take kindly to being told how to run his kitchen.  别人教他怎么管厨房，他很不高兴。

3042.e: That little painting sold for a king's ransom at auction.  那幅小画在拍卖会上卖了一大笔钱。

3043.i: blow, send, etc. sb to kingdom ˈcome
3043.e: One spark near that tank could blow us all to kingdom come.  那个油罐旁边一点火星就能把我们全送上西天。

3044.e: She refused to kiss and tell, even when the papers offered money.  即便报社出钱，她也不肯把私情抖出去。

3045.e: Come here and let Mummy kiss your knee better.  过来，妈妈亲亲你的膝盖就不疼了。

3046.i: the kiss of ˈdeath (informal, often humorous)
3046.cn: 死亡之吻；看似有利实则致命
3046.e: His public support was the kiss of death for the candidate.  他的公开支持成了那位候选人的催命符。

3047.cn: 口对口人工呼吸；起死回生之举
3047.e: A lifeguard gave the boy the kiss of life on the beach.  一名救生员在沙滩上给男孩做了人工呼吸。

3048.e: The lads dared him to get his kit off and jump in the river.  几个小伙起哄让他脱光跳进河里。

3049.i: everything but/bar the kitchen ˈsink (informal, humorous)
3049.cn: 什么都带上；一大堆东西
3049.e: For a two-day trip she packed everything but the kitchen sink.  才去两天，她却把家当都带上了。

3050.e: The minister flew a kite about raising the tax to see the reaction.  部长放风说要加税，试探各方反应。

3051.e: He left the village and all his kith and kin behind.  他离开了村子，也离开了所有亲友。

3052.e: Mum was having kittens because we hadn't called all evening.  我们一晚上没打电话，妈妈急得团团转。

3053.e: I've known Tom since he was knee-high to a grasshopper.  汤姆还是个小不点儿时我就认识他了。

3054.cn: 使某人屈服；彻底击败某人
3054.e: Two years of strikes brought the company to its knees.  两年的罢工让这家公司彻底屈服。

3055.e: The cyber attack brought the whole rail network to its knees.  那次网络攻击让整个铁路系统陷入瘫痪。

3056.e: My knees were knocking as I walked up to give my speech.  上台演讲时，我腿肚子直打颤。

3057.e: He was on his knees in the garden pulling out weeds.  他跪在花园里拔草。

3058.i: get/have your ˈknickers in a twist (BrE, informal)
3058.e: Don't get your knickers in a twist — the train is only ten minutes late.  别慌，火车才晚点十分钟。

3059.i: get/have your ˈpanties in a knot (AmE, informal)
3059.e: He got his panties in a knot over a tiny spelling mistake.  为一个小拼写错误，他就急得不行。

3060.i: get your ˈknife into sb ◆ have your ˈknife in sb
3060.cn: 跟某人过不去；屡屡刁难
3060.e: The supervisor has had her knife in him since the argument.  自从那次争吵，主管就一直跟他过不去。

3061.e: She goes under the knife on Thursday for her shoulder.  她周四要做肩膀手术。

3062.e: The new saw went through the log like a knife through butter.  这把新锯子切木头像切黄油一样轻松。

3063.e: He waited until the meeting to put the knife in about my figures.  他专等开会时，拿我的数据狠狠捅了我一刀。

3064.e: Mentioning his ex at dinner really twisted the knife.  晚饭时提起他前妻，真是往他伤口上撒盐。

3065.i: you could cut the atmosphere with a ˈknife
3065.e: After the argument you could cut the atmosphere with a knife.  那场争吵之后，气氛紧张得让人窒息。

3066.i: on a ˈknife-edge (also on a ˈrazor's edge)
3066.cn: 处于危险（或难以预料）的境地
3066.e: The whole election is on a knife-edge with two seats left.  只剩两个席位，整场选举悬在刀刃上。

3067.e: The driver was robbed at knifepoint outside the station.  司机在车站外被人持刀抢劫。

3068.i: a knight in shining ˈarmour (BrE) (AmE a knight in shining ˈarmor) (usually humorous)
3068.cn: 救人于危难的侠士；救星
3068.e: My neighbour arrived like a knight in shining armour with jump leads.  邻居像救星一样，拿着搭电线赶来了。

3069.e: A white knight bought the failing bookshop and saved every job.  一位白衣骑士买下濒临倒闭的书店，保住了所有工作。

3070.e: She knitted her brows as she read the strange letter again.  她又读了一遍那封奇怪的信，眉头紧锁。

3071.e: After the third defeat, the knives are out for the manager.  三连败之后，众人对主教练磨刀霍霍。

3072.e: It's the same old plan with knobs on, just a new name.  还是那套老计划，只是变本加厉换了个名。

3073.e: Wear the blue dress tonight — you'll knock them dead.  今晚穿那条蓝裙子，保证惊艳全场。

3074.i: knock sb/sth into a cocked ˈhat (BrE)
3074.e: Her homemade bread knocks the supermarket stuff into a cocked hat.  她自己烤的面包把超市卖的比得一无是处。

3075.e: Knock it off, you two, I'm trying to work in here.  你俩别闹了，我这儿还在干活呢。

3076.cn: 把某人拉下神坛；灭某人威风
3076.e: One bad season knocked the champion off his pedestal.  一个糟糕的赛季就把这位冠军拉下了神坛。

3077.i: knock sth on the ˈhead (BrE, informal)
3077.e: Let's knock the whole idea on the head before we waste more money.  趁没再浪费钱，咱们把这想法叫停吧。

3078.i: knock the ˈstuffing out of sb (informal)
3078.cn: 使某人一蹶不振；打垮某人
3078.e: The rise in airfares knocked the stuffing out of our travel plans.  机票涨价把我们的旅行计划彻底打垮了。

3079.cn: 使某人震惊得不知所措
3079.e: The news of the closure knocked us all sideways.  关闭的消息让我们都懵了。

3190.e: In a last-ditch attempt to save the shop, they started selling online.  为救下这家店，他们最后一搏，开始网上卖货。

3191.e: I'll leave the back door on the latch so you can get in.  我把后门虚掩着，你自己进来就行。

3192.e: It's a bit late in the day to complain about the design now.  现在才抱怨设计，未免太迟了。

3193.e: The speaker was Dr Grant, late of the university's biology department.  演讲人是格兰特博士，不久前还在该校生物系任职。

3194.e: He has been noticeably quieter of late, which worries his mother.  他近来明显话少了，他母亲很担心。

3195.e: Finish your homework now and we can watch a film later on.  先写完作业，过会儿我们看电影。

3196.i: get into a ˈlather • work yourself into a ˈlather
3196.e: Don't work yourself into a lather over one late email.  别为一封迟到的邮件急得团团转。

3197.e: He got into a right lather when the taxi failed to turn up.  出租车没来，他急得直冒火。

3198.e: She was in a lather about the inspection all weekend.  整个周末她都为检查的事紧张得不行。

3199.e: We had a good laugh about it once the panic was over.  慌乱过去以后，我们为这事好好笑了一场。

3200.cn: 别逗了；别让我笑掉大牙
3200.e: Him, run a marathon? Don't make me laugh.  他？跑马拉松？别逗了。

3201.e: They swapped name badges just for a laugh at the conference.  在会上他们换了胸牌，纯粹图个乐子。

3202.e: We still have a good laugh about the day the tent blew away.  帐篷被风刮跑那天的事，我们至今笑个不停。

3203.i: laugh all the way to the ˈbank (informal)
3203.cn: 大赚一笔；数钱数到手软
3203.e: The critics hated the film, but the producers laughed all the way to the bank.  影评人骂惨了这部片，制片方却赚得盆满钵满。

3204.e: Wearing this to the party would make me a laughing stock.  穿这个去派对我会成为笑柄的。

3205.cn: 不是闹着玩的事；严肃的事
3205.e: Losing your passport abroad is no laughing matter.  在国外弄丢护照可不是闹着玩的。

3206.i: a barrel/bundle of ˈlaughs (informal, often ironic)
3206.e: Three hours of safety training—what a barrel of laughs that was.  三小时安全培训，可真是「有趣」极了。

3207.i: he who laughs last laughs ˈlongest (saying)
3207.cn: 谁笑到最后谁笑得最好
3207.e: They mocked his savings plan, but he who laughs last laughs longest.  他们笑话他的储蓄计划，可谁笑到最后谁笑得最好。

3208.cn: 谨防被人超越；力保荣誉
3208.e: With that new bakery opening, the old shop must look to its laurels.  新面包店一开，老店可得当心自己的地位了。

3209.e: Rather than argue for months, they decided to go to law.  与其吵上几个月，他们决定打官司。

3210.i: have the ˈlaw on sb (BrE, informal)
3210.e: Touch my fence again and I'll have the law on you.  再碰我的篱笆，我就报警告你。

3211.e: The mayor promised to restore law and order in the town centre.  市长承诺恢复市中心的治安。

3212.e: By the law of averages, this team has to win a match eventually.  按概率算，这支队总该赢一场了。

3213.e: In that industry it's the law of the jungle—only the ruthless survive.  那个行业奉行丛林法则，只有狠角色能活下来。

3214.i: a law unto himˈself, herˈself, etc.
3214.cn: 我行我素的人；独断专行的人
3214.e: The old caretaker is a law unto himself and ignores every memo.  老看门人我行我素，什么通知都不理。

3215.i: a person who does what they want
3215.cn: 独断专行的人；我行我素的人
3215.e: She is a person who does what they want, whatever the rules say.  她是个我行我素的人，规矩管不住她。

3216.i: take the law into your own ˈhands
3216.e: When the police did nothing, the villagers took the law into their own hands.  警察不管，村民就自己动手处置了。

3217.cn: 这又不犯法；谁也管不着
3217.e: I'm singing in my own garden—there's no law against it.  我在自家院子唱歌，又不犯法。

3218.e: The failure of the merger was laid at the chairman's door.  合并失败的责任被归到了董事长头上。

3219.e: The diary lays bare the loneliness he hid from everyone.  这本日记揭示了他瞒着所有人的孤独。

3220.e: The report lays bare the shocking housing conditions in the city.  报告披露了这座城市恶劣的住房条件。

3221.e: Two families now lay claim to the same patch of farmland.  两家人如今都声称这块农地归自己。

3222.e: The rebels agreed to lay down their arms in return for an amnesty.  叛军同意放下武器，换取特赦。

3223.e: He walked in and started laying down the law about parking spaces.  他一进来就对停车位的事发号施令。

3224.e: Thousands laid down their lives for a country they barely knew.  成千上万的人为一个他们几乎不了解的国家献出了生命。

3225.e: His opening joke laid an egg and the room went silent.  他开场的笑话砸了锅，全场鸦雀无声。

3226.cn: （常用于否定句）动某人一根手指头
3226.e: If you lay a finger on my little brother, you'll answer to me.  你敢动我弟弟一根手指头，我跟你没完。

3227.i: lay it on ˈthick/with a ˈtrowel (also pile it on ˈthick, pile it ˈon)
3227.e: He laid it on thick about how brilliant her cooking was.  他把她的厨艺夸得天花乱坠。

3228.e: The coach laid it on the line: train harder or leave the squad.  教练把话挑明了：要么加练，要么走人。

3229.e: A nasty chest infection laid him low for the whole of January.  一场严重的肺部感染让他整个一月都躺在床上。

3230.e: Reporters laid siege to the actor's house for a full week.  记者把这位演员的住所围了整整一周。

3231.i: speak to or question the people living there
3231.e: Officers went door to door to speak to or question the people living there.  警员挨家挨户向当地居民了解情况。

3232.i: an army tries to capture a town by surrounding it
3232.e: For months an army tried to capture the town by surrounding it and waiting.  几个月里，军队围困该城，坐等其降。

3233.e: Arguing about who started it will lead us nowhere tonight.  今晚争论谁先挑事，一点用也没有。

3234.e: She was laid to rest beside her husband in the village churchyard.  她被安葬在村里教堂墓地丈夫的身旁。

3235.e: The company's statement finally laid the takeover rumours to rest.  公司的声明终于平息了收购传闻。

3236.i: lay sth ˈwaste • lay ˈwaste to sth (formal)
3236.e: The fire laid waste to thousands of hectares of forest in two days.  大火两天内烧毁了数千公顷森林。

3237.cn: 把某人引入歧途；把某人带坏
3237.e: His parents blamed the older boys for leading him astray.  他父母怪那些大孩子把他带坏了。

3238.cn: 牵着某人鼻子走；完全控制某人
3238.e: She lets her business partner lead her by the nose on every decision.  每件事她都让合伙人牵着鼻子走。

3239.i: make sb do everything you want; control sb
3239.cn: 完全操控某人；牵着某人走
3239.e: A good manager doesn't make sb do everything you want by fear alone.  好的管理者不会只靠威吓让人事事听命。

3240.cn: 有影响的人物；头面人物
3240.e: She was a leading light in the campaign to save the old cinema.  她是拯救老影院运动中的核心人物。

3241.e: The lawyer objected that it was a leading question and the judge agreed.  律师反对说这是诱导性提问，法官同意了。

3242.i: take a leaf out of sb's ˈbook
3242.e: You should take a leaf out of your sister's book and start saving.  你该学学你姐姐，开始存点钱。

3243.cn: 非某人能力（或财力）所及
3243.e: That flat by the river is way out of our league on one salary.  靠一份工资，河边那套公寓我们根本买不起。

3244.e: The guard turned out to be in league with the thieves all along.  原来那名保安一直和窃贼串通一气。

3245.i: not be in the same ˈleague/ˈclass/ˈstreet
3245.e: He plays well, but he's not in the same league as his older brother.  他打得不错，可跟他哥比差着档次。

3246.e: Pull over at the next services—I need to take a leak.  在下个服务区停一下，我要去撒尿。

3247.cn: 冒险之举；后果难料的行动
3247.e: Quitting a steady job to open a café was a real leap in the dark.  辞掉稳定工作去开咖啡馆，实在是一场冒险。

3248.e: Read the whole contract first—look before you leap.  先把合同读完，三思而后行。

3249.e: Her Chinese has improved by leaps and bounds since she moved to Beijing.  搬到北京后，她的中文突飞猛进。

3250.e: He's learnt his lesson and never lends money to friends now.  他吸取了教训，如今再不借钱给朋友。

3251.i: a (new) lease of ˈlife (BrE) (AmE a (ˌnew) lease on ˈlife)
3251.e: The new knee gave my grandmother a whole new lease of life.  新换的膝关节让我奶奶像换了个人。

3252.i: at the (very) ˈleast • ˌleave it ˈout (BrE, spoken)
3252.e: The repairs will cost two thousand pounds at the very least.  修理费至少也要两千英镑。

3253.i: (not) in the ˈleast • leave sb ˈto it (informal)
3253.e: I'm not in the least bothered about who gets the credit.  功劳算谁的，我一点也不在意。

3254.i: not ˈleast (written) • without (so much as) a ˌby your ˈleave
3254.e: Everyone was exhausted, not least the driver who had done nine hours.  人人都累坏了，尤其是开了九小时车的司机。

3255.cn: 赶上进度；挽回失去的时间
3255.e: After the strike the factory worked weekends to make up leeway.  罢工过后，工厂周末加班赶进度。

3256.i: be (way out/over) in left ˈfield (AmE, informal)
3256.e: His theory about the missing cat was way out in left field.  他关于那只走失猫的说法离谱得很。

3257.i: the ˌleft hand doesn't know what the ˌright hand's ˈdoing
3257.cn: 左手不知右手在做什么；内部不通气
3257.e: In that department the left hand doesn't know what the right hand's doing.  那个部门左手不知右手在干什么。

3258.cn: （同一机构内）各自为政，互不通气
3258.e: Two teams booked the same hall—clearly the left hand doesn't know what the right hand's doing.  两个组订了同一个厅，显然内部完全不通气。

3259.i: the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing
3259.cn: 内部沟通不畅；各行其是
3259.e: Obviously the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing at that bank.  显然那家银行内部完全不通气。

3260.e: The part-timers felt left out in the cold when the bonuses were announced.  发奖金时，兼职员工觉得自己被晾在一边。

3261.i: ˌleft, right and ˈcentre • ˌright, left and ˈcentre
3261.e: He was handing out business cards left, right and centre at the fair.  在展会上他四处发名片。

3262.i: ˈcentre (BrE) (AmE ˌleft, right and ˈcenter, ˌright, left and ˈcenter) (informal)
3262.e: The new café is being recommended left, right and center online.  网上到处都在推荐这家新咖啡馆。

3263.e: Break a leg tonight—I'll be in the third row cheering.  今晚演出加油，我坐第三排给你鼓劲。

3264.e: All he talked about that summer was getting his leg over.  那年夏天他张口闭口都是男女那点事。

3265.e: We legged it down the alley as soon as the alarm went off.  警报一响，我们撒腿沿小巷跑了。

3266.i: not have a ˌleg to ˈstand on (informal)
3266.e: Without a receipt you haven't got a leg to stand on in this dispute.  没有收据，你在这场纠纷里根本站不住脚。

3267.e: That documentary really has legs—people still discuss it a year later.  那部纪录片很有后劲，一年后大家还在讨论。

3268.cn: 托某人一把；助某人一臂之力
3268.e: Give me a leg-up and I'll climb over and open the gate.  托我一把，我翻过去把门打开。

3269.e: Take the brochure home and read it at your leisure.  把册子拿回家，有空慢慢看。

3270.i: lend ˈcolour to sth (BrE) (AmE lend ˈcolor to sth)
3270.cn: 使…显得可信；增加可信度
3270.e: The photographs lend colour to his story about the storm.  这些照片让他讲的暴风雨经历显得更可信。

3271.e: Thanks for lending an ear—I just needed to talk it through.  谢谢你听我说，我就是想倾诉一下。

3272.e: Could you lend me a hand with these boxes before you go?  走之前能帮我搬一下这些箱子吗？

3273.e: Several actors lent their names to the campaign against the new road.  几位演员公开支持反对修新路的运动。

3274.i: lend supˈport, ˈweight, ˈcredence, etc. to sth
3274.e: The new findings lend weight to her theory about early migration.  新发现为她关于早期迁徙的理论提供了佐证。

3275.e: He spoke at length about the changes coming to the department.  他详详细细讲了部门即将发生的变化。

3276.i: the length and ˈbreadth of sth
3276.e: They cycled the length and breadth of Ireland one wet summer.  一个多雨的夏天，他们骑车走遍了爱尔兰。

3277.i: go to any, great, etc. ˈlengths (to do sth)
3277.e: She went to great lengths to find the owner of the lost dog.  为找到走失狗的主人，她费尽了心思。

3278.i: try very hard (to do sth); do whatever is necessary
3278.cn: 竭尽全力；无所不用其极
3278.e: He will try very hard to do whatever is necessary to keep the shop open.  为保住这家店，他会想尽一切办法。

3279.i: a leopard cannot change its ˈspots (saying)
3279.e: He promised to stop gossiping, but a leopard cannot change its spots.  他保证不再说闲话，可本性难移。

3280.e: He can't boil an egg, much less cook dinner for twelve.  他连鸡蛋都煮不好，更别提给十二个人做饭了。

3281.e: Take half the furniture out—with this room, less is more.  搬走一半家具吧，这屋子少即是多。

3282.e: She was invited to dinner by the ambassador, no less.  她竟然被大使请去吃饭。

3283.e: No less than four hundred people turned up for the free concert.  免费音乐会来了多达四百人。

3284.e: Taking the night train was the lesser of two evils, given the airport chaos.  机场一团糟，坐夜车算是两害相权取其轻。

3285.e: She let fall that the manager had already handed in his notice.  她无意中说漏，经理已经递了辞呈。

3286.i: ˌlet sb/sth ˈgo • ˌlet ˈgo (of sb/sth)
3286.e: Don't let go of the rope until I say so.  我没喊之前别松开绳子。

3287.e: It's your birthday—let yourself go for once and dance.  今天你生日，就放开一回跳跳舞吧。

3288.cn: 狠狠教训某人；严厉斥责
3288.e: When he finally came home at three, his father let him have it.  他凌晨三点才回家，被父亲狠狠训了一顿。

3289.e: He apologized, so let's let it go at that.  他道歉了，这事就到此为止吧。

3290.e: Let me see—I think we last met at Kate's wedding.  让我想想，我们上次好像是在凯特婚礼上见的。

3291.i: the ˌletter of the ˈlaw (often disapproving)
3291.e: He stuck to the letter of the law and ignored its purpose entirely.  他死抠法律条文，完全不顾立法本意。

3292.cn: 不折不扣地；一丝不差地
3292.e: Follow the recipe to the letter or the bread won't rise.  严格照食谱来，不然面包发不起来。

3293.i: do/try your level ˈbest (to do sth)
3293.e: I'll do my level best to get the report to you by Friday.  我一定尽全力周五前把报告交给你。

3294.e: She kept a level head while everyone else panicked about the fire.  别人为火灾慌成一团，她始终保持冷静。

3295.e: The two candidates were level pegging right up to the final count.  两位候选人一直不分上下，直到最后计票。

3296.e: Small firms just want a level playing field when they bid for contracts.  小公司投标时只求一个公平的竞争环境。

3297.e: Free school meals help level the playing field for poorer children.  免费校餐有助于让贫困孩子起点更公平。

3298.i: on the ˈlevel (AmE also on the ˌup and ˈup)
3298.e: Is this deal really on the level, or should I ask a lawyer?  这笔交易真的正当吗，还是我该问问律师？

3299.e: The film takes liberties with the facts of her early life.  这部电影对她早年经历的处理相当随意。

3300.e: He uses our phone without asking, which I think is taking liberties.  他未经同意就用我们的电话，我觉得太随便了。

3301.e: I'm not at liberty to discuss the details of the case.  案件细节我无权透露。

3302.i: take the liberty of doing sth (formal)
3302.e: I took the liberty of booking you a table for eight o'clock.  我冒昧替你订了八点的位子。

3303.e: Driving without a licence could cost him his job as well as a fine.  无证驾驶可能让他丢了工作还要罚款。

3304.cn: 艺术上的自由发挥；破格处理
3304.e: The painter used a bit of artistic licence with the shape of the hills.  画家在山形上作了些艺术化处理。

3305.e: I used some poetic licence in describing that table as an antique.  我自由发挥了一下，把那张桌子说成了古董。

3306.i: show too much respect for sb in authority
3306.e: He shows too much respect for anyone in authority and never disagrees.  他对上司一味逢迎，从不表示异议。

3307.e: The front door just needs a lick of paint and it'll look new.  前门刷层新漆就跟新的一样。

3308.cn: 舔舐伤口；失败后恢复元气
3308.e: After the election defeat he went home to lick his wounds.  竞选失利后，他回家舔舐伤口。

3309.i: get your confidence back after a defeat or disappointment
3309.cn: 失败或失望后恢复信心
3309.e: Give her a week to get her confidence back after a defeat like that.  输成那样，给她一周时间恢复信心吧。

3310.e: The company tried to keep a lid on the safety report for months.  公司试图把那份安全报告压了好几个月。

3311.i: lift, blow, etc. the ˈlid off sth (informal)
3311.e: Her book blows the lid off conditions inside the factories.  她的书揭开了这些工厂内部状况的盖子。

3312.e: These statistics give the lie to the claim that crime is falling.  这些统计数据戳穿了犯罪率下降的说法。

3313.e: He lay doggo in the barn until the search party had gone.  他躲在谷仓里一动不动，直到搜寻的人走远。

3314.e: I won't employ anyone who lies down on the job—I want workers.  我不会雇磨洋工的人，我只要肯干活的。

3315.e: The former president will lie in state for two days before the funeral.  前总统的遗体将在葬礼前供公众瞻仰两天。

3316.e: Photographers lay in wait outside the hotel all night.  摄影师们在酒店外守了一整夜。

3317.e: He's lying low at his cousin's until the fuss dies down.  风头过去之前，他躲在表哥家不露面。

3318.i: the ˌlie of the ˈland (BrE) (AmE the ˌlay of the ˈland)
3318.e: Let me talk to a few people first and get the lie of the land.  我先找几个人聊聊，摸摸情况。

3319.e: He was lying through his teeth when he said he'd never met her.  他说从没见过她，纯属睁眼说瞎话。

3320.i: lie your way into/out of sth
3320.e: He lied his way into the job and was found out within a month.  他靠撒谎得到这份工作，一个月就露馅了。

3321.i: lie your way out of sth
3321.e: You can't lie your way out of it this time, I'm afraid.  恐怕你这次靠撒谎是过不了关了。

3322.e: Staff were given extra days off in lieu of a pay rise.  员工没加薪，改为多给了几天假。

3323.cn: 是某人的命根子；至关重要
3323.e: That little bookshop was her life for nearly forty years.  那家小书店是她近四十年的命根子。

3324.e: A few old photographs really brought the story to life for the children.  几张老照片让这个故事在孩子们眼里活了起来。

3325.e: The square only comes to life after nine, when the bars open.  这个广场要到九点酒吧开门后才热闹起来。

3326.i: frighten/scare the ˈlife out of sb
3326.e: Don't creep up like that—you scared the life out of me!  别这么悄悄摸过来，吓死我了！

3327.cn: 别这么无聊；找点正事做
3327.e: You're counting my typos again? Get a life.  你又在数我的错别字？找点正事干吧。

3328.e: Since he retired he's been living the life of Riley by the sea.  退休后他在海边过着悠哉的日子。

3329.e: She lost her faith in life after death when her brother died.  弟弟去世后，她不再相信有来世。

3330.e: Getting the medicine there tonight is a matter of life and death.  今晚把药送到，是人命关天的事。

3331.i: the life and ˌsoul of the ˈparty (BrE)
3331.cn: 全场最活跃的人；气氛担当
3331.e: Give him a guitar and he's the life and soul of the party.  给他一把吉他，他就是全场的气氛担当。

3332.e: In those mines life was cheap and accidents were barely reported.  那些矿井里人命不值钱，出了事故都没人报道。

3333.cn: （某物）像有生命一般；自行发展
3333.e: The rumour took on a life of its own and reached the local paper.  这条传言像长了腿，一路传到了本地报纸上。

3334.e: Three firefighters lost their lives trying to reach the top floor.  三名消防员在试图冲上顶层时殉职。

3335.e: Fortunately there was no loss of life in the warehouse fire.  幸运的是这场仓库火灾没有人员死亡。

3336.cn: 给某人找麻烦；使日子难过
3336.e: Changing the rules midweek just makes life difficult for everyone.  周中改规则，只会让大家都难做。

3337.cn: 折磨某人；使某人痛苦不堪
3337.e: The constant noise from upstairs made her life a misery.  楼上没完没了的噪音折磨得她苦不堪言。

3338.cn: 你生命中的那个男人（或女人）
3338.e: So, is he the man in your life now, or just a good friend?  怎么，他现在是你的那位了，还是只是好朋友？

3339.i: not for the ˈlife of me, etc.
3339.cn: 无论如何也不能；怎么也想不起
3339.e: I cannot for the life of me remember where I parked the car.  我怎么也想不起来车停在哪儿了。

3340.e: He couldn't for the life of him understand why she was so annoyed.  他无论如何也不明白她为什么这么生气。

3341.e: Lend him the van again? Not on your life.  再把货车借给他？没门儿。

3342.e: Two years driving a taxi at night certainly made him see life.  开了两年夜班出租，他可真见了世面。

3343.e: The train was cancelled and I missed the wedding—such is life.  火车取消了，婚礼也错过了，这就是生活。

3344.cn: 杀害某人；夺去某人性命
3344.e: No argument over money can justify taking another person's life.  再大的金钱纠纷也不能成为杀人的理由。

3345.i: take your ˌlife in your ˈhands
3345.e: You take your life in your hands crossing that road at rush hour.  高峰期过那条马路简直是玩命。

3346.e: The poet took his own life at the age of thirty-two.  这位诗人三十二岁时自杀身亡。

3347.i: ˌthat's ˈlife (also ˌc'est la ˈvie from French)
3347.e: I worked all weekend and someone else got the credit—that's life.  我干了整个周末，功劳算别人的，生活就是这样。

3348.i: there's ˌlife in the old dog ˈyet (humorous)
3348.e: Grandad won the fun run again—there's life in the old dog yet.  爷爷又赢了趣味长跑，真是老当益壮。

3349.e: Sun, a cold drink and no emails—this is the life!  阳光、冷饮、没有邮件，这才叫生活！

3350.e: The old sailor in the painting is drawn to the life.  画里那位老水手画得活灵活现。

3351.cn: 这日子真难熬；人生太苦了
3351.e: Two jobs, three kids and a leaking roof—what a life!  两份工作、三个孩子、屋顶还漏水，这日子真够呛！

3352.cn: 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧
3352.e: The shop's barely surviving, but where there's life there's hope.  店勉强撑着，可留得青山在，不怕没柴烧。

3353.i: the chance, etc. of a ˈlifetime
3353.e: Studying in Kyoto for a year was the chance of a lifetime.  去京都读一年书是千载难逢的机会。

3354.e: He never lifts a finger to help with the washing-up.  洗碗的事他从来不搭把手。

3355.e: We missed the last bus and had to thumb a lift into town.  我们错过末班车，只好搭便车进城。

3356.e: Move over a bit—you're in my light and I can't read.  挪一挪，你挡着光，我没法看书。

3357.e: The report is a bit light on hard evidence, to be honest.  说实话，这份报告缺乏有力证据。

3358.cn: 很快睡着；突然失去知觉
3358.e: He hit the pillow and went out like a light.  他头一沾枕头就睡着了。

3359.e: The audit brought to light years of missing payments.  这次审计揭出了多年来的欠款问题。

3360.e: The letters shed new light on why she left the country.  这些信件让人重新理解她为何离开这个国家。

3361.e: New details about the accident came to light this morning.  今早又有关于这起事故的新细节曝光。

3362.i: in a ˌgood, ˌbad, ˌfavourable, etc. ˈlight
3362.e: The interview showed the company in a very bad light.  这次采访把公司衬得很不堪。

3363.i: in the ˈlight of sth (BrE) (AmE in ˈlight of sth)
3363.e: In the light of these new figures, we should redo the budget.  鉴于这些新数字，我们该重做预算。

3364.e: The little suitcase was as light as a feather when empty.  这只小行李箱空着时轻得像羽毛。

3365.i: (see the) ˌlight at the end of the ˈtunnel
3365.cn: （看到）苦尽甘来的希望；曙光在望
3365.e: After three years of building work we can finally see light at the end of the tunnel.  施工三年，我们总算看到曙光了。

3366.i: in the future, especially after a long period of difficulty
3366.cn: 长期艰难后的希望；曙光在望
3366.e: There's hope in the future, especially after a long period of difficulty like this.  熬过这么长一段苦日子，前面总算有盼头了。

3367.e: Then the light dawned—she'd been reading the wrong timetable.  这时她恍然大悟，原来看错了时刻表。

3368.e: The novel he wrote at twenty never saw the light of day.  他二十岁写的那部小说从未面世。

3369.e: That scruffy little dog is the light of my father's life.  那只脏兮兮的小狗是我父亲的心肝宝贝。

3370.e: She handled the complaint with a light touch and nobody felt blamed.  她处理投诉举重若轻，谁都没觉得被指责。

3371.e: He made light of the injury, but he could hardly walk.  他对伤势轻描淡写，其实几乎走不了路。

3372.cn: 轻而易举地完成；轻松取胜
3372.e: The two of them made light work of clearing the whole garden.  他们俩三下五除二就把整个花园清理干净了。

3373.cn: 轻松击败；毫不费力地做成
3373.e: They made light work of their match against Lazio and took the cup.  他们轻松击败拉齐奥队，捧得奖杯。

3374.e: After months of arguing, he finally saw the light and sold the car.  争了几个月，他终于想通，把车卖了。

3375.e: Someone set light to a pile of rubbish behind the shops.  有人点着了店铺后面的一堆垃圾。

3376.e: She handed in the last exam paper with a light heart.  交上最后一份考卷时，她心情轻松。

3377.e: A warning? He got off lightly, if you ask me.  就一个警告？要我说他算是轻判了。

3378.cn: 以闪电般的速度；飞快地
3378.e: News of the closure spread through the office at lightning speed.  关门的消息在办公室里飞快传开。

3379.i: ˌlightning never strikes (in the same place) ˈtwice
3379.cn: 同样的倒霉事不会重演
3379.e: We were burgled last year, but lightning never strikes twice.  去年我们家被偷了，不过倒霉事不会连着来。

3380.cn: 倒霉事不会在同一处（或同一人身上）重演
3380.e: Relax—lightning never strikes in the same place twice.  放宽心吧，这种倒霉事不会再来一次。

3381.i: the lights are ˈon but nobody's ˈhome
3381.e: You can talk to him all day, but the lights are on and nobody's home.  你跟他说一天也没用，他压根没往心里去。

3382.e: Bring towels, sunscreen and the like—we'll be there all day.  带上毛巾、防晒霜之类的，我们要待一整天。

3383.e: I never said anything like that about her work.  我从没说过她工作方面这类话。

3384.e: How would you like it if someone read your messages?  要是有人翻你的短信，你会怎么想？

3385.i: I like your ˈnerve, ˈcheek, etc. • I like ˈthat!
3385.cn: 亏你说得出口（或做得出来）
3385.e: You want me to pay for the taxi too? I like that!  还要我付出租车钱？亏你说得出口！

3386.cn: 如果你愿意；你要是想的话
3386.e: We can eat at home instead, if you like.  你要是愿意，我们可以改在家里吃。

3387.i: (as) like as ˈnot • like eˈnough • most/very ˈlike
3387.e: As like as not he's stuck in traffic again on the ring road.  他多半又堵在环路上了。

3388.e: Most like he forgot the whole thing the moment you told him.  他八成你一说完就忘了。

3389.e: She stood up, walked out and quit, just like that.  她站起来，走出去，就那么辞职了。

3390.e: After the scandal he stayed out of the limelight for years.  丑闻之后，他多年不露面。

3391.e: Turning up two hours late is the absolute limit.  迟到两个小时，真是让人忍无可忍。

3392.e: With her talent and that scholarship, the sky's the limit.  凭她的天赋加上奖学金，前途不可限量。

3393.cn: 在一定程度上；有限度地
3393.e: You can decorate the room however you want, within limits.  房间随你怎么布置，但要有个限度。

3394.i: all along/down the ˈline • right down the ˈline
3394.e: The project was badly managed all down the line.  这个项目从头到尾管理得一塌糊涂。

3395.e: They supported her right down the line during the dispute.  纠纷期间他们自始至终支持她。

3396.e: The new rules bring our pay scales into line with the industry.  新规定使我们的薪级与行业水平接轨。

3397.e: She's in line for promotion if the department expands next year.  如果明年部门扩编，她有望升职。

3398.cn: 在执行公务时；在履行职责时
3398.e: The officer was injured in the line of duty last Saturday.  这名警官上周六在执勤中受伤。

3399.e: His account of the meeting is completely out of line with mine.  他对会议的说法跟我的完全不一致。

3400.e: The changes being made are in line with the new policy.  正在进行的变革符合新政策的要求。

3401.i: (choose, follow, take, etc.) the line of least reˈsistance
3401.cn: 走阻力最小的路；图省事
3401.e: He took the line of least resistance and agreed to everything.  他图省事，什么都答应了。

3402.e: Following the line of least resistance won't fix this problem.  一味图省事解决不了这个问题。

3403.e: The contractor was lining his own pockets with the repair money.  承包商把修缮款装进了自己腰包。

3404.e: His whole reputation is on the line with this one trial.  这一场官司关系到他的全部声誉。

3405.cn: 在某个时刻；在某个环节
3405.e: Somewhere along the line the two files got mixed up.  不知在哪个环节，这两份档案弄混了。

3406.cn: 在两难间小心行事；如履薄冰
3406.e: Comedians walk a fine line between funny and offensive.  喜剧演员在好笑和冒犯之间走钢丝。

3407.e: The bottom line is we can't afford another delay.  关键在于，我们再也拖不起了。

3408.e: He said something along the lines of never wanting to see me again.  他说了句大概是再也不想见我之类的话。

3409.e: We want a garden along the lines of the one in that magazine.  我们想要个跟杂志上那个差不多的花园。

3410.e: English serves as a lingua franca among the engineers on this site.  英语是工地上这些工程师的通用语。

3411.cn: 链条中的一环；过程中的一个环节
3411.e: Every delivery driver is an important link in the chain.  每个送货司机都是链条上重要的一环。

3412.cn: 龙潭虎穴；难以应付的场合
3412.e: Walking into that board meeting felt like entering the lion's den.  走进那场董事会，感觉像进了龙潭虎穴。

3413.e: Her brother took the lion's share of the inheritance.  遗产中最大的一份被她哥哥拿走了。

3414.e: The kids were licking their lips as the cake came out of the oven.  蛋糕一出炉，孩子们就馋得直咂嘴。

3415.e: Tell me the gossip—my lips are sealed, I promise.  跟我说说八卦吧，我保证守口如瓶。

3416.e: That singer's name was on everyone's lips after the final.  决赛之后，那位歌手的名字人人都在谈。

3417.e: The doctors say he's off the danger list and can have visitors.  医生说他脱离危险了，可以探视。

3418.cn: 心不在焉地听；半听不听
3418.e: He listened with half an ear while scrolling through his phone.  他一边刷手机，一边心不在焉地听着。

3419.cn: 有人私下告诉我；小道消息说
3419.e: A little bird told me you're moving to Shanghai next month.  有人偷偷告诉我，你下个月要搬去上海。

3420.e: Little by little she taught herself to play the piano.  她一点一点自学会了弹钢琴。

3421.e: He made little of the injury so his mother wouldn't worry.  他把伤说得轻描淡写，免得母亲担心。

3422.i: more than a little exˈcited, ˈshocked, etc.
3422.e: She was more than a little shocked to find the door wide open.  发现门大敞着，她着实吓了一跳。

3423.cn: 任意摆布某人；玩弄于股掌之间
3423.e: That child can twist his grandmother round his little finger.  那孩子把奶奶哄得团团转。

3424.cn: 全身心投入；痴迷于某事
3424.e: He lives and breathes football, even on his wedding day.  他痴迷足球，连结婚那天也不例外。

3425.cn: 活到老学到老；吃一堑长一智
3425.e: I'll never buy a used phone online again—live and learn.  我再也不网购二手手机了，吃一堑长一智。

3426.cn: 自己活也让别人活；彼此宽容
3426.e: My neighbours and I live and let live, and we get along fine.  我和邻居互不干涉，相处得挺好。

3427.e: They lived beyond their means for years and ended up in debt.  他们多年入不敷出，最后欠了一身债。

3428.cn: 靠机智谋生；随机应变过活
3428.e: He left home at sixteen and lived on his wits in the city.  他十六岁离家，在城里靠机灵劲儿讨生活。

3429.cn: 勉强糊口；挣一天吃一天
3429.e: They lived hand to mouth all winter until the work picked up.  整个冬天他们勉强糊口，直到活儿多起来。

3430.e: I live in hope that one day he'll return my ladder.  我一直盼着他哪天把梯子还我。

3431.e: The Johnsons live in hope that one day their son will come home.  约翰逊一家一直盼着儿子有一天能回家。

3432.e: Her grandmother still says the two of them are living in sin.  她奶奶至今还说他们俩是未婚同居。

3433.e: They lived it up in Barcelona for a week on his bonus.  他们拿着奖金在巴塞罗那潇洒了一周。

3434.i: keep sth important about yourself a secret from others
3434.e: He kept something important about himself a secret from everyone for years.  多年来他向所有人隐瞒着自己的重要秘密。

3435.cn: 过帝王般的生活；生活阔绰
3435.e: On that salary you could live like a king in this town.  拿那份薪水，在这座小城你能过得像个国王。

3436.i: live off/on the ˌfat of the ˈland (informal)
3436.e: They sold the company and have lived off the fat of the land since.  他们卖了公司，从此过上了锦衣玉食的日子。

3437.e: For a whole summer they lived off the land in the hills.  整整一个夏天，他们在山里靠山吃山。

3438.e: We lost the vote, but we live to fight another day.  这次表决输了，但我们还有下回。

3439.i: live to tell the ˈtale (informal, often humorous)
3439.e: He fell off the roof and somehow lived to tell the tale.  他从屋顶摔下来，居然还活着讲这段经历。

3440.e: It'll be a difficult trip, but I expect you'll live to tell the tale.  这趟不好走，不过我相信你能挺过来。

3441.e: The restaurant certainly lived up to its reputation for slow service.  这家餐厅上菜慢的名声果然名不虚传。

3442.e: The new booking system goes live at midnight on Sunday.  新的预订系统将于周日午夜上线。

3443.cn: 生龙活虎的人；活跃分子
3443.e: Our new receptionist is a real live wire and everyone loves her.  新来的前台特别有活力，人人都喜欢她。

3444.e: You've never eaten hotpot in Chengdu? You haven't lived!  你没在成都吃过火锅？那你算白活了！

3445.e: Look lively, you two—the bus for town leaves in four minutes.  你俩快点，进城的车四分钟后就开。

3446.e: My uncle is living proof that you can start again at sixty.  我叔叔就是六十岁还能重新开始的活证据。

3447.e: It was the worst flood in living memory in this valley.  这是本地人记忆中这条山谷最严重的一次洪水。

3448.i: a living ˈlegend (also a ˌlegend in your own ˈlifetime)
3448.e: Among local fishermen the old skipper is a living legend.  在本地渔民中，那位老船长是个活着的传奇。

3449.cn: （引出意外之事）你瞧，真想不到
3449.e: I opened the cupboard and, lo and behold, there was the missing cat.  我打开橱柜，你瞧，走失的猫就在里面。

3450.e: He carried a heavy load of bricks across the yard without stopping.  他扛着一大摞砖头一口气穿过院子。

3451.e: Get a load of this—they want us to work on Christmas Day.  听听这个，他们想让我们圣诞节上班。

3452.i: a load of (old) ˈrubbish, ˈnonsense, etc.
3452.e: That article about the diet is a load of old rubbish.  那篇讲减肥的文章纯属一派胡言。

3453.cn: 严阵以待；准备大干一场
3453.e: She walked into the negotiation loaded for bear.  她带着一身火气走进谈判现场。

3454.e: The two directors locked horns over the budget again.  两位主管又为预算问题争执起来。

3455.e: They sold the farm lock, stock and barrel and moved abroad.  他们把农场连同一切全卖了，搬去了国外。

3456.e: The old letters are kept under lock and key in the archive.  那些旧信件锁在档案室里严加保管。

3457.e: Teachers on the trip act in loco parentis for the whole week.  带队老师整整一周都代行父母职责。

3458.e: The two families have been at loggerheads over that fence for years.  两家为那道篱笆争执了好多年。

3459.e: The council is at loggerheads with residents over the new car park.  市政会与居民在新停车场问题上争执不下。

3460.e: He's always been a lone wolf and prefers to work nights alone.  他一向独来独往，喜欢一个人上夜班。

3461.e: You can borrow the car as long as you fill the tank.  只要你把油加满，车就借你。

3462.i: be in sth for the long ˈhaul
3462.cn: 打持久战；愿意坚持到底
3462.e: We're in this campaign for the long haul, not just one winter.  这场运动我们打算长期坚持，不止一个冬天。

3463.e: I haven't seen her for so long that I barely recognized her.  太久没见她了，我差点没认出来。

3464.e: Those two go back a long way—they were at school together.  他们俩交情很久了，是同学。

3575.e: Whoever priced this flat at two million is completely out to lunch.  把这套公寓标价两百万的人脑子进水了。

3576.e: She quit two days before the show and left the whole cast in the lurch.  她在演出前两天辞演，把全组人晾在那里。

3577.e: They cut his hours without warning, and he won't take it lying down.  他们不打招呼就减他工时，他可不会忍气吞声。

3578.e: My nephew is mad keen on dinosaurs and can name about forty.  我侄子对恐龙着迷得很，能说出四十来种。

3579.e: The old man who feeds the crows is as mad as a hatter, but harmless.  那个喂乌鸦的老头疯疯癫癫，不过没有恶意。

3580.e: She danced through the office in slippers, mad as a March hare.  她穿着拖鞋在办公室里跳舞，简直疯疯癫癫。

3581.cn: 对某事非常满意；乐坏了
3581.e: He was made up about getting into his first-choice university.  考上第一志愿的大学，他乐坏了。

3582.e: With a paid-off house and a pension like that, he's got it made.  房贷还清，还有那样的退休金，他这辈子不愁了。

3583.e: Those two argue about films all night—they're made for each other.  那两个人整晚争论电影，真是天生一对。

3584.cn: 某人的真本事；某人有几分能耐
3584.e: The final round will show us what this young boxer is made of.  最后一轮就能看出这个年轻拳手到底有几分能耐。

3585.i: Go out and show them what you're made of
3585.cn: 出去让他们见识你的本事
3585.e: Go out and show them what you're made of—you've trained all year for this.  出去让他们见识见识你的本事，你练了一整年就为这个。

3586.cn: 有过人的本领；有点石成金的本事
3586.e: She has the magic touch with nervous dogs; they calm down instantly.  她对付胆小的狗有一手，狗一见她就安静了。

3587.e: At thirty her aunts already called her an old maid, which infuriated her.  她三十岁时姑姑们就叫她老姑娘，把她气坏了。

3588.e: In the main, the students were polite, though a few arrived late.  总体来说学生都很有礼貌，只有几个迟到。

3589.i: make as if to do sth (written)
3589.e: He made as if to leave, then sat back down and ordered another beer.  他做出要走的样子，又坐下再要了一杯啤酒。

3590.e: When the guard turned his back, the two men made a break for it.  警卫一转身，那两人就撒腿跑了。

3591.i: make ˈdo (with sth) • make sth ˈdo
3591.e: There's no rice left, so we'll make do with noodles tonight.  米没了，今晚就将就吃面吧。

3592.e: They're determined to make a go of the bakery despite the rent.  尽管房租很高，他们还是决心把面包店做起来。

3593.cn: 发家致富；白手起家获得成功
3593.e: He left the village with nothing and made good in the shipping trade.  他身无分文离开村子，靠海运生意发了家。

3594.e: The builder promised to make good the damage to our garden wall.  建筑商答应把我们花园墙的损坏修好。

3595.i: mechanic explained that they would have to
3595.cn: 修理工说必须先修复损坏处
