3595.e: The mechanic explained that they would have to make good the dents first.  修理工解释说，他们得先把凹痕修复好。

3596.e: Two of the three startups failed, but hers actually made it.  三家创业公司倒了两家，她那家真做成了。

3597.e: He kept bragging that he'd made it with the singer, which nobody believed.  他一直吹嘘和那位歌手上过床，没人信。

3598.e: The sun's finally out—let's make the most of it and eat outside.  太阳总算出来了，咱们抓紧到外面吃饭。

3599.i: make the ˈmost of yourself, himself, etc.
3599.e: A decent haircut helps you make the most of yourself at interviews.  剪个像样的头发，面试时能更好地展现自己。

3600.e: The papers made much of his humble background during the campaign.  竞选期间报纸大肆渲染他出身寒微。

3601.e: I read the contract twice and could make nothing of clause nine.  合同我读了两遍，第九条完全看不懂。

3602.i: The more he thought about it, the less he under-
3602.e: The more he thought about it, the less he understood her sudden silence.  他越琢磨，越不明白她为何突然沉默。

3603.e: This launch will make or break the company, so nobody's sleeping much.  这次发布决定公司成败，大家都睡不好。

3604.e: His mother worked two jobs so he could make something of himself.  他母亲打两份工，就为了让他有出息。

3605.e: Half the people at that party were politicians on the make.  那场聚会上一半人是钻营名利的政客。

3606.cn: 是某人（或某事）成功的关键
3606.e: Two years in the countryside were the making of that spoiled boy.  在乡下的两年成就了那个被宠坏的男孩。

3607.e: Watching her rehearse, you can see a fine violinist in the making.  看她排练就知道，一位出色的小提琴家正在成长。

3608.e: The debt crisis at the club was entirely of their own making.  俱乐部的债务危机完全是他们自己造成的。

3609.e: That kid has the makings of a first-class goalkeeper if he keeps training.  那孩子要是坚持练，会成为一流门将。

3610.e: The prosecution argued he acted with malice aforethought, not in panic.  控方主张他是蓄意行凶，而非惊慌失措。

3611.cn: 是（做某事）最合适的人选
3611.e: If you need someone to fix that old boiler, Tom's your man.  要修那台老锅炉，找汤姆准没错。

3612.i: be ˈman enough (to do sth/for sth)
3612.e: Be man enough to apologize to her in person, not by text.  拿出点担当，当面跟她道歉，别发短信。

3613.i: be no good/use to ˈman or ˈbeast (informal)
3613.e: This rusted old lawnmower is no use to man or beast now.  这台生锈的旧割草机现在一点用都没有了。

3614.e: Since going freelance she's finally her own woman again.  自从做了自由职业，她终于又能自己做主了。

3615.i: every man has his ˈprice • everyone has
3615.cn: 人皆有价；人人都可能被收买
3615.e: The lawyer smiled and said every man has his price, including judges.  律师笑着说人皆有价，法官也不例外。

3616.cn: 人皆有价；重赏之下必有勇夫
3616.e: Offer enough and everyone has their price, or so the cynics claim.  出价够高，人人都有价，愤世嫉俗者如是说。

3617.e: When the funding was cut, it was every man for himself in that department.  经费一砍，那个部门就人人自顾了。

3618.i: make a ˈman of/out of sb
3618.cn: 使某人成为男子汉；使人长大成人
3618.e: His father thought two winters at sea would make a man of him.  他父亲认为在海上过两个冬天能让他成为男子汉。

3619.cn: 交际场上的活跃人物；社交名流
3619.e: In his thirties he was a man about town who knew every club owner.  三十多岁时他是个社交场上的活跃人物，认识每家夜店老板。

3620.e: He worked at that mill man and boy for forty-two years.  他从小到大在那家工厂干了四十二年。

3621.i: the ˌman (and/or ˌwoman) in the ˈstreet
3621.e: The man in the street cares about rent, not about party slogans.  老百姓关心的是房租，不是政党口号。

3622.e: Would the man on the Clapham omnibus think this contract fair?  普通百姓会觉得这份合同公平吗？

3623.i: a ˌman of ˈGod/the ˈcloth (old-fashioned, formal)
3623.e: As a man of the cloth, he was expected to visit the sick weekly.  身为神职人员，他每周都要去探望病人。

3624.i: the ˌman of the ˈmatch (BrE, sport)
3624.e: The keeper saved two penalties and was named man of the match.  门将扑出两个点球，当选全场最佳。

3625.cn: 体察民情的人；平民出身的领袖
3625.e: He rides the bus to work and calls himself a man of the people.  他坐公交上班，自称是体察民情的人。

3626.e: The new chairman turned out to be a man of straw with no real authority.  新任主席原来是个没有实权的软弱角色。

3627.cn: （男人之间）坦诚地；开诚布公地
3627.e: Let's talk man to man about why you've been avoiding the office.  咱们男人之间坦白讲，你为什么老躲着办公室。

3628.e: After the rescue, everyone agreed the dog was truly man's best friend.  救援之后，大家都说狗真是人类最好的朋友。

3629.e: He's a man's man—football, beer and very little small talk.  他是那种典型的男人堆里的男人：足球、啤酒，很少闲聊。

3630.i: one man's ˌmeat is another man's ˈpoison (saying)
3630.cn: 各人口味不同；甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜
3630.e: He loves durian and I can't stand it—one man's meat is another man's poison.  他爱吃榴莲我却受不了，真是各人口味不同。

3631.e: The committee voted, to a man, against selling the old library.  委员会一致投票反对出售那座旧图书馆。

3632.i: you can't keep a good man ˈdown (saying)
3632.e: He lost everything in the fire and reopened a year later—you can't keep a good man down.  一场火烧光了他的一切，一年后他又开张了，有能耐的人压不垮。

3633.e: Half my salary goes on rent for a flat the size of a shoebox.  我半份工资都交了房租，房子却小得像鞋盒。

3634.i: There are a great many places in the world I'd
3634.cn: 世界上有许多地方我想去
3634.e: There are a great many places in the world I'd like to visit before forty.  世界上有很多地方我想在四十岁前去看看。

3635.e: Their farmhouse is completely off the map—no signal, no neighbours.  他们的农舍偏僻得很，没信号，也没邻居。

3636.e: One viral video put the tiny noodle shop on the map overnight.  一条爆红视频让这家小面馆一夜成名。

3637.e: Selling the car to buy a boat? Have you lost your marbles?  卖车买船？你是不是疯了？

3638.e: We're moving house in March, right after the lease runs out.  我们三月搬家，正好租约到期。

3639.i: march to (the beat of) a different
3639.e: She's always marched to a different beat, wearing red boots to funerals.  她从来特立独行，参加葬礼都穿红靴子。

3640.i: ˈdrummer/drum (also march to a different ˈtune less frequent)
3640.cn: 与众不同；另有一套想法
3640.e: He marches to a different drummer and refuses every trend going.  他自有一套，任何潮流都不跟。

3641.e: The band kept marching down the street despite the pouring rain.  尽管大雨倾盆，乐队仍沿街行进。

3642.e: After three warnings about lateness, he finally got his marching orders.  迟到被警告三次后，他终于被辞退了。

3643.i: give sb their ˈmarching orders (BrE, informal)
3643.cn: 解雇某人；命令某人走人
3643.e: She gave her business partner his marching orders after the audit.  审计之后，她让合伙人卷铺盖走人。

3644.cn: 看似重大实则无用的发现；混乱局面
3644.e: The investigation turned up a mare's nest of rumours and no facts.  调查挖出一堆传言，全无实据，白忙一场。

3645.e: Your guess of two thousand yuan was pretty close to the mark.  你猜两千块，已经八九不离十了。

3646.cn: 反应快（或慢）；行动敏捷（或迟缓）
3646.e: You have to be quick off the mark to get concert tickets these days.  现在抢演唱会门票，手慢就没了。

3647.e: The striker finally got off the mark in his eighth game for the club.  这名前锋加盟后第八场比赛终于开了张。

3648.e: She made her mark as a designer before she turned twenty-five.  她二十五岁前就在设计界崭露头角。

3649.e: Mark my words, that bridge will need repairs within five years.  记住我的话，那座桥不出五年就得修。

3650.e: He's just marking time in that job until his visa comes through.  他在那份工作上原地踏步，就等签证下来。

3651.e: He paid for dinner, mark you, which he's never done before.  他请了客，注意啊，这可是头一回。

3652.e: The kitchen wasn't up to the mark, so the inspector closed the café.  厨房不达标，检查员把咖啡馆关了。

3653.cn: 被盯上的人；成为攻击目标的人
3653.e: After testifying against the gang, he was a marked man in that city.  指证那伙人之后，他在那座城市就成了被盯上的人。

3654.e: We're in the market for a used van big enough for the band.  我们想买辆二手面包车，得装得下乐队的家伙。

3655.e: Their house has been on the market since last spring with no offers.  他们的房子从去年春天挂到现在，无人出价。

3656.e: He started playing the market with his student loan, which ended badly.  他拿助学贷款去炒股，结果很惨。

3657.i: on your ˌmarks, get ˌset, ˈgo!
3657.e: The teacher shouted 'on your marks, get set, go!' and the children sprinted off.  老师喊“各就位，预备，跑！”，孩子们冲了出去。

3658.cn: 使某人冷彻骨髓；使不寒而栗
3658.e: The scream from the empty stairwell chilled us to the marrow.  空楼梯间传来的尖叫让我们不寒而栗。

3659.i: marry in ˈhaste (, repent at ˈleisure) (saying)
3659.e: They married after six weeks—marry in haste, repent at leisure, as they say.  他们认识六周就结婚，正应了那句：结婚太急，后悔莫及。

3660.e: Her cousin married money and hasn't worked a day since.  她表姐嫁了个有钱人，从此一天班都没上过。

3661.e: By June the hillside is a mass of wild orange poppies.  到六月，山坡上开满了野生的橙色罂粟花。

3662.e: Running the shop alone is hard, but at least I'm my own master.  一个人开店很辛苦，但至少我自己说了算。

3663.i: take sb/sth to the ˈmat (AmE, informal)
3663.cn: 与…激烈争辩；与…较量到底
3663.e: The union is ready to take management to the mat over overtime pay.  工会准备为加班费和资方斗到底。

3664.i: lay, put, roll, etc. out the welcome ˈmat
3664.e: The village rolled out the welcome mat for the returning soldiers.  村里张灯结彩，热情迎接归来的士兵。

3665.e: Our little team was no match for the champions last Saturday.  上周六我们这支小队根本不是冠军队的对手。

3666.i: not be as good, etc. as sb/sth; not be able to
3666.e: Cheap copies are not as good as the original and can't be repaired.  廉价仿品不如原版，还没法修。

3667.i: match for the Japanese when it comes to making
3667.cn: 在制造方面比不上（日本人）
3667.e: We're no match for the Japanese when it comes to making precision lenses.  论精密镜头制造，我们比不过日本人。

3668.e: The chess champion finally met his match in a twelve-year-old girl.  这位象棋冠军最终败给了一个十二岁的女孩。

3669.e: The hotel changes the towels daily as a matter of course.  酒店照例每天更换毛巾。

3670.e: As a matter of fact, today happens to be my fortieth birthday.  事实上，今天正好是我四十岁生日。

3671.i: (do sth) as a matter of ˈform
3671.e: They asked for my ID as a matter of form, then waved me through.  他们例行公事查了我的证件，就放我过去了。

3672.e: Reading Chinese is fine; speaking it fluently is another matter entirely.  读中文没问题，但流利地说完全是另一回事。

3673.e: You look pale—what's the matter with you this morning?  你脸色发白，今天早上怎么了？

3674.cn: 见仁见智；看法因人而异
3674.e: Whether the film is a masterpiece is very much a matter of opinion.  这部电影算不算杰作，实在见仁见智。

3675.e: The truth of the matter is that nobody checked the figures.  事实真相是，根本没人核对过数字。

3676.e: I've never been to Paris, or to France for that matter.  我没去过巴黎，其实整个法国都没去过。

3677.i: a matter of ˈdays, ˈmiles, ˈpounds, etc.
3677.cn: 只有几天（或几英里、几镑等）
3677.e: The nearest hospital is a matter of miles away, luckily for us.  最近的医院不过几英里，我们算走运。

3678.i: a particular number of days, miles, etc., espe-
3678.e: It took a particular number of days, miles and arguments to get there.  到那儿花了整整几天、几百英里，还吵了不少架。

3679.i: no matter who, what, where, when, etc.
3679.cn: 无论谁（或什么、何处、何时）
3679.e: No matter what she says, don't lend him money again.  不管她怎么说，都别再借钱给他。

3680.i: take matters into your own ˈhands
3680.cn: 自己动手解决；自行处理
3680.e: The council ignored the potholes, so residents took matters into their own hands.  市政不管坑洼路面，居民只好自己动手修。

3681.cn: 成熟的；经过深思熟虑的
3681.e: After mature consideration, she turned down the offer from the bank.  经过深思熟虑，她拒绝了那家银行的邀约。

3682.e: He pushed the old engine to the max and it finally gave out.  他把那台老发动机催到极限，它终于报废了。

3683.i: be that as it ˈmay • that's
3683.e: Be that as it may, we still have to hand the report in tomorrow.  尽管如此，我们明天还是得交报告。

3684.e: This isn't a copy—the violin is the real McCoy, made in 1890.  这不是仿品，这把小提琴货真价实，1890年制。

3685.e: Mea culpa—I booked the tickets for the wrong weekend entirely.  是我的错，我把票订到了另一个周末。

3686.i: make a ˈmeal of/out of sth (informal)
3686.cn: 小题大做；把事情弄得过于复杂
3686.e: It's one email; don't make a meal of it and rewrite it six times.  就一封邮件，别小题大做改上六遍。

3687.cn: 饭票；供养自己的人或物
3687.e: He treated his older girlfriend as little more than a meal ticket.  他把年长的女友几乎只当成一张长期饭票。

3688.cn: 是很了不起的…；相当出色的…
3688.e: She's no mean cook—that dumpling stall of hers has queues every night.  她厨艺可不含糊，那个饺子摊每晚都排队。

3689.cn: 对某人不重要；某人毫不在意
3689.e: Those old awards mean nothing to him now that his kids are grown.  孩子都大了，那些旧奖项对他已毫无意义。

3690.e: Between strict dieting and eating whatever, she found the golden mean.  在严格节食和放开吃之间，她找到了中庸之道。

3691.e: When the landlord changed the locks, we knew he meant business.  房东把锁换了，我们就知道他是来真的。

3692.i: be serious about what you plan to do; be deter-
3692.e: You have to be serious about what you plan to do, or nobody will back you.  你得认真对待自己的计划，否则没人支持你。

3693.e: Do you mean to say you walked home twelve miles in the rain?  你是说你冒雨走了十二英里回家？

3694.e: He glanced at the clock twice, and I got his meaning and left.  他看了两次钟，我明白了他的意思就走了。

3695.i: not know the meaning of the ˈword
3695.cn: 根本不懂…；完全不知何为…
3695.e: My brother works weekends—he doesn't know the meaning of the word rest.  我哥连周末都干活，他根本不懂什么叫休息。

3696.e: By all means borrow the car, just fill the tank before you return it.  车尽管借去开，还的时候把油加满就行。

3697.i: by ˈno (manner of) means • not by ˈany
3697.e: The deal is by no means settled, so don't celebrate yet.  这笔交易远未敲定，先别庆祝。

3698.e: That new ramen place is meant to be the best in the city.  那家新开的拉面店据说是全城最好的。

3699.e: The doctor sees you at four; in the meantime, grab a coffee downstairs.  医生四点见你，这期间你先去楼下喝杯咖啡。

3700.i: the whole of sth or less of sth than you expect
3700.e: You may get the whole of something or less of something than you expect.  你可能拿到足量，也可能比预期的少。

3701.i: get/have/take the ˈmeasure of sb • get/
3701.cn: 摸清某人的底细；掂出某人的分量
3701.e: After two meetings she had the measure of her new boss completely.  开了两次会，她就把新上司摸透了。

3702.cn: 看透某人；估量某人的能力
3702.e: The old coach took the boy's measure in a single training session.  老教练一堂训练课就看出了这男孩的斤两。

3703.e: The project's success was in large measure due to volunteers.  项目的成功在很大程度上要归功于志愿者。

3704.e: Both parents are in equal measure responsible for the mess.  这烂摊子父母双方要负同等责任。

3705.e: His suits are made to measure by a tailor in the old town.  他的西装是老城区一位裁缝量身定做的。

3706.cn: 是某人的一大乐事；正合某人胃口
3706.e: Arguing about politics at dinner is meat and drink to my uncle.  饭桌上争论政治，正是我舅舅的一大乐事。

3707.e: Let's skip the slides and get to the meat-and-potatoes issues.  别放幻灯片了，直接谈最实质的问题。

3708.i: give sb a taste/dose of their own ˈmedicine
3708.cn: 以其人之道还治其人之身
3708.e: She ignored his calls for a week, giving him a dose of his own medicine.  她一周不接他电话，让他也尝尝被冷落的滋味。

3709.i: take your ˈmedicine (like a ˈman) (usually humorous)
3709.e: You broke the window, so take your medicine and tell your dad.  窗户是你打破的，认了吧，去告诉你爸。

3710.e: A sea of broken glass met our eyes when we opened the door.  门一开，满地碎玻璃映入眼帘。

3711.i: meet sb's ˈeyes (also meet sb's ˈgaze, ˈlook, etc.)
3711.cn: 与某人目光相遇；直视某人
3711.e: He couldn't meet her eyes when she asked where the money went.  她问钱去哪儿了，他不敢与她对视。

3712.e: I wanted eight thousand, he offered six, so we met halfway.  我要八千，他出六千，最后各让一步。

3713.e: If I eat one more of these chillies, I'll meet my Maker tonight.  再吃一个这种辣椒，我今晚就得去见上帝。

3714.e: The unbeaten team met their Waterloo against a squad of amateurs.  这支不败之师栽在了一群业余选手手里。

3715.e: The braised pork was so tender it melted in your mouth.  那道红烧肉嫩得入口即化。

3716.cn: 处于变化之中；尚未定型
3716.e: The team's plans for next season are still in the melting pot.  球队下赛季的计划仍在变动之中。

3717.e: If memory serves, we last met at that awful conference in Leeds.  如果我没记错，我们上次见面是在利兹那场糟糕的会议上。

3718.i: go down/take sb down ˌmemory ˈlane •
3718.e: Those old photographs took us all down memory lane for an hour.  那些老照片让我们追忆往事，聊了一个钟头。

3719.i: take a trip down ˌmemory ˈlane
3719.e: Visiting my old school was a real trip down memory lane.  重回母校，真是一次难忘的回忆之旅。

3720.i: be getting better after an illness or injury
3720.e: She's getting better after an illness that kept her in bed for weeks.  她大病一场卧床数周，如今正在康复。

3721.i: be on the ˈmend (informal, especially BrE)
3721.e: Jane was very ill, but she's on the mend and eating properly again.  简曾病得很重，现在正在康复，也能好好吃饭了。

3722.e: Don't mention it—driving you to the airport was no trouble at all.  别客气，送你去机场根本不费事。

3723.i: mention sb/sth in the same ˈbreath
3723.e: You can't mention that pub band and a symphony orchestra in the same breath.  你不能把那个酒吧乐队和交响乐团相提并论。

3724.e: The flat is tiny and damp, not to mention the noise from the road.  这公寓又小又潮，更别提路上的噪音了。

3725.e: Small farmers here are at the mercy of the weather every single year.  这里的小农年年都得看老天爷脸色。

3726.e: With the only key in his pocket, he had us at his mercy.  唯一的钥匙在他兜里，我们只能任他摆布。

3727.i: leave sb/sth to the mercy/mercies of sb/sth
3727.e: They left the old dog to the mercy of the winter streets.  他们把那条老狗丢在寒冬的街头自生自灭。

3728.cn: 请求某人宽恕；乞求某人开恩
3728.e: He threw himself on the judge's mercy and asked for one more chance.  他向法官求情，请求再给一次机会。

3729.cn: 低调不张扬；不引人注意
3729.e: At parties he merges into the background and watches everyone else.  聚会上他总是低调地待在一旁看别人。

3730.cn: 人越多越热闹；多多益善
3730.e: Bring your cousins to the barbecue—the more the merrier.  把你表亲们也带来烧烤吧，人越多越热闹。

3731.e: The villagers made merry in the square until well past midnight.  村民们在广场上尽情欢闹，直到后半夜。

3732.i: make a ˈmess/ˈhash of sth/of doing sth
3732.cn: 把某事搞砸；弄得一团糟
3732.e: I made a complete hash of the interview by arriving twenty minutes late.  我迟到二十分钟，把面试彻底搞砸了。

3733.e: She kept looking at her watch until he finally got the message.  她不停看表，他终于会意了。

3734.e: He fixed the leak in ten minutes, no messing.  他十分钟就把漏水修好了，干脆利落。

3735.i: keep/put the ˈpedal to the ˈmetal (AmE, informal)
3735.e: We put the pedal to the metal and still reached the airport late.  我们一路油门踩到底，到机场还是晚了。

3736.i: be on, show, prove, etc. your ˈmettle
3736.cn: 显示自己的勇气和能力
3736.e: The young surgeon showed her mettle during that twelve-hour operation.  那台十二小时的手术让这位年轻外科医生展现了真本事。

3737.e: A tough opponent puts you on your mettle better than any coach.  强劲的对手比任何教练都更能激发你的斗志。

3738.i: take the ˈmickey/ˈmick (out of sb/sth) (BrE, informal)
3738.e: The lads took the mickey out of his new haircut all afternoon.  伙计们拿他的新发型取笑了一下午。

3739.cn: 以缩影的形式；具体而微地
3739.e: That noisy little street shows the whole country's changes in microcosm.  那条嘈杂的小街就是整个国家变迁的缩影。

3740.cn: 点石成金的本领；赚钱的本事
3740.e: Every shop she opens turns a profit; the woman has the Midas touch.  她开的每家店都赚钱，这女人真有点石成金的本事。

3741.i: be in the middle of sth/of doing sth
3741.e: I was in the middle of dinner when your call came through.  你打电话来的时候我正在吃饭。

3742.e: Patience is my middle name—I once queued six hours for tickets.  耐心是我的招牌，我曾为买票排过六小时队。

3743.e: The mayor is looking for a middle way between the two angry camps.  市长正在两个对立阵营之间寻求折中之道。

3744.cn: 住在偏远的地方；荒郊野岭
3744.e: They bought a cottage in the middle of nowhere with no phone signal.  他们在荒郊野岭买了间小屋，连手机信号都没有。

3745.cn: 夹在两方之间左右为难
3745.e: When my parents argue, I'm always piggy in the middle.  父母吵架时，我总是夹在中间受夹板气。

3746.i: in our, their, its, etc. ˈmidst (formal)
3746.e: We had no idea there was a famous novelist in our midst.  我们完全不知道当中还有一位著名小说家。

3747.i: in the ˈmidst of sth/of doing sth
3747.e: In the midst of packing, she realized her passport had expired.  正收拾行李时，她发现护照过期了。

3748.e: He stopped the speech in midstream and asked for a glass of water.  他讲到一半停下来，要了杯水。

3749.e: In that office might is right, and the loudest voice always wins.  在那个办公室里强权即公理，嗓门大的总赢。

3750.cn: 说得婉转些；说得客气点
3750.e: The meal was disappointing, to put it mildly, and cost a fortune.  那顿饭说得客气点叫令人失望，还贵得要命。

3751.cn: 多付出一份努力；再加把劲
3751.e: Our nurse went the extra mile and phoned every family personally.  我们的护士格外用心，挨个给家属打了电话。

3752.cn: 避之唯恐不及；吓得逃开
3752.e: Mention commitment and he'd run a mile in the opposite direction.  一提承诺，他就躲得远远的。

3753.i: see, spot, smell, etc. sth a ˈmile off (informal)
3753.cn: 一眼就能看出；老远就察觉
3753.e: You could spot that fake designer bag a mile off.  那个假名牌包老远就能看出来。

3754.cn: 极其明显；一眼就看得出
3754.e: His nerves stuck out a mile during the whole presentation.  整场演讲中他的紧张显而易见。

3755.e: The two sides are still miles apart on the question of pay.  双方在薪酬问题上仍然分歧巨大。

3756.i: miles apart on our understanding of the problem.
3756.cn: 对问题的理解大相径庭
3756.e: We are miles apart on our understanding of the problem, which slows everything down.  我们对问题的理解大相径庭，这拖慢了一切。

3757.e: Sorry, what did you say? I was miles away just then.  抱歉，你说什么？我刚才走神了。

3758.e: The car broke down miles from anywhere on a dark country road.  车在漆黑的乡间路上抛锚，四周荒无人烟。

3759.cn: 就在附近（间接指称某人某事）
3759.e: The person who leaked it is not a million miles from this room.  泄密的人就在这屋里，不用往远处找。

3760.i: I'm talking about is not a hundred miles from
3760.e: The factory I'm talking about is not a hundred miles from where we stand.  我说的那家工厂离我们站的地方并不远。

3761.cn: 人的善良天性；恻隐之心
3761.e: After that phone call, the milk of human kindness had quite dried up in me.  接完那通电话，我心里那点善意全没了。

3762.i: go through/put sb through the ˈmill
3762.cn: 经受磨练；使某人吃苦头
3762.e: The new recruits were put through the mill during their first fortnight.  新兵在头两周吃尽了苦头。

3763.e: In that new suit he looked like a million dollars at the reception.  穿上那套新西装，他在招待会上看起来神气极了。

3764.cn: 万里挑一；难得的人（或物）
3764.e: A neighbour who shovels your snow is one in a million.  会替你铲雪的邻居，真是万里挑一。

3765.cn: 沉重的负担；甩不掉的累赘
3765.e: That empty second flat became a millstone around their necks.  那套空置的第二套房成了他们甩不掉的包袱。

3766.i: not mince your ˈwords (also not ˈmince matters)
3766.cn: 直言不讳；说话不绕弯子
3766.e: The coach didn't mince his words about our defending last night.  教练对我们昨晚的防守直言不讳，毫不留情。

3767.cn: 彻底击败；驳得体无完肤
3767.e: The lawyer made mincemeat of the witness in ten minutes.  律师十分钟就把证人驳得体无完肤。

3768.i: at/in the ˌback of your ˈmind
3768.e: At the back of my mind I knew the trip was a mistake.  我心里隐隐知道，这趟旅行是个错误。

3769.cn: 纯属想象；是自己吓自己
3769.e: The doctor said the pain was all in my mind, which annoyed me.  医生说疼痛纯属心理作用，这话让我恼火。

3770.i: be of one/the same ˈmind (about/on sb/sth)
3770.e: For once my sister and I are of one mind about selling the house.  这次我和姐姐难得在卖房子上意见一致。

3771.e: Swimming in that river in February? You're out of your mind.  二月在那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。

3772.i: bear/keep sb/sth in ˈmind • bear/keep in
3772.e: Keep in mind that the last bus leaves at half past eleven.  记住，末班车十一点半发车。

3773.e: Bear in mind that the museum closes early on public holidays.  记住，博物馆节假日提前闭馆。

3774.e: That smell of wet wool brings my grandmother's kitchen to mind.  湿羊毛的味道让我想起外婆的厨房。

3775.e: No good excuse came to mind, so I just told her the truth.  一时想不出好借口，我就跟她说了实话。

3776.cn: 你介意吗（用于征求许可）
3776.e: Do you mind if I open the window? It's stifling in here.  我开下窗你介意吗？这里太闷了。

3777.e: Don't mind me, just carry on with your rehearsal.  别管我，你们继续排练。

3778.e: If you gave your mind to it, you'd finish that essay by lunchtime.  你要是专心去写，午饭前就能写完那篇文章。

3779.i: go over sth in your ˈmind
3779.e: She went over the conversation in her mind all the way home.  回家的一路上，她都在心里反复回想那段对话。

3780.i: have a good mind to ˈdo sth • have half a
3780.cn: 很想做某事；真想那么干
3780.e: I've a good mind to write to the council about these potholes.  我真想为这些坑洼给市政写封信。

3781.cn: 有点想做某事（但不一定去做）
3781.e: I've half a mind to quit and open a bookshop by the sea.  我有点想辞职，去海边开家书店。

3782.e: We have someone in mind for the job, but nothing's confirmed.  这职位我们心里有人选，不过还没定。

3783.i: have it in mind to do sth • have sth in
3783.cn: 打算做某事；有意做某事
3783.e: He's had it in mind to learn the guitar since he was twelve.  他从十二岁起就想学吉他。

3784.i: have a mind of your ˈown
3784.e: My daughter is six and already has a mind of her own about clothes.  我女儿六岁，穿什么衣服已经很有主见了。

3785.i: have your ˌmind on other ˈthings • your
3785.e: He burnt the rice because he had his mind on other things.  他把饭烧糊了，因为心思在别处。

3786.e: Sorry I missed the turning; my mind was on other things.  抱歉走错了路口，我刚才走神了。

3787.i: have a mind to do sth
3787.cn: 想要做某事；有意做某事
3787.e: I have a mind to sell this old piano before we move.  搬家前我想把这架旧钢琴卖掉。

3788.i: have sth on your ˈmind • sth is on your
3788.cn: 心里惦记着某事；为某事发愁
3788.e: You've clearly got something on your mind—out with it.  你显然有心事，说出来吧。

3789.e: Her son's exams have been on her mind for weeks.  儿子的考试让她惦记了好几个星期。

3790.i: I don't mind adˈmitting, ˈtelling you..., etc.
3790.e: I don't mind admitting I cried at the end of that film.  我不妨承认，那部电影结尾我哭了。

3791.i: I don't mind if I ˈdo (spoken, informal)
3791.e: Another slice of cake? I don't mind if I do.  再来块蛋糕？那我就不客气了。

3792.i: if you ˌdon't ˈmind • if you ˌwouldn't ˈmind
3792.cn: 如果你不介意（用于礼貌请求）
3792.e: I'll take the window seat, if you don't mind.  如果你不介意，我坐靠窗的位子。

3793.i: if you ˌdon't mind me/my ˈsaying so...
3793.cn: 恕我直言；你别介意我这么说
3793.e: If you don't mind my saying so, that colour really doesn't suit you.  恕我直言，那个颜色真的不适合你。

3794.e: In my mind's eye I can still see the old bridge before the flood.  在我脑海里，还能看见洪水前的那座老桥。

3795.e: I wouldn't mind a cold beer after carrying boxes all afternoon.  搬了一下午箱子，来杯冰啤酒倒是不错。

3796.i: I wouldn't mind living abroad for a few years.
3796.e: I wouldn't mind living abroad for a few years while the kids are small.  趁孩子还小，我倒想去国外住几年。

3797.i: keep your mind on sth • your mind is on
3797.e: Keep your mind on the road and stop fiddling with the radio.  专心开车，别老摆弄收音机。

3798.cn: 使人如释重负；心里石头落地
3798.e: Hearing the biopsy was clear took a huge weight off my mind.  听说活检结果没事，我心里的石头落了地。

3799.e: If this printer jams once more I'm going to lose my mind.  这台打印机再卡一次纸，我就要疯了。

3800.i: make up your ˈmind • make your ˈmind up
3800.e: She finally made up her mind to study medicine instead of law.  她最终决定学医而不是学法律。

3801.e: Make up your mind now, because tomorrow you can't change it.  现在就拿定主意，明天可就改不了了。

3802.i: the mind ˈboggles (at sth) • it boggles the
3802.e: The mind boggles at how much they spent on that wedding.  他们那场婚礼花了多少钱，简直难以想象。

3803.cn: 令人难以置信；使人摸不着头脑
3803.e: It boggles the mind that anyone approved such an ugly building.  居然有人批准这么丑的楼，真让人费解。

3804.e: Mind how you go—the pavement's icy near the corner.  路上小心，拐角那儿人行道结冰了。

3805.cn: 精神胜过物质；意志战胜身体
3805.e: Finishing that marathon was pure mind over matter for her.  跑完那场马拉松，全靠她的意志力。

3806.e: How much I earn is my affair, so mind your own business.  我挣多少是我的事，你别多管闲事。

3807.i: sitting in a cafe minding my own business when a
3807.cn: 我在咖啡馆坐着没招惹谁
3807.e: I was sitting in a cafe minding my own business when a stranger sat down.  我在咖啡馆坐着没招谁惹谁，一个陌生人就坐了下来。

3808.e: Mind your P's and Q's at your girlfriend's parents' house tonight.  今晚在你女友父母家要注意礼貌。

3809.i: 'please' and the pronunciation of ˈthank you.
3809.e: The phrase may come from 'please' and the pronunciation of thank you.  这个说法可能源自“请”和“谢谢”的发音。

3810.i: mind the ˈshop (BrE) (AmE mind the ˈstore)
3810.cn: 临时照看店铺；代管事务
3810.e: Can you mind the shop while I run to the bank?  我去趟银行，你能帮忙看会儿店吗？

3811.e: He's always late. Mind you, the traffic here is genuinely awful.  他总迟到。不过话说回来，这儿的交通确实糟糕。

3812.e: Mind your backs, please—hot soup coming through!  劳驾让让，热汤过来了！

3813.e: Never mind about the broken glass, I'll sweep it up.  杯子碎了没关系，我来扫。

3814.e: Never mind washing up—sit down and eat your dinner first.  别管洗碗了，先坐下吃饭。

3815.e: Never you mind how I got the tickets; just be there at seven.  别问我票怎么弄来的，七点到就是了。

3816.i: put you in mind of sb/sth (old-fashioned)
3816.e: That song puts me in mind of long car journeys as a child.  那首歌让我想起小时候漫长的汽车旅行。

3817.e: One text from her would put my mind at rest for the night.  她发条短信来，我今晚就能安心了。

3818.cn: 专心做某事；下功夫去做
3818.e: You could pass this exam easily if you set your mind to it.  你要是肯下功夫，这门考试轻松就过。

3819.i: put/get sth out of your ˈmind
3819.cn: 把某事抛在脑后；不再去想
3819.e: Put that argument out of your mind and enjoy the weekend.  把那场争吵忘了吧，好好过个周末。

3820.cn: 让某人转移注意力；暂时忘掉某事
3820.e: A long walk took my mind off the results for an hour.  长途散步让我把成绩的事忘了一个钟头。

3821.e: To my mind, the second candidate interviewed far better.  依我看，第二位候选人面试表现好得多。

3822.i: a practical, scientific, etc. turn of ˈmind
3822.cn: 务实（或科学等）的思维方式
3822.e: With her practical turn of mind, she fixed the leak herself.  她思维务实，自己就把漏水修好了。

3823.i: turn sth over in your ˈmind
3823.e: He turned the offer over in his mind for three sleepless nights.  他把那个提议反复琢磨了三个不眠之夜。

3824.e: We chose this flat with the children's school in mind.  我们选这套公寓，主要是考虑孩子上学。

3825.cn: 知识宝库；消息灵通的人
3825.e: Old Mr Chen is a mine of information about the neighbourhood.  老陈头对这一带的事情知道得比谁都多。

3826.e: Those who still prefer paper maps are in a small minority.  仍偏爱纸质地图的人只占极少数。

3827.i: be in a minority of ˈone (often humorous)
3827.e: I was in a minority of one in wanting pineapple on the pizza.  只有我一个人想在披萨上放菠萝。

3828.e: He sold me a 1970s camera in mint condition for very little.  他把一台崭新如初的七十年代相机低价卖给了我。

3829.i: exactly in mint condition so I really can't ask
3829.cn: 并非全新，因此不能要价太高
3829.e: My bike isn't exactly in mint condition so I really can't ask much.  我的自行车算不上全新，所以真不能要价太高。

3830.e: He made a mint selling face masks during that first winter.  头一个冬天他靠卖口罩赚了大钱。

3831.cn: 上下；正负（表示误差范围）
3831.e: The journey takes two hours, plus or minus twenty minutes.  路上要两小时，上下差个二十分钟。

3832.e: The delivery van should be here any minute now.  送货车马上就该到了。

3833.e: Call me the minute you land, no matter how late it is.  你一落地就给我打电话，多晚都行。

3834.e: I didn't for one minute believe his story about the missing keys.  他说钥匙丢了的那套说辞我一点也不信。

3835.e: Not for an instant did she consider giving up the case.  她一刻也没想过放弃这个案子。

3836.e: Come down here this minute and clean up the kitchen.  马上下来把厨房收拾干净。

3837.e: The Shanghai train arrived at 6.02, to the minute.  上海来的火车六点零二分到站，分秒不差。

3838.e: The app gives you up to the minute scores from every match.  这款应用提供每场比赛的最新比分。

3839.e: A week by the sea worked wonders for her mood.  在海边待一周，她的心情大为好转。

3840.i: do sb/yourself a ˈmischief (BrE, informal or humorous)
3840.e: Lift that box properly or you'll do yourself a mischief.  抬箱子姿势要对，不然你会伤到自己。

3841.e: She loves making mischief between the two departments.  她就爱在两个部门之间挑拨离间。

3842.e: Don't be such a misery guts—it's only a bit of rain.  别老拉着个脸，不过下点小雨罢了。

3843.i: put sb/sth out of their/its ˈmisery
3843.cn: 解除某人的悬念；结束（动物的）痛苦
3843.e: Put me out of my misery and just tell me who won.  别吊我胃口了，直接说谁赢了。

3844.e: Announce the results now and don't prolong the agony.  现在就公布结果吧，别再折磨大家了。

3845.i: he, she, etc. doesn't miss a ˈtrick (also he,
3845.e: Our accountant doesn't miss a trick when it comes to expenses.  说到报销，我们的会计什么都逃不过她的眼睛。

3846.cn: 什么都看在眼里；很少疏漏
3846.e: Grandma is ninety and still doesn't miss much around the house.  奶奶九十岁了，家里的事还是什么都瞒不过她。

3847.i: give sth a ˈmiss (informal, especially BrE)
3847.e: I'll give the gym a miss tonight; my knee is playing up.  今晚健身房我就不去了，膝盖不舒服。

3848.e: We missed the boat on cheap flights and now they've doubled.  我们错过了便宜机票，现在价格翻倍了。

3849.i: a ˌmiss is as ˌgood as a ˈmile (saying)
3849.cn: 差之毫厘，谬以千里；小错也是错
3849.e: He lost by two votes, but a miss is as good as a mile.  他只差两票落选，可差一点也是输。

3850.cn: 不知道自己错过了什么好东西
3850.e: You've never tried sushi? Honestly, you don't know what you're missing.  你从没吃过寿司？说真的，你不知道自己错过了什么。

3851.e: Two hours of scrubbing later, the kitchen was spotless — mission accomplished.  刷了两个小时，厨房一尘不染，任务完成。

3852.e: That was the coldest winter we've had in years, and no mistake!  那是我们多年来最冷的一个冬天，这是毫无疑问的。

3853.e: I took someone else's umbrella by mistake and only noticed on the bus.  我错拿了别人的伞，上了公交车才发现。

3854.e: He grabbed the salt in mistake for the sugar and ruined the whole cake.  他把盐错当成糖，整个蛋糕都毁了。

3855.cn: 毫无疑问；完全可以肯定
3855.e: Make no mistake about it, this decision will cost the company millions.  毫无疑问，这个决定会让公司损失几百万。

3856.e: There's no mistaking that laugh — Danny must be back from his trip.  那笑声绝不会认错，丹尼肯定旅行回来了。

3857.e: You can mix and match the plates; nobody expects a matching dinner set.  盘子可以随便混搭，没人指望你有整套餐具。

3858.i: ˈmix it (with sb) (BrE) (AmE ˌmix it ˈup (with sb))
3858.cn: 与某人吵架；找某人的茬
3858.e: Don't mix it with the referee or you'll be off the pitch in seconds.  别跟裁判吵，不然你几秒钟就被罚下场。

3859.cn: 卷入（尤指非法或不正当的事）；与某事有牵连
3859.e: His brother got mixed up in some shady business and ended up in court.  他哥哥卷进了一些见不得光的事，最后上了法庭。

3860.cn: 与（不正当的人）交往；和某人鬼混
3860.e: She got mixed up with a bad crowd during her first year at college.  她大一那年跟一帮不三不四的人混在了一起。

3861.e: I have mixed feelings about moving abroad — excited, but scared of losing friends.  对出国我心情复杂，既兴奋又怕失去朋友。

3862.cn: 大杂烩；五花八门的人或物
3862.e: The applicants were a mixed bag: two experts, three students and a retired chef.  应聘者五花八门：两个专家、三个学生和一个退休厨师。

3863.cn: 福祸参半的事物；利弊并存的事
3863.e: Working from home is a mixed blessing — no commute, but no escape either.  在家办公利弊参半：不用通勤，却也无处可逃。

3864.cn: 善于（或不善于）交际的人
3864.e: Tom's a good mixer; he knew half the room within ten minutes of arriving.  汤姆很会social，到场十分钟就认识了半屋子人。

3865.i: put the ˈmockers on sth (BrE, informal)
3865.cn: 挫败；使落空；使成功无望
3865.e: The rain really put the mockers on our barbecue plans for Saturday.  这场雨彻底毁了我们周六烧烤的计划。

3866.cn: 使成为笑柄；嘲弄；使显得荒唐
3866.e: Letting him off with a fine makes a mockery of the whole justice system.  只罚他点钱，简直是把整个司法制度当笑话。

3867.cn: （房屋）配备各种现代生活设施
3867.e: The flat is tiny but comes with all mod cons, including a dishwasher.  这公寓虽小，但各种现代设施齐全，连洗碗机都有。

3868.i: if the mountain will not come to Muˈhammad, Muˌhammad must go to the ˈmountain (saying)
3868.cn: 山不就我，我便就山；人要懂得变通
3868.e: She won't visit, so I'll fly over — if the mountain will not come to Muhammad.  她不肯来，那我飞过去，山不就我我就山。

3869.e: I can't talk at the moment — can I call you back in an hour?  我现在不方便讲话，一小时后回你电话行吗？

3870.cn: 此刻；目前（用于说明当前状况）
3870.e: The number is engaged at the moment, so I'll try again later.  这个号码目前占线，我稍后再打。

3871.i: the man, woman, etc. of the ˈmoment
3871.cn: 当前红极一时的人；最受关注的人
3871.e: After that winning goal, he's the man of the moment in every newspaper.  那记制胜球之后，他成了各家报纸的头号风云人物。

3872.cn: 关键时刻；见分晓的时刻
3872.e: The envelope was in my hand — this was the moment of truth.  信封就在我手里，见分晓的时刻到了。

3873.e: The committee has several matters of moment to settle before Friday.  委员会周五前还有几件要紧事要解决。

3874.e: If you want a pay rise, pick your moment — don't ask when she's stressed.  想加薪就挑好时机，别在她焦头烂额时开口。

3875.cn: 也有精彩（或得意）的时候
3875.e: The film drags in places, but it definitely has its moments.  这片子有些地方拖沓，但确实也有出彩的时候。

3876.cn: 事后诸葛亮；马后炮的人
3876.e: Every Monday morning quarterback in the office knew how to fix the deal.  办公室里每个马后炮都知道那笔交易该怎么救。

3877.cn: 钱多得花不完；有用不完的钱
3877.e: Only someone with money to burn would pay that much for a pair of shoes.  只有钱多得没处花的人才会花那么多买双鞋。

3878.cn: 事后诸葛亮式的评论；马后炮
3878.e: Enough Monday morning quarterbacking — nobody could have predicted that storm.  别再放马后炮了，那场暴风雨谁也预料不到。

3879.cn: 周一上午的低落情绪；假期后不想上班
3879.e: I've got that Monday morning feeling and it's only nine o'clock.  我这会儿满是周一综合症，可才九点钟。

3880.e: If this contract goes through, we'll be in the money by Christmas.  这份合同要是签成，圣诞节前我们就发财了。

3881.cn: 极其富有；钱多得用不完
3881.e: Another new phone? I'm not made of money, you know.  又要新手机？我可不是印钞机。

3882.e: For my money, she's the best singer this competition has ever produced.  依我看，她是这个比赛出过的最好的歌手。

3883.e: Your guess about the traffic was right on the money — we took two hours.  你对路况的判断完全准确，我们开了两小时。

3884.e: They put money into stocks and shares instead of leaving it in the bank.  他们把钱投进了股票，而不是放在银行里。

3885.e: My uncle put money into a friend's café and lost every penny.  我叔叔投钱给朋友开咖啡馆，结果血本无归。

3886.e: The government should put more money into the film industry.  政府应该在电影业投入更多资金。

3887.e: I'd put my money on the grey horse — she's won her last three races.  我押那匹灰马，她前三场都赢了。

3888.i: put your money where your ˈmouth is
3888.cn: 说话算数；用行动兑现承诺
3888.e: If you really believe in the project, put your money where your mouth is.  你要真看好这个项目，就拿钱出来证明。

3889.cn: 物有所值的收获；有力的竞争
3889.e: They lost, but they gave the champions a good run for their money.  他们输了，但让冠军队费了不少劲。

3890.cn: 为挽回损失再砸钱；把钱扔进无底洞
3890.e: Repairing that old van again would just be throwing good money after bad.  再修那辆破面包车就是往无底洞里扔钱。

3891.e: He throws his money around in bars to impress people he barely knows.  他在酒吧里挥金如土，就为了在半生不熟的人面前显摆。

3892.cn: 只砸钱了事；往某事上白扔钱
3892.e: You can't fix a broken school system just by throwing money at it.  光靠砸钱是修不好一个烂掉的教育体系的。

3893.i: I don't/couldn't give a ˈmonkey's (BrE, slang)
3893.cn: 我压根儿不在乎；无所谓
3893.e: He can think what he likes — I couldn't give a monkey's.  他爱怎么想怎么想，我压根不在乎。

3894.i: make a ˈmonkey out of sb
3894.cn: 拿某人当猴耍；使某人出洋相
3894.e: They made a monkey out of him by sending him to a meeting that didn't exist.  他们让他去开一个根本不存在的会，把他耍得团团转。

3895.e: I want no monkey business while I'm out — just finish your homework.  我出去这段时间不许胡闹，把作业写完。

3896.cn: 难以摆脱的负担（或毒瘾、难题）
3896.e: That unpaid loan has been a monkey on his back for three years.  那笔没还的贷款压了他三年，甩都甩不掉。

3897.e: The kids ran outside laughing at the monkey's wedding falling on the garden.  孩子们跑到院子里，笑着看这场太阳雨。

3898.e: My cousin only calls once in a blue moon, usually when he needs a favour.  我表哥难得打一次电话，多半是有事求人。

3899.e: Month after month she saved a little, until she could afford the deposit.  她月复一月地攒钱，直到攒够首付。

3900.e: His health improved month by month after he finally quit smoking.  他戒烟之后，身体一个月比一个月好。

3901.e: You won't get him to apologize, not in a month of Sundays.  想让他道歉？八辈子也不可能。

3902.i: be in the ˈmood for sth/for doing sth
3902.cn: 有心情做某事；想做某事
3902.e: I'm not in the mood for a party tonight; let's just order pizza.  今晚我没心情去派对，我们叫披萨吧。

3903.i: be in no ˈmood for sth/for doing sth
3903.cn: 没心思做某事；无意做某事
3903.e: After that phone call she was in no mood for jokes about her boss.  接完那通电话，她可没心情听关于她老板的玩笑。

3904.i: be over the ˈmoon (informal, especially BrE)
3904.e: She was over the moon when the university finally sent her an offer.  大学终于发来录取通知时，她高兴得不得了。

3905.i: cry/ask for the ˈmoon (also want the ˈmoon)
3905.cn: 想要办不到的事；异想天开
3905.e: Asking for a pay rise and a shorter week is crying for the moon here.  在这里既要加薪又要减少工时，简直是异想天开。

3906.e: The tenants did a moonlight flit, leaving three months' rent unpaid.  那些租客连夜跑了，欠了三个月房租。

3907.e: Many moons ago I could run a marathon without stopping once.  很久以前我能一口气跑完马拉松。

3908.cn: 很久以前；那是很早的事了
3908.e: Many moons ago, when I was young, this whole street was farmland.  很久以前我年轻时，这整条街都是农田。

3909.cn: 有争议的问题；尚无定论的事
3909.e: Whether the new rule actually helps students is still a moot point.  新规定是否真对学生有帮助，仍然众说纷纭。

3910.cn: （给某人）道义上的支持；精神支持
3910.e: I can't fix the car, but I'll come along and give you moral support.  我修不了车，但我可以陪着你，给你打打气。

3911.i: take, claim, seize, etc. the moral ˈhigh ground
3911.cn: 占据道德制高点；自居正义
3911.e: He seized the moral high ground by refusing to take the company's money.  他拒收公司的钱，从而占据了道德制高点。

3912.i: be ˈmore than glad, ready, etc. (to do sth)
3912.e: I'd be more than glad to look after your cat while you're away.  你不在的时候，我非常乐意帮你照看猫。

3913.e: Now that's more like it — the soup's finally hot enough.  这才像话嘛，汤总算够烫了。

3914.e: The report is more or less finished; I just need to add the charts.  报告差不多写完了，我只要再加上图表。

3915.cn: 宿醉；狂饮之后次日的难受
3915.e: He staggered in at noon with a classic case of the morning after.  他中午晃进来，一副典型的宿醉模样。

3916.e: She practises that violin morning, noon and night, and the neighbours complain.  她一天到晚拉小提琴，邻居都有意见了。

3917.e: The two families have been mortal enemies since a dispute over land.  这两家自从争地之后就成了死对头。

3918.e: The whole trip will take an hour at the most if the roads are clear.  路上要是不堵，全程最多一个小时。

3919.e: He learned those old fishing songs at his mother's knee.  那些古老的渔歌是他小时候在母亲膝下学会的。

3920.e: Shall I be mother and pour the tea for everyone?  我来当东道，给大家倒茶吧？

3921.e: After forty years abroad, he still calls Ireland the mother country.  在国外待了四十年，他仍然把爱尔兰称作祖国。

3922.e: We got caught in the mother of all traffic jams on the way home.  回家路上我们碰上了史上最恐怖的大堵车。

3923.e: Even after years in Berlin, she counts money in her mother tongue.  在柏林待了这么多年，她数钱时还是用母语。

3924.i: put/set sth in ˈmotion (also set the wheels in ˈmotion)
3924.e: One phone call set the wheels in motion for the whole rescue operation.  一通电话就启动了整个救援行动。

3925.i: go through the ˈmotions (of doing sth)
3925.e: He's just going through the motions at work until his notice period ends.  离职期没结束前，他在公司只是应付差事。

3926.i: break the ˈmould (of sth) (BrE) (AmE break the ˈmold (of sth))
3926.cn: 打破常规；改变固有模式
3926.e: Her first novel broke the mould of what a detective story could be.  她的第一部小说打破了侦探小说的固有套路。

3927.i: break the ˈmould (of sth) (BrE) (AmE break the ˈmold (of sth))
3927.e: This design really breaks the mould — no other container looks like it.  这个设计真的打破了常规，没有别的容器长这样。

3928.i: if the mountain will not come to Muˈhammad, Muˌhammad must go to the ˈmountain (saying)
3928.cn: 山不就我，我便就山；要懂变通
3928.e: He never answers emails, so I flew there: if the mountain will not come to Muhammad.  他从不回邮件，我只好飞过去，山不就我我就山。

3929.i: make a ˌmountain out of a ˈmolehill (disapproving)
3929.e: It's one late payment; don't make a mountain out of a molehill.  不过晚交了一次款，别小题大做。

3930.e: Get a move on — the train leaves in eleven minutes and we're still here.  快点，火车十一分钟后就开，我们还在这儿呢。

3931.i: be all ˈmouth (BrE also be all mouth and no ˈtrousers) (informal)
3931.e: He swears he'll quit tomorrow, but he's all mouth and no trousers.  他发誓明天就辞职，其实光说不练。

3932.i: be all ˈmouth and no ˈtrousers (BrE, informal)
3932.e: Ignore his threats — the man is all mouth and no trousers.  别理他的威胁，那人就是嘴上厉害。

3933.e: You've looked down in the mouth all week — is something wrong at home?  你这一周都无精打采的，家里出事了吗？

3934.cn: 使某人垂涎；令人流口水
3934.e: The smell of garlic bread from the kitchen made my mouth water.  厨房飘来的蒜香面包味让我直流口水。

3935.i: run off at the ˈmouth (AmE, informal)
3935.e: He ran off at the mouth for twenty minutes and said absolutely nothing useful.  他滔滔不绝讲了二十分钟，一句有用的都没有。

3936.i: out of the ˌmouths of ˈbabes (and ˈsucklings) (saying)
3936.cn: 童言有理；小孩说话常有道理
3936.e: My six-year-old solved it instantly — out of the mouths of babes!  我六岁的孩子一下就说出答案了，童言有理啊！

3937.e: If we don't get a move on, we'll miss the start of the film.  再不抓紧，我们就赶不上电影开头了。

3938.e: It's nearly midnight; I think we should make a move.  快半夜了，我看我们该走了。

3939.e: He made a move on her at the party and got politely turned down.  他在派对上向她示好，被客气地拒绝了。

3940.i: move the ˈgoalposts (informal, disapproving, especially BrE)
3940.cn: 中途改变规则（使人为难）
3940.e: Every time we meet the target, management moves the goalposts again.  我们每次达标，管理层就又改一次标准。

3941.e: Police finally arrested the Mr Big behind the whole smuggling network.  警方终于抓到了整个走私网络背后的老大。

3942.e: I've been Mr Nice Guy for months; from today I'm saying no.  我当了几个月好好先生，从今天起我要学会拒绝。

3943.cn: 如意郎君；理想的结婚对象
3943.e: She's still waiting for Mr Right and refuses to settle for less.  她还在等她的白马王子，不肯将就。

3944.e: I thought he'd forget, and he did as much — no card, no call.  我就知道他会忘，果然如此，没卡片也没电话。

3945.i: as much as sb can/could ˈdo (not) to do sth
3945.cn: 尽最大努力才（没有）做某事
3945.e: It was as much as I could do not to laugh during his speech.  他讲话时我拼命忍着才没笑出来。

3946.i: be not so much sth as sth
3946.e: She's not so much angry as deeply disappointed in all of us.  与其说她生气，不如说她对我们大失所望。

3947.cn: （对某人来说）承受不了；太过分
3947.e: Three night shifts in a row was too much for him, so he quit.  连上三个夜班他实在吃不消，就辞职了。

3948.e: Much as I love the city, I couldn't live there all year round.  尽管我很爱这座城市，却没法常年住在那里。

3949.i: not be much of a sth
3949.e: I'm not much of a cook, but I can manage scrambled eggs.  我算不上会做饭，但炒鸡蛋还行。

3950.e: Both offers are decent; honestly, there's not much in it.  两份工作都不错，说实话差别不大。

3951.e: The hotel was cheap, but the breakfast wasn't up to much.  酒店挺便宜，可早餐实在不怎么样。

3952.e: The car broke down again — so much for the mechanic's guarantee.  车又坏了，那修车师傅的保证也不过如此。

3953.cn: 到这种程度以致；如此以至于
3953.e: She loves the sea, so much so that she moved to a fishing village.  她爱海爱到搬去了一个渔村住。

3954.e: I'll say this much for him: he never once complained about the hours.  我得替他说句公道话：他从没抱怨过工时。

3955.e: Was the concert worth the ticket price? Very much so.  演唱会值那个票价吗？太值了。

3956.i: without so much as sth/as doing sth
3956.e: He walked out without so much as a goodbye to anyone.  他就那么走了，连声再见都没跟人说。

3957.e: The two hotels are much of a muchness, so pick the cheaper one.  两家酒店半斤八两，挑便宜的那家吧。

3958.i: where there's ˌmuck there's ˈbrass (BrE, saying)
3958.e: He cleans drains and drives a new car — where there's muck there's brass.  他通下水道却开新车，脏活儿才来钱。

3959.e: Both candidates spent the debate throwing mud at each other.  两位候选人整场辩论都在互相泼脏水。

3960.i: mud ˈsticks (also if you ˌthrow enough ˈmud, ˌsome of it will ˈstick) (saying)
3960.cn: 污名难洗；谣言总会留下痕迹
3960.e: He was cleared in court, but mud sticks and clients still avoid him.  他已被判无罪，可污名难洗，客户仍躲着他。

3961.cn: 把水搅浑；使问题更复杂
3961.e: Bringing up last year's budget only muddies the waters in this discussion.  提去年的预算只会把这场讨论搅得更乱。

3962.cn: 混淆视听；使事情不明朗
3962.e: They're just muddying the waters with all this talk of a new deadline.  他们拿新截止日期这套说辞纯粹是在混淆视听。

3963.i: be a ˈmug's game (disapproving, especially BrE)
3963.cn: 傻子才干的事；徒劳无益的事
3963.e: Buying lottery tickets every week is a mug's game, if you ask me.  要我说，每周买彩票是傻子才干的事。

3964.cn: 掩盖种种实情；遮住许多不足
3964.e: The phrase 'cosy flat' can cover a multitude of sins in an advert.  广告里“温馨小屋”这几个字能掩盖一大堆问题。

3965.e: Keep mum about the party — it's supposed to be a surprise for Jen.  派对的事别说出去，那是给珍的惊喜。

3966.e: You're getting engaged? Congratulations — and mum's the word!  你要订婚了？恭喜，我一定保密！

3967.cn: 突然特别想吃东西；嘴馋
3967.e: It's midnight and I've got the munchies — is there any bread left?  半夜了我又嘴馋，还有面包吗？

3968.e: Whenever he studies late he gets the munchies and empties the biscuit tin.  他一熬夜学习就嘴馋，把饼干罐吃个精光。

3969.i: get away with ˈmurder (informal, often humorous)
3969.cn: 为所欲为而不受惩罚；无法无天
3969.e: That kid gets away with murder because his grandmother never says no.  那孩子无法无天，因为他奶奶从不说不。

3970.e: After that long walk I could murder a cold beer right now.  走了那么远，我现在特别想来杯冰啤酒。

3971.i: he, she, etc. will ˈmurder you (spoken)
3971.e: Don't touch Dad's toolbox — he'll murder you if anything's missing.  别动爸的工具箱，少了东西他会宰了你。

3972.e: She worked two extra shifts without a murmur and went home smiling.  她一声不吭地多上了两班，回家时还笑着。

3973.cn: 墨菲定律（可能出错的事终会出错）
3973.e: The printer died five minutes before the deadline — Murphy's Law again.  截止前五分钟打印机坏了，又是墨菲定律。

3974.cn: 墨菲定律；越怕出事越出事
3974.e: By Murphy's Law, it rained the one day I left my umbrella at home.  按墨菲定律，我偏偏在没带伞那天赶上下雨。

3975.cn: 是好消息；听着让人高兴
3975.e: Hearing that the loan was approved was music to my ears.  听说贷款批下来了，简直是天籁之音。

3976.cn: （虽不赞同但允许）你非要那样就…
3976.e: Smoke outside if you must, but please don't do it in the kitchen.  你非抽不可就去外面抽，别在厨房里抽。

3977.e: He's friendly enough, but he just doesn't cut the mustard as a manager.  他人挺好，可当经理实在不够格。

3978.i: be mutton dressed (up) as ˈlamb (BrE, informal, disapproving)
3978.e: That miniskirt on her is mutton dressed as lamb, my aunt whispered.  我姑姑小声说，她穿那条超短裙就是老来俏。

3979.i: be mutton dressed (up) as ˈlamb (BrE, informal, disapproving)
3979.e: Somebody should remind her that she's fifty-five — mutton dressed as lamb.  该有人提醒她已经五十五了，别再装嫩了。

3980.i: nail your colours to the ˈmast (especially BrE)
3980.cn: 公开表明立场；明确表态
3980.e: The mayor nailed her colours to the mast and backed the new hospital.  市长公开表态，支持修建这家新医院。

3981.cn: 促使失败的因素；致命一击
3981.e: Losing the last big client was the final nail in the firm's coffin.  失去最后一个大客户，成了公司的致命一击。

3982.cn: 导致某事终结之物；雪上加霜的事
3982.e: The new tax has driven another nail into the coffin of the film industry.  新税又给电影业的棺材钉上一颗钉子。

3983.cn: 严惩某人；狠狠教训某人
3983.e: If the auditors find those receipts, they'll nail him to the wall.  审计员要是找到那些收据，会把他往死里整。

3984.e: He bought the van and paid cash on the nail, no haggling at all.  他买下那辆车，当场付现，一点都没还价。

3985.e: The comet is faint but still visible to the naked eye tonight.  这颗彗星很暗，但今晚肉眼仍能看到。

3986.e: The naked truth is that we simply cannot afford another car.  赤裸裸的事实是，我们根本买不起第二辆车。

3987.e: The teacher knew every child by name within the first two weeks.  头两周内老师就叫得出每个孩子的名字。

3988.e: A young man by the name of Carter has been asking to see you.  一个名叫卡特的年轻人一直要见你。

3989.e: He writes crime novels and goes by the name of J. L. Frost.  他写犯罪小说，笔名叫 J. L. 弗罗斯特。

3990.i: have (sb's) ˈname on it • with your ˈname on it (informal)
3990.cn: 注定属于某人的；命中注定的
3990.e: That corner house has your name on it — you'll love the garden.  那栋角落的房子简直就是为你留的，你会爱死那个花园。

3991.e: He arrived in London without a penny to his name.  他到伦敦时身无分文。

3992.e: She's been running the department in all but name for two years.  这两年她实际上一直在管这个部门，只是没名分。

3993.i: in ˈGod's/ˈHeaven's name • in the name of ˈGod/ˈHeaven
3993.e: What in God's name were you thinking when you signed that?  你签那玩意儿的时候到底在想什么？

3994.i: in ˈGod's/ˈHeaven's name • in the name of ˈGod/ˈHeaven
3994.cn: （用于强调）究竟；看在上帝份上
3994.e: Why in Heaven's name did nobody tell me the meeting was cancelled?  究竟为什么没人告诉我会议取消了？

3995.i: in the name of ˈsb/ˈsth • in sb's/sth's ˈname
3995.e: Terrible things have been done in the name of progress.  多少可怕的事都是以进步的名义干出来的。

3996.e: He's the boss in name only; his deputy makes all the decisions.  他只是名义上的老板，一切都由副手拍板。

3997.i: make a ˈname for yourself • make your ˈname
3997.e: She made a name for herself photographing storms across the Midwest.  她靠拍摄中西部的风暴打出了名气。

3998.i: make a ˈname for yourself • make your ˈname
3998.e: He made his name with one song and has been touring ever since.  他靠一首歌成名，从此巡演不断。

3999.e: They've been engaged for years but still haven't named the day.  他们订婚好几年了，婚期却一直没定。

4000.i: your, his, etc. name is ˈmud (informal, usually humorous)
4000.e: After he forgot her birthday again, his name is mud in that house.  他又忘了她生日，如今在那个家里臭名昭著。

4001.e: The witness refused to name names, even under pressure from the court.  即便法庭施压，证人仍拒绝指名道姓。

4002.e: I won't name names, but some people in this room broke the rules.  我不点名，不过在座有人违反了规定。

4003.e: In this business, patience is the name of the game.  干这行，耐心才是关键。

4004.cn: 赫赫有名的名字；响当当的人物
4004.e: In local politics, her grandfather is still a name to conjure with.  在本地政坛，她祖父的名字至今响当当。

4005.e: I know that actor's face but I can't put a name to him.  那演员的脸我认得，就是叫不出名字。

4006.cn: 妄称某人之名；背后议论某人
4006.e: Were you two taking my name in vain while I was out?  我不在的时候你俩是不是在背后编排我？

4007.i: you ˌname it, sb's ˈgot it (informal)
4007.cn: 凡是你说得出的，应有尽有
4007.e: Screwdrivers, drills, saws — you name it, my dad's got it.  螺丝刀、电钻、锯子，只要你说得出，我爸都有。

4008.e: Somebody who shall remain nameless ate the last slice of cake.  某位就不点名了的人，吃掉了最后一块蛋糕。

4009.e: A colleague who will remain nameless left the fridge door open all weekend.  某位不便点名的同事让冰箱门开了整个周末。

4010.cn: 保姆式国家（政府管得太多）
4010.e: Banning salt in restaurants is the nanny state gone too far.  禁止餐馆放盐，这保姆式管理未免管得太宽。

4011.e: The van missed us by inches — that was a narrow escape.  那辆面包车差几厘米就撞上我们，真是死里逃生。

4012.e: The argument turned nasty when someone mentioned the money.  有人提到钱之后，争吵一下子就变难看了。

4013.i: a nasty piece of ˈwork (BrE, informal)
4013.e: Steer clear of the landlord; he's a nasty piece of work.  离那房东远点，他不是什么好东西。

4014.e: After a year in Naples he's gone native — espresso standing at the bar.  在那不勒斯待了一年，他彻底本地化了，站在吧台喝浓缩咖啡。

4015.cn: 对某人来说不费力；是天生的本事
4015.e: Talking to strangers comes naturally to her, which is why she sells so much.  跟陌生人搭话是她的天分，所以她业绩才这么好。

4016.e: Getting up before five feels completely against nature to me.  五点前起床对我来说完全违背天性。

4017.e: They sold the flat and went back to nature on a small farm.  他们卖掉公寓，搬到小农场回归自然。

4018.e: His remark was in the nature of a warning rather than a joke.  他那句话与其说是玩笑，不如说是警告。

4019.cn: 理所当然；事物本该如此
4019.e: In the nature of things, children eventually leave home.  照事物的常理，孩子终归要离家的。

4020.e: The vet said to stop worrying and let nature take its course.  兽医说别担心了，顺其自然吧。

4021.i: as ˌnear as ˈdammit (also as ˌnear as makes no ˈdifference) (BrE, spoken)
4021.e: The bill came to fifty pounds, as near as dammit.  账单差不多正好五十镑。

4022.e: We've been waiting an hour, near enough, and nobody has come.  我们差不多等了一个钟头，一个人也没来。

4023.e: Two planes had a near miss above the airport this morning.  今早两架飞机在机场上空险些相撞。

4024.e: Some of his jokes at the wedding were a bit near the knuckle.  他在婚礼上讲的有些笑话有点儿荤。

4025.e: The repairs are nowhere near finished, and the money has run out.  修缮工作离完工还远着呢，钱却花光了。

4026.i: so ˌnear and ˌyet so ˈfar
4026.cn: 功亏一篑；差一点就成了
4026.e: We lost in the final minute — so near and yet so far.  我们在最后一分钟输了，功亏一篑。

4027.i: your ˌnearest and ˈdearest (informal, often humorous)
4027.e: At Christmas we squeeze all our nearest and dearest round one table.  圣诞节我们把所有至亲都挤在一张桌子边。

4028.e: This coat is not nearly warm enough for a Moscow winter.  这件外套对莫斯科的冬天来说远远不够暖和。

4029.e: Expensive wine is not necessarily better than the bottle on offer.  贵的葡萄酒未必就比促销那瓶好。

4030.e: Being busy does not necessarily mean you are getting anything done.  忙碌未必意味着你真做成了什么。

4031.cn: 必要之恶；不得已而为之的坏事
4031.e: For most freelancers, chasing unpaid invoices is a necessary evil.  对多数自由职业者来说，催欠款是不得不干的苦差。

4032.i: neˌcessity is the ˌmother of inˈvention (saying)
4032.e: We built a stove from a tin can — necessity is the mother of invention.  我们用铁罐做了个炉子，需要真是发明之母。

4033.i: neˌcessity is the ˌmother of inˈvention (saying)
4033.cn: 需要是发明之母；急中生智
4033.e: With no printer, she wrote the signs by hand: necessity is the mother of invention.  没有打印机，她就手写标牌，需要是发明之母。

4034.cn: 将无奈之举说成美德；变被动为主动
4034.e: Stuck at home, he made a virtue of necessity and finally learned to bake.  困在家里，他索性顺势而为，终于学会了烘焙。

4035.i: be up to your ˈneck in sth • be in sth up to your ˈneck
4035.e: I'm up to my neck in paperwork, so lunch will have to wait.  我埋在文件堆里，午饭只能往后拖了。

4036.i: be up to your ˈneck in sth • be in sth up to your ˈneck
4036.e: He's in debt up to his neck and still buying rounds at the pub.  他债台高筑，还在酒吧请客买单。

4037.i: break your ˈneck (doing sth/to do sth)
4037.e: I broke my neck to finish the report and nobody even read it.  我拼了命赶完报告，结果没人看。

4038.e: Our team won by a neck after a photo finish.  经过终点摄影判定，我们队以微弱优势获胜。

4039.i: get it in the ˈneck (BrE, informal)
4039.e: If the shop opens late again, you'll get it in the neck from the manager.  店里再晚开门，你就要挨经理骂了。

4040.i: in your, this, etc. ˌneck of the ˈwoods (informal)
4040.cn: 在某地一带；在这一片地区
4040.e: What brings you to this neck of the woods on a Tuesday?  周二这天什么风把你吹到我们这一带了？

4041.i: ˌneck and ˈneck (with sb/sth) (also ˌnip and ˈtuck (with sb) especially AmE)
4041.e: The two candidates were neck and neck right up to the final count.  两位候选人一直到最后计票都难分伯仲。

4042.e: I'll sleep on the sofa if need be; just don't book a hotel.  必要的话我睡沙发，别订酒店了。

4043.cn: 这下可好；真是雪上加霜
4043.e: A flat tyre in the rain — that's all I need!  下着雨还爆胎，这下可好！

4044.i: like looking for/trying to find a ˌneedle in a ˈhaystack
4044.e: Finding one file on that laptop is like looking for a needle in a haystack.  在那台笔记本上找一个文件简直是大海捞针。

4045.i: like looking for/trying to find a ˌneedle in a ˈhaystack
4045.e: Tracking him down in Shanghai was like trying to find a needle in a haystack.  在上海找到他，简直如同大海捞针。

4046.e: I sat cross-legged too long and now I have pins and needles.  我盘腿坐太久，现在腿麻得不行。

4047.e: Needless to say, he arrived twenty minutes after the interview started.  不用说，他在面试开始二十分钟后才到。

4048.e: I hate night shifts, but needs must when the devil drives.  我讨厌上夜班，可形势所迫也没办法。

4049.i: in the ˈneighbourhood of sth (BrE) (AmE in the ˈneighborhood of sth)
4049.e: The repairs will cost in the neighbourhood of two thousand pounds.  修理费大约在两千英镑上下。

4050.i: not on your ˈnelly (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
4050.e: Lend him the car again? Not on your nelly.  再把车借他？门儿都没有。

4051.e: You've got a nerve, asking for a lift after what you said.  你说了那种话还敢让我捎你，脸皮真厚。

4052.e: Mentioning his old job clearly touched a raw nerve.  提到他从前的工作，显然戳到了他的痛处。

4053.cn: 非常紧张的人；焦虑不安的人
4053.e: She was a bundle of nerves the morning of her driving test.  路考那天早上她紧张得不行。

4054.cn: 使某人心烦；惹某人厌烦
4054.e: That dripping tap is really getting on my nerves tonight.  今晚那滴水的龙头真让我心烦。

4055.e: You need nerves of steel to land a plane in that wind.  这种风里降落飞机，得有钢铁般的胆量。

4056.e: They built up a decent nest egg before their first child arrived.  第一个孩子出生前，他们攒下了一笔不错的积蓄。

4057.cn: 空巢（子女离家后的家庭）
4057.e: After the twins left for university, they had to get used to the empty nest.  双胞胎上大学后，他们得慢慢适应空巢生活。

4058.e: Cast your net wide when job-hunting; don't apply to just one city.  找工作要广撒网，别只投一个城市。

4059.cn: 在中立地点；在第三方场所
4059.e: Let's meet on neutral ground — a café rather than either office.  我们找个中立地点见吧，去咖啡馆，别在谁的办公室。

4060.e: They bought the whole kitchen on the never-never and regretted it later.  他们分期买下整套厨房设备，后来后悔了。

4061.e: A bit of polish and the old table looked as good as new.  稍一打蜡，这张旧桌子看起来就跟新的一样。

4062.e: Everyone keeps saying that fifty is the new thirty these days.  如今人人都说五十岁就是新的三十岁。

4063.e: The new head teacher changed everything in a month — a new broom sweeps clean.  新校长一个月内改了个遍，新官上任三把火。

4064.i: a/the ˌnew kid on the ˈblock (informal)
4064.e: As the new kid on the block, he ate lunch alone for a week.  作为新来的，他独自吃了一星期午饭。

4065.cn: 新好男人（分担家务育儿的男性）
4065.e: He cooks, cleans and does the school run — a proper new man.  他做饭、打扫、接送孩子，是个标准的新好男人。

4066.e: Coffee with butter in it? That's a new one on me.  咖啡里加黄油？我还是头一回听说。

4067.e: He's turned over a new leaf and hasn't missed a shift since January.  他已痛改前非，一月以来一天班都没缺过。

4068.e: Hey, long time no see — what's new?  嘿，好久不见，最近怎么样？

4069.e: A wet summer is bad news for farmers around here.  多雨的夏天对这一带的农民来说是个坏消息。

4070.e: Lower interest rates are good news for anyone with a mortgage.  利率下调对所有背房贷的人都是好消息。

4071.e: Nobody wanted to break the news to her that the dog had died.  谁也不愿告诉她狗死了的消息。

4072.cn: 我可从没听说；这我倒是头一回知道
4072.e: The office is closing on Friday? That's news to me.  周五办公室要关门？我怎么不知道。

4073.e: She hasn't rung from the hospital, but no news is good news.  她还没从医院打电话来，不过没消息就是好消息。

4074.e: He'd take that job in a New York minute if they offered it.  他们要是给他那份工作，他一秒钟都不会犹豫。

4075.i: as good, well, etc. as the ˈnext person
4075.cn: 和一般人一样（好）；不比别人差
4075.e: I enjoy a lazy Sunday as much as the next person.  懒散的周日我和谁一样喜欢。

4076.cn: 仅次于最佳的选择；退而求其次
4076.e: We couldn't get tickets, so watching it in the pub was the next best thing.  我们没买到票，去酒吧看算是退而求其次。

4077.e: The hospital needs the name of your next of kin on this form.  医院要在这张表上填你的直系亲属姓名。

4078.i: ˌnice ˈwork if you can get it (informal)
4078.cn: 轻松的好差事；这活儿谁不想干
4078.e: He gets paid to taste chocolate — nice work if you can get it.  他靠试吃巧克力赚钱，这好差事谁不想要。

4079.e: The new café is doing nicely, even in its first winter.  这家新咖啡馆生意不错，头一个冬天就挺好。

4080.i: in good, bad, etc. ˈnick (BrE, informal)
4080.e: The bike's twenty years old but still in good nick.  这车有二十年了，可状况还很好。

4081.e: The ambulance arrived in the nick of time and saved him.  救护车在紧要关头赶到，救了他一命。

4082.e: He's tired of nickel-and-dime jobs and wants a real career.  他厌倦了这些赚小钱的零工，想有份正经事业。

4083.e: I'm having an early night; the alarm goes off at five.  我今晚早点睡，闹钟五点就响。

4084.e: The baby had a bad night, so nobody in the house slept.  宝宝夜里不安生，全家都没睡好。

4085.e: We only meant to have one drink, but we made a night of it.  本来只想喝一杯，结果玩了个通宵。

4086.i: ˌnight and ˈday • ˌday and ˈnight
4086.e: The builders worked night and day to finish before the rain came.  工人们日夜赶工，要在下雨前完工。

4087.e: Night night, sweetheart — I'll leave the hall light on.  晚安，宝贝，我把走廊的灯留着。

4088.e: They haven't had a night out together since the twins were born.  自从双胞胎出生，他俩就没一起出去玩过。

4089.e: She's a night owl and does her best writing after midnight.  她是个夜猫子，午夜后写得最好。

4090.e: That cat has nine lives — it fell three floors and walked away.  那猫命真大，从三楼摔下来还能自己走。

4091.cn: 昙花一现；轰动一时的人或事
4091.e: His scandal was a nine days wonder and then everyone forgot.  他那桩丑闻热闹了几天，之后就没人记得了。

4092.i: nine times out of ˈten (also ˌninety-nine ˌtimes out of a ˈhundred)
4092.e: Nine times out of ten the printer jams the moment I'm late.  十有八九我一赶时间打印机就卡纸。

4093.e: After ten years of nine to five, he quit and opened a bakery.  朝九晚五干了十年，他辞职开了家面包店。

4094.i: the ˌwhole ˌnine ˈyards (informal, especially AmE)
4094.e: They had a marquee, a band, fireworks — the whole nine yards.  他们搭了篷子、请了乐队、放了烟花，全套都来了。

4095.i: go down, drop, etc. like ˈninepins (informal)
4095.cn: （许多人）纷纷倒下（病倒或死亡）
4095.e: The flu hit the office and people went down like ninepins.  流感袭击了办公室，同事一个接一个地倒下。

4096.i: talk, etc. nineteen to the ˈdozen (BrE, informal)
4096.e: The two of them were talking nineteen to the dozen in the kitchen.  她俩在厨房里说个没完。

4097.cn: 把…扼杀在萌芽状态；防患未然
4097.e: Nip that rumour in the bud before the whole school hears it.  趁全校还没传开，赶紧把那谣言掐灭。

4098.e: I think the government's new proposal should be nipped in the bud.  我觉得政府的新提议应该趁早否掉。

4099.cn: 谈实质问题；讨论关键细节
4099.e: Enough small talk — let's get down to the nitty-gritty of the contract.  客套够了，我们来谈合同的实质内容吧。

4100.cn: 触及问题的本质；谈到要点
4100.e: We talked for an hour without really getting down to the nitty-gritty.  我们聊了一小时，也没真触及问题的核心。

4101.e: Her design finally got the nod from the planning committee.  她的设计终于得到了规划委员会的首肯。

4102.e: As soon as the boss gives us the nod, we'll start printing.  老板一点头，我们就开印。

4103.i: a ˌnod is as good as a ˈwink (to a ˈblind man) (saying)
4103.e: Say no more — a nod is as good as a wink.  别说了，我懂，一点就明白。

4104.e: The budget went through on the nod in under two minutes.  预算案不到两分钟就无异议通过了。

4105.i: be on ˈnodding terms with sb
4105.e: I'm only on nodding terms with my neighbours after five years here.  住了五年，我跟邻居也就是点头之交。

4106.i: have a nodding acˈquaintance with sb/sth
4106.cn: 与…是泛泛之交；对…略知一二
4106.e: I have a nodding acquaintance with Spanish, enough to order dinner.  我西班牙语略懂一点，够点个晚餐。

4107.e: After dark that estate became a no-go area even for the police.  天黑后那片小区连警察都不敢进。

4108.e: Residents made a lot of noise about the new car park and won.  居民对新停车场大闹了一通，最后赢了。

4109.e: We searched every nook and cranny and still couldn't find the keys.  我们把每个角落都翻遍了，还是没找到钥匙。

4110.e: As per usual, he turned up late and without his notes.  照例，他又迟到了，笔记也没带。

4111.i: cut off your ˈnose to spite your ˈface (informal)
4111.cn: 为泄愤反害自己；损人不利己
4111.e: Quitting to annoy your boss is cutting off your nose to spite your face.  为气老板而辞职，纯粹是害自己。

4112.i: cut off your ˈnose to spite your ˈface (informal)
4112.cn: 赌气伤己；因怒生怨反害自身
4112.e: Refusing their help just cuts off your nose to spite your face.  拒绝他们帮忙，只是跟自己过不去。

4113.e: His constant humming really gets up my nose during meetings.  开会时他老哼小曲，真让我烦。

4114.cn: 对…很敏感；有发现…的本事
4114.e: She has a nose for a bargain and never pays full price.  她对便宜货特别敏感，从不付全价。

4115.i: have your nose in a ˈbook, magaˈzine, etc. (informal)
4115.e: He sat all afternoon with his nose in a book about volcanoes.  他整个下午都埋头看一本讲火山的书。

4116.i: have your nose in a ˈbook, magaˈzine, etc. (informal)
4116.cn: 专心致志地看书（或杂志）
4116.e: She always has her nose in a magazine while waiting for the bus.  她等公交时总是埋头看杂志。

4117.e: The estate agent let us have a nose round the empty flat.  中介让我们在空公寓里四处看了看。

4118.e: Keep your nose clean for six months and you'll get the promotion.  安分守己半年，升职就是你的。

4119.i: keep your ˈnose out of sth (informal)
4119.e: Keep your nose out of my finances, thanks very much.  我的钱怎么花不劳你操心，谢谢。

4120.i: keep your ˌnose to the ˈgrindstone (informal)
4120.e: Keep your nose to the grindstone this term and the exams will look easy.  这学期埋头苦读，考试就不难了。

4121.i: look down your ˈnose (at sb/sth) (informal, especially BrE)
4121.e: She looks down her nose at anyone who shops in the market.  她瞧不起任何在集市买东西的人。

4122.e: The traffic was nose to tail all the way to the tunnel.  车辆首尾相接，一直堵到隧道口。

4123.e: Her estimate of the crowd size was right on the nose.  她对人数的估计分毫不差。

4124.i: put sb's ˈnose out of joint (informal)
4124.cn: 使某人难堪；让某人不痛快
4124.e: Giving the office to the newcomer put a few noses out of joint.  把办公室给了新人，惹得几个人心里不痛快。

4125.i: turn your ˈnose up at sth (informal)
4125.e: He turned his nose up at the sandwiches and ordered a steak instead.  他嫌那些三明治不上档次，改点了牛排。

4126.e: The keys were right under my nose on the hall table all along.  钥匙一直就在门厅桌上，我眼皮底下。

4127.i: with your ˈnose in the air (informal, disapproving)
4127.e: She walks past the whole team with her nose in the air.  她从全队面前走过，一副目中无人的样子。

4128.i: with your ˈnose in the air (informal, disapproving)
4128.e: He sat there with his nose in the air, ignoring everyone who spoke.  他坐在那儿一脸傲气，谁跟他说话都不理。

4129.i: not see beyond/past the end of your ˈnose
4129.e: Politicians who can't see beyond the end of their noses ruin long-term plans.  目光短浅的政客会毁掉长远规划。

4130.i: a ˌnosy ˈparker (BrE, informal, becoming old-fashioned)
4130.cn: 爱管闲事的人；好打听的人
4130.e: The nosy parker next door counts how many visitors we get.  隔壁那个爱管闲事的还数我们家来几个客人。

4131.e: His speech struck exactly the right note at such a sad occasion.  在那样悲伤的场合，他的致辞分寸拿捏得刚好。

4132.e: Nothing of note happened at the meeting apart from the free biscuits.  会上除了有免费饼干，没什么值得一提的事。

4133.e: The manager struck a note of caution about next year's sales.  经理对明年的销售表达了一丝谨慎。

4134.e: Take note of the exit doors before the film starts.  电影开演前先留意一下安全出口。

4135.i: be/have nothing to ˈdo with sb/sth
4135.e: Where I spend my weekends has nothing to do with my colleagues.  我周末去哪儿跟同事没有半点关系。

4136.i: be/have nothing to ˈdo with sb/sth
4136.e: She will have absolutely nothing to do with that organization any more.  她再也不想跟那个组织有任何牵连。

4137.e: My neighbour fixed the bike for nothing and refused a cup of tea.  邻居免费帮我修好了车，连茶都不肯喝。

4138.e: They were giving sweets away for nothing at the supermarket this morning.  今早超市在免费送糖果。

4139.cn: 远比不上某人；相形见绌
4139.e: My cooking has nothing on my grandmother's, and everyone knows it.  我做的菜远不如我外婆，大家都清楚。

4140.i: not for ˈnothing do I, will they, etc.
4140.cn: 并非没有理由；不是没道理
4140.e: Not for nothing is this street called the coldest place in town.  这条街被叫作全城最冷的地方，不是没道理的。

4141.e: For a week he ate nothing but rice and boiled eggs.  他整整一周只吃米饭和水煮蛋。

4142.e: Borrow the car for the whole weekend? Nothing doing.  借车用一整个周末？不行。

4143.e: His plan is nothing if not ambitious, whatever else you say about it.  不管别的怎么说，他的计划野心十足。

4144.e: Both runners finished together; there was nothing in it at all.  两名选手同时冲线，完全难分高下。

4145.e: Her recovery after the crash was nothing less than a miracle.  车祸后她的康复简直就是奇迹。

4146.e: The film is nothing like the book I read as a child.  这部电影跟我小时候读的那本书完全不一样。

4147.e: The whole argument was nothing more than a misunderstanding about money.  整场争吵只不过是钱上的一场误会。

4148.e: There's nothing much in the fridge except half a lemon.  冰箱里没什么东西，就剩半个柠檬。

4149.i: there's nothing (else) ˈfor it (but to do sth)
4149.e: The lift was broken, so there was nothing for it but to climb.  电梯坏了，只好爬楼梯。

4150.cn: 没有什么比得上…；…最好不过
4150.e: There's nothing like a hot shower after a day on the mountain.  在山上跑一天后，没什么比热水澡更舒服了。

4151.e: Once you've done it twice, there's nothing to it.  做过两次以后，这活儿一点都不难。

4152.e: The old villas are being bought up by the nouveau riche.  那些老别墅正被暴发户们买下。

4153.i: any minute, day, time, etc. ˈnow
4153.e: The results will be up on the website any minute now.  成绩随时会公布在网站上。

4154.e: As of now, nobody uses the back entrance without a pass.  从现在起，没有通行证谁都不许走后门。

4155.cn: 机不可失；就这一次机会
4155.e: The gallery closes on Sunday, so it's now or never.  画廊周日就闭馆了，机不可失。

4156.e: Every now and then we drive out to the coast for the day.  我们偶尔会开车去海边玩一天。

4157.e: She sat by the window, looking out now and then to see if they'd come.  她坐在窗边，不时向外张望看他们来了没有。

4158.cn: （转入新话题）下面轮到；接下来
4158.e: That's the weather done — and now for the sports headlines.  天气就说到这儿，接下来是体育要闻。

4159.e: The music was now loud, now barely a whisper, all evening long.  那音乐整晚时而高亢，时而轻若耳语。

4160.cn: 现在又怎么了；接下来该怎么办
4160.e: The engine's dead and the phone's flat — now what?  发动机熄火，手机也没电了，现在怎么办？

4161.cn: 不知第多少次；说过无数遍
4161.e: For the nth time, please take your boots off at the door.  第无数次说了，请在门口脱靴子。

4162.e: She plans every trip to the nth degree, right down to snacks.  她把每次旅行都规划到极致，连零食都算好。

4163.e: The artist prefers to paint her subjects in the nude.  这位画家更喜欢画裸体模特。

4164.i: ˌnudge ˈnudge, ˌwink ˈwink • a ˌnudge and a ˈwink
4164.e: He mentioned their 'business trip' with a nudge nudge, wink wink.  他提起他俩的“出差”时挤眉弄眼的。

4165.i: ˌnudge ˈnudge, ˌwink ˈwink • a ˌnudge and a ˈwink
4165.e: There was a nudge and a wink every time her name came up.  每次提到她的名字，大家就眉来眼去。

4166.e: Without both signatures the contract is null and void.  少了任何一方签字，合同就无效。

4167.i: do a ˈnumber on sb/sth (informal, especially AmE)
4167.e: That storm really did a number on our garden fence.  那场风暴把我们家院墙折腾得够呛。

4168.cn: 看透某人；摸清某人底细
4168.e: You can't fool her twice; she's had your number since day one.  你骗不了她第二次，她第一天就把你看透了。

4169.e: His lucky number came up and he finally got the flat he wanted.  他时来运转，终于买到了心仪的公寓。

4170.e: When the engine caught fire, he thought his number was up.  发动机着火时，他以为自己完了。

4171.cn: 头号人物；最重要的人或事
4171.e: In this house, the dog is number one and everyone knows it.  在这个家里，狗是老大，人人都知道。

4172.e: While the director travels, her number two runs the whole office.  主任出差时，整个办公室由她的二把手管。

4173.e: He teaches by numbers and never answers an interesting question.  他上课照本宣科，从不回答有意思的问题。

4174.cn: 严格照规矩办；一板一眼
4174.e: The inspection was done by the numbers, with no shortcuts anywhere.  这次检查完全照章办事，没有任何变通。

4175.cn: 数字游戏（只看数量不问实质）
4175.e: Hiring has become a numbers game rather than a search for talent.  招聘变成了数字游戏，而不是真的找人才。

4176.e: Dad will do his nut when he sees the scratch on the car.  爸看到车上的划痕会气炸的。

4177.cn: 棘手的难题；难对付的人
4177.e: Getting him to change his mind is a tough nut to crack.  想让他改主意可是块难啃的骨头。

4178.e: Swimming in that river in January? You're off your nut.  一月份还去那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。

4179.e: She understands the nuts and bolts of running a restaurant kitchen.  她懂得经营餐厅后厨的各种实际门道。

4180.cn: 基本知识；实际操作要点
4180.e: He worked there long enough to learn the nuts and bolts of the trade.  他在那儿干得够久，学会了这行的门道。

4181.e: In a nutshell, we spent too much and sold too little.  简而言之，我们花得太多，卖得太少。

4182.e: Her uncle is as nutty as a fruitcake, but everyone adores him.  她叔叔疯疯癫癫的，可人人都喜欢他。

4183.i: great/tall ˌoaks from little acorns ˈgrow (saying)
4183.cn: 合抱之木生于毫末；万事起于微末
4183.e: The shop began in her kitchen — great oaks from little acorns grow.  这家店最早只是她的厨房，万丈高楼平地起。

4184.e: We nearly agreed until his brother stuck his oar in.  我们差点谈妥了，结果他哥来横插一杠。

4185.e: The witness admitted under oath that he had lied to police.  证人在宣誓后承认曾向警方撒谎。

4186.e: He's been in a much better mood since he started getting his oats.  自从他有了固定的性生活，脾气好多了。

4187.i: money, ˌexpense, etc. is no ˈobject
4187.cn: 钱不成问题；费用不在话下
4187.e: Money is no object for that family when it comes to holidays.  在度假这件事上，那家人从来不心疼钱。

4188.cn: 可供借鉴的实例；活生生的教训
4188.e: His failed shop is an object lesson in ignoring your customers.  他倒闭的店铺是无视顾客的活教材。

4189.cn: 有理由做某事；有必要做
4189.e: I have had occasion to complain about that driver twice this month.  这个月我已经有两次不得不投诉那位司机。

4190.e: On occasion he still cooks the Sunday roast for the whole family.  他偶尔还会给全家做周日烤肉。

4191.i: an ocean of sth (BrE also oceans of sth)
4191.e: There's an ocean of paperwork waiting on my desk tomorrow.  明天我桌上等着一大堆文件。

4192.e: He does odd jobs around the village for a bit of extra cash.  他在村里干点零活，赚些外快。

4193.cn: 与众不同的人（或物）；多余的一个
4193.e: In a family of doctors, the musician was always the odd one out.  在一家子医生里，那个搞音乐的总显得格格不入。

4194.i: an odd/a queer ˈfish (BrE, becoming old-fashioned)
4194.e: The new caretaker is an odd fish, but he keeps the place spotless.  新来的管理员是个怪人，不过把楼里打理得一尘不染。

4195.cn: 尽管困难重重；出人意料地
4195.e: Against all the odds, the little team reached the national final.  这支小球队克服重重困难打进了全国决赛。

4196.e: His account of the evening is at odds with what the neighbours saw.  他对那晚的说法与邻居所见不符。

4197.i: it makes no ˈodds (to sb/sth) (spoken, especially BrE)
4197.e: Tea or coffee — it makes no odds to me.  茶还是咖啡，我都无所谓。

4198.i: ˌodds and ˈends (BrE also ˌodds and ˈsods)
4198.cn: 零碎物品；杂七杂八的东西
4198.e: The drawer is full of odds and ends we never use.  抽屉里塞满了我们从不用的零碎东西。

4199.e: The odds are that she'll be late again, so order without her.  她十有八九又要迟到，别等她点吧。

4200.i: the odds are aˈgainst sth/sb doing sth
4200.e: The odds are against us finishing the roof before winter.  我们赶在冬天前修好屋顶希望不大。

4201.e: We paid well over the odds for the flat because of the location.  因为地段好，我们买这套公寓多花了不少钱。

4202.cn: 那有什么关系；有什么要紧
4202.e: So we arrive an hour late — what's the odds?  就算晚到一小时，那又怎么样？

4203.cn: 夺冠热门；最被看好的人选
4203.e: She's the odds-on favourite to win Saturday's race.  她是周六比赛夺冠的大热门。

4204.e: He's in bad odour with the head after missing three deadlines.  连误三次期限后，他在主管那儿很不受待见。

4205.cn: 某物有…数量；某物的储备情况
4205.e: How are we off for milk before I go to the shop?  我去商店前问一下，牛奶还剩多少？

4206.i: ˌoff and ˈon • ˌon and ˈoff
4206.e: It rained off and on all afternoon, so we stayed indoors.  整个下午断断续续下雨，我们就待在屋里。

4207.i: take ofˈfence (at sth) (BrE) (AmE take ofˈfense (at sth))
4207.e: Don't take offence, but that jacket really doesn't suit you.  别生气啊，那件夹克真的不适合你。

4208.e: No offence, but your singing woke the whole street.  无意冒犯，可你的歌声吵醒了整条街。

4209.e: The company has been on the offensive since the story broke.  消息曝光后，公司一直在主动反击。

4210.i: go on(to) the ofˈfensive • take the ofˈfensive
4210.e: After half-time the team went on the offensive and scored twice.  下半场球队转守为攻，连进两球。

4211.i: go on(to) the ofˈfensive • take the ofˈfensive
4211.e: Her lawyers took the offensive and sued the newspaper first.  她的律师先发制人，抢先起诉了那家报社。

4212.e: The town has plenty to offer families with young children.  这座小城为有小孩的家庭提供了不少去处。

4213.cn: 可买到的；提供的；在特价出售
4213.e: There were three jobs on offer, all of them badly paid.  有三份工作可选，但薪水都很低。

4214.e: The cottage went under offer within a week of being listed.  那栋小屋挂牌一周内就有人出价了。

4215.cn: 经某人斡旋；承某人帮忙
4215.e: Through the good offices of a friend, we got a table at the restaurant.  多亏一位朋友帮忙，我们在那家餐厅订到了位子。

4216.e: There are big changes in the offing at head office.  总部即将有大变动。

4217.e: Every so often she rings just to check that we're all right.  她时不时打个电话来，看看我们好不好。

4218.i: (as) ˌoften as ˈnot • more ˌoften than ˈnot
4218.e: More often than not, the bus arrives before I reach the stop.  多半情况下，我还没到站公交就先到了。

4219.e: He's no oil painting, but he's the kindest man I know.  他长得一般，却是我认识的最善良的人。

4220.i: oil the ˈwheels (BrE) (AmE grease the ˈwheels)
4220.cn: 疏通关系；使事情顺利进行
4220.e: A good lunch can oil the wheels of any difficult negotiation.  一顿好饭能让再难的谈判都顺畅些。

4221.e: Since the second shop opened, they're doing okay for money.  第二家店开张后，他们经济上过得挺宽裕。

4222.cn: 生意兴隆；日子过得不错
4222.e: They're doing more than okay with those new restaurants downtown.  他们市中心那几家新餐馆生意好得很。

4223.e: We can start digging as soon as the council gives us the okay.  市政厅一批准，我们就能开挖。

4224.e: Someone called the Old Bill when the shouting started.  一开始吵嚷，就有人报了警。

4225.e: He'd thrown his clothes into the case any old how.  他把衣服胡乱塞进了箱子。

4226.i: ˈany old thing, time, place, etc. (spoken)
4226.e: Come round any old time; there's always someone at home.  你随时来都行，家里总有人。

4227.cn: 看在旧日情分上；念及老交情
4227.e: Let's walk home the long way, for old times' sake.  看在从前的份上，我们绕远路走回去吧。

4228.e: Grandad still talks about the good old days before the mine closed.  爷爷还常说起矿场关闭前的好日子。

4229.cn: 又是老一套；老问题又来了
4229.e: It's the same old story: big promises and no funding.  又是老一套：大话说尽，钱一分没有。

4230.e: The knights of old would have ridden through this very valley.  昔日的骑士想必就是穿过这道山谷的。

4231.e: He's a teacher of the old school and still marks in red ink.  他是位老派教师，至今还用红笔批改。

4232.e: That joke is as old as the hills and still nobody laughs.  那个笑话老掉牙了，还是没人笑。

4233.e: Don't call her an old bag; she's only sixty and very sharp.  别叫她老婆子，她才六十，脑子灵光得很。

4234.e: The old bat next door complains every time we play music.  隔壁那老太太一听我们放音乐就投诉。

4235.cn: 老兄；老姐；年长的男子或妇女
4235.e: The old boy next door still cycles to the market every single morning.  隔壁那位老先生每天早上还骑车去市场。

4236.cn: 校友关系网；老同学之间的互相关照
4236.e: He got that job through the old boy network, not because of his skills.  他靠校友关系拿到那份工作，根本不是凭本事。

4237.e: Not that old chestnut about your fishing trip again — we've heard it twice.  别又讲你钓鱼那个老段子了，我们都听两遍了。

4238.e: An old dear on the bus insisted on giving my daughter a boiled sweet.  公交车上一位老太太非要给我女儿一颗水果糖。

4239.e: She bumped into an old flame at the wedding and blushed all evening.  她在婚礼上碰见旧情人，整晚脸都红着。

4240.e: My dad calls himself an old fogey because he refuses to use a smartphone.  我爸不肯用智能手机，自称是个老顽固。

4241.cn: 保守派；元老派；保守势力
4241.e: The old guard on the committee blocked every idea the new members proposed.  委员会里的元老派否决了新成员提出的每个想法。

4242.i: an old ˈhand (at sth/at doing sth)
4242.e: Ask Wei to fix it — he's an old hand at repairing these old engines.  找小魏修吧，他修这种老发动机是老手。

4243.e: Fax machines are old hat now; nobody in this office uses one.  传真机早就过时了，办公室里没人再用。

4244.i: (have) an ˌold head on young ˈshoulders
4244.cn: 少年老成；年轻而有见识
4244.e: At sixteen she handled the crisis calmly — an old head on young shoulders.  才十六岁就能冷静处理危机，真是少年老成。

4245.e: In those days people cruelly called any unmarried woman over thirty an old maid.  那年头，过了三十还没结婚的女人都被刻薄地叫作老姑娘。

4246.e: My old man taught me to drive in an empty car park one Sunday.  我老爸在一个周日的空停车场里教我开车。

4247.cn: 私立学校校友之间的互助情谊
4247.e: Promotion here still depends on the old school tie rather than actual results.  这里的升迁靠的还是校友关系，不是实际业绩。

4248.e: Going out with wet hair causes colds? That's just an old wives' tale.  湿着头发出门会感冒？那不过是无稽之谈。

4249.cn: 老婆；老妈；婆婆妈妈的人
4249.e: Stop fussing about the curtains — you're being a real old woman today.  别为窗帘瞎操心了，你今天真够婆婆妈妈的。

4250.i: a chip off the old ˈblock (informal)
4250.cn: 酷似父母的人；一个模子刻出来的
4250.e: He argues about football just like his dad — a chip off the old block.  他争论足球的样子活脱脱他爸，真是一个模子刻出来的。

4251.i: hold out/offer an ˈolive branch (to sb)
4251.cn: 伸出橄榄枝；表示愿意和好
4251.e: After weeks of silence, she offered an olive branch by inviting him to dinner.  沉默数周后，她请他吃饭，算是伸出了橄榄枝。

4252.e: He made a cheese omelette for supper because the fridge was almost empty.  冰箱快空了，他就做了个奶酪蛋饼当晚饭。

4253.i: you can't make an omelette without breaking ˈeggs (saying)
4253.cn: 不花代价难成大事；有得必有失
4253.e: Layoffs are painful, but you can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.  裁员很痛苦，但不破不立，总得付出代价。

4254.e: What on earth are you on about? I can't follow your story at all.  你到底在说什么？我完全听不懂你讲的事。

4255.cn: 唠叨没完；喋喋不休地抱怨
4255.e: He keeps on about the noisy neighbours every time we visit his flat.  我们每次去他家，他都唠叨邻居太吵。

4256.i: be/go/keep ˈon at sb (to do sth) (informal, disapproving)
4256.cn: 对某人唠叨；喋喋不休地催促
4256.e: My mum keeps on at me to tidy my room before the guests arrive.  我妈一直唠叨要我在客人来之前收拾房间。

4257.e: Turning up two hours late without calling is just not on.  迟到两小时还不打个电话，这实在不能接受。

4258.cn: 连续不停地；没完没了地
4258.e: The lecturer talked on and on while half the students quietly dozed off.  那讲师没完没了地讲，一半学生悄悄睡着了。

4259.e: All at once the lights went out and the whole street fell silent.  忽然间灯全灭了，整条街都安静下来。

4260.e: Put the phone down and come here at once — this is urgent.  放下电话马上过来，这事很急。

4261.e: For once, let me pay the bill — you've treated me all month.  就这一次让我买单吧，你请了我一个月了。

4262.e: Once again the train was delayed, and we missed the connecting flight.  火车又一次晚点，我们错过了转机航班。

4263.cn: 一次为…便永远是…（本性难改）
4263.e: Once a cheat, always a cheat — I wouldn't trust him with money.  一次骗人，终身骗人，钱的事我不会信他。

4264.cn: 一劳永逸地；彻底地；最终
4264.e: Let's settle this argument once and for all and never mention it again.  咱们一劳永逸地了结这场争论，以后别再提。

4265.cn: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳
4265.e: He won't lend money to friends now — once bitten, twice shy.  他现在不借钱给朋友了，一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳。

4266.e: My brother phones home once in a blue moon, usually when he needs money.  我弟弟难得往家里打电话，通常是缺钱的时候。

4267.e: Every once in a while we drive to the coast just to see the sea.  我们偶尔开车去海边，就为看看大海。

4268.e: I've met her once or twice at conferences, but we never really talked.  我在会上见过她一两次，但没真正聊过。

4269.cn: 屡犯而终遭报应；这次没能幸免
4269.e: He cheated on the test once too often and was finally expelled.  他考试作弊次数太多，终于被开除了。

4270.e: Once upon a time this quiet village had three pubs and a cinema.  很久以前，这个安静的村子有三家酒馆和一间电影院。

4271.e: The mechanic gave my car the once-over and said the brakes needed work.  修理工把我的车草草检查了一遍，说刹车得修。

4272.e: The crowd rose as one when the injured player walked back onto the pitch.  受伤球员重回球场时，观众齐刷刷地站了起来。

4273.e: Sitting by the lake at dawn, he felt completely at one with nature.  黎明时坐在湖边，他觉得自己与自然融为一体。

4274.i: be (a) one for sth/for doing sth (informal)
4274.e: She's a great one for organizing surprise parties at the last minute.  她特别喜欢临时张罗惊喜派对。

4275.e: Finishing the report early got her one up on the rest of the team.  提前交报告让她比组里其他人略胜一筹。

4276.cn: 胜人一筹的伎俩；争强好胜
4276.e: Their constant upmanship about holidays and cars makes dinner parties exhausting.  他们总在假期和车子上比来比去，饭局累人。

4277.cn: 我（或你等）就是其中之一
4277.e: I for one think the new schedule is far better than the old mess.  我个人认为新排班比原先那一团乱强多了。

4278.cn: 占某人便宜；捉弄某人；胜过
4278.e: He loves getting one over on his brother at cards every Christmas.  他每年圣诞打牌都爱赢他哥一把。

4279.i: (you've, he's, etc.) got it in ˈone (informal)
4279.cn: 一下子就猜到；一下子明白
4279.e: You think she's quitting to travel? You've got it in one.  你猜她辞职是想去旅行？一下就猜中了。

4280.i: (you've, he's, etc.) got it in ˈone (informal)
4280.e: So you're resigning, Dick? Got it in one, boss.  这么说你要辞职了，迪克？您一下就猜到了，老板。

4281.e: He'd clearly had one too many, so we took his car keys away.  他显然喝多了，我们就把他车钥匙收走了。

4282.e: This gadget is a torch, radio and phone charger in one.  这个小玩意儿集手电、收音机和充电器于一身。

4283.i: it's a hundred, etc. to ˈone that sb/sth will (not) do sth
4283.cn: 几乎可以肯定会（或不会）发生
4283.e: It's a hundred to one that he'll forget her birthday again this year.  几乎可以肯定他今年又会忘了她的生日。

4284.e: One after another the guests made excuses and slipped quietly out.  客人们一个接一个找借口悄悄溜走了。

4285.e: Good evening one and all, and welcome to our little village concert.  各位晚上好，欢迎来到我们的小村音乐会。

4286.cn: 唯一的；独一无二的；大名鼎鼎的
4286.e: Please welcome the one and only Amy Chen to the stage tonight.  今晚请欢迎独一无二的陈艾米登台。
