4287.e: The quiet gardener and the famous poet turned out to be one and the same.  那个安静的园丁和著名诗人原来是同一个人。

4288.e: One by one the candles went out until the room was dark.  蜡烛一根接一根熄灭，房间终于全黑了。

4289.i: when you've seen, heard, etc. ˈone, you've seen, heard, etc. them ˈall (saying)
4289.cn: 见过一个就等于都见过；大同小异
4289.e: When you've seen one of these shopping malls, you've seen them all.  这种商场看过一个，其余的也就都一样了。

4290.i: when you've seen, heard, etc. ˈone, you've seen, heard, etc. them ˈall (saying)
4290.cn: 见过一个就都见过了；大同小异
4290.e: Once you've seen one of his films, you've seen them all.  他的电影看过一部，其他的也就那样了。

4291.cn: 毫无悬念的比赛；只有一方可能获胜
4291.e: With their star striker back, the league became a one-horse race.  头号前锋回归后，联赛就成了毫无悬念的角逐。

4292.e: He grew up in a one-horse town with a single shop and no cinema.  他在一个只有一家小店、没有影院的偏僻小镇长大。

4293.e: She insisted it was just a one-night stand and nothing more serious.  她坚称那只是一夜情，没什么别的。

4294.cn: 一次性的事物；绝无仅有的事物
4294.e: This discount is a one-off, so don't expect it again next month.  这个折扣只有一次，别指望下个月还有。

4295.cn: 一门心思只想一件事；思路狭隘
4295.e: During exam season he has a one-track mind and talks only about revision.  考试季他一门心思只想复习，别的什么都不聊。

4296.e: She not only cooked dinner but also cleaned the whole kitchen afterwards.  她不但做了晚饭，之后还把厨房全打扫了。

4297.e: I'll go to the party only if you promise to drive me home.  只有你答应送我回家，我才去这个派对。

4298.e: Only if the red light comes on are the workers in any danger.  只有红灯亮起时，工人们才会有危险。

4299.e: We only just caught the last bus home after the concert ended.  音乐会散场后，我们刚好赶上末班车。

4300.e: He rushed to the station only to find the train had already left.  他赶到车站，结果发现火车已经开走了。

4301.i: only too ˈglad, ˈready, etc. (to do sth)
4301.e: She was only too glad to lend us her flat for the weekend.  她非常乐意把公寓借给我们过周末。

4302.cn: 得到某人的支持；争取某人站在自己一边
4302.e: We need to get the finance team onside before we present the plan.  提交方案前我们得先争取到财务部门的支持。

4303.cn: 察觉某人的错事；盯上某人
4303.e: The police are onto him after that suspicious bank transfer last week.  上周那笔可疑转账之后，警方已经盯上他了。

4304.cn: 发现有价值的东西；有了眉目
4304.e: I think we're onto something big with this new battery design.  我觉得这个新电池设计让我们有了重大发现。

4305.cn: 愿意考虑某事；易受…影响
4305.e: The boss says she's open to suggestions about changing our working hours.  老板说她愿意听取关于调整工时的建议。

4306.e: Keep an open mind about the new manager until you've actually worked with him.  在真正共事之前，对新经理别抱成见。

4307.e: The scandal finally came out into the open when a nurse spoke to reporters.  一名护士向记者开口后，丑闻终于公之于众。

4308.e: We ate breakfast in the open air, watching mist rise off the lake.  我们在户外吃早饭，看着湖面升起薄雾。

4309.e: The painting would fetch millions if it were sold on the open market.  这幅画若在公开市场出售，能卖到几百万。

4310.cn: 极坦率的人；一目了然的事
4310.e: My little sister is an open book — you can read her face instantly.  我妹妹是本打开的书，看脸就知道她想什么。

4311.e: That internship opened the door to a career in publishing for her.  那次实习为她打开了出版业的职业大门。

4312.e: Working in the shelter opened my eyes to how many families struggle.  在收容所工作让我看清有多少家庭在苦苦挣扎。

4313.e: The soldiers were ordered not to open fire unless they were attacked first.  士兵接到命令，除非先遭攻击否则不得开火。

4314.cn: 打开闸门；放开限制引发大量涌入
4314.e: Cutting the fee would open the floodgates to thousands of new applicants.  降低费用会引来成千上万的新申请者。

4315.e: After a second glass of wine she opened her heart to me about her divorce.  喝到第二杯酒，她向我倾诉了离婚的事。

4316.cn: 热情好客；随时欢迎客人来访
4316.e: My grandparents kept open house every Sunday, and neighbours just walked in.  我祖父母每周日都门户大开，邻居们径直就进来了。

4317.cn: 随时欢迎来访的邀请；诱人犯罪的可乘之机
4317.e: Leaving your laptop on the seat is an open invitation to thieves.  把笔记本电脑放在座位上等于给小偷发请帖。

4318.e: Hundreds of scientists signed an open letter urging the government to act.  数百名科学家联署公开信，敦促政府采取行动。

4319.e: Why did you open your big mouth about the surprise party?  你干嘛多嘴把惊喜派对说出去？

4320.i: an ˌopen ˈquestion (also ˌopen to ˈquestion)
4320.cn: 悬而未决的问题；有待商榷
4320.e: Whether the policy actually saves money remains an open question.  这项政策是否真能省钱，仍是个悬而未决的问题。

4321.e: It's an open secret that the two managers can't stand each other.  那两位经理互相看不顺眼，这是公开的秘密。

4322.cn: 芝麻开门；打开门路的法宝
4322.e: A good reference from her seems to be the open sesame in this industry.  在这行，她的一封推荐信似乎就是芝麻开门。

4323.i: open the ˈway for sb/sth (to do sth)
4323.cn: 为…开辟道路；开方便之门
4323.e: The treaty opened the way for trade between the two countries to resume.  这项条约为两国恢复贸易铺平了道路。

4324.cn: 张开双臂热情欢迎；诚挚地
4324.e: The village welcomed the new doctor with open arms and homemade cakes.  村里张开双臂欢迎新医生，还端来自制蛋糕。

4325.cn: 一目了然的；显而易见的
4325.e: The lawyer said the dispute was open-and-shut and would not reach court.  律师说这场纠纷一目了然，不会闹上法庭。

4326.e: With three witnesses and a video, it's an open-and-shut case.  有三名证人加一段录像，这案子一目了然。

4327.e: For openers, tell me exactly where you were on Friday night.  首先，告诉我周五晚上你到底在哪里。

4328.e: The new parking rules come into operation at the start of next month.  新的停车规定将于下月初开始生效。

4329.cn: 在运转中；在使用中；有效
4329.e: Only two of the four lifts are in operation while repairs continue.  维修期间四部电梯只有两部在运行。

4330.e: The council will put the recycling scheme into operation in June.  市政会将于六月启动这项回收计划。

4331.e: He said he'd try to help — and 'try' is the operative word here.  他说会尽量帮忙，这里的关键词是「尽量」。

4332.e: The committee is of the opinion that the current rules need urgent revision.  委员会认为现行规则亟需修订。

4333.i: have a good, bad, high, low, etc. oˈpinion of sb/sth
4333.e: She has a very high opinion of her new assistant's writing skills.  她对新助理的写作能力评价很高。

4334.e: In my considered opinion, we should delay the launch until spring.  依我深思熟虑后的看法，我们该把发布推迟到春天。

4335.e: This job is a rare opportunity to work abroad with a great team.  这份工作是难得的机会，能和优秀团队在国外共事。

4336.e: We want steady growth, as opposed to a quick profit this quarter.  我们要的是稳定增长，而不是这个季度的快钱。

4337.cn: 职位对等的人；对口人员
4337.e: Our sales director met her opposite number from the Japanese firm.  我们的销售总监会见了那家日企的对口负责人。

4338.e: At fourteen he was suddenly shy around members of the opposite sex.  十四岁那年，他在异性面前忽然变得腼腆。

4339.cn: 异性相吸；性格相反的人互相吸引
4339.e: She's loud and he's quiet, but opposites attract, I suppose.  她外向他内向，不过大概真是性格相反才互相吸引吧。

4340.e: Thousands marched in opposition to the plan to close the hospital.  数千人游行，反对关闭医院的计划。

4341.cn: 轻松的选择；避重就轻的做法
4341.e: Dropping the difficult module would be the easy option, but you'd regret it.  放弃那门难课是省事的选择，但你会后悔。

4342.cn: 保留选择余地；暂不作决定
4342.e: He's applied to three universities to keep his options open.  他申请了三所大学，好保留选择余地。

4343.cn: （文件）有效合法；井然有序；适宜
4343.e: The inspector checked our passports and said everything was in order.  检查员查了护照，说一切都没问题。

4344.i: in/of the ˈorder of (BrE) (AmE on the ˈorder of) (formal)
4344.e: Repairs will cost something in the order of five thousand pounds.  修理费大约在五千英镑上下。

4345.e: We left at dawn in order that we might reach the border by noon.  我们黎明出发，以便中午前抵达边境。

4346.e: She took a second job in order to pay off her student loan.  为了还清助学贷款，她又找了份兼职。

4347.i: of the highest/first ˈorder ◆ of a high ˈorder
4347.e: His performance last night was showmanship of the highest order.  他昨晚的表演是第一流的舞台功夫。

4348.e: The parts are on order and should arrive by the end of the week.  零件已经订了，本周末前应该能到。

4349.cn: 当时盛行的做法；应时之举
4349.e: During the heatwave, cold drinks and short meetings were the order of the day.  热浪期间，冷饮和短会成了常态。

4350.cn: 出故障；不合规矩；次序颠倒
4350.e: The coffee machine is out of order again, so we walked to the café.  咖啡机又坏了，我们只好走去咖啡馆。

4351.cn: 担任圣职；成为神职人员
4351.e: He gave up law and took holy orders at the age of forty.  他四十岁放弃律师工作，接受了圣职。

4352.e: The guards were under orders to let nobody past the gate.  卫兵奉命不许任何人通过大门。

4353.e: After turning up drunk twice, he finally got his marching orders.  醉着上了两次班后，他终于被炒了鱿鱼。

4354.e: In the ordinary way I'd walk, but the rain is far too heavy.  换作平常我会走路，可今天雨太大了。

4355.e: Did you notice anything out of the ordinary on the night of the fire?  失火那晚你有没有注意到什么反常的事？

4356.e: She goes to the gym every other day, usually before breakfast.  她每隔一天去一次健身房，通常在早饭前。

4357.cn: 前不久的一天（或一个上午等）
4357.e: I ran into your cousin at the market the other day.  前几天我在市场上碰见你表弟了。

4358.e: Nobody other than the manager can unlock the safe in here.  除了经理，这里没人能打开保险柜。

4359.e: She's gone off to Spain or somewhere or other for the winter.  她跑去西班牙还是哪儿过冬了。

4360.e: Her calmness, real or otherwise, kept the whole team from panicking.  她的镇定，无论真假，让整个团队没有慌乱。

4361.i: be (all) out to do sth ◆ be (all) out for sth
4361.cn: 一心想做某事；全力以赴争取
4361.e: That newspaper is all out to ruin his reputation before the election.  那家报纸一心想在选举前毁掉他的名声。

4362.e: After three weeks in bed she's finally out and about again.  卧床三周后，她终于又能出门走动了。

4363.cn: 神志不清；昏昏然；被冷落
4363.e: He was completely out of it after the painkillers and slept all afternoon.  吃了止痛药他整个人昏昏沉沉，睡了一下午。

4364.e: Her fashion ideas are a bit out there, but the crowd loved them.  她的时装想法有点怪，但观众很喜欢。

4365.e: You've been sulking all morning — come on, out with it!  你整个上午都绷着脸，快说出来吧！

4366.e: From the outset of the trip we knew the weather would be terrible.  旅行一开始我们就知道天气会很糟。

4367.e: The whole job will take three hours at the outside.  这活儿最多也就三个小时。

4368.e: On the outside he seemed calm, but his hands were shaking badly.  他表面镇定，可双手抖得厉害。

4369.i: the ˌoutside ˈworld ◆ the world outˈside
4369.e: The monks have almost no contact with the outside world all winter.  整个冬天，僧侣们几乎与外界没有联系。

4370.cn: 非某人所能理解；超出某人的知识范围
4370.e: How the software actually works is completely beyond my ken.  这软件到底怎么运作，我完全搞不懂。

4371.e: The file was deleted, so I had to type the whole report over again.  文件被删了，我只好把报告从头再打一遍。

4372.e: He gets a big annual bonus over and above his basic salary.  除了基本工资，他每年还有一笔丰厚的年终奖。

4373.e: I'll have two eggs over easy and a slice of brown toast.  我要两个两面煎的蛋，加一片全麦吐司。

4374.e: He overshot the mark by promising results nobody could possibly deliver.  他许诺了根本没人做得到的结果，说得太过了。

4375.e: Joking about her weight really overstepped the mark this time.  拿她的体重开玩笑，这次真的过分了。

4376.cn: （想象力等）异常活跃；超负荷运转
4376.e: Her imagination was working overtime after she heard those strange noises.  听到那些怪声后，她的想象力就开始过度活跃了。

4377.e: The company's friendly overtures were met with complete silence from the union.  公司友好的表示换来了工会的沉默。

4378.e: His clumsy romantic overtures made everyone at the table uncomfortable.  他笨拙的示爱让在座的人都很尴尬。

4379.cn: 主动接近某人；向某人示好
4379.e: The rebels made overtures to the government about a possible ceasefire.  叛军主动向政府示好，商谈停火的可能。

4380.cn: 得以充分发挥；有用武之地
4380.e: A four-wheel drive really comes into its own on these muddy tracks.  在这些泥泞小路上，四驱车才真正派上用场。

4381.e: She got her own back on him by telling everyone his embarrassing nickname.  她把他难堪的绰号说给所有人听，算是报了仇。

4382.e: He built that whole shed on his own in a single weekend.  那整间小棚子是他一个周末独自搭起来的。

4383.cn: 一切皆有可能；天地任你闯
4383.e: You're twenty-two with a degree — the world is your oyster.  你二十二岁又有学位，天地任你闯。

4384.cn: 考验某人的能力；测试某物的性能
4384.e: The coach put the new goalkeeper through his paces for two hours.  教练把新守门员操练了整整两小时。

4385.cn: 处于领先位置；抢先于对手
4385.e: Investing in solar early kept the firm ahead of the pack.  早早投资太阳能让这家公司领先同行。

4386.cn: 收拾东西走人；永远离开
4386.e: After that row with his boss he packed his bags and quit.  和老板大吵一架后，他收拾东西辞职了。

4387.e: Pack it in, you two — I can't hear the phone over your shouting.  你们俩别闹了，你们一嚷我听不见电话。

4388.e: His story about missing the train was a pack of lies.  他说错过火车那套说辞完全是一派谎言。

4389.e: For such a small speaker, this thing really packs a punch.  这么小的音箱，声音出奇地有劲。

4390.i: ˌpack them ˈin ◆ ˌpack the ˈhouse
4390.cn: 吸引大批观众；场场爆满
4390.e: That comedian still packs them in at theatres across the country.  那位喜剧演员在全国各地剧场依然场场爆满。

4391.i: ˌpack them ˈin ◆ ˌpack the ˈhouse
4391.cn: 吸引大批观众；座无虚席
4391.e: This group's been playing for twenty years and they still pack the house.  这支乐队演了二十年，场子照样爆满。

4392.cn: 挤得像沙丁鱼罐头；拥挤不堪
4392.e: We stood packed like sardines on the last train out of the city.  我们挤在末班车上，像沙丁鱼罐头一样。

4393.i: make, lose, spend, etc. a ˈpacket (informal)
4393.e: He made a packet selling his flat just before prices dropped.  他赶在房价跌前卖掉公寓，赚了一大笔。

4394.i: be on the same ˈpage (especially AmE)
4394.e: Let's meet Monday to make sure everyone is on the same page.  周一碰个头，确保大家想法一致。

4395.e: A broken ankle put paid to his hopes of running the marathon.  脚踝骨折让他跑马拉松的希望化为泡影。

4396.cn: 已缴费的会员；铁杆成员
4396.e: She's a fully paid-up member of the local cycling club now.  她现在是本地骑行俱乐部的正式会员了。

4397.e: Workers were forbidden to discuss the case on pain of dismissal.  员工不得讨论此案，违者解雇。

4398.i: a ˌpain in the ˈneck (BrE also a ˌpain in the ˈarse△/ˈbum/ˈbackside) (AmE also a ˌpain in the ˈass△/ˈbutt) (informal)
4398.e: Filling in these forms every month is a real pain in the neck.  每月填这些表格实在烦人。

4399.i: be at (great) ˈpains to do sth
4399.cn: 煞费苦心地做某事；竭力
4399.e: He was at great pains to explain that the delay wasn't his fault.  他费尽口舌解释延误不是他的错。

4400.i: for your ˈpains (especially BrE, often ironic)
4400.e: I helped him move house all weekend and got a cold coffee for my pains.  我帮他搬了整个周末的家，回报是一杯凉咖啡。

4401.i: take (great) ˈpains with sth/to do sth
4401.cn: 煞费苦心；尽心竭力做某事
4401.e: She took great pains with the wedding invitations, writing each one by hand.  她在婚礼请柬上下足功夫，每张都手写。

4402.i: go to great ˈpains to do sth
4402.cn: 尽心竭力地做某事；小心谨慎地做
4402.e: The chef goes to great pains to source every vegetable locally.  这位厨师费尽心思，所有蔬菜都从本地采购。

4403.i: paint a terrible, depressing, rosy, etc. ˈpicture (of sb/sth)
4403.cn: 把…描绘得很糟糕（或美好）
4403.e: The report paints a depressing picture of housing conditions in the city.  报告把这座城市的住房状况描绘得十分令人沮丧。

4404.i: paint a terrible, depressing, rosy, etc. ˈpicture (of sb/sth)
4404.cn: 以某种方式描绘；给人某种印象
4404.e: His letters painted a rosy picture of life abroad that wasn't true.  他的信把国外生活描绘得很美好，其实并非如此。

4405.e: After finals we painted the town red and stumbled home at dawn.  期末考完我们出去尽情狂欢，天亮才跌跌撞撞回家。

4406.i: paint sth with a ˌbroad ˈbrush
4406.cn: 粗线条描绘；大致地描述
4406.e: The minister painted the reforms with a broad brush and dodged details.  部长只是粗线条地讲了改革，回避了细节。

4407.i: be like painting the Forth ˈBridge (BrE)
4407.cn: （工作）没完没了；做完又得重来
4407.e: Tidying up after three kids is like painting the Forth Bridge.  给三个孩子收拾东西，简直没完没了。

4408.i: I've only got one pair of ˈhands (spoken)
4408.cn: 我只有一双手；实在忙不过来
4408.e: Wait your turn — I've only got one pair of hands here!  等等，我只有一双手，忙不过来！

4409.e: We need an extra pair of hands in the kitchen on Saturday nights.  周六晚上厨房需要多一个帮手。

4410.e: The children walked to the museum in pairs, holding hands tightly.  孩子们两人一组紧牵着手走去博物馆。

4411.e: He answered the door in his pajamas at two in the afternoon.  下午两点他还穿着睡衣去开门。

4412.cn: 出格；越轨；令人无法容忍
4412.e: Shouting at the waiter like that was completely beyond the pale.  那样冲服务员吼叫实在太过分了。

4413.i: ˈpale beside/next to sth ◆ ˈpale in/by comparison (with sth)
4413.cn: 相形见绌；相比之下逊色
4413.e: My cooking pales beside my grandmother's, but I keep practising.  我的厨艺跟奶奶比相形见绌，但我一直在练。

4414.i: have sb in the ˌpalm of your ˈhand
4414.cn: 完全控制某人；把某人攥在手心
4414.e: Within ten minutes the speaker had the audience in the palm of her hand.  不到十分钟，演讲者就把听众牢牢抓住了。

4415.e: Two years of research went down the pan when the funding stopped.  资金一断，两年的研究全打了水漂。

4416.e: Their first hit turned out to be a flash in the pan.  他们的首支热门歌曲结果只是昙花一现。

4417.cn: 潘多拉的盒子；灾祸之源
4417.e: Asking about their family history opened a real Pandora's box.  一问起他们的家史，等于打开了潘多拉的盒子。

4418.e: It was panic stations in the kitchen when forty guests arrived early.  四十位客人提早到，厨房里顿时乱成一团。

4419.e: Don't push the panic button just because sales dipped for one month.  只不过一个月销量下滑，别慌了手脚。

4420.i: scare, bore, etc. the ˈpants off sb (informal)
4420.e: That horror film scared the pants off my little brother.  那部恐怖片把我弟弟吓坏了。

4421.e: On paper the plan looks perfect, but nobody has tested it yet.  这计划纸面上很完美，可还没人试过。

4422.cn: 掩饰问题或分歧；权且遮掩
4422.e: The apology just papered over the cracks in their friendship.  那句道歉不过是掩盖了他们友情中的裂痕。

4423.cn: 纸老虎；外强中干的人或事物
4423.e: Their new competitor turned out to be a paper tiger with no real funding.  他们的新对手原来是只纸老虎，根本没有资金。

4424.e: His performance was below par all season after that knee injury.  膝伤之后，他整个赛季状态都不如平常。

4425.i: be on a ˈpar with sb/sth
4425.e: The local bakery's bread is on a par with anything in Paris.  这家本地面包店的面包不输巴黎的任何一家。

4426.e: Waiting an hour at that clinic is about par for the course.  在那家诊所等一小时算是家常便饭。

4427.cn: 在意料之中；没什么稀奇
4427.e: The food on this plane is terrible, but that's par for the course.  这架飞机上的餐食很糟，不过也在意料之中。

4428.e: Delays on this line are par for the course, so bring a book.  这条线晚点是常事，带本书吧。

4429.e: Her latest essay is well above par for a first-year student.  她这篇论文对大一学生来说远超水准。

4430.cn: 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
4430.e: He is a storyteller par excellence, holding children spellbound for hours.  他是个出类拔萃的故事家，能让孩子听上几个钟头。

4431.cn: 道德楷模；完美无缺的人
4431.e: She's no paragon of virtue, but she'd never steal from a friend.  她算不上什么道德楷模，但绝不会偷朋友的东西。

4432.e: The two investigations ran in parallel with each other for six months.  这两项调查并行了六个月。

4433.e: Ann wanted to pursue her own career in parallel with her husband's.  安想和丈夫同时追求各自的事业。

4434.i: be ˌpart and ˈparcel of sth
4434.e: Late nights are part and parcel of working in a busy newsroom.  熬夜是在繁忙新闻编辑室工作的一部分。

4435.e: Pardon me, did you say the meeting starts at eight or nine?  对不起，你是说会议八点还是九点开始？

4436.e: Pardon me for asking, but who exactly invited you here tonight?  恕我多问一句，今晚到底是谁请你来的？

4437.cn: 帕金森定律；工作总会拖满时限
4437.e: Give them a month and they'll take a month — Parkinson's law again.  给他们一个月他们就用满一个月，又是帕金森定律。

4438.cn: 鹦鹉学舌般地；机械模仿地
4438.e: He learned the poem parrot-fashion without understanding a single line.  他鹦鹉学舌般背下那首诗，一句也没懂。

4439.i: be ˌpart and ˈparcel of sth
4439.cn: 是…的基本组成部分；不可分割
4439.e: Rejection is part and parcel of being an actor, sadly.  遗憾的是，被拒绝是当演员必然要经历的一部分。

4440.e: We waited the better part of three hours for a table.  我们为了等位子等了将近三个小时。

4441.e: For my part, I'd rather stay home than sit in traffic all day.  就我而言，我宁愿待在家也不想堵一天车。

4442.e: The delay was caused in part by the storm and in part by staff shortages.  延误一部分因风暴，一部分因人手不足。

4443.cn: 外表或穿着与身份相称
4443.e: In that tailored suit he really looks the part of a lawyer.  穿上那套定制西装，他看着还真像个律师。

4444.cn: 习以为常的人；不为人注意的老面孔
4444.e: After thirty years here, old Tom is part of the furniture.  在这儿干了三十年，老汤姆早成了固定风景。

4445.e: Bad weather certainly played a part in the team's poor result.  恶劣天气无疑对球队的糟糕成绩起了作用。

4446.cn: 不介意；从容接受（玩笑等）
4446.e: They teased him about his haircut, but he took it in good part.  大家取笑他的发型，他倒毫不介意。

4447.e: Over two hundred runners took part in the charity race yesterday.  昨天有两百多名跑者参加了慈善赛跑。

4448.cn: 支持某人；站在某人一边
4448.e: My sister always takes my mother's part whenever we argue.  我们一吵架，我姐姐总是站在我妈那边。

4449.e: I enjoyed the whole trip, but the mountain hike in particular.  整趟旅行我都喜欢，尤其是那次登山。

4450.cn: 分道扬镳；各奔前程之时
4450.e: After ten years together, the band reached a parting of the ways.  合作十年后，乐队走到了分道扬镳的时刻。

4451.i: a ˌparting ˈshot (also a ˌParthian ˈshot)
4451.cn: 临别时不友好的话或举动
4451.e: As a parting shot, she said the office had never respected her.  临走时她撂下一句：这办公室从没尊重过她。

4452.e: He farms, teaches piano and writes poetry — a man of many parts.  他种地、教钢琴、写诗，是个多面手。

4453.e: She refused to be a party to any deal involving the company's rivals.  她拒绝参与任何牵涉到公司对手的交易。

4454.e: Every spokesman repeated the party line without answering our questions.  每位发言人都在重复官方口径，不回答我们的问题。

4455.cn: 聚会上的拿手戏；表演节目
4455.e: After dinner Uncle Ray did his party piece on the old piano.  饭后雷叔叔在旧钢琴上表演了他的拿手节目。

4456.cn: 好日子到头了；该干正事了
4456.e: Funding has been cut, so I'm afraid the party's over for us.  经费被砍了，恐怕我们的好日子到头了。

4457.i: come to such a ˈpass ◆ come to a pretty ˈpass
4457.cn: 落到这步田地；陷入困境
4457.e: Things have come to a pretty pass when neighbours won't even say hello.  连邻居都不打招呼了，真是落到这步田地。

4458.e: He made a rude remark, but I decided to let it pass.  他说了句难听的话，我决定不去计较。

4459.e: He made a pass at her during the office party and she left early.  他在公司派对上挑逗她，她提早就走了。

4460.e: Not a word of complaint passed his lips throughout the long journey.  整趟长途旅程他一句抱怨都没说过。

4461.cn: 推卸责任；把难题推给别人
4461.e: Stop passing the buck and admit the mistake was yours.  别推卸责任了，承认错在你自己。

4462.e: The public is tired of all the buck-passing between the two departments.  民众受够了两个部门之间互相推诿。

4463.i: pass the ˈhat round/around ◆ pass round/around the ˈhat (informal)
4463.e: We passed the hat round to buy the caretaker a leaving present.  我们凑份子给门卫买了份离别礼物。

4464.i: pass the ˈhat round/around ◆ pass round/around the ˈhat (informal)
4464.e: Someone passed around the hat and we raised eighty pounds in minutes.  有人传帽募捐，几分钟就凑了八十英镑。

4465.i: pass ˈjudgement (on/about sb/sth) (especially BrE) (AmE usually pass ˈjudgment (on/about sb/sth))
4465.e: Don't pass judgement on her until you know the whole story.  在了解全部情况前别对她妄下评判。

4466.e: My handwriting barely passes muster, but at least it's readable.  我的字勉强过关，好歹还认得出来。

4467.e: We passed the time playing cards while waiting for the delayed flight.  等晚点航班时，我们打牌消磨时间。

4468.i: pass the time of ˈday (with sb)
4468.cn: 与某人寒暄；打招呼闲聊
4468.e: She stopped to pass the time of day with the woman in the flower shop.  她停下来和花店的女人寒暄了几句。

4469.e: The doctor asked whether it hurt when he passed water.  医生问他小便时是否疼痛。

4470.e: He's a bird of passage who never stays in one city long.  他是个过客，从不在一个城市久留。

4471.e: She mentioned in passing that she might move to Berlin.  她顺口提了一句可能会搬去柏林。

4472.e: At forty he was told he was past it for professional football.  四十岁时人家就说他踢职业足球太老了。

4473.e: These strawberries are past their best, but they'll do for jam.  这些草莓已经不新鲜了，做果酱还行。

4474.e: That management theory is well past its sell-by date now.  那套管理理论早就过时了。

4475.i: I wouldn't put it ˈpast sb (to do sth)
4475.cn: 相信某人干得出这种事
4475.e: I wouldn't put it past him to read your emails while you're out.  我相信他趁你不在偷看你邮件这种事干得出来。

4476.e: She's a past master at getting difficult customers to calm down.  她是安抚难缠客户的老手。

4477.i: give sb/get a ˈpasting (informal, especially BrE)
4477.e: Our team got a real pasting in the second half on Saturday.  周六下半场我们队被打得很惨。

4478.i: put sb out to ˈpasture (informal, humorous)
4478.e: They put him out to pasture at sixty, though he was still sharp.  他六十岁就被劝退了，其实脑子还很灵光。

4479.e: After eight years here she's off to pastures new in Canada.  在这儿干了八年后，她要去加拿大另谋新天地了。

4480.i: give sb/yourself a ˌpat on the ˈback ◆ pat sb/yourself on the ˈback (for doing sth)
4480.e: Give yourself a pat on the back — that presentation went brilliantly.  该给自己点个赞，那场演示做得棒极了。

4481.i: give sb/yourself a ˌpat on the ˈback ◆ pat sb/yourself on the ˈback (for doing sth)
4481.e: The coach patted the whole squad on the back for their effort.  教练表扬了全队的拼劲。

4482.i: have/know/get sth off ˈpat (BrE) (AmE have/know sth down ˈpat)
4482.e: She had her whole speech off pat before she even reached the hall.  还没到会场，她整篇讲稿就已经烂熟于心。

4483.cn: 坚持原有决定；固执己见
4483.e: The board decided to stand pat and keep the current pricing.  董事会决定按兵不动，维持现行定价。

4484.i: go through, hit, etc. a ˈbad/ˈsticky patch
4484.cn: 遇到难关；处于困难时期
4484.e: Their marriage hit a bad patch after he lost his job.  他失业后，他们的婚姻遇到了难关。

4485.i: not be a ˈpatch on sb/sth (informal, especially BrE)
4485.cn: 远不如；相比之下差得多
4485.e: This café isn't a patch on the one that used to be here.  这家咖啡馆远不如从前那家。

4486.i: the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob
4486.cn: 极大的耐心；圣人般的耐性
4486.e: Teaching that class needs the patience of a saint.  教那个班需要圣人般的耐心。

4487.i: the patter of tiny ˈfeet (informal or humorous)
4487.cn: 小孩子的脚步声；指要有孩子了
4487.e: They're hoping for the patter of tiny feet before next Christmas.  他们盼着明年圣诞前家里能添个小宝宝。

4488.i: give (sb) pause for ˈthought ◆ give (sb) ˈpause (formal)
4488.e: The doctor's warning about his blood pressure gave him pause for thought.  医生对他血压的警告让他认真思量起来。

4489.i: give (sb) pause for ˈthought ◆ give (sb) ˈpause (formal)
4489.e: The huge repair bill gave us pause before buying that old house.  高昂的修缮费让我们买那栋老房子前犹豫了。

4490.cn: 意味深长的停顿；耐人寻味的沉默
4490.e: There was a pregnant pause before she finally answered his question.  她终于回答他的问题前，出现了一段意味深长的沉默。

4491.e: Her research paved the way for a much cheaper vaccine.  她的研究为一种廉价得多的疫苗铺平了道路。

4492.i: be in the pay of sb/sth ◆ be in sb's/sth's ˈpay
4492.cn: 受雇于（常指秘密地）；被…豢养
4492.e: The journalist claimed two officials were in the pay of the company.  这名记者称有两名官员受雇于该公司。

4493.e: There'll be hell to pay if your father finds the car scratched.  要是你爸发现车被刮了，可有大麻烦了。

4494.cn: 突然发财；意外获得成功
4494.e: They struck pay dirt with their third app, which sold millions.  他们的第三款应用大卖，一举发了财。

4495.e: Learning Spanish before the trip really paid dividends in every village.  出发前学西班牙语，在每个村子都派上了大用场。

4496.e: The solar panels will pay for themselves within about six years.  这些太阳能板大约六年就能收回成本。

4497.cn: 口惠而实不至；嘴上说说而已
4497.e: The firm pays lip-service to equality but promotes only its old friends.  这家公司口头讲平等，提拔的却全是老熟人。

4498.i: pay the ˈprice/ˈpenalty (for sth/for doing sth)
4498.e: He partied all week and paid the price in Friday's exam.  他玩了一星期，周五考试自食其果。

4499.cn: 向某人致敬；作礼节性拜访
4499.e: Hundreds came to pay their respects to the old headmaster.  数百人前来向老校长致敬。

4500.cn: 付出过高价钱；被敲竹杠
4500.e: We paid through the nose for a hotel room with no window.  我们花了大价钱订了间没窗户的酒店房。

4501.e: The mayor paid tribute to the volunteers who cleared the flooded streets.  市长向清理水淹街道的志愿者致敬。

4502.i: pay sb/sth a ˈvisit ◆ pay a ˈvisit to sb/sth
4502.e: We should pay Grandma a visit before the weather gets worse.  趁天气变坏前，我们该去看看奶奶。

4503.e: He's been paying his own way since he was seventeen.  他从十七岁起就自食其力了。

4504.e: Each part of the business must be able to pay its own way.  每一块业务都必须能够自负盈亏。

4505.e: They humiliated us last season — now it's payback time.  上赛季他们让我们难堪，现在该我们讨回来了。

4506.i: he who pays the ˌpiper calls the ˈtune (saying)
4506.e: Her father funded the shop, so he who pays the piper calls the tune.  店是她父亲出的钱，自然是他说了算。

4507.i: it always/never pays to do sth
4507.cn: 做某事总是明智（或不明智）的
4507.e: It always pays to read the contract before you sign anything.  签字前先读合同，永远是明智之举。

4508.i: you ˌpays your ˌmoney and you ˌtakes your ˈchoice (saying)
4508.cn: 全凭个人喜好；选哪个都差不多
4508.e: Both phones are much the same — you pays your money and you takes your choice.  两款手机差不多，全看你自己喜欢哪个。

4509.i: you ˌpays your ˌmoney and you ˌtakes your ˈchoice (saying)
4509.cn: 各选项差别不大；碰运气罢了
4509.e: Train or coach? You pays your money and you takes your choice.  坐火车还是大巴？反正差不多，随你挑。

4510.cn: 处于和平状态；内心平静；安息
4510.e: After the treaty was signed, the region was at peace for a decade.  条约签署后，这个地区太平了十年。

4511.e: I wanted to argue, but I held my peace for my mother's sake.  我本想争辩，但为了我母亲还是没吭声。

4512.e: Two officers stood by the gate to keep the peace during the march.  游行期间两名警察守在门口维持秩序。

4513.e: He finally made his peace with his brother after twelve silent years.  沉默十二年后，他终于和哥哥和解了。

4514.e: All I want this weekend is a bit of peace and quiet.  这个周末我只想要一点清静。

4515.cn: 和平红利（削减军费省下的钱）
4515.e: The government promised to spend the peace dividend on schools and hospitals.  政府承诺把和平红利用在学校和医院上。

4516.e: Buying good insurance gave my parents real peace of mind.  买了好保险让我父母真正安了心。

4517.e: He arrived with flowers as a peace offering after their silly argument.  那场无聊争吵之后，他带着花来赔罪。

4518.i: there's no ˌpeace/ˌrest for the ˈwicked (humorous)
4518.e: Another shift tonight? No rest for the wicked, I suppose.  今晚又要值班？看来是不得清闲了。

4519.e: Thanks for those pearls of wisdom, but I've already booked the flight.  多谢您的金玉良言，不过机票我已经订了。

4520.e: He joked that he'd be arguing with St Peter at the Pearly Gates.  他打趣说自己会在天国之门跟圣彼得争辩。

4521.e: The whole evening turned pear-shaped when the power went out.  停电之后，整个晚上就全乱套了。

4522.e: Our camping trip went pear-shaped when the tent leaked in the storm.  暴雨中帐篷漏水，我们的露营就搞砸了。

4523.e: Dave did well all term, but the last week went a bit pear-shaped.  戴夫整学期都不错，可最后一周出了点问题。

4524.i: as alike/like as (two) ˈpeas in a pod (informal)
4524.e: The twins are as like as two peas in a pod, even their laughs.  这对双胞胎一模一样，连笑声都像。

4525.i: not the ˈonly pebble on the beach (informal, disapproving)
4525.cn: 并非绝无仅有；大有人在
4525.e: Remind him he's not the only pebble on the beach around here.  提醒他一句，这地方少了他照样转。

4526.i: not the ˈonly pebble on the beach (informal, disapproving)
4526.cn: 并非唯一人选；别把自己看得太重
4526.e: She thinks she should go to Paris, but she's not the only pebble on the beach.  她觉得该派她去巴黎，可她并非唯一人选。

4527.i: not the ˈonly pebble on the beach (informal, disapproving)
4527.cn: 不是唯一的选择；大有人在
4527.e: He's talented, sure, but he's not the only pebble on the beach.  他确实有才，但也不是非他不可。

4528.e: Neighbours called the police about a Peeping Tom in the back lane.  邻居报警说后巷有个偷窥狂。

4529.e: In this newsroom the pecking order is obvious within about five minutes.  在这间编辑室，五分钟就能看出谁大谁小。

4530.e: Keep your pecker up — there'll be other job interviews soon.  打起精神来，很快还会有别的面试。

4531.cn: 把某人捧上神坛；过分崇拜某人
4531.e: Don't put your teachers on a pedestal; they make mistakes too.  别把老师捧上神坛，他们也会犯错。

4532.i: ˌbring/ˌtake sb ˈdown a peg (or two) (informal)
4532.cn: 挫某人的锐气；杀某人威风
4532.e: Losing to a junior player took him down a peg or two.  输给一名年轻选手挫了挫他的锐气。

4533.i: ˌbring/ˌtake sb ˈdown a peg (or two) (informal)
4533.cn: 杀某人的威风；挫其傲气
4533.e: It's time somebody took that woman down a peg or two.  该有人挫挫那个女人的傲气了。

4534.i: off the ˈpeg (BrE) (AmE ˌoff the ˈrack)
4534.e: He bought the suit off the peg and had the trousers shortened.  他买了套成衣，把裤子改短了些。

4535.i: a peg to ˈhang sth on ◆ a peg on which to ˈhang sth
4535.e: The anniversary gave reporters a peg to hang the story on.  周年纪念给了记者做这篇报道的由头。

4536.i: a peg to ˈhang sth on ◆ a peg on which to ˈhang sth
4536.e: She used the survey as a peg to hang her argument on.  她拿那份调查当由头来支撑自己的论点。

4537.i: be a ˌsquare ˈpeg (in a ˌround ˈhole)
4537.cn: 不称职的人；格格不入的人
4537.e: In that formal bank he was a square peg in a round hole.  在那家刻板的银行里，他显得格格不入。

4538.i: the ˌpen is ˌmightier than the ˈsword (saying)
4538.cn: 笔杆胜过刀剑；文胜于武
4538.e: Her articles toppled the minister, proving the pen is mightier than the sword.  她的文章扳倒了部长，证明笔杆胜过刀剑。

4539.e: He thought about the novel for years before he put pen to paper.  这部小说他想了好几年才真正动笔。

4540.e: The vicar received a poison pen letter accusing him of stealing funds.  牧师收到一封匿名信，指控他挪用资金。

4541.e: Let me add my pennyworth before you finalize the plan.  在你定案之前，让我也说两句浅见。

4542.i: ˌin for a ˈpenny, ˌin for a ˈpound (saying)
4542.cn: 一不做二不休；既已开始就干到底
4542.e: We've repainted two rooms, so in for a penny, in for a pound.  两间屋子都刷了，索性一不做二不休。

4543.i: ˌin for a ˈpenny, ˌin for a ˈpound (saying)
4543.cn: 一不做二不休；干脆做到底
4543.e: The new carpet made everything look old, so in for a penny, in for a pound.  新地毯衬得其他都旧了，索性一不做二不休。

4544.e: He stared at the photo, and then suddenly the penny dropped.  他盯着照片看，忽然恍然大悟。

4545.i: a ˌpenny for your ˈthoughts (also a ˈpenny for them) (saying)
4545.e: You've been quiet all evening — a penny for your thoughts.  你一晚上没说话，在想什么呢？

4546.e: Skipping the survey to save money was penny wise and pound foolish.  为省钱不做房屋检测，真是因小失大。

4547.i: turn up like a bad ˈpenny (informal)
4547.e: Every family party, that cousin turns up like a bad penny.  每次家庭聚会，那个表亲总是不请自来。

4548.i: ˌtwo/ˌten a ˈpenny (BrE) (AmE a ˌdime a ˈdozen)
4548.cn: 多得不值钱；廉价而常见
4548.e: Cafés like this are ten a penny in the city centre.  这种咖啡馆在市中心多得是。

4549.e: You took a lift from Mike, of all people, in this weather?  这种天气，你偏偏搭了迈克的车？

4550.i: people who live in glass houses shouldn't throw ˈstones (saying)
4550.cn: 自身有短，勿责他人；五十步莫笑百步
4550.e: You criticize his spelling? People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.  你还笑他拼写？自己也好不到哪儿去。

4551.i: people who live in glass houses shouldn't throw ˈstones (saying)
4551.cn: 自己有缺点就别指责别人
4551.e: Tell him from me that people who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.  替我告诉他，自己屁股不干净就别说别人。

4552.cn: 鼓舞士气的话；打气的动员
4552.e: The captain gave the team a short pep talk before extra time.  加时赛前队长给全队打了打气。

4553.cn: 励志讲话；加油鼓劲的话
4553.e: Before the exams our teacher gave us all a pep talk.  考试前老师给我们所有人加油鼓劲。

4554.cn: 自担风险地做某事；后果自负
4554.e: You ignore the safety instructions at your own peril.  你不理会安全须知，后果自负。

4555.e: Me, run a marathon in the desert? Perish the thought, I'd collapse!  让我去沙漠跑马拉松？想都别想，我准趴下。

4556.e: The land was given to the village in perpetuity by its former owner.  这块地由前主人永久赠予村庄。

4557.e: He always carries a small notebook about his person.  他随身总带着一个小本子。

4558.e: You'll have to collect the documents in person and bring your passport.  你得亲自来取文件，还要带上护照。

4559.cn: 以某人为代表；由某人体现
4559.e: Help arrived in the person of a passing nurse.  一位路过的护士出现，成了及时的援手。

4560.e: After leaking the memo he became persona non grata in the office.  泄露备忘录后，他在办公室成了不受欢迎的人。

4561.cn: 把泛泛之言当成针对自己而不悦
4561.e: It's a general reminder, so please don't take it personally.  这只是普遍提醒，请别往心里去。

4562.cn: 对号入座；认为是针对自己
4562.e: I wasn't blaming you, Sue, so don't take it personally.  苏，我不是在怪你，别对号入座。

4563.i: get, put, etc. sth in/out of perˈspective
4563.cn: 正确（或不正确）地看待事物
4563.e: Losing one client hurts, but let's get it in perspective.  丢一个客户是难受，但要放在大局里看。

4564.e: Guests of every political persuasion argued cheerfully round the dinner table.  各种政治立场的客人围着餐桌高高兴兴地争论。

4565.cn: 妨碍司法公正；扰乱司法程序
4565.e: He was jailed for trying to pervert the course of justice by hiding evidence.  他因藏匿证据妨碍司法公正而入狱。

4566.i: your, his, etc. pet ˈhate (BrE) (AmE your, his, etc. pet ˈpeeve)
4566.cn: 特别厌恶的东西；最烦的事
4566.e: People chewing loudly on trains is my pet hate.  我最烦的就是有人在火车上大声咀嚼。

4567.i: be hoist/hoisted by/with your own peˈtard
4567.cn: 作茧自缚；搬起石头砸自己的脚
4567.e: He banned phones in meetings and was hoist by his own petard.  他禁止开会用手机，结果自己也被这规矩绊住。

4568.cn: 看在老天的份上；拜托（表示不耐烦）
4568.e: For Pete's sake, close the window before the rain soaks everything.  拜托，趁雨没把东西淋透赶紧关窗。

4569.e: Come in and take a pew — the kettle's just boiled.  进来坐吧，水刚烧开。

4570.cn: 协调；不协调；同步或不同步
4570.e: The traffic lights are out of phase, so the junction is chaotic.  红绿灯不同步，路口一片混乱。

4571.e: She's been on the phone to her sister for over an hour.  她跟她姐姐通电话已经一个多小时了。

4572.e: He has a lovely turn of phrase that makes dull topics interesting.  他措辞漂亮，能把枯燥的话题讲得有趣。

4573.cn: 套用一句老话；恕我杜撰一词
4573.e: To coin a phrase, we're all in the same leaky boat here.  套句老话，咱们都在同一条漏水的船上。

4574.e: With so few offers, you can't afford to pick and choose.  机会这么少，你没资格挑三拣四。

4575.cn: 向某人讨教；请教某人的想法
4575.e: Can I pick your brains about which laptop to buy?  能向你请教一下买哪款笔记本吗？

4576.e: He'd had too much to drink and started picking a fight with strangers.  他喝多了，开始跟陌生人找茬儿。

4577.e: She picked holes in my plan without suggesting anything better.  她把我的方案挑得一无是处，却拿不出更好的。

4578.e: He locked himself out and had to pay someone to pick the lock.  他把自己锁在门外，只好花钱请人撬锁。

4579.e: Of all the applicants, that young engineer was the pick of the bunch.  所有应聘者中，那位年轻工程师最出色。

4580.e: Someone picked his pocket on the crowded metro platform.  有人在拥挤的地铁站台上扒了他的口袋。

4581.e: After the fire, the family had to pick up the pieces alone.  火灾之后，这家人只能自己收拾残局。

4582.e: The train picked up speed once it left the station behind.  火车驶离车站后就加快了速度。

4583.e: Her uncle insisted on picking up the tab for the whole meal.  她叔叔坚持要为整顿饭买单。

4584.cn: 中断后重新开始；恢复原状
4584.e: After a year abroad she came home and picked up the threads quickly.  在国外待了一年后，她回家很快就恢复了原来的生活。

4585.i: pick your ˈway (across, over, etc. sth)
4585.e: We picked our way across the rocks to reach the little beach.  我们小心地在礁石间择路，走到那片小沙滩。

4586.e: You certainly picked a winner when you hired that new designer.  你雇那位新设计师，眼光真准。

4587.e: There are five spare rooms upstairs, so take your pick.  楼上有五间空房，随你挑。

4588.e: We were in a real pickle when the car broke down miles from town.  车在离镇几英里处抛锚，我们真是麻烦大了。

4589.e: Raising three kids on one salary is no picnic.  靠一份工资养三个孩子可不轻松。

4590.e: The garden looks a picture now that the roses are out.  玫瑰开了，花园现在美得像画一样。

4591.i: be the ˌpicture of ˈhealth, ˈhappiness, etc.
4591.cn: 显得非常健康（或幸福等）
4591.e: At eighty my grandfather is still the picture of health.  我祖父八十岁了，看上去依然十分硬朗。

4592.e: She's not answering his calls — I think you get the picture.  她不接他电话，我想你明白是怎么回事了。

4593.e: Since the merger, the old management is completely out of the picture.  合并之后，原来的管理层彻底出局了。

4594.cn: 向某人介绍情况；让某人了解进展
4594.e: Email me weekly to keep me in the picture while I'm away.  我不在时，每周发邮件让我了解情况。

4595.cn: 空中楼阁；不切实际的空想
4595.e: A high-speed line to this village is pie in the sky.  往这个村子修高铁纯属空中楼阁。

4596.i: give sb a piece of your ˈmind (informal)
4596.cn: 直言斥责；把某人痛骂一顿
4596.e: If he parks across my gate again, I'll give him a piece of my mind.  他要再堵我家大门，我非说他一顿不可。

4597.e: The bike is scratched, but at least you got home in one piece.  自行车刮花了，好在你人平安到家。

4598.e: His rudeness tonight is all of a piece with his behaviour last year.  他今晚的无礼跟他去年的表现如出一辙。

4599.e: He rebuilt the old motorbike piece by piece over two winters.  他用两个冬天把那辆旧摩托一件件重装起来。

4600.i: a piece of ˈcake (informal) (BrE also a piece of ˈpiss△, slang)
4600.cn: 小菜一碟；轻而易举的事
4600.e: Once you've done it twice, the whole process is a piece of cake.  做过两次之后，整个流程就是小菜一碟。

4601.cn: 最精彩的作品；压轴之作
4601.e: The chocolate tart was the pièce de résistance of the whole meal.  巧克力挞是整顿饭的压轴之作。

4602.e: That armchair is falling to pieces, but Dad refuses to throw it out.  那把扶手椅都快散架了，我爸还是不肯扔。

4603.e: She went to pieces when she heard the news about her brother.  听到她弟弟的消息，她整个人垮了。

4604.e: He says he'll pay me back tomorrow — in a pig's eye!  他说明天还我钱，鬼才信呢！

4605.e: Apparently this is the best hotel in town. In a pig's eye it is!  据说这是城里最好的宾馆，才怪呢！

4606.e: I made a pig of myself at the buffet and regretted it later.  我在自助餐上吃撑了，后来很后悔。

4607.i: make a pig's ˈear (out) of sth (BrE, informal)
4607.cn: 把事情办砸；弄得一团糟
4607.e: He made a pig's ear of painting the door and had to start again.  他把门刷得一塌糊涂，只好重来。

4608.e: Buying a car online without seeing it is buying a pig in a poke.  网上买车不看实物，等于隔山买牛。

4609.i: a pig of a sth (BrE, informal)
4609.e: It's been a pig of a week, with two deadlines and a broken boiler.  这周真够呛，两个截稿期还赶上锅炉坏了。

4610.cn: 是某人的分内事；由某人负责
4610.e: Timetables aren't my pigeon — ask the office downstairs.  排课表不归我管，去楼下办公室问。

4611.i: pigs might ˈfly (BrE) (AmE when ˌpigs ˈfly)
4611.cn: 太阳打西边出来；绝无可能
4611.e: He'll tidy his room on time? Yes, and pigs might fly.  他会按时收拾房间？太阳打西边出来吧。

4612.e: New rules on data privacy are coming down the pike this year.  今年会出台新的数据隐私规定。

4613.e: He made his pile in shipping and retired at forty-five.  他做航运发了财，四十五岁就退休了。

4614.i: pile on the ˈagony/ˈgloom (informal, especially BrE)
4614.cn: 大肆渲染痛苦；添油加醋博同情
4614.e: Stop piling on the agony — it was only a scratch.  别再夸大其词了，就是擦破点皮。

4615.i: at the ˈbottom/ˈtop of the pile/heap
4615.cn: 处于最底层；处于最上层
4615.e: Part-time cleaners are still at the bottom of the pile here.  在这里，兼职清洁工仍处在最底层。

4616.e: She's been on the pill since she was at university.  她从大学时起就一直在服避孕药。

4617.cn: 使不愉快的事较易接受；给苦药裹糖衣
4617.e: They sweetened the pill of relocation with a generous moving allowance.  他们用一笔丰厚的搬迁补贴让调职不那么难接受。

4618.i: be driven, pushed, etc. from ˌpillar to ˈpost
4618.cn: 被迫四处奔走；到处碰壁
4618.e: She was sent from pillar to post before anyone answered her question.  她被推来推去，才终于有人回答她的问题。

4619.e: The old doctor was regarded as a pillar of society in this town.  这位老医生被视为镇上的中坚人物。

4620.e: Everyone was shocked when a pillar of the community was arrested for fraud.  当社区栋梁因诈骗被捕时，所有人都惊呆了。

4621.cn: 枕边私房话；枕边悄悄话
4621.e: He admitted he had leaked the company secret during pillow talk with his girlfriend.  他承认自己在和女友说枕边话时泄露了公司机密。

4622.e: She's pinning her hopes on that scholarship, because she can't afford the tuition otherwise.  她把希望全押在那笔奖学金上，不然她根本付不起学费。

4623.i: at a ˈpinch/ˈpush (BrE) (AmE in a ˈpinch)
4623.e: This sofa sleeps two people comfortably, and three at a pinch.  这张沙发睡两个人很舒服，挤一挤三个人也行。

4624.cn: 省吃俭用；一分钱掰两半花
4624.e: We had to pinch pennies for a year to save up for the wedding.  为了攒下婚礼的钱，我们省吃俭用了整整一年。

4625.e: His penny-pinching finally paid off when he bought the flat with cash.  他的精打细算终于有了回报，他全款买下了那套公寓。

4626.i: take sth with a pinch of ˈsalt (informal)
4626.e: Take his stories about meeting film stars with a pinch of salt.  他那些见过影星的故事，你听听就好，别当真。

4627.e: After two weeks by the sea, Grandpa came back in the pink.  在海边住了两周，爷爷回来时红光满面。

4628.e: One more whisky and you'll be seeing pink elephants, my friend.  朋友，再来一杯威士忌你就要出现幻觉了。

4629.e: I sat cross-legged too long and now I have pins and needles in my left foot.  我盘腿坐太久了，现在左脚一阵发麻。

4630.cn: 靠自己的腿站立（或行走）
4630.e: At ninety-two she's still steady on her pins and walks to the shops daily.  九十二岁了她腿脚还很稳，每天都走着去商店。

4631.i: pip sb at/to the ˈpost (BrE, informal)
4631.cn: 以微弱优势险胜；最后关头击败
4631.e: Our team was pipped at the post by a single goal in the final minute.  我们队在最后一分钟被一个进球险胜，功亏一篑。

4632.e: Owning a house in this city is a pipe dream on my current salary.  就我现在的工资，在这座城市买房纯属白日梦。

4633.i: put ˈthat in your pipe and smoke it (informal)
4633.cn: 不管爱不爱听你都得接受
4633.e: I got the promotion instead of you, so put that in your pipe and smoke it.  升职的是我不是你，你就好好受着吧。

4634.e: There are two new albums in the pipeline, but nothing has been announced yet.  有两张新专辑正在筹备中，不过还没有正式公布。

4635.i: pique sb's ˈinterest, curiˈosity, etc. (especially AmE)
4635.cn: 引起某人的兴趣（或好奇）
4635.e: The strange title on the cover immediately piqued my curiosity.  封面上那个古怪的标题一下子勾起了我的好奇心。

4636.e: The whole team was on the piss all weekend after winning the cup.  夺冠之后，全队整个周末都在拼命喝酒。

4637.cn: 笑得不能自制；笑破肚皮
4637.e: We were pissing ourselves laughing at his impression of the boss.  他模仿老板的样子，把我们笑得直不起腰。

4638.i: take the ˈpiss (out of sb/sth) (BrE, △, slang)
4638.e: Stop taking the piss out of my accent — I've only been here a month.  别拿我的口音开涮了，我才来一个月。

4639.e: By midnight he was as pissed as a newt and singing on the table.  到了午夜他已经烂醉如泥，还站在桌上唱歌。

4640.i: make a ˈpit stop (informal, especially AmE)
4640.e: Let's make a pit stop at the next services — I need coffee badly.  我们在下个服务区歇一下吧，我特别需要来杯咖啡。

4641.e: When I saw the police car outside, I felt sick in the pit of my stomach.  看到门外的警车，我心窝里一阵发慌。

4642.e: Every Sunday he pits his wits against the newspaper's hardest crossword.  每个周日他都要和报纸上最难的填字游戏斗一斗智。

4643.cn: 无底洞；无穷无尽的东西
4643.e: That old house has become a bottomless pit for our savings.  那栋老房子成了吞掉我们积蓄的无底洞。

4644.i: make a ˈpitch for sb/sth • make a ˈpitch to do sth
4644.e: Three agencies will make a pitch for the contract on Friday morning.  周五上午会有三家公司来竞标这份合同。

4645.e: He pitched me some line about his car breaking down again.  他又跟我编了套车子抛锚的说辞。

4646.e: The protest turned into a pitched battle between demonstrators and riot police.  抗议演变成示威者与防暴警察之间的一场激战。

4647.e: The food was fine but the service was absolutely the pits.  东西还行，可服务简直糟透了。

4648.e: She won't be joining us tonight, more's the pity.  她今晚不能和我们一起了，真是遗憾。

4649.e: His notes were all over the place, so nobody could follow the argument.  他的笔记乱七八糟，谁也看不懂他的论证。

4650.i: (not) be sb's ˈplace to do sth
4650.e: It's not my place to tell your parents what you did last night.  你昨晚干了什么，轮不到我去告诉你父母。

4651.e: Once she mentioned the missing key, everything fell into place.  她一提到那把不见的钥匙，一切就都说得通了。

4652.e: The old market gave place to a shopping centre in the nineties.  九十年代，老市场让位给了一座购物中心。

4653.i: if ˌI was/were in ˈyour place
4653.cn: 如果我是你；换了我的话
4653.e: If I were in your place, I'd take the job and move to Berlin.  如果我是你，我会接下这份工作，搬去柏林。

4654.e: In her place, I doubt anyone would have stayed so calm.  换作她那种处境，我想没几个人能这么冷静。

4655.e: All the safety measures are in place, so we can start tomorrow.  各项安全措施都已就位，我们明天就能开工。

4656.i: in place of sb/sth • in sb's/sth's ˈplace
4656.e: Use honey in place of sugar if you want a milder taste.  想要味道柔和些的话，可以用蜂蜜代替糖。

4657.cn: 位置不当；不合时宜；格格不入
4657.e: In my old jeans I felt completely out of place at the gala dinner.  穿着旧牛仔裤，我在那场晚宴上觉得格格不入。

4658.cn: 有发展前途的地位；出头之日
4658.e: After years of small roles, she finally found her place in the sun.  演了多年小角色后，她终于熬出了头。

4659.cn: 灭某人威风；让某人识相
4659.e: One cool sentence from the chairman put the young manager in his place.  董事长一句冷冷的话就让那位年轻经理老实了。

4660.e: The wedding will take place in a small church outside town.  婚礼将在城外一座小教堂举行。

4661.i: take sb's ˈplace • take the place of sb
4661.e: No one can really take the place of a friend you grew up with.  一起长大的朋友，谁也真的替代不了。

4662.e: Please take your places, everyone — the performance starts in two minutes.  请各位就座，演出两分钟后开始。

4663.i: be well, ideally, better, etc. ˈplaced (for sth/to do sth)
4663.cn: 处于有利地位；有良好条件
4663.e: With her contacts, she's ideally placed to launch the new campaign.  凭她的人脉，她最适合来发起这场新活动。

4664.e: I wouldn't change places with him for all the money in the world.  给我全世界的钱，我也不愿和他换个位置。

4665.e: That girl really knows how to sell — she's going to go places.  那姑娘太会卖东西了，将来肯定有出息。

4666.i: be (all) plain ˈsailing (AmE also be clear ˈsailing)
4666.e: Once we got the permit, the rest of the project was plain sailing.  拿到许可证之后，项目剩下的部分就一帆风顺了。

4667.e: Could you explain the contract in plain English for once?  你能不能就这一次用大白话解释一下这份合同？

4668.i: (as) plain as a ˈpikestaff • (as) plain as ˈday
4668.e: It was as plain as day that he had never read the report.  他压根没读过那份报告，这一点显而易见。

4669.i: (as) plain as the nose on your ˈface (informal)
4669.e: The mistake was as plain as the nose on your face, yet nobody spotted it.  这个错误明摆着的，却没有一个人发现。

4670.e: In the film she plays a plain Jane who turns out to be a genius hacker.  片中她演一个其貌不扬、却是天才黑客的姑娘。

4671.i: be on another ˈplanet • what ˈplanet is sb on?
4671.cn: 异想天开；不知在想什么
4671.e: If he thinks we can finish this by Friday, what planet is he on?  他要是觉得我们周五就能做完，那他脑子里想的是什么呀？

4672.cn: 埋下…的种子；播下…的祸根
4672.e: That summer trip planted the seeds of her lifelong love of the sea.  那年夏天的旅行埋下了她一生爱海的种子。

4673.i: have enough, a lot, etc. on your ˈplate
4673.cn: 手头事情一大堆；忙得不可开交
4673.e: Don't ask her for favours — she's got enough on her plate already.  别再麻烦她了，她手头的事已经够多了。

4674.i: have too much on your ˈplate
4674.e: She has too much on her plate at the moment, which is why she looks so anxious.  她现在有一堆事要操心，所以看上去一直很焦虑。

4675.e: The new rules bring several safety checks into play before every flight.  新规定让每次飞行前都要启动好几项安全检查。

4676.cn: 开始起作用；开始有影响
4676.e: Luck comes into play far more often than most investors like to admit.  运气起作用的时候，比多数投资者愿意承认的多得多。

4677.i: have money, time, etc. to ˈplay with (informal)
4677.cn: 有充裕的钱（或时间等）可用
4677.e: We've got two hours to play with before the train leaves.  火车开车前我们还有两个小时可以随便安排。

4678.e: The referee shouted that the ball was still in play, so nobody stopped.  裁判喊球还在界内，所以没人停下来。

4679.i: make great, much, etc. ˈplay of/with sth
4679.e: The minister made great play of the falling unemployment figures.  部长对失业率下降的数字大做文章。

4680.i: make a ˈplay for sb/sth (especially AmE)
4680.e: He's clearly making a play for her job while she's on leave.  她休假期间，他明显在想方设法谋她的职位。

4681.cn: 在搞什么名堂（表示气愤）
4681.e: What on earth is he playing at, parking right across our driveway?  他到底在搞什么鬼，车正好停在我们车道口？

4682.e: Two coffees and a glass of water, if you please.  劳驾，两杯咖啡和一杯水。

4683.e: The garden was designed to please the eye in every single season.  这座花园的设计让人一年四季看着都赏心悦目。

4684.e: Please God, the rain will stop before the wedding starts tomorrow.  但愿明天婚礼开始前雨能停。

4685.e: You don't want to come? Fine, please yourself.  你不想来？行啊，随你的便。

4686.e: I don't think I'll bother finishing this. Please yourself, I'm going home.  我想我不必费心做完这个了。随你的便吧，我要回家了。

4687.i: ˌplease yourˈself • ˌdo as you ˈplease
4687.cn: 随心所欲；想怎样就怎样
4687.e: Once the kids move out, you can finally do as you please on Sundays.  等孩子们搬出去，你周日总算可以想怎么过就怎么过了。

4688.e: I'm very pleased to meet you — I've heard so much about your research.  很高兴认识您，久闻您的研究大名。

4689.e: Dad was none too pleased when he saw the scratch on his new car.  爸爸看到新车上的划痕，非常不高兴。

4690.e: I'd be only too pleased to look after the cat while you're away.  你不在的时候，我非常乐意帮你照看猫。

4691.e: Grandma was as pleased as Punch when we all turned up for her birthday.  我们全都来给奶奶过生日，她高兴得合不拢嘴。

4692.e: He looked very pleased with himself after beating me at chess.  下棋赢了我之后，他一脸得意。

4693.cn: 按某人的意愿；随某人高兴
4693.e: The room is available at your pleasure for as long as you need it.  这间房随您的意愿使用，需要多久都行。

4694.e: I don't believe I've had the pleasure — I'm Daniel, her brother.  我想我们还没被介绍过吧，我是丹尼尔，她哥哥。

4695.e: Thanks for driving me to the airport. It's a pleasure, really.  谢谢你送我去机场。别客气，真的。

4696.e: Could you say a few words at the ceremony? With pleasure.  典礼上您能讲几句吗？我很乐意。

4697.e: After that awful night, he took the pledge and hasn't touched a drop since.  那个糟糕的晚上之后，他发誓戒酒，从此滴酒未沾。

4698.e: Halfway through the meeting the chairman completely lost the plot.  会开到一半，主席就完全乱了套。

4699.cn: 情节（或情况）变得复杂起来
4699.e: So her ex-husband was there too? The plot thickens.  这么说她前夫也在场？情况越来越复杂了。

4700.i: put your hand to the ˈplough (old-fashioned)
4700.e: Once you put your hand to the plough, there's no turning back.  一旦动手干起来，就没有回头路了。

4701.i: ˌplough a lonely, your own, etc. ˈfurrow
4701.e: She's ploughed her own furrow for years, ignoring every trend in fashion.  多年来她一直我行我素，对时尚潮流毫不理会。

4702.cn: 化干戈为玉帛；变武器为农具
4702.e: After the treaty, both sides promised to beat swords into ploughshares.  条约签订后，双方都承诺化干戈为玉帛。

4703.cn: 化干戈为玉帛；由战转和
4703.e: The old factory now makes tractors — swords into ploughshares at last.  那家老厂现在造拖拉机了，总算是化干戈为玉帛。

4704.i: pluck sth out of the ˈair
4704.cn: 随口说出；不加思索地说
4704.e: He plucked a number out of the air and hoped nobody would check it.  他随口报了个数字，指望没人去核对。

4705.cn: 陷入…的深渊；到了…的极点
4705.e: That documentary plumbs the depths of human cruelty during the war.  那部纪录片揭示了战争中人性残忍的极致。

4706.cn: 果断行动；下决心冒险一试
4706.e: After months of hesitating, they finally took the plunge and opened a bakery.  犹豫了几个月后，他们终于下定决心开了家面包店。

4707.e: The trip takes about six hours, plus or minus thirty minutes.  这趟路程大约六小时，上下差个半小时。

4708.cn: 从好的方面说；有利的一面是
4708.e: The flat is small, but on the plus side it's two minutes from the station.  房子小，但好处是离车站只要两分钟。

4709.i: plus ça ˈchange (, plus c'est la même ˈchose) (from French, saying)
4709.cn: 万变不离其宗；换汤不换药
4709.e: New boss, same old rules — plus ça change, as my father used to say.  新老板，还是那套老规矩，正如我父亲常说的，万变不离其宗。

4710.i: the more it ˈchanges, the more it stays the ˈsame
4710.e: They renamed every department, but the more it changes, the more it stays the same.  他们把每个部门都改了名，可越变越是老样子。

4711.e: Dozens of taxis ply for hire outside the station until well past midnight.  几十辆出租车在车站外候客，一直到后半夜。

4712.cn: 从事本行；做自己的营生
4712.e: For thirty years he has plied his trade as a shoemaker on this corner.  三十年来他一直在这个街角做鞋匠营生。

4713.cn: 由偷猎者变成护猎人；角色反转的人
4713.e: As a former hacker now advising banks, he's a classic poacher turned gamekeeper.  他从前是黑客，如今给银行当顾问，典型的角色反转。

4714.e: After the repairs, I'm about three hundred pounds out of pocket.  修完之后，我大概倒贴了三百英镑。

4715.cn: 受某人控制；被某人操纵
4715.e: Everyone knew the inspector was in the developer's pocket.  谁都知道那个督察早被开发商收买了。

4716.e: She paid for the students' tickets out of her own pocket.  她自掏腰包给学生们买了票。

4717.e: Those two have lived in each other's pockets since primary school.  那两个人从小学起就形影不离。

4718.cn: 报应；善有善报，恶有恶报
4718.e: It was poetic justice that the thief's own car got stolen that night.  那晚小偷自己的车被偷了，真是报应。

4719.i: ask, tell, etc. sb point ˈblank
4719.e: I asked him point blank whether he had taken the money.  我直截了当地问他是不是拿了那笔钱。

4720.i: be on the ˈpoint of doing sth
4720.e: I was on the point of leaving when she finally called back.  我正要出门，她终于回了电话。

4721.e: Whether you like him is beside the point; he's the best candidate.  你喜不喜欢他不是重点，他是最合适的人选。

4722.e: Let me get straight to the point: we can't afford another delay.  我就直说了，我们再拖不起了。

4723.e: I still don't get the point of these endless weekly reports.  我到现在也不明白这些没完没了的周报有什么意义。

4724.e: You have a point there — we really should test it before launching.  你说得有道理，我们上线前确实该测一测。

4725.i: if/when it ˌcomes to the ˈpoint
4725.cn: 到了必须作决定的时候
4725.e: He talks tough, but when it comes to the point he always backs down.  他嘴上很硬，可真到了紧要关头总是退缩。

4726.e: In point of fact, she had already resigned two weeks before the scandal.  事实上，在丑闻爆发前两周她就已经辞职了。

4727.e: You've made your point, so let's move on to the next item.  你的意思已经说清楚了，我们继续下一项吧。

4728.i: make a ˈpoint of doing sth
4728.e: She makes a point of calling her mother every Sunday evening.  她每周日晚上都特意给母亲打电话。

4729.cn: 更重要的是；更中肯的是
4729.e: It's expensive and, more to the point, it doesn't even work properly.  它很贵，更要命的是，它根本用不好。

4730.e: Before you point a finger at me, check who left the door unlocked.  在你指责我之前，先查查是谁没锁门。

4731.e: Sarah will be your main point of contact while the project runs.  项目期间莎拉是你的主要联络人。

4732.e: Her essay uses that old photograph as its point of departure.  她的文章以那张老照片作为出发点。

4733.i: a ˌpoint of ˈhonour (BrE) (AmE a ˌpoint of ˈhonor)
4733.cn: 事关名节的事；关乎荣誉之举
4733.e: It was a point of honour for him to pay back every penny he owed.  把欠的每一分钱都还清，对他来说是事关名节的事。

4734.i: (get to, reach, etc.) the ˌpoint of ˌno reˈturn
4734.e: Once we sign this lease, we've reached the point of no return.  一旦签下这份租约，我们就没有退路了。

4735.e: From a parent's point of view, the new timetable is a nightmare.  从家长的角度看，新的时间表简直是噩梦。

4736.cn: 指明方向；预示发展趋势
4736.e: This small trial may point the way towards a cheaper treatment.  这项小规模试验可能为更便宜的疗法指明方向。

4737.cn: 理解并接受某人的观点
4737.e: I take your point about the cost, but safety has to come first.  你说的成本问题我接受，但安全必须放在第一位。

4738.e: Her answers were short, honest and very much to the point.  她的回答简短、坦诚，而且非常切中要害。

4739.i: to the ˈpoint of sth/of doing sth
4739.e: He was blunt to the point of rudeness during the whole interview.  整场面试他都直白得近乎无礼。

4740.e: I agree with you up to a point, but the data tells a different story.  我在一定程度上同意你，但数据说的是另一回事。

4741.i: have your ˈgood, ˈplus, etc. points
4741.e: The old flat was cold, but it had its good points, like the huge windows.  那套老公寓很冷，但也有好处，比如窗户特别大。

4742.cn: 恶意匿名信；匿名诽谤信
4742.e: She received a poison pen letter accusing her husband of stealing.  她收到一封匿名信，指控她丈夫偷东西。

4743.e: Come in and sit down — right, what's your poison tonight?  进来坐吧，说说，今晚想喝点什么？

4744.cn: 金杯毒酒；看似诱人实则棘手的事
4744.e: That promotion turned out to be a poisoned chalice for the young manager.  那次升职对这位年轻经理来说成了金杯毒酒。

4745.e: I had a poke around in the attic and found Dad's old records.  我在阁楼里翻了翻，找到了爸爸的旧唱片。

4746.i: take a ˈpoke at sb/sth (old-fashioned, AmE, informal)
4746.e: The comedian took a poke at politicians on both sides of the aisle.  那位喜剧演员把两党的政客都调侃了一遍。

4747.i: be up the ˈpole (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
4747.e: If you think I'll work three weekends in a row, you're up the pole.  你要是以为我会连上三个周末的班，那你是疯了。

4748.cn: 被政客当作争斗工具的问题
4748.e: School funding has become a political football again this election year.  在今年的选举年，学校拨款又成了政治斗争的筹码。

4749.e: The coronation was staged with all the pomp and circumstance you'd expect.  加冕典礼办得极尽隆重，正如人们预料的那样。

4750.e: My cousin has been living across the pond in Chicago for a decade.  我表哥在大西洋彼岸的芝加哥住了十年。

4751.e: Critics called the film a poor man's Godfather with worse dialogue.  影评人说这部片子是廉价版《教父》，台词还更差。

4752.e: When they married they were as poor as church mice, sharing one small room.  他们结婚时一贫如洗，挤在一间小屋里。

4753.cn: 受冷落的一方；无足轻重的角色
4753.e: In this company, marketing has always been the poor relation of sales.  在这家公司，市场部一直是销售部的陪衬。

4754.e: He joked that he'd leave the cottage to me when he popped his clogs.  他开玩笑说等他翘辫子了就把那间小屋留给我。

4755.e: He finally popped the question on the beach at sunset.  他终于在日落时的海滩上开口求婚了。

4756.e: By popular demand, the exhibition will stay open another two weeks.  应观众要求，展览将再延长两周。

4757.e: He did porridge for two years before turning his life around.  他坐了两年牢，之后彻底改变了自己的人生。

4758.e: The hostel was filthy, but any port in a storm at two in the morning.  那家旅舍很脏，可凌晨两点了，也只能将就。

4759.e: Our first port of call in Rome was a tiny café near the station.  我们到罗马的第一站是车站附近的一家小咖啡馆。

4760.e: She cleaned the whole house like a woman possessed before her in-laws arrived.  公婆来之前，她像着了魔一样把整间屋子打扫了一遍。

4761.e: He wrote like one possessed and finished the novel in six weeks.  他像着了魔一样写作，六周就写完了这部小说。

4762.i: what(ever) posˈsessed sb to do sth?
4762.cn: 究竟为什么会那样做；鬼迷心窍
4762.e: Whatever possessed you to tell the boss what we said at lunch?  你究竟是鬼迷心窍了，把午饭时说的话告诉老板？

4763.i: possession is nine points of the ˈlaw (saying)
4763.e: He won't return the trailer, and possession is nine points of the law.  他不肯还那辆拖车，而现实占有者往往占上风。

4764.i: possession is nine tenths/parts of the ˈlaw (saying)
4764.cn: 占有者在争讼中占上风
4764.e: She's living in the house already, and possession is nine tenths of the law.  她已经住进那房子了，占着的人总是占便宜。

4765.e: He couldn't pay the tax, so the state took possession of his land.  他交不起税，于是政府没收了他的土地。

4766.i: as quickly, much, soon, etc. as ˈpossible
4766.e: Send me the figures as soon as possible — the meeting is at nine.  尽快把数字发给我，会议九点开始。

4767.e: The kids played possum when their mother came to check on them.  妈妈来查看时，孩子们全都装睡。

4768.e: Dad will go postal if he sees what you did to the garage door.  爸爸要是看到你把车库门弄成这样，肯定暴跳如雷。

4769.e: Keep me posted on how your mother's operation goes.  你母亲手术的情况随时告诉我。

4770.e: That startup became the poster child for reckless spending.  那家创业公司成了乱花钱的典型。

4771.e: The messenger rode post-haste to the castle with the king's orders.  信使带着国王的命令火速赶往城堡。

4772.e: The garden has gone to pot since Grandpa stopped looking after it.  自从爷爷不再打理，这园子就荒了。

4773.i: the ˌpot calling the kettle ˈblack (saying, informal)
4773.cn: 五十步笑百步；锅笑壶黑
4773.e: You calling me lazy is the pot calling the kettle black.  你说我懒，真是五十步笑百步。

4774.e: We didn't book anywhere, so we'll just take pot luck tonight.  我们没订地方，今晚就碰碰运气吧。

4775.e: The whole schedule is in the melting pot until the funding is confirmed.  在资金落实之前，整个日程都还没定下来。

4776.e: Journalists took potshots at the mayor throughout the entire press conference.  整场记者会上，记者们不断向市长发难。

4777.cn: 近距离的随意射击；随口的抨击
4777.e: He took a potshot at the rabbit and missed it by a mile.  他朝兔子随手打了一枪，差得老远。

4778.i: (have, demand, claim, etc.) your pound of ˈflesh
4778.e: The landlord wanted his pound of flesh, right down to the last day's rent.  房东连最后一天的租金都要算清，一分不让。

4779.cn: 死要讨回的欠债；应得却苛刻的索取
4779.e: They lent us the money, but they'll want their pound of flesh eventually.  他们借了钱给我们，但迟早会连本带利讨回去。

4780.cn: 不顾情面地索取应得之物
4780.e: I didn't know work here was this hard — they really demand their pound of flesh.  我不知道在这里工作这么辛苦，他们简直不顾别人死活。

4781.e: In theory it's a great idea, but in practice nobody has the time.  理论上这主意很好，可实际上谁都没那个时间。

4782.e: I'm badly out of practice — I haven't touched the piano in years.  我手生得厉害，好几年没碰钢琴了。

4783.e: Your serve is getting better already; practice makes perfect.  你的发球已经有进步了，熟能生巧嘛。

4784.e: It's time to put all that theory into practice on a real project.  该把那些理论放到真实项目里去实践了。

4785.cn: 养成…的习惯；经常做某事
4785.e: Don't make a habit of borrowing money from your colleagues.  别养成向同事借钱的习惯。

4786.e: If you want the team to arrive early, practise what you preach.  想让团队早到，你自己得先做到。

4787.e: The critics praised her first novel to the skies.  评论家把她的第一部小说捧上了天。

4788.i: not have a ˈprayer (of doing sth)
4788.e: Without a lawyer, he doesn't have a prayer of winning this case.  没有律师，他打赢这场官司毫无希望。

4789.cn: 正是某人求之不得的东西
4789.e: A cheap flat near the office was the answer to my prayers.  办公室附近有间便宜公寓，正是我求之不得的。

4790.i: preach to the conˈverted (AmE also preach to the ˈchoir)
4790.cn: 对已信服的人说教；多此一举
4790.e: Telling me to recycle is preaching to the converted — I've done it for years.  跟我说要回收利用纯属多余，我做了好多年了。

4791.e: There's precious little food left in the fridge before payday.  发工资前，冰箱里剩下的吃的少得可怜。

4792.e: It happened last week — on Thursday evening, to be more precise.  这事发生在上周，更确切地说，是周四晚上。

4793.e: The school gives preference to children living within a mile.  这所学校优先录取一英里内居住的孩子。

4794.e: She chose the small college in preference to a famous university.  她宁愿选那所小学院，也不去名牌大学。

4795.cn: 意味深长的停顿（或沉默）
4795.e: After his question there was a pregnant pause that made everyone uneasy.  他问完之后是一阵意味深长的沉默，弄得大家都不自在。

4796.e: The offer is made without prejudice to any future claim.  此项提议不影响今后提出任何索赔。

4797.e: Parking spaces are at a premium in this part of town.  在城里这一带，停车位一位难求。

4798.e: This company puts a premium on honesty rather than clever sales talk.  这家公司看重的是诚实，而不是花哨的推销话术。

4799.e: Her early research prepared the ground for today's vaccines.  她早期的研究为如今的疫苗打下了基础。

4800.i: in sb's ˈpresence • in the presence of sb
4800.cn: 当着某人的面；在某人在场时
4800.e: He never swears in the presence of his grandmother.  他从不当着祖母的面说粗话。

4801.e: She asked them not to discuss the matter in her presence.  她要求他们不要当着她的面讨论这件事。

4802.cn: 让人感受到自己的存在（或影响）
4802.e: The new coach made his presence felt within the first week.  新教练第一周就让大家感受到了他的存在。

4803.e: She had the presence of mind to switch off the gas before running out.  她临危不乱，跑出去前先关掉了煤气。

4804.e: Twelve chairs, twelve name cards — all present and correct.  十二把椅子，十二张名牌，全都齐了。

4805.cn: 应到的都到了；如数到齐
4805.e: I've checked the list twice: all present and accounted for.  名单我核对了两遍，人全都到齐了。

4806.e: At present we have no plans to open a second shop.  目前我们没有开第二家店的打算。

4807.i: make a ˈpresent of sth (to sb)
4807.e: By leaving the gate open, we made a present of the bikes to any passing thief.  门开着没关，等于把自行车白送给过路的小偷。

4808.e: On present form, they'll be lucky to finish in the top ten.  就目前的状态看，他们能进前十就算走运。

4809.i: present company exˈcepted (also excepting present ˈcompany)
4809.e: Most managers here are useless — present company excepted, of course.  这里多数经理都不顶用，当然，在座各位除外。

4810.e: The museum traces the city's story from Roman times to the present day.  博物馆讲述了这座城市从罗马时代至今的历史。

4811.i: get/have a good, bad, etc. ˈpress
4811.e: The new tax has had a very bad press since it was announced.  这项新税自公布以来一直恶评如潮。

4812.e: The candidate spent all morning pressing the flesh in the market square.  候选人整个上午都在集市广场上与选民握手。

4813.e: She pressed her argument home until the committee finally agreed.  她一再强调自己的论点，直到委员会最终同意。

4814.cn: 乘胜追击；充分利用优势
4814.e: Two goals up, they pressed home their advantage in the second half.  领先两球后，他们在下半场乘胜追击。

4815.e: We pressed an old door into service as a table for the party.  我们把一扇旧门临时拿来当聚会的桌子。

4816.e: The gutter press hounded the family for weeks after the trial.  庭审后，低俗小报追着这家人纠缠了好几个星期。

4817.i: be pressed for ˈmoney, ˈspace, ˈtime, etc.
4817.e: I'm rather pressed for time, so let's keep this short.  我时间比较紧，咱们长话短说。

4818.i: put ˈpressure on sb (to do sth)
4818.cn: 向某人施加压力（要其做某事）
4818.e: They're putting pressure on him to resign before the report comes out.  他们正施压要他在报告公布前辞职。

4819.i: bring pressure to ˈbear (on sb) (to do sth)
4819.e: Local residents brought pressure to bear on the council to save the library.  当地居民向议会施压，要求保住图书馆。

4820.e: He makes silly mistakes when he's working under pressure.  他在压力下工作时会犯些低级错误。

4821.i: under false preˈtences (BrE) (AmE under false preˈtenses)
4821.e: He got into the building under false pretences, claiming to be an engineer.  他谎称自己是工程师，骗进了那栋大楼。

4822.cn: 不只有漂亮脸蛋；并非徒有其表
4822.e: She fixed the engine in ten minutes — not just a pretty face, then.  她十分钟就修好了发动机，看来可不只是长得好看。

4823.e: The kitchen after their cooking lesson was not a pretty sight.  上完烹饪课后的厨房，那场面惨不忍睹。

4824.e: The village in the snow was as pretty as a picture.  雪中的村庄美得像一幅画。

4825.e: I've pretty much finished the report; just the conclusion is left.  报告我差不多写完了，只剩结论部分。

4826.e: We were pretty near giving up when the rescue team arrived.  救援队赶到时，我们几乎已经要放弃了。

4827.e: That antique clock must have cost him a pretty penny.  那座古董钟一定花了他不少钱。

4828.cn: 预防胜于治疗；防患于未然
4828.e: Get the boiler serviced now — prevention is better than cure.  现在就把锅炉检修了吧，预防胜于补救。

4829.i: an ˌounce of preˈvention is worth a ˌpound of ˈcure (AmE) (saying)
4829.cn: 防患于未然胜过事后补救
4829.e: Back up your files today; an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.  今天就把文件备份了吧，防患于未然胜过事后补救。

4830.e: The director gave us a sneak preview of the final scene.  导演让我们提前看了最后一场戏。

4831.e: Elderly people often fall prey to phone scams like this one.  老年人常常成为这类电话诈骗的受害者。

4832.i: prey on sb's ˈmind (also ˌplay on sb's ˈmind)
4832.e: That argument with my sister has been preying on my mind all week.  和妹妹的那场争吵让我一整周都放不下。

4833.e: She wanted that gallery job at any price.  她不惜一切代价也要得到画廊那份工作。

4834.cn: 代价高昂；要付出很大代价
4834.e: You can get a table on Saturday night, but at a price.  周六晚上是能订到桌，不过价钱不便宜。

4835.e: To a refugee, a passport can be beyond price.  对难民来说，一本护照可能是无价之宝。

4836.cn: 无论如何也不；给多少钱也不干
4836.e: I wouldn't work for that man again, not at any price.  我不会再给那个人干活了，给多少钱也不行。

4837.e: The outlaw fled north with a price on his head.  那名逃犯带着悬赏令逃往北方。

4838.i: price yourself/sth out of the ˈmarket
4838.cn: 因要价过高而失去市场
4838.e: They priced themselves out of the market and lost every regular client.  他们要价太高，把市场做丢了，老客户全跑光了。

4839.e: It's hard to put a price on a good night's sleep.  一夜好眠的价值很难用钱衡量。

4840.e: What price fame if you can't walk down the street in peace?  要是连安静走在街上都做不到，出名又有什么用？

4841.i: prick your ˈconscience • your ˈconscience pricks you
4841.e: His conscience pricked him every time he walked past the beggar.  每次走过那个乞丐身边，他都会良心不安。

4842.i: ˌprick up your ˈears • your ˈears prick up
4842.e: The dog pricked up its ears the moment it heard the car outside.  一听到外面的车声，狗立刻竖起了耳朵。

4843.e: That vintage motorbike in the garage is his pride and joy.  车库里那辆老式摩托车是他的心头宝。

4844.e: He bragged all week about winning, and then lost badly — pride comes before a fall.  他吹了一周要赢，结果输得很惨，真是骄兵必败。

4845.e: Her grandmother's clock has pride of place on the mantelpiece.  祖母那座钟摆在壁炉台最显眼的位置。

4846.e: He takes real pride in keeping the old bookshop spotless.  他把那家旧书店打理得一尘不染，很以此为傲。

4847.e: Our new neighbour is far too prim and proper to enjoy a party like that.  我们的新邻居太一本正经了，不会喜欢那样的派对。

4848.e: The lead singer is a complete prima donna about hotel rooms.  那位主唱在酒店房间上简直是个难伺候的大牌。

4849.e: He gave up racing in the prime of his life to look after his father.  他在风华正茂时放弃了赛车，去照顾父亲。

4850.e: She was the prime mover behind the campaign to clean up the river.  她是这场治河运动背后的主要推动者。

4851.e: The government cut taxes to prime the pump during the downturn.  政府在经济下行时减税以刺激市场。

4852.i: the primrose ˈpath (to ruin, destruction, etc.) (literary)
4852.cn: 享乐之路；通向堕落的道路
4852.e: Easy money led the young star down the primrose path to ruin.  轻易得来的钱把这位年轻明星引上了毁灭之路。

4853.e: She's still waiting for Prince Charming to turn up at the bus stop.  她还在等着白马王子出现在公交站呢。

4854.e: They agreed in principle, but the details will take months.  他们原则上同意了，但细节还要谈上几个月。

4855.cn: 出于原则；根据道德准则
4855.e: He refuses to fly on principle because of the pollution.  出于原则，他因为污染问题拒绝坐飞机。

4856.e: It took her four years to get her poems into print.  她的诗歌用了四年才得以出版。

4857.e: Amazingly, that cookbook has stayed in print since 1962.  令人惊讶的是，那本菜谱从1962年起一直在印。

4858.e: The novel is out of print, so I hunted for it in second-hand shops.  这本小说已经绝版，我只好去二手书店找。

4859.e: My grandfather still trusts the printed word more than any website.  我祖父至今仍更相信白纸黑字，而不是网站。

4860.e: Get your priorities straight — sleep first, emails later.  分清主次吧，先睡觉，邮件晚点再说。

4861.e: In negotiations she takes no prisoners and everyone knows it.  谈判桌上她毫不留情，这一点人尽皆知。

4862.e: They hired a private eye to find out where the money had gone.  他们请了个私家侦探去查那笔钱的去向。

4863.e: The doctor asked politely whether he had any pain in his private parts.  医生客气地问他私处有没有疼痛。

4864.e: In all probability the train will be delayed again this evening.  今晚这趟车十有八九又要晚点。

4865.i: do you have a ˈproblem with that? (spoken)
4865.e: I'm taking Friday off. Do you have a problem with that?  我周五要请假，你对此有意见吗？

4866.e: If he forgot to book the room, that's not my problem.  他忘了订房间，那不关我的事。

4867.e: Could you pick me up at seven? No problem, see you then.  你能七点来接我吗？没问题，到时见。

4868.i: that's ˈyour, ˈhis, etc. problem (spoken, informal)
4868.cn: 那是你（或他等）自己的事
4868.e: You spent all your wages on shoes? That's your problem.  你把工资全花在鞋上了？那是你自己的事。

4869.cn: 你到底怎么了（表示不满）
4869.e: You've been snapping at everyone all morning — what's your problem?  你一上午对谁都没好气，你到底怎么了？

4870.cn: 有初期的小毛病；遇到起步困难
4870.e: The new app still has a few teething problems on older phones.  这款新应用在旧手机上还有些初期小毛病。

4871.e: Can you swap shifts with me on Tuesday? No probs.  周二能和我换个班吗？没问题。

4872.cn: 在（做某事）的过程中；同时
4872.e: He fixed the tap and flooded the kitchen in the process.  他修好了水龙头，同时也把厨房淹了。

4873.i: a/the prodigal ˈson (formal, disapproving or humorous)
4873.cn: 回头的浪子；改过自新的人
4873.e: The prodigal son returned after five years with no money and no job.  这位浪子五年后回来了，身无分文，也没工作。

4874.e: Students get half-price tickets on production of a valid card.  学生凭有效证件可买半价票。

4875.i: adopt, keep, etc. a ˌhigh/ˌlow ˈprofile
4875.cn: 保持高（或低）姿态；张扬（或低调）
4875.e: After the scandal he kept a low profile for almost a year.  丑闻之后，他低调了将近一年。

4876.e: In profile she looks exactly like her mother at that age.  从侧面看，她和她母亲那个年纪时一模一样。

4877.e: Get with the program, Dave — everyone else filed their reports yesterday.  戴夫，跟上节奏吧，别人昨天就交报告了。

4878.e: If you want to stay on this team, get with the programme.  想留在这个团队，就照规矩来。

4879.e: The coach told the players to get with the programme or leave.  教练告诉队员们要么照做，要么走人。

4880.cn: 延长痛苦；拖延难熬的局面
4880.e: Just tell me the result and don't prolong the agony.  直接告诉我结果吧，别再折磨我了。

4881.e: You'll regret selling that guitar, I can promise you.  卖掉那把吉他你会后悔的，我敢保证。

4882.e: The salesman promised us the earth and delivered almost nothing.  那个推销员对我们许下天大的承诺，结果几乎什么都没做到。

4883.e: For many migrants that city was the promised land of steady work.  对许多移民来说，那座城市就是有稳定工作的希望之乡。

4884.e: The first chapter promises well, though the ending is weak.  第一章很有看头，只是结尾差了些。

4885.i: the proof of the ˈpudding (is in the ˈeating) (saying)
4885.cn: 空谈不如实践；实践出真知
4885.e: The design looks clever, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating.  设计看着很巧妙，不过好不好用还得试了才知道。

4886.e: The video was proof positive that he had never left the building.  这段视频铁证如山，说明他根本没离开过大楼。

4887.e: He props up the bar every evening instead of looking for work.  他每天晚上都泡在酒吧里，也不去找工作。

4888.e: We got soaked good and proper walking home in that storm.  在那场暴雨里走回家，我们被淋了个透。

4889.i: a ˌprophet of ˈdoom • a ˈdoom merchant
4889.e: Ignore the prophets of doom; the shop is doing better every month.  别理那些唱衰的人，店里生意一个月比一个月好。

4890.e: It's one bad review — let's keep this in proportion.  不过是一条差评，咱们别小题大做。

4891.e: His anger was completely out of all proportion to the mistake.  他发的火跟这点小错完全不成比例。

4892.e: I'd like to propose a toast to the happy couple.  我提议为这对新人干杯。

4893.e: We spent the evening weighing up the pros and cons of moving abroad.  我们花了一晚上权衡出国的利弊。

4894.e: She signed the new contract under protest and told everyone so.  她很不情愿地签了新合同，还逢人便说。

4895.e: Her parents did us proud with a huge Sunday lunch.  她父母做了一大桌周日午餐，把我们招待得非常周到。

4896.e: The choir did the school proud at the national competition.  合唱团在全国比赛上为学校争了光。

4897.i: the exˈception that proves the ˈrule
4897.cn: 例外恰恰证明规律的存在
4897.e: He's never late, so today is the exception that proves the rule.  他从不迟到，所以今天算是那个证明规律的例外。

4898.e: A fox was on the prowl behind the bins again last night.  昨晚又有只狐狸在垃圾桶后面转悠。

4899.cn: 最佳时机；最恰当的时刻
4899.e: He waited for the psychological moment before asking for a raise.  他一直等到最合适的时机才开口要求加薪。

4900.e: They went on a pub crawl through the old town on his birthday.  他生日那天，他们在老城区一家家酒吧喝了过来。

4901.cn: 人人皆知；成为公众话题
4901.e: Once you're famous, your private life becomes public property.  一旦出了名，你的私生活就成了公众谈资。

4902.e: The company went public last spring and the shares doubled.  这家公司去年春天上市，股价翻了一番。

4903.e: Raising children in the public eye can't be easy for them.  在公众目光下养育孩子对他们来说肯定不容易。

4904.cn: 头号公敌；危害最大的人（或事物）
4904.e: Sugar has become public enemy number one for many nutritionists.  在许多营养学家眼中，糖已成为头号公敌。

4905.e: He came up the last flight of stairs puffing and panting.  他爬上最后一段楼梯时已经气喘吁吁。

4906.i: be puffed up with ˈpride, etc.
4906.e: The boy was puffed up with pride after scoring the winning goal.  打进制胜球后，那男孩得意得不得了。

4907.e: The lads were clearly on the pull in that nightclub on Friday.  周五在那家夜店，几个小伙子明显是去找姑娘的。

4908.i: pull the ˌcarpet/ˌrug out from under sb's ˈfeet (informal)
4908.cn: 突然停止对某人的支持
4908.e: The sponsors pulled the rug out from under our feet three weeks before opening.  开幕前三周，赞助方突然撤了对我们的支持。

4909.i: pull the ˈrug out from under sb's feet (informal)
4909.cn: 突然撤走支持；釜底抽薪
4909.e: Cutting the budget now pulls the rug out from under the whole research team.  现在砍预算等于把整个研究团队的支撑抽走了。

4910.i: pull the ˈcarpet out from under sb's feet (informal)
4910.cn: 突然不再帮助（或支持）某人
4910.e: The bank has pulled the carpet out from under his feet, so he must sell the business.  银行突然停止支持他，他只能卖掉企业了。

4911.e: Stop pulling faces at your brother and eat your dinner.  别对你弟弟做鬼脸了，快吃饭。

4912.e: The dealer pulled a fast one on us with the mileage.  那个车商在里程数上把我们给骗了。

4913.cn: 开某人的玩笑；捉弄某人
4913.e: Relax, nobody's been fired — I was only pulling your leg.  别紧张，没人被解雇，我只是逗你玩。

4914.i: pull the ˈother one (— it's got ˈbells on!) (BrE, informal)
4914.e: You cooked this yourself? Pull the other one, it's got bells on.  这是你自己做的？别逗了，我才不信。

4915.e: I've been offered a job in New York. Pull the other one!  我在纽约找到工作了。别逗了！

4916.cn: 竭尽全力；使出浑身解数
4916.e: The staff pulled out all the stops to get the shop open on time.  员工们使出了浑身解数，让店铺按时开张。

4917.e: Head office pulled the plug on the project after two bad quarters.  两个季度业绩糟糕后，总部叫停了这个项目。

4918.e: The review didn't pull any punches about the film's terrible script.  这篇影评对片子糟糕的剧本毫不留情。

4919.i: pull sth/a ˌrabbit out of the ˈhat (informal)
4919.cn: 突然想出妙计；出奇制胜
4919.e: With ten minutes left, the coach pulled a rabbit out of the hat.  比赛还剩十分钟，教练突然使出了一招妙棋。

4920.e: He pulled rank and took the only window office for himself.  他仗着职位高，把唯一那间靠窗的办公室占为己有。

4921.e: You'd better pull your socks up before the exams next month.  下个月就要考试了，你最好赶紧振作起来。

4922.i: pull ˈstrings (for sb) (AmE also pull ˈwires)
4922.e: His uncle pulled strings to get him an interview at the ministry.  他叔叔走后门给他弄了个部里的面试机会。

4923.e: The chairman may be new, but his father still pulls the strings.  董事长虽然是新的，可幕后掌权的还是他父亲。

4924.e: They pulled up stakes in Ohio and started over in Texas.  他们离开俄亥俄，搬到得州重新开始。

4925.cn: 尽自己的一份力；做好分内事
4925.e: Everyone shares the rent, so everyone has to pull their weight.  房租大家分摊，所以每个人都得出力。

4926.i: pull the ˈwool over sb's eyes (informal)
4926.e: Don't try to pull the wool over my eyes — I saw the receipt.  别想蒙我，我看到收据了。

4927.e: Pull yourself together — the interview starts in five minutes.  振作点，面试五分钟后就开始了。

4928.e: Getting a straight answer out of him is like pulling teeth.  想从他嘴里得到一句实话，比登天还难。

4929.cn: 给某人大量注射（或灌输）
4929.e: They pumped him full of painkillers before moving him.  搬动他之前，他们给他打了大量止痛药。

4930.e: He pumps iron at the gym every morning before work.  他每天上班前都在健身房练器械。

4931.e: Doctors had to pump the child's stomach after she swallowed the pills.  孩子吞了药片后，医生只好给她洗胃。

4932.i: he, she, etc. couldn't ˌpunch his, her, etc. way out of a paper ˈbag (informal, humorous)
4932.e: Their new striker couldn't punch his way out of a paper bag.  他们新来的前锋简直是软脚虾。

4933.i: couldn't ˌpunch your way out of a paper ˈbag (informal, humorous)
4933.e: He talks tough but couldn't punch his way out of a paper bag.  他嘴上很横，其实一点本事也没有。

4934.cn: 做超出（或低于）自身能力的事
4934.e: The little bakery punches well above its weight in national awards.  这家小面包店在全国评奖中的表现远超其规模。

4935.i: sell sb/buy a ˈpup (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
4935.cn: 把次货卖给某人；买到次货
4935.e: That second-hand laptop died in a week — I've been sold a pup.  那台二手笔记本一周就坏了，我买到次品了。

4936.e: What happened at the border was theft, pure and simple.  边境上发生的事就是抢劫，不折不扣。

4937.i: (as) pure as the driven ˈsnow (often humorous)
4937.e: He acts as pure as the driven snow, but I know about the expenses.  他装得一尘不染，可我知道那些报销的事。

4938.e: She spilled the drink on his shirt on purpose, I'm certain of it.  我敢肯定，她是故意把饮料洒在他衬衫上的。

4939.cn: 收效甚微（或很大、有些、毫无）
4939.e: We argued with the officials for hours, to no purpose at all.  我们和官员们争了几个小时，一点用也没有。

4940.e: In that family it's the grandmother who holds the purse strings.  在那个家里，管钱的是奶奶。

4941.i: make a silk ˈpurse out of a ˈsow's ear (saying)
4941.cn: 化腐朽为神奇（通常指办不到）
4941.e: With that script, even a great cast can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.  就那个剧本，再好的演员也无法化腐朽为神奇。

4942.e: He got the push after arguing with a customer in front of everyone.  他当众和顾客吵架，结果被炒了。

4943.cn: 迫不得已时；到了关键时刻
4943.e: If push comes to shove, we can always sleep in the car.  实在不行，我们还可以睡车里。

4944.e: They really pushed the boat out for their daughter's wedding.  女儿结婚，他们真是花了大钱。

4945.i: ˌpush sb's ˈbuttons (also ˌpress sb's ˈbuttons especially in BrE) (informal)
4945.cn: 触动某人情绪；惹某人发作
4945.e: My brother knows exactly how to push my buttons at dinner.  我弟弟最清楚吃饭时怎么惹毛我。

4946.e: The band keeps pushing the envelope with every new album.  这支乐队每出一张新专辑都在突破边界。

4947.e: You got away with it once; don't push your luck again.  你侥幸过了一次，别再冒险了。

4948.i: push sth to the ˌback of your ˈmind
4948.cn: 把…抛到脑后；刻意不去想
4948.e: She pushed the diagnosis to the back of her mind and went to work.  她把诊断结果抛到脑后，照常去上班。

4949.e: Sales dipped for one month and management pressed the panic button.  销售额只降了一个月，管理层就慌了神。

4950.e: He's pushing fifty but still plays football every Sunday morning.  他快五十了，还是每周日上午踢球。

4951.e: By the time that law changes, I'll be pushing up the daisies.  等那条法律改了，我坟头草都长高了。

4952.cn: 私生活不检点；到处乱搞
4952.e: There were nasty rumours at work that he put it about a lot.  单位里有难听的传言，说他私生活很乱。

4953.e: She isn't really that upset — she's putting it on for sympathy.  她其实没那么难过，是装出来博同情的。

4954.cn: 来握握手吧（表示同意或赞赏）
4954.e: You agree we should split the profit fifty-fifty? Put it there!  你同意利润五五分？来，握个手！

4955.i: put sb ˈthrough it (especially BrE, informal)
4955.cn: 使某人吃苦头；让某人经受考验
4955.e: The interview panel really put me through it for two hours.  面试小组足足折腾了我两个小时。

4956.e: She earns more than the rest of the department put together.  她挣的比部门其他人加起来还多。

4957.cn: 任人摆布；对某人百依百顺
4957.e: One smile from his granddaughter and he's putty in her hands.  孙女一笑，他就任由她摆布了。

4958.e: The whole auction was a put-up job to raise the price.  整场拍卖就是个抬价的局。

4959.e: They won the case but lost their savings — a Pyrrhic victory.  他们赢了官司却赔光积蓄，实在是得不偿失。

4960.e: Nobody complained, nobody left early, QED: the talk was good.  没人抱怨，没人早退，可见这场讲座不错。

4961.e: I'm in a quandary about whether to tell her the truth.  要不要告诉她实情，我实在左右为难。

4962.i: a quantum ˈleap (also a quantum ˈjump less frequent)
4962.e: This treatment represents a quantum leap in cancer care.  这种疗法是癌症治疗上的一次巨大飞跃。

4963.i: get/pour/put a ˌquart into a pint ˈpot (BrE)
4963.e: Fitting six people in that car is putting a quart into a pint pot.  那车里塞六个人，简直是强人所难。

4964.e: It's easy to be a Monday morning quarterback after the deal collapses.  交易谈崩之后，谁都能当事后诸葛亮。

4965.e: You only notice the cracks when you see the painting at close quarters.  只有近距离看这幅画，才会注意到那些裂纹。

4966.cn: 对某人摆架子；盛气凌人
4966.e: She queens it over the junior staff whenever the manager is away.  经理一不在，她就对新员工颐指气使。

4967.i: queer sb's ˈpitch • queer the ˈpitch (for sb) (BrE, informal)
4967.cn: 破坏某人的计划；从中作梗
4967.e: Announcing his own plan early really queered the pitch for us.  他提前公布自己的方案，把我们的计划搅黄了。

4968.e: The caretaker is a queer fish, but he's kind to the children.  那位看门人是个怪人，不过对孩子们很好。

4969.e: She is beyond question the best pianist in the school.  她无疑是全校最好的钢琴手。

4970.e: The missing receipts call his honesty into question.  丢失的收据让人怀疑他是否诚实。

4971.e: Why is the deadline a Friday? Good question — nobody knows.  为什么截止日定在周五？问得好，没人知道。

4972.e: The evening in question, he was three hundred miles away.  在所说的那个晚上，他在三百英里之外。

4973.i: it's (just, etc.) a ˈquestion of sth
4973.e: It's just a question of finding the right person for the job.  这只不过是找到合适人选的问题。

4974.e: Another loan is out of the question until you clear this one.  在你还清这笔之前，再贷一笔想都别想。

4975.i: a ˈquestion mark hangs over sb/sth
4975.e: A question mark hangs over the future of the whole department.  整个部门的前途都还是个问号。

4976.i: there's a ˈquestion mark (hanging) over sb/sth
4976.e: There's a question mark hanging over whether the stadium will be finished.  体育场能否完工还是个问号。

4977.i: there's a ˈquestion mark over sth
4977.e: There's a question mark over his loyalty to the company.  他对公司是否忠诚还是个问号。

4978.i: there's some/no question of sth/of doing sth
4978.e: There's no question of us moving house before the baby arrives.  在孩子出生前，我们不可能搬家。

4979.cn: 毫无异议地；不加质疑地
4979.e: The young soldiers followed every one of his orders without question.  年轻士兵们不加质疑地执行了他的每一道命令。

4980.cn: 深深刺痛某人；伤到某人痛处
4980.e: Her remark about his cooking cut him to the quick.  她那句关于他厨艺的话深深刺伤了他。
