4981.e: My uncle has a quick temper but he calms down just as fast.  我叔叔脾气挺急，不过消气也快。

4982.e: I'll do a quick and dirty fix now and rewrite it properly later.  我先临时补一下，回头再好好重写。

4983.e: Quick as a flash, she caught the glass before it hit the floor.  说时迟那时快，她在杯子落地前一把接住了。

4984.e: Right, quick march everyone, the bus leaves in three minutes.  好了，大家快走，公交三分钟后就开。

4985.e: The sergeant shouted 'Quick march!' and the whole line moved off.  中士喊了一声“齐步走”，整队人马就出发了。

4986.e: Fancy a quick one at the pub before your train?  火车前去酒吧快喝一杯怎么样？

4987.e: He's only in this business to make a fast buck.  他做这行只是为了捞快钱。

4988.e: They'll help with the paperwork, but expect a quid pro quo later.  他们会帮着办手续，但以后会要回报的。

4989.i: not the full ˈquid (AustralE, NZE, informal)
4989.e: People say he's not the full quid, but he's sharper than he looks.  人家说他脑子不太灵光，其实他精着呢。

4990.e: If the flat sells at that price, we're quids in.  房子要是能卖到那个价，我们就赚翻了。

4991.i: keep ˈquiet about sth • keep sth ˈquiet
4991.e: Let's keep the party quiet until her birthday morning.  聚会的事先保密，到她生日那天早上再说。

4992.i: on the ˈquiet (also on the ˈq.t. old-fashioned)
4992.e: He'd been taking Spanish lessons on the quiet for months.  他偷偷学了好几个月西班牙语。

4993.e: The children were as quiet as mice while the baby slept.  宝宝睡觉时，孩子们安静得像小老鼠。

4994.e: Wearing trainers to the funeral was not quite the thing.  穿运动鞋去参加葬礼不太得体。

4995.e: That was quite a speech — half the room was in tears.  那真是一场了不起的演讲，半屋子人都哭了。

4996.i: quite the ˈbest, the ˈworst, etc. sth (informal)
4996.cn: 绝对是最好（或最差等）的
4996.e: That was quite the worst meal I've eaten all year.  那绝对是我今年吃过的最难吃的一顿饭。

4997.i: quite a ˈfew (BrE also a good ˈfew)
4997.e: Quite a few of my classmates have already moved abroad.  我不少同学都已经移居国外了。

4998.e: So the whole plan depends on the weather? Quite so.  这么说整个计划全看天气？正是如此。

4999.e: We waited quite some time before anyone came to the desk.  我们等了好一阵子才有人到柜台来。

5000.e: You bought lunch and I paid for the taxi, so we're quits.  你请了午饭，我付了车费，咱俩两清了。

5001.e: He called it a quote friendly discussion unquote, which it definitely wasn't.  他说那是场所谓的“友好讨论”，其实根本不是。

5002.e: It was a race against time to get the roof on before the storm.  要在暴风雨来临前把屋顶盖好，真是一场与时间的赛跑。

5003.e: Cutting wages again would only start a race to the bottom.  再降工资只会引发一场恶性的逐底竞争。

5004.e: The old farmhouse has gone to rack and ruin since they left.  他们搬走后，那栋老农舍已经破败不堪。

5170.e: The government has put its own housing policy into reverse this month.  政府本月把自己的住房政策来了个大转向。

5171.e: Just do the same steps in reverse and the shelf comes apart easily.  把步骤倒过来做，架子很容易就拆开了。

5172.e: He behaved for a fortnight, then reverted to type and skipped training again.  他老实了两周，就故态复萌，又翘了训练。

5173.i: have a hide/skin like a rhiˈnoceros (informal)
5173.cn: 脸皮极厚；不怕别人批评
5173.e: You need a skin like a rhinoceros to survive in this newsroom.  在这个新闻编辑室待下去，你得脸皮厚得像犀牛皮。

5174.i: there's no ˌrhyme or ˈreason to/for sth
5174.cn: 毫无道理可言；莫名其妙
5174.e: There's no rhyme or reason to the way this office allocates parking spaces.  这家公司分配车位毫无道理可言。

5175.e: She stopped speaking to me without rhyme or reason halfway through the term.  学期过半时她莫名其妙就不跟我说话了。

5176.i: cut, tear, etc. sth to ˈribbons
5176.cn: 把…撕成碎片；驳得体无完肤
5176.e: The wind tore our old tent to ribbons during the night.  夜里大风把我们的旧帐篷撕成了碎片。

5177.e: His uncle is as rich as Croesus but still drives a rusty van.  他叔叔富得流油，却还开着辆生锈的货车。

5178.cn: 真是荒唐；亏你说得出口
5178.e: He's calling me lazy? That's rich, coming from someone who naps daily.  他说我懒？他天天睡午觉，真好意思。

5179.e: I'll be glad to be rid of this cough before the holidays.  假期前能摆脱这咳嗽，我就谢天谢地了。

5180.e: We finally got rid of that broken sofa in the spare room.  我们终于把客房那张破沙发处理掉了。

5181.cn: 总算摆脱了；谢天谢地走了
5181.e: The noisy tenants upstairs have moved out at last — good riddance!  楼上吵闹的租客终于搬走了，真是谢天谢地！

5182.cn: 充斥；布满（尤指不好的东西）
5182.e: The report was riddled with errors and had to be written all over again.  报告错误百出，只好重写。

5183.e: I don't really care who wins; I'm just along for the ride.  我其实不在乎谁赢，只是来凑个热闹。

5184.i: have/give sb a rough/an easy ˈride (informal)
5184.e: The new coach had a rough ride from the fans all season.  新教练整个赛季都被球迷刁难。

5185.e: I noticed the mistake but decided to let it ride for now.  我发现了错误，但决定暂时先不追究。

5186.cn: 处于鼎盛时期；趁势大获成功
5186.e: The band is riding the crest of a wave after that festival performance.  那场音乐节演出后，乐队正处在事业顶峰。

5187.e: Someone has to ride herd on these interns or nothing ever gets finished.  得有人盯着这些实习生，不然什么都做不完。

5188.e: The developers rode roughshod over every objection the local residents raised.  开发商对当地居民的反对意见全然不顾。

5189.e: The manager ran roughshod over the committee and signed the contract himself.  经理无视委员会，自己把合同签了。

5190.e: My little brother always shouts that he gets to ride shotgun.  我弟弟总抢着喊要坐副驾驶。

5191.cn: 趁…之势；受益于某种潮流
5191.e: She rode a wave of public sympathy all the way into the mayor's office.  她借着一股民意同情的浪潮当上了市长。

5192.e: That mechanic took us for a ride and charged for parts he never fitted.  那修车师傅骗了我们，收了根本没装的零件钱。

5193.e: The bill will have a bumpy ride through parliament next month.  这项法案下月在议会将历经波折。

5194.e: Borrowing that much to open a second shop, he's riding for a fall.  借那么多钱开第二家店，他这是自找麻烦。

5195.cn: 春风得意；很成功很自信
5195.e: The team is riding high after four straight wins away from home.  客场四连胜后，球队正春风得意。

5196.cn: 依法有权；作为合法权利
5196.e: Every employee here gets four weeks' paid holiday as of right.  这里每位员工依法享有四周带薪假。

5197.e: That's all right — anyone could have knocked that glass over.  没关系，谁都可能碰倒那个杯子。

5198.cn: 有些人就是走运（表示羡慕）
5198.e: Three weeks in Italy? It's all right for some, isn't it?  去意大利三周？有些人可真走运啊。

5199.cn: 随声附和；口头上表示支持
5199.e: The minister made all the right noises but promised no extra money.  部长说得很好听，却没承诺增加一分钱。

5200.e: The plumber came back the next day and put everything right.  水管工第二天回来把问题都修好了。

5201.cn: 纠正某人的错误看法；澄清事实
5201.e: I thought the museum opened on Mondays, but she soon put me right.  我以为博物馆周一开门，她很快纠正了我。

5202.e: Right you are, I'll pick the kids up at four then.  好的，那我四点去接孩子。

5203.i: right and ˈleft • left and ˈright
5203.e: He was handing out free samples right and left outside the station.  他在车站外到处派发免费样品。

5204.e: A night's sleep and a hot meal and he'll be right as rain.  睡一觉再吃顿热饭，他就好利索了。

5205.e: Tell the driver to turn round and come back here right away.  叫司机马上掉头回来。

5206.e: It's cold right enough, but at least the rain has finally stopped.  确实挺冷，不过雨总算停了。

5207.e: I can't talk right now — I'm halfway through a job interview.  我现在没法说话，正在面试中。

5208.cn: 说得对，好极了；政治观点激进的
5208.e: Right on! That's exactly what this neighbourhood has needed for years.  说得好！这正是这个社区多年来需要的。

5209.e: Make sure the box stays right side up or the cake will collapse.  务必让盒子正面朝上，不然蛋糕会塌。

5210.cn: 纠正错误；弥补过失；平反
5210.e: The apology came thirty years late, but it did right an old wrong.  道歉迟了三十年，但总算弥补了旧日的过失。

5211.i: see sb (all) ˈright (AmE also do sb ˈright)
5211.cn: 不亏待某人；保证某人得到应得的
5211.e: Help me move the piano and I'll see you right afterwards.  帮我搬钢琴，事后我不会亏待你。

5212.cn: 没事的；一切都会好起来
5212.e: The tyre's a bit flat, but she'll be right for the drive home.  轮胎有点瘪，不过开回家没问题。

5213.e: Too right the tickets are overpriced — I'm not paying that again.  票价确实太贵了，我不会再花这钱。

5214.i: would ˌgive your right ˈarm for sth/to do sth
5214.e: I'd give my right arm for a quiet weekend with no phone calls.  我愿付出一切换一个没有电话打扰的周末。

5215.e: Their offer and ours are at least in the same ballpark now.  他们的报价和我们的现在总算差不多了。

5216.e: For twenty years he was the director's right-hand man at the theatre.  二十年来，他一直是剧院院长的得力助手。

5217.e: By rights that promotion should have gone to someone with more experience.  按理说，那次升职应该给更有经验的人。

5218.e: It took the new head two years to put the school to rights.  新校长花了两年才把学校整顿好。

5219.e: You're perfectly within your rights to ask for a written receipt.  你完全有权索要书面收据。

5220.e: Don't get all riled up about a parking ticket; just pay it.  别为一张罚单气成这样，交了就是。

5221.e: Give me a ring when you get home so I stop worrying.  你到家给我打个电话，我好放心。

5222.cn: 听起来耳熟；引起模糊的回忆
5222.e: That name rings a bell, but I can't picture his face at all.  这名字听着耳熟，可我完全想不起他长什么样。

5223.e: She rings the changes on the same three recipes all winter long.  整个冬天她就靠那三个菜谱变着花样做。

5224.e: His warning about the deadline was still ringing in my ears.  他关于截止日期的警告仍在我耳边回响。

5225.e: The phone has been ringing off the hook since the story went online.  报道上线后，电话就没停过。

5226.i: ring out the ˌold (year) and ˌring in the ˈnew
5226.e: We gather on the hill each December to ring out the old and ring in the new.  每年十二月我们都聚在山上辞旧迎新。

5227.e: Fireworks over the harbour will ring in the new year at midnight.  午夜港口的烟花将迎来新年。

5228.cn: 听起来真实（或虚假、空洞）
5228.e: His apology didn't ring true to anyone who had heard the recording.  听过录音的人都觉得他的道歉不真诚。

5229.cn: 成功的良机；难得的机会
5229.e: She grabbed the brass ring and moved to New York at twenty-two.  她抓住良机，二十二岁就搬去了纽约。

5230.e: The young winger ran rings around their defence for ninety minutes.  这位年轻边锋九十分钟里把对方后防耍得团团转。

5231.cn: 处于绝佳观看位置；近距离目睹
5231.e: Living opposite the town hall, we had a ringside seat for the protest.  住在市政厅对面，我们近距离目睹了这场抗议。

5232.cn: 撒野失控；（想象等）放任驰骋
5232.e: The children ran riot in the garden while their parents chatted indoors.  父母在屋里聊天，孩子们在花园里撒了欢。

5233.e: Once we hit the motorway he let the old van rip.  一上高速，他就让那辆旧货车撒开了跑。

5234.cn: 尽情发泄；毫无顾忌地大讲（或大干）
5234.e: She let rip at the council about the terrible state of the roads.  她对着议会大吐苦水，痛批路况糟糕。

5235.i: rip sb/sth aˈpart/to ˈshreds, ˈbits, etc.
5235.e: The reviewers ripped his second album to shreds within a single day.  乐评人一天之内就把他的第二张专辑批得体无完肤。

5236.i: at/to a ˈripe old age • at/to the ripe old age of...
5236.e: Her grandfather kept cycling to market to a ripe old age.  她祖父到了高龄还骑车去赶集。

5237.e: One factory closing had a ripple effect on shops across the whole town.  一家工厂关闭，对全镇商铺产生了连锁反应。

5238.i: get a ˈrise out of sb
5238.cn: 故意惹恼某人；逗某人发火
5238.e: He only says that to get a rise out of his sister.  他那么说只是为了逗他姐姐上火。

5239.i: get a ˈrise out of sb (informal)
5239.cn: 把某人惹火；逗某人急眼
5239.e: She always got a rise out of him by copying his strong accent.  她总学他的口音说话，把他惹得发火。

5240.e: The delay gave rise to rumours that the project had been cancelled.  延期引发了项目已被取消的传言。

5241.e: Rise and shine! The bus to the airport leaves in forty minutes.  快起床！去机场的车四十分钟后就走。

5242.e: The club rose from the ashes of bankruptcy and won promotion twice.  俱乐部从破产中重生，两次冲级成功。

5243.e: He teased her about her cooking, but she refused to rise to the bait.  他拿她做的饭打趣，她却不上他的当。

5244.cn: 从容应对难局；不负所望
5244.e: The understudy rose to the occasion and got a standing ovation.  替补演员临场发挥出色，赢得全场起立鼓掌。

5245.i: a rising ˌtide lifts all ˈboats (saying, especially AmE) (politics)
5245.cn: 水涨船高；经济向好人人受益
5245.e: The mayor argued that a rising tide lifts all boats in the local economy.  市长认为地方经济好转会让所有人受益。

5246.e: Thousands of homes are at risk of flooding along this stretch of coast.  这段海岸沿线有数千户住宅面临水淹风险。

5247.i: at the ˈrisk of doing sth
5247.cn: 冒着…的风险（引出可能冒犯的话）
5247.e: At the risk of sounding rude, that shirt really doesn't suit you.  恕我直言，那件衬衫真的不适合你。

5248.cn: 冒着伤害自己（或他人）的危险
5248.e: He pulled the driver out at considerable risk to himself.  他冒着极大危险把司机拖了出来。

5249.i: do sth at your ˌown ˈrisk
5249.e: You can swim beyond the buoys, but you do so at your own risk.  你可以游到浮标外，但风险自担。

5250.e: Firefighters risk life and limb every time that alarm goes off.  每次警铃响起，消防员都冒着生命危险。

5251.e: I'm not risking my neck climbing that ladder in this wind.  这么大风，我可不冒险爬那梯子。

5252.i: run the ˈrisk (of doing sth) • run ˈrisks
5252.e: Post it today or you run the risk of missing her birthday.  今天就寄，不然可能赶不上她的生日。

5253.e: We don't want to run the risk of losing their business over this.  我们不想冒因此丢掉这笔生意的风险。

5254.e: Every investor has to take risks; the trick is choosing which ones.  投资人都得冒险，关键是选对哪些险值得冒。

5255.cn: 呆立不动；吓得挪不开步
5255.e: I was riveted to the spot when the bear stepped onto the path.  熊走上小路时，我吓得动弹不得。

5256.e: My car's been off the road for a fortnight waiting for a part.  我的车等零件已经趴窝两周了。

5257.cn: 在途中；（尤指）在长途巡演旅行中
5257.e: The band has been on the road for eight months without a break.  乐队已连续巡演了八个月没休息。

5258.i: on the ˌroad to reˈcovery, ˈstardom, etc.
5258.cn: 走在康复（或成名等）的路上
5258.e: After the operation she's firmly on the road to recovery now.  手术后她正稳步走向康复。

5259.i: on the ˌroad to ˈruin, diˈsaster, etc.
5259.e: Borrowing more to cover old debts puts you on the road to ruin.  借新债还旧债只会把你推向毁灭。

5260.i: be on the ˌroad to diˈsaster
5260.e: Ignoring the safety reports put the whole plant on the road to disaster.  无视安全报告，让整个工厂走上了灾难之路。

5261.e: Stay for one for the road before you head off into the snow.  走进雪地前，再喝一杯上路酒吧。

5262.e: Some road hog overtook us on the bend and nearly caused a crash.  有个莽撞司机在弯道超车，差点撞上。

5263.i: the road to ˌhell is paved with good inˈtentions (saying)
5263.cn: 光有善意无用；好心未必办成好事
5263.e: He meant to help, but the road to hell is paved with good intentions.  他本想帮忙，可空有好意于事无补。

5264.cn: 良好的意愿；未付诸行动的善意
5264.e: The charity was built on good intentions but almost no practical planning.  这家慈善机构全凭一腔善意，几乎没有实际规划。

5265.e: The umbrella sellers did a roaring trade during yesterday's sudden downpour.  昨天突降暴雨，卖伞的生意火爆。

5266.e: He came home roaring drunk and woke the entire street singing.  他烂醉如泥地回家，唱歌吵醒了整条街。

5267.e: The goalkeeper got a roasting from his manager at half-time.  守门员中场休息时被主教练痛骂了一顿。

5268.cn: 骗取某人大量钱财；向某人漫天要价
5268.e: That garage robbed us blind over a simple exhaust repair.  那家修车行修个排气管就把我们宰惨了。

5269.cn: 老牛吃嫩草（与年龄小很多的人交往）
5269.e: His new girlfriend is twenty-three — everyone says he's robbing the cradle.  他新女友才二十三，大家都说他老牛吃嫩草。

5270.cn: 与比自己年轻很多的人恋爱
5270.e: Stop teasing me about cradle-robbing; she's only four years younger.  别再拿老牛吃嫩草打趣我了，她才小四岁。

5271.cn: 与年轻得多的人恋爱的人
5271.e: His friends jokingly call him a cradle-robber whenever she picks him up.  每次她来接他，朋友们都开玩笑叫他老牛吃嫩草。

5272.cn: 拆东墙补西墙；借新债还旧账
5272.e: Paying the credit card with another loan is just robbing Peter to pay Paul.  用另一笔贷款还信用卡，纯属拆东墙补西墙。

5273.i: before you can say Jack ˈRobinson (old-fashioned)
5273.e: Before you could say Jack Robinson, the whole cake had disappeared.  一眨眼工夫，整个蛋糕就没了。

5274.i: (caught/stuck) between a ˌrock and a ˈhard place
5274.e: Caught between a rock and a hard place, she resigned rather than choose.  进退两难之下，她索性辞职了。

5275.cn: 跌至谷底；降到最低水平
5275.e: House prices in the village hit rock bottom two winters ago.  村里的房价在两个冬天前跌到了谷底。

5276.e: I really hit rock bottom after my marriage broke up last spring.  去年春天婚姻破裂后，我的人生跌到了谷底。

5277.e: For rock-bottom prices on sofas, come to MacArthur's Furniture this weekend.  要买最便宜的沙发，本周末来麦克阿瑟家具店。

5278.e: Nobody wanted to rock the boat so close to the merger.  合并在即，谁也不想惹事。

5279.i: ˌoff your ˈrocker (informal, spoken, especially BrE)
5279.e: You're off your rocker if you think I'm cycling home in this.  这种天气你以为我会骑车回家？你疯了吧。

5280.e: The editor gave the whole team a rocket over that front-page mistake.  编辑因头版那个错误把全组痛骂了一顿。

5281.e: Changing a tyre isn't rocket science; I'll show you in five minutes.  换轮胎不难，我五分钟就能教会你。

5282.i: you don't have to be a ˈrocket scientist (to do sth)
5282.cn: 用不着多聪明就懂；显而易见
5282.e: You don't have to be a rocket scientist to see this plan will fail.  用不着多聪明也能看出这个计划会失败。

5283.i: it doesn't take a ˈrocket scientist (to do sth)
5283.cn: 谁都能明白；不需要什么高智商
5283.e: It doesn't take a rocket scientist to work out why the shop closed.  谁都能想明白那家店为什么关门。

5284.e: Their marriage was on the rocks long before he moved to Leeds.  他搬去利兹之前，他们的婚姻早就摇摇欲坠了。

5285.i: make a rod for your own ˈback
5285.e: By doing his homework for him you're making a rod for your own back.  替他写作业，你这是自找麻烦。

5286.cn: 罪犯照片档案；一群坏家伙
5286.e: The pub wall was covered with a rogues' gallery of old regulars.  酒吧墙上贴满了老主顾们的搞怪照片。

5287.e: Don't stop her now — she's on a roll with these sales calls.  别打断她，她这几通销售电话正顺风顺水。

5288.e: Roll on Friday — I've had quite enough of this week already.  周五快来吧，这一周我已经受够了。

5289.cn: 摩拳擦掌；准备大干一场
5289.e: We rolled up our sleeves and cleared the flooded cellar before lunch.  我们撸起袖子，午饭前把淹水的地窖清理干净了。

5290.cn: 顺势应对；随机应变挺过困境
5290.e: Freelancing teaches you to roll with the punches when clients suddenly disappear.  做自由职业让你学会在客户突然消失时随机应变。

5291.e: She's our accountant, receptionist and marketing team all rolled into one.  她一个人兼任会计、前台和市场部。

5292.e: His impression of the head teacher had us rolling in the aisles.  他模仿校长，把我们笑得前仰后合。

5293.e: They're absolutely rolling in it since they sold that patent last year.  自从去年卖掉那项专利，他们富得流油。

5294.cn: 滚石不生苔；转业不聚财
5294.e: He's changed jobs six times — a rolling stone gathers no moss.  他换了六份工作，真是滚石不生苔。

5295.i: shout, etc. sth from the ˈrooftops/ˈhousetops
5295.e: She got the job and wanted to shout it from the rooftops.  她拿到了工作，恨不得四处宣扬。

5296.i: no room to swing a ˈcat (informal)
5296.cn: 地方极其狭小；转不开身
5296.e: The kitchen in that flat has no room to swing a cat.  那套公寓的厨房小得转不开身。

5297.cn: 九尾鞭（旧时鞭打水手的刑具）
5297.e: Sailors who stole from the stores were flogged with a cat-o'-nine-tails.  偷仓库东西的水手会被九尾鞭抽打。

5298.i: get to the ˈroot of sth
5298.cn: 追根溯源；查明根本原因
5298.e: The engineer spent all morning getting to the root of the heating problem.  工程师花了一上午查明供暖问题的根源。

5299.e: The new director reformed the department root and branch within a year.  新主任一年内对部门进行了彻底改革。

5300.e: Poor drainage was the root cause of the damp in these old houses.  排水不畅是这些老房子潮湿的根本原因。

5301.e: The idea of a village library slowly took root over several years.  办村图书馆的想法几年间慢慢扎下了根。

5302.e: After years of moving, they finally put down roots in a seaside town.  漂泊多年后，他们终于在一个海边小镇安顿下来。

5303.e: They pulled up stakes and drove west with everything in one van.  他们举家迁走，一辆货车装下全部家当，一路西行。

5304.i: give sb enough ˈrope (and he'll/she'll ˈhang himself/herself) (saying)
5304.cn: 任其自作自受；听任自取灭亡
5304.e: Say nothing and give him enough rope — he'll expose himself soon enough.  什么都别说，由着他去，他很快会露馅。

5305.cn: 濒于失败；处境岌岌可危
5305.e: The company was on the ropes until that unexpected order finally arrived.  在那笔意外订单到来前，公司几乎撑不下去了。

5306.cn: 指点门道；学会（或掌握）诀窍
5306.e: Sam will show you the ropes during your first week here.  第一周山姆会带你熟悉门道。

5307.i: a ˈrose by any other name (would smell as ˈsweet) (saying)
5307.cn: 名称无关紧要，本质才重要
5307.e: Call it a cottage or a shack — a rose by any other name.  管它叫小屋还是棚子，叫法不重要。

5308.e: He sees his schooldays through rose-coloured glasses and forgets the bullying.  他把学生时代看得过于美好，忘了那些欺凌。

5309.i: be all ˈroses • be a bed of ˈroses (also be ˌroses, ˌroses all the ˈway) (informal)
5309.e: Running your own café is not a bed of roses, believe me.  自己开咖啡馆可不是什么美差，相信我。

5310.e: Since she started that course, everything's coming up roses for her.  自从上了那门课，她事事顺心。

5311.i: put the ˈroses back in your cheeks (BrE, informal)
5311.cn: 使脸色红润；使恢复气色
5311.e: A fortnight in the mountains will put the roses back in your cheeks.  在山里待两周会让你恢复好气色。

5312.i: everything in the ˈgarden is lovely/rosy (BrE, saying)
5312.cn: 一切都很美好；诸事顺遂
5312.e: They smile for photographs as if everything in the garden is rosy.  他们对着镜头微笑，好像一切都很美好。

5313.e: The rot set in when their best two players left the club.  两名主力离队后，情况就开始一路下滑。

5314.e: One rotten apple in the team can spoil the mood for everyone.  队里一个害群之马就能坏了所有人的心情。

5315.e: The landlord cut up rough when we asked about the broken boiler.  我们一问锅炉坏了的事，房东就翻了脸。

5316.e: Sketch the layout in rough first, then we'll decide on the colours.  先粗略画出布局，然后再定颜色。

5317.e: He slept rough for two winters before the charity found him a flat.  慈善机构给他找到公寓前，他露宿了两个冬天。

5318.cn: 粗陋但实用的；将就能用的
5318.e: The shelter was rough and ready but it kept us completely dry.  那个棚子简陋，却让我们一点没淋着。

5319.e: He enjoys the rough and tumble of local politics far too much.  他太享受地方政治的这种混战了。

5320.i: a ˌrough ˈdiamond (BrE) (AmE a ˌdiamond in the ˈrough)
5320.cn: 外粗内秀的人；未经雕琢的璞玉
5320.e: Our foreman is a rough diamond — blunt, but kinder than anyone here.  我们工头外粗内秀，说话冲，心却最善。

5321.e: The performance still has a few rough edges, but the energy is wonderful.  演出还有些瑕疵，但活力十足。

5322.i: the ˌrough end of the ˈpineapple (AustralE, informal)
5322.cn: 受到不公正对待；吃亏的一方
5322.e: Casual workers always get the rough end of the pineapple in these deals.  这类协议里，临时工总是吃亏的一方。

5323.cn: 将就着过；暂时过艰苦生活
5323.e: We roughed it in a tent for a fortnight and loved every minute.  我们在帐篷里将就了两周，却乐在其中。

5324.i: take the ˌrough with the ˈsmooth
5324.cn: 甘苦与共；好坏都能接受
5324.e: Farming means taking the rough with the smooth, year after year.  务农就得年复一年地承受好年景和坏年景。

5325.e: In round figures, the repairs will cost us about three thousand pounds.  取整来说，修理大概要花三千英镑。

5326.e: There are three good pubs round about, all within ten minutes' walk.  附近有三家不错的酒馆，走十分钟都能到。

5327.e: Nobody locks their bikes round here, which surprised me at first.  这一带没人锁自行车，起初让我很吃惊。

5328.e: The staff sent a round robin asking for the canteen to reopen.  员工联名递交请愿书，要求食堂重新开放。

5329.cn: 请一轮酒；做东请大家喝一杯
5329.e: It's my birthday, so I'll stand a round for everyone at the bar.  今天我生日，吧台这边我请一轮。

5330.i: do the ˈrounds (of sth) (BrE) (also make the ˈrounds AmE, BrE)
5330.cn: 巡视；逐一走访；四处流传
5330.e: The nurse does the rounds of every ward before the doctors arrive.  护士在医生到来前会巡视每个病房。

5331.e: We stopped for coffee en route to the airport and nearly missed check-in.  去机场路上我们停下喝咖啡，差点误了值机。

5332.cn: 眼睛乱瞟；到处寻花问柳
5332.e: Everyone knows he has a roving eye, which is why she left.  谁都知道他眼睛乱瞟，所以她才离开了。

5333.e: That's the fourth Monday in a row he's turned up late.  这是他连续第四个周一迟到了。

5334.i: rub sb's ˈnose in it (also rub it ˈin) (informal)
5334.cn: 老揭人短处；反复提及某人的过失
5334.e: Yes, I got the answer wrong — do you have to rub it in?  是，我答错了，你非得反复提吗？

5335.i: rub ˈsalt into the wound/into sb's wounds
5335.cn: 往伤口上撒盐；使雪上加霜
5335.e: Losing was bad enough; his laughing rubbed salt into the wound.  输了就够难受了，他还笑，简直是往伤口上撒盐。

5336.i: rub ˈshoulders with sb (AmE also rub ˈelbows with sb) (informal)
5336.cn: 与（名人、富人等）交往接触
5336.e: At that gallery opening she rubbed shoulders with three famous novelists.  在那次画廊开幕式上，她与三位著名小说家有了交往。

5337.i: rub sb up the ˈwrong way (BrE) (AmE rub sb the wrong ˈway) (informal)
5337.cn: 无意中惹恼某人；让人不舒服
5337.e: Something about his cheerful voice rubs me up the wrong way.  他那副欢快的声音总让我莫名不爽。

5338.i: there is/lies the ˈrub (formal or humorous)
5338.cn: 问题就在这里；难处正在于此
5338.e: We need money to make money — and there lies the rub.  要赚钱先得有钱，难处就在这儿。

5339.cn: 猛然醒悟；残酷的现实教训
5339.e: First-year students get a rude awakening when the exam results appear.  考试成绩一出来，大一新生就猛然清醒了。

5340.e: Her blunt speech ruffled a few feathers among the older committee members.  她直言不讳的发言惹恼了几位年长的委员。

5341.e: One careless email left his twenty-year career completely in ruins.  一封粗心的邮件毁了他二十年的职业生涯。

5342.e: As a general rule, we don't answer emails after seven in the evening.  一般来说，我们晚上七点后不回邮件。

5343.i: make it a ˈrule to do sth
5343.cn: 总是做某事；使之成为习惯
5343.e: I make it a rule to walk the dog before breakfast every day.  我总是坚持早饭前遛狗。

5344.cn: 经验法则；粗略的估算方法
5344.e: As a rule of thumb, allow one hour of cooking per kilo.  按经验法则，每公斤肉烤一小时。

5345.e: In that kitchen the head chef's mother still rules the roost.  在那间厨房里，主厨的母亲仍然说了算。

5346.i: rule (sb/sth) with a rod of ˈiron/with an ˈiron hand
5346.cn: 实行铁腕统治；严格管制
5346.e: The old headmaster ruled the school with a rod of iron.  老校长以铁腕手段管理学校。

5347.e: The librarian bent the rules and let me keep the book longer.  图书管理员通融了一下，让我多借几天。

5348.i: play by sb's ˈrules • play by your own ˈrules
5348.cn: 按某人的规矩办事；自行其是
5348.e: If you join his company, you play by his rules or leave.  进了他的公司，要么按他的规矩来，要么走人。

5349.e: That director plays by her own rules and still wins every award.  那位导演我行我素，却照样拿遍大奖。

5350.cn: 按规则办事；处事公正诚实
5350.e: He played by the rules his whole career and never once cheated.  他整个职业生涯都按规矩办事，从没作过弊。

5351.cn: 游戏规则；公认的行为准则
5351.e: Late payment is just part of the rules of the game in publishing.  拖延付款在出版界就是游戏规则的一部分。

5352.i: give sb/get/have the ˈrun of sth (informal)
5352.cn: 获准随意使用；可自由出入
5352.e: While they're away we have the run of their entire house.  他们不在的时候，整栋房子随我们用。

5353.e: The pair were on the run for six weeks before police caught them.  两人在逃六周后被警方抓获。

5354.e: When the alarm went off we grabbed our coats and ran for it.  警报一响，我们抓起外套就跑。

5355.e: The insurance company gave me the runaround for three whole months.  保险公司跟我踢了整整三个月皮球。

5356.e: I had a run-in with the traffic warden about parking on Tuesday.  周二我为停车的事跟交警吵了一架。

5357.cn: 溜之大吉；（干坏事后）逃走
5357.e: Two of them did a runner without paying for the meal.  他们中两个没付饭钱就溜了。

5358.e: He only has to whistle and she comes running every single time.  他一声招呼，她每次都马上跑来。

5359.e: Two more goals and we're back in the running for the cup.  再进两球，我们就重新有望夺杯。

5360.e: Small local firms are making the running in solar panel installation.  在太阳能板安装方面，本地小公司走在了前头。

5361.cn: 持续的争斗；旷日持久的争论
5361.e: The council and residents have fought a running battle over the car park.  议会与居民为停车场问题长期争执不下。

5362.e: He asked to borrow money again, so I told him to take a running jump.  他又来借钱，我叫他哪儿凉快哪儿待着去。

5363.cn: 正常运转；顺利运行起来
5363.e: The new website should be up and running by the end of March.  新网站三月底前应该就能正常运行。

5364.e: It was a run-of-the-mill hotel with tiny rooms and weak coffee.  那是家普通的酒店，房间很小，咖啡很淡。

5365.i: have a rush of blood to the ˈhead (humorous)
5365.e: He had a rush of blood to the head and bought the motorbike.  他头脑一热，把那辆摩托车买下了。

5366.e: They gave the heckler the bum's rush before the speech even started.  演讲还没开始，起哄的人就被轰了出去。

5367.cn: 忙得团团转；忙得脚不沾地
5367.e: The café staff were run off their feet all through the bank holiday.  整个公休假期，咖啡馆员工都忙得脚不沾地。

5368.e: Ten years in the same office and I'm stuck in a rut.  在同一间办公室待了十年，我的生活一成不变。

5369.cn: 生活刻板无变化；停滞不前
5369.e: I suddenly realised I'd been in a rut for years: same job, same everything.  我忽然意识到自己多年一成不变：同样的工作，同样的一切。

5370.e: He got the sack for turning up drunk on a Monday morning.  他因周一早上醉醺醺来上班被炒了。

5371.i: put on, wear, etc. ˌsackcloth and ˈashes
5371.e: There's no need for sackcloth and ashes; just apologise and move on.  用不着痛哭流涕地忏悔，道个歉往前走就行。

5372.cn: 毫无禁忌；什么都敢拿来开玩笑
5372.e: In this comedy club nothing is sacred, not even the mayor's funeral.  在这家喜剧俱乐部没有禁忌，连市长的葬礼都能拿来说。

5373.cn: 神圣不可冒犯的人（或制度、信念）
5373.e: The free bus pass has become a sacred cow no politician dares touch.  免费公交卡成了没有政客敢碰的神圣之物。

5374.e: With the founder back in the saddle, the company changed direction quickly.  创始人重新掌权后，公司很快改变了方向。

5375.e: Let's play it safe and book the earlier train to Manchester.  我们稳妥点，订去曼彻斯特那趟早一些的火车吧。

5376.e: All four climbers were found safe and sound the following morning.  四名登山者第二天早上都被安然找到。

5377.e: He said the investment was as safe as houses, and it wasn't.  他说这项投资绝对安全，结果并非如此。

5378.cn: 十拿九稳的事；有把握的选择
5378.e: Ordering the fish here is always a safe bet on a Friday.  周五在这儿点鱼总是没错的选择。

5379.e: She slept well, safe in the knowledge that the tickets were already booked.  她睡得很香，因为确信票已经订好了。

5380.cn: 因确知某事而安心；料定
5380.e: He signed the lease safe in the knowledge that his job was secure.  他确信工作稳当，才安心签下了租约。

5381.i: to be on the ˈsafe side
5381.e: Take an umbrella to be on the safe side; the forecast keeps changing.  带把伞以防万一，天气预报老在变。

5382.e: We walked home together because there's safety in numbers after midnight.  我们结伴回家，午夜之后人多才安全。

5383.e: He's late again and hasn't called — enough said, really.  他又迟到，还不打电话，不必多说了。

5384.e: About last night's argument, the less said the better, I think.  关于昨晚那场争吵，我看还是少说为妙。

5385.i: there's something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for sth/for doing sth
5385.e: There's something to be said for arriving early and choosing your own seat.  早点到、自己挑座位还是有好处的。

5386.i: sth has something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for it
5386.cn: 某事有（或没有）可取之处
5386.e: Living above the shop has quite a lot to be said for it.  住在店铺楼上其实有不少好处。

5387.i: something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for it
5387.cn: 有（或没有）多少可取之处
5387.e: The plan is cheap, and there's not much else to be said for it.  这方案便宜，除此之外没什么可取之处。

5388.i: not much to be ˈsaid for sth
5388.cn: 某事物没什么可取之处
5388.e: There's not much to be said for this book; it's the worst I've read.  这本书没什么可标榜的，是我读过最糟的。

5389.i: when ˌall is said and ˈdone
5389.e: When all is said and done, she did far more good than harm.  说到底，她做的好事远多过坏事。

5445.cn: say 的第三人称单数，读作 /sez/
5445.e: She says the shop opens at nine, so we should leave right now.  她说店里九点开门，我们现在就该走了。

5446.i: (it) does (eˈxactly) what it says on the ˈtin
5446.cn: 名副其实；与宣传的一样
5446.e: This app does exactly what it says on the tin — no ads, no nonsense.  这个应用完全名副其实：没广告，不啰嗦。

5447.i: it, etc. says a ˈlot, ˈmuch, etc. about/for sb/sth
5447.cn: 很能说明…的品质（或特点）
5447.e: It says a lot about him that he drove four hours to help.  他开了四个小时车来帮忙，这很说明他的为人。

5448.e: Who says men can't dance? Watch my dad at a wedding sometime.  谁说男人不会跳舞？改天看看我爸在婚礼上的样子。

5449.cn: 仅凭某人一句话；经某人许可
5449.e: I'm not spending that much on his say-so without seeing the figures.  没看到数据，我不会光凭他一句话就花这么多钱。

5450.i: the ˌscales fall from sb's ˈeyes (literary)
5450.e: The scales fell from her eyes when she read his old letters.  读了他从前的信，她才恍然大悟。

5451.e: Dad's in a foul mood, so make yourself scarce until dinner is ready.  老爸心情很差，开饭前你还是躲远点。

5452.i: scare the ˈshit out of sb • scare sb ˈshitless (△, slang)
5452.e: That horror film scared the shit out of me and I slept badly.  那部恐怖片把我吓得半死，一晚上没睡好。

5453.e: Police arrived on the scene minutes after the alarm started ringing.  警报响起几分钟后警察就赶到了现场。

5454.cn: 大吵大闹（尤在公共场合）
5454.e: Please don't make a scene in the restaurant over a cold soup.  别为一碗凉汤在餐厅里大吵大闹。

5455.e: Loud nightclubs really aren't my scene; I'd rather find a quiet pub.  吵闹的夜店真不合我口味，我宁愿找家安静的酒吧。

5456.e: The opening chapter sets the scene for everything that goes wrong later.  开篇一章为后面的所有变故作了铺垫。

5457.e: A lot of negotiating went on behind the scenes before the deal closed.  交易达成前，幕后进行了大量谈判。

5458.e: Reporters were on the scent of the story long before it broke.  这条新闻爆出来之前，记者早就嗅到味儿了。

5459.cn: 使某人失去线索；引某人走偏
5459.e: He booked a fake flight to throw the detectives off the scent.  他订了张假机票，好把警探引到岔路上。

5460.e: In the grand scheme of things, a late train hardly matters at all.  从大局来看，火车晚点根本算不上什么。

5461.e: There's a school of thought that says children learn best through play.  有一种观点认为孩子在玩耍中学得最好。

5462.e: Keep schtum about the party — it's meant to be a surprise.  聚会的事你可别说漏嘴，本来是个惊喜。

5463.i: have/get sth down to a ˈscience (especially AmE, often humorous)
5463.cn: 把某事做得又准又高效
5463.e: She has packing for holidays down to a science, never forgetting anything.  她收拾行李已经练成一门学问，从来不会漏东西。

5464.e: The car's cheap to run, so don't worry on that score at all.  这车养起来便宜，这方面你完全不用操心。

5465.e: He kept trying to score points off his brother during the whole dinner.  整顿饭他都在想办法把哥哥比下去。

5466.e: Critics poured scorn on the plan before they had even read it.  评论者连方案都没看就大加嘲讽。

5467.e: He crashed the van and somehow got off scot-free with a warning.  他把货车撞了，居然只挨了个警告就没事了。

5468.cn: 源自古英语 sceot（税），指不用纳税
5468.e: In those days landowners went scot-free while the poor paid every tax.  那时候地主不用纳税，穷人却什么税都得交。

5469.e: After the factory closed, hundreds of skilled workers were on the scrap heap.  工厂一关，几百名熟练工人就被扔在了一边。

5470.e: He scraped an acquaintance with the manager hoping it would land him work.  他想方设法结识了经理，指望能弄到活干。

5471.e: Casting him as the hero really is scraping the bottom of the barrel.  让他演男主角，实在是没人可选了。

5472.e: We lost the file and had to write the report from scratch.  文件丢了，报告只能从头再写。

5473.i: scratch ˌA and you'll find ˈB
5473.cn: 剥开表象，某类人骨子里是…
5473.e: Scratch a cynic and you'll find a disappointed idealist underneath.  剥开愤世嫉俗的外壳，里头是个失望的理想主义者。

5474.e: Engineers are still scratching their heads over why the engine keeps stalling.  发动机老熄火，工程师们到现在还摸不着头脑。

5475.e: Two weeks in India only scratches the surface of such a huge country.  在印度待两周，对这么大的国家不过是走马观花。

5476.e: Your essay isn't up to scratch yet, so rewrite the middle section.  你这篇文章还不合格，中间那部分重写。

5477.cn: 互相吹捧；互开方便之门
5477.e: There's far too much back-scratching between the council and local builders.  市政厅和本地建筑商之间的互相关照实在太多了。

5478.i: scream blue ˈmurder (BrE) (AmE scream bloody ˈmurder) (informal)
5478.e: Residents screamed blue murder when the council announced the parking charges.  市政厅一宣布停车收费，居民们就闹翻了天。

5479.e: Anyone who swims in that river in January has a screw loose.  一月份还下那条河游泳的人，脑子准是有点毛病。

5480.i: screw ˈhim, ˈyou, ˈthat, etc. (△, slang)
5480.e: Screw him — if he can't apologise, I'm not going to his wedding.  去他的，他要是不肯道歉，他的婚礼我不去了。

5481.cn: 雪上加霜；变本加厉的施压
5481.e: The new tax was another turn of the screw for struggling small shops.  新税对本就艰难的小店来说又是一次加压。

5482.e: The bank put the screws on us when we missed two payments.  我们漏还了两期，银行就开始逼债了。

5483.i: be/go on the ˈscrounge (for sth) (BrE, informal, disapproving)
5483.cn: 讨要（钱财、食物等）；伸手索要
5483.e: He's always on the scrounge for cigarettes instead of buying his own.  他从来不自己买烟，总是四处讨。

5484.i: by the scruff of sb's/the ˈneck
5484.e: She grabbed the puppy by the scruff of the neck and carried him inside.  她揪住小狗的后颈皮，把它抱进了屋。

5485.e: People who steal from the elderly are the scum of the earth.  偷老人东西的人真是人渣。

5486.e: I was completely at sea during the maths lecture this morning.  今天上午的数学课我完全听懵了。

5487.e: The recipe finally got my grandmother's seal of approval last Sunday.  上周日这个菜谱总算得到了我奶奶的认可。

5488.cn: 使…圆满收官；为…画上句号
5488.e: Winning the cup set the seal on a remarkable season for them.  夺杯为他们精彩的一个赛季画上了圆满句号。

5489.e: Don't worry about the surprise party — my lips are sealed.  惊喜派对的事你放心，我守口如瓶。

5490.i: be bursting/bulging at the ˈseams (with sth)
5490.e: The little classroom was bursting at the seams with thirty-five children.  三十五个孩子把那间小教室挤得满满当当。

5491.e: My suitcase was full to bursting with presents for the whole family.  我的行李箱塞满了给全家人的礼物，快撑爆了。

5492.e: The novel shows the seamy side of city life in the eighties.  这部小说写的是八十年代城市生活的阴暗面。

5493.e: Search your conscience before you accuse a colleague of stealing anything.  指控同事偷东西之前，先扪心自问一下。

5494.e: The divorce forced him into months of painful soul-searching about everything.  这场离婚让他痛苦地反省了好几个月。

5495.e: 'Where's the corkscrew?' 'Search me — I haven't touched it all week.'  “开瓶器呢？”“我哪知道，我一周都没碰过。”

5496.e: Strawberries taste far better in season and cost half as much too.  草莓当令时好吃得多，价钱还便宜一半。

5497.cn: 节日问候（尤用于圣诞贺卡）
5497.e: Season's greetings to you and all the family from everyone at the office.  办公室全体同人向你和家人致以节日问候。

5498.i: (fly) by the seat of your ˈpants
5498.cn: 凭直觉行事；无计划地瞎闯
5498.e: We had no budget and flew by the seat of our pants for months.  我们没有预算，好几个月都是走一步看一步。

5499.cn: 退居次要地位；不起主导作用
5499.e: Since her promotion, hobbies have taken a back seat to work entirely.  自从升职以后，她的爱好就完全给工作让路了。

5500.cn: 成为第二天性；习以为常
5500.e: After twenty years of driving, changing gear is second nature to him.  开了二十年车，换挡对他来说完全是本能。

5501.e: In terms of size, this lake is second only to Lake Superior.  论面积，这个湖仅次于苏必利尔湖。

5502.e: I got my second wind around midnight and finished the whole essay.  半夜前后我又来了精神，把整篇论文写完了。

5503.cn: 改变主意；重新考虑；心生疑虑
5503.e: She's having second thoughts about moving abroad now that winter is coming.  眼看冬天要到了，她对出国的事又犹豫起来。

5504.i: on ˈsecond thoughts (BrE) (AmE on ˈsecond thought)
5504.e: On second thoughts, let's take the train instead of driving through town.  再想想，我们还是坐火车吧，别开车穿城了。

5505.e: He got tired of playing second fiddle to his more famous brother.  给名气更大的哥哥当陪衬，他早就厌烦了。

5506.e: I refuse to settle for second best when it comes to safety.  在安全问题上，我绝不肯将就。

5507.e: Grandad bought a skateboard — he's clearly enjoying his second childhood.  爷爷买了块滑板，显然是返老还童了。

5508.e: My aunt claims she has second sight and knew about the accident.  我姑妈说她有预见力，早就知道会出事。

5509.cn: 首屈一指；不亚于任何人
5509.e: Their after-sales service is second to none in the whole industry.  他们的售后服务在整个行业里首屈一指。

5510.e: She jumped into the freezing canal without a second thought to save him.  她想都没想就跳进冰冷的运河去救他。

5511.i: a second/another bite at/of the ˈcherry
5511.cn: 第二次机会；再试一次的机会
5511.e: Losing the tender hurt, but we got a second bite of the cherry.  丢了那个标很心疼，好在我们又有了一次机会。

5512.e: It's an open secret that the manager is leaving at Christmas.  经理圣诞节要走，这已经是公开的秘密了。

5513.i: be glad, etc. to see the ˈback of sb/sth
5513.e: I'll be glad to see the back of this cold, wet February.  这个又冷又湿的二月总算要过去了，真好。

5514.i: see a lot, nothing, etc. of sb
5514.e: We've seen a lot of the neighbours since our kids started school.  孩子上学以后，我们和邻居来往多了不少。

5515.i: see sb/sth for what they ˈare/it ˈis
5515.e: Eventually she saw the offer for what it was — a cheap trick.  她终于看清那个提议不过是个廉价的把戏。

5516.e: Don't take my word for it; come and see for yourself tomorrow.  别光听我说，明天你自己来看看。

5517.e: See to it that the doors are locked before you leave tonight.  今晚走之前，务必把门都锁好。

5518.i: ˌsee you (aˈround) • ˌsee you ˈlater (also (Iˈll) be ˈseeing you) (spoken)
5518.e: See you around, then — I'll message you when I'm back in town.  那回头见，我回城了给你发消息。

5519.cn: 我看出来了（多用于回应不快之事）
5519.e: You've spilled paint on the carpet — so I see, unfortunately.  你把油漆洒到地毯上了。可不是嘛，我看到了。

5520.cn: 你知道；要知道（作解释时说）
5520.e: I can't come tonight; you see, my mother is arriving from Spain.  今晚我去不了，你知道，我妈从西班牙过来。

5521.e: The old tennis club has really gone to seed since the owner died.  老板去世后，那家老网球俱乐部彻底荒废了。

5522.cn: 播下…的种子；埋下…的根源
5522.e: That summer job planted the seeds of her interest in medicine.  那份暑期工作播下了她对医学感兴趣的种子。

5523.e: Seeing as it's your birthday, dinner tonight is definitely on me.  既然今天你生日，晚饭肯定我请。

5524.e: I doubted the trick worked until he showed me — seeing is believing.  他演示之前我一直不信，果然眼见为实。

5525.cn: 外出闯天下；寻求发财之路
5525.e: At eighteen he left the village to seek his fortune in London.  十八岁那年他离开村子，去伦敦闯天下。

5526.cn: 淘金者；碰运气发财的人
5526.e: The gold rush drew fortune seekers from every corner of the country.  淘金热把全国各地想发财的人都吸引来了。

5527.i: be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself
5527.e: After the illness he was a shadow of his former self.  生了那场病以后，他整个人都大不如前了。

5528.e: He sold his colleagues down the river to save his own job.  为了保住饭碗，他把同事全出卖了。

5529.cn: 缺斤短两；给某人的东西不足
5529.e: That market stall sold me short by nearly half a kilo.  那个市场摊位缺了我将近半公斤的秤。

5530.cn: 出卖灵魂（为好处不择手段）
5530.e: He'd sell his soul for a seat in the front row.  为了坐第一排，他什么都干得出来。

5531.e: Don't sell yourself short — you're the best candidate they've interviewed.  别小看自己，你是他们面试过最合适的人选。

5532.e: It's a seller's market right now, so houses go within days.  现在是卖方市场，房子几天就卖掉了。

5533.cn: 打发某人走；叫某人卷铺盖
5533.e: The landlord sent the noisy tenants packing after only two months.  才住了两个月，房东就把那些吵闹的租客赶走了。

5534.e: The whole team sent him to Coventry after he criticised the coach.  他批评了教练，全队都不再理他。

5535.i: work all the ˌhours God ˈsends
5535.cn: 拼命工作；没日没夜地干
5535.e: She works all the hours God sends to keep the little café going.  为了撑住这家小咖啡馆，她没日没夜地干。

5536.e: This is in no sense an admission that we made a mistake.  这绝不表示我们承认犯了错。

5537.i: in a ˈsense • in ˈone sense
5537.e: In a sense we were lucky the storm hit before the roof was finished.  从某种意义上说，暴雨在屋顶完工前来还算走运。

5538.cn: 开导某人别犯傻；使某人清醒
5538.e: Someone needs to knock some sense into that boy before he quits school.  在那孩子退学之前，得有人把他敲醒。

5539.e: Your plan makes sense, but we'll need more money to pull it off.  你的方案有道理，只是要办成还得再加钱。

5540.e: I can't make sense of these instructions; they must be badly translated.  这说明书我看不懂，八成是翻译得太差。

5541.e: Her father finally saw sense and agreed to sell the old car.  她父亲总算想通了，同意把那辆旧车卖掉。

5542.e: The candles and live music gave the evening a real sense of occasion.  烛光加现场音乐，让那一晚很有仪式感。

5543.e: Buying a third sports car? He has more money than sense.  又买第三辆跑车？他真是钱多得没处花。

5544.e: I hope he comes to his senses before he sells the family farm.  但愿他在卖掉家里农场之前能清醒过来。

5545.i: take ˌleave of your ˈsenses (informal, humorous)
5545.e: Have you taken leave of your senses, cycling home in this blizzard?  你疯了吧，这么大的暴风雪还骑车回家？

5546.i: these things are ˌsent to ˈtry us
5546.cn: 这类倒霉事是对人的考验
5546.e: The boiler's broken again — well, these things are sent to try us.  锅炉又坏了，唉，这也是老天在考验人吧。

5547.e: After graduation we went our separate ways and rarely spoke again.  毕业后我们各奔东西，几乎不再联系。

5548.i: sort out/separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats
5548.e: The first exam will sort out the sheep from the goats quickly.  第一场考试很快就能把好坏分出来。

5549.cn: 不合逻辑的推论；前言不搭后语
5549.e: Saying it's cold so taxes must rise is a complete non sequitur.  说天冷所以得加税，完全是不合逻辑的推论。

5550.e: Nobody took his warning seriously until the river burst its banks.  直到河水决堤，才有人把他的警告当回事。

5551.e: In all seriousness, you should see a doctor about that cough.  说正经的，你这咳嗽该去看医生了。

5552.i: serve a, his, its, etc. ˈpurpose
5552.e: This old crate serves its purpose as a table for now.  这只旧木箱暂时当桌子用也够了。

5553.e: The meeting served the purpose of getting everyone talking to each other.  这次会议起到了让大家彼此交流的作用。

5554.e: Every spare van was pressed into service to deliver the flood supplies.  所有闲置的货车都被调来运送救灾物资。

5555.cn: 一仆二主；同时效忠两方
5555.e: You can't serve two masters — pick a side and stick with it.  你不能一仆二主，选一边站稳了。

5556.i: it ˌserves you, him, her, etc. ˈright
5556.e: It serves you right for cheating — now you have to retake the exam.  作弊活该，现在只能重考了。

5557.cn: 听候某人吩咐；为某人效劳
5557.e: Our driver is at your service for the whole weekend, sir.  先生，整个周末司机都听您差遣。

5558.cn: 对某人有益；对某人并无好处
5558.e: You do him no service by finishing his homework every single night.  你天天替他把作业写完，这对他没有半点好处。

5559.e: Give her a garden and a dog and she's in seventh heaven.  给她一个院子加一条狗，她就快活似神仙。

5560.cn: 使…相形见绌；使黯然失色
5560.e: Her homemade bread puts every bakery in town in the shade.  她自己烤的面包让全城面包店都相形见绌。

5561.i: be frightened/nervous/scared of your own ˈshadow
5561.e: Since the burglary he's been scared of his own shadow at night.  自从家里遭贼，他晚上连自己的影子都怕。

5562.i: be scared of your own ˈshadow
5562.e: That dog is scared of his own shadow, let alone the postman.  那条狗连自己的影子都怕，更别说邮递员了。

5563.e: Beyond a shadow of a doubt, this is the best team we've had.  毫无疑问，这是我们有过的最好的一支队伍。

5564.i: there isn't a ˌshadow of a ˈdoubt (that...)
5564.e: There isn't a shadow of a doubt that he took the money.  钱是他拿的，这一点毫无疑问。

5565.i: there isn't a ˌshadow of ˈdoubt in my mind
5565.cn: 我心中毫无疑虑；我深信不疑
5565.e: There isn't a shadow of doubt in my mind that she's telling the truth.  我一点也不怀疑她说的是实话。

5566.cn: 在…近旁；笼罩在…的阴影下
5566.e: They live in the shadow of the old power station on the hill.  他们就住在山上那座旧电厂脚下。

5567.i: be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself
5567.e: The high street is a shadow of its former self these days.  如今这条商业街早已不复当年的热闹。

5568.cn: 亏待某人；不公正地对待某人
5568.e: The company gave him the shaft after fifteen years of loyal work.  他忠心干了十五年，公司却亏待了他。

5569.cn: 冗长无趣的故事（或笑话）
5569.e: Uncle Ray told another shaggy-dog story that lasted the entire car journey.  雷叔又讲了个又臭又长的故事，一路上没停。

5570.cn: （向某人）挥拳（表示愤怒或威胁）
5570.e: The old man shook his fist at the boys racing past his gate.  那些男孩从他家门口飞奔而过，老头儿冲他们挥了挥拳头。

5571.i: shake ˈhands (with sb) • shake sb's ˈhand
5571.e: The two leaders shook hands for the cameras and then said nothing.  两位领导人对着镜头握了握手，之后一言未发。

5572.cn: 握某人的手；与某人握手
5572.e: He shook me by the hand and thanked me for coming so far.  他握着我的手，谢我跑这么远过来。

5573.cn: 摇头（表示拒绝、难过、不同意等）
5573.e: She just shook her head and walked out without saying another word.  她只是摇了摇头，一句话没说就走了。

5574.e: Shake a leg, you two, or we'll miss the last bus home.  你们俩快点，不然赶不上末班车了。

5575.e: He was shaking like a leaf before his driving test this morning.  今早路考前他抖得像片叶子。

5576.e: We agreed a price and shook hands on it right there.  我们谈好价钱，当场就握手成交了。

5577.cn: 使…相形见绌；使某人自愧不如
5577.e: Her garden puts mine to shame, and she barely spends anything on it.  她的花园让我的相形见绌，可她几乎没花什么钱。

5578.e: Shame on you for laughing when the poor kid dropped his ice cream.  那孩子冰淇淋掉了你还笑，真不害臊。

5579.e: It's a crying shame they knocked down that beautiful old cinema.  把那座漂亮的老电影院拆了，实在太可惜。

5580.e: The buses had stopped, so we got home on Shanks's pony.  公交停运了，我们只好走着回家。

5581.cn: 身体（或状况）良好；状况不佳
5581.e: For a man of seventy, Dad is in remarkably good shape.  七十岁的人了，我爸身体好得出奇。

5582.e: Two flights of stairs left me gasping — I'm badly out of shape.  爬两层楼就喘，我这体能真是差透了。

5583.i: a ˌtaste of ˌthings to ˈcome
5583.e: That freak storm was a taste of things to come, scientists warn.  科学家警告说，那场怪异的风暴只是个开头。

5584.e: I've started swimming to get myself back into shape before the wedding.  为了婚礼前恢复身材，我开始游泳了。

5585.e: Give me a month to knock this sales team into shape.  给我一个月，把这支销售团队整顿像样。

5586.e: These sketches finally give shape to an idea I've had for years.  这些草图总算让我多年的想法有了形状。

5587.e: I won't support this project in any way, shape or form.  这个项目我以任何形式都不会支持。

5588.e: Help arrived in the shape of a neighbour with a tow rope.  帮手来了，是位带着拖车绳的邻居。

5589.i: ˈshape up or ship ˈout (AmE, informal)
5589.e: The coach told the players to shape up or ship out.  教练告诉队员们，要么拿出状态，要么走人。

5590.e: After weeks of talking, the plan is finally starting to take shape.  谈了好几周，方案总算开始成形了。

5591.i: come in all ˌshapes and ˈsizes
5591.e: Good teachers come in all shapes and sizes, as my old head said.  好老师什么样的都有，我以前的校长这么说过。

5592.e: There's one pizza left, so share and share alike, you two.  只剩一张比萨了，你们俩平分。

5593.i: a trouble ˈshared is a trouble ˈhalved (saying)
5593.e: Tell me what's wrong — a trouble shared is a trouble halved.  跟我说说怎么了，说出来就轻松一半。

5594.e: My aunt has a sharp tongue but a very generous heart underneath.  我姑妈嘴上厉害，心肠却极好。

5595.cn: 尖刻的言辞；刻薄的口舌
5595.e: Her sharp tongue has cost her more than one close friendship.  她嘴太毒，害得不止一个好朋友跟她断了交。

5596.i: ˌsharp-ˈtongued adj.: a sharp-tongued old man
5596.e: A sharp-tongued old man runs the corner shop and frightens all the children.  街角小店的老头嘴巴刻薄，孩子们都怕他。

5597.e: At ninety-two, Grandma is still as sharp as a tack.  九十二岁的奶奶脑子还是特别清楚。

5598.e: Nurses are at the sharp end of every crisis in the health service.  医疗系统一有危机，护士总是顶在最前线。

5599.cn: 不诚实的手段；欺诈行径
5599.e: The regulator fined the firm for sharp practice in selling pensions.  监管机构因该公司在卖养老金时耍花招而处以罚款。

5600.e: Look lively, lads — the delivery van arrives in ten minutes.  伙计们麻利点，送货车十分钟后就到。

5601.i: not the sharpest knife in the ˈdrawer
5601.e: He's kind, but he's not the sharpest knife in the drawer.  他人很好，就是脑子不太灵光。

5602.i: (also not the sharpest tool in the ˈbox) (humorous)
5602.e: Bless him, he's not the sharpest tool in the box, is he?  这孩子人不坏，就是不太开窍，是吧？

5603.e: That was a close shave — the lorry missed us by inches.  真是好险，那辆卡车擦着我们过去了。

5604.e: Tent, sleeping bags, stove — she packed the whole shebang in one rucksack.  帐篷、睡袋、炉子，她把全套家什塞进了一个背包。

5605.e: The crowd followed the guide like sheep, nobody asking a single question.  人群像羊群一样跟着导游，没人问一句话。

5606.i: sort out/separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats
5606.e: The final round will separate the sheep from the goats once and for all.  最后一轮会彻底把高下分出来。

5607.i: separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats
5607.e: This tough interview separates the sheep from the goats very quickly indeed.  这种硬碰硬的面试很快就能分出优劣。

5608.cn: 害群之马；家中的败家子
5608.e: Uncle Joe was the black sheep of the family and moved abroad.  乔叔是家里的败家子，后来搬到了国外。

5609.i: buy, get, etc. sth off the ˈshelf
5609.e: We bought the software off the shelf instead of paying for custom work.  我们买了现成的软件，没花钱做定制。

5610.cn: 被搁置；（女子）年岁大嫁不出去
5610.e: The project has been on the shelf since the funding was cut.  经费一砍，这个项目就搁置到现在。

5611.cn: 不再羞怯；变得活跃开朗
5611.e: She came out of her shell once she joined the hiking club.  加入徒步俱乐部以后，她整个人开朗了起来。

5612.i: bring sb out of their ˈshell (informal)
5612.cn: 使某人不再羞怯；使活跃起来
5612.e: A summer job in a café brought him out of his shell.  在咖啡馆干了个暑期工，他变得放得开了。

5613.i: go, retreat, withdraw, etc. into your ˈshell
5613.cn: 变得孤僻内向；不愿与人接触
5613.e: After the divorce he retreated into his shell and stopped calling friends.  离婚后他把自己封闭起来，也不再给朋友打电话。

5614.e: Every time we corner him in debate, he shifts his ground again.  每次辩论把他逼到墙角，他就又换个说法。

5615.cn: 变幻不定的局势；不牢靠的基础
5615.e: Investors hate the shifting sands of government policy on renewable energy.  政府在可再生能源上的政策变来变去，投资者很反感。

5616.e: The rain took the shine off our first day at the beach.  一场雨让我们在海边的第一天大打折扣。

5617.e: The boss has taken a shine to you, so ask for that raise.  老板挺看好你，去提加薪的事吧。

5618.i: make ˈhay while the sun ˈshines (saying)
5618.e: Orders are pouring in, so make hay while the sun shines.  订单源源不断，趁着行情好赶紧干。

5619.i: be a shining eˈxample (of sb/sth) (also be a shining ˈlight)
5619.e: That little library is a shining example of what volunteers can achieve.  那间小图书馆是志愿者能做成什么事的典范。

5620.e: When my ship comes in, I'll buy us a cottage by the sea.  等我发达了，就给咱们在海边买栋小屋。

5621.i: be (like) ˌships that ˌpass in the ˈnight (informal)
5621.e: We work opposite shifts and are like ships that pass in the night.  我们班次相反，就像夜里错身而过的两条船。

5622.i: be up ˌshit ˈcreek (without a ˈpaddle) (△, slang)
5622.cn: 陷入大麻烦；处境糟透了
5622.e: If the bank refuses the loan, we're up shit creek without a paddle.  银行要是不批贷款，我们就彻底完了。

5623.i: not give a ˈshit (about sb/sth) (△, slang)
5623.e: He doesn't give a shit about deadlines, which drives the whole team mad.  他压根不在乎截止日期，全组都被他气疯。

5624.i: shit all over sb/sth (△, slang, especially AmE)
5624.cn: 极其恶劣地对待某人（或某事）
5624.e: They shit all over their staff and then wonder why everybody leaves.  他们把员工往死里糟践，还纳闷人为什么都跑了。

5625.cn: 倒霉事难免；天有不测风云
5625.e: Shit happens; you just pick yourself up and carry on regardless.  倒霉事总会有，爬起来接着走就是了。

5626.i: (when) the ˌshit hits the ˈfan (△, slang)
5626.e: When the shit hits the fan, don't expect the manager to defend you.  真出了事，别指望经理会替你说话。

5627.i: a ˈshiver runs/goes down sb's spine
5627.e: A shiver ran down my spine when I heard footsteps upstairs.  听到楼上的脚步声，我脊背一阵发凉。

5628.i: send a ˈshiver up/down sb's spine
5628.cn: 使人脊背发凉；令人战栗
5628.e: His calm description of the crash sent a shiver down my spine.  他平静地讲述那场车祸，听得我脊背发凉。

5629.e: That empty hospital corridor gives me the shivers every single time.  那条空荡荡的医院走廊，我每次走都发怵。

5630.e: Shock horror — the teenager actually tidied his bedroom without being asked.  天大的新闻，这小子居然没人催就收拾了房间。

5631.e: I wouldn't want to be in his shoes when the auditors arrive.  审计的人一来，我可不想站在他那个位置上。

5632.e: Put yourself in her shoes before you judge how she handled it.  在评价她的做法之前，先设身处地想一想。

5633.e: They filmed the whole documentary on a shoestring using borrowed cameras.  他们借来摄影机，用极少的钱拍完了整部纪录片。

5634.e: With that record, she's a shoo-in for the manager's job.  凭这样的业绩，经理的位子非她莫属。

5635.cn: 已竭尽全力（尤指过早发力）
5635.e: He shot his bolt in the first mile and faded badly afterwards.  他头一英里就把力气使光了，后面掉得很厉害。

5636.i: shoot the ˈbreeze (also shoot the ˈbull/ˈshit △)
5636.e: We sat on the porch shooting the breeze until well past midnight.  我们坐在门廊上闲聊，一直聊到后半夜。

5637.cn: 彻底驳倒；把…批得一无是处
5637.e: The committee shot our proposal down in flames within about five minutes.  委员会五分钟就把我们的提案批得体无完肤。

5638.cn: 鲁莽行事；不假思索地开口
5638.e: The new director shoots from the hip and upsets people constantly.  新主管说话不过脑子，老是得罪人。

5639.e: We used to shoot hoops in the driveway until it got dark.  我们以前在车道上打篮球，一直打到天黑。

5640.e: The robbers shot it out with police outside the bank.  劫匪在银行门外和警察展开了枪战。

5641.e: He shot the lights on Main Street and got a hefty fine.  他在主街闯了红灯，被重罚了一笔。

5642.e: Don't shoot the messenger — I only passed on what the boss said.  别拿我撒气，我只是转达老板的话。

5643.cn: 信口开河；乱说（不该说的事）
5643.e: Someone shot their mouth off about the merger before it was announced.  合并还没公布，就有人把消息说漏了嘴。

5644.e: He shot himself in the foot by insulting the client's hometown.  他嘲笑客户的家乡，纯属自毁前程。

5645.e: She sold the shop, the van, the whole shooting match, last spring.  去年春天她把店、车，所有家当全卖了。

5646.i: all ˈover the shop (AmE also all ˈover the lot)
5646.e: His notes were all over the shop, so nobody could follow the argument.  他的笔记乱七八糟，谁也理不清他的思路。

5647.e: They set up shop in a tiny unit behind the railway station.  他们在火车站后头一间小铺面开了张。

5648.i: at (very) short ˈnotice (also at a moment's ˈnotice)
5648.e: She found us a hotel at very short notice on Christmas Eve.  平安夜她临时给我们找到了酒店。

5649.cn: 突然内急（附近却没厕所）
5649.e: I was caught short halfway up the mountain with no toilet anywhere.  爬到半山腰我突然内急，四下连个厕所都没有。

5650.e: Patience was in short supply after four hours on the motorway.  在高速上堵了四小时，谁都没耐心了。

5651.e: Dad's on a short fuse today, so don't mention the car.  老爸今天火气大，别提车的事。

5652.e: Keep the speech short and sweet; everyone wants to start eating.  致辞简短点，大家都等着开饭呢。

5653.e: We're running short of milk, so grab some on your way home.  牛奶快没了，你回来的路上买点。

5654.cn: 使某人猛然止步；使一下子怔住
5654.e: Her question brought me up short and I forgot my whole argument.  她一句话把我问住了，我把要说的全忘了。

5655.e: Drive carefully on that road or you'll come short one dark night.  那条路开车小心点，不然哪个黑夜就出事了。

5656.e: The chairman cut her short before she could finish the second point.  她第二点还没讲完，主席就把她打断了。

5657.e: We cut our holiday short when Mum was taken into hospital.  妈妈住院了，我们提前结束了假期。

5658.e: The building falls short of the new fire safety standards.  这栋楼达不到新的消防安全标准。

5659.e: His name is Bartholomew, but everyone calls him Bart for short.  他叫巴塞洛缪，大家都简称他巴特。

5660.i: get/have sb by the short and ˈcurlies (informal)
5660.cn: 完全掌控某人；使某人任其摆布
5660.e: With that contract, the supplier has us by the short and curlies.  有那份合同在手，供应商把我们捏得死死的。

5661.i: give sb/sth short ˈshrift • get short ˈshrift
5661.e: My complaint got short shrift from the manager, who barely looked up.  经理头都没抬，把我的投诉打发了。

5662.e: The children never went short of food, whatever else we lacked.  不管别的多缺，孩子们从没饿过肚子。

5663.e: In short, we need more money and a lot more time.  简言之，我们需要更多钱和更多时间。

5664.e: The plumber arrived and fixed the leak in short order.  水管工赶到后，很快就把漏水修好了。

5665.e: My nerves were shot to pieces after two nights without any sleep.  两晚没合眼，我的神经彻底垮了。

5666.e: I'll be glad to get shot of this leaky old van.  能把这辆漏雨的破车处理掉，我求之不得。

5667.i: have/take a ˈshot (at sth/at doing sth) (also give sth a ˈshot) (informal)
5667.e: I've never baked bread, but I'll have a shot at it tonight.  我从没烤过面包，今晚打算试一把。

5668.cn: 立刻；飞快地；毫不犹豫地
5668.e: If they offered me that job, I'd take it like a shot.  他们要是给我那份工作，我二话不说就答应。

5669.e: The email was a warning shot across the bows of every late payer.  那封邮件是对所有拖欠者的一记警告。

5670.cn: 一针强心剂；有力的鼓舞
5670.e: The grant was a real shot in the arm for our little theatre.  这笔拨款对我们这家小剧场来说是一针强心剂。

5671.e: Her speech was shot through with humour and a surprising amount of anger.  她的发言里满是幽默，还夹着出人意料的怒气。

5672.e: It was a shotgun wedding, but they stayed happily married for decades.  那是场奉子成婚，可两人恩爱了几十年。

5673.cn: 告诉某人；跟某人打声招呼
5673.e: Give me a shout when you're ready and I'll bring the car.  你收拾好了喊我一声，我把车开过来。

5674.i: put your shoulder to the ˈwheel
5674.cn: 奋力干起来；开始拼命工作
5674.e: Everyone put their shoulder to the wheel and we finished by Friday.  大家一齐使劲，周五前就干完了。

5675.cn: 可倾诉的对象；可依靠的肩膀
5675.e: After the breakup she just needed a shoulder to cry on.  分手之后，她只想找个人诉诉苦。

5676.e: The apology was just for show; nothing about his behaviour actually changed.  那句道歉不过是做样子，他的行为一点没变。

5677.e: They gave the new neighbour the cold shoulder for a whole year.  他们冷落了那位新邻居整整一年。

5678.i: have something, nothing, etc. to ˈshow for sth
5678.e: Ten years of work and he has nothing to show for it.  干了十年，他却什么成果都没有。

5679.e: It just goes to show that hard work sometimes beats raw talent.  这就说明，苦干有时候胜过天赋。

5680.i: put on a good, poor, wonderful, etc. ˈshow
5680.e: The youth team put on a good show against far stronger opponents.  面对强得多的对手，青年队表现不俗。

5681.e: Officially she's the deputy, but everyone knows she runs the show.  名义上她是副手，可谁都知道是她说了算。

5682.i: show (sb) a clean pair of ˈheels (informal)
5682.cn: 逃之夭夭；把人远远甩开
5682.e: The thief showed the guards a clean pair of heels down the alley.  小偷顺着巷子跑得没影，保安只能干瞪眼。

5683.cn: 下逐客令；把某人赶出去
5683.e: When he started shouting, the landlord showed him the door immediately.  他一开始嚷嚷，老板立刻请他出去。

5684.e: After that argument, I doubt he'll show his face here again.  吵成那样，我看他不会再来这儿露面了。

5685.i: show good ˈcause (for sth/for doing sth)
5685.e: You must show good cause for missing three weeks of lectures.  你得说明缺课三周的正当理由。

5686.e: Tanks rolled through the square in an obvious show of force.  坦克开过广场，明显是在示威。

5687.e: Let's settle this by a show of hands rather than another debate.  这事举手表决吧，别再辩了。

5688.e: The union finally showed its teeth and called a one-day strike.  工会终于亮出了獠牙，发起了一天的罢工。

5689.e: Their small factory showed the way on recycling long before it was fashionable.  早在回收还没流行时，他们那家小厂就带了个好头。

5690.e: Train the puppy early and show him who's boss from day one.  小狗要早训，第一天就让它知道谁说了算。

5691.e: Even peeling a few potatoes would show willing at his mother's house.  在他妈家哪怕削几个土豆，也算是有个态度。

5692.cn: 被撕成碎片；被彻底摧毁
5692.e: My confidence was in shreds after that awful performance review.  那次糟糕的绩效面谈把我的信心撕得粉碎。

5693.e: She's no shrinking violet; she'll argue with anyone about football.  她可不是害羞的人，谈起足球跟谁都能吵。

5694.e: Keep shtum about the bonus until everyone has been told officially.  奖金的事先别声张，等正式通知了再说。

5695.e: Her application got lost in the shuffle when the office moved buildings.  办公室搬家那阵，她的申请被忙乱中漏掉了。

5696.i: shuffle off this mortal ˈcoil (old-fashioned or humorous)
5696.e: Before I shuffle off this mortal coil, I'd like to see Japan.  在我两腿一蹬之前，我想去趟日本。

5697.e: Have a shufti at this photo and tell me who that is.  瞧一眼这张照片，告诉我那是谁。

5698.i: put up or ˈshut up (especially BrE)
5698.cn: 要么拿出行动，要么闭嘴
5698.e: If you think you can do better, put up or shut up.  你要觉得自己更行，就拿出真本事，否则闭嘴。

5699.cn: 封住某人的嘴（不让说出秘密）
5699.e: They paid him well to shut his mouth about the accident.  他们出了大价钱，让他把事故的事咽回去。

5700.e: Keep your mouth shut and nobody will ever know we were here.  你把嘴闭紧，没人会知道我们来过。

5701.e: The bakery shuts up shop at two on a Saturday afternoon.  这家面包店周六下午两点就打烊。

5702.cn: 封闭内心；不再理会某事
5702.e: Whenever I mention his father, he brings down the shutters completely.  一提他父亲，他就彻底把心门关上。

5703.e: Three of the drivers are off sick, so buses will run late.  有三个司机请了病假，公交会晚点。

5704.e: The child was sick twice on the coach before we reached Dover.  还没到多佛，那孩子在大巴上就吐了两回。

5705.e: It makes me sick to see food thrown away like that.  看着这么扔食物，我心里堵得慌。

5706.e: I was as sick as a dog after that dodgy prawn curry.  吃了那份不新鲜的虾咖喱，我吐得死去活来。

5707.i: get/keep on the right/wrong ˈside of sb
5707.e: Get on the right side of the caretaker and life becomes much easier.  和门卫处好关系，日子会好过得多。

5708.e: We lost the vote, but we have time on our side.  投票输了，可时间站在我们这边。

5709.cn: 把…搁在一边；留待以后处理
5709.e: Let's put that question to one side and finish the budget first.  这个问题先放一放，先把预算做完。

5710.e: Turn up on time — don't let the side down again tomorrow.  准时到，明天别再给大家掉链子。

5711.e: The dog didn't leave her side for the whole week she was ill.  她病的那一周，狗一步都没离开过她。

5712.i: the other side of the ˈcoin
5712.e: Cheap flights are great, but pollution is the other side of the coin.  廉价机票是好事，可污染是硬币的另一面。

5713.e: The two old churches stand side by side at the end of the lane.  两座老教堂并排立在巷子尽头。

5714.i: my, her, the other, the same, etc. side of the ˈfence
5714.cn: 我方（或对方、同一方）的立场
5714.e: It's easy to judge from the other side of the fence, isn't it?  站在对面说风凉话总是容易的，对吧？

5715.i: on the other side of the ˈfence
5715.e: Last year he was on the other side of the fence, defending the company.  去年他还站在对面，替公司辩护呢。

5716.e: That's only one side of the story; ask her brother what happened.  那只是一面之词，问问她哥哥到底怎么回事。

5717.cn: 把某人拉到一边（悄悄说话）
5717.e: The coach took me to one side and asked about my knee.  教练把我拉到一边，问我膝盖怎么样。

5718.e: We won't finish this side of Christmas at the rate we're going.  照这个速度，圣诞节前是干不完了。

5719.e: He spent the whole crisis on the sidelines, offering advice to nobody.  整场危机他都袖手旁观，一句建议也没给。

5720.i: from/on all ˈsides • from/on every ˈside
5720.e: Criticism came from all sides after the council announced the cuts.  市政厅一宣布削减开支，批评声就从四面八方涌来。

5721.i: see both ˈsides (of the question, problem, etc.)
5721.e: A good mediator can see both sides of a family argument.  好的调解人能看清家庭争吵中双方的道理。

5722.e: I refuse to take sides when my two best friends are arguing.  两个最要好的朋友吵架，我不站队。

5723.e: The embassy was under siege for three days before help arrived.  救援到来之前，使馆被围困了三天。

5724.i: have a mind/memory like a ˈsieve (informal)
5724.e: Write it down for me; I've got a memory like a sieve.  给我写下来吧，我这记性跟筛子似的。

5725.e: After six hours of walking, the village was finally in sight.  走了六个小时，村子终于出现在眼前。

5726.i: be a ˌsight for sore ˈeyes (spoken)
5726.cn: 见了就让人高兴；养眼的人（或物）
5726.e: A hot bath after that hike was a sight for sore eyes.  徒步回来能泡个热水澡，简直太让人舒心了。

5727.e: The guards had orders to arrest him on sight at the border.  卫兵接到命令，在边境一见到他就抓。

5728.i: hate, be sick of, etc. the ˈsight of sb/sth
5728.e: I'm sick of the sight of this kitchen after painting it twice.  这厨房刷了两遍漆，我看见就烦。

5729.i: keep sight of sb/sth • keep sb/sth in sight
5729.e: Keep the children in sight while the tide is coming in.  涨潮的时候，别让孩子离开你的视线。

5730.e: I looked a sight after cycling home through the rain and mud.  冒着雨踩着泥骑车回家，我狼狈极了。

5731.e: We mustn't lose sight of why we started this charity ten years ago.  别忘了十年前我们办这个慈善机构是为了什么。

5732.i: out of ˈsight, ˌout of ˈmind (saying)
5732.e: He never writes now — out of sight, out of mind, I suppose.  他现在从不来信，大概就是眼不见心不想吧。

5733.i: a (damn, etc.) sight ˈbetter, ˈworse, etc.
5733.e: This coffee is a damn sight better than the stuff at work.  这咖啡比单位那玩意儿强多了。

5734.e: My old bike was a sight better than this expensive rusty thing.  我那辆旧自行车比这贵价锈货强多了。

5735.e: They bought the flat sight unseen and regretted it within a month.  他们没看房就买下了那套公寓，一个月不到就后悔了。

5736.e: After three rejections he lowered his sights and applied to smaller firms.  被拒了三次后，他放低了目标，改投小公司。

5737.e: We had one free day in Rome to see the sights properly.  在罗马我们有一整天空闲，好好逛了逛景点。

5738.e: She set her sights high and applied to study medicine at Oxford.  她志向很高，申请去牛津读医学。

5739.i: set your ˈsights on sth/on doing sth
5739.cn: 立志要得到（或实现）某事
5739.e: He's set his sights on running a marathon before he turns forty.  他立志要在四十岁前跑一次马拉松。

5740.i: have your sights ˈset on sth/on doing sth
5740.cn: 一心想要得到（或做）某事
5740.e: She has her sights set on a job with the United Nations.  她一心想进联合国工作。

5741.e: Empty shops on the high street are a sign of the times.  商业街上空置的店铺就是这个时代的写照。

5742.i: it's a ˌsign of the ˈtimes
5742.e: Half of last year's graduates are still jobless; it's a sign of the times.  去年一半毕业生还没工作，这就是时代的写照。

5743.e: Read the contract twice before you sign on the dotted line.  签字之前，把合同看两遍。

5744.e: By insulting the investors he signed his own death warrant that evening.  那天晚上他得罪了投资人，等于自寻死路。

5745.e: The deal is signed, sealed and delivered, so we can celebrate tonight.  交易全部办妥，今晚可以庆祝了。

5746.e: The contract is signed and sealed, so nobody can back out now.  合同已经签字盖章，谁也别想反悔。

5747.e: In a meeting like that, silence is golden — say nothing at all.  那种会上沉默是金，一句都别说。

5748.cn: 对某人不理不睬；遭到冷落
5748.e: She gave me the silent treatment for a week after our row.  吵完架她整整一周没理我。

5749.e: At three in the morning the whole village is silent as the grave.  凌晨三点，整个村子静得像坟场。

5750.e: Politicians love to claim they speak for the silent majority.  政客总爱说自己代表沉默的大多数。

5751.i: make a silk ˌpurse out of a sow's ˈear
5751.cn: 化腐朽为神奇；用劣材做精品
5751.e: Renovating that ruin is making a silk purse out of a sow's ear.  把那片废墟翻新，简直是化腐朽为神奇。

5752.i: ˌdrink, ˌlaugh, ˌshout, etc. yourself ˈsilly
5752.e: The kids laughed themselves silly at the clown's enormous flapping shoes.  小丑那双又大又晃的鞋逗得孩子们笑翻了。

5753.e: Stop playing silly buggers with the thermostat and let me work.  别再瞎捣鼓恒温器了，让我干活。

5754.e: It must be the silly season; the front page is about a duck.  肯定是新闻淡季了，头版居然是只鸭子。

5755.i: (hand sth to sb) on a silver ˈplatter
5755.e: Nobody handed him success on a silver platter; he worked nights for years.  没人把成功端到他面前，他熬了好些年的夜。

5756.e: Her grandmother was a star of the silver screen in the fifties.  她奶奶是五十年代的银幕明星。

5757.e: The old dog is ugly as sin but everybody in the street loves him.  那条老狗丑得要命，可整条街的人都喜欢它。

5758.cn: 谨启；敬上（正式信函结尾语）
5758.e: End the letter with 'Yours sincerely' when you know the person's name.  知道对方姓名时，信末用“谨启”收尾。

5759.i: a ˌsine qua ˈnon /ˌsɪneɪ kwɑː ˈnəʊn/ (from Latin, formal)
5759.cn: 必要条件；必不可少的前提
5759.e: Trust is a sine qua non of any lasting business partnership.  信任是任何长久商业合作的必要前提。

5760.e: He'll sing a different tune once he sees the repair bill.  等他看到修车账单，调子就会变了。

5761.cn: 先付出后受惠；为报答而效劳
5761.e: Free tickets, but we had to sing for our supper by helping backstage.  票是免费的，可我们得去后台帮忙才算数。

5762.i: sing from the same ˈsong/ˈhymn sheet
5762.e: Before the press conference, make sure we're singing from the same hymn sheet.  开发布会前，先保证咱们口径一致。

5763.e: My dentist keeps singing the praises of that electric toothbrush.  我的牙医一个劲儿地夸那款电动牙刷。

5764.cn: 功能齐全的；花样繁多的
5764.e: They installed an all-singing, all-dancing coffee machine nobody knows how to use.  他们装了台功能全得没人会用的咖啡机。

5765.e: The two parties sank their differences long enough to pass the budget.  两党暂时放下分歧，把预算通过了。

5766.cn: 不沉即浮；成败全靠自己
5766.e: They threw me into the job and left me to sink or swim.  他们把我扔上岗位，是死是活全看自己。

5767.i: sink so ˈlow • sink to sth
5767.e: I never thought he'd sink so low as to steal from friends.  我没想到他会堕落到偷朋友东西的地步。

5768.cn: 自降身份，与某人一般见识
5768.e: Don't sink to his level by shouting insults across the car park.  别隔着停车场骂回去，跟他一般见识。

5769.cn: （如老鼠）弃船逃生；见势不妙就溜
5769.e: Senior staff are leaving a sinking ship, and everyone can see it.  高层纷纷弃船而逃，明眼人都看得出来。

5770.e: I got that sinking feeling when I saw the exam paper.  一看到卷子，我心里就凉了半截。

5771.i: (do/be sth) for your sins (spoken, humorous, especially BrE)
5771.e: I coach the under-tens on Sundays, for my sins, every single week.  我每个周日都得带十岁以下的队，算我倒霉。

5772.i: ˌno ˈsir! • ˌno sir ˈree! (spoken, especially AmE)
5772.e: No sir, I'm not lending him my car after last time.  绝对不行，上次之后我不会再借车给他。

5773.i: ˌyes ˈsir! • ˌyes sir ˈree! (spoken, especially AmE)
5773.e: Yes sirree, that's the biggest pumpkin I've ever seen at the fair.  没错，这是我在集市上见过最大的南瓜。

5774.e: Rich or poor, we're all brothers under the skin when disaster strikes.  灾难来时，无论贫富，我们本质上都是一样的人。

6050.e: Their grandparents spoil those twins rotten every summer.  每年夏天，祖父母都把那对双胞胎宠得不像话。

6051.cn: 因小失大；贪小便宜吃大亏
6051.e: Skipping the final coat of paint is spoiling the ship for a ha'porth of tar.  省下最后一遍漆，纯属因小失大。

6052.cn: 贪小失大；省小钱误大事
6052.e: Don't spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar; buy the proper bolts.  别为省点小钱坏了大事，买正规螺栓吧。

6053.i: ha ˈporth or ha ˈpenny-worth referred to a very
6053.e: Here ha'porth referred to a very small amount of money indeed.  这里的半便士指的是极小的一点钱。

6054.e: With twelve dessert options we were spoilt for choice.  甜点有十二种，我们都挑花了眼。

6055.i: be ˌspoiling for a ˈfight, argument, etc.
6055.e: He came in slamming doors, clearly spoiling for a fight.  他进门就摔门，明摆着想吵一架。

6056.e: In that street of bookshops you're spoiled for choice.  在那条书店街上，你会挑花眼。

6057.i: put a ˈspoke in sb's wheel (BrE)
6057.e: The landlord put a spoke in our wheel by refusing to renew.  房东拒绝续租，把我们的计划搅黄了。

6058.i: Dutch of spaak meaning ˈbar' or ˈstick.
6058.cn: 源自荷兰语，意为棒或棍
6058.e: The word comes from Dutch spaak, meaning bar or stick.  这个词源自荷兰语 spaak，意思是棒或棍。

6059.e: Be a good sport and give me a lift to the station.  你行行好，捎我去趟车站吧。

6060.e: With another week we'd have a sporting chance of finishing.  再给一周，我们完工还是很有希望的。

6061.e: She stood rooted to the spot when the alarm went off.  警报响起时，她呆立在原地。

6062.e: Luckily a doctor was on the spot when he collapsed.  幸好他倒下时现场有医生。

6063.cn: 使某人为难；让人下不来台
6063.e: Asking about his salary in front of everyone really put him on the spot.  当众问他工资，真让他下不来台。

6064.e: Your estimate of the repair cost was spot on.  你对维修费的估算分毫不差。

6065.cn: 受媒体关注；处于聚光灯下
6065.e: The scandal left him getting attention from newspapers and television for months.  这桩丑闻让他被报纸电视追了好几个月。

6066.e: Our holiday plans went up the spout when the airline collapsed.  航空公司倒闭，我们的假期计划泡汤了。

6067.i: (be) a ˌsprat to catch a ˈmackerel (informal)
6067.cn: 施小惠得大利；抛砖引玉
6067.e: The free trial is just a sprat to catch a mackerel.  免费试用不过是放长线钓大鱼。

6068.e: News of the resignation spread like wildfire through the building.  辞职的消息在楼里飞快传开。

6069.e: After graduation she spread her wings and moved abroad.  毕业后她展翅高飞，出国了。

6070.e: Spread the word: the meeting has moved to Thursday.  帮忙通知一下，会议改到周四了。

6071.cn: 摊子铺得太大；分身乏术
6071.e: Taking on three projects means you're spreading yourself too thin.  同时接三个项目，你是摊得太开了。

6072.i: Don't you think you're spreading yourself a bit
6072.cn: 你不觉得摊得太开了吗
6072.e: Another night shift? Don't you think you're spreading yourself a bit thin?  又加一个夜班？你不觉得顾不过来吗？

6073.e: We had to cast our net wide to find a decent candidate.  为找到合适人选，我们不得不广撒网。

6074.e: I'll help you move, but remember I'm no spring chicken.  我帮你搬家，不过我可不年轻了。

6075.e: The boat sprang a leak about a mile from shore.  离岸大约一英里时，船开始漏水。

6076.cn: 突然活跃起来；立即行动
6076.e: The whole newsroom sprang into action when the story broke.  消息一出，整个编辑部立刻忙了起来。

6077.e: The police sprang the trap just as the van pulled away.  货车刚要开走，警方就收网了。

6078.i: (do sth) on the ˌspur of the ˈmoment
6078.e: We booked the flight on the spur of the moment last Friday.  上周五我们一时冲动就订了机票。

6079.e: She earned her spurs covering the war as a young reporter.  她年轻时做战地记者，由此扬名。

6080.e: The kids get three square meals a day at that school.  那所学校每天给孩子三顿饱饭。

6081.i: the squeaky wheel gets the ˈgrease/ˈoil
6081.e: Complain loudly; the squeaky wheel gets the grease around here.  大声抱怨吧，这儿是会哭的孩子有奶吃。

6082.i: put the ˈsqueeze on sb (to do sth) (informal)
6082.e: The bank put the squeeze on him to repay early.  银行逼他提前还款。

6083.cn: 榨干某人的钱财或信息
6083.e: The landlords squeezed the tenants dry before selling up.  房东把租客榨干后就把房子卖了。

6084.e: Six of us in that car was a tight squeeze.  我们六个挤那辆车，实在太挤了。

6085.i: have a stab at sth/at doing sth (informal)
6085.e: I'll have a stab at fixing the tap myself tonight.  今晚我自己试试修那个水龙头。

6086.i: stab sb in the ˈback ◆ get, etc. a stab in the
6086.e: His own deputy stabbed him in the back at the board meeting.  他的副手在董事会上给了他一刀。

6087.cn: 被信任的人暗算；背后中伤
6087.e: Losing the contract that way felt like a stab in the back.  那样丢掉合同，简直像被人背后捅了一刀。

6088.i: ˈback-stabbing noun: This party is full of
6088.e: This party is full of back-stabbing and always has been.  这个党内暗箭伤人的事从来没断过。

6089.i: dark a shot/stab in the dark
6089.e: It was a shot in the dark, but the password worked.  纯属瞎蒙，可那密码居然对了。

6090.i: shut/lock/close the stable door after the
6090.e: Adding locks now is shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted.  现在才装锁，是马跑了才关厩门。

6091.i: horse has ˈbolted (BrE) (AmE shut, etc. the)
6091.e: They fixed the alarm after the horse had bolted, as usual.  照例是马跑了才修警报器。

6092.i: barn door after the horse has eˈscaped)
6092.cn: 贼走关门；补救为时已晚
6092.e: Backing up files now is closing the barn door after the horse has escaped.  现在才备份文件，早就晚了。

6093.i: the cards/odds are stacked aˈgainst sb/sth
6093.e: The odds were stacked against the small firm from day one.  从第一天起，形势就对这家小公司不利。

6094.i: the cards/odds are stacked in ˈfavour of sb/
6094.e: The odds are stacked in favour of the defending champion tonight.  今晚形势明显对卫冕冠军有利。

6095.cn: 形势有利于某人或某事
6095.e: Emily thought the odds were stacked in favor of her rival.  埃米莉以为形势对她的对手有利。

6096.e: In that village bread is still the staff of life.  在那个村子里，面包仍是命根子般的主食。

6097.e: He decided to go stag to the graduation dance.  他决定不带舞伴去毕业舞会。

6098.e: Against her parents' wishes, she went on the stage at nineteen.  她十九岁不顾父母反对当了演员。

6099.cn: 利害攸关；处于成败关头
6099.e: There's a lot at stake in tomorrow's negotiation.  明天的谈判利害攸关。

6100.e: She staked her claim to the corner office before anyone else moved in.  别人还没搬进来，她就先占下了那间角落办公室。

6101.e: He does badly in the punctuality stakes but writes beautifully.  论守时他很糟，可文章写得漂亮。

6102.i: etc. can't ˈstand the sight/sound of sb/sth
6102.cn: 受不了看到或听到某人某物
6102.e: I can't stand the sound of that drill next door.  隔壁那台电钻的声音我实在受不了。

6103.i: make a ˈstand (against/for/over/about/on sth) ◆ take a ˈstand (on/over sth)
6103.e: Someone has to take a stand on how the money is spent.  总得有人对这笔钱怎么花表明立场。

6104.e: The whole campaign stands or falls by the first week's numbers.  整个活动的成败取决于第一周的数据。

6105.e: Two ambulances were on standby outside the stadium all evening.  整晚有两辆救护车在体育场外待命。

6106.i: do sth standing on your ˈhead (informal)
6106.e: He could fix that engine standing on his head.  修那台发动机对他来说轻而易举。

6107.cn: 远远胜过；把对手甩在后面
6107.e: Her new laptop leaves my old one standing.  她的新笔记本把我这台老的甩出几条街。

6108.cn: 道理显而易见；这是自然的
6108.e: It stands to reason that tired drivers make more mistakes.  司机疲劳就更容易出错，这是明摆着的。

6109.i: hair your hair stands on end
6109.cn: 毛骨悚然；吓得头发直竖
6109.e: That scream in the corridor made my hair stand on end.  走廊里那声尖叫吓得我汗毛倒竖。

6110.e: Bankruptcy was staring the family business in the face.  破产已经摆在这家家族企业面前。

6111.e: The toddler ran through the garden stark naked, laughing.  那小家伙光着身子笑着跑过花园。

6112.e: She arrived in the city with stars in her eyes and no money.  她满怀憧憬来到这座城市，身上却没钱。

6113.e: I hit my head on the shelf and saw stars for a moment.  我头撞到架子上，眼前直冒金星。

6114.i: ˌdon't ˈstart (also ˌdon't ˈyou start) (spoken, informal)
6114.e: Don't you start, I've already heard it from your brother.  你别又来了，你弟弟已经念叨过了。

6115.i: for a ˈstart ◆ to ˈstart with (also for ˈstarters informal)
6115.e: For a start, the price is double what we agreed.  首先，价钱比说好的贵了一倍。

6116.e: He'd had three beers and was clearly looking to start something.  他喝了三瓶啤酒，明显想找事。

6117.i: you, he, she, etc. ˈstarted it (spoken, informal)
6117.cn: 是你（或他、她）先挑起来的
6117.e: Don't blame me, she started it by taking my chair.  别怪我，是她先抢我椅子的。

6118.e: The runners are under starter's orders and the crowd goes quiet.  选手已就位待发令，观众安静下来。

6119.i: be ˈstarving (for sth) (also be ˈstarved especially AmE) (informal)
6119.e: Is there anything to eat? I'm absolutely starving.  有吃的吗？我饿坏了。

6120.i: be in a ˈstate ◆ get into a ˈstate (informal)
6120.e: She got into a real state waiting for the test results.  等检查结果时她紧张得不行。

6121.e: In that blue dress she looked a picture.  穿上那条蓝裙子，她美极了。

6122.e: Three managers in one year is a sorry state of affairs.  一年换三个经理，这局面真够糟的。

6123.e: The hospital's new scanner is genuinely state of the art.  医院的新扫描仪确实是顶尖水平。

6124.e: This computer uses state-of-the-art technology in every single component.  这台计算机每个部件都采用了最尖端的技术。

6125.e: Can you update me on the state of play with the lawsuit?  你能跟我说说官司的进展吗？

6126.e: At seventy he's become an elder statesman of British theatre.  七十岁的他已成为英国戏剧界的元老。

6127.e: Older members of the club want to preserve the status quo.  俱乐部里年长的会员想维持现状。

6128.e: For him that watch is less a timepiece than a status symbol.  对他来说那块表与其说计时，不如说是身份象征。

6129.i: be here to ˈstay ◆ have come to ˈstay
6129.cn: 已被普遍接受；将长期存在
6129.e: Whatever critics say, remote working is here to stay.  不管批评者怎么说，远程办公是长久之势。

6130.e: Only four of the twelve trainees stayed the course.  十二名学员里只有四个坚持到了最后。

6131.e: Only her plea stayed his hand at the last moment.  最后一刻，是她的哀求让他住了手。

6132.e: It's too late to drive back, why not stay the night?  开回去太晚了，不如住一晚吧？

6133.e: Stay put by the fountain and I'll come find you.  你就在喷泉边别动，我来找你。

6134.e: The deputy attended the ceremony in the minister's stead.  副手代替部长出席了仪式。

6135.e: Those years in the kitchen stood her in good stead later.  在厨房干的那几年后来让她受益匪浅。

6136.e: They've been going steady since the summer fair.  夏季集市之后他们就正式交往了。

6137.e: Even after twelve hours, the surgeon's hands were steady as a rock.  连做十二小时后，那位外科医生的手依然稳如磐石。

6138.e: Steady on! That's my brother you're talking about.  慢着，你说的可是我弟弟。

6139.e: The teacher shouted "Ready, steady, go!" and the children sprinted off.  老师喊了声预备跑，孩子们就冲了出去。

6140.e: Two hundred for that bike? It's a steal.  那辆车两百块？简直白捡。

6141.e: He stole a glance at her across the crowded table.  隔着挤满人的桌子，他偷看了她一眼。

6142.e: That scruffy little puppy stole her heart immediately.  那只脏兮兮的小狗一下就俘获了她的心。

6143.e: He stole a kiss under the streetlamp before running for his train.  他在路灯下偷吻了她，然后赶火车去了。

6144.cn: 抢在某人前面；抢得先机
6144.e: By launching in April they stole a march on their rivals.  四月就上市，他们抢在了对手前头。

6145.e: The eight-year-old violinist stole the show at the concert.  那位八岁的小提琴手在音乐会上抢尽了风头。

6146.e: She announced the results early and stole my thunder completely.  她提前公布了结果，把我的风头全抢了。

6147.e: The campaign is finally picking up steam in the northern towns.  这场活动在北部各镇终于势头起来了。

6148.e: The kids need to run around and let off steam after school.  孩子们放学后得跑跑跳跳发泄一下。

6149.e: The project ran out of steam halfway through the second year.  项目到第二年中期就没了后劲。

6150.e: We'll meet you there; can you get to the hotel under your own steam?  我们在那儿碰头，你能自己到酒店吗？

6151.e: He got all steamed up about a two-minute delay.  就晚了两分钟，他就气得不行。

6152.e: She was really steamed about being left off the list.  没被列进名单，她气坏了。

6153.e: You need nerves of steel to land a plane in that wind.  在那种风里降落飞机，你得有钢铁般的神经。

6154.e: Forty pounds for a taxi across town seems a bit steep.  穿城打车四十镑，未免贵了点。

6155.e: The whole town is steeped in mining history.  整座小镇浸透着采矿业的历史。

6156.e: They scrubbed the old boat from stem to stern in one weekend.  他们一个周末就把那条旧船从头到尾刷了一遍。

6157.e: New rules did little to stem the tide of complaints.  新规几乎没能遏止投诉的浪潮。

6158.e: His views are badly out of step with the rest of the board.  他的看法和董事会其他人很不合拍。

6159.cn: 与某人齐步同行；与…步调一致
6159.e: She fell into step beside me as we crossed the bridge.  过桥时她跟上来和我并肩同行。

6215.cn: 想尽一切办法；竭尽全力
6215.e: Police left no stone unturned in the search for the missing girl.  警方为寻找失踪女孩想尽了一切办法。

6216.e: Stone the crows, you've painted the whole house in one weekend!  天哪，你一个周末就把整栋房子刷完了！

6217.e: Their flat is a stone's throw from the beach, which we loved.  他们的公寓离海滩一箭之遥，我们特别喜欢。

6218.e: My coffee went stone-cold while I was stuck on that call.  我被那通电话缠住，咖啡都凉透了。

6219.e: He was stone-cold sober and still couldn't remember where he parked.  他一滴酒没喝，却还是想不起车停哪儿了。

6220.cn: 吸毒后神志不清；晕乎乎
6220.e: They were stoned out of their minds and missed the last bus.  他们嗑得晕头转向，错过了末班车。

6221.e: His appeal for volunteers fell on stony ground at the parish meeting.  他在教区会上招募志愿者的呼吁没人搭理。

6222.i: stoop so ˈlow (as to do sth) (written)
6222.e: I never thought she'd stoop so low as to read my emails.  我没想到她会卑鄙到偷看我的邮件。

6223.e: He'll stop at nothing to get his name on that report.  为了让报告署上自己的名字，他什么都干得出来。

6224.e: A new coach was hired to stop the rot after five straight defeats.  五连败之后，球队请了新教练来止住颓势。

6225.e: She stopped short in the doorway when she saw who was waiting.  她看清等在那儿的是谁，在门口猛地停住了。

6226.cn: 责任到此为止；由我担责
6226.e: I'm the manager, so the buck stops here when things go wrong.  我是经理，出了事责任就在我这儿。

6227.e: Nobody knew what was in store for them on that first morning.  头一天早上谁也不知道等着他们的是什么。

6228.i: put/set (no, great, little, etc.) ˈstore by sth
6228.e: She sets great store by punctuality, so don't arrive late tomorrow.  她非常看重守时，明天别迟到。

6229.i: store up ˈtrouble, etc. for yourself
6229.e: Ignoring that cough is just storing up trouble for yourself later on.  不管那咳嗽，只是给自己以后埋下麻烦。

6230.e: The office is quiet today, but it's the calm before the storm.  今天办公室很安静，不过是暴风雨前的平静。

6231.i: dance, talk, etc. up a ˈstorm (informal, especially AmE)
6231.e: They danced up a storm at the wedding until the band packed up.  婚礼上他们一直跳得热火朝天，直到乐队收摊。

6232.i: write up a ˈstorm (informal, especially AmE)
6232.e: Since moving to the coast she's been writing up a storm every morning.  搬到海边后，她每天上午都写得停不下来。

6233.e: Small shops that weathered the storm are now busier than ever.  挺过难关的小店如今生意比以前还好。

6234.i: a storm in a ˈteacup (BrE) (AmE a ˌtempest in a ˈteapot) (informal)
6234.cn: 小题大做；茶杯里的风波
6234.e: The whole argument was a storm in a teacup and blew over quickly.  整场争吵不过是小题大做，很快就过去了。

6235.e: Her debut album took the country by storm within just three weeks.  她的首张专辑三周之内就风靡全国。

6236.e: Cooking at home is cheap; eating out every night is quite another story.  在家做饭便宜，天天下馆子就完全是另一回事了。

6237.cn: 情况完全不同；另一码事
6237.e: He's polite at work, but at home it's a quite different story.  他在单位彬彬有礼，在家却完全是另一副样子。

6238.i: so the story ˈgoes •the story ˈgoes (that)...
6238.e: The house is haunted, or so the story goes around this village.  据村里人说，那栋房子闹鬼。

6239.i: that's the ˌstory of my ˈlife (informal)
6239.e: Missed the train by ten seconds, and that's the story of my life.  差十秒没赶上火车，我这辈子就这命。

6240.i: give it to me ˈstraight (spoken, informal)
6240.e: Give it to me straight, doctor: how long will the recovery take?  医生您直说吧，得多久才能恢复？

6241.e: He's gone straight since prison and now runs a small bakery.  出狱后他改邪归正，现在开了家小面包房。

6242.e: Joining the club helped him keep to the straight and narrow.  加入那个俱乐部帮他一直走在正道上。

6243.i: play it ˈstraight (also play a straight ˈbat)
