6243.e: Just play it straight with the client and admit the delay was ours.  跟客户实话实说，承认是我们拖延了。

6244.e: Let me put you straight about what actually happened at the meeting.  我来跟你说清楚会上到底发生了什么。

6245.e: Give me ten minutes to put the room straight before they arrive.  给我十分钟把房间收拾好，他们就到了。

6246.e: She got straight A's last term without ever missing a hockey practice.  上学期她门门拿优，还没落下一次曲棍球训练。

6247.e: The new road runs straight as an arrow across the empty plain.  新修的公路笔直地穿过空旷的平原。

6248.i: run as ˈstraight as an arrow
6248.e: Take this road; it runs as straight as an arrow through the forest.  走这条路，它笔直地穿过整片树林。

6249.e: The old canal is straight as a die for almost ten miles.  那条老运河笔直地延伸了将近十英里。

6250.e: Call me straight away if the fever gets any worse tonight.  今晚要是烧得更厉害，马上给我打电话。

6251.e: I could hardly keep a straight face during his terrible karaoke.  他唱卡拉OK唱得那么惨，我差点没憋住笑。

6252.e: She told him straight from the shoulder that the plan wouldn't work.  她直截了当地告诉他这方案行不通。

6253.e: He asked her straight out whether she still wanted the job.  他直截了当地问她还想不想要这份工作。

6254.e: Straight up, I saw him carry that fridge upstairs on his own.  真的，我亲眼看见他一个人把冰箱扛上楼。

6255.cn: 急不可耐；渴望摆脱束缚
6255.e: The new recruits were straining at the leash to start real work.  新人个个跃跃欲试，急着上手真活儿。

6256.e: He's straining at the leash to leave Britain for somewhere sunny and warm.  他急不可待地想离开英国，去个阳光明媚的地方。

6257.e: They strained every sinew to finish the bridge before the rains came.  他们竭尽全力，赶在雨季前修完了桥。

6258.cn: 奇怪的组合；不搭调的伙伴
6258.e: Punk music and classical violin make strange bedfellows on this new album.  朋克和古典小提琴在这张新专辑里凑成了奇怪的组合。

6259.e: As a night nurse she is no stranger to difficult conversations.  身为夜班护士，她对难开口的谈话早已不陌生。

6260.e: We're strapped for cash this month, so let's cook at home.  这个月手头紧，咱们在家做饭吧。

6261.i: be the last/final ˈstraw (also be the ˌstraw that breaks the camel's ˈback)
6261.cn: 最后一根稻草；忍无可忍之事
6261.e: His third late arrival was the last straw, and she fired him.  他第三次迟到成了最后一根稻草，她把他辞了。

6262.e: Falling ticket sales may be a straw in the wind for the industry.  票房下滑也许是这个行业的一个风向信号。

6263.cn: 抓救命稻草；病急乱投医
6263.e: Trying that herbal tea was clutching at straws, but she felt desperate.  喝那种草药茶纯属抓救命稻草，可她实在没辙了。

6264.e: The second reactor comes on stream early next year, creating fifty jobs.  第二座反应堆明年初投产，将创造五十个岗位。

6265.i: go, swim, etc. with the ˈstream/ˈtide
6265.e: Most students just go with the stream and pick the popular courses.  多数学生都随大溜，挑热门课上。

6266.i: go, swim, etc. against the ˈstream/ˈtide
6266.e: She swims against the tide by refusing to use social media at all.  她偏不随大溜，压根儿不用社交媒体。

6267.e: This puzzle book is right up your street and you'll finish it tonight.  这本谜题书正合你的口味，你今晚就能做完。

6268.e: A job mixing travel and photography is right up your alley.  又能旅行又能拍照的工作正对你的路子。

6269.e: Their software is streets ahead of anything else on the market.  他们的软件比市面上其他产品领先一大截。

6270.e: Losing that flat left him on the streets for most of the winter.  丢了那套公寓，他整个冬天大半时间都流落街头。

6271.i: the streets are ˌpaved with ˈgold (saying)
6271.e: He came south believing the streets are paved with gold, then found nothing.  他以为南方遍地黄金才南下，结果一无所获。

6272.e: The little bakery has gone from strength to strength since it opened.  那家小面包店开业以来生意越做越红火。

6273.e: She got the loan on the strength of one very optimistic forecast.  她凭着一份过于乐观的预测拿到了贷款。

6274.e: My sister was a tower of strength during those months in hospital.  住院那几个月，姐姐是我最大的精神支柱。

6275.e: Fans turned out in force despite the rain and the early start.  尽管下雨又开赛早，球迷还是大批到场。

6276.e: The election result strengthened her hand in the coming budget talks.  选举结果让她在接下来的预算谈判中更有底气。

6277.e: Play to your strengths and let someone else handle the spreadsheets.  发挥你的长处，表格让别人去弄。

6278.e: He can code for eight hours at a stretch without a break.  他能一口气写八小时代码不休息。

6279.i: by ˈno stretch of the imagination •not by ˌany stretch of the imagiˈnation
6279.cn: 无论怎么想也不；绝对不是
6279.e: By no stretch of the imagination could that meal be called cheap.  那顿饭再怎么说也算不上便宜。

6280.e: Let's stop at the next services and stretch our legs for ten minutes.  下个服务区停一下，活动活动腿脚。

6281.e: The librarian stretched a point and let me keep the book longer.  图书管理员破了个例，让我多借几天。

6282.e: Strictly speaking, this cheese isn't vegetarian, though most people assume so.  严格说来这种奶酪并非素食，尽管大家都以为是。

6283.i: get into your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE hit (your) ˈstride)
6283.e: By the second week the new teacher had got into her stride.  到第二周，新老师已经完全进入状态了。

6284.e: The camera flash put the goalkeeper off his stride at the worst moment.  闪光灯在最要命的时刻让门将乱了阵脚。

6285.e: The underdog matched the champion stride for stride until the final lap.  那位无名选手一直和冠军并驾齐驱到最后一圈。

6286.i: take sth in your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE take sth in ˈstride)
6286.e: She took the criticism in her stride and rewrote the chapter.  她从容接受批评，把那一章重写了。

6287.i: make great, rapid, etc. ˈstrides (in sth/in doing sth)
6287.e: He has made great strides in Spanish since moving to Seville.  搬到塞维利亚后，他的西班牙语大有长进。

6288.i: strike a ˈbalance (between A and B)
6288.e: It's hard to strike a balance between work and time with kids.  在工作和陪孩子之间找平衡很难。

6289.e: They struck a deal with the landlord to paint the flat themselves.  他们和房东谈妥，自己动手粉刷公寓。

6290.e: The ruling strikes a blow for tenants across the whole country.  这项裁决为全国的租户争了一口气。

6291.i: strike ˌfear, ˌterror, etc. into sb/sb's ˈheart
6291.e: The sound of that siren struck fear into everyone's heart that night.  那晚警报声让每个人都心头一紧。

6292.e: The label struck gold with a band nobody else wanted to sign.  这家唱片公司签下一支没人要的乐队，结果大赚一笔。

6293.e: He struck it rich selling phone cases online during the lockdown.  封城期间他在网上卖手机壳发了财。

6294.e: We struck lucky and found a cheap flat near the university.  我们运气不错，在大学附近找到了便宜公寓。

6295.e: She struck a pose on the steps while her friend took photos.  她在台阶上摆姿势，朋友给她拍照。

6296.i: strike while the ˌiron is ˈhot (saying)
6296.e: They liked your pitch, so strike while the iron is hot.  他们看好你的方案，趁热打铁吧。

6297.e: The cottage is within striking distance of both the lake and town.  那间小屋离湖和镇上都很近。

6298.e: She kept him on a string for months without ever saying yes.  她吊了他好几个月，始终没答应。

6299.e: The loan comes with no strings attached, which sounds too good.  这笔贷款不附带任何条件，好得让人生疑。

6300.e: The new law wiped out those fees at a stroke last April.  去年四月新法一出，那些收费一下子全取消了。

6301.e: He hasn't done a stroke of work since the holidays began.  放假以来他一点活儿都没干过。

6302.i: on/at the ˌstroke of ˈeight, ˈmidnight, etc.
6302.e: The bells rang on the stroke of midnight and everyone cheered loudly.  午夜钟声一响，大家高声欢呼。

6303.e: Constant questions put the surgeon off his stroke during the operation.  不停发问打乱了外科医生手术的节奏。

6304.e: This phone is strong on battery life but weak on camera quality.  这款手机胜在续航，摄像头就差些。

6305.e: Patience has never been my strong point, as my students know.  耐心从来不是我的强项，学生都清楚。

6306.e: He came on strong at the party and made everyone uncomfortable.  他在派对上太咄咄逼人，弄得大家都不自在。

6307.e: You need a strong stomach to watch that documentary about the slaughterhouse.  看那部屠宰场纪录片得有个好胃口。

6308.e: I was struck by how calm she stayed during the whole crisis.  整场危机中她那么镇定，我很受触动。

6309.e: We were struck dumb with shock when they announced the winner.  宣布获奖者时，我们惊得一句话都说不出。

6310.e: She stood dumbstruck when they read out her name as the winner.  念到她名字是冠军时，她愣在那里目瞪口呆。

6311.e: The dancers strutted their stuff in the square all Saturday afternoon.  舞者们整个周六下午都在广场上大展身手。

6312.e: Grandad is stubborn as a mule about using his old flip phone.  爷爷死活要用他那部老翻盖手机，倔得像头驴。

6313.i: get stuck ˈin •get stuck ˈinto sth (BrE, informal)
6313.e: Everyone got stuck into the painting and finished the hall by lunchtime.  大家撸起袖子刷漆，午饭前就把门厅刷完了。

6314.e: Stand back and let the sound engineer do her stuff for once.  往后站，这回让音响师露一手。

6315.e: He doesn't give a stuff what the neighbours think of his garden.  邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。

6316.e: Stuff and nonsense, nobody ever caught a cold from wet hair.  一派胡言，谁会因为头发没干就感冒。

6317.e: Stuff him, we're going to the concert whether he approves or not.  去他的，不管他同不同意我们都去看演唱会。

6318.e: That's the stuff, keep your elbow up and hit through the ball.  这就对了，胳膊肘抬高，把球打透。

6319.i: get ˈstuffed (also get ˈknotted less frequent)
6319.e: I told the caller to get stuffed and hung up the phone.  我让那个打电话的滚开，然后挂了电话。

6320.cn: 一本正经的人；古板的人
6320.e: The new director is a stuffed shirt who hates any kind of joke.  新主任古板得很，一点玩笑都开不得。

6321.e: Loud parties really aren't my style, but I'll come for an hour.  闹哄哄的派对不合我的口味，不过我会去待一小时。

6322.i: from the subˈlime to the riˈdiculous
6322.e: The concert went from the sublime to the ridiculous in about ten minutes.  这场音乐会十分钟内就从崇高滑向了荒唐。

6323.i: a woman, man, person, etc. of ˈsubstance
6323.cn: 有钱有势的人；举足轻重的人
6323.e: Everyone treated him as a man of substance once the factory succeeded.  工厂一做起来，人人都把他当成有头有脸的人物。

6324.e: After one hit film she had five offers, since nothing succeeds like success.  一部电影火了，她就接到五个邀约，真是一顺百顺。

6325.cn: 就其本身而言；严格意义上
6325.e: There's no rule as such, just a habit everyone here follows.  严格说没什么规定，只是这里大家的习惯。

6326.e: Bring something warm, such as a fleece, because the evenings get cold.  带件保暖的，比如抓绒衫，晚上会冷。

6327.cn: 尽管质量不高；虽说不怎么样
6327.e: You can borrow my bike, such as it is, but the brakes squeak.  我的自行车你可以骑，虽说破了点，刹车还吱吱响。

6328.e: We can't predict the result, so let's suck it and see.  结果没法预测，试试才知道。

6329.e: Nobody likes the night shift, but we just suck it up.  谁都不爱上夜班，可我们只能忍着。

6330.e: All of a sudden the lights went out and the music stopped.  突然间灯灭了，音乐也停了。

6331.e: The final went to sudden death after ninety minutes without a goal.  九十分钟没进球，决赛进入了突然死亡决胜。

6332.e: My editor doesn't suffer fools gladly, so check your facts twice.  我的编辑最容不得糊涂虫，材料你多核两遍。

6333.e: He stayed in the flat on sufferance until he found his own place.  在找到自己的住处前，他勉强被容许住在那套公寓里。

6334.e: Suffice it to say that the interview did not go very well.  只需说一句：面试很不顺利。

6335.cn: 包养年轻女子的阔老头
6335.e: She joked that she needed a sugar daddy to pay her rent.  她开玩笑说自己需要个阔老头来付房租。

6336.cn: 加点甜头；使坏事易于接受
6336.e: They sugared the pill with a bonus before announcing the pay freeze.  宣布冻薪前，他们先发了笔奖金当甜头。

6337.e: At my sister's suggestion we booked the tickets three months early.  按我姐的建议，我们提前三个月订了票。

6338.cn: 合某人心意；对某人方便
6338.e: The later meeting suits my book because I can drop the kids off.  会议改晚点正合我意，我可以先送孩子。

6339.i: suit sb (right) ˌdown to the ˈground (BrE, informal)
6339.e: Working from home suits me right down to the ground these days.  这阵子居家办公完全合我的心意。

6340.e: Suit yourself, but I'm taking the early train whatever you decide.  随你便，反正不管你怎么定我都坐早班车。

6341.e: The men in grey suits decided her fate long before the vote.  早在投票前，幕后那些人就定了她的命运。

6342.i: be greater/more than the ˌsum of its ˈparts
6342.e: This band is greater than the sum of its parts on stage.  这支乐队在台上的效果远胜过成员各自相加。

6343.e: In sum, the trial worked but costs far more than we expected.  总之，试点有效，但花费远超预期。

6344.cn: 深秋的晴暖时节；晚年的黄金期
6344.e: We had an Indian summer that October and ate outside every evening.  那年十月出了个小阳春，我们天天在户外吃晚饭。

6345.e: He finally summoned up the courage to ask her out for coffee.  他终于鼓起勇气约她去喝咖啡。

6346.e: They sell every kind of cheese under the sun at that market.  那个市场上天底下的奶酪品种都有得卖。

6347.e: Grandma made us wear our Sunday best for the family photograph.  奶奶让我们穿上最好的衣服拍全家福。

6348.e: He told all and sundry about the promotion before it was confirmed.  升职还没定，他就见人就说。

6349.e: She was sunk in thought and didn't hear me come in.  她陷在沉思里，没听见我进来。

6350.e: I'll have two eggs sunny-side up with toast and black coffee.  我要两个单面煎蛋，配吐司和黑咖啡。

6351.e: I don't suppose you could give me a lift to the station?  不知你能不能捎我去车站？

6352.e: 'Can Tom come too?' 'I suppose so, if he behaves himself.'  “汤姆也能来吗？”“我想可以吧，只要他老实点。”

6353.e: You're not supposed to park here between eight and six on weekdays.  工作日八点到六点不准在这儿停车。

6354.cn: 你这话什么意思（表气愤或不解）
6354.e: 'You've changed a lot lately.' 'What's that supposed to mean, exactly?'  “你最近变了不少。”“你这话到底什么意思？”

6355.i: be sure to do sth (also be sure and do sth spoken)
6355.e: Be sure to lock the back door before you leave tomorrow morning.  明早出门前一定要锁好后门。

6356.e: He'll be late again, that's for sure, so order without him.  他肯定又要迟到，别等他先点吧。

6357.e: Make sure the oven is off before we head out to dinner.  出门吃饭前确认一下烤箱关了没有。

6358.i: (as) sure as eggs is ˈeggs (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
6358.e: Sure as eggs is eggs, he'll ask for money again next week.  千真万确，下周他准又来借钱。

6359.e: I sure as hell won't drive four hours for a ten-minute meeting.  我才不会为个十分钟的会开四小时车。

6360.e: I said it would rain, and sure enough the picnic was cancelled.  我说会下雨，果然野餐取消了。

6361.e: She's very sure of herself for someone who started only last month.  上个月才来的人，她可真够自信的。

6362.e: 'Can you cover my shift?' 'Sure thing, just tell me when.'  “能替我上班吗？”“没问题，说个时间就行。”

6363.e: The house is small, to be sure, but the garden is enormous.  房子固然小，但花园大得很。

6364.e: Beneath the surface, the two sides still disagree about almost everything.  表面之下，双方几乎在所有问题上仍有分歧。

6365.e: On the surface everything seemed fine, but the accounts told another story.  表面上一切正常，账目却是另一回事。

6366.e: Surprise, surprise, he forgot to bring the tickets he promised to print.  瞧吧，他答应打印的票果然忘带了。

6367.e: The question took me by surprise and I answered it badly.  那个问题把我问懵了，我答得很糟。

6368.e: In that market it's survival of the fittest and prices decide everything.  那个市场就是适者生存，价格决定一切。

6369.e: As treasurer, her accounts must be above suspicion at all times.  身为司库，她的账目任何时候都必须清白无疑。

6370.e: Two staff members are under suspicion of leaking the client list.  两名员工涉嫌泄露客户名单。

6371.e: The finger of suspicion quickly pointed at the only key holder.  怀疑的矛头很快指向了唯一有钥匙的人。

6372.e: That excuse sounds suspiciously like the one you used last Friday.  这借口听着跟你上周五用的那个特别像。

6373.i: one ˌswallow doesn't make a ˈsummer (saying)
6373.cn: 一燕不成夏；勿以偏概全
6373.e: We won once, but one swallow doesn't make a summer, so stay focused.  我们只赢了一场，一燕不成夏，别松劲。

6374.i: one swallow does not make a ˈsummer (saying)
6374.cn: 一花独放不是春；别过早乐观
6374.e: One swallow does not make a summer, so don't celebrate a single order.  独燕不成夏，一张订单还不值得庆祝。

6375.e: They swallowed the bait and clicked the link in that fake email.  他们上了钩，点开了那封假邮件里的链接。

6376.e: Shoppers take the bait whenever they see the words free gift.  一看到“免费赠品”几个字，顾客就会上钩。

6377.e: He swallowed his pride and asked his younger brother for help.  他放下面子，向弟弟开口求助。

6378.e: The storm cut a swathe through the orchards along the whole valley.  风暴横扫了整条山谷的果园。

6379.e: That old theory held sway over economists for nearly fifty years.  那套旧理论主宰了经济学界将近五十年。

6380.e: He swore blind he'd posted the letter, but it was still there.  他一口咬定信寄了，可信还在那儿。

6381.e: My gentle aunt swears like a trooper whenever she watches football.  我那温柔的姑妈一看足球就满嘴脏话。

6382.e: She swore us all to secrecy about the surprise party next month.  她让我们全都发誓，对下月的惊喜派对保密。

6383.e: I was in a sweat about the deadline all weekend long.  整个周末我都为截止日期急得冒汗。

6384.e: He carried both heavy suitcases upstairs without even breaking sweat.  他把两只重箱子搬上楼，连汗都没出。

6385.i: by the sweat of your ˈbrow (literary)
6385.e: He built that farm by the sweat of his brow over thirty years.  那片农场是他三十年血汗一点点挣出来的。

6386.e: Don't sweat it, we can easily reprint the flyers tomorrow morning.  别担心，明早重印传单很容易。

6387.i: don't sweat the ˈsmall stuff (AmE, spoken)
6387.e: Don't sweat the small stuff; the guests won't notice the napkin colour.  别为鸡毛蒜皮操心，客人不会注意餐巾颜色。

6388.e: 'Can you drive me over?' 'No sweat, I'm going that way anyway.'  “能开车送我过去吗？”“小事一桩，我正好顺路。”

6389.e: We sweated blood to get the exhibition ready in three weeks.  为了三周内布好展，我们拼了命。

6390.e: He sweated it out in the waiting room until the results came.  他在候诊室里苦等，直到结果出来。

6391.e: I was sweating like a pig by the time I reached the summit.  爬到山顶时我已经大汗淋漓。

6392.e: The little Irish film swept the board at the awards last night.  昨晚那部爱尔兰小成本电影包揽了所有奖项。

6393.cn: 使某人倾倒；令某人着迷
6393.e: He swept her off her feet with letters and terrible poetry.  他用一封封信和蹩脚的诗把她迷得神魂颠倒。

6394.i: do sth in your ˌown sweet ˈtime/way (informal)
6394.cn: 随心所欲地做；不慌不忙
6394.e: He'll finish the shed in his own sweet time, so stop asking.  他会按自己的节奏把棚子搭完，别再催了。

6395.e: She has such a sweet tooth that dessert always comes first.  她太爱吃甜食了，永远先吃甜点。

6396.e: Keep the landlord sweet and he might fix the boiler quickly.  把房东哄好点，他也许会赶紧修锅炉。

6397.e: Don't worry about the booking, mate, she's sweet, I called them already.  订位的事别操心，兄弟，都搞定了，我打过电话了。

6398.i: sweet FˈA (also less frequent sweet Fanny ˈAdams) (BrE, informal)
6398.e: I did sweet FA all weekend except watch films and eat toast.  整个周末我啥也没干，就看电影吃吐司。

6399.e: They sat whispering sweet nothings while the rest of us ordered food.  我们点菜的时候，他俩坐在那儿说悄悄情话。

6400.e: After ten years of rejection she finally tasted the sweet smell of success.  被拒了十年，她终于尝到了成功的滋味。

6401.e: He's all sweetness and light until you question his budget figures.  他一团和气，除非你质疑他的预算数字。

6402.e: Joining the choir got her back into the swim of things quickly.  加入合唱团让她很快重新融入了大家。

6403.e: Give it a week and you'll get into the swing of things.  过一周你就适应节奏了。

6404.e: The party went with a swing once the neighbours brought their guitars.  邻居抱来吉他后，派对一下子热闹起来。

6405.e: He mentioned casually that he swings both ways and nobody blinked.  他随口说自己是双性恋，谁也没觉得意外。

6406.e: The rescue team swung into action minutes after the call came in.  电话打来几分钟后，救援队就出动了。

6407.e: The foreman thinks half the crew are swinging the lead today.  工头觉得今天有一半人在装病偷懒。

6408.cn: 有得有失；失之东隅收之桑榆
6408.e: Cheaper rent but a much longer commute, so it's swings and roundabouts.  房租便宜可通勤远多了，算是有得有失。

6409.i: what you gain on the swings you lose on the ˈroundabouts (saying)
6409.e: What you gain on the swings you lose on the roundabouts, as Dad says.  正如老爸所说，有所得必有所失。

6410.cn: 达摩克利斯之剑；随时降临的祸患
6410.e: The threat of redundancy hung over us like a sword of Damocles.  裁员的威胁像达摩克利斯之剑一样悬在我们头上。

6411.cn: 铸剑为犁；化干戈为玉帛
6411.e: The treaty promised to turn swords into ploughshares across the whole region.  条约承诺让整个地区铸剑为犁。

6412.cn: 用最浅显的话；通俗地说
6412.e: Explain it in words of one syllable, because I'm completely lost.  用最简单的话讲吧，我完全听糊涂了。

6413.e: For him that watch is a status symbol rather than a timepiece.  对他来说那块表是身份象征，而不是看时间的。

6414.e: Share prices fell in sympathy with the slump in oil this week.  本周股价随油价大跌而下滑。

6415.e: She resigned, being completely out of sympathy with the new party line.  她辞职了，因为完全不认同新的党派路线。

6416.e: The sound was out of sync with the picture for the whole film.  整部电影的声音和画面都不同步。

6417.i: get sth out of your ˈsystem (informal)
6417.e: Go for a run and get the anger out of your system.  去跑一圈，把这股火发出去。

6418.e: It's all systems go for the launch on Friday at last.  周五的发布终于万事俱备了。

6419.e: That jacket fits you to a T, as if it was tailored.  那件外套你穿正合身，像是量身做的。

6420.e: She described the room to the smallest detail, right down to the wallpaper.  她把房间描述得极其细致，连墙纸都说到了。

6421.e: The pay offer is on the table until Friday afternoon at five.  这份薪资方案的有效期到周五下午五点。

6422.i: put/lay your ˈcards on the table
6422.e: Let's put our cards on the table and discuss the real budget.  咱们摊开来谈，说说真实的预算。

6423.e: She turned the tables on her rivals with one very clever question.  她用一个巧妙的问题反将了对手一军。

6424.e: The bank keeps close tabs on every transaction over ten thousand pounds.  银行密切监控每一笔超过一万英镑的交易。

6425.e: There's a police car on our tail, so slow down a bit.  后面有辆警车跟着，慢一点开。

6426.e: We arrived at the tail end of the party and missed the cake.  我们赶到时派对已近尾声，蛋糕都没吃上。

6427.i: the tail (is) wagging the ˈdog (also let the tail wag the ˈdog)
6427.e: When marketing decides the science, that's the tail wagging the dog.  让营销来定科研方向，就是本末倒置。

6428.e: The fox turned tail and ran the moment the dog barked.  狗一叫，狐狸转身就跑。

6429.i: with your tail between your ˈlegs (informal)
6429.e: He came back with his tail between his legs after the argument.  吵完架他夹着尾巴回来了。

6430.e: Two officers were on the take for years before anyone noticed.  两名警官受贿多年才被人察觉。

6431.i: I, ˌyou, ˌetc. can't take sb ˈanywhere (informal, often humorous)
6431.e: He spilled wine on the host, so honestly, you can't take him anywhere.  他把酒洒在主人身上，真是带不出去。

6432.e: We have no plan for the trip; we'll take it as it comes.  这趟旅行没做计划，走到哪算哪。

6433.e: The training is brutal, but she can take it better than anyone.  训练很残酷，可她比谁都扛得住。

6434.e: I take it that you've already spoken to the landlord about this.  我想这事你已经跟房东说过了吧。

6435.e: Draft the outline and I'll take it from there next week.  你先拟个提纲，下周剩下的我来接手。

6436.e: Let's meet the client first and take it from there next month.  下个月先见客户，再看下一步怎么走。

6437.e: Take it from me, that road is closed every single winter morning.  信我一句，那条路每个冬天早上都封。

6438.i: take it on/upon yourself to do sth
6438.e: She took it upon herself to rewrite the entire report overnight.  她自作主张，连夜把整份报告重写了。

6439.i: take it ˈout of sb •take a lot ˈout of sb
6439.e: Those night shifts really take it out of you after a while.  上久了夜班真会把人累垮。

6440.e: Don't take it out on the kids just because work was awful.  别因为工作不顺就拿孩子撒气。

6441.i: take sb ˈout of himself, herself, etc.
6441.e: A weekend by the sea took her out of herself for once.  在海边过了个周末，她总算散了散心。

6442.i: have what it ˈtakes (to do sth) (informal)
6442.e: He has what it takes to run this kitchen on his own.  他有本事独自撑起这间厨房。

6443.e: With two rivals injured, the title was hers for the taking.  两个对手受伤，冠军对她来说唾手可得。

6444.e: The market was there for the taking and nobody moved fast enough.  那块市场唾手可得，却没人动作够快。

6445.e: He's all talk and no action when it comes to fixing things.  一说到修东西，他就光说不做。

6446.e: Her wedding dress was the talk of the village for weeks afterwards.  她的婚纱成了村里好几周的谈资。

6447.i: be the talk of the ˈtown
6447.e: Overnight she became the talk of the town after that radio interview.  那次电台采访后，她一夜之间成了全城的话题。

6448.i: ˈyou can/can't talk (also look who's ˈtalking) (spoken)
6448.e: You can't talk, your desk is even messier than mine right now.  你还好意思说，你桌子比我的还乱。

6449.i: you're a ˈfine one to talk (spoken)
6449.e: You're a fine one to talk about being late, Mr Nine-Thirty.  你还有脸说人家迟到，九点半先生。

6450.e: Talk about bad luck, the tyre burst outside the wedding venue.  真是倒霉，轮胎就在婚礼场地门口爆了。

6451.e: He talks big about his contacts but never introduces anyone to us.  他把人脉吹得天花乱坠，却从没给我们引荐过谁。

6452.e: He started talking dirty on the phone and she hung up.  他在电话里开始说下流话，她直接挂了。

6453.i: talk sb's ˈear off (especially AmE, informal, especially disapproving)
6453.e: My neighbour talked my ear off about her cats for an hour.  邻居拉着我聊了一小时她的猫，耳朵都磨出茧了。

6454.e: She talked her head off the whole way to the airport.  去机场一路上她嘴就没停过。

6455.i: talk the hind leg(s) off a ˈdonkey (informal, humorous)
6455.e: Uncle Ray could talk the hind legs off a donkey at parties.  雷叔在聚会上能说得没完没了。

6456.e: No talking shop at dinner, we agreed that before we sat down.  吃饭不谈工作，坐下前就说好的。

6457.i: talk through the back of your ˈhead (informal)
6457.e: He's talking through the back of his head about those tax rules.  他讲那些税法完全是胡说八道。

6458.e: Ignore him, he's talking through his hat about the election again.  别理他，他又在瞎扯选举的事。

6459.e: Explaining anything to that department is like talking to a brick wall.  跟那个部门解释什么都跟对墙说话一样。

6460.e: Politicians talk tough on crime, then cut the police budget again.  政客对犯罪问题口气强硬，转头又削减警力预算。

6461.e: Let's stop the small talk and talk turkey about the price.  别寒暄了，咱们直接谈价钱。

6462.i: talk your way out of sth/out of doing sth
6462.e: He talked his way out of a speeding ticket somehow last night.  昨晚他不知怎么靠一张嘴躲过了超速罚单。

6463.e: The salesman was a fast talker and I signed without reading anything.  那推销员嘴皮子太溜，我什么都没看就签了。

6464.e: Free pizza? Now you're talking, count me in for the evening.  免费披萨？这话我爱听，晚上算我一个。

6465.e: Talking of holidays, have you booked anything for the summer yet?  说到假期，你暑假订好行程了吗？

6466.e: She stood tall and read her statement to the whole courtroom.  她昂首挺胸，向全庭宣读了自己的陈述。

6467.e: Finishing this by Friday is a tall order with two people off.  两个人请假，周五完工实在强人所难。

6468.i: a ˌtall ˈstory (especially BrE) (AmE usually a ˌtall ˈtale)
6468.e: Grandpa told another tall story about wrestling a bear in Canada.  爷爷又讲了个在加拿大跟熊搏斗的离奇故事。

6469.e: The two charities work in tandem to house families every winter.  这两家慈善机构每年冬天协同安置无家可归的家庭。

6470.i: go off at a ˈtangent (BrE) (AmE go off on a ˈtangent)
6470.e: He goes off at a tangent whenever anyone mentions his old school.  一有人提起他的母校，他就扯到别处去。

6471.e: The stock went in the tank after the recall was announced.  召回消息一出，股价就一路跳水。

6472.i: throw a ˈtantrum (BrE also throw a ˈwobbly)
6472.e: The toddler threw a tantrum in the cereal aisle again today.  今天那小家伙又在麦片货架前撒泼。

6473.e: There's free legal advice on tap for students during exam week.  考试周期间随时都有免费法律咨询供学生使用。

6474.e: After a month she had the whole filing system taped.  一个月后，整套归档系统她已摸得门儿清。

6475.i: tar sb/sth with the same ˈbrush
6475.cn: 一概而论；视为一丘之貉
6475.e: Don't tar every landlord with the same brush because of one.  别因为一个房东就把所有房东一竿子打死。

6476.i: wouldn't do sth for all the ˌtea in ˈChina
6476.e: I wouldn't move back to that town for all the tea in China.  给我再多好处，我也不搬回那个镇子。

6477.e: The head took him to task over the missing exam papers.  校长为丢失试卷的事狠狠训了他一顿。

6478.e: Blue cheese is an acquired taste, but I really love it now.  蓝纹奶酪要慢慢才吃得惯，现在我可爱吃了。

6479.i: be in bad, the worst possible, etc. ˈtaste
6479.e: That joke about the funeral was in the worst possible taste.  拿葬礼开的那个玩笑实在低俗透顶。

6480.i: be in good, the best possible, etc. ˈtaste
6480.e: The memorial was simple and in the best possible taste.  那场追思会朴素而得体。

6481.i: leave a bad/nasty ˈtaste in the/your mouth
6481.e: The way they fired him left a nasty taste in my mouth.  他们辞退他的方式让我心里很不是滋味。

6482.e: Add salt and pepper to taste, then let the sauce simmer gently.  按口味加盐和胡椒，然后让酱汁慢慢煨着。

6483.e: His reputation was in tatters after the newspaper published those photos.  报纸登出那些照片后，他的名声一败涂地。

6484.e: She tore herself loose from his grip and ran towards the door.  她奋力挣脱他的手，朝门口跑去。

6485.e: The dog tore loose and chased the ducks across the whole park.  狗挣脱绳子，追着鸭子跑遍了整个公园。

6486.i: tear sb ˈoff a strip •tear a ˈstrip off sb (BrE, informal)
6486.e: The coach tore a strip off him for arguing with the referee.  他跟裁判顶嘴，被教练骂得狗血淋头。

6487.cn: 批得体无完肤；撕成碎片
6487.e: The critics tore his second novel to shreds within a single week.  评论界一周之内就把他的第二部小说批得体无完肤。

6488.e: She left in a tearing hurry and forgot her laptop on the table.  她走得慌慌张张，把笔记本电脑忘在桌上了。

6489.e: The description of my brother fits him to a tee.  对我弟弟的那段描述简直分毫不差。

6490.i: teeter on the ˈbrink/ˈedge of sth
6490.e: The company teetered on the brink of collapse for most of last year.  去年大半年里公司都在崩盘边缘摇摇欲坠。

6491.cn: 初试身手；从中积累经验
6491.e: She cut her teeth on local radio before moving to television news.  她先在地方电台练手，之后才转到电视新闻。

6492.e: Finally a project I can really sink my teeth into this month.  这个月总算有个能让我全力投入的项目了。

6493.e: The new rules only work if the regulator's powers actually have teeth.  只有监管机构真有牙齿，新规才管用。

6494.e: They pressed ahead in the teeth of fierce opposition from local residents.  他们不顾当地居民的强烈反对，执意推进。

6495.e: The scrape of that chalk sets my teeth on edge every time.  粉笔那种刮擦声每次都让我牙根发酸。

6496.cn: 初期的困难；起步阶段的问题
6496.e: The app had teething problems, but the latest update fixed most bugs.  这款应用起步时毛病不少，最新更新修掉了大部分。

6497.e: She's been on the phone with the insurance company for forty minutes.  她跟保险公司通电话已经四十分钟了。

6498.e: Don't tell me you've locked the keys inside the car again.  别告诉我你又把钥匙锁车里了。

6499.e: We met in March, no, I tell a lie, it was April.  我们三月认识的，不对，我说错了，是四月。

6500.i: I ˈtell you •I can ˈtell you •I'm ˈtelling you
6500.e: I'm telling you, that was the best curry in the entire city.  我跟你说，那是全城最好吃的咖喱。

6501.i: I can't ˈtell you how, etc. ... (spoken)
6501.e: I can't tell you how glad I am that you came tonight.  你今晚能来，我真是说不出的高兴。

6502.i: I'll ˌtell you ˈwhat •I know ˈwhat (spoken)
6502.e: I'll tell you what, let's split the bill and call it even.  我看这样吧，账平摊，就算扯平了。

6503.e: I like her because she tells it like it is, however awkward.  我喜欢她，因为她再难堪的话也照直说。

6504.i: (go) tell it/that to the maˈrines (saying, informal)
6504.e: You fixed it yourself? Go tell that to the marines, mate.  你自己修好的？骗鬼去吧，兄弟。

6505.e: The empty shelves in the shop told their own story that winter.  那年冬天店里空空的货架已经说明了一切。

6506.e: Tell me, how did you first get into repairing old clocks?  你说说，你当初怎么迷上修老钟表的？

6507.e: 'Mondays are exhausting.' 'Tell me about it, I've had three meetings.'  “周一累死人。”“可不是嘛，我已经开了三个会。”

6508.e: You ran a marathon without training? Tell me another, please.  你没训练就跑完马拉松？别逗了。

6509.e: He's telling porkies about how much that watch actually cost him.  那块表到底花了多少钱，他在瞎编。

6510.e: Every farm in the valley tells the same story of falling prices.  山谷里每个农场都反映出同样的价格下跌。

6511.i: tell a ˈdifferent, aˈnother, etc. tale/story
6511.e: The official figures tell a different story from what workers describe.  官方数字反映的情况和工人说的截然不同。

6512.e: Nobody likes a kid who tells tales about classmates to the teacher.  谁都不喜欢向老师打同学小报告的孩子。

6513.e: I shouldn't tell tales out of school, but the accounts were fiction.  我本不该外传，可那些账目纯属编的。

6514.e: My daughter learned to tell the time on an old analogue clock.  我女儿是在一台老式指针钟上学会看时间的。

6515.i: tell sb ˌwhere to get ˈoff (BrE, informal)
6515.cn: 严厉斥责某人；叫某人放规矩些
6515.e: When he criticized her cooking, she told him where to get off.  他挑剔她做的菜，她把他狠狠顶了回去。

6516.i: tell sb ˌwhere they get ˈoff (BrE, informal)
6516.e: Someone should tell that man where he gets off ordering us around.  该有人让那家伙明白，他没资格对我们指手画脚。

6517.i: tell sb where to ˈput/ˈstick sth (informal)
6517.e: They offered half the fee, so I told them where to stick it.  他们只肯给一半费用，我直接让他们免谈。

6518.i: tell sb what they can ˈdo with sth (informal)
6518.cn: 拒不接受；让某人收起那套
6518.e: He told the boss exactly what he could do with the extra overtime.  他直截了当地让老板收起那些加班安排。

6519.e: Keep it quiet, don't tell the whole world before the contract is signed.  先别声张，合同签之前别到处宣扬。

6520.e: To tell you the truth, I've never really liked that restaurant.  老实说，我从来没真心喜欢过那家餐厅。

6521.i: what did I ˈtell you? (also I ˈtold you so)
6521.e: What did I tell you? The queue is enormous on Saturday mornings.  我早说了吧？周六上午队伍长得吓人。

6522.i: you ˌnever can ˈtell •you can ˌnever ˈtell
6522.e: He might apologize tomorrow, but you never can tell with him.  他明天说不定会道歉，不过跟他这种人谁说得准。

6523.i: not know/not be able to tell one ˈend of sth from the other
6523.e: I can't tell one end of a car engine from the other.  汽车发动机我完全一窍不通。

6524.e: 'That hill is steep.' 'You're telling me, I pushed my bike up.'  “那坡真陡。”“可不是嘛，我是推着车上去的。”

6525.e: I lost my temper with the call centre after the third transfer.  被第三次转接后，我对客服发了火。

6526.e: The survey takes the temperature of small businesses across the north.  这项调查摸的是北部小企业的经营状况。

6527.e: She's running a temperature, so keep her home from school today.  她在发烧，今天别让她去上学了。

6528.e: That tweet raised the temperature of an already bitter dispute.  那条推文让本已激烈的争端更加火上浇油。

6529.e: The nurse took his temperature twice before letting him into the ward.  护士给他量了两次体温才放他进病房。

6530.e: Don't tempt fate by driving that old van across the mountains.  别开那辆破面包车翻山，纯属冒险。

6531.i: ten out of ˈten (for sth) (BrE, often ironic)
6531.e: Ten out of ten for effort, but the spelling still needs work.  态度满分，可拼写还得下功夫。

6532.e: Ten to one he'll be late again and blame the traffic.  十有八九他又要迟到，然后怪路上堵。

6533.i: (be) on ˈtenterhooks (AmE also be on ˌpins and ˈneedles)
6533.e: We were on tenterhooks waiting for the exam results all morning.  等成绩的那一上午我们如坐针毡。

6534.e: In the long term, renting here will cost more than buying.  从长期看，在这儿租房比买房还贵。

6535.i: be on good, bad, friendly, etc. ˈterms (with sb)
6535.cn: 与某人关系好（或不好等）
6535.e: They're still on good terms with each other despite the divorce.  尽管离了婚，两人关系依然不错。

6536.e: It took him years to come to terms with his father's death.  他花了好几年才接受父亲去世的事实。

6537.e: She returned to work on her own terms, three days a week.  她按自己的条件复工，一周只上三天班。

6538.e: In terms of cost, the train beats flying for this short trip.  就费用而言，这趟短途坐火车比飞机划算。

6539.e: Late nights come with the territory when you work in restaurants.  干餐饮这行，熬夜是免不了的。

6540.e: The storm put our new roof to the test on the first night.  头一晚的暴风雨就把新屋顶考验了一番。

6541.e: Few pop songs stand the test of time as well as this one.  没几首流行歌能像这首一样经得起时间考验。

6542.e: We're testing the water with a small pop-up shop before committing.  我们先开个快闪小店探探反应，再决定投入。

6543.e: They had a long tete-a-tete in the corner about the merger.  他们在角落里就并购的事密谈了很久。

6544.i: be at the end of your ˈtether (BrE)
6544.e: After three sleepless nights she was at the end of her tether.  三个晚上没合眼，她已经到了崩溃边缘。

6589.i: have a thin ˈtime (of it) (BrE, informal)
6589.cn: 日子不好过；生意不景气
6589.e: Small bookshops have had a thin time of it since the mall opened.  商场开了以后，小书店的日子一直不好过。

6600.cn: 对…有强烈的好感（或恶感）
6600.e: My brother has a thing about spiders and won't go in the shed.  我弟弟特别怕蜘蛛，死活不肯进那间棚屋。

6601.i: it isn't my, his, etc. ˈthing
6601.cn: 这不是我（或他等）喜欢的事
6601.e: Thanks for the invitation, but loud clubs really aren't my thing.  谢谢邀请，不过吵闹的夜店真不是我的菜。

6602.i: it's ˌone thing to do ˈA, it's (quite) aˌnother (thing) to do ˈB
6602.cn: 做甲是一回事，做乙则是另一回事
6602.e: It's one thing to promise help, it's quite another to turn up at dawn.  答应帮忙是一回事，天亮就到场是另一回事。

6603.i: A is ˈone thing, B is (quite) aˈnother
6603.cn: 甲是一回事，乙则是另一回事
6603.e: Reading about cooking is one thing, feeding twenty guests is quite another.  看菜谱是一回事，招待二十位客人是另一回事。

6604.i: A is ˈone thing, B is (quite) aˈnother
6604.e: Talent is one thing, discipline is quite another, and he lacks the second.  天赋是一回事，自律是另一回事，他缺的是后者。

6605.e: You wouldn't understand the joke — it's a medical student thing.  这个笑话你不会懂，是医学生之间才明白的梗。

6606.i: make a (big) ˈthing of/out of sth (informal)
6606.e: Please don't make a big thing of my birthday; a quiet dinner is fine.  别把我的生日搞得那么隆重，安静吃顿饭就好。

6607.cn: 坏事一桩接一桩；祸不单行
6607.e: Burst pipe, dead car, lost passport — it's one thing after another.  水管爆了，车坏了，护照丢了，真是祸不单行。

6608.cn: （因为）这样那样的事；忙这忙那
6608.e: What with one thing and another, I never got round to calling her back.  忙这忙那的，我一直没顾上给她回电话。

6609.e: We met at a wedding, one thing led to another, and now we're married.  我们在婚礼上认识，顺理成章，现在我们结婚了。

6610.i: there's no such ˌthing as a free ˈlunch
6610.e: That free trial wants your card details — there's no such thing as a free lunch.  免费试用要你的银行卡号，天下没有免费的午餐。

6611.i: there's only ˌone thing ˈfor it
6611.cn: 只有一个办法；别无选择
6611.e: The road is flooded, so there's only one thing for it — we walk.  路淹了，只有一个办法，我们走过去。

6612.e: He's really into the whole camping thing now, tent and all.  他现在特别迷露营那一套，帐篷什么都齐了。

6613.e: I'd love to come; the only thing is, I'm working till nine.  我很想来，只是我要工作到九点。

6614.cn: 事实是；主要原因是；问题是
6614.e: The thing about this job is that nobody ever tells you the rules.  这份工作的问题在于，从来没人告诉你规矩。

6615.e: Handwritten letters have become a thing of the past in our office.  在我们办公室，手写信早就成了老黄历。

6616.e: Wearing trainers to the funeral was not quite the thing, everyone noticed.  穿运动鞋去葬礼不太得体，大家都注意到了。

6617.cn: 从总体来看；考虑到各种因素
6617.e: All things considered, the trip went pretty well despite the rain.  总的来说，虽然下雨，这趟旅行还算顺利。

6618.e: She sells candles, soap and things like that at the weekend market.  她在周末集市上卖蜡烛、香皂之类的东西。

6619.cn: 照目前的情况；就眼下的形势看
6619.e: As things stand, we can't afford to hire anyone before spring.  照目前的情况，开春之前我们雇不起人。

6620.i: be all ˌthings to all ˈmen/people (saying)
6620.e: A good politician tries to be all things to all people and pleases nobody.  好政客想八面玲珑，结果谁也讨好不了。

6621.cn: 深深打动某人；让某人心动
6621.e: That old jazz record really does things to me every time I hear it.  那张老爵士唱片我每次听都心头一颤。

6622.e: In all things he showed the same patience, even when the plan collapsed.  无论何事他都同样有耐心，连计划崩了也一样。

6623.cn: 难免的倒霉事；在所难免的事
6623.e: Missing the ferry by two minutes was just one of those things.  差两分钟没赶上渡轮，这种倒霉事难免。

6624.e: All things being equal, I'd rather take the earlier train home.  其他条件相同的话，我宁愿坐早一班火车回家。

6625.e: He apologized and offered to pay, hoping to put things right.  他道了歉还提出赔钱，想把事情弥补过来。

6626.e: I must be hearing things — did that cat just say my name?  我肯定是幻听了，那只猫刚叫我名字？

6627.i: these things are sent to ˈtry us (saying)
6627.cn: 这是上天对我们的考验
6627.e: The boiler broke on Christmas Day, but these things are sent to try us.  锅炉圣诞节坏了，只能说是上天考验我们。

6628.cn: 这种事总会发生；谁都会碰上
6628.e: Don't cry over the broken vase — these things happen to everyone.  花瓶碎了别哭，这种事谁都会碰上。

6629.i: things that go ˌbump in the ˈnight (informal, humorous)
6629.cn: 夜里的怪响；无法解释的怪事
6629.e: My little sister still won't sleep alone, afraid of things that go bump in the night.  我妹妹还是不敢独睡，怕夜里的怪响。

6630.i: make the best of sth/things/a bad job
6630.cn: 尽量把坏事往好里做；随遇而安
6630.e: The tent leaked, but we made the best of things and lit a fire.  帐篷漏雨，我们只好将就着生了堆火。

6631.cn: （评价怪异行为）别人还以为…呢
6631.e: Anyone would think you'd won the lottery, the way you're smiling.  看你笑成那样，别人还以为你中彩票了。

6632.cn: （评价怪异行为）按说应该…；别人会以为…
6632.e: You would have thought he'd call after borrowing my car for a week.  借了我一周的车，按说他总该打个电话吧。

6633.i: come to ˈthink of it (also ˈthinking about it)
6633.e: Come to think of it, I did see her at the station yesterday morning.  对了，我昨天上午确实在车站见过她。

6634.i: give sb something to think about (informal)
6634.cn: 让某人好好想想；促使某人反省
6634.e: Losing the first round gave the champion something to think about.  首轮失利让这位冠军好好反省了一番。

6635.e: If he thinks I'll work every weekend, he's got another thing coming.  他要以为我会每个周末加班，那可想错了。

6636.e: When you think about it, we've never actually met her parents.  仔细想想，我们其实从没见过她父母。

6637.i: I should think ˈso/ˈnot (also I should think she, etc. ˈis/ˈdoes/ˈdid, etc.)
6637.cn: （强调赞同）我看也是；当然如此
6637.e: 'He apologized to the waiter.' 'I should think so too.'  「他向服务员道歉了。」「那是应该的。」

6638.i: I shudder/dread to ˈthink (how, what, etc....)
6638.e: I dread to think what this kitchen renovation is going to cost us.  我都不敢想这次厨房翻修要花多少钱。

6639.cn: （表示兴奋或震惊）想想看；只要想想
6639.e: Just think — this time next week we'll be swimming in the sea.  想想看，下周这时候我们就在海里游泳了。

6640.i: not ˈthink of sth/of doing sth
6640.cn: 决不考虑；根本不会想到
6640.e: She wouldn't think of leaving the dog alone for a whole weekend.  她根本不会考虑把狗独自留一整个周末。

6641.i: (used with wouldn't, couldn't, won't or can't)
6641.cn: （与否定式连用）从没想过；肯定不会
6641.e: Used with wouldn't or can't, the phrase means you would never consider it.  与 wouldn't 或 can't 连用时，这个说法表示你绝不会考虑。

6642.e: If you believe a diet alone will fix this, you should think again.  你要是觉得光靠节食就能解决，还是再想想吧。

6643.cn: 自言自语；把想法说出来
6643.e: Sorry, ignore me — I'm just thinking aloud about next year's budget.  抱歉别理我，我只是在把明年预算的想法念叨出来。

6644.e: I thought the better of him after he admitted the mistake publicly.  他当众承认错误后，我对他评价更高了。

6645.i: think ˈbetter of it/of doing sth
6645.e: She raised her hand to argue, then thought better of it and sat down.  她举手想争辩，转念一想又坐了回去。

6646.e: Stop planning a stall and think big — open a proper restaurant.  别老想着摆摊，眼光放大点，开家像样的餐馆。

6647.e: Our clients think very highly of her, especially her attention to detail.  客户对她评价很高，尤其欣赏她注重细节。

6648.i: think ˈnothing of sth/of doing sth
6648.cn: 觉得不算什么；习以为常
6648.e: My grandfather thinks nothing of walking ten miles before breakfast.  我爷爷早饭前走上十英里，根本不当回事。

6649.i: not think ˈanything of sth/of doing sth
6649.cn: 觉得不算什么；认为很平常
6649.e: She doesn't think anything of driving five hours to see a concert.  开五小时车去看演唱会，她觉得不算什么。

6650.e: 'Thanks for carrying my bags.' 'Think nothing of it, really.'  「谢谢你帮我拎包。」「别客气，真的。」

6651.e: When the projector died, she had to think on her feet and keep talking.  投影仪坏了，她只能随机应变继续讲下去。

6652.i: think out of the ˈbox (also think outside the ˈbox)
6652.cn: 跳出常规思考；换个角度看问题
6652.e: We need someone who can think outside the box, not follow old rules.  我们需要能跳出框框思考的人，而不是守旧的人。

6653.i: think out of the ˈbox (also think outside the ˈbox)
6653.cn: 创新思维；打破常规地想问题
6653.e: Thinking out of the box would improve public education far more than money.  创新思维对公共教育的提升远大于砸钱。

6654.i: think you ˈown the place (also behave/act as if you ˈown the place) (disapproving)
6654.e: The new intern walks around like he thinks he owns the place.  那个新来的实习生走起路来一副老板派头。

6655.i: behave/act as if you ˈown the place (disapproving)
6655.e: He acts as if he owns the place, rearranging everyone's desks without asking.  他一副主人做派，不打招呼就把大家的桌子挪来挪去。

6656.e: Think positive — the interview went badly, but there are other jobs.  往好处想，这次面试搞砸了，还有别的机会。

6657.e: I'd had four hours' sleep and simply couldn't think straight at the meeting.  我只睡了四小时，开会时脑子完全转不动。

6658.i: think the sun shines out of sb's ˈarse ⚠ (BrE)
6658.cn: 把某人捧上天；对某人极其崇拜
6658.e: Her parents think the sun shines out of her arse, whatever she does.  不管她做什么，她父母都把她捧上天。

6659.i: think the sun shines out of sb's ˈbackside (BrE) (AmE think the sun shines out of sb's ˈass ⚠) (slang)
6659.cn: 极为看重某人；对某人事事满意
6659.e: The coach thinks the sun shines out of that striker's backside.  教练觉得那个前锋做什么都对。

6660.i: (not) think ˈtwice about sth/about doing sth
6660.e: She didn't think twice about lending him the money she'd saved.  她二话不说就把攒的钱借给了他。

6661.i: (not) think ˈtwice about sth/about doing sth
6661.e: If they offered me a job abroad, I wouldn't think twice about taking it.  要是有人给我一份国外的工作，我会毫不犹豫地答应。

6662.e: The children think the world of their swimming teacher.  孩子们特别喜欢他们的游泳老师。

6663.e: To think that this quiet street was once full of noisy factories!  真没想到这条安静的街当年满是喧闹的工厂！

6664.i: who does sb think they ˈare? (disapproving, informal)
6664.e: Who does he think he is, telling me how to raise my own children?  他以为自己是谁，教我怎么带孩子？

6665.e: Put your thinking cap on — we need a name for the new café by Friday.  动动脑筋，周五之前得给新咖啡馆起个名字。

6666.e: My mum gave me the third degree about where I'd been all night.  我妈追问了我一整晚上哪儿去了。

6667.i: third time ˈlucky (AmE also third time is the ˈcharm)
6667.cn: 第三次就走运了；事不过三
6667.e: He failed his driving test twice, but third time lucky — he passed.  他驾照考砸了两次，第三次总算过了。

6668.i: ˌthis and ˈthat (also ˌthis, that and the ˈother)
6668.cn: 这样那样的事；各种各样的东西
6668.e: We sat in the kitchen chatting about this and that until midnight.  我们坐在厨房东拉西扯聊到半夜。

6669.e: 'Nobody reads the manual anyway.' 'This is it — they just click around.'  「反正没人看说明书。」「就是这样，大家乱点一通。」

6670.i: be a thorn in your ˈflesh/ˈside
6670.cn: 眼中钉；不断让人烦心的人（或事）
6670.e: That noisy pub has been a thorn in our side for the past three years.  那家吵闹的酒吧三年来一直是我们的心头刺。

6671.e: 'He forgot the tickets.' 'I thought as much when he ran back inside.'  「他忘了带票。」「他跑回屋时我就料到了。」

6672.cn: 重要的是心意；情义胜过礼物
6672.e: The cake was burnt, but it's the thought that counts.  蛋糕烤糊了，不过心意最重要。

6673.i: in (sb's/sth's) ˈthrall • in ˈthrall to sb/sth
6673.e: The whole village was in thrall to one wealthy landowner for decades.  几十年来整个村子都受一个大地主的控制。

6674.e: She threaded her way through the crowd to reach the front of the stage.  她在人群中穿行，挤到了舞台前面。

6675.i: (yes sir, no sir) three bags ˈfull (sir) (old-fashioned, humorous)
6675.cn: 唯唯诺诺；一味顺从（含讽刺）
6675.e: It's all yes sir, no sir, three bags full sir with him around the manager.  他在经理面前就是一味点头哈腰。

6676.e: Let's give three cheers for the cooks who fed two hundred people today.  让我们为今天做了两百人饭的厨师们欢呼三声。

6677.cn: 欢呼三声；高声喝彩表示赞扬
6677.e: The crowd gave three cheers for the lifeboat crew as they came ashore.  救生艇队员上岸时，人群为他们欢呼三声。

6678.e: The old headmaster insisted the three R's mattered more than anything else.  老校长坚持认为读写算三门基础课最重要。

6679.e: By ten o'clock the groom was already three sheets to the wind.  才十点钟，新郎就已经醉得东倒西歪了。

6680.i: be on the ˈthreshold of sth (formal)
6680.e: At eighteen she stood on the threshold of a completely new life.  十八岁的她正站在全新生活的门槛上。

6681.e: He misses the thrills and spills of racing motorbikes every weekend.  他怀念每个周末赛摩托车的那种刺激。

6682.cn: 自取灭亡；搬起石头砸自己的脚
6682.e: By insulting his only client, he was cutting his own throat.  他辱骂唯一的客户，这是自断财路。

6683.i: ram, force, thrust, etc. sth down sb's ˈthroat (informal)
6683.e: Stop ramming your diet advice down my throat every single mealtime.  别每顿饭都把你的节食理论硬塞给我。

6684.i: ram, force, thrust, etc. sth down sb's ˈthroat (informal)
6684.cn: 强迫某人接受；强行灌输
6684.e: The adverts force the same slogan down your throat all evening.  那些广告整晚把同一句口号硬灌进你耳朵。

6685.cn: 激烈争吵；打得不可开交
6685.e: The two brothers were at each other's throats over their father's house.  兄弟俩为父亲的房子吵得不可开交。

6686.cn: 激烈争吵（或打斗）；互不相让
6686.e: Within an hour of the meeting, the two departments were at one another's throats.  会议开了不到一小时，两个部门就吵翻了天。

6687.i: in the ˈthroes of sth/doing sth
6687.cn: 正忙于（困难之事）；正处于…的困难期
6687.e: We're in the throes of moving house, so the place is chaos.  我们正忙着搬家，家里乱成一团。

6688.e: After two hours in that storm I was soaked through and through.  在那场暴雨里待了两小时，我浑身湿透了。

6689.e: The concert tickets were eighty pounds a throw, so we stayed home.  演唱会门票每张八十镑，我们就待家里了。

6690.cn: 激烈的论战；白热化的竞争
6690.e: She loved the cut and thrust of courtroom debate far more than paperwork.  比起文书工作，她更爱法庭辩论的针锋相对。

6691.e: The company thumbed its nose at the regulators and kept polluting.  这家公司无视监管部门，继续排污。

6692.e: He's been under his older sister's thumb since they were children.  他从小就完全听姐姐的摆布。

6693.i: be all ˈthumbs (also be all ˌfingers and ˈthumbs)
6693.e: I'm all thumbs today — that's the second glass I've dropped.  我今天笨手笨脚的，这已经是摔的第二个杯子了。

6694.e: Hold thumbs for me — I hear about the scholarship tomorrow morning.  帮我祈祷吧，明天上午奖学金结果就出来了。

6695.cn: 表示赞成（或反对）；获批准（或否决）
6695.e: The council finally gave our playground plan the thumbs up.  市政会终于批准了我们的游乐场方案。

6696.i: get, buy, etc. sth on ˈtick (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
6696.e: In those days you could buy groceries on tick and pay at month's end.  那年头买菜可以赊账，月底再结。

6697.i: tick sth off on your ˈfingers
6697.e: He ticked off on his fingers all the towns he'd cycled through.  他掰着手指数出骑车经过的每一座小镇。

6698.cn: 某人的行为动机；某人心里想什么
6698.e: After ten years I still don't know what makes my neighbour tick.  认识十年了，我还是摸不透邻居到底怎么想。

6699.cn: 这正是所需要的；这才对
6699.e: A hot bath and an early night — that's the ticket after a day like this.  洗个热水澡早点睡，这样一天下来正需要这个。

6700.e: If the rain doesn't stop by noon, it's tickets for the outdoor wedding.  中午前雨要不停，这场户外婚礼就完了。

6701.i: be tickled ˈpink (also be tickled to ˈdeath)
6701.e: Gran was tickled pink when the whole family turned up unannounced.  全家人突然登门，奶奶乐得合不拢嘴。

6702.cn: 形势发生变化（尤指好转）
6702.e: The tide turned in the second half and our team scored three goals.  下半场形势逆转，我们队连进三球。

6703.cn: 束缚某人的手脚；使某人无法自主
6703.e: The new regulations tie our hands when it comes to hiring students.  新规定让我们在招学生这件事上束手束脚。

6704.e: The lawyer tied the witness in knots within five minutes.  律师五分钟内就把证人问得晕头转向。

6705.e: They finally tied the knot last June after twelve years together.  在一起十二年后，他们去年六月终于结婚了。

6706.e: He tied one on after the exams and slept until three the next day.  考完试他喝得烂醉，第二天睡到下午三点。

6707.e: Lending him the deposit put us in a tight spot that whole winter.  把押金借给他，害我们整个冬天都很拮据。

6708.i: keep a tight ˈrein on sb/sth (also keep sb/sth on a tight ˈleash)
6708.e: The new manager keeps a tight rein on travel expenses.  新经理把差旅费管得很严。

6709.e: She runs a tight ship; nothing in that kitchen is ever out of place.  她管理有方，那间厨房里从没有东西乱放。

6710.e: Six of us in that little car was a tight squeeze, but we managed.  六个人挤那辆小车里真够呛，不过还是挤下了。

6711.e: With the rent going up again, we'll have to tighten our belts.  房租又涨了，我们只能勒紧裤腰带过日子。

6712.cn: 走钢丝；如履薄冰地行事
6712.e: He walks a tightrope between pleasing his boss and protecting his team.  他在讨好老板和保护团队之间走钢丝。

6713.cn: 处境微妙；如走钢丝般艰难
6713.e: The negotiator was on a tightrope with both sides threatening to leave.  两边都威胁要退出，谈判代表如走钢丝。

6714.i: have your ˌfingers/ˌhand in the ˈtill (BrE, informal)
6714.e: The accountant had his hand in the till for almost four years.  那位会计监守自盗了将近四年。

6715.cn: 跟假想敌搏斗；徒费精力
6715.e: Complaining to that office is tilting at windmills; nobody ever replies.  向那个办公室投诉是白费劲，从来没人回。

6716.i: This expression comes from Cervantes' novel Don Quixote.
6716.cn: 此语出自塞万提斯的小说《堂吉诃德》
6716.e: This expression comes from Cervantes' novel, in which the hero fights windmills.  这个说法出自塞万提斯的小说，书中主人公与风车搏斗。

6717.cn: 早该如此；也该是时候了
6717.e: They're finally fixing the road, and about time too.  他们总算要修那条路了，也该是时候了。

6718.e: The heating came back on at last, and not before time.  暖气总算又来了，早就该修好了。

6719.e: The rescue team worked against time to reach the trapped miners.  救援队争分夺秒地赶去营救被困矿工。

6720.e: The builders finished the extension two weeks ahead of time.  施工队提前两周完成了加建工程。

6721.i: all the ˈtime • the whole ˈtime
6721.e: I was looking for my glasses, and they were on my head the whole time.  我到处找眼镜，其实一直在我头上。

6722.cn: （回应致谢）不客气；随时乐意效劳
6722.e: 'Thanks for the lift home.' 'Any time, just give me a call.'  「谢谢你送我回家。」「随时效劳，打电话就行。」

6723.e: He climbed the stairs two at a time to catch her before she left.  他两级一步跑上楼，想在她走前拦住她。

6724.e: It seemed like a good idea at the time, but now I regret it.  当时看着是个好主意，现在我后悔了。

6725.i: at ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. time of life
6725.e: At my time of life I'm not going to start learning to ski.  我这个岁数了，不会去学滑雪。

6726.i: be ahead of/before/in advance of your ˈtime
6726.cn: 超越时代；思想（或做法）超前
6726.e: Her ideas about school design were well ahead of their time.  她关于校舍设计的想法远远超越了那个时代。

6727.i: be ahead of/before/in advance of your ˈtime
6727.e: That composer was before his time and died completely unknown.  那位作曲家生不逢时，去世时无人知晓。

6728.cn: 在某人记事之前；早于某人的年代
6728.e: The old cinema closed in 1975, so it was before my time.  那家老电影院一九七五年就关了，我那时还没出生。

6729.cn: 停留在过去；仿佛困在旧时光里
6729.e: That barber's shop is stuck in a time warp, right down to the posters.  那家理发店活像停在了过去，连海报都没换。

6730.e: He did time for fraud and now warns students about easy money.  他因诈骗坐过牢，如今告诫学生别想着走捷径。

6731.e: Homemade bread over supermarket bread, every time.  自家烤的面包比超市的强，我永远选前者。

6732.i: for the time ˈbeing (also for the ˈmoment/ˈpresent)
6732.e: For the time being we're staying with my parents until the flat's ready.  房子弄好之前，我们暂时住在我父母家。

6733.e: Fishermen have used this harbour since time immemorial.  自古以来渔民就使用这个港口。

6734.e: From time to time she still sends me a postcard from Athens.  她偶尔还会从雅典给我寄张明信片。

6735.i: give sb a rough, hard, bad, etc. ˈtime (of it)
6735.cn: 故意为难某人；让某人不好过
6735.e: The other kids gave him a hard time about his accent all term.  整个学期其他孩子都拿他的口音取笑他。

6736.i: have a lot of ˈtime for sb/sth (informal, especially BrE)
6736.e: I have a lot of time for our postman; he checks on the elderly.  我很欣赏我们的邮递员，他会去看看独居老人。

6737.e: She has no time for people who complain but never vote.  她瞧不上那些只会抱怨却从不投票的人。

6738.i: not have much ˈtime for sb/sth (informal)
6738.e: He doesn't have much time for meetings that could have been emails.  他很不喜欢那些本可以发邮件解决的会议。

6739.i: have a (hard, rough, bad, etc.) ˈtime of it
6739.e: They've had a rough time of it since the factory closed last spring.  自从去年春天工厂关门，他们的日子一直很难过。

6740.i: have the ˌtime of your ˈlife (informal)
6740.cn: 玩得非常痛快；快活极了
6740.e: The kids had the time of their lives at the seaside last weekend.  上周末孩子们在海边玩得别提多开心了。

6741.cn: 闲着没事；空闲时间太多
6741.e: Since retiring he's had time on his hands and started painting.  退休后他闲得慌，就开始画画了。

6742.cn: 到时候自然会；不用着急
6742.e: You'll hear the results all in good time, so stop refreshing your inbox.  结果到时候自然会通知，别老刷邮箱了。

6743.e: We arrived at the airport in good time and had breakfast there.  我们提前到了机场，还在那儿吃了早饭。

6744.e: She fixed the bike in no time and we were back on the road.  她三两下就把自行车修好，我们又上路了。

6745.cn: 等自己方便时；等自己准备好再说
6745.e: He'll tell us what happened in his own good time; don't push him.  他想说的时候自然会说，别逼他。

6746.cn: 在业余时间；用自己的时间
6746.e: She learnt Spanish in her own time, mostly on the train to work.  她利用业余时间学西班牙语，大多是在上班的火车上。

6747.e: We got to the hospital in time to see him before the operation.  我们及时赶到医院，在他手术前见了一面。

6748.e: It's high time you learned to cook something other than noodles.  你早就该学着做点面条以外的东西了。

6749.i: it's only, just, etc. a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)
6749.cn: 只是时间问题；迟早的事
6749.e: It's only a matter of time before that old bridge has to close.  那座老桥关闭只是时间问题。

6750.i: it's only a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)
6750.cn: 迟早的事；只是时间问题
6750.e: With those cracks, it's just a question of time before the wall falls.  裂成那样，墙塌下来是迟早的事。

6751.e: That old kitchen clock still keeps perfect time after forty years.  厨房那只老钟用了四十年，走得还是很准。

6752.e: She lost no time in reporting the leak to the landlord.  她一刻没耽误，马上向房东报告了漏水的事。

6753.cn: 行程顺利；走得比预期快
6753.e: We made good time on the motorway and arrived before lunch.  高速上走得挺顺，午饭前就到了。

6754.e: However busy he is, he makes time to read to his daughter.  不管多忙，他都抽时间给女儿读书。

6755.i: ˈmany a time • ˈmany's the time (that)...
6755.e: Many a time I've walked home from that station in the rain.  我不知多少次冒雨从那个车站走回家。

6756.i: but then we wouldn't see the children growing up
6756.cn: 可那样就看不到孩子长大了
6756.e: We could move to Australia, but then we wouldn't see the children growing up.  我们可以搬去澳大利亚，可那样就看不到孩子长大了。

6757.i: (the) next, first, second, etc. time aˈround/aˈround
6757.cn: 下一次（或第一次等）同样的事发生时
6757.e: The first time around we panicked; the second time around we knew better.  第一次我们慌了神，第二次就有数了。

6758.i: not give sb the ˌtime of ˈday
6758.e: Ever since the argument, she won't give me the time of day.  自从那次争吵，她再也不肯搭理我。

6759.cn: 现在就是最好的时机；说做就做
6759.e: You want to call her? There's no time like the present.  你想给她打电话？现在就打，别等了。

6760.e: Many fans still call him the greatest goalkeeper of all time.  很多球迷仍称他为有史以来最伟大的门将。

6761.e: For once the six-fifteen train arrived bang on time.  六点一刻那班火车难得地准点到了。

6762.e: He kept asking pointless questions, clearly playing for time.  他不停问些没用的问题，明摆着是在拖时间。

6763.i: take your ˈtime (doing sth/to do sth/over sth)
6763.e: Take your time over the exam; you've still got forty minutes left.  考试慢慢做，你还有四十分钟。

6764.cn: 刻不容缓；一刻也不能耽搁
6764.e: The tide is coming in fast, so there's no time to lose.  潮水涨得快，一刻也不能耽搁。

6765.i: there's no time to be ˈlost (saying)
6765.cn: 必须立刻行动；没时间可耽搁
6765.e: The storm is two hours away, so there's no time to be lost.  风暴两小时后就到，没时间可耽搁了。

6766.i: ˌtime after ˈtime • ˌtime and (time) aˈgain
6766.e: Time and again I've told him to lock the back gate at night.  我一遍又一遍告诉他晚上要锁后门。

6767.cn: 时间过得真快；光阴似箭
6767.e: Time flies — our little nephew starts secondary school this autumn.  时间过得真快，小侄子今年秋天就上中学了。

6768.e: Time hangs heavy on his hands now that the workshop has closed.  作坊关了以后，他闲得日子都不好打发。

6769.cn: 时间不早了；没多少时间了
6769.e: Time's getting on — we should leave if we want that last bus.  时间不早了，想赶末班车我们该走了。

6770.e: Hurry up and load the van; time is money in this business.  快点装车，干这行时间就是金钱。

6771.i: time is on sb's ˈside (also have time on your side)
6771.cn: 有的是时间；时间对某人有利
6771.e: She's only twenty-two, so time is on her side.  她才二十二岁，有的是时间。

6772.i: the time is ˈripe (for sb) (to do sth)
6772.e: The time is ripe for us to open a second shop in the old town.  在老城区开第二家店，时机已经成熟。

6773.i: the time is ˈripe for sth/for doing sth (literary)
6773.cn: 时机成熟；正是做某事的时候
6773.e: With prices falling, the time is ripe for buying a small flat.  房价在跌，正是买小户型的好时机。

6774.cn: 曾经有那么个时候；那年头
6774.e: Time was when you could leave your front door unlocked all night.  那年头你家大门整夜不锁都没事。

6775.i: time (alone) will ˈtell • only time will ˈtell
6775.e: Whether this new manager is any good, only time will tell.  这位新经理行不行，只有时间能证明。

6776.e: Visitors must wear their badges at all times inside the laboratory.  在实验室内，访客必须随时佩戴证件。

6777.e: At times he can be difficult, but he's a loyal friend.  他有时挺难相处，但是个讲义气的朋友。

6778.e: Their booking system is paper-based; they're really behind the times.  他们的预订还用纸质记录，实在太落伍了。

6779.i: keep up, move, etc. with the ˈtimes
6779.e: The old library moved with the times and now lends e-books too.  那家老图书馆与时俱进，现在也出借电子书。

6780.e: I love singing, but I've got a tin ear and everybody knows it.  我爱唱歌，可惜五音不全，大家都知道。

6781.i: be on the tip of your ˈtongue
6781.e: Her name was on the tip of my tongue the whole evening.  她的名字整晚都在我嘴边，就是想不起来。

6782.i: be the tip of the ˈiceberg
6782.cn: 只是冰山一角；只是问题的一小部分
6782.e: Those two complaints are just the tip of the iceberg, believe me.  信我的，那两起投诉不过是冰山一角。

6783.i: tip the ˈbalance/ˈscales (also swing the ˈbalance/ˈscales)
6783.cn: 使天平倾斜；起决定性作用
6783.e: Her experience abroad tipped the balance in favour of hiring her.  她的海外经历成了录用她的决定因素。

6784.e: The prize pumpkin tipped the scales at nearly ninety kilos.  那个获奖南瓜足足有近九十公斤重。

6785.i: tip sb the ˈwink • tip the ˈwink to sb (BrE, informal)
6785.e: A friend at the agency tipped me the wink about the job opening.  中介的朋友偷偷给我透了那个职位的信儿。

6786.e: Don't go out now, it's absolutely tipping it down out there.  现在别出门，外面正下着瓢泼大雨。

6787.e: That rent rise was the tipping point that made us leave the city.  那次涨房租成了我们离开这座城市的临界点。

6788.e: She crossed the room on tiptoe so as not to wake the baby.  她踮着脚穿过房间，怕吵醒宝宝。

6789.e: He never tires of telling that story about the fish he caught.  他百说不厌那条鱼的故事。

6790.e: I'm getting tired of hearing the same excuse every Monday morning.  每周一早上听同样的借口，我烦透了。

6791.e: His account of that night turned out to be a tissue of lies.  他对那晚的说法后来证明全是谎话。

6792.e: They blocked our driveway, so we parked in theirs — pure tit for tat.  他们堵我们车道，我们就停他们那儿，纯属以牙还牙。

6793.e: Mum got into a tizzy about the guests arriving an hour early.  客人早到一小时，妈妈就慌了神。

6794.e: The old ferry chugs to and fro across the river all day long.  那艘老渡轮整天突突地在河上来回。

6795.cn: 完全归某人独享（或独用）
6795.e: With everyone away, I had the whole beach to myself.  大家都走了，整片沙滩就归我一个人了。

6796.e: If the boss sees this spreadsheet, we're toast.  老板要是看到这张表，我们就完了。

6797.cn: 在…广受赞誉；成为…的红人
6797.e: After that goal he was the toast of the entire town for weeks.  那个进球之后，他好几周都是全城的名人。

6798.cn: （在某地）广受赞誉；被众口称赞
6798.e: Her first novel made her the toast of literary London that year.  她的处女作让她那一年成了伦敦文坛的宠儿。

6799.e: He spent the whole bank holiday on his tod watching old films.  整个公休日他一个人在家看老电影。

6800.e: These trends are here today, gone tomorrow, so don't invest much.  这些潮流来得快去得也快，别投太多钱。

6801.e: The small firm went toe to toe with a giant and somehow won.  那家小公司跟巨头正面硬碰，居然赢了。

6802.i: toe the ˈline (AmE also toe the ˈmark)
6802.e: New staff are expected to toe the line for the first six months.  新员工头六个月都得规规矩矩听指挥。

6803.cn: 使某人保持警惕；让人不敢松懈
6803.e: Surprise inspections keep the kitchen staff on their toes.  突击检查让厨房的人不敢松懈。

6804.cn: 使某人尴尬；让人浑身不自在
6804.e: His speech about my childhood made my toes curl.  他讲我童年的那段话让我尴尬得脚趾抠地。

6805.e: Stay on your toes; the fire alarm test could come any minute.  保持警觉，火警测试随时可能开始。

6806.i: can't do sth for ˈtoffee (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)
6806.cn: 做某事很蹩脚；完全不在行
6806.e: She's a brilliant writer but can't spell for toffee.  她文章写得极好，可拼写差得一塌糊涂。

6807.e: Send your passport together with two recent photographs.  请把护照连同两张近照一并寄来。

6808.e: After weeks of toing and froing, they finally agreed on a price.  来回折腾了好几周，他们总算谈妥了价钱。

6809.e: He's never late, and by the same token he expects punctuality from us.  他从不迟到，同样地，他也要求我们守时。

6810.e: All told, about two hundred people turned up for the beach clean-up.  总共有大约两百人来参加海滩清理。

6811.i: take its ˈtoll (on sb/sth) (also take a (heavy) ˈtoll (of sth))
6811.cn: 造成损失；带来严重后果
6811.e: Those night shifts are taking their toll on his health.  那些夜班正在损害他的健康。

6812.i: every/any ˌTom, ˌDick and/or ˈHarry (usually disapproving)
6812.e: You can't let every Tom, Dick and Harry borrow the studio key.  你不能随便什么人都借给他工作室的钥匙。

6813.e: In American English, tomorrow is often pronounced with the vowel in 'more'.  在美式英语里，tomorrow 常带 more 里的那个元音。

6814.i: do sth as if/like there's no toˈmorrow (informal)
6814.cn: 拼命地做；仿佛没有明天似的
6814.e: He was spending money like there's no tomorrow after the bonus arrived.  奖金一到手，他就花钱如流水。

6815.i: be/come down on sb like a ton of ˈbricks
6815.cn: 严厉斥责某人；狠狠训一顿
6815.e: The coach came down on him like a ton of bricks for missing training.  他缺席训练，被教练狠狠地骂了一顿。

6816.e: Her warm welcome set the tone for the whole weekend.  她热情的欢迎为整个周末定下了基调。

6817.e: I still can't get my tongue round the name of that Welsh village.  那个威尔士村名我到现在都念不利索。

6818.e: The new brand name doesn't exactly trip off the tongue, does it?  这个新牌子名字念着不太顺口，是吧？

6819.e: With his silver tongue he talked the landlord into lowering the rent.  他嘴皮子利索，说得房东降了租金。

6820.i: (with) tongue in ˈcheek (also with your tongue in your ˈcheek)
6820.cn: 开玩笑地；半开玩笑不当真地
6820.e: He suggested, tongue in cheek, that we hold the meeting in the pub.  他半开玩笑地提议把会开到酒吧去。

6821.cn: 惹人说长道短；引起议论纷纷
6821.e: Their arriving together at the party set tongues wagging immediately.  他俩一起到派对，立刻惹得众人议论纷纷。

6822.e: Tongues wagged for months after the manager left so suddenly.  经理走得那么突然，之后好几个月都有闲话。

6823.e: The builders downed tools at noon over the unpaid wages.  工人们因为拖欠工资，中午就停工了。

6824.e: A sharp knife and a heavy pan are the tools of her trade.  一把快刀和一口厚锅就是她吃饭的家伙。

6825.i: at the top of your ˈvoice
6825.e: He sang at the top of his voice all the way down the hill.  他一路下山都在扯着嗓子唱歌。

6826.e: It took a month, but she's finally on top of the paperwork.  花了一个月，她总算把文书工作理顺了。

6827.e: After a long legal fight, the tenants came out on top.  经过漫长的官司，租户们最终赢了。

6828.e: We cleaned the house from top to bottom before the inspection.  检查前我们把房子从上到下彻底打扫了一遍。

6829.e: He came in from the garden covered in mud from top to toe.  他从花园进来，浑身上下全是泥。

6830.cn: （困难、工作等）压得某人受不了
6830.e: The constant deadlines are really getting on top of him lately.  接连不断的截止日期最近压得他喘不过气。

6831.i: off the ˌtop of your ˈhead (informal)
6831.cn: 不加思索地；凭印象随口说
6831.e: Off the top of my head, I'd say about forty people came.  我随口一说，大概来了四十个人吧。

6832.e: On top of everything else, the washing machine broke this morning.  除了别的糟心事，今早洗衣机又坏了。

6833.e: She felt on top of the world after passing her final exam.  通过期末考试后，她觉得自己快乐得要飞起来。

6834.i: pay, earn, charge, etc. top ˈdollar
6834.e: Collectors pay top dollar for early editions of that comic.  收藏者愿出高价买那套漫画的早期版本。

6835.e: That was close, everyone — let's take it from the top once more.  差不多了，各位，我们再从头来一遍。

6836.e: Top and tail the green beans before you drop them in the water.  下锅前先把四季豆的头尾去掉。

6837.e: The top brass are flying in tomorrow to inspect the new plant.  高层明天飞过来视察新厂。

6838.cn: 居首位的人（或团体）；巨头
6838.e: That little bakery is now top dog in the local wedding-cake market.  那家小面包房如今是当地婚礼蛋糕市场的老大。

6839.i: the top of the ˈhour (especially AmE)
6839.e: We'll have the traffic report again at the top of the hour.  整点我们会再播一次路况。

6840.i: opposite: the bottom of the hour
6840.e: The opposite of the top of the hour is the bottom of the hour, meaning half past.  the top of the hour 的反义是 the bottom of the hour，即半点。

6841.e: At forty she was already at the top of the tree in her profession.  四十岁时她已经站在本行业的顶端。

6842.e: The recipe is top secret and only two people in the family know it.  这个配方是绝密，家里只有两个人知道。

6843.e: Their second single stayed in the top ten for eleven weeks.  他们的第二支单曲在前十名榜上待了十一周。

6844.cn: 每周最畅销的前十（或二十）首歌曲
6844.e: She checks the top twenty every Sunday evening without fail.  她每周日晚上雷打不动地看一遍前二十名榜单。

6845.e: We missed the train and, to top it all, it started pouring.  我们没赶上火车，更要命的是还下起了大雨。

6846.e: He's not much to look at, but there's plenty going on up top.  他外表一般，脑子却很好使。

6847.cn: 领衔演出；名列演出海报之首
6847.e: A local jazz trio will top the bill at the festival this year.  今年音乐节由一支本地爵士三重奏领衔演出。

6848.e: The retreating army put the whole warehouse district to the torch.  撤退的军队把整个仓库区付之一炬。

6849.cn: （计划被打乱时说）糟了；这下完了
6849.e: The last bus has gone — well, that's torn it.  末班车开走了，这下完了。

6850.e: 'Oops, that's torn it,' she thought, as the surprise was ruined.  「啊呀，糟了。」她心想，惊喜就这么泡汤了。

6851.e: He mentioned the party in front of her — that's torn it completely.  他当着她的面提起派对，这下全砸了。

6852.i: not give a ˈtoss (about sb/sth) (BrE, slang)
6852.e: He doesn't give a toss about what the neighbours think of his garden.  邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。

6853.i: toss a ˈcoin • ˈtoss for sth (especially BrE)
6853.e: We tossed a coin to see who would sleep on the sofa.  我们掷硬币决定谁睡沙发。

6854.i: (also flip a ˈcoin, ˈflip for sth usually both AmE)
6854.e: Let's flip a coin for the last slice of pizza.  最后一块披萨我们掷硬币决定吧。

6855.i: be a ˈtoss-up (between A and B) (informal, especially BrE)
6855.cn: 难以定夺；两者机会均等
6855.e: It's a toss-up between the blue coat and the grey one.  蓝大衣还是灰大衣，我实在难以决定。

6856.i: be, etc. in/out of ˈtouch (with sth)
6856.cn: 了解（或不了解）某事的最新情况
6856.e: After ten years abroad he's completely out of touch with local politics.  在国外待了十年，他对本地政治完全脱节了。

6857.i: be, keep, etc. in ˈtouch (with sb)
6857.e: We've kept in touch with our old landlady for over twenty years.  我们和以前的房东太太保持联系二十多年了。

6858.e: I've been out of touch with my cousins since the funeral.  葬礼之后我就和表亲们断了联系。

6859.e: Get in touch with the landlord before you sign anything.  签任何东西之前先联系房东。

6860.i: have, etc. a ˌtouch of ˈclass
6860.e: The fresh flowers on every table give the café a touch of class.  每张桌上的鲜花让这家咖啡馆多了几分格调。

6861.e: We lost touch after university and only met again last year.  大学毕业后我们就断了联系，去年才重逢。

6862.e: This cake is dry — I think Gran is losing her touch.  这蛋糕太干了，我看奶奶手艺不如从前了。

6863.i: not touch sb/sth with a ˈbargepole (BrE)
6863.cn: 唯恐避之不及；不愿沾边
6863.e: That flat is damp and overpriced; I wouldn't touch it with a bargepole.  那套房又潮又贵，我碰都不会碰。

6864.i: put sb in ˈtouch with sb/sth
6864.e: Can you put me in touch with a decent plumber in the area?  你能给我介绍个这一带靠谱的水管工吗？

6865.cn: 心软的人；容易被说动的人
6865.e: Ask Dad for the money; he's always been a soft touch.  找爸要钱吧，他一向心软。

6866.e: Let's touch base on Friday once the figures are in.  等数据出来，我们周五碰个头。

6867.e: Prices seem to have touched bottom and are slowly rising again.  价格似乎已经见底，正在慢慢回升。

6868.cn: 但愿好运；碰碰木头求吉利
6868.e: I haven't had a cold all winter, touch wood.  整个冬天我都没感冒，但愿别乌鸦嘴。

6869.i: People still often try to touch something wooden.
6869.cn: 人们说此语时仍常去碰木质物件
6869.e: People still often try to touch something wooden as they say the phrase.  人们说这句话时仍常常去碰碰木头。

6870.cn: 结果难料；不确定；有风险
6870.e: It was touch-and-go whether the surgeon could save his leg.  能不能保住他的腿，当时很难说。

6871.e: Her voice was touched with sadness as she read the letter aloud.  她朗读那封信时，声音里带着一丝伤感。

6872.cn: 对…态度强硬；采取强硬手段
6872.e: The school is getting tough with students who skip lessons.  学校对逃课的学生开始动真格了。

6873.e: She's seventy and as tough as nails; she still swims in the sea.  她七十岁了还硬朗得很，照样下海游泳。

6874.e: The steak was as tough as old boots and we sent it back.  那块牛排硬得像鞋底，我们退了回去。

6875.cn: 很有主见的人；不易被说动的人
6875.e: Don't expect a discount from her; she's a tough cookie.  别指望她给你打折，她可不好对付。

6876.e: He plays the tough guy on screen but faints at the dentist.  他在银幕上演硬汉，看牙医却会晕过去。

6877.cn: 严爱；用严厉方式表达关心
6877.e: Cutting off his allowance was tough love, but it finally worked.  断了他的零花钱是严爱，可最后管用了。

6878.cn: 严厉的爱；为对方好的严格管教
6878.e: She believes in tough love for children who constantly misbehave.  她认为对屡屡捣蛋的孩子要严爱。

6879.i: when the ˌgoing gets ˈtough (the ˌtough get ˈgoing) (saying)
6879.cn: 艰难之路唯勇者行；越难越向前
6879.e: When the going gets tough, the tough get going — so let's start again.  艰难之路唯勇者行，我们重新来过吧。

6880.e: The previous head teacher was a hard act to follow.  前任校长是个很难超越的标杆。

6881.e: Her final scene was a tour de force that left the audience silent.  她的最后一场戏堪称绝技，观众鸦雀无声。

6882.i: (out) on the ˈtown (also a night (out) on the ˈtown/on the ˈtiles) (informal)
6882.e: After the exams we all went out on the town until three in the morning.  考完试我们出去嗨到凌晨三点。

6883.e: The little fishing boat vanished without a trace off the north coast.  那条小渔船在北岸海域消失得无影无踪。

6884.cn: 商业机密；不外传的诀窍
6884.e: How she gets the pastry so light is a trade secret.  她怎么把酥皮做得那么松，这是商业机密。

6885.e: The factory closure brought unemployment and poverty in its train.  工厂倒闭带来了失业和贫困。

6886.cn: 尾随某人；跟在某人后面
6886.e: The old professor arrived with a dozen students in his train.  老教授来了，身后跟着十几个学生。

6887.e: Plans for the new footbridge are already well in train.  新人行桥的规划已在顺利推进。

6888.e: The phone rang and I completely lost my train of thought.  电话一响，我的思路全断了。

6889.i: fall into/avoid the trap of doing sth
6889.cn: 落入（或避免落入）…的陷阱
6889.e: Don't fall into the trap of buying more than you can carry.  别掉进买得太多拿不动的陷阱。

6890.e: She always travels light, just a rucksack and a toothbrush.  她出门总是轻装上阵，一个背包一把牙刷。

6891.e: He trod the boards for thirty years before turning to directing.  他登台演了三十年戏，后来转做导演。

6892.e: Tread carefully when you mention the redundancies to her.  跟她提裁员的事时要小心措辞。

6893.i: tread a difficult, solitary, etc. ˈpath
6893.cn: 走一条艰难（或孤独等）的路
6893.e: As the only woman on the board, she trod a lonely path for years.  作为董事会里唯一的女性，她孤独地走了很多年。

6894.e: The younger runners were treading on his heels all the way up the hill.  上坡的一路上，年轻选手都紧咬着他不放。

6895.e: I don't want to tread on your toes, but that's really my department's job.  我不想越界，可那本来是我们部门的活。

6896.cn: 得罪某人；插手他人职责
6896.e: He rewrote her report and stepped on her toes badly.  他把她的报告重写了一遍，狠狠得罪了她。

6897.cn: 踩水；停滞不前；原地观望
6897.e: The company is just treading water until the new owner arrives.  在新东家到来之前，公司只是在原地打转。

6898.e: Your lemon cake went down a treat at the school fair.  你的柠檬蛋糕在学校义卖上大受欢迎。

6899.cn: 把某人当垃圾；蔑视某人
6899.e: That restaurant treats its kitchen staff like dirt.  那家餐厅把后厨员工当垃圾对待。

6900.e: A spoonful of salt worked a treat on that red wine stain.  一勺盐对付那块红酒渍效果特别好。

6901.e: She gave him the silent treatment for three whole days.  她整整三天没搭理他。

6902.i: be out of your ˈtree (BrE also be out of your ˈbox) (informal)
6902.e: By midnight half the party was completely out of their trees.  到了半夜，派对上一半人都醉得不省人事。

6903.e: He learnt to bake sourdough by trial and error over two years.  他花了两年反复摸索，学会了烤酸面包。

6904.e: We did a trial run of the new booking system last Tuesday.  上周二我们对新预订系统做了一次试运行。

6905.e: She wrote honestly about the trials and tribulations of single parenthood.  她如实写下了单亲育儿的种种艰辛。

6906.e: The waiter cleared the whole table in a trice.  服务员转眼间就把整桌收拾干净了。

6907.cn: 不给糖就捣蛋（万圣节讨糖用语）
6907.e: Three small witches knocked and shouted 'trick or treat' at our door.  三个小女巫敲门喊着「不给糖就捣蛋」。

6908.i: try, use, etc. every trick in the ˈbook
6908.cn: 使尽浑身解数；千方百计
6908.e: He used every trick in the book to get out of jury duty.  他使尽了各种花招想逃掉陪审义务。

6909.e: The film follows a young woman turning tricks to pay her rent.  影片讲述一个年轻女子靠卖身付房租的故事。

6910.e: The old mechanic arrived with his usual bag of tricks.  老技工照例带着他那一整套家伙什来了。

6911.i: be up to your (old) ˈtricks (informal, disapproving)
6911.e: He's up to his old tricks, borrowing money he'll never repay.  他又故伎重演，借钱从来不还。

6912.e: Hello stranger, how's tricks? I haven't seen you in months.  嘿，稀客，最近怎么样？好几个月没见你了。

6913.e: The old baker taught him all the tricks of the trade.  老面包师把行业里的门道全教给了他。

6914.i: ˌtried and ˈtested/ˈtrusted (BrE) (AmE ˌtried and ˈtrue)
6914.cn: 久经考验的；屡试不爽的
6914.e: For a sore throat she uses the tried and tested honey and lemon.  嗓子疼时她用蜂蜜柠檬这个老方子，屡试不爽。

6915.i: be, keep, etc. in ˈtrim (BrE, informal)
6915.cn: 身体状态不错；保持健康
6915.e: He cycles to work every day to keep in trim.  他每天骑车上班，保持身材。

6916.e: With sales falling, the shop had to trim its sails sharply.  销量下滑，这家店只好大幅缩减开支。

6917.e: Swimming in that river in January? You're off your trolley.  一月份去那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。

6918.e: They've won five matches on the trot since the new coach arrived.  新教练来了以后，他们连赢五场。

6919.e: In those days a boy who got a girl into trouble had to marry her.  那年头男孩让女孩怀了孕就得娶她。

6920.cn: 给（某人）惹麻烦；带来问题
6920.e: My knee has been giving me some trouble since the marathon.  跑完马拉松后我的膝盖一直有点毛病。

6921.cn: 给某人添麻烦（或没添麻烦）
6921.e: The children didn't give me any trouble at all while you were out.  你们出去的时候孩子们一点儿也没给我添麻烦。

6922.e: Arguing with the referee like that is just looking for trouble.  那样跟裁判争执纯属自找麻烦。

6923.i: take trouble over/with sth • take trouble to do sth
6923.e: She took great trouble over the seating plan for the dinner.  她为这次晚宴的座位安排费了不少心思。

6924.cn: 要出乱子了；麻烦要来了
6924.e: Judging by those emails, there's trouble brewing in the finance team.  从那些邮件看，财务组要出乱子了。

6925.i: a trouble ˌshared is a trouble ˈhalved (saying)
6925.e: Tell me what's wrong — a trouble shared is a trouble halved.  说说怎么了，有人分担，烦恼就少一半。

6926.cn: 关键时刻帮上大忙；出乎意料地成功
6926.e: Our neighbour came up trumps and drove us to the airport at dawn.  邻居真够意思，天没亮就送我们去机场。

6927.e: Her fluent Japanese was the trump card in the interview.  她那口流利的日语是面试中的王牌。

6928.i: in sb's ˈtrust • in the trust of sb
6928.cn: 由某人保管；托付给某人照管
6928.e: The house was left in his sister's trust until the children grew up.  房子交由他姐姐保管，直到孩子们长大。

6929.e: He smiles a lot, but I wouldn't trust him an inch.  他老是笑呵呵的，可我一点也不信他。

7018.e: He was on his uppers for a year before the new job came along.  找到新工作前，他潦倒了整整一年。

7095.e: Turn that music down, it is loud enough to wake the dead.  把音乐关小点，吵得能把死人闹醒。

7096.i: wake up and smell the ˈcoffee (AmE, informal)
7096.e: Wake up and smell the coffee, nobody is going to fix this for you.  醒醒吧，没人会替你收拾这个烂摊子。

7097.cn: 警钟；起警示作用的事件
7097.e: His heart attack at forty was a real wake-up call for the whole family.  他四十岁心脏病发作，给全家敲响了警钟。

7098.i: (try to) run before you can ˈwalk (informal)
7098.cn: 还没学会走就想跑；急于求成
7098.e: You are trying to run before you can walk with this business plan.  这份创业计划，你还没学会走就想跑了。

7099.e: He kept bothering the waitress until the manager told him to take a walk.  他一直骚扰服务员，经理让他滚蛋。

7100.e: Do not let your new colleagues walk all over you like that.  别让新同事那样欺负你。

7101.cn: 无罪释放；以自由之身离开法庭
7101.e: Two of the accused walked free after the main witness changed her story.  主要证人改口后，两名被告被当庭释放。

7102.i: a walk in the ˈpark (especially AmE)
7102.e: After climbing that mountain, the morning run felt like a walk in the park.  爬完那座山，早上跑步简直不值一提。

7103.cn: 轻易取胜；不费吹灰之力
7103.e: With their best players back, our rivals will probably walk it this season.  主力都回来了，对手这赛季八成能轻松夺冠。

7104.e: People from every walk of life turned up to support the campaign.  各行各业的人都来支持这场活动。

7105.e: Three hundred drivers walked off the job over the new shift pattern.  三百名司机因新排班制度罢了工。

7106.e: The guide walked us off our feet on the first day in Rome.  在罗马的头一天，导游就把我们走得腿都软了。

7107.e: Since the argument, everyone at home has been walking on eggshells.  那次争吵之后，家里人说话都小心翼翼。

7108.e: Someone has to walk the plank for losing the biggest client.  丢了最大的客户，总得有人卷铺盖走人。

7109.e: He walked the streets for hours trying to clear his head.  他在街上转了好几个小时，想让脑子清静一下。

7110.cn: 昂首挺胸；感到自豪自信
7110.e: After finishing the marathon she could finally walk tall again.  跑完马拉松，她终于又能昂首挺胸了。

7111.i: give sb their ˈwalking papers • get your
7111.e: After the audit, two managers were given their walking papers.  审计之后，两位经理被炒了鱿鱼。

7112.e: Ask Priya about local history, she is a walking encyclopedia.  本地历史问普丽娅就行，她就是本活百科全书。

7113.cn: 活字典；活百科全书（指博学者）
7113.e: My grandfather was a walking dictionary of old farming words.  我爷爷简直是一本关于旧时农事词汇的活字典。

7114.e: Joking about the boss's divorce means you are skating on thin ice.  拿老板离婚的事开玩笑，你这是在冒险。

7115.e: That dripping tap is driving me up the wall at night.  夜里那个滴水的龙头快把我逼疯了。

7116.e: Several small bookshops went to the wall during the recession.  经济衰退期间，好几家小书店都倒闭了。

7117.i: have your ˈback to the wall
7117.e: With the rent due tomorrow, he really had his back to the wall.  房租明天就到期，他真是走投无路了。

7118.e: Her ideas are a bit off the wall, but they often work.  她的点子有点古怪，可往往真管用。

7119.i: be/come up against a brick ˈwall
7119.cn: 碰壁；遇到难以逾越的障碍
7119.e: We came up against a brick wall when we asked for the records.  我们要求查看记录时碰了一鼻子灰。

7120.e: Keep your voice down in the corridor, walls have ears around here.  在走廊里小声点，这地方隔墙有耳。

7121.e: Interest in the old festival has been on the wane for years.  人们对这个老节日的兴趣多年来一直在减退。

7122.e: The whole project failed for want of a few thousand pounds.  整个项目就因为缺那几千英镑而告吹。

7123.e: The old church roof is badly in want of repair before winter.  这座老教堂的屋顶入冬前急需修缮。

7124.e: I told him about the leak, but he just did not want to know.  我跟他说了漏水的事，他压根不想搭理。

7125.e: Their children want for nothing, yet they still seem unhappy.  他们的孩子什么都不缺，却似乎并不快乐。

7126.i: want ˈrid of sb/sth (BrE, spoken, informal)
7126.e: I want rid of that old sofa before the new one arrives.  新沙发到之前，我想把那张旧的处理掉。

7127.e: The two sides fought a war of nerves for weeks before signing.  签约前双方打了好几周的心理战。

7128.e: A bitter war of words broke out between the two candidates online.  两位候选人在网上展开了激烈的口水战。

7129.i: keep sb's ˈseat, etc. warm (for them) (informal)
7129.cn: 替某人暂时占位或代职
7129.e: I am only keeping the chairman's seat warm until he returns.  我只是在主席回来之前替他暂时守着这个位子。

7130.e: Under that thick duvet the children were as warm as toast.  盖着那床厚被子，孩子们暖烘烘的。

7131.cn: 使人心里暖洋洋；令人欣慰
7131.e: Seeing the neighbours help her move really warmed the cockles of my heart.  看到邻居帮她搬家，我心里暖烘烘的。

7132.cn: 怒气冲冲；准备兴师问罪
7132.e: Look busy, the manager is on the warpath about the missing files.  装忙点，经理正为丢文件的事发火呢。

7133.cn: 老是受点小伤；伤痕累累
7133.e: Poor Tom has been in the wars again, that is his third bruise.  可怜的汤姆又挂彩了，这已经是第三处淤青。

7134.cn: 缺点也不隐瞒；原原本本
7134.e: The documentary shows the band warts and all, including the fights.  这部纪录片把乐队的一切都拍了，连争吵也不回避。

7135.i: it will (all) come out in the ˈwash (spoken)
7135.cn: 事情终会解决；真相终会大白
7135.e: Do not worry about the mix-up, it will all come out in the wash.  别为这场误会发愁，最后总会弄清楚的。

7136.i: wash your dirty linen in ˈpublic (BrE, disapproving)
7136.cn: 家丑外扬；公开谈论私事
7136.e: Posting about their divorce online is washing dirty linen in public.  把离婚的事发到网上，就是家丑外扬。

7137.e: After the third warning, the school washed its hands of him.  第三次警告之后，学校就不管他了。

7138.i: can't just wash my hands of the whole business.
7138.e: I cannot just wash my hands of the whole business, I signed the contract.  我不能说撇清就撇清，合同是我签的。

7139.e: That excuse about the traffic will not wash with your teacher.  堵车这个借口在你老师那儿说不过去。

7140.e: Take the leftovers home so all this good food does not go to waste.  把剩菜带回家，别让这么好的东西白白糟蹋了。

7141.e: Do not waste your breath arguing with him, he never changes his mind.  别白费口舌跟他争，他从不改主意。

7142.e: He called the new intern a waste of space, which was unfair.  他说那个新实习生是废物，这话不公道。

7143.e: Be on the watch for pickpockets around the station at night.  晚上在车站附近要提防扒手。

7144.e: You keep watch by the door while I look for the keys.  你在门口望风，我去找钥匙。

7145.e: Staff who watch the clock all afternoon rarely get promoted.  整个下午都盯着钟等下班的人很难升职。

7146.e: Watch it, that pan handle has been on the flame for ages.  当心，那锅把手在火上烤了半天了。

7147.e: The examiner watched us like a hawk for the whole three hours.  监考老师整整三个小时都紧紧盯着我们。

7148.e: Watch your mouth, my grandmother is sitting right behind you.  说话注意点，我奶奶就坐在你后面。

7149.e: We cannot announce the venue yet, but watch this space.  场地还不能公布，请大家关注后续消息。

7150.cn: 闲看人来人往；静观世事
7150.e: We sat outside the cafe with coffee and watched the world go by.  我们坐在咖啡馆外喝咖啡，闲看人来人往。

7151.i: keep a close ˈeye/ˈwatch on sb/sth
7151.e: Please keep a close eye on the soup while I answer the door.  我去开门，你帮我盯着点汤。

7152.e: Stop refreshing your inbox, a watched pot never boils.  别老刷邮箱了，越盯着越觉得慢。

7153.i: Don't you know that a watched pot never boils?
7153.cn: 越着急越觉得慢；心急水不开
7153.e: Do not you know that a watched pot never boils? Go and read something.  你不知道越等越觉得慢吗？去看点书吧。

7154.i: be (like) water off a ˌduck's ˈback (informal)
7154.e: Criticism from strangers is like water off a duck's back to her.  陌生人的批评对她来说就是耳边风。

7155.e: We argued a lot back then, but it is all water under the bridge now.  当年我们没少吵，但都是过去的事了。

7156.cn: （理论等）站得住脚；经得起推敲
7156.e: His alibi simply does not hold water once you check the times.  一核对时间，他的不在场证明就站不住脚了。

7157.e: He spends money like water whenever he goes back home for holidays.  他每次回家过节都花钱如流水。

7158.e: The company is heading into difficult waters with these new tariffs.  在这些新关税下，公司正驶入难以应付的水域。

7159.cn: 陷入未知或险恶的境地
7159.e: Selling data to advertisers takes the app into murky waters legally.  把数据卖给广告商，这款应用在法律上进了灰色地带。

7160.e: As soon as she was told off, she turned on the waterworks.  刚一挨说，她就哭开了。

7161.cn: 像变魔法一样解决问题
7161.e: I cannot wave a magic wand and make your student debt disappear.  我又不能一挥魔杖就让你的助学贷款消失。

7162.i: be on the same ˈwavelength/on different
7162.e: My sister and I are on the same wavelength about almost everything.  我和我姐几乎在所有事情上都想到一块儿去。

7163.cn: 思路相同或不同；合拍与否
7163.e: The two designers are clearly on different wavelengths about the colour scheme.  两位设计师在配色上明显不在一个频道上。

7164.e: The new director likes to make waves in her first month.  这位新主管喜欢在上任头一个月就搅动一下局面。

7165.e: Public interest in the scandal waxed and waned over several months.  几个月来，公众对这桩丑闻的兴趣时高时低。

7166.e: He waxed lyrical about the fish market for the entire train journey.  一路上他都在火车上眉飞色舞地大谈那个鱼市。
