7167.i: across the ˈway (BrE also over the ˈway)
7167.e: The family across the way have just bought a huge trampoline.  街对面那家人刚买了个巨大的蹦床。

7168.e: She supported the project all the way, even when funding dried up.  她自始至终支持这个项目，连没钱的时候也是。

7169.e: The bus comes late when you are in a hurry, it is always the way.  你一赶时间公交就晚点，老是这样。

7170.i: any way you ˈslice it (AmE, informal)
7170.e: Any way you slice it, we are going to be short of money.  不管怎么算，我们的钱都不够。

7171.e: Her father is in a bad way after the second operation.  第二次手术之后，她父亲情况很不好。

7172.e: Cash payments are on the way out in most of the city's cafes.  在这座城市多数咖啡馆，现金支付快要没人用了。

7173.i: be (well) on the/your way to/towards sth
7173.e: With another win, they are well on their way to the final.  再赢一场，他们就基本上打进决赛了。

7174.e: He cannot help being blunt, he was just born that way.  他就是嘴直，天生这脾气。

7175.e: Repairs on the bridge are already underway and should finish by autumn.  桥梁维修已经动工，预计秋天完工。

7176.i: by the ˈway (also by the ˈby/ˈbye less frequent)
7176.cn: 顺便说一句；附带问一句
7176.e: By the way, did you ever return that book to the library?  顺便问一句，那本书你还给图书馆了吗？

7177.e: Take the internship, chances like this do not come your way often.  接下这个实习吧，这种机会可不常有。

7178.i: do sth in a big/small ˈway
7178.cn: 大张旗鼓地做；小打小闹地做
7178.e: They celebrate birthdays in a big way, with fifty guests and a band.  他们过生日很铺张，请五十位客人还有乐队。

7179.e: I will pick up the dry cleaning on the way to the station.  我去车站的路上顺便取一下干洗的衣服。

7180.i: ˈeither way • one way or the ˈother
7180.e: We can drive or take the train, either way it takes three hours.  开车或坐火车都行，反正都要三小时。

7181.e: When the alarm rang, people ran every which way across the car park.  警报一响，人们在停车场四散奔逃。

7182.e: Do not let your phone get in the way of your revision tonight.  今晚别让手机耽误你复习。

7183.i: get into/out of the way of sth/of doing sth
7183.e: I have got into the way of walking to work every morning.  我已经养成了每天早上走路上班的习惯。

7184.i: get sth out of the ˈway
7184.cn: 把某事处理掉；先解决掉
7184.e: Let us get the paperwork out of the way before lunch.  咱们先把文书工作弄完再去吃午饭。

7185.cn: 事事随心所欲；一切照自己的意思
7185.e: You cannot always have everything your own way at work.  在单位你不可能事事都随自己的意思。

7186.e: The old wooden balcony gave way under the weight of the guests.  客人一多，那个旧木阳台就塌了。

7187.e: Drivers must give way to cyclists at this junction.  在这个路口司机必须给骑车人让行。

7188.cn: 完全赞同；与某人发生性关系
7188.e: I go all the way with you on cutting the training budget.  在削减培训预算这件事上我完全同意你。

7189.i: go out of your ˈway (to do sth)
7189.e: Our neighbours went out of their way to help us settle in.  邻居们特别费心帮我们安顿下来。

7190.e: He ignored all the advice and went his own way as usual.  他把所有建议都当耳旁风，照旧我行我素。

7191.cn: 与某人同路；（事情）合某人心意
7191.e: Nothing went my way at all during that first month abroad.  刚出国那个月，什么事都不顺我的意。

7192.i: go the way of all ˈflesh
7192.e: Even the greatest emperors go the way of all flesh in the end.  再伟大的帝王最后也难免一死。

7193.i: have a way of doing sth
7193.e: Problems have a way of solving themselves if you sleep on them.  很多问题搁一晚上往往就自己解决了。

7194.i: have your (wicked) ˈway with sb (old-fashioned, humorous)
7194.cn: 说服某人与自己发生性关系
7194.e: In the film the count finally has his wicked way with the heroine.  电影里伯爵最终把女主角弄到了手。

7195.i: in a ˈway • in ˈone way (also in ˈsome ways)
7195.cn: 在某种程度上；从某方面说
7195.e: In a way I am relieved that the whole thing is finally over.  从某种程度上说，这事总算结束了，我反而松了口气。

7196.i: in his, her, its, etc. (own) ˈway
7196.e: He is not romantic, but in his own way he is very caring.  他不浪漫，但用他自己的方式很体贴。

7197.e: Those boxes are in the way, could you move them into the hall?  那些箱子挡道了，能搬到走廊去吗？

7198.e: Stay out of his way today, he lost a big client this morning.  今天躲着他点，他上午丢了个大客户。

7199.e: Officials looked the other way while the factory dumped waste in the river.  工厂往河里排废水，官员们却装作没看见。

7200.e: We lost our way in the fog and ended up back at the car park.  我们在雾里迷了路，最后又转回了停车场。

7201.i: a lot, not much, etc. in the way of sth
7201.e: The flat has a great view but not much in the way of storage.  这套公寓视野很好，但储物空间不多。

7202.e: The old market was demolished to make way for a car park.  老市场被拆掉，给停车场腾了地方。

7203.e: Please make your way to gate twelve, boarding starts in ten minutes.  请前往十二号登机口，十分钟后开始登机。

7204.e: It is not easy to make your way in journalism without contacts.  没有人脉，在新闻界闯出名堂并不容易。

7205.i: my way or the ˈhighway (AmE, informal)
7205.e: With that coach it is always my way or the highway.  跟那个教练打交道，永远是要么听他的，要么走人。

7206.e: No way am I lending him my car after what happened last time.  上次那事之后，我绝不会再把车借给他。

7207.cn: 不阻拦某人；不妨碍某人
7207.e: If you really want to study abroad, I will not stand in your way.  你要是真想出国念书，我不会拦着你。

7208.e: One way or another, we will get the money together before Friday.  不管想什么办法，周五前我们都会把钱凑齐。

7209.e: The ambulance is on its way and should be here in five minutes.  救护车已经在路上，五分钟内应该就到。

7210.e: She did not leave him, it was actually the other way around.  不是她甩了他，其实正相反。

7211.e: Once the exams are out of the way we can plan the trip.  等考完试没这事儿了，我们就能计划旅行。

7212.e: Dropping me home is completely out of your way, I will take the bus.  送我回家太绕路了，我坐公交就行。

7213.i: see your ˈway (ˈclear) to doing sth
7213.cn: 觉得能够做；方便做某事
7213.e: If you could see your way clear to lending us the hall, we would be grateful.  您要是方便把礼堂借给我们，我们感激不尽。

7214.i: see which way the ˈwind blows
7214.e: He is waiting to see which way the wind blows before choosing sides.  他在观望风向，然后再决定站哪边。

7215.e: Keep your elbow down when you swing, that is the way.  挥杆时胳膊肘放低，对，就这样。

7216.i: that's the way the cookie ˈcrumbles (also that's the way it ˈgoes) (informal)
7216.cn: 情况就是这样，没别的办法
7216.e: We lost the contract by one point, but that is the way the cookie crumbles.  就差一分丢了合同，可事情就是这样。

7217.i: there's more than ˈone way to skin a ˈcat
7217.cn: 办法不止一个；条条大路通罗马
7217.e: If the front door is locked, remember there is more than one way to skin a cat.  前门锁了也没事，办法总不止一个。

7218.i: to ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. way of thinking
7218.e: To my way of thinking, we should fix the roof before buying furniture.  依我看，先修屋顶再买家具。

7219.e: We first met way back when we were both working night shifts.  我们初次见面还是很久以前一起上夜班的时候。

7220.e: Fishing is not just a job here, it is a whole way of life.  在这儿捕鱼不只是工作，而是一整套生活方式。

7221.e: The rich get the best seats, and sadly that is the way of the world.  好位子都归有钱人，可惜世道就是如此。

7222.e: You finished the whole race in the rain? Way to go!  下着雨你还跑完了全程？干得漂亮！

7223.e: Home-made soup is definitely the way to my father's heart.  自家熬的汤绝对是讨我爸欢心的法宝。

7224.i: work, etc. your way through sth
7224.cn: 从头到尾做完；逐一处理
7224.e: She worked her way through a pile of marking before midnight.  她在午夜前把一摞作业全批完了。

7225.i: eating his way through all the restaurants that
7225.cn: 逐一吃遍；一家家吃过来
7225.e: He is eating his way through all the restaurants that the guide recommends.  他正把指南推荐的餐馆一家家吃过来。

7226.i: ˌwork your way through ˈcollege, etc.
7226.e: She worked her way through college by waiting tables at weekends.  她靠周末端盘子挣钱读完了大学。

7227.e: He worked his way up from cleaner to head of the department.  他从清洁工一路干到了部门主管。

7228.i: way out of a paper bag
7228.cn: 极其无能；一点本事也没有
7228.e: He could not fight his way out of a paper bag, let alone win the title.  他连个纸袋都打不破，更别说夺冠了。

7229.e: Grandad is too set in his ways to try a new phone.  爷爷太固执了，新手机说什么也不肯试。

7230.i: you, etc. can't have it ˈboth ways
7230.e: You cannot have it both ways, either you save or you travel.  鱼与熊掌不可兼得，要么存钱，要么旅行。

7231.cn: 有利也有弊；是把双刃剑
7231.e: Working from home cuts both ways: more freedom, but far more distractions.  居家办公是双刃剑：更自由，但也更分心。

7232.cn: 不止一层意思；在好几方面
7232.e: Moving to the coast changed our lives in more ways than one.  搬到海边从好几方面改变了我们的生活。

7233.e: There are ways and means of getting tickets if you know the right people.  只要认识人，弄到票总有门路。

7234.e: Half the class started Japanese, but most fell by the wayside by March.  班上一半人开始学日语，三月前大都半途而废了。

7235.cn: 词源说明（本书标注习语来源）
7235.e: The ORIGIN note says the seed that fell by the wayside never grew.  词源说明指出，落在路旁的种子没有发芽。

7236.e: He has got old vinyl records out the wazoo in that basement.  他地下室里的旧黑胶唱片多得没处放。

7237.e: The new phone has features up the wazoo that nobody ever uses.  这款新手机功能多得要命，可根本没人用。

7238.e: One look from him and she went weak at the knees.  他一个眼神就让她腿都软了。

7239.e: Our defence is still the weak link in the chain this season.  这个赛季我们的防守仍然是最薄弱的一环。

7240.i: a weak ˈmoment • a moment of ˈweakness
7240.cn: 一时心软；意志薄弱的时候
7240.e: In a weak moment I agreed to look after their three dogs.  我一时心软，答应帮他们照看三条狗。

7241.e: The deposit covers damage but not normal wear and tear.  押金赔的是损坏，不包括正常磨损。

7242.i: wear your ˌheart on your ˈsleeve
7242.e: He wears his heart on his sleeve, so you always know his mood.  他喜怒都写在脸上，心情如何一看便知。

7243.e: His excuses about the traffic are starting to wear a bit thin.  他那套堵车的借口越来越说不过去了。

7244.i: wear the ˈtrousers (BrE) (AmE wear the ˈpants) (often disapproving)
7244.e: Everyone knows who wears the trousers in that household.  谁都知道那家里是谁说了算。

7245.i: keep a ˈweather eye on sth/open for sth
7245.e: Keep a weather eye on the forecast before we set off tomorrow.  明天出发前留意一下天气预报。

7246.e: I am feeling a bit under the weather, so I will skip dinner.  我有点不舒服，晚饭就不去了。

7247.cn: 不论天气好坏；风雨无阻
7247.e: The postman cycles up that hill in all weathers.  不管什么天气，邮递员都骑车上那个坡。

7248.i: weave your ˈmagic • weave a ˈspell (over sb) (especially BrE)
7248.cn: 表现出色令人入迷；施展魅力
7248.e: The old pianist wove his magic over the audience for two hours.  那位老钢琴家让全场听众入迷了两个小时。

7249.e: The children ran outside laughing at the monkey's wedding that afternoon.  那天下午下起太阳雨，孩子们笑着跑到外面。

7250.e: Week after week he sent applications and heard nothing back.  他一周又一周地投简历，却没有任何回音。

7251.e: Week by week her Chinese improved until she could argue in it.  她的中文一周比一周好，最后都能用中文吵架了。

7252.cn: 每星期都如此；周复一周
7252.e: He drives two hundred miles week in, week out to see his mother.  他周复一周开两百英里去看母亲。

7253.i: a ˌweek toˈmorrow, on ˈMonday, etc. (BrE)
7253.cn: 一星期后的明天（或周一等）
7253.e: Our exams start a week tomorrow, so revision begins tonight.  考试从下周的明天开始，所以今晚就得复习。

7254.i: (also a ˌweek from toˈmorrow, ˈMonday, etc. AmE, BrE)
7254.cn: 一星期后的明天（或周一等）
7254.e: The lease ends a week from Monday, so we must pack soon.  租约到下下周一就到期，我们得赶紧收拾。

7255.i: a ˌweek ˈyesterday, last ˈMonday, etc. (especially BrE)
7255.cn: 一星期前的昨天（或周一等）
7255.e: They moved out a week yesterday and left the keys with me.  他们上周的昨天搬走了，钥匙留给了我。

7256.e: The ferry weighed anchor just as the storm clouds appeared.  乌云刚一出现，渡轮就起锚了。

7257.e: The unpaid bills have been weighing on my mind for weeks.  那些没付的账单压在我心头好几周了。

7258.e: Careful with that suitcase, it weighs half a ton.  小心那个行李箱，重得要命。

7259.e: She weighed her words carefully before replying to the journalist.  回答记者之前，她仔细斟酌了措辞。

7260.i: be a ˌweight off your ˈshoulders
7260.e: Handing in that thesis was a huge weight off my shoulders.  交上论文那一刻，我如释重负。

7261.e: The mayor threw her weight behind the campaign to save the library.  市长全力支持了保住图书馆的活动。

7262.i: take the ˈweight off your feet (informal)
7262.e: Come in and take the weight off your feet, the kettle is on.  进来坐下歇歇脚，水正烧着呢。

7263.e: The new supervisor started throwing his weight around on day one.  新主管上任第一天就开始耀武扬威。

7264.e: The protesters won by sheer weight of numbers rather than argument.  抗议者靠的是人多势众，而不是道理。

7265.e: The market sells all sorts of weird and wonderful kitchen gadgets.  这个市场卖各种稀奇古怪的厨房小工具。

7266.i: lay, put, roll, etc. out the ˈwelcome mat
7266.cn: 热情迎客；设法吸引来访者
7266.e: The village rolled out the welcome mat for the returning team.  全村热情迎接凯旋的球队。

7267.e: They stayed three weeks and definitely outstayed their welcome.  他们住了三个星期，实在是待得太久招人烦了。

7268.e: You are welcome, it was really no trouble at all to help.  不用谢，帮这点忙一点儿也不麻烦。

7269.e: All being well, we should reach the campsite before dark.  一切顺利的话，我们天黑前能到营地。

7270.i: ˌall very ˈwell/fine (for sb) (to do sth) but...
7270.e: It is all very well telling me to relax, but I have four children.  叫我放松说得轻巧，可我有四个孩子。

7271.e: A pay rise is all well and good, but we also need shorter hours.  加薪固然好，可我们还需要缩短工时。

7272.e: We missed the ferry but caught a better one; all's well that ends well.  我们错过了渡轮却赶上更好的一班，结局好就都好。

7273.e: She speaks Arabic as well as French and a little Portuguese.  她除法语外还会阿拉伯语，还懂点葡萄牙语。

7274.i: She's a talented musician as well as being a
7274.e: She is a talented musician as well as being a very patient teacher.  她既是出色的音乐家，又是个非常有耐心的老师。

7275.e: It is just as well to book a table before the match starts.  比赛开始前还是先订个位子为好。

7276.e: Mother and baby are both doing well after a long night.  熬了一整夜，母子都恢复得不错。

7277.i: be ˌwell aˈware of sth • be ˌwell aˌware
7277.e: I am well aware of the risks, but I still want to try.  这些风险我很清楚，可我还是想试。

7278.e: Once he found a decent editor, he was well away with the novel.  找到一位好编辑后，他的小说就写得顺风顺水。

7279.cn: 与（要人）关系密切；过往甚密
7279.e: She is well in with the people who decide the funding.  她跟决定拨款的那些人关系很铁。

7280.e: His grandparents were well off, but he never took a penny.  他祖父母很有钱，可他一分也没要过。

7281.e: We are well off for blankets, so bring your own pillow instead.  我们毯子很多，你带个枕头就行。

7282.i: be ˌwell ˈout of sth (BrE, informal)
7282.e: Given how that project ended, you are well out of it.  那个项目落得那种下场，你幸好没掺和。

7283.e: Ask Meera, she is well up on the new tax rules.  问米拉吧，她对新税规很熟。

7284.e: Her small bakery has done well since the new estate was built.  新小区建好后，她那家小面包房生意一直不错。

7285.e: The company has done well by its long-serving staff over the years.  这些年公司待老员工一直不薄。

7286.e: He has done well for himself since he moved to Singapore.  搬到新加坡以后他混得相当不错。

7287.e: The estate agents did very well out of the housing boom.  房地产中介靠这波楼市大涨赚了不少。

7288.e: You would do well to keep a copy of that email.  你最好把那封邮件留个备份。

7289.i: hanged/hung for a sheep as (for) a ˈlamb
7289.cn: 一不做二不休；反正都要受罚
7289.e: We have broken the diet already, so hanged for a sheep as a lamb.  反正减肥计划已经破了，索性一不做二不休。

7290.e: I know only too well how hard the first year of teaching is.  头一年教书有多难，我太清楚了。

7291.e: Very well, we will postpone the decision until the next meeting.  好吧，这个决定推迟到下次会议再说。

7292.e: By the time we found the path, we were well and truly lost.  等找到那条小路时，我们已经彻底迷路了。

7293.e: Well said! Somebody finally told the committee the truth.  说得好！总算有人跟委员会说了实话。

7294.e: If you think the deal is safe, you are all wet.  你要是觉得这笔交易稳当，那就大错特错了。

7295.e: The new father took us to the pub to wet the baby's head.  这位新爸爸带我们去酒吧喝酒庆祝孩子出生。

7296.e: He still wets the bed occasionally when he is anxious about school.  他一为上学的事紧张，偶尔还会尿床。

7297.e: That reporter is still wet behind the ears but asks sharp questions.  那个记者还嫩着呢，可问题问得挺尖锐。

7298.e: Do not be such a wet blanket, everyone else wants to dance.  别这么扫兴，别人都想跳舞。

7299.e: Come inside and wet your whistle before the second half starts.  下半场开始前先进来喝一杯润润嗓子。

7300.e: The children laughed so hard that the youngest nearly wet herself.  孩子们笑得太厉害，最小的那个差点尿了裤子。

7301.e: Volunteer at the clinic to get your feet wet before applying properly.  正式申请前先去诊所做志愿者，试试水。

7302.e: The office thermostat is out of whack again, so bring a jumper.  办公室的温控器又不好使了，带件毛衣来。

7303.i: have a ˈwhale of a time (informal)
7303.e: The kids had a whale of a time at the water park yesterday.  孩子们昨天在水上乐园玩得特别开心。

7304.e: Rising rent and a pay freeze were a double whammy for young staff.  房租上涨加上工资冻结，对年轻员工是双重打击。

7305.i: and ˈwhat not • and what ˈhave you (informal)
7305.cn: 诸如此类；以及其他类似的东西
7305.e: The drawer is full of chargers, old keys and what have you.  抽屉里塞满了充电器、旧钥匙之类的东西。

7306.e: My mother gave me what for when she saw the broken window.  我妈看见碎玻璃窗，把我骂了个狗血淋头。

7307.e: So what if he disagrees? We still have enough votes to pass it.  他不同意又怎样？我们的票数照样够。

7308.cn: 那个什么（想不起名称）；怎么了
7308.e: Pass me the what-d'you-call-it, the thing for opening wine bottles.  把那个什么递给我，就是开红酒瓶的那个东西。

7309.e: What is with all these boxes in the hallway this morning?  今天早上走廊里这么多箱子是怎么回事？

7310.e: I am going to the bar now, so what is yours?  我这就去吧台，你想喝点什么？

7311.cn: 或诸如此类；或别的什么
7311.e: Bring a salad or some bread or whatever, it does not matter.  带个沙拉、面包或者别的什么都行，无所谓。

7312.e: Whatever you do, do not mention her ex-husband at dinner tonight.  今晚吃饭时无论如何别提她前夫。

7313.i: sort out/separate the ˌwheat from the
7313.e: The first interview helps us separate the wheat from the chaff quickly.  第一轮面试能帮我们很快分出优劣。

7314.e: A tough audition sorts the wheat from the chaff among young dancers.  严格的试镜能在年轻舞者中筛出真正的好苗子。

7315.e: He fell asleep at the wheel and drove straight into a ditch.  他开车时睡着了，径直冲进了沟里。

7316.e: Going to the movies with those two made me feel like a fifth wheel.  跟他们俩一起去看电影，让我觉得自己是个多余的人。

7317.e: You look exhausted — let me take the wheel for the next hundred miles.  你看着累坏了，接下来一百英里让我来开吧。

7318.cn: （在商界或政界）玩弄手段做交易
7318.e: He spent years wheeling and dealing in property before the market collapsed.  他在房地产界投机钻营多年，直到市场崩盘。

7319.cn: 投机钻营者；玩弄手段的人
7319.e: The company was founded by a wheeler-dealer who never took no for an answer.  这家公司是一个从不接受拒绝的投机高手创立的。

7320.i: the ˌwheel has come/turned full ˈcircle
7320.cn: 兜了一圈又回到原点；轮回
7320.e: Vinyl records are selling well again — the wheel has come full circle.  黑胶唱片又好卖了，真是兜了一圈回到原点。

7321.e: Don't expect a simple answer; in this office there are wheels within wheels.  别指望有简单答案，这个办公室里的事盘根错节。

7322.e: For live jazz in this city, that little basement bar is where it's at.  在这座城市听现场爵士，那家地下小酒吧才是最棒的去处。

7323.e: I don't need the whys and the wherefores of the delay, just a new date.  我不用知道延误的来龙去脉，给我个新日期就行。

7324.cn: 引起某人的兴趣；吊胃口
7324.e: The trailer really whetted my appetite for the film coming out next month.  预告片真把我对下个月上映那部电影的胃口吊起来了。

7325.e: The twins dress identically, so I can never tell which is which.  这对双胞胎穿得一模一样，我从来分不清哪个是哪个。

7326.i: get, have, hold, etc. the ˈwhip hand (over sb)
7326.e: Now that she owns most of the shares, she has the whip hand over the board.  如今她持有大部分股份，在董事会里占了上风。

7327.cn: （因失败或受罚）显得羞愧沮丧
7327.e: He slunk back into the meeting like a whipped dog after his idea was rejected.  提议被否决后，他像条挨了打的狗一样溜回会议室。

7328.e: The junior staff became the whipping boy for every mistake the manager made.  经理犯的每个错都由初级员工来当替罪羊。

7329.e: I've never skated before, but I'll give it a whirl.  我从没滑过冰，不过我可以试一试。

7330.e: After three job offers in one week, my head was in a whirl.  一周内接到三份工作邀约，我脑子都晕了。

7331.i: be, come, etc. within a ˈwhisker of sth/of doing sth
7331.e: She came within a whisker of winning the race, losing by half a second.  她差一点就赢了比赛，仅以半秒之差落败。

7332.e: They won the election by a whisker after a recount of every ballot.  重新清点全部选票后，他们以毫厘之差赢得选举。

7333.i: You, etc. can ˈwhistle for it (BrE, spoken)
7333.e: If he wants his deposit back, he can whistle for it.  他要是想把押金要回去，那就休想。

7334.e: Saying the company will recover next quarter is just whistling in the dark.  说公司下季度就能恢复，不过是自己壮胆罢了。

7335.cn: 走马观花式的巡回访问
7335.e: The minister made a whistle-stop tour of five factories in one afternoon.  部长一个下午走马观花地视察了五家工厂。

7336.e: His confidence was not a whit shaken by the crowd's booing.  观众的嘘声丝毫没有动摇他的自信。

7337.e: She came out of the doctor's office as white as a sheet.  她从医生办公室出来时脸色惨白。

7338.cn: 白色圣诞节（下雪的圣诞节）
7338.e: The kids are praying for snow so we finally get a white Christmas.  孩子们盼着下雪，好让我们终于过个白色圣诞节。

7339.cn: 昂贵而无用的东西；累赘
7339.e: The new stadium has become a white elephant the city cannot afford.  这座新体育场成了这座城市负担不起的昂贵累赘。

7340.e: I told a white lie and said her new haircut looked great.  我撒了个善意的谎，说她的新发型很好看。

7341.e: No politician in this scandal is whiter than white, whatever they claim.  这桩丑闻里没有哪个政客是清白的，不管他们怎么说。

7342.e: A white-van man cut me off at the roundabout and then swore at me.  一个开白色货车的莽汉在环岛抢我的道，还骂了我。

7343.e: They hired a twenty-three-year-old whizz-kid to run the whole trading desk.  他们请了个二十三岁的神童来管理整个交易部门。

7344.i: who am ˈI, are ˈyou, etc. to do sth?
7344.cn: 某人有什么资格做某事
7344.e: Who am I to tell her how to raise her own children?  我有什么资格教她怎么带自己的孩子？

7345.cn: 谁是谁；各人的身份情况
7345.e: Give me a minute at the party to work out who's who.  在派对上给我点时间，好搞清楚谁是谁。

7346.e: The team played badly, but as a whole the season was a success.  球队打得不好，但总体而言这个赛季是成功的。

7347.e: On the whole, I'd rather spend the holiday at home than fly anywhere.  总的来说，假期我宁愿待在家里，也不想飞去哪儿。

7348.e: This coffee tastes a whole lot better than the stuff at the office.  这咖啡比办公室里那种好喝多了。

7349.e: We wasted a whole lot of money on furniture we never actually used.  我们在从没真正用过的家具上浪费了一大笔钱。

7350.e: He ate the whole lot before anyone else got to the table.  别人还没上桌，他就把全部吃光了。

7351.e: They were whooping it up downstairs until three in the morning.  他们在楼下狂欢作乐，一直闹到凌晨三点。

7352.e: The whole village made whoopee when the team finally won the cup.  球队终于捧杯时，全村人都狂欢庆祝。

7353.e: Why ever did you tell him about the surprise party?  你究竟为什么要把惊喜派对的事告诉他？

7354.e: A weekend in the mountains? Why not? I could use the fresh air.  去山里过周末？好啊，我正需要点新鲜空气。

7355.e: Nobody explained the whys and the wherefores of the sudden policy change.  没人解释政策突然改变的原因和缘由。

7356.e: His constant humming really gets on my wick during meetings.  他开会时不停哼歌，真让我恼火。

7357.i: there's no peace/rest for the ˈwicked (usually humorous)
7357.cn: 恶人一刻不得闲（抱怨活太多）
7357.e: Another late shift tonight — there's no rest for the wicked, I suppose.  今晚又要上晚班，看来是恶人一刻不得闲。

7358.i: be/fall wide of the ˈmark (also be (a long) way off the ˈmark)
7358.e: Their sales forecast for the year turned out to be wide of the mark.  他们对全年销售额的预测结果偏得离谱。

7359.e: With three teams on equal points, the championship is still wide open.  三支球队积分相同，冠军归属仍然难以预料。

7360.e: I give that noisy pub a wide berth on Friday nights.  周五晚上我对那家吵闹的酒吧总是避而远之。

7361.cn: 做买卖不诚实的人；奸商
7361.e: Some wide boy sold him a car with the mileage clocked back.  有个奸商把一辆调过里程表的车卖给了他。

7362.cn: 使自己易受攻击（或指责）
7362.e: By signing without a lawyer you leave yourself wide open to a lawsuit.  不找律师就签字，等于让自己随时可能吃官司。

7363.e: Their kids run wild all summer while the parents are at work.  父母上班的整个夏天，他们家孩子都撒野没人管。

7364.e: That address sent us on a wild goose chase across half the city.  那个地址让我们跑遍半座城，白忙一场。

7365.cn: 什么也无法阻止某人；八匹马也拉不回
7365.e: Wild horses wouldn't drag me back to that awful restaurant again.  八匹马也拉不动我再去那家糟糕的餐厅。

7366.e: After ten years in the wilderness, the party finally won an election.  在野十年之后，这个政党终于赢了一次选举。

7367.cn: 做梦也想不到；远超想象
7367.e: The little app made him rich beyond his wildest dreams.  这个小应用让他富得超出了自己最疯狂的想象。

7368.e: She was kept in the hospital against her will for three days.  她违背自己的意愿被留在医院三天。

7369.e: Members can cancel the subscription at will, with no penalty at all.  会员可以随意取消订阅，不收任何违约金。

7370.i: where there's a ˌwill there's a ˈway (saying)
7370.e: She learned Japanese at sixty — where there's a will there's a way.  她六十岁学会了日语，真是有志者事竟成。

7371.e: The volunteers set to work with a will and cleared the beach by noon.  志愿者们干劲十足，中午前就把海滩清理干净了。

7372.cn: 使某人紧张不安；令人毛骨悚然
7372.e: That empty old hospital at night really gives me the willies.  那座夜里空荡荡的旧医院真让我心里发毛。

7373.cn: 不由自主地做某事；违背意愿
7373.e: He was dragged willy-nilly into a family argument he wanted no part of.  他不由自主地被卷进一场根本不想掺和的家庭争吵。

7374.e: If I cook she complains, if I don't she sulks — I can't win.  我做饭她抱怨，不做她生气，我怎么做都不对。

7375.e: He won her heart with nothing more than patience and terrible jokes.  他仅凭耐心和糟糕的笑话就赢得了她的心。

7376.e: Win or lose, I'm proud of how hard this team has worked.  无论输赢，我都为这支队伍的努力感到骄傲。

7377.i: you ˌwin some, you ˈlose some (spoken)
7377.cn: 有得必有失；不可能事事如意
7377.e: We missed that contract, but you win some, you lose some.  那份合同没拿到，不过有得就有失嘛。

7378.e: All right, you win — we'll watch your film instead of mine.  好吧，你赢了，我们看你选的电影，不看我的。

7379.e: Her calm arguments carried the day at the shareholders' meeting.  她冷静的论证在股东大会上占了上风。

7380.e: Someone broke wind in the crowded lift and nobody said a word.  有人在拥挤的电梯里放了个屁，没人吭声。

7381.cn: 听到……的风声；获悉秘密消息
7381.e: The press got wind of the merger before the board had even voted.  董事会还没表决，媒体就听到了合并的风声。

7382.i: get/have the ˈwind up (about sth) (BrE, informal)
7382.e: He got the wind up when the police asked to see his licence.  警察要看他驾照时，他慌了神。

7383.i: go, run, etc. like the ˈwind
7383.e: The boy grabbed the ball and ran like the wind towards the goal.  男孩抓起球，像风一样朝球门冲去。

7384.e: There are big changes in the wind at head office, apparently.  据说总部那边正在酝酿重大变动。

7385.i: put the ˈwind up sb (BrE, informal)
7385.e: The tax inspector's letter really put the wind up my boss.  税务稽查员的信真把我老板吓坏了。

7386.i: take the ˈwind out of sb's sails (informal)
7386.cn: 挫某人锐气；使某人泄气
7386.e: Her calm apology took the wind out of his sails completely.  她平静的道歉彻底让他没了脾气。

7387.i: be, go, etc. ˌout of the ˈwindow (informal)
7387.e: Once the rain started, our plans for a picnic went out of the window.  雨一下起来，我们野餐的计划就泡汤了。

7388.e: We have a short window of opportunity to sell before prices drop.  在价格下跌前，我们只有很短的一段机会可以卖出。

7389.e: For my grandmother, the radio was her only window on the world.  对我奶奶来说，收音机是她了解世界的唯一窗口。

7390.e: The firm wined and dined us for two days before mentioning the contract.  那家公司连着两天盛情款待我们，之后才提合同的事。

7391.i: on a ˌwing and a ˈprayer
7391.cn: 只有一线成功的希望；勉强硬撑
7391.e: We finished the project on a wing and a prayer, with hours to spare.  我们全凭一线希望赶完了项目，只剩几小时富余。

7392.e: A flock of geese passed overhead, on the wing towards the south.  一群大雁从头顶飞过，正振翅南飞。

7393.e: The startled pheasants took wing as the dog crashed through the hedge.  狗撞穿树篱时，受惊的野鸡展翅飞走了。

7394.e: I hadn't prepared any slides, so I just winged it for twenty minutes.  我没准备幻灯片，就即兴讲了二十分钟。

7395.e: Your parcel is winging its way to you and should arrive tomorrow.  你的包裹正飞速送来，明天应该就能到。

7396.cn: 伺机而动；随时准备接替
7396.e: A younger manager is waiting in the wings to take over the department.  有位更年轻的经理正伺机接管这个部门。

7397.cn: 稳操胜券；找到了赚钱的门路
7397.e: With this recipe and that location, I think we're onto a winner.  有这个配方加上那个地段，我觉得我们稳赚不赔。

7398.e: Our debating team wiped the floor with them in the final round.  我们的辩论队在决赛中把他们打得一败涂地。

7399.cn: 把……从地球上抹去；彻底摧毁
7399.e: One flood was enough to wipe the little fishing village off the map.  一场洪水就足以把那个小渔村从地图上抹去。

7400.e: Let's wipe the slate clean and start the partnership again from scratch.  我们把过去一笔勾销，重新开始合作吧。

7401.i: wipe the/that ˈsmile, ˈgrin, etc. off sb's face
7401.e: One look at the final bill wiped the grin off his face.  看一眼最后的账单，他脸上的笑容就没了。

7402.i: go, come, etc. (right) down to the ˈwire
7402.cn: 僵持到最后一刻才分胜负
7402.e: The election went right down to the wire, decided by a few hundred votes.  这场选举一直僵持到最后一刻，只靠几百票定胜负。

7403.cn: 直到最后一刻；分秒必争
7403.e: The match went down to the wire, with a goal in the final minute.  这场比赛直到最后一刻才见分晓，终场前一分钟才进球。

7404.e: Conventional wisdom says you should buy a house, but renting suits us.  传统观念说该买房，但租房更适合我们。

7405.cn: 公认的说法；大多数人的看法
7405.e: Received wisdom holds that small firms innovate faster than large corporations.  普遍看法认为小公司比大企业创新更快。

7406.cn: 以其（无限的）智慧（含讽刺）
7406.e: Management, in their infinite wisdom, has decided to remove all the chairs.  管理层以其无穷的智慧，决定把所有椅子都撤走。

7407.i: be ˌwise after the eˈvent (often disapproving)
7407.e: It's easy to be wise after the event and say we should have sold earlier.  事后诸葛亮谁都会当，说什么当初该早点卖掉。

7408.e: It's no good complaining now; the tickets are completely sold out.  现在抱怨也没用，票已经全卖光了。

7409.e: The neighbours finally got wise to his excuses about the missing rent.  邻居们终于识破了他关于欠租的种种借口。

7410.e: Someone should put the new intern wise to how this office really works.  该有人告诉新实习生这办公室实际是怎么运作的。

7411.i: a ˈwise guy (informal, disapproving, especially AmE)
7411.e: Don't be a wise guy — just answer the question properly.  别自作聪明，好好回答问题。

7412.i: be none the ˈwiser • not be any the ˈwiser
7412.cn: 仍然不明白；还是没弄懂
7412.e: He explained the rules twice and I was still none the wiser.  他把规则解释了两遍，我还是一头雾水。

7413.e: If we put the money back tonight, nobody will be any the wiser.  只要今晚把钱放回去，就没人会察觉。

7414.e: Just as you wish, sir — we can deliver the order on Friday instead.  悉听尊便，先生，我们可以改到周五送货。

7415.e: A week off in Italy? I wish! I'll be here doing paperwork.  去意大利休一周假？想得美！我还得在这儿做文书。

7416.i: the wish is father to the ˈthought (saying)
7416.cn: 愿望是思想之父；一厢情愿
7416.e: He's sure the team will win, but the wish is father to the thought.  他笃定球队会赢，可惜愿望是思想之父，不过一厢情愿。

7417.i: wish sb/sth ˈwell • wish sb/sth ˈill (formal)
7417.cn: 祝某人顺利；希望某人倒霉
7417.e: Whatever our differences, I genuinely wish her well in the new job.  不管我们有什么分歧，我真心祝她新工作顺利。

7418.i: wouldn't wish sth on my, your, etc. worst ˈenemy
7418.cn: 连仇人也不希望遭此罪
7418.e: That kind of back pain is something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.  那种背痛，我连最恨的人都不希望他遭这个罪。

7419.e: Coffee with two sugars? Your wish is my command, madam.  加两块糖的咖啡？遵命，悉听吩咐，夫人。

7420.i: if wishes were ˌhorses, beggars would ˈride (saying)
7420.cn: 空想无用；愿望不等于现实
7420.e: Dreaming of a yacht won't help — if wishes were horses, beggars would ride.  空想游艇没用，要是愿望能当马，乞丐早骑上了。

7421.e: Expecting him to apologise first is pure wishful thinking.  指望他先道歉纯属一厢情愿。

7422.e: Only one person can sign the cheques, to wit, the treasurer.  只有一个人能签支票，即财务主管。

7423.cn: 支持某人；与某人站在一起
7423.e: We're with you all the way on this, whatever the committee decides.  不管委员会怎么决定，我们都全力支持你。

7424.e: I'm not with you — why would selling the car save us any money?  我没听懂你的意思，卖车怎么会替我们省钱？

7425.e: Get with it, Dad — nobody sends faxes any more these days.  跟上时代吧，爸，现在没人发传真了。

7426.e: For a man of seventy he's remarkably with it about technology.  作为七十岁的人，他对科技出奇地跟得上潮流。

7427.e: She slammed the folder on the desk and with that, walked out.  她把文件夹摔在桌上，随即走了出去。

7428.e: Without funding, the whole research programme simply withered on the vine.  没有资金，整个研究项目就这样慢慢夭折了。

7429.cn: 吓得魂不附体；无聊透顶
7429.e: I was scared witless when the lift stopped between two floors.  电梯卡在两层之间时，我吓得魂都没了。

7430.cn: 目击；亲眼看见（某事发生）
7430.e: She was a witness to the whole argument outside the pub.  她目击了酒吧外的整场争吵。

7431.e: The burnt fields bear witness to how dry this summer has been.  焦黑的田地证明了今年夏天有多干旱。

7432.cn: 束手无策；全然不知所措
7432.e: I'm at my wits' end with this baby who refuses to sleep.  这孩子怎么都不肯睡，我实在束手无策了。

7433.e: Give me a second to gather my wits before I go on stage.  上台前给我一秒钟定定神。

7434.i: frighten/scare sb out of their ˈwits
7434.e: You scared me out of my wits jumping out from behind that door!  你从门后跳出来，把我魂都吓飞了！

7435.e: Keep your wits about you when you're cycling through the city centre.  在市中心骑车时可得保持警觉。

7436.e: Woe betide anyone who forgets Grandma's birthday in this family.  在我们家，谁要是忘了奶奶的生日可就倒霉了。

7437.i: keep the ˈwolf from the door (informal)
7437.e: Two evening shifts a week just about keep the wolf from the door.  一周两个晚班勉强能糊口。

7438.e: That charming landlord turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing.  那个和气的房东原来是披着羊皮的狼。

7439.e: Management threw the junior engineer to the wolves at the press conference.  管理层在新闻发布会上把那位初级工程师推出来顶雷。

7440.cn: 我一点也不觉得奇怪；很可能
7440.e: They'll be late again, I shouldn't wonder, given the traffic tonight.  今晚这交通，他们又要迟到，我一点也不奇怪。

7441.e: It's little wonder that she's tired, working twelve hours every single day.  她每天工作十二小时，累也不奇怪。

7442.cn: 令人惊奇的是；真是奇迹
7442.e: It's a wonder that nobody was hurt when the roof came down.  屋顶塌下来居然没人受伤，真是奇迹。

7443.i: wonders will ˌnever ˈcease (spoken, usually ironic)
7443.cn: 真是无奇不有；怪事年年有
7443.e: He washed the dishes without being asked — wonders will never cease.  他没人催就把碗洗了，真是无奇不有。

7444.e: No wonder you're cold — you're standing there in a thin T-shirt.  怪不得你冷，就穿件薄T恤站在那儿。

7445.e: A week by the sea worked wonders for my mother's mood.  在海边待一周，我妈的心情大为好转。

7446.e: This spray works wonders on grease stains and old coffee marks.  这种喷剂对油渍和陈年咖啡渍有奇效。

7447.e: Sorry, I need more time — I'm a doctor, not a miracle-worker.  抱歉，我需要更多时间，我是医生，不是神仙。

7448.cn: 尚未摆脱困境；尚未渡过难关
7448.e: The patient is stable, but she's not out of the woods yet.  病人情况稳定，但还没有脱离危险。

7449.i: not see the ˌforest for the ˈtrees (informal)
7449.cn: 见树不见林；只见细节不见全局
7449.e: You're checking commas again — you can't see the forest for the trees.  你又在数逗号了，真是只见树木不见森林。

7450.cn: 请多保重；好好照顾自己
7450.e: See you next month, Joe — and don't take any wooden nickels.  下个月见，乔，路上多保重。

7451.i: get, win, take, etc. the ˌwooden ˈspoon (BrE, informal)
7451.cn: 获得最后一名；成为末名
7451.e: Our team took the wooden spoon again after losing every single match.  我们队一场没赢，又拿了倒数第一。

7452.e: When the bill arrived, he quietly faded into the woodwork.  账单一来，他就悄悄溜得没影了。

7453.i: come/crawl out of the ˈwoodwork (informal, disapproving)
7453.e: As soon as he won the lottery, distant cousins came out of the woodwork.  他一中彩票，远房表亲就纷纷冒了出来。

7454.i: be as ˌgood as your ˈword
7454.e: He said he'd fix the fence, and he was as good as his word.  他说会修好篱笆，果然说到做到。

7455.i: be a man/woman of his/her ˈword
7455.cn: 守信用的人；说话算数的人
7455.e: You can trust the builder; he's a man of his word.  这个建筑工你可以信任，他说话算数。

7456.e: The little bakery got all its customers by word of mouth.  这家小面包店的顾客全靠口口相传。

7457.e: The project was doomed right from the word go, honestly.  说实话，这个项目从一开始就注定要失败。

7458.i: (not) get a word in ˈedgeways (BrE) (AmE (not) get a word in ˈedgewise) (informal)
7458.e: My aunt talked for an hour and I couldn't get a word in edgeways.  我姑妈讲了一小时，我一句嘴都插不上。

7459.i: give sb your ˈword (that...) • have sb's ˈword (that...)
7459.cn: 向某人许诺；得到某人的保证
7459.e: I give you my word that the money will be back by Friday.  我向你保证，这笔钱周五前一定还上。

7460.e: He went back on his word and sold the bike to someone else.  他食言了，把自行车卖给了别人。

7461.e: Can I have a word with you about next week's schedule?  下周的日程我能跟你谈两句吗？

7462.i: have a word in sb's ˈear (BrE)
7462.e: The coach had a quiet word in the striker's ear at half-time.  中场休息时教练私下和前锋说了几句。

7463.e: In a word, the whole evening was an absolute disaster.  一句话，整个晚上糟透了。

7464.e: She kept her word and turned up at six with all the tools.  她说话算数，六点就带着全套工具来了。

7465.e: That's my final word on the subject — we are not moving house.  这事我最后表个态：我们不搬家。

7466.e: He left word with the receptionist that he'd be back by three.  他跟前台留了话，说三点前回来。

7467.e: Upon my word, I never expected to see you here again!  哎呀，我真没想到还能在这儿见到你！

7468.i: not be the ˈword for it
7468.e: Annoyed isn't the word for it — I was absolutely furious with him.  说恼火根本不够，我简直被他气炸了。

7469.i: not/never have a good word to ˈsay about/for sb/sth
7469.e: She never has a good word to say about her old employer.  她从不说前雇主一句好话。

7470.cn: 只字不提；别透露半个字
7470.e: Not a word to Mum about the party, or the surprise is ruined.  这派对的事别对妈妈说半个字，不然惊喜就没了。

7471.cn: 为某人说好话；替某人美言
7471.e: Could you put in a good word for me with the hiring manager?  你能在招聘经理面前替我美言几句吗？

7472.e: Years of radio taught her the real power of the spoken word.  多年的广播生涯让她懂得了口头语言的力量。

7473.cn: 完全相信某人的话并照办
7473.e: He offered to help, so I took him at his word and called.  他说愿意帮忙，我就当真了，给他打了电话。

7474.e: I haven't checked the figures, so you'll have to take my word for it.  我没核对数字，你只能信我这一说了。

7475.e: She repeated his apology word for word to the rest of us.  她把他的道歉一字不差地转述给了我们其他人。

7476.i: your, his, etc. word is your, his, etc. ˈbond
7476.e: Shake hands with old Tom and you're fine; his word is his bond.  跟老汤姆握个手就行，他一诺千金。

7477.i: your, his, etc. ˌword is ˈlaw
7477.cn: 某人说了算；某人之言即是法律
7477.e: In that kitchen the head chef's word is law, and nobody argues.  在那间厨房里主厨说了算，没人敢争。

7478.i: your, his, etc. ˌword of ˈhonour (BrE) (AmE your, his, etc. ˌword of ˈhonor)
7478.e: Give me your word of honour that you'll never mention this again.  你用名誉向我担保，绝不再提这件事。

7479.cn: 对聪明人不用细说；提个醒
7479.e: A word to the wise: don't argue with the boss on Mondays.  提个醒：周一别跟老板争论。

7480.e: I had words with my neighbour about his barking dog again last night.  昨晚我又为他家狗叫的事跟邻居吵了几句。

7481.e: He's between jobs — in other words, he's unemployed at the moment.  他正处于职业过渡期，换句话说，他现在失业了。

7482.e: He didn't say I was fired, not in so many words anyway.  他没直说我被解雇了，至少没那么明说。

7483.cn: 简单明了地说；用大白话讲
7483.e: Explain it to me in words of one syllable, please, because I'm lost.  请用最简单的话给我解释一下，我完全懵了。

7484.e: The shop's name is a clever play on words that always makes me smile.  这家店名是个巧妙的双关，总让我会心一笑。

7485.e: You said we'd never finish on time — now you can eat your words.  你说过我们绝不可能按时完工，现在收回你的话吧。

7486.e: Don't put words into my mouth; I never said the plan was stupid.  别硬安我头上，我从没说过这计划愚蠢。

7487.i: take the words (right) out of sb's ˈmouth
7487.e: You took the words right out of my mouth — I was about to suggest that.  你把我想说的话说出来了，我正打算这么建议。

7488.i: too funny, sad, etc. for ˈwords
7488.e: The ending of that film was too sad for words.  那部电影的结局悲伤得无法形容。

7489.e: You cycled all the way here from Scotland? Words fail me.  你从苏格兰一路骑车过来的？我真是无话可说了。

7490.i: all ˌwork and no ˈplay (makes Jack a dull ˈboy) (saying)
7490.cn: 整天用功不玩耍，聪明孩子也变傻
7490.e: Put the laptop away — all work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.  把电脑收起来吧，只知道干活不玩耍可不行。

7491.e: You can see the same forces at work in every failing high street.  在每条衰落的商业街上都能看到同样的力量在起作用。

7492.e: She went about her work quietly, ignoring all the noise around her.  她不理会周围的嘈杂，安静地做着自己的工作。

7493.i: go/set to ˈwork (on sth) (also get (down) to ˈwork (on sth))
7493.e: They set to work on the leaking roof before the rain got worse.  雨下大之前，他们就动手修那漏水的屋顶。

7494.i: have your ˈwork cut out (to do sth/doing sth) (informal)
7494.e: You'll have your work cut out persuading her to move abroad.  要说服她移居国外，你可有得忙了。

7495.e: He's been out of work since the factory closed down last spring.  自从去年春天工厂关门，他就一直失业。

7496.e: Can you work it so that we all fly out on the same day?  你能安排一下让我们同一天飞出去吗？

7497.e: She worked like a dog for two years to get the shop open.  她拼命干了两年才把这家店开起来。

7498.e: It was only the cat — your imagination is working overtime again.  不过是只猫，你的想象力又在超负荷运转了。

7499.i: have a ˌworking ˈknowledge of sth
7499.cn: 具备足够使用某物的知识
7499.e: The job needs a working knowledge of Spanish and some basic accounting.  这份工作需要会用西班牙语，还要懂点基础会计。

7500.i: in (full/good) working ˈorder (also in running ˈorder)
7500.e: The old tractor is still in perfect working order after forty years.  这台老拖拉机用了四十年，仍然运转正常。

7501.e: She's still remembered in the village for her good works during the war.  村里人至今记着她战时所做的种种善举。

7502.e: A sequel is already in the works, according to the director.  据导演说，续集已经在筹备中了。

7503.e: He ordered a burger with the works — cheese, bacon, onions, everything.  他点了个全套汉堡，奶酪、培根、洋葱，什么都有。

7504.i: be, live, etc. in a world of your ˈown
7504.e: My brother sits there in a world of his own for hours.  我弟弟能在那儿一坐几个钟头，活在自己的世界里。

7505.cn: 对某人极其重要；是某人的一切
7505.e: That battered old guitar means all the world to him.  那把破旧的吉他对他来说就是一切。

7506.e: They've come up in the world since he sold the software company.  自从他卖掉那家软件公司，他们家就飞黄腾达了。

7507.e: She came into the world during a snowstorm in the middle of February.  她是在二月中旬的一场暴风雪中降生的。

7508.i: for all the ˈworld as if/though...
7508.e: He stared at me for all the world as though we had never met.  他盯着我看，活像我们素未谋面。

7509.i: look, etc. for all the ˈworld like sb/sth (written)
7509.e: In that hat she looked for all the world like her own grandmother.  戴上那顶帽子，她看上去活像她奶奶。

7510.i: have the ˌworld at your ˈfeet
7510.e: At twenty-one, with two gold medals, he had the world at his feet.  二十一岁拿下两枚金牌，他前途无量。

7511.e: In a perfect world we'd all work four days a week.  在理想的世界里，我们都可以每周只上四天班。

7512.e: What in the world made you paint the kitchen bright orange?  你究竟为什么把厨房刷成亮橙色？

7513.cn: 见多识广的人；老成持重的人
7513.e: Talk to Ray about it; he's a man of the world.  这事跟雷谈谈吧，他见多识广。

7514.e: I wouldn't miss your wedding for all the world, you know that.  你知道的，你的婚礼我说什么也不会错过。

7515.i: not/never set the ˈworld on fire (informal)
7515.cn: 不会有惊人之举；不会引起轰动
7515.e: His first novel won't set the world on fire, but it sells steadily.  他的第一部小说不会轰动一时，但销量稳定。

7516.i: not/never set the ˈThames on fire (BrE, informal)
7516.cn: 成不了大器；不会引起轰动
7516.e: He's a decent player, though he'll never set the Thames on fire.  他球打得不错，不过成不了什么大器。

7517.e: The Einsteins of this world don't come along very often.  像爱因斯坦这样的人可不是常有的。

7518.e: The chocolate cake at that little café is out of this world.  那家小咖啡馆的巧克力蛋糕好吃得不得了。

7519.e: He joined the navy at eighteen because he wanted to see the world.  他十八岁参加海军，就是想去见见世面。

7520.i: what is the world ˈcoming to? (saying)
7520.cn: 这世道成什么样了；太不像话
7520.e: Children robbing children in broad daylight — what is the world coming to?  光天化日之下小孩抢小孩，这世道成什么样了？

7521.i: I don't know ˌwhat the world's ˈcoming to (saying)
7521.cn: 真不知这世道要变成什么样
7521.e: Six pounds for a coffee — I don't know what the world's coming to.  一杯咖啡六镑，真不知这世道要变成什么样。

7522.e: The world and his wife turned up at the beach on Sunday afternoon.  周日下午海滩上人山人海，谁都来了。

7523.e: You've got a degree and no debts — the world is your oyster.  你有学位又没负债，天地任你闯。

7524.i: a/the ˈworld of difference (between A and B) (informal)
7524.e: There's a world of difference between reading about Rome and actually living there.  读关于罗马的书和真住在那里，有天壤之别。

7525.e: Parents worry about exactly the same things the whole world over.  全世界的父母担心的事情都一模一样。

7526.i: (think) the world ˌowes you a ˈliving (disapproving)
7526.e: He's thirty and still thinks the world owes him a living.  他都三十了，还觉得这世界欠他的。

7527.e: Village life here is worlds away from her old flat in London.  这里的乡村生活与她在伦敦的旧公寓有天壤之别。

7528.cn: 兔子急了也咬人；老实人也会反抗
7528.e: After years of insults he finally answered back — the worm turns.  忍了多年羞辱他终于回嘴了，兔子急了也咬人。

7529.i: the ˌearly bird catches the ˈworm (saying)
7529.e: I queued at six and got the last ticket — the early bird catches the worm.  我六点就去排队，抢到最后一张票，早起的鸟儿有虫吃。

7530.cn: 底层视角；小人物的看法
7530.e: This memoir gives a worm's-eye view of life in a wartime factory.  这本回忆录提供了战时工厂生活的底层视角。

7531.i: be worried ˈsick • be sick with ˈworry
7531.e: Call your mother — she's been worried sick since last night.  给你妈打个电话，她从昨晚起就担心得要命。

7532.e: You had me worried there — I thought you'd missed the flight.  你可把我吓着了，我还以为你误机了。

7533.e: No worries, mate — I'll drop the parcel off on my way home.  没问题，伙计，我回家路上顺道把包裹送过去。

7534.e: Not to worry, we can always catch the later train instead.  别担心，我们可以改坐晚一班的火车。

7535.e: You should worry! You've already passed every one of your exams.  你有什么好担心的！你考试全都过了。

7536.e: After the tax changes most families are worse off than last year.  税制改革后，多数家庭比去年境况更差。

7537.i: you could do ˈworse (than do sth)
7537.cn: 不妨试试；倒不失为可取
7537.e: You could do worse than take the job while you look around.  你一边找工作一边先接下这份活儿，倒也不错。

7538.e: He argued with the referee and definitely came off worse.  他跟裁判争执，结果明显吃了亏。

7539.e: The weather went from bad to worse as we climbed higher.  我们越往上爬，天气就越糟。

7540.e: The dog fell in the canal but seems none the worse for it.  狗掉进了运河，看上去倒也没什么事。

7541.e: He arrived at the party already clearly the worse for drink.  他到派对时显然已经喝多了。

7542.e: My boots look a bit the worse for wear after that long hike.  走完那趟长途山路，我的靴子看着有点破旧了。

7543.e: I have to work on Saturday morning as well, worse luck.  我周六上午也得上班，真倒霉。

7544.i: sb's ˈbark is worse than their ˈbite (saying)
7544.cn: 刀子嘴豆腐心；嘴狠心软
7544.e: The old caretaker shouts a lot, but his bark is worse than his bite.  那老看门人爱嚷嚷，其实是刀子嘴豆腐心。

7545.e: She's her own worst enemy, turning down every offer of help.  她自己害自己，别人给的帮助一概拒绝。

7546.i: bring out the ˈworst in sb
7546.cn: 使某人显露最坏的一面
7546.e: Long queues in the heat really bring out the worst in people.  大热天排长队真能把人最糟的一面激出来。

7547.cn: 有什么手段尽管使出来
7547.e: Tell the newspapers if you like — go on, do your worst.  你愿意就去告诉报社好了，尽管使出你的招数。

7548.i: get the ˈworst of it • come off ˈworst
7548.e: Both cars were damaged, but the little hatchback got the worst of it.  两辆车都撞坏了，但那辆小两厢车损失最惨。

7549.i: if the ˌworst comes to the ˈworst (AmE also if ˌworst comes to ˈworst)
7549.e: If the worst comes to the worst, we can always sleep in the car.  万一实在不行，我们可以睡在车里。

7550.cn: 集各种不利因素于一身
7550.e: Renting there gives you the worst of both worlds: high rent and long commutes.  在那儿租房是两头吃亏：房租高，通勤还远。

7551.cn: 值得（花时间、金钱、精力等）
7551.e: The queue took an hour, but the view from the top was worth it.  排了一小时队，但山顶的景色值了。

7552.i: be worth your/its ˌweight in ˈgold
7552.e: A reliable babysitter is worth her weight in gold these days.  如今一个靠谱的保姆真是千金难求。

7553.i: do sth for ˌall you are ˈworth
7553.e: He rowed for all he was worth against the incoming tide.  他拼尽全力逆着涨潮划船。

7554.cn: 仅供参考；不论有用与否
7554.e: For what it's worth, I think you should turn the offer down.  仅供参考，我觉得你应该拒绝这个提议。

7555.i: not worth the paper it's ˈprinted/ˈwritten on
7555.e: Without a signature that contract isn't worth the paper it's printed on.  没有签字，那份合同连纸都不值。

7556.e: Any electrician worth his salt would have spotted that fault immediately.  但凡称职的电工都会立刻发现那个故障。

7557.e: It's well worth your while booking the tickets a month early.  提前一个月订票很值得。

7558.e: Everyone had spoken, so I added my two pennyworth about the parking.  大家都发言了，我就停车问题也说了点浅见。

7559.i: worthy of the ˈname (also worth the ˈname)
7559.e: No chef worthy of the name would ever use bottled lemon juice.  任何名副其实的厨师都不会用瓶装柠檬汁。

7560.i: wrap sb up in cotton ˈwool (informal)
7560.e: You can't wrap your kids up in cotton wool for ever.  你不可能永远把孩子捧在手心里过度保护。

7561.e: He's so wrapped up in his research that he forgets to eat.  他一门心思扑在研究上，连吃饭都忘了。

7562.i: keep sth, stay, etc. under ˈwraps (informal)
7562.e: The design was kept under wraps until the launch in March.  这个设计一直保密，直到三月发布。

7563.e: Stop wringing your hands and just phone the insurance company.  别在那儿干着急了，给保险公司打电话吧。

7564.e: There was plenty of hand-wringing at the meeting but no real decisions.  会上一片唉声叹气，却没做出任何实际决定。

7565.cn: 拧断某人的脖子（表示愤怒）
7565.e: If he scratches my car again I swear I'll wring his neck.  他要是再刮花我的车，我发誓要拧断他脖子。

7566.e: The interview panel really put him through the wringer for two hours.  面试小组足足折腾了他两个小时。

7567.e: He crashed the company van and got nothing but a slap on the wrist.  他撞了公司的货车，却只挨了轻描淡写的批评。

7568.e: Her disappointment was writ large across her face all evening.  整个晚上她的失望都明明白白写在脸上。

7569.i: be nothing, not much, etc. to write ˈhome about (informal)
7569.e: The hotel was clean but the breakfast was nothing to write home about.  酒店很干净，但早餐实在不怎么样。

7570.i: be nothing, not much, etc. to ˈshout about (informal)
7570.cn: 没什么值得夸耀的；一般般
7570.e: We won, though a one-nil result is nothing to shout about.  我们赢了，不过一比零的结果没什么好吹的。

7571.e: Please confirm the cancellation in writing before the end of the month.  请在月底前以书面形式确认取消。

7572.i: the ˌwriting (is) on the ˈwall (AmE the ˌhandwriting (is) on the ˈwall) (saying)
7572.cn: 不祥之兆；厄运临头的预兆
7572.e: When they closed two branches, the writing was on the wall for us.  他们关掉两家分店时，我们就知道大事不妙了。

7573.i: be written all over sb's ˈface
7573.e: Guilt was written all over his face when I mentioned the missing cash.  我一提丢钱的事，他脸上就写满了心虚。

7574.i: have sb/sth written all ˈover it (informal)
7574.e: This prank has your little brother written all over it.  这个恶作剧一看就是你弟弟干的。

7575.e: The investors backed the wrong horse and lost almost everything.  投资人押错了宝，几乎血本无归。

7576.e: Don't get me wrong, I like him — I just wouldn't hire him.  别误会，我喜欢他，只是不会雇他。

7577.i: get (hold of) the ˌwrong end of the ˈstick
7577.e: She got the wrong end of the stick and thought we were moving out.  她完全弄错了，以为我们要搬走。

7578.e: Something went wrong with the boiler in the middle of winter.  隆冬时节锅炉出了毛病。

7579.e: Admit you were in the wrong and she'll probably forgive you.  你承认自己错了，她多半就原谅你了。

7580.i: on the ˌwrong side of the ˈlaw
7580.e: He's been on the wrong side of the law since he was fifteen.  他从十五岁起就一直在跟法律作对。

7581.e: Please don't take this the wrong way, but that shirt doesn't suit you.  请别误会，不过那件衬衫不适合你。

7582.e: You can't go wrong with a black coat and a plain scarf.  黑大衣配素围巾，绝对错不了。

7583.e: He missed the last putt, and that's all she wrote.  他最后一推没进，比赛就此结束。

7584.e: Relax, I'm just yanking your chain about the parking ticket.  别紧张，罚单的事我只是逗你玩儿。

7585.e: She planned the wedding with flowers, a band, fireworks — the whole nine yards.  她把婚礼安排得鲜花、乐队、烟花一应俱全。

7586.e: Oh yeah? And who exactly told you that piece of news?  哦是吗？到底是谁跟你说的这个消息？

7587.i: in the ˌyear of ˈOur Lord (old use)
7587.e: The church was built in the year of Our Lord fourteen hundred and two.  这座教堂建于公元一四〇二年。

7588.e: The pool is heated, so we can swim there all year round.  游泳池有供暖，我们一年到头都能在那儿游泳。

7589.i: from, since, etc. the year ˈdot (BrE, informal)
7589.e: That pub has stood on the corner since the year dot.  那家酒吧从老早以前就立在那个街角了。

7590.i: from, since, etc. the year ˈone (AmE, informal)
7590.cn: 很久很久以前；从老早起
7590.e: My grandfather has been telling that same joke since the year one.  我爷爷从老早以前就一直讲那个笑话。

7591.e: Year after year the same family wins the village flower competition.  年复一年，村里花卉比赛的冠军都是同一家人。

7592.e: Year by year the coastline here is being eaten away by the sea.  这里的海岸线正被海水逐年侵蚀。

7593.e: He takes the same two weeks in Cornwall, year in, year out.  他年复一年都去康沃尔度那同样的两周假。

7594.e: Sales have risen eight percent year on year despite the downturn.  尽管经济下滑，销售额仍同比增长了百分之八。

7595.i: not/never in a hundred, etc. ˈyears (spoken)
7595.e: Not in a hundred years would I lend him my car again.  我再也绝不会把车借给他了。

7596.cn: 使某人显老；使人感到老迈
7596.e: That long illness has really put years on my poor father.  那场大病让我可怜的父亲一下子老了许多。

7597.e: That shorter haircut really takes years off you, you know.  说真的，这个短发让你看着年轻好几岁。

7598.e: I haven't seen Pete in donkey's years — how is he doing?  我好多年没见过皮特了，他还好吗？

7599.e: There's a yellow streak in him that shows whenever things get tough.  一遇到难事，他骨子里的怯懦就显露出来。

7600.e: Are you happy here? Yes and no — the work's good, the hours aren't.  你在这儿开心吗？说不准，工作不错，时间不行。

7601.e: The chairman surrounds himself with yes-men who never challenge anything.  董事长身边全是唯唯诺诺、从不提异议的人。

7602.cn: 某人没那么好骗；不是三岁小孩
7602.e: Don't try that excuse on me — I wasn't born yesterday.  别拿那种借口糊弄我，我又不是三岁小孩。

7603.e: As yet, nobody has claimed responsibility for the damage to the fence.  到目前为止，还没有人对篱笆的损坏负责。

7604.e: The castle stands as a reminder of the knights of yore.  这座城堡让人想起昔日的骑士。

7605.i: be, stay, etc. young at ˈheart
7605.e: At eighty he's still young at heart and dances every Friday night.  他八十岁了仍然人老心不老，每周五晚上都去跳舞。

7606.cn: 青春只有一次；及时行乐
7606.e: Take the trip while you can — you're only young once.  能去就去旅行吧，毕竟青春只有一次。

7607.e: Doctors are getting younger — mine looks about seventeen years old.  医生越来越年轻了，我的主治医生看着像十七岁。

7608.e: I'd better book that hike now; I'm not getting any younger.  我还是趁早订那次徒步吧，毕竟岁月不饶人。

7609.e: Best wishes to you and yours for a peaceful and happy Christmas.  祝你和家人圣诞平安喜乐。

715.e: The theatre needs a famous name to get bums on seats.  剧院需要请个名角来拉观众。

716.i: have a ˈbun in the oven (informal, humorous)
716.e: Judging by that grin, she's got a bun in the oven.  看她那笑容，八成是有了。

717.i: burn your ˈbridges (BrE also burn your ˈboats)
717.e: Don't burn your bridges with that firm; you may need them later.  别跟那家公司把关系闹死，以后可能还用得着。

718.i: burn the candle at both ˈends
718.cn: 起早贪黑；过度耗费精力
718.e: She's burning the candle at both ends, working days and studying nights.  她白天上班晚上读书，简直是在透支自己。

719.e: We burned the midnight oil to get the proposal in on time.  为了按时交上方案，我们熬了通宵。

720.e: I forgot the toast and burned it to a crisp again.  我忘了烤面包，又给烤成了炭。

721.e: The kitchen extension is on the back burner until next spring.  厨房扩建的事要搁到明年春天再说。

722.i: his, her, etc. ˈears are burning
722.cn: 感觉有人在背后议论自己
722.e: My ears were burning all evening; I knew they were gossiping.  我整晚都觉得耳朵发烫，知道他们在议论我。

723.e: He got his fingers burnt investing in that friend's little café.  他投资朋友的小咖啡馆，结果栽了跟头。

724.e: Calm down before you burst a blood vessel over a parking ticket.  为张罚单别气坏了身子，冷静点。

725.cn: 打破某人的美梦；泼冷水
725.e: I hate to burst your bubble, but the tickets sold out yesterday.  我不想扫你的兴，可票昨天就卖完了。

726.e: The cupboard door burst open and tins rolled across the kitchen floor.  柜门猛地弹开，罐头滚了一地。

727.e: She was bursting to tell someone about the new job offer.  她迫不及待想把新工作的事告诉别人。

728.cn: 我快憋不住了（要上厕所）
728.e: Stop at the next services — I'm bursting and it's getting urgent.  下个服务区停一下，我实在憋不住了。

729.e: Hurry up in there, will you? I'm absolutely bursting out here!  里面快点行吗？我在外面憋得不行了！

730.i: ˌbury the ˈhatchet • ˌbury your ˈdifferences
730.e: The brothers finally buried the hatchet at their mother's birthday dinner.  兄弟俩终于在母亲的生日宴上冰释前嫌。

731.cn: 小道消息的传播；口耳相传
731.e: News of the closure spread by bush telegraph before any official announcement.  停业的消息还没正式公布就已口耳相传开了。

732.e: The generator's fixed, so we're back in business by lunchtime.  发电机修好了，午饭前我们就恢复运转了。

733.i: be none of sb's ˈbusiness • be no business of sb's
733.e: How much I paid for the ring is none of your business.  这戒指我花多少钱买的不关你的事。

734.e: Never point the business end of a drill at anyone, ever.  千万别把电钻的钻头对着人。

735.e: I like him, but business is business and his quote is too high.  我挺喜欢他，可生意归生意，他报价太高。

736.e: Right, the coffee's finished, so let's get down to business.  好了，咖啡喝完了，咱们说正事吧。

737.e: The market traders went about their business as if nothing had happened.  市场里的摊贩照常忙活，好像什么都没发生。

738.i: have no business doing sth/to do sth
738.cn: 无权做某事；不该做某事
738.e: You had no business reading my letters while I was away.  我不在的时候你没资格看我的信。

739.e: Despite the flood damage, it's business as usual at the bakery.  尽管遭了水灾，面包店照常营业。

740.e: That old dog of theirs can still run like nobody's business.  他们那条老狗跑起来还是快得不得了。

741.i: not be in the business of doing sth
741.cn: 无意做某事；不做那种事
741.e: We're not in the business of giving refunds after six months.  我们不做六个月后还退款这种事。

742.e: Two more shops on this street went out of business last month.  这条街上个月又有两家店倒闭了。

743.e: A chef cooking at a friend's wedding is a real busman's holiday.  厨师去朋友婚礼上掌勺，真是休假不离本行。

744.i: bust sb's ˈchops (AmE, rather old-fashioned, slang)
744.e: Quit busting my chops about the dishes; I'll do them later.  别老唠叨洗碗的事，我一会儿就洗。

745.e: I've been busting my hump all week to finish this project.  为了完成这个项目，我拼命干了一整周。

746.e: Don't bust a gut trying to finish the whole thing tonight.  别拼了命想今晚就全干完。

747.e: The travel agency went bust and left hundreds of people stranded.  那家旅行社倒闭了，几百人滞留在外。

748.cn: 不成功便成仁；豁出去了
748.e: It's the coast by Friday or bust, whatever the weather does.  不管天气怎样，周五必须赶到海边。

749.e: The sergeant broke our balls for three solid months of training.  那个中士在整整三个月训练里把我们往死里操。

750.e: Gran's been as busy as a bee getting the house ready.  奶奶为收拾房子忙得像只蜜蜂。

751.e: You're a busy bee this morning, up before six again.  你今早可真忙，六点前又起来了。

752.cn: 让自己有事可做；不让自己闲着
752.e: Since retiring he keeps himself busy with the allotment and the choir.  退休后他侍弄菜地、参加合唱，让自己不闲着。

753.cn: 成为嘲弄（或批评）的对象
753.e: He was the butt of every joke at the office party.  在公司聚会上，他成了所有玩笑的靶子。

754.cn: 装出一副天真无辜的样子
754.e: She looks as if butter wouldn't melt in her mouth.  她看上去一副天真无辜的样子。

755.e: Repair work is our bread and butter; the new builds are bonuses.  维修活儿是我们的饭碗，新建项目算是额外收入。

756.e: I get butterflies in my stomach before every parents' evening.  每次家长会前我心里都七上八下。

757.e: Button it, both of you — the baby has only just gone down.  你俩闭嘴，宝宝刚睡着。

758.e: The train arrived at nine on the button for once.  火车难得一回九点整准时到站。

759.i: buy the ˈfarm (informal, humorous, especially AmE)
759.e: He nearly bought the farm when the ladder slipped last summer.  去年夏天梯子一滑，他差点没命。

760.e: Asking for more figures was just a way to buy time.  要更多数据不过是拖延时间的手段。

761.cn: 卖（或买）到无用之物；上当
761.e: I bought a pup with that car; it has broken down twice.  那辆车我买亏了，都抛锚两次了。

762.e: With so many flats standing empty, it's a buyer's market now.  这么多房子空着，现在是买方市场。

763.e: Give me a buzz when you get home from the airport.  你从机场到家后给我打个电话。

764.i: get a ˈbuzz out of/from sth (informal)
764.e: She gets a real buzz out of teaching small children to swim.  教小孩子游泳让她特别有成就感。

765.e: He sold the boat, the trailer, the whole caboodle, in one weekend.  一个周末他把船、拖车，全套家当都卖了。

766.e: They packed the whole kit and caboodle into one small van.  他们把全部家当塞进了一辆小货车。

767.e: Let's cut the cackle and decide who is driving tonight.  别闲扯了，定一下今晚谁开车。

768.e: The guard was in cahoots with the thieves the whole time.  那个保安一直和窃贼串通一气。

769.i: have your cake and ˈeat it (BrE)
769.cn: 又要马儿跑又要马儿不吃草
769.e: You can't have your cake and eat it — choose one job.  你不能又要这个又要那个，选一份工作吧。
